product_title: Moultrie M-1100i Game Camera
review_headline: but my cell phone takes far superior videos. Had to return 2 of them for ...
review_body: I bought 5 of these 1100i cameras in April, 2015. Have not used any other trail cams, so can't compare. But I got them to supplement other video taken with a DSLR. I expected decent "full HD" quality from them, but my cell phone takes far superior videos. Had to return 2 of them for replacement already (one failed to power up, second stopped turning on IR lights at night). Moultrie was good about replacing them quickly, but they shouldn't have failed so quickly. Main issues now: they often turn on IR lights when not needed, resulting in useless, white-out videos; in bright daylight conditions, video colors are grossly over-saturated, and/or over-exposed. If you just want these to identify what's out there, they're ok. But if you hope to get good quality hd video, you might be disappointed. I have gotten some reasonably good videos, but many disappointments too. And detection/startup time does not appear to be sub-second, or even close. Contacted Moultrie by email via website expressing these concerns, and a week later I still have rcvd no response at all. I just called them, asking if there might be a firmware update to correct issues, and was told there may be one next year (2016), but not before. Asked if there was a process where I could request these issues be addressed in the next update, and the rep had no clue how it's handled. Another issue is that the lenses are cheap, and some cameras have a blurry area in the video. Also, playback feature often hangs up unexplainably and I have to power off/on again, or better yet, just  take the SD card home and put it in a computer. All in all, they're useful, but in today's world of technology, the performance is sub-par. Moultrie: your support people should be better informed and responsive, your firmware updates more frequent, your product performance improved; I would rather have to pay a little more for a better camera than to put up with this.

product_title: Moultrie Game Spy A-5 Gen 2 Low Glow 5.0 MP Camera, Green
review_body:
It's a toss-up as to which is more user-unfriendly - the device or the instructions.

Some things I've learned:

1. You will have to put 8 AA batteries in the unit for proper functioning - even if you plan to use an external power source for long-term operation. The unit apparently does not have non-volatile memory for retention of settings, and the AA batteries are necessary for that purpose.

2. The port for the external 12 volt power source is on the bottom. Therefore, as a consequence, the power plug that goes into the port will extend from the bottom of the unit. No problem here, except when you fasten the unit to a photo tripod - be careful you don't crush or damage anything.

3. Data/photo cable readout - Tricky here - use a cable with a micro USB connector - then select set-up mode, then plug your cable in. "USB" appears on the little LCD readout and the usual dialog box appears on your computer screen. Moultrie HQ had not the foggiest about how to do this..

4. Since you will have to periodically remove the SD memory card for data retrieval, it would be nice if it could be easily done. But, no, that is not the case because the port for the card is located behind the latching mechanism for the front panel and is barely accessible - better have very small fingers here.

5. Turning the unit on and actually taking some pictures - not so easy either. You have to unlatch and open the front panel, throw the switch, and then latch everything up again. Ok, but again not so easy if the unit is on a tripod.

6. The actual pictures - if you get that far - don't look like 5 megapixel photos to me - not nearly so.

7 The instruction sheet has a section entitled "Setting time delay". I think this is intended to denote "setting minimum interval" between photos. Without a prescribed interval, the thing would go crazy snapping pix as fast as the hardware permitted..

8. I am currently using the cam with the Moultrie 12 volt battery external battery pack. I measured the current drain to ensure that, in fact, the power was coming from the external battery (it was). I also measured the current drain. When not busy, the current drain is negligible - in the low microamps. When the device snaps a picture, current drain jumps up to about 50 milliamps for a second or two. So it should remain operational for many days, if not weeks..

product_title: WOSS Attack Trainer Pro Suspension Fitness System with Rubber Sleeve Grips (Gunmetal Gray)
review_body:
It would be hard for me to overstate how much I love these straps. They are a game-changer for me, as I'll detail below.

First off, what do you get? Well, you get some adjustable nylon straps, a c ring, and some handles. Simple. Yes, comparable to other suspension systems, but at a fraction of the price. These are highly durable - I've put them to the test a number of times with my full weight (195 lbs), and there has never been an issue. I can't imagine that even someone who weighs close to 300 lbs could harm these things. They're tough. And they cost a fraction of what some other leading suspension training systems cost.

So the straps come with a metal door anchor - you simply close a door and the anchor locks them in place. They slide freely through a c clip, which is where you get to the challenge - exercising and balancing at the same time. If you want, you can simply loop these over a tree branch, play set, etc. - anything that is strong enough to hold your weight. So you can really work out just about anywhere (a word of caution - avoid those light weight hollow-core interior doors - I don't think those will hold).

I niavely thought I'd be able to bang out push ups like I had before. The first time I got maybe 5. These require a lot of focus, a lot of core, and the straps permit a greater range of motion. So this is also a great way to add a challenge to your workout routine - I did a simple chest/back routine and in the middle of that night woke up to my muscles firing like I couldn't believe. The attack trainer comes with a sheet of paper showing a number of different exercises, but to be honest, if you've lifted at a gym, these will be intuitive.

These straps are portable - the way they changed my life is that I can take them anywhere with me. So now working out at a hotel is simple - no excuses. And they've caused me to re-think how I exercise - now I'll simply read a book or do whatever, and then bang out a few sets. I can spread my work out over long periods of time, and I've found this spikes my metabolism and allows me to get a "deeper" workout. Net result has been that my body has started to transform - I'm not looking to be a body builder, but I definitely have a lot more tone and definition, and I'm not having to schlep to a gym, work out for an hour or an hour and a half, and then get changed. I'm working out as hard as I want, when I want, without really changing my life.

I train hard, like have to wipe the floor sometimes from sweat hard and I've never once felt like these could possibly slip. Now I start with 100 or 90s and plan on stepping up to 110s in the next two weeks. Absolutely no way I could do that without these straps.

Regular straps are a PITA to use on dumbells; these, again, let me use a false grip on 100 lb dumbells! Scary the first time but now it's just natural.

Over all these two small changes have increased my lifting, decreased my pain and the dinner I promised him to thank him will surely cost a lot more than these did. Get off the fence and buy these. product_title: Trijicon TR22 AccuPoint 2.5-10x56 Riflescope MIL-Dot Crosshair with Green Dot, 30mm Tube
review_body: I bought this scope off eBay about 6 months ago. I have had a Swift 4-12x50 on my A-bolt 300WSM for about the last 8 years. It has been a very good scope and has killed alot of deer. I have been wanting to step it up to the next level and now i finally have. My boss owns the TR23 5-20x50. Using his rifle on an afternoon hunt sold me on the accupoints. I wanted a low light scope with an illuminated reticle mainly for deer hunting. This scope has met and exceeded my expectations. There is a point in fading light where i can make out the deer but i can not see my cross-hairs. This scope will defiantly fix that problem and without using batteries. The tritium dot is perfect for my needs. If the sun is shining on the fiber optic bundle on top of the scope the dot will be lit up. If you are set up in the shade (shooting house or thick cover) and are looking into a bright field you will not see the lit up dot. It will look like normal cross-hairs, but as the light fades the dot will become more visible. In total darkness the tritium will light up the fiber optic bundle which lights up the dot. So if you have to have a lit up dot AT ALL TIMES (in very bright sunlight) this scope might not be for you. But for all practical purposes this is an excellent design. My dad has a Leopold VX-3 3.5-10x50. I have had both these scopes side by side in low light and the Leopold just cant hang with the Trijicon on light gathering capability. This is a very large scope and the 56mm objective is very big. I have the mil-dot reticle and i would recommend them to any hunter because of the range finding capability. I would recommend this scope to anyone looking for a low light capable illuminated scope. Trijicon's are made in the USA execpt for the Accupoints, they are made in Japan. The coolest part of the scope i never realized until after i bought it. There is a bible verse inscribed on the scope as part of the serial number on ALL trijicon optics. So I am defiantly going to be a repeat customer. Looking into getting the 1-4x24 for my AR. Hope this review helps and have a blessed day....

product_title: Stamina 1690 Power Tower
review_headline: Almost perfect, and definitely worth the price
review_body:
You cannot beat this for the price. It does its job beautifully and I am glad I got it.

I have 3 suggestions that would make this product better :

1) The spacing between the metal tubes holding the pull up bar is unfortunately a little more than shoulder width apart for me. So I can do a close grip pull up, or a wide grip pull up or a super wide grip pull up.. but if I try to do a shoulder width pull up my pinky rubs against the tube and it is annoying. The fix would have been to simple have the metal tube of the frame hold the entire pull up bar from the ENDS, so that the entire pull up bar was suspended with no interruptions in between and a full length of padding.

2) I have to periodically tighten the bolts on the frame. After a few days of use the frame doesn't feel as solid any more and it starts to rattle. This does not impact the functionality.. but just makes you want to go re-tighten everything. I am fine retightening the bolts, but I would have liked to have gone longer between having to retighten it.

3) Sometimes when I am doing a cheat rep on my last pull up I swing my body to get that additional rep in.. I have had the stand rock, but never felt it would tip over. However I weigh 174 lbs so I imagine this could be a little scarier for someone taller than me. It would be easy for the manufacturer to add a little more weight to the bottom part of the frame just to lower the center of gravity a little more. It isn't a big issue because I just place a couple of dumbbells on the frame to add a little more stability.

Like I said. Totally worth the price and I whole heartedly recommend it. Sometimes you have to make a few tradeoffs to get a quality product at a reasonable price.. But if the manufacturer had addressed the above three points for me, or perhaps even just the first point, it would have gotten a 5 star rating from me.

* Very easy installation, including tools needed (although I grabbed a socket wrench & cordless screwdriver to speed it up, you do not have to have any additional tools)

Cons:
* Bike seats are bike seats, so don't expect this to feel like a memory foam mattress. It is not extremely comfortable, but probably as good as you can expect from a bike seat.
* It would be nice to have a little more 'play' in the location of the desk. For me, being taller means I have to raise the seat. Every notch the seat goes up, it also goes further away from the desk, which results in me feeling further away than I would like.

Other Notes:
* I personally only use it for 'passive' work, like conference calls, watching presentations, etc. I don't find it extremely easy to peddle & do much active work (Excel, PPT, email), but perhaps I will get more used to that.
* I can not imagine this being a full time replacement desk from a comfort/ergo standpoint. I plan to try to find a 2 hour block every day that I can use it.

product_title: Longquan sword/Tang Jian/Carbon steel blade/Dark wood scabbard/Alloy fitted/Full Tang/Length 39"
review_body:
I'm giving this only 3 stars, due to a quality/construction issue.

The sword is nice enough--the blade is good quality, and the wood of the handle and scabbard seem to be good as well. Where this sword failed is in the handle pins.

Upon initial inspection, I found that the second pin (holding the tassel, which has a ring on one side--seen in the photos) was loose. Upon further inspection, I found that the peen of this pin was not well executed. So bad, in fact, that it was removed without any tools (pulled out by hand). I then found that the pin itself was bent...this was due to the size of the pin vs. the size of the hole. The hole was slightly larger than the pin material, allowing it to bend when the pin was peened. This also allowed for the tang to rattle around inside the handle. Not good. Pins need to be EXACTLY the same diameter as the hole they go through. (ETA: top pin, near the guard, is bamboo with metal coverings...)

To repair this, I am replacing both pins with steel pins (original pin material is a zinc alloy...rather soft) of the same diameter as the hole through the handle and tang. I'm still using the decorative washers (which I re-drilled) that give the sword handle some of its decoration. This will yield a good looking, functional sword. (ETA: completed the replacement of the pins, much more solid now. Quite pleased with the modification)

Not meaning this to be a "bad" review--aside from the pin issue (which is fixable), this is a good sword, worth the price paid. So long as the buyer has the know-how to make this slight repair (or has a friend/relative who can), the sword is a good purchase. With 10 minutes of your time to replace the pins, it's a good addition to any collection.

review_headline: This is a great item for everyday use and I've been carrying it ...
review_body:
I would have given a 3 but the price is so low it bumped me up a star. This is a great item for everyday use and I've been carrying it for around 3 weeks daily, everyday. The good.. The clip is held in place by the striking tip, which has very lose screws. Twice while in my pocket the top and clip have unscrewed and fallen off. Lucky both times I've been able to recover them as they make a racket falling to the floor but I would suggest using locktite or similar product to add resistance.

All in all I might suggest using a real Parker ink refill and adding some locktite to the striker screws but for the price this pen is pretty decent.

Thanks,
Eric

product_title: Guide Gear Deluxe Hunting Hang-On Tree Stand
review_headline: Great Value but make some inexpensive tweaks before hunting
review_body: I've bought quite a few of these directly from SG over the last 5 years... they are a great value but I recommend a few inexpensive tweaks when assembling them.  The packaging can be inconsistent as far as nuts, bolts, and washers go... definitely not a showstopper from buying these stands. If there are not any (or enough) nylon washers included, buy some and add them when mounting the seat to the frame.  After a year or so in the weather, they will develop some squeaks and sounds that could alarm a deer at the worst possible time.  By ensuring there are nylon washers on both the bolt head and nut sides of the seat mount, you'll save yourself a lot of heartache.  Another thing I do is to forego the strap-on seat and mount a 1' x 2' piece of treated 1/2" plywood by simply drilling a hole through both the plywood and seat rail, then bolt it together... it's completely silent (no buckles to clang when you raise the seat).  Also, I just carry a comfortable seat pad and I can stay out all day very comfortably.  For the money, you cannot beat this stand... just be ready to make a couple of inexpensive adjustments to prevent missing a chance at a big one.

review_body:
I LOVE my new chair.

It was slightly 'damaged' in shipping, but not enough for me to return it. The metal posts poked out of the cardboard box in shipping, slightly bending the post for the chair-back. I was able to unbend it enough with pliers to get the chair-back put on.

I haven't had any problems with the ball.

The only drawback is that the locking levers on the wheels are very sensitive. I often hit at least one of the levers with the back of my shoe when I move my foot around, thus locking up that wheel. I then have to stand up, unlock the wheel, and sit down again, trying very hard to not bump the lock AGAIN as I scoot forward towards the desk.

I'm testing my plan for dealing with this. I've taken duct tape and am trying to keep the levers in an unlocked position by taping the lever 'upwards.' It has worked so for with only 2 days of testing, but I have hope this will be a long-term fix.

The chair is more comfortable than I expected. I no longer have hip pain when I stand up after sitting for a while, like with a traditional chair. I definitely feel like I'm sitting up high enough for my desk. I don't 'feel' like I'm getting core workout or anything, but that wasn't my goal. I do feel like I am being forced to sit with proper posture, else I'd fall off of the ball. I'm only 5'2" and I'm happy with how it accommodates my short stature comfortably with the legs in their lowest position.

review_body:
I ordered a pair of these mops because they supposedly are suitable for cleaning 7.62 weapons. I have a Century International C39V2 AK-47. I like to use a mop as the last stage of cleaning the bore after firing the weapon. I went to use one of these mops and it is way too small for a 7.62mm bore. I followed it up with two or three more clean patches before all traces of the solvent were gone.

These mops look very similar size wise to the 22 caliber bore mops I have. However, the have 30 for 30 caliber stamped into the metal at the base of the mop. I have used other Remington products on the various calibers of fire arms which I own and those products have always been the right size and performed well but not in this case.

product_title: Velocity Recurve Pistol Crossbow, Black
review_headline: 2) Most pistol crossbows require two people to string them to make it fast and easy. Do it right the string won't break
review_body:
As with every pistol crossbow I have seen, they all require assembly.
1) Assemble it wrong it will break, not work right or misfire. Some safeties are touchier than others. Learn how the safety works.
2) Most pistol crossbows require two people to string them to make it fast and easy. Do it right the string won't break.
3) ALL strings will break/fray fast if you don't keep them waxed.
4) Keep the rails lubed and cleaned.
5) ALL pistol crossbows are somewhat hard to cock. They have a lot of power in a small package. I place my on my right leg, hold the front grip and cock it.
6) If your target is too hard (plywood) the bolts won't last but a few shots. If you target is too soft (cardboard box) the vanes (feathers) won't last but a few shots. Find the right target to shoot at. The bolt should only go about half way in making it easier to pull out.
7) The sights are cheap? Buy a better sight.

These seem to be the most common complaints. It takes about 10 minutes to fully research how to use and maintain a pistol crossbow. Spend those 10 minutes instead of finding out things the hard or costly way. And stop complaining! :D

This is one of the best pistol crossbows on the market. Exercise some common sense and do some research and this will last a long time.

product_title: Silicone Wedding Ring - Set of 2 - Logo Free - Men's Black and Blue Rubber Wedding Band Collection for Active Lifestyles by WarriorRing
review_headline: Variety is the spice of life, but durability is key...
review_body:
These rings are awesome. I wanted something to wear when my wedding ring didn't seem to fit the bill. While my wedding ring is a beautifully crafted piece of jewelry that we selected to compliment my wife's engagement ring there are times I'd rather not wear it. I've noticed over the years because it has some grooves cut in the backside to reduce weight it gains a lot of gunk. I don't like to go without a wedding band at any time. It just makes my hand feel strange. The Warrior Ring is a fantastic alternative to my wedding ring for sports, mechanic work, remodeling, etc. I really like that Warrior Ring offers a duo pack. I tend to like to have some variety in my life. Being able to switch between the two is a nice added bonus. If there was one small complaint I could have, it would be that the rings aren't available in half sizes. I know minimizing production costs allows manufacturers to provide quality products at the best price; so, I'm fine with it being a smidge loose.

These rings feel extremely durable and strong; yet, they are soft, light, and comfortable. They stay put on my finger and after a couple minutes, I sometimes find myself checking to make sure the silicone wedding band hasn't disappeared. My wife and I are both partial to the blue band. It's very vibrant, but the black ring also offers a really nice looking option. I'm EXTREMELY satisfied with the quality of these products.

Warrior Ring also includes a one year warranty from date of purchase. I could understand if you are doing mechanic work how you could scuff, cut, or snap a band like this. Warrior Ring has accounted for this with their warranty program.

If your someone who works a job or participates in activities/hobbies that lend themselves to scratching, bending, or otherwise damaging your wedding band, or if you want a lightweight durable option backed by a company's quality promise to substitute for your current wedding band, the Warrior Ring is for you. If your significant other participates in any of the aforementioned activities/occupations I'm sure they'd welcome this gift.

I really can't see any reasons why every man couldn't find some useful times to dawn the Warrior Ring. Get one. I don't think you'll be disappointed.

Versa Peep
3 different size inserts w/ 3 different colors
Insert/removal tool

Pros:
Versatility
Customization
Build quality
Price point

Cons:
Haven't found any yet

The main benefit of this tape over traditional athletic tape is that it is specifically designed to allow for freedom of movement and flow of body fluids that speed healing times. Studies have also proven that Kinesiology tape is both sweat-proof and waterproof, Therefore it will not come loose during and intense work out and it can be worn in the shower or pool. Application can last anywhere from 3-5 days and most athletes notice changes to treated areas in as little as 24 hours. The taping is non restrictive with 180% stretch and allows for full range of motion which is critical for those who are recovering from or seeking to avoid injury. You should always be properly trained on how to apply it so as not to further injure yourself. The tape is applied from the origin of the muscle to where it inserts for support and the opposite direction is stretched and taped for rehabilitation. The ultimate goal of the tape is to help the muscles work with proper biomechanics. In fact, he has become so good swimming around with this thing, we have taken it off a few times and he can swim short distances. I never would have thought a child would feel more secure in this than in the larger Puddle Jumper, but I think he does. It saved our summer!

product_title: Zoma Swimming Goggles with Anti Fog Technology - 3 Piece Adjustable Nose Bridge for Perfect Comfortable Fit for Adults and Kids - Ergonomic Silicone Earplugs Included
review_body:
Best. Goggles. Ever. I have gotten back into swimming after a few years. I always had Speedo Vanquisher because everyone just buys Speedo and my daughter (who is a young teen competitive swimmer) wears them. My eyes would hurt, the suction was too great, they would fog up even with anti-fog spray, and they leaked after one season so I bought new ones every year. I was skeptical thinking I didn't need another brand, but I have no idea why... SO HAPPY I made the switch. I'm no longer stopping after a 50 to adjust the goggles and give my eyes a break. I wasn't thrilled with the mirrored lenses but the clarity I have in the pool is so amazing I don't care. Something as simple as a $20 well-fitted goggle has taken my workout to a new level. Thank you!

UPDATE: So it's been 5 months or so since my first review. I'm on my second pair. I wore out the old ones, since I do swim almost daily and the anti-fog coating got smudged so my view wasn't very clear. I don't know if any pair of goggles are going to last as long as I'd like them to but the price is now $10 for these so I can afford to buy a new pair whenever I need to. Still 5 stars, still very happy.

product_title: Kershaw Shallot Knife with Partially Serrated Blades and 410 Stainless Steel Handle
review_headline: The largest, and one of the best, in the Kershaw Ken Onion line
review_body: I own several Kershaw knives, and this is now one of my favorites.  It is long enough to take serrations and still leave plenty of blade, so if you're thinking of getting a serrated Leek or Scallion, this might be a better bet.  My thinking also is that the recurve on the non-serrated Shallot might be a pain to sharpen, but with serrations instead it eliminates that potential concern (sharpening on a recurve) and turns it into a plus, for me anyway.  With it's stainless handle and quick assisted opening, this knife basically reminds me of a beefier, larger Leek.  The blade has enough of a point, and is thin enough, to do detailed work, but the overall impression is that this is a much more substantial knife, capable of handling most tasks. This is a flipper only knife, and I've come to really appreciate them when done correctly, like this one -- there is no foolish jimping in the flipper area, jimping is on the back of the blade (the flipper itself).  The knife might prove a bit large for EDC if you're an office type, but that's why there is so much variety -- no knife is perfect for every task, but instead is a compromise within a set of parameters.

product_title: Hatsan HC9522VORT 95 Combo Vortex Piston, .22, Walnut
review_body:
I've had this air rifle for about a month now and love it. Not much I can add to the positive reviews and I'm glad that I read them. I pretty much knew what I would be getting. A couple of points that have been discussed before:

1. This is a full sized rifle, definitely not for children or smaller people. Weighs around 9 lb. plus with scope.
2. I ordered a Hammers 3-9 scope along with the rifle, so can't speak about the included scope, just put it away.
3. I'll stress this point - don't judge the accuracy until you run at least 150 or so pellets through it. I had the usual combination of sighting in the scope, loose screws (yep, blue loctite time), and figuring out which pellets MY rifle liked and learning how different a air rifle is from a typical .22 rifle.
4. Once you learn how to handle and cock the rifle, life gets easier. I enjoy target shooting at 25 yards, and the method that works for me from a sitting position is to put the top of the stock butt against my left foot, rap the end of the barrel with my open hand to open it, then use both hands to cock it. Load the pellet and close smartly. I can shoot all day with this method. Using the standing method with stock against my left thigh and cocking with one hand soon has me wheezing and in search of a beer.

There are lots of videos out there from airgun depot and pyramid air with great info. Also, you need to learn about the "artillery hold". They speak the truth about this method. What works well for a .22 rimfire rifle doesn't work so well with the 2-way recoil of an air rifle.

Love these Bushnells. They are about the same zoom range as our 350$ pair of Nikon Binoculars. My grandmother and I use this for spotting and viewing wildlife in Yellowstone National Park. It is amazing to not have to focus when we swap the binocs to each other, and it is wonderful lending to other tourists and their children.

Our expensive pair of Nikons has a slightly lower zoom range, and is manual focus. There is a very large blur and distortion of the image (almost fisheye effect when looking through them), whereas the bushnells have no distortion and are perfectly clear. And the best part? I compared it to my optishot and I don't really know which is more accurate but I would assume the optishot is more accurate but swing speed on swing talk was consistently a bit higher by 3-5 mph. Also make sure to readjust the device to line it up correctly with the club head after every few swings. The alignment of the device makes a huge difference.

I would definitely recommend Swingtalk. It gives a lot of information that would otherwise be impossible to get at the range. It's also a lot cheaper than its competitors.

product_title: Schwinn 270 Recumbent Bike
review_headline: Working out while sitting on your butt watching TV. What a time to be alive!
review_body:
This bike offers a wonderful no-impact option that is very easy on joints and bones.

If even I can assemble this, so can you.

It's easily assembled solo. Very minor lifting required. Make sure the delivery guy brings the box into your house - the box by itself is pretty heavy. The pieces inside weight as much as 20 pounds or so individually.

It's very easy to drop screws (or tools, or earrings, or anything really) into the wheel well while you're assembling it. If you do this, get a good strong flashlight, tip the bike back, and the objects will be hiding on two screws near the front of the wheel well.

The heart rate monitor is meh. I have to grip the handles pretty hard for it to get a reading, and it doesn't seem accurate. I would recommend just pretending this bike doesn't have a heart rate monitor.

The tablet holder is great and does just what it says it will - hold your tablet up so that you can watch videos while you work out. C'mon, you know you want to.

The seat is moderately cushioned. As a woman with a lot of "fluff" this seat does fine for me. The bike is pretty friendly to big people like myself. It doesn't even seem to be silently judging me that often.

There are several built in programs. I was hoping for programs that adopted based on the length of the workout, or challenges where you could set it to complete a certain number of miles in a certain amount of time. If there's a way to do this, I haven't found it.

Overall, a very good bike, very easy to use, and easy to assemble even for the mechanically challenged.

product_title: Harbinger Training Grip Wristwrap Weightlifting Gloves with TechGel-Padded Leather Palm (Old Style), XX-Large
review_headline: Oustanding quality, terrific support, and surprisingly not bulky for cross training workouts
review_body:
Believe the hype.

Needing an upgrade over older Harbinger (beaten to death and now peeling) and BNooch (Velcro keeps falling aparty gloves, terrific reviews led me to purchase a pair of these bad boys.

For my purposes, I want/ed a glove for lifting, one that can take the grind of pushups/mountain climbers on concrete/turf, sled pushes/rope swings, barbell/kettle bell lifts, etc. Also not get disgusting from heavy sweating (it is W FL, after all). In short, a 'beat the bejeebuz out them' glove set.

These, my friends, are it. The pictures tell a tale of a seemingly bulky set of gloves...with a tail-length wrist wrap. Nope, and thankfully nope. Streamlined, well made, and with a nice support system that doesn't overwrap, these guys are a winner. Yes, they're around $10 more than I would've liked to spend, but - in this instance - you really do get what you pay for.

On the sizing part, get yourself a $1 sewing kit...and properly measure hand radius, as described, with the included tape. Using this info, I found these gloves a perfect fit...at a size larger than I usually purchase.

product_title: Pinnacle Tiny Deadbolt Spinning Reel
review_body:
Nice enough reel. I use this reel mainly for trout fishing in small mountain streams, attached to a 5'6" ultralight rod. Currently spooled with 4lb test. The design is fine. It also looks very nice with a matte gold finish, and wooden handle. The front drag is easy to adjust. I had to make some adjustments to the bail out of the package. After casting, bail was tight and would not close completely. I had to loosen the screws, and now it works well for the most part. One of the issues with this reel (and I have encountered this with all UL reels I have used) is the tiny spool. Because the diameter is small, even with high quality, "zero memory" mono line, the line gets coiled after a while. This leads to some tangles occasionaly. The gearing is 5.1:1, which is good, but again with the small spool, still creates a slower retrieve. Overall, reeling and the drag are smooth enough. The instant anti reverse is nice as well, which I did not have in some of my older UL reels.

This is not a top end reel, so expectations should be moderate, but it performs well enough. For ~$20, this is one of the better UL reels I have used. I have landed a few smaller trout and a smallmouth bass so far with no problems.

product_title: Kharma Khare Hybrid Bliss Non Slip Eco-Friendly Yoga Mat - 5 Mm
review_body:
Ok, I'll start with the positives: it doesn't stretch and it's compactly cushy. The positives, the reason why I gave it 2 stars and not 1, unfortunately stop there.

I sweat buckets when I do yoga, so I was blindly suckered into buying this mat with the promo pics of a woman doing a plank on a Kharma Khare mat that was laden with puddles of water. I saw this and thought, "I sweat less than puddles of water, so this will be perfect for me."
The colorful side of the mat is essentially completely smooth and IS NOT grippy or sticky in the least. I still needed my yoga towel so that I wouldn't fall on my face doing downward dog.
I thought then to try the black side, the side that is chopped up exposed recycled tire. This side is nicely sticky, however the tire side leaves tire crumbs all over my skin. Not only that, there is already a divot forming on the exposed tire side that is getting bigger. I used this side once.

Now to the weight: from what I can tell, this is the heaviest mat on the market, weighing in at a whopping 8 lbs. The Clever Yoga Mat strap http://www.amazon.com/gp/aw/d/B00UVOS7NW/ref=mp_s_a_1_2?qid=1438957346&sr=8-2&pi=AC_SY200_QL40&keywords=clever+yoga+strap&dpPl=1&dpID=41-WKIKa0tL&ref=plSrch makes a huge difference so it doesn't feel as heavy while wearing it on my shoulder, but rolling the mat hurts my wrists and picking the mat up isn't great for my scoliosis; ironically, I started doing yoga to help straighten my spine.

I tried to find the perfect mat, one that didn't negatively impact the environment and one that helped my practice, and with this mat purchase, I failed. Please look somewhere else.

product_title: Gold's Gym 310 Elliptical Stride Trainer
review_body:
I've been using this elliptical trainer for over 6 months now - 5x a week. It was a bit squeaky in the beginning (like other commenters noted) but once the bolts started to settle in I was able to find the part that was squeaking the most/loudest (left handle joint, middle) and take it apart, re-oil it, and the squeaking is minimal now. I don't even hear it over my earbuds.

It's a pretty good deal for the price. The assembly took me, at just 5'4" and 130Lbs, one hour. (IQ may account for some of the assembly time, too?) The onscreen workouts are actually pretty tough - the pedals seem very center-driven, even level "0" resistance requires some leg or arm power, that's to say the pedals aren't spinning out of control when you want to slow down. It switches between resistance really smooth. The calories burned aren't too far off from my heart monitor's reading, usually off by about 50 cals more.

My only gripe is that is counts revolutions per minute so I had to figure out how many revolutions equals a mile - and math is not my strong suit. My calculations gave me 960 revolutions to 1 mile. But you can do your own math. The equation is readily available through a search engine inquiry.

Also, this machine is all about resistance. There are no incline adjustments, but it's still one heck of a workout!

product_title: AccuMed CMS-50D Pulse Oximeter Finger Pulse Blood Oxygen SpO2 Monitor w/ Carrying case, Landyard Silicon Case & Battery (Black)
review_body:
First, full disclosure, I received this item at a greatly reduced price from the distributor in exchange for an honest review, which is what I intend to give.
This is my fourth pulse oximeter and until they embed them into smartphones, I believe it will be my last, as it does everything I could want and does it very simply.
The box comes with the device, strap, case and batteries. Even though they look like cheap heavy-duty, they are in fact alkaline so they should last a very long time. They are easy to install with no tools. They did come bundled with a plastic that is hard to break. I had to use scissors.
The device is strong and the hinge appears durable. It has a single button that turns it on and then cycles the screen through different views of basically the same information. There's a view for every possible orientation of the device, so choose the one you like and the device will remember it next time you use it.
Operation is pretty fast, normally only a couple of seconds to stabilize readings. Seems faster than my previous ones.I have found that if my hands are a bit dirty, from example from working on my car and then washing them, it will not read well.
I carry mine in its case inside my backpack and it holds very well to normal wear and tear. The protective film on the screen has not even fallen off.
This is the same brand that they use in the hospital where they had a relative of mine, so I guess it's accurate and reliable.
I would definitely recommend it to anyone who needs it.

product_title: Sougayilang Carbon Fishing Rod Telescopic Saltwater Spinning Fishing Pole (1pc)
review_headline: Nice Feel And Action...But Very Light Weight..Good For Kids..
review_body:
This rod looked pretty impressive out of the box. It has a nice solid feel to it and it extended very well. I was able to effortlessly get it to collapse again without a problem. After I attached a reel to it I full extended it hard and tried out a few casts in the back yard. It had a nice light, but solid feel to it. I took it to a pond with a 7 pound line installed...

Unfortunately, this reel didn't stand up to anything that gave me any fight. It was fine for a couple of pumpkinseeds that I pulled in. But when I hooked a crappie, it near snapped in half and I was lucky to land it. As much as I like the feel and action of it, it really is a very light weight rod that I would suggest for a kid to use. Not bad for a backup since it folds up nicely and can be carried along on a hike. Not a bad choice at all for carrying along on a trip where you are going to be backpacking it. . But as a main pole in your arsenal I cannot recommend it for anything but a starter pole, or regular use for a kid...

Free unit supplied in exchange for an honest review..

product_title: MetalTac Airsoft Speed Loader with Capacity of 100 Bbs
review_headline: You get what you pay for.
review_body:
It's not bad, it works, but not perfectly, I have had some trouble getting the BBs to go into the mags a few times and a few times where the mechanics inside jam up a little and it can sometimes eject BBs before they go into a magazine. But beyond that, it's far far superior to jamming 6mm spheres one at a time into a magazine with a heavy spring and will save you fingers and time. The little tip comes separate from the loader and only slips on over the end the BBs come out of but it doesn't stay on too well, relying on a pair of plastic hooks that look prone to breakage. I solved this by super gluing it on and it seems to work just fine all the same I would caution you to be careful where you apply it and to not use too much as you could end up jamming the opening or the insides up and ruining it. It's easy to load with a little flip open door at the bottom near the plunger, just flip it open and pour them in and you're set to go. A neat little feature is the ability to lock the plunger down keeping it safe, the mechanism on mine is a bit loose and can pop out accidentally but it's never really been an issue as it fits perfectly into one of my pistol mag pouches even with the tip permanently glued on.

All in all it's a good cheap buy, it's under ten bucks and it will quickly earn a place in your heart as one of your "Do not forget" pieces of gear, if you're a pistol enthusiast or just have terrible aim, this little gadget will help cut back on the tedious task of thumbing BBs into a tiny tiny opening.

product_title: Brunswick Mastermind Scholar Bowling Ball
review_body:
The Scholar has an Ultra low rg core combined with a high differential making this ball one of the most aggressive and angular pearl bowling balls ever produced. The great thing about this ball is how easily it gets through the front part of the lane regardless of what happens to the heads. When it clears the pattern it has complete stored energy making a strong angular shape to the pocket. Do to its flipping power, this ball can recover from almost anywhere. You can use this ball on almost any pattern, its incredibly versatile allowing you to play multiple angles. With its an awesome color combination this ball looks awesome going down the lane. It looks even better as it penetrates the pins. This ball hits so hard which is a product of all the stored energy its able to sustain due to the cover and core combination.

I’ve drilled one 75 x 4 1/2 x 70. This is a pin down drilling. I wanted to create some versatility in my ball motion. If for some reason my pin above drilling (see below) is going to lane, I can easily switch to this ball to get the ball going sooner. The characteristics of this drilling has made the ball pick up soon, but looks like it has a heavy roll. When the ball clears the pattern it makes a hard aggressive arc to the pins. Then it has a continuous monition through the pins allowing for optimal carry. Since this ball stores so much energy you can still have a pin under drilling look very strong down lane. The Honor Roll A+ cover gets this ball through the fronts with ease. This can easily be the first ball out of the bag.

The second one I drilled 75 x 5 x 35 which is a pin above drilling. I tend to use this drilling on my more competitive sport conditions. By drilling the Scholar this way, I’m able to really get the ball down lane, when it clears the pattern, you can literally see the ball flip quickly and make an angular move to the pocket. I really love the forgiveness of this ball as well as the versatility of the Scholar. If you miss right, with its strong flipping characteristics this ball can recover from almost anywhere. The other perk, is if you tug it a bit into the longer part of the oil pattern, where with most balls you’d leave a flat 10 or 7 (left handers), this ball will react very strongly and punch those corner pins out.

Since the ball has so much stored energy, it hits the pins with strong continuous motion. Also with this potential energy your carry with this ball is amazing. It gives great versatility and forgiveness to every bowler. It is the most incredible pearl bowl I’ve ever thrown. My carry is amazing with this ball, this is a must for your bowling arsenal.
Please feel free to email me at troy_300_1999@yahoo.com with any questions.

Troy Schaefer
Brunswick Regional Staff Player
#bowlwithbruns #teamBrunswick

product_title: Cold Steel 97MKM Magnum Kukri
review_body:
I just purchased this blade for some yard brush clearing.
Ordering and shipping was fast and easy as always. Fresh out of the package I found a fair edge; I would personally have liked a sharper edge, but this was sufficient. I was able to clear out the brush as well as a few saplings with ease.
The grip fit well in my hand, comfortable and almost cushy; I've held grips that I felt gripped my hand in return, this came close to that feeling. Not bad for a hot and humid day. Never felt any slipping or loss of grip or control at any point.
There is also a lanyard hole if anyone is so inclined to add a length of 550 cord ( http://titanparacord.com/survivorcord/ ) or whatever you like.

This kukri machete has a nice feel while swinging; good forward balance, where I expected it. I read reviews of this blade that said it was "heavy," I did not think it was given what it is and its purpose. I am not trying to swing a battle axe or split wood with a five- or ten-pound splitting axe; this was a two-pound machete.

The sheath is decent; it has what appears to be a cordura or ballistic material for most of the length with a poly cap at the point. Stitching looks decent at a cursory once-over. There is a one-inch wide hook-and-loop for a belt up to about two-inches wide.
Overall, I like this blade. It made light work of some thickening, encroaching brush.

product_title: Schrade SCHF45 Leroy Full Tang Bowie Fixed Blade Knife
review_headline: Baddest Blade in the Whole Damn Town!
review_body:
Okay, I hate to pull the cliché out, but THAT's A KNIFE!
I got mine from another online vendor but I would have happily paid the "retail" price Schrade has here. Mine came hair-popping sharp right out of the box which is what I've come to expect from Schrade. I took mine out in the yard and went through 3 and 4" dried oak firewood like an axe when I chopped with it. Didn't even have to baton until I hit some thicker knotted stuff. Still went through like butter. This bad boy is a CHOPPER! I've got a Schrade Schbolo and it didn't chop as deeply or as effectively as "Leroy" here. The TPE scales/grips did a lot to minimize the normal vibration you get from chopping with such a large completely full tang blade.
Feather sticks were no problem with the forward choil. I did take a metal file to the aggressive jimping on the back because it was biting into my thumb, but now, it's smooth enough to where it's useful and not painful. I don't think you'd notice the original jimping if you wear gloves, but in the desert, I don't always want to wear them.
Now, I'm no expert on metals, but it seemed like Leroy held his own considering all the chopping and cutting I did. When I got back inside, it still shaved paper, but didn't pop any hair until I made a couple of passes on my Smiths TriHone system. After that, it was sharper than it was out of the box and with minimal effort. I will say that my SCHF9 stayed sharp even after about the same amount of wood processing, so there must be something to the 1095 that the SCHF9 is made of. That and the fact that the SCHF9 and SCHF42 are made in Taiwan might help also.
This SCHF45 is made in China and has caused me to change my mind about certain Chinese made blades. I deal with crappy Chinese made guitars and have yet to find any that are worth their price. This SCHF45 has made me see that with the proper quality control, like the efforts Schrade has shown, good blades can be produced at an amazing value. This is not too unbelievable in that the Chinese have been making blades far longer than they've been making guitars. However, I still "prefer" Schrade's Taiwanese blades.
Speaking of "value"... if you're looking for a tool that can take the place of a hatchet with less weight... a true CHOPPER that won't break your wallet like a TOPS Armageddon, then the SCHF45 is exactly what you need. "Leroy" fits right in with my Schrade collection. First, the SCHF42 for light bushcraft, the SCHF9 for heavier tasks and some chopping, the SCHF45 for heavy bushcraft and heavy chopping and I am pretty much covered. The best thing about these knives is that they can fill in and cover for each other while at the same time filling their own special niches in my survival kit. I would have no trouble taking care of myself and my family in a survival situation with any or all of these three products.
One last word... the sheath for the SCHF45 is a great thick, HARD nylon (ABS?) sheath that will protect both the blade and YOU if you happen to be wearing it on your belt when you go sliding/tumbling down a wet hill side. Many modern "nylon cloth" sheaths cannot guarantee that the sharp tip of the blade they hold won't come through, piercing both the sheath and your body. Which is why I always make an interior plastic sheath for my blades with soft plastic milk jug covers. I still like some of my MTech blades like this because they have nice pockets that hold full sized Altoids tins. But THIS hard sheath for Leroy saves me from having to do that. It has lots of riveted holes and slots for lashing to your pack and best of all, for attaching a pouch to carry your fire starting materials! I can't wait to experiment with this sheath and being able to carry Ferro rod, lighter, tinder, etc... now, to find the right pouch! The ONLY thing I didn't really like about the sheath is the Velcro retention strap around the grip. But upon closer inspection, you can see that since the sheath is made of such thick nylon, there is really no way to replace the strap if it was a button snap. And since straps will always need to be replaced at some point, the ability to slide in another strip of Velcro is actually very thoughtful and well executed.
All in all, LEROY is an outstanding value. Get one. You won't regret it.
Leroy could literally be that best pal who saves your ass one of these days.
Again, Well done, Schrade! Keep listening to your customers... Hint: 1070!...(I keep hearing this number whenever this blade is discussed in the blogosphere, so my next quest is to try a good 1070 blade in comparison... Yes, I have one in mind so it's off to do some more shopping here on Amazon! Yay!
So, Schrade, just keep 'em coming!

product_title: PowerLine PPR200X Power Rack
review_headline: body solid sucks but this rack doesn't
review_body:
I actually got mine off craigslist for $100 bit I'll go ahead and review it here.

It was over ten years old when I bought it with very little rust and no real issues. That said I hated the color it came in and the fact that it wasn't powder coated. It can hold up to 500lbs according to body solid bit if I start moving more than that is probably be buying a rogue rack. I had a few pet peeves that are not the racks fault but more so issues that body solid did not have the foresight to address.

1) there are no real attachments for this rack like plate holders or anything

2) it is not power coated

3) some of the welds were questionable

4) I don't like the way this rack supports the uprights. It's 2x2 tubing sitting on the base parts. There's no plate or anything to keep the metal from bending or anything especially with 11 gauge

Now I do like that this rack was very height and width and appropriate. I'm 5"9 and I can sumo squat inside.the height of the rack is the whole reason I bought it.

I had to redecorate and improve the rack so I did a few things.

-I re welded some of the welds
-Got it powder coated lime green
-added plate storage to the rear by making two 2x2 L shaped post and removing the bottom cross bar
-secured it to the floor with brackets I made
-made safety straps similar to the ones rogue has

It is now a lime green power rack with plate storage in the rear like high end racks have. Bolted to the floor and the storage is currently holding 770lbs worth of plates. The improvements I made to the rack were things companies like rogue and legend offer bit apparently body solid does not, so even if you don't want or need all the things I did to this rack

It's incredible.

This Muscle Foam Roller Is Excellent As a Back Foam Roller, for Physical Therapy or As a Massage Foam Roller. 100% Satisfaction - No Risk. Full Free 60 Day Mo
review_headline: It got out so many knots!!
review_body:
This was my first time ordering this kind of back roll, which is hollow and has raised bumps on it. I had always used the plain foam rollers, and some of them would dip over time. I finally found a very dense plain foam roller which did pretty good, so I was very interested to see how this type of roller compared.

I was surprised to see it was hollow, on the image it looked like it wasn't to me. So that made me a bit nervous that it would collapse over time. But once I held it in my hand and used it I absolutely loved it! The internal lining is extremely strong, even with all my strength and body weight I couldn't make it bend in the slightest. The outer foam is very dense as well, with just enough give to make it work perfectly. The rim where the outer colored foam connects to the hard inner lining is very tight, I tried to pick at it with my fingers and it was completely stuck. So very nice high-quality design.

I have a tendency toward what I call "snap-crackle-pop knots" in my upper back and shoulders. I can physically hear them when they are moved over and they can cause a lot of pain for me. When I would use my regular foam roller I could catch two, maybe three knots really well. I was so surprised when I began rolling on this roller to hear "pop-pop-pop-pop-pop"! It was catching knots in places I didn't even realize I had! This roller got much deeper and when I went to roll again a few hours later (which normally I would still have knots) I couldn't find any! So I began feeling around my shoulders myself and found my big normal knots to be significantly smaller and less painful! And the actual rolling itself wasn't as painful as my plain super-dense roller, but I felt as though it was going deeper.

Overall very positive experience and this will definitely increase the time between massages and chiropractic adjustments for me! I love it!

product_title: Orlimar Men's Sport Fireline GI Complete Golf Set, Right Hand, Graphite/Steel, Regular Flex, Black/Red, Bag, Headcovers
review_headline: Great Set for the Occasional Novice
review_body:
I am an occasional golfer, and I am still very much a novice, so take this review with a grain of salt.

I had a 10 year old hand-me-down set and since I wanted to start playing more frequently I decided to do a bit of research for a new set. Reviews for these clubs (and similar ones) were mostly positive on other sites, and the Wilson Profile set that I wanted jumped way above budget, so I decided to gamble on these. So far they have definitely been worth it.

The clubs arrived and everything was in very good condition; all of the clubs were packaged securely and the bag looked very nice. A couple of the irons had a few imperfections present but not in any way that currently impacts performance. I have used them once since purchase and I noticed they have a better feel than my old set. The club length is just right for me (for reference I am just shy of 6'0"). The irons have a great weight to them and felt great to hit in any lie. The putter is certainly good enough; I enjoy this style of putter but I don't have much else to compare or critique about it. The driver is 460cc and much larger than my old one; I still have to get used to it but the driver was really nice to hit. My distance already improved by several yards on average. Also, the woods have a large amount of flex compared to my old set but I have not had to adjust my swing at all. My friend tried out the 3-wood in this set and fell in love with it. This set also includes a 4 and 5 Hybrid, which I have never used before buying these clubs. I am much more accustomed to using a 4 iron for long holes but I absolutely love the 4 hybrid; I got great loft and even better distance compared to my old 4 iron.

The bag is extremely light weight, but well constructed, with shoulder straps and a bag stand that I can no longer do without. Storage space is plentiful in the bag, and the bag cover barely takes up any room when folded up.

The only club that was not included in this set was a Sand wedge; I wound up buying a utility wedge but the total cost was still less than a lot of other comparable sets. Overall this set is great and I cannot wait to use them in my next round.

product_title: Ecotarget Ice Target Mold, 2 Target Sizes
review_body:
We've got a well stocked backyard airgun range with everything from paintballs on golf tees to steel swingers and poppers. These ice targets were a great addition and are a bunch of fun and a literal blast to shoot. Even a low velocity .177 airgun will shatter these with good effect. The targets are a bit big for adult airgun use (the smaller one is still over an inch) but of course you can continue to improve your skill blasting the leftover ice bases and chips. If they were really small you wouldn't get the cool poof you get with higher powered or larger bore airguns (and real guns) which shatter these into an ice dust cloud which looks pretty cool. Add a little food coloring if you like, in the end there is nothing cheaper nor easier to cleanup.

The tray isn't silicone but rather a stiff plastic. If you try to twist it to pop the targets out it they will likely crack. I just pull it out of the freezer and let it sit on the counter for a few minutes. This is enough to let the sides melt just enough so the targets fall out when its turned over.
I try to make them pretty often and have an old tupperware in the freezer to keep them in so I always have some to blast.

I'd give it 5 stars if it was a bit cheaper (it is just a plastic tray after all) or if it was made of silicone so the targets could be worked out easier. Even so I still recommend buying one.

product_title: Bushnell 8MP Trophy Cam HD LED Trail Camera with Night Vision, Black
review_headline: Not Suitable for Evening or Morning Shots
review_body: Please listen to the other reviewers about poor dusk/dawn shots.  I have had this camera for 11 months and can verify it switches over to IR too early in the evening and too late in the morning, resulting is washed out (basically completely white) images at dusk and dawn.  The same thing happens on video, although the camera corrects it over the course of the 10 second clips.  So you get about 6 seconds of properly exposed video at the end of the clip.  It is therefore unsuitable for low light shots or hunting. Bushnell customer service has not been helpful.  There is no firmware update to fix this.  Their suggestion was to move the camera to a spot with more ambient light, but I have had this in 25-30 different spots with varying degrees of light, and varying directional exposure, all with the same results.  Bushnell had no other suggestions except to send it in for testing (I pay shipping both ways) at the same time they told me there was likely nothing wrong with it (so I am likely just wasting $25 on shipping).  It's a shame because I have an older model Trophy Cam HD (without black LED) that does not have this problem at all.  The black LED has some real benefits but not at this cost.  I will either buy another older model or look for another brand.

review_body:
Resistance bands are a gentle and relatively safe method of building strength and range of motion. They are very versatile and can be used to develop a workout routine or to increase the effectiveness of an existing routine, and are helpful in rehabilitative physical therapy. They can be used indoors or out, alone or with a workout partner. I have even used them in a swimming pool. There are thousands of videos on YouTube demonstrating a wide range of possible exercises and complete routines, from beginning to advanced.

This set includes five bands in fun colors:

★ Yellow - 6-8 lbs.
★ Green - 9-11 lbs.
★ Red - 12-14 lbs.
★ Blue - 15-18 lbs.
★ Black - 22 lbs.

Since the forces are additive, they can be combined to increase resistance.

The 1 m or 39 in. long resistance bands are made of rubbery tubing with a swivel snap hook at each end.

The attachments include two 1 1/2 in. wide straps that are 17 in. long when laid flat, with a D-ring and hook & loop fastener; two very comfortable foam-covered handles attached to straps 1 in. wide, with a D-ring; and a 1 1/2 in. wide loop with a marble to use in a door. All of the stitching is reinforced.

Resistance bands are much easier to store than weights and are easily transported and a nylon storage bag with a drawstring and toggle is included.

Gonex provided resistance bands for evaluation and review.

product_title: Voodoo Tactical 42" Discrete Weapons Case
review_body: My primary reason for purchase was for discrete carry.  This case does not fulfill my expectations.  Positive is the case is manufactured with very good seam work and zippers.  Quality assembly and materials.  Unfavorable:  It is heavy and wide--too big to be "discrete".  And, even the wife and kids noticed the Voodoo skull logo on the front because it is a different material, lighter color and sufficient size to "give away" that this is not luggage or a music case...  I used a stitch remover to cut it off.  It is awkward to carry due to the strap design (lacks "reasonable" padding or "reasonable" stickiness to stay on the shoulder).  The strap connections cross-over the zipper.  So, you cannot quickly remove anything--have to undo the carrying strap to do so.  I do like the pouches because they are deep enough for magazines and some commercial-sized ammo boxes, small scope tools.  So, one advantage is you can carry sufficient stuff in one case for a range day.  The size, weight, and design are better for closet or vehicle trunk storage than for carrying to your weapon any distance.  In hindsight, I should have looked at this case before I bought it.  Because I believe there are better choices if convenience of use, discretion, and weight, I would not recommend this to a friend and I would not buy again.

product_title: Crosman PCP Challenger .177 Caliber Pre-Charged Pneumatic PCP Air Rifle with Sight
review_headline: I will list the good things about it
review_body:
I had a chance to use the Crosman PCP challanger at our local range. They had a few for rent there. I am use a Daystate PCPS ($1500 guns) so I did not expect much from this gun. I will list the good things about it.
1. Very lightweight, much lighter than my Daystate so this would be easy to carry around hunting.
2. Easy to load pellets, very easy draw on the bolt.
3. 60 shots per fill is good.
5. Low fill pressure, 2000psi vs mine which takes 3000 psi.
6. well balanced
ok now for the bads.
1. The sights are terrible. Almost useless at anything past 8 yards. It could be accurate but hard to say with the crappy sights.
2. Weak power, probably only 12 ftlb I prefer 25-30 ftlb pcps.
3. Over priced. I would rather have a .25 caliber Benjamin Maurader for $600.00. This gun would be ok at $350.00.

product_title: Covert The Outlook Panoramic Wide IR Game Camera
review_body: I have two Moultrie 150 panoramic cameras and two Covert panoramic cameras.  The Moultrie photos never blend.  If the animal is not contained in one panel of the three shots the animal will be distorted or only partially photographed.  I purchased a Covert panoramic to attempt to avoid segmented animals.  The first Covert I purchased was great.  Due to the fisheye lens, the animals were clear and the 12MP produced more detail.  The coverage of the camera was good and only distorted the animals at the very edges.  I was pleased with the Covert so I ordered a second Covert panoramic.  The second Covert panoramic has been a disappointment.  The second camera seems to only focus correctly in a narrow area directly in front of the camera and for a short distance.  Also, the battery life of the Covert cameras is poor.  Even using rechargeable batteries and the Covert solar panel, battery life is about two weeks before the batteries need to be recharged and put back in the camera.  These cameras are in a very remote mountain top area which I sometimes do not get to within two weeks.  Finally, the design of the Covert for use with the Covert solar panel is poor.  To access the inside of the camera to check the screen or batteries the solar must be unplugged from the bottom of the camera before the front can be opened.  I should be able to open up the camera without unplugging the solar.  The Moultrie cameras can be opened without disturbing the solar.

product_title: Dometic 385316140 Base to Bowl Seal Kit - EcoVac 157/158/159
review_body: We live full time in our RV and the last two times the seal went out I replaced them with the kit that has the hard plastic ring and the RUBBER seal. Both of those began leaking within about nine months. The original seal lasted about eight years. This seal is made of TEFLON, which should last much longer, and the hole is beveled to exactly fit the arc of the flush ball whereas the rubber one is a straight cut with a sharp edge with minimum contact with the ball and wears out rapidly. This seal will fit both the toilet with the overflow hole or without by flipping the thicker ring over. Tip: before removing the bowl, I poured two five gallon buckets of water down the toilet to flush the tank and sewer hose, then I filled toilet bowl with water and added about a half cup of laundry bleach to it and flushed it down and then experienced no odor at all during the procedure. Be sure to cut off the water supply because you will need to activate the flush valve in order to clean the surface of the flush ball.

Also, the instructions for changing the pipes is missing key information. There is a narrow and larger end to the pipes, which is difficult to notice, unless you knew or looked closely. The instructions don't mention that. The end you want to push on with the plastic tip on the red "key" they provide is the end that has a bit of a ridged ball on the end. Once you get it started, you'll be able to see that the end coming out first has a larger diameter. Again, look closely and push on the end that has the ridged ball. Honestly, I had an extra oem Ruger front sight that I had used bright orange nail polish, then clear, and it shows up better than these. Also, the Hi Viz are more narrow than the Ruger oem sight, that may be a + or - to you.

product_title: Trijicon Reflex M16 Handle Mount
review_headline: Best option for a M16/M4 with permenant carry-handle.
review_body: Perfect mount for an M16A1.  I purchased a Vietnam "kit" and built most of it on my own.  When I got finished - I realized how much I hated the standard "iron" sights (despite the fact that I really liked the standard look of an unmodified M16).  I purchased this to use in-conjunction with an RX01 and I'll be damned it that sight wasn't perfectly lined up with the barrel of my rifle.  It was like the two were made for each-other!  If you want to put a red dot on a M-16/M-4 config with a permanent carry handle - this is your ticket.  I understand that there are a couple of other choices (like C-More and others) that are a bit cheaper but to be honest - they are not as reliable nor as good-looking (fit and finish) as Trijicon.  My honest recommendation is this: stick with Trijicon because those sights will honestly last forever.  Electronic sights will eventually lose the fight with your rifle's recoil whereas Trijicon's sights tend to be more of a lamp (created by the sun's energy and tritium).  The RX01 was one of their best all-time sellers (and, in my opinion, their best all-around option for reflex sights) and is my personal recommendation.  Just realize that the RX06 doesn't fit this mount and I believe Trijicon makes a separate different mount for those sights.

product_title: NU Waist Belt - Weight Loss Belt As Workout Equipment Stomach Fat Burner or Belly Fat Belt Burner, Waist Slimmer , Fat Reducer & Waist Support - Fat Burning Belt and Back Support to Relieve Back Pain
review_body:
I was given the chance to purchase this item at a discount for my honest and unbiased review, so here it is. Many of the other reviewers commented on sizing issues when purchasing. I am usually a medium in woman's clothing and I purchased the large. The belt itself is just under 100cm long, so if you are measuring your waist account for about 8-10cm minimum for overlap in closure when choosing your size. One issue that I found was that while the main closure to the belt was fine, I was not able to tighten the secondary elastic supports as tight as I would like because they would overlap and they do not stick to themselves, only to the belt. I don't know if I should of had the medium or if this was just the way it was designed.

There is some crazy technology in this belt in that it does cause a heat sensation on the skin (tourmaline according to the instructions that came with it.) For me, it did take about 40 minutes for the sensation to start the first time. At first I thought this would be a great alternative to a heating pad for aches and pains. I do not have sensitive skin and consider myself to have a pretty good pain threshold, but after about half an hour of the heat I had to take the belt off. My skin was bright red and the sensation continued for quite a while. I gave it another try with similar results. I did not like the continued burning sensation. It was not something I was willing to put up with. In this case for me, the pain was not worth the possible gain.

product_title: Real Avid AVREVX4 Revelation Lighted Knife
review_headline: Real Avid Revelation x4 - Another quality product
review_body: I've had this knife for a little over a week now and I'm pretty pleased with it and excited to get to try it out this fall. First off, the main draw of this knife is obviously the 4 LEDs that it has to light the blade and game during cleaning. Anyone who hunts knows that often times we're retrieving our game with the light waning or completely gone. This knife has 2 LEDs on each side of the blade, one towards the top of the blade and the other towards the bottom. The LEDs put out a good amount of light and illuminate the blade, tip, and beyond well. It is powered by 2 CR2032 batteries. The battery cover uses a sort of tongue in groove with an O ring and attaches to the handle with two small screws that go into two threaded brass inserts in the handle. This will be good to help prevent the screws rusting in place after being exposed to moisture. The battery cover seems to do a superb job keeping the batteries nice and dry from the tests I've done. The handle is very comfortable and the rubberized grip provides an extremely secure purchase on the knife, even when wet. The blade was VERY sharp right out of the package and has a nice, thick spine with a full tang. The thumb grip on the spine is very aggressive and provides a good grip for detailed work, but not so much as to be uncomfortable. The sheath is made of ballistic nylon with a velcro closure around the knife grip and both secures and protects the knife well. The only reason that I gave this knife 4 instead of 5 stars is that I would not necessarily consider the on/off switch for the LEDs to be recessed. I can see that the switch could possibly be activated when the knife is on your belt or in your pack. I don't think it would be very likely, but possible none the less. But there would definitely be things you could do to prevent it from activating if you found it to be a problem. Overall this is a great quality knife and most definitely worth the very humble price tag. I've also attached some pictures to hopefully help show the features I've described in my review.

product_title: Ipow Anti-fog Mirrored Swim Swimming Goggles with Uv Protection Plating Glasses + Premium Goggles Case
review_body:
I swim all year long and always wear mirrored goggles because my eyes are so light sensitive. So when Ipow offered me a pair of mirrored goggles to review I jumped at the chance. Previously I have worn Speedo mirrored goggles and they are way more expensive.

The case these come in is very impressive. To open the case you need to push in a "button"; to me that's not easy to do because I don't have much strength in my hands. But the case is so nice that I do want to keep the goggles in it to keep them safe.

One thing I really like is that the headstrap is one piece and adjusts on the sides. That makes it so much easier to adjust the length than goggles that have two straps and adjust in the back. The only neg there is I need to adjust them tight and the strap gets wider as it goes back, so the wider part goes over my ears. What I've done to help that is to fold the bottom double strap up so that way it doesn't hurt my ears.

The lenses are bigger on these goggles than the Speedo's and I like that because I don't need to adjust them as much for them to be comfortable around my eyes. There are different size nose pieces, but the ones that were on are working fine. Sometimes I adjust the Speedo's every lap because the water is getting in my eyes and I haven't had to do that with these Ipow goggles. I may adjust these once or twice during my approximately 45 minute swim, but mainly they keep a good seal.

The first time I wore these I noticed the sunlight was brighter and I could see clearer. These are not mirrored on the sides like my Speedo's, but they are still very dark on the sides and haven't bothered my light-sensitive eyes. I have returned goggles that were mirrored but clear on the sides.

I am very impressed with these; I won't be spending twice as much on Speedo goggles now when I can get these.

product_title: MTech USA MT-20-30 Series Fixed Blade Neck Knife, Drop Point Blade, G10 Handle, 4-3/4-Inch Overall
review_headline: Exactly what I was looking for
review_body: Well, this little knife, and I do mean little, is exactly what I was looking for. I have been looking for an inexpensive, small, light weight, simple designed neck knife for quite a while. Was searching YouTube for reviews for a few weeks. Then I stumbled across this little gem. I use my knives every day & quite hard sometimes, so I usually do not spend a lot of money on them. I'm not cheap, but try to keep it reasonable. This little neck knife is great. I use it several times per day for opening packages, cutting nylon webbing & zip ties, sharpening a pencil & cutting cardboard boxes. It came nice & paper cutting sharp out of the box & so far in the 3 weeks I have had it, I just run it through my Smith's pocket sharpener a few times every couple days & have run it on my leather strope a few times. Stays nice & sharp. The Kydex sheath holds it securely & I hardly even notice it around my neck its so light. Please note that this is a very small knife. I noticed a few reviewers giving it a lower rating because it's so small. Well, the description is very clear, this thing is only 4.75" total length. That is the main reason I bought it. It has replaced my CRKT dogfish neck knife, which has a warrencliff style blade which I am not really a fan of after using it for several months. For a small neck knife with an actual Kydex sheath, you really can't beat it for this price. I also bought another MTech knife, a larger fixed blade, based on how much I like this one & I am pretty impressed they can provide the quality they do for the price point.

product_title: 380 AUTO Reloading Brass Casings. Cleaned and Polished. Count: 500 +3%. Headstamp: MIXED
review_body:
I just finished decapping/resizing a lot of 500 of these .380 cases and am very pleased with this brass. The 3% overage ( I didn't count them) more than made up for the 2@ .32 auto cases and 1@ .380 cases that had a bad primer or 1@ that had a dent on the mouth too bad to resize. I don't count the other 29 unusable cases against the seller as they were Fiocci and Geco cases that had too thick a rim to fit in my #26 Lyman shell holder. There were a great many of these cases in the lot but there seems to be some variation in rim thickness by these manufacturers. I presume these thicker rimmed cases fired and extracted so perhaps my Lyman shell holder is just too finicky; your mileage may vary with other shell holders.
The brass was clean and shiny, though not polished and was overall in excellent condition. I would not hesitate to buy more brass from this company.

product_title: Everlast MMA Omni Strike Stand
review_headline: Do not purchase - it is flashy but cheap
review_body:
Packaging: Weak - parts scattered in box and box was torn in multiple places - no missing parts, though.

Assembly: difficult the further you went along, due to some of the parts being warped or bent a bit.

Stand: Very good, strong and sturdy stand.

Use: Let me start by saying that I use this bag stand 7 days a week for a minimum of one hour daily, performing a solid boxing/mma workout. I have been in martial arts and boxing for almost 15 years now and I was looking for a moderate bag stand for my 100 pound bag. My back porch did not have the rafter support needed for consistent abuse.

The stand took 180 pounds of sandbags and olympic weights for stability with a 100# Everlast bag. I also have the Everlast water bladder for bag center stability, while in use.

I am 6' tall and the highest adjustment for the cable is too low for a good jab or cross, as you are almost striking the D-rings on the bag. I doubled under the chain attachment for the bag and raised it sufficiently to correct this issue.

The second issue however is that the cables have been ruined after one month of use; due to their dragging and having excessive wear in spots (as posted in other reviews) - to keep using the bag, I removed it from the cable attachment and used the pin with a bag swivel... This only fixed the issue a few days, because the pin attachment 'weld' broke off.

I now have the bag stand 'rigged' with a chain through the cable holes attached to a swivel that the bag is hanging on. I should have just gotten the cheaper, simple bag stand - the kind that 'only' holds a bag...

I am dissatisfied with this bag stand.

I would not purchase it again.

review_headline: Poor decision. This series has the potential to be ...

You have to try and watch the video to see what is happening and also do the exercise. The exercises involve getting up and down off the floor more than once during each circuit. I'm still fairly flexible but prefer to do all my standing/sitting and floor exercises at one time not switch back and forth. The routines are done in 3 circuits and the way they are presented has one side of your body doing the exercise for one circuit and the other side for 2 circuits. Not well thought out. review_body: When I started doing heavier squats on the SL 5X5 program, I began having trouble with knees buckling and pain after I left the gym.
