If you're looking for "wraps," and aren't too familiar with the difference, I'd research a bit more and base your decision on the type of program you are doing and what you hope to achieve. product_title: First Pitch The Baseline Baseball & Softball Pitching Machine Baseline Legs Up To 70 mph
review_headline: Why buy a jugs when you can buy this for half the price?
review_body:
Bought this for my 8u machine pitch team to practice with, and also grow with. It is a wonderful machine for the price and I highly recommend this over a jugs machine that runs for $1200 plus.
Pros: -- throws consistent when you drop the ball consistent the same way. two seam fastballs work the best on my machine.
-- light enough to carry anywhere and breaks down nicely
-- set up is quick and easy
-- can be used for hitting, ground balls, pop flys and line drives at practice with consistency - get more reps in the same amount of time
-- the adjustable features are really nice for using it for more than hitting practice.

Cons: -- its not a jugs, but its close.
-- there needs to be a hole drilled into the pole that the machine mounts to. I find the machine would walk to the left after every pitch because of the torque of the ball, without clamping the screw down as tight as possible it got worse. hurts your hand when you have to do that every 10 pitches. I took my drill and made my own hole and voila! no more walking. I like that I can loosen it back up for other applications, but do yourself a favor and get your drill out.

Time will tell if this machine stands up, but for now I couldn't be happier with it. for a team of 12 it costs under 60 bucks to have a hitting machine; how much would those parents spend on cage time at a facility? Makes sense to have it.

Recommendation: use the Honda eu2000 generator with this machine, don't have to worry about a power course and its rather quiet.

product_title: Universal Selectorized 445 Dumbbells and Stand
review_headline: These Allow Me To Workout At Home!
review_body: I have been doing strength training for three years now. I started out with bodyweight workouts and moved to using dumbbells. I had a set-up at home of 3 lb. through 20 lb. dumbbells as well as a 35 & 45 pound sets. I had progressed in my workouts to the point that for many of my lifts the 20 pound set was too light, but there was no way I could jump to using 35 pound dumbbells. For a few months I had to join the local recreation commission gym. Then my husband surprised me with the Universal Power-Pak 445 Adjustable Dumbbells for Christmas 2014. I have been using them 2 to 3 times per week since then (six months). I purposely waited to write this review until I had the chance to use these weights for several months.  I am very happy with this product. I did a lot of research regarding adjustable dumbbells and for the price this set seemed to be the best buy and I have certainly not been disappointed. While the stand is included when you order this set, I have not used it. The dumbbells sit on the floor in my little workout room and it is no problem for me to squat down and pick them up when I need them. When changing the weight  it is done easily by turning a dial. I have never had an issue when changing the weight amount. The handle has a comfortable grip, probably more comfortable than the dumbbells I've used at the local gym I belonged to at one time.The only negative with these weights, as far as I'm concerned, is that they are a bit bulky, but that is an issue with any set of adjustable dumbbells. Occasionally, when I go to put them back in their base the plates are leaning too far one way and they won't slide in place easily, but that is a very minor inconvenience. I simply use my opposite hand to nudge the plates where they need to be and then set it in the base.  I love having the Universal Power-Pak 445 Adjustable Dumbbells in my little home gym so that I can workout at my convenience.

product_title: Sunny Health & Fitness SF-E3416 Magnetic Elliptical Trainer, Gray
review_body:
Mine arrived with some faulty parts. The mainframe had been drilled incorrectly and an essential bolt would not fit into the bearing. After 3 days of aggravation (trying everything possible to make the bolt screw in), I contacted the manufacturer directly to address the problem. It took 2 days to get a response and the representative was very helpful-she said they could send out replacement parts and sent a pdf with instructions on how to disassemble and reassemble the mainframe (which appeared pretty complicated). I responded with an inquiry as to how long it would take to receive the replacement parts and 5 days later (yes, 5!!), I received a return email from a different representative explaining that they were sorry for my trouble, but they did not have those parts in stock so I would need to return this item to Amazon. That was pretty disappointing since I had already been given the info on how I was going to fix this thing. Anyway, I proceeded with an Amazon return and replace-getting this thing back into its original box was a beast!! I got the replacement a few days later and it went together easily.
I have been using it daily and am pretty pleased with the quality of this elliptical. Of course it's not gym quality, but for the price, it's hard to complain!
I will tell you that the digital fitness monitor does not work correctly. The speed, mileage, and caloric burn are way off (and yes, I tried both before I returned the one that I originally purchased). The heart rate monitoring function does not work either. It normally displays my heart rate around 80-90 beats per minute when in actuality, it is 160-180 beats per minute during my workout, so there is a huge discrepancy Not a big deal for me as I'm capable to taking my own HR and I'm comfortable enough with fitness equipment to know approximately what the caloric burn and distance are based on time and intensity of workout.
The tension is not something to base your purchase on either. There is only a minuscule difference between level 1 and level 8-so small that my husband didn't think that the tension was even working but I can feel a slight difference. There are ways to increase the tension by adding your own bungee cords but if that's not something you want to do and are looking for a difficult workout-look elsewhere.
This machine is fairly stable, but there is some wobble when going at higher speeds/intensity. I have mine on carpet, so this could be slightly different if you are placing it on a hard floor offering more stability.
Overall Impression: Good buy for the money and I love being able to work out in the comfort of my own home while watching TV or listening to some tunes. I'm 5'5" and my hubby is 6'3" and we both fit comfortably on the machine. Keep in mind that there is no height adjustment feature, but it still works well for a variety of heights. The tension leaves more than a little to be desired and the digital monitor does not work at all except to keep an accurate time of your workout. It is very easy to assemble, but if yours arrives with faulty parts, just plan on returning to Amazon as Sunny's customer service is less than awesome. With all of this in mind, I would still recommend purchasing this item. Price+easy assembly+being able to work out in the comfort of your own home without taking up much space=a steal of a deal!ither. product_title: E-Force Heatseeker 3.0 160 Racquetball Racquet
review_body:
this plays like a 170g, but the power is unreal. the accuracy is great. i think i'm more of a 160g player, so i'm on the look out for something else, but i can't knock stars for this.

--- updated 7/27/15

I've owned and used:

E-Force Lethal NXT Gen 160g - duration: 1-2 year(s)
E-Force Heatseeker 3.0 160g - duration: 6 months
E-Force Missle 230g - duration: 3 years
E-Force Gladiator 205g? - duration: 5+ years

I've demo'ed for a week:
Ektelon EXO3 Toron Lite 160g
Head Graphene Radical 160g
E-Force Apocalyse 160g
Head GrapheneXT 165g

In depth review:
E-Force Lethal NXT Gen 160g - duration: 1-2 year(s) - this is my favorite racquet. it fits my playing abilities very well. it's accurate and has good power. Not as good as the HeatSeeker 3.0 though.
E-Force Heatseeker 3.0 160g - duration: 6 months - the power! this thing makes this sonic boom like sound with new fresh racquetballs on power hits. I'm not sure if it's because this racquet plays like a 170g or if it has a higher strung swingweight than the Lethal NXT Gen, but the biggest flaw for me is the slow split second reaction it gives me at the front court. For me that's a game changer, and puts the Lethal NXT Gen as my favorite racquet so far.
E-Force Missle 230g - duration: 3 years - decent racquet to continue playing and learning. Better than the gladiator despite the weight, i think it just had newer technology in it.
E-Force Gladiator 205g? - duration: 6+ years - i think this thing was $40-60 when i bought it. I went from some $20-30 racquet, and it was night and day! This thing had power and accuracy! It was worth every penny!
Ektelon EXO3 Toron Lite 160g - duration: 7 days - my next replacement for the E-Force Lethal NXT Gen?!?! I was surprised by this racquet. I really thought the next racquet, Head Graphene Radical, was going to be the supreme replacement. I had 3 other friends try this Ektelon racquet and they all couldn't put their finger on it, but they all had better games with this racquet. I'm going to consider this the magical hit factor on this racquet. Personally the stock handle seemed a bit too thick from the rubber grip. But I had a very good game with it too. If I buy this racquet, I may switch out the grip right away.
Head Graphene Radical 160g - duration: 7 days - good racquet, but i would say the accuracy for just not as good as the EXO3. decent power.
E-Force Apocalyse 160g - duration: 7 days - power! sonic boom like sounds from this and a new fresh racquetball!!! just like the Heatseeker 3.0. the accuracy isn't as good as the EXO3. I would say the front court control was thing was improved from the Heatseeker 3.0 though. I was able to get that split second reaction speed in the front court. If this had the accuracy of the Head Graphene Radical, then I'd get this one instead.
Head GrapheneXT 165g - duration: 7 days - Nothing special here. It was a good racquet with power, movement speed and accuracy, but there just didn't seem to be a magical hit from this.

About me: When I read this chart I would consider myself a Level C player (http://www.whitefishwave.com/site_media/media/uploads/racquetballskilllevels.pdf) but to be embarrassingly honest, when I get in the court with seasoned players, I fell like a novice! I "thought" I knew how to play position and how to read the ball. Are these players Level B? I think they consider themselves Level C or D... I guess it's all a matter of perspective.
I play racquetball casually with friends and been doing so with different people since a young age. My years of experience would then be at 20 years, but I don't think I play well enough to really advertise that. I've had no professional training, but I just love playing the game. It's a great work out that's fun (i hate treadmill running! that's so boring!)
I enjoy the fast pace front court action, but a strategic back court high corner can be very helpful.

product_title: Markwort Kenko Soft Tennis Starter Kit
review_body:
My husband and I purchased one of these kits about a year ago and are very pleased with it. Soft tennis originated in Japan (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soft_tennis), and we became interested in it when hosting Japanese exchange students.

The ball has a teeny tiny hole and you use the pump to inflate it. It stays inflated very well. The racket is light, well-balanced, and easy to grip.

Having a softer ball makes the game easier to play for someone who is trying to get into better shape like me. When I played with a normal tennis ball, sometimes the impact of the ball on the racket would hurt my arm, but the soft tennis ball doesn't hurt. The ball doesn't bounce quite as vigorously as a hard tennis ball, but you can still get some nice height and distance. This benefits beginners, since the soft tennis ball is a lot more difficult to accidentally knock out of the court.

The other fun part of owning this set is that it confuses other people and is an interesting conversation piece. A time or two ago when we were playing, a guy next to us said, "We have some *real* balls if you want." I said, "No thanks, these are real--they're soft tennis balls."

I'm going to buy another one. Who's with me?

product_title: CAP Barbell Black A Frame Dumbbell Rack
review_headline: Smell isn't great, but the REAL issue is the QUALITY CONTROL
review_body: I agree the item had a smell, but that went away within a couple of days. My HUGE issue was the quality control on this item. It arrived with lock nuts that were too small. As a result, I could put the rack together but there were huge gaps where the screws would not tighten to flush. After a trip to Home Depot, I discovered the nuts sent in the package were lock nuts and were preventing the screws from fully tightening. Also the screws are metric so I had to buy "special sized" nuts to make this thing stable.  A trip to Home Depot and $5 later, I had a secure rack that was safe to hold weights. I noticed from other reviews and my question that some buyers had this issue and others didn't. Sounds like Cap Barbell needs to revisit their quality control as I'm not expecting a refund for the extra $5 I had to shell out to make this product safe.

Make yourself be seen from oncoming motorists and stay safe!

product_title: FitDesk 2.0 Desk Exercise Bike with Massage Bar
review_headline: I can now watch TV and browse the computer without feeling like a couch potato.
review_body: I've only used this twice, but I wanted to write a review now since their marketing materials say they donate a FitDesk for every 10 reviews.  -Installation was fairly easy, and I did it myself. -The machine runs very quietly and smoothly. -Tension can be adjusted so that I can get a decent workout while watching TV (which is why I bought it). There are 8 levels of tension, and so far I've done an hour at a time on level 7. Those of high athletic prowess may want more tension. -Resistance bands are a nice touch, though the instructions say not to pedal and use the resistance bands at the same time. I'm a rule-breaker, so I've used the bands while pedaling easily. Hopefully, I won't lose an arm or leg performing these actions at the same time.  The only CON I have is regarding the "Performance Monitor". It measures time of workout, speed, distance, and calories burned. For each workout, these have to be separately reset. It takes too many button presses to do this. It's a first world problem, I know, but aggravating nonetheless.  I thought about giving this machine 5 stars, but nothing is perfect--though I'd say this thing is a pretty great device.

product_title: Millett 6-25 X 56 LRS-1 Illuminated Side Focus Tactical Riflescope (35mm Tube .25 MOA with Rings), Matte
review_headline: The clarity is much better than I expected
review_body: I purchased this scope about 6 months ago. It was originally supposed to go on a hunting rifle. When I saw how big it actually was I decided to save it for another rifle and another time. Well, I just took delivery of a new rifle and put the Millett on it so I could go shoot it right away. While zeroing the rifle I took notice of how precise and positive the clicks were. Walking my shots in to zero took only three rounds once on paper at 100yds.  Once zeroed I took it from 100 to 200, to 300yds. and back again. The gun and scope came right back to zero. Exactly same number of clicks. The clarity is much better than I expected. In my opinion you'd have to have a pretty sharp eye to see any appreciable difference between this scope and either of my Night Force. Longevity has yet to be determined. Be advised, however, this IS a  big scope. Perhaps, like many of you researching this scope, I thought "yeah, it doesn't seem THAT big". Trust me it is.  If the gun it's going on is meant to be carried or packed for any distance I'd save the weight and bulk and look for something else. If you've only got a short distance to your stand or it's going on a target gun then go for it. As others have said the rings are too high. You will likely need the low. BTW: I mounted this,for the short term, on a Tikka CTR stainless with the low rings. The objective sits about 1/4 off the barrel. The only reasons for rating only four stars is the ridiculously high rings and the fact that I can't speak to it's longevity. Good luck. Shoot safe.

product_title: Meprolight Ruger Tru-Dot Night Sight, fits P90, 91, 93 & 95 fixed set
review_body:
Nice sights. Not only from the brightness standpoint, but also provides a slightly larger sight picture than the "stock" P90.
Had to lightly file the rear sight to get a good fit in the slide dovetail. Be careful of the firing pin block spring "plunger" when removing the old rear sight and installing the new one... it can get caught up into the allen screw hole in the sight.
For drilling the new front sight, I made a drill guide from a 16 gauge hypodermic needle. Cut the point and syringe base off, smooth the ends, spin it in a drill press and file or sand one end down to .062" (the needle measures .065"). A # 57 drill bit fits perfectly inside the needle and you can pilot drill the new front sight in place without messing up the slide's roll pin holes (someone else mentioned drilling from both sides... a good idea). Then finish the sight on a drill press with a 1/16" bit. Take your time and I think you'll be really happy with the finished product.

review_body:
I took some time to write this review because I wanted to make sure it actually helped. I had a problem with my left knee. It gradually got worse each week so I tried Tommy Copper which helped a little bit. The problem I had with TC is it fit really tight and I could only wear it for just a couple of hours before I had to take it off. Once I did, my pain in my knee returned within 10 minutes.

I bought the Kunto Knee Brace for 2 reasons; 1 - it looked great; 2 - I read the other reviews and thought why not try it.

I've had this for 1 week and I no longer have the pain in my knee. I've worn it 24/7 and only take it off when I shower in the morning. I don't really know why this has worked for me but I'm one happy customer. I highly recommend anyone who has trouble with joint pain to try it. Hopefully you will be amazed as well.

I'm going golfing tomorrow ..... which I haven't been able to do for a month. If it improves my golf game .... that would be nice too.

review_body: This product did not work for me.. I cannot say I hate it, but I do not like it.. It seemed like a neat design, but in the real world, it did not work.. And, that is were the process stopped.. Actually that is not where the process stopped.. So, I contacted AMAZON, and true to their customer service motto or whatever, they stepped in and made things right for me.. It is a long story, and that can be shared somewhere else, but the short of it is, Amazon came through for me and we are still the best of buddies!!!! So, even if this did not work out on the product, I am still buying Amazon.. And, if I learned anything from all this, let me tell you what you should take away from this...... if it does not say sold by and shipped by AMAZON, leave it alone.. product_title: Smith & Wesson 327 TRR8 CO2 BB Revolver, Black
review_headline: My all time favorite BB gun.
review_body: I love this bb gun. It looks extremely realistic. I know some bb guns look real but this will undoubtedly be seen as a real hand gun at first glance. The adjustable rear sights make for very accurate target acquisition. Every detail of this gun is amazing, from the glossy Smith & Wesson logos on the handle, to the shells. The accessory rail i felt was extremely ugly. luckily, it can be removed by using a pin or toothpick to poke out a small pin in front of the rear sights, after this is removed, unscrew the screw on top of the rear sights, DO THIS IN THIS ORDER! otherwise the rear sights with break. after you remove the rear sights, use a bit of force to remove the accessory rail. I putting this in here because I did not remove the pin before removing the screw, and busted the sights. The shells are made of what i assume is brass or aluminium. They feel very real. The top part of the shell is were you place the .177 or 4,5mm cal bb's. It is made of a very high quality rubber substance and can be reused hundreds of times over. The detail on the back of the shells is amazing. it has an inlaid print that says,"S&W cal.4,5(.177)" which makes it look crazy realistic. Side note, if you happen to own a Dan Wesson BB gun revolver, the shells from that gun work the same on this gun. This gun is pretty heavy for a bb gun. It weight the same as my real Smith & Wesson .357 magnum revolver. The handles can be problematic if you have smaller hands. The trigger has grooves that go down it which makes it a bit uncomfortable after shooting it awhile. The hammer protrudes out well enough for you to cock it single action with ease. The CO2 is placed in the handle (as it is for most bb guns). It takes 12 gram CO2 cartridges. I don't like the handle slide because it easily comes off when you pull it back to put the CO2 in it. The screw used to put the CO2 into the slot is really good. When you are loading the CO2 there is literally no leakage when the top is punctured. The screwhas a fold-able handle which flops around the inside of the handle when it is closed. I found this to be mildly irritating, but i quickly forgot about it. The speed re-loader is a piece of s***. You first have to load the bullets into the re-loader, then push it into the cylinder. There are a few problems with this. 1.) the re-loader cannot work because it is to large to be close enough to the gun to load it. the cylinder release/ safety slide gets in the way. 2.) The shells rattle around and if the reload er even slightly tips, all of the shells quickly fall out. 3.) it would be 100 times easier just to load the bullets into the cylinder, just cut out the middle man. The slide release works very well. You pull it towards you to turn on the safety, push it forward to unlock the cylinder. The cylinder has microscopic horizontal groves which i though was a nice touch. The cylinder has some problems. 1.) there is a small lip of metal to keep the cylinder from coming off, however this will catch a shell and keep it in the cylinder when you are trying to unload it. This can be fixed by giving it more force when tipping the gun. 2.) the shells can also be caught when putting the cylinder back into it's place. These are very minor problems and will not effect your over all experience with this gun. This gun is crazy awesome. I would not recommend this to anyone who is looking for a first time BB gun as it can require some maintenance. If you are looking for a gun to look amazing, with an over high quality, and is basically a steal for the price, look no further.

product_title: Polar M400 GPS Smart Sports Watch
review_headline: ... have had this watch about a week and absolutely love it despite some shortcomings
review_body: I have had this watch about a week and absolutely love it despite some shortcomings. Tried a FitBit Surge first and sent it back. Battery life too short and NON-REPLACEABLE - dealbreaker. Im not paying $250 for a watch that will have a useful life of 2-3 years. This is a sophisticated multisport GPS HRM watch, with activity tracking functions. Unbelievably capable for the money. Comes with a chest strap HRM which may sound like a pain, but wrist strap HRM is not accurate enough. Shortcomings - Syncing to the Polar Website is sometimes difficult. Talked a to Polar rep today. He told me it was down to server 'overload', which means try syncing at off peak times. Bottom line, if your having problems syncing its probably nothing to do with you watch or computer.  Ive tried syncing early AM - MUCH faster & more reliable. Polar need to be up front with this kind of info.  Syncing is a big deal.   Some people are reporting that the miniusb port has been rusting out after 3-4 months. The same people often state that they have not swam or been in the shower with it on. Seems that sweat builds up around the rubber cap cover and just a little bit gets in. Heres the kicker. When the same people send the watch back in under warranty, in some cases Polar told them that they must have left the cover off & presumably did not want to honor the warranty. ??? Your very unlikely to be able to wear the watch with the cover unseated, it would stick in your arm. Anyway, despite these 2 issues, the watch is so good, Im sticking with it. Unbeatable for the money.

review_body:
There is already a very helpful review on this bag by "thatguywithpoles" so I'm not going to go into unnecessary info on this since he already covers a lot about the bag. My review will be more of spotting the 'differences' between this and the Maxpedition.

First I'd like to say that I'm OK with knock-off or imitation products as long as the products work and are of a good price point. I don't know anything about Yukon Outfitters to really claim that their products are "all" knock-offs, but in comparing this bag and the original Maxpedition Kodiak Gearslinger, you can see the differences if you own both. If you've never owned a Maxpedition bag then you will be none the wiser.

Comparisons:
Fabric - One of the first things I noticed between the two is the materials used to construct the bag. Maxpedition uses a 1000 denier watter/abrasion/ballistic nylon. The Yukon uses a 600denier polyester, though it's not bad, but I would not rely on it for field or heavy wear use. Also, the Yukon doesn't use 550 cord (paracord) and is missing a security feature that binds some of the zippers together.
Plastics - The plastics (buckles, d-rings, fasteners, etc...) all feel and appear to be very flimsy, but again, probably better than a standard backpack (benefit of the doubt).
Zippers - Appear to be similar and I can't complain since they function as they should and have not split on me (yet). Although, the pouch closest to your back is only a single direction zipper, whereas the Maxpedition has the option to zip in either direction with 2 pulls.
Hydration - Yukon (see questions in the Q&A section of this product) claim that this pack was not "designed" for a hydration pack. But the contrary is that it actually fits a 1 liter hydration pack with a hole at the top to feed the drink tube through.
Stitching - I'm noticing a lot of single stitching throughout the Yukon bag. I've literally hooked my Maxpedition to a pull-up bar while strapped in and wearing the backpack. Without a doubt, I can trust the Maxpedition to be able to carry my weight (160lbs) and not have it rip or tear at the seams. I'm not going to put the Yukon through the same test for reasons mentioned in construction of this bag.
Molle - The Yukon offers a lot more molle straps on both sides of the bag and even divides the molle in half on the shoulder strap. I'm not so sure at how much more use or function having more molle on the sides will provide me. The one thing I do like about it is that the side drink holder is removable, whereas the Maxpedition is affixed.
Size - Some reviews compared this to the Maxpedition "Sitka" but it is more in line of comparison with the Maxpedition "Kodiak" Gearslinger. The Sitka is smaller. This Yukon MG-5032 is comparable in size to the Maxpedition Kodiak.

In summary:
...is this bag a good imitation? -Yes
...is this bag worth the price? -Yes
...is this bag useful for an every day carry? -Yes
...is the bag strong enough for field or heavy use? -No (probably not)
...would I buy this over the Maxpedition? -No (if you can pay a little extra, for the quality, then get the Maxpedition)

He says that these are VERY comfortable, and fit just right. Even with the hard knuckles, he claims that they give him free range of motion of his hands, and he can hardly tell that the hard plastic is there. They don't hinder him at all.

The finger-less feature is great as with any finger-less glove. It gives you free range of your fingertips for texting, or feeling out parts that you need to while wearing them. If you are needing to keep your fingertips warm in the winter, these are thin enough that you can wear them under regular work gloves as well, while still protecting your hands under them.

Overall these gloves are fantastic and I highly recommend them. I received these for free for the purpose of an honest review. My opinion is my own, or that of my husband, and is not influenced in any way.

review_body:
EDIT:

I have used this extensively in the hot summer in my garden and on a few hikes. It is wonderful but very pink. It's been wet, dried, stressed, and holds up well though there is some minor tearing where it was really pulled hard. It makes a wonderful shawl and helps keep the mosquitoes from getting through my clothes!

ORIGINAL:

This has just now arrived and not been tested in the field.

After reading a lot of reviews I was afraid I'd get something flimsy, dirty, or smaller than described. I was wrong.

This came precisely as described. Not including the tassles, it measures 42x42 (actually a hair short of 42 on one side and a hair long on the other, less than 1/4" difference each way.)

The weave is better/tighter than I expected. The holes in the weave are too small to measure - much less than 1mm each.

The color (pink) is really pink.

It feels strong. Pulling one edge from the other, I feel like I could rip it if I wanted to, but it would take effort. I'm sure I could hold one end down with a foot and rip the other with my hand. But for a lightweight item, it feels sturdy. I won't feel like I have to be dainty with it.

The finish is a textured matte black which is a little different than most other small black gun parts out there but it's fine and seems very durable. In fact it's nicer than the BO finish which tends to show surface rust if not ceracoated.
I'll continue to add these to my builds.

product_title: 1911 Mat Tact Ext Thumb Safety
review_body:
Replaced a low mount safety with this tactical thumb safety from Wilson Combat. The size is perfect for carry and the lever is super easy to access. One caution-- it will take a while to fit this part. If you're not comfortable filing on parts to fit to your 1911, get a gunsmith to install. The pin was a tight fit in the frame and very tight through the grip safety. Sandpaper on the pin reduced the diameter just enough to fit. A small file on the sear engagement lug (careful) took care of that fit. The detent in the thumb safety as provided fit the plunger pin nicely.
Wilson Combat parts are built oversized to allow for the fitting process. With a little patience, you can get a very nice, tight fit on a quality part.

product_title: Red Rock Outdoor Gear Assault Pack
review_headline: It's okay for the price, but there is better out there
review_body:
Honestly, it's not a bad pack for the price. You can't expect a bag at this price point to be a miracle. But there are better packs of this type.
Pros: lots of MOLLE webbing, which is good if you want to expand, as I do. The price: it's cheaper than most packs of this design out there (Condor Compact Assault, Explorer). Waist and sternum straps are solid, with plenty of adjustability.
Cons: The stitching on the insides of the pockets sucks. As I'm filling the bag, one of the interior pockets just falls apart with only minor pressure on the stitch. The shoulder straps are very narrow, they have padding, but it still hurts the shoulders after not much time. They aren't very adjustable: you'll get maybe 3 inches of strap length in either direction with the adjuster, also, there's no quick drop clips on the ends, it's just a regular strap adjuster. Honestly, that is minor, but other packs have it with this same design, so it seems like it should be there. It seems like just a design flaw.

If you have read this entire review, here's my recommendation: get a different pack. I have the Condor Compact Assault and I like it a whole lot more. Higher quality, not a great deal more expensive, and every extra cent is worth it. Condor in general is a good brand. As for Red Rock, if this pack is any indication, it's okay, but could be a lot better. Hope they make improvements in the future.

product_title: Everlast ProTex2 EverGel Training Gloves
review_headline: Oh Everlast, you could have gone so far with this glove...
review_body:
The glove itself is awesome in terms of padding. I've owned other Everlast and RDX among other brands, and have never liked both the fit of the glove and the feel on impact of a bag as much as I have with these.

The fatal flaw was that both velcro/elastic straps ripped loose from the stitching within four sessions. Everlast offered to replace them, but it was not a defect in the gloves, it is just poor design, so it would happen again on a replacement pair. Any stress on the straps loosens the stitching. I have noticed they've gone back to the full wraparound style strap in their new Ergonomic glove.

My speculation is if you have larger hands and don't need to put much pull on the elastic straps you may be fine. But if you need to tighten the elastic, which is what elastic designed for, expect the straps to give out as other reviewers have also indicated. I thought about having a tailor do some fixing, but then I would be into the gloves for the same price as a much higher end brand so I passed on that idea.

review_body:
When I was in school I studied Latin, French, and Spanish. I wish now that I'd skipped all of them and learned Chinese so that I could read directions. However, even without much by way of instructions in English this is still a good product.

My sister bikes almost every day and always carries her phone with her in case of emergencies. She loved the idea of being able to attach her phone to the bike handle so that she can see who's calling, but wasn't sure that she trusted a piece of plastic not to drop her expensive phone onto the concrete (or asphalt.) She's been using this for a week and has had no problems and feels very comfortable trusting her phone to it.

It's sturdy and ingeniously designed. There are two buttons (red) on the back that you push sideways to make the "arms" slide out. After that, you just put your phone in, make sure that it's resting against the lower rim that keeps it from sliding out, and push the arms in until they grasp your phone firmly. She uses an iPhone5s and it fits very well indeed.

The holder attaches to the adjustable ring with a screw, so there's no chance that the holder will become disengaged as you ride. And the adjustable ring fits snugly onto the handlebars and won't come off until you take it off.

I was given a free sample of this product in exchange for an honest review. It's too early to tell how long it will hold up, but it certainly looks and feels like it would give years of service. The yellow and black combination is very attractive. So far, we've found nothing to dislike about it. It's not cheap, but seems like a fair price for the quality and workmanship.

product_title: Cold Steel MAA European Spear - 95MEP
review_body:
Here is the lowdown:

This is made in India.
The head consists of 2 stamped sheet metal "clam-shells" that are welded together on the edges. They did a good job of grinding the welds smooth. There is (what appears to be lead) metal poured in about the front half of the head. Because the stamped and welded hollow spear head is so light, this lead weight is probably needed for balance. This adds significant weight and causes it to appear more robust then it really is. It looks like the final finish is probably polished hot bluing--but I am not sure. The edge on mine was not sharp at all. While cleaning the cosmoline off, I did not have to even pay any attention to it. I would have to hit myself with it with great force to cause a cut.

This head would have to be sharpened if somebody were to use it for hunting. I hope the sharpening does not destroy the welds.

The shaft appears to be adequate. It has a curve, but I do not think this will be an issue for my purposes.

The directions indicate the shaft needs to be attached to the head with the 2 included screws. I could not find any screws, and many other reviewers have indicated the same problem. The instructions do not provide any size for the screws--so I was in a bit of a quandary.

Finally, I found the 2 screws. They were screwed into some of the inner packaging--interesting. So, search closely if you purchase this item. The 2 screws appear to be #6 sheetrock screws. I will replace these with pan head screws for a better fit. I will probably also glue the shaft into the head. If I break the shaft, I probably will not bother replacing it--I will just throw the whole thing away.

Like most cheap products from third world countries, do not expect this to be finely made.

review_headline: Add these to your arsenal of pain fighters!
review_body: As a runner who has been plagued by Achilles tendinitis for about a year, I bought these to wear at night while I am sleeping. To illustrate how well they work, let me tell you about the last 24 hours.  On Saturday morning I ran 6 miles. Saturday night I went to sleep with a sleeve on my right foot. On Sunday morning I woke up and began walking around my house only to find that the tendons in my left ankle were snapping while the ones in my right (with the compression sleeve still on) were fine. I quickly transferred the sleeve to my left ankle, resumed walking only to find that no tendons were snapping.  Due to the tendinitis, it feels like snakes are swimming around my ankle. product_title: Manduka eko Lite Yoga and Pilates Mat
review_headline: Arrived damaged; not caused by shipping
review_body: I ordered the Manduka eKO in Thunder, 79". The package arrived quickly and in decent shape. When I opened the box, the mat itself had a significant depression that does not appear to have been caused by packing or shipping. Just above the plastic label that holds the mat in rolled position, there is a spot about 2 inches long by half an inch high where some kind of damage happened. I can feel it when I step on my mat and it's a bummer for the price. I unrolled the mat and left it in a room with a fan and open window for a week to air out the rubber smell- it helped a little bit but not much. Thought about returning this item but it would have been too much money and hassle. I made a water/apple cider vinegar cleaning solution and wiped the mat down several times to try and "break it in" so it's not as slippery. I've gone to 4 classes, including warm vinyasa and hot yoga, and the mat is starting to wear but I still slip in down dog. Also, my whole body smells like rubber after I practice on this mat. I like having the extra length on the mat, I'm 5'9" and I tend to travel a lot. I also like the color, dark grey- it doesn't really have a green or blue tint as shown in some of the photos online. But beware- this color mat shows marks easily, specifically sliding feet in and out of poses leaves trails on the mat. I chose the eKO over the PRO because I do a lot of hot yoga and work up quite a sweat, this mat was supposed to be the best for wet conditions. I wish I had gone with the PRO Black instead of this eKO. Disappointing, but I'll use it until it's broken in and then just keep it as a spare or for home use. Considering the condition of the mat and the return policy, I would not buy from this retailer again. Side note- if you do buy an eKO, do not buy the Manduka Mat Renew spray. You'll want the Refresh spray as it's made for the natural rubber.

product_title: Zepp Tennis Swing Analyzer
review_headline: Tells you what you should already know - but possibly useful for long term trend tracking
review_body:
When I first got the device I likely would have given it a 4 star review. After owning it for a season, rating it as 3 stars.

First, the device does what it claims. My only real complaint on the hw/sw is that battery life is pretty short (really can only go one hitting session before needing a recharge). Should note that I'm a 4.5 player.

The real issue with the device is that it simply confirms what you mostly already know. 60% forehands, 40% backhands? Yup - kind of already knew that was my ratio. 80% forehand topspin? Yup, already knew that. etc. Now this device will fine tune your awareness (i.e. you will know you were at 62.3% forehands rather than a little more than half). But I have not found this knowledge that game changing for me.

Where I think the device can be helpful is in tracking long term goals/trends. Say I want to slowly change my game to be more offensive. I can track over years the percentage of forehands I am taking (assuming forehand is my offensive weapon). But this long term tracking would be far more effective with additional data (such as shot speed, etc). I know there is a new update which attempts to calculate actual velocity rather than the relative hit speed. I have not tried that yet.

But my summary is this device kind of just tells you what you know already for any short term feedback.

review_headline: I am pleased with the Umarex Octane rifle (and scope)
review_body:
I am pleased with the Umarex Octane rifle (and scope). There are some things that may seem like I am complaining about the rifle, but I don't intend for that to be the case. 1st, it is (like many of the reveiwers stated) heavy. If I was going to be walking the better part of a day hunting with it, I would definately get a shoulder sling. But since it is for use in my neighborhood, I have no problem with the weight; as a matter of fact, I appreciate it. 2nd, it is substantially more difficult to cock than I was expecting. This might get better with time and rounds put through it but, you won't have to worry about younger children using it. Again, this is not an issue for me. 3rd and lastly, even with the quiting chambers, it is substantially louder than I had expected. Granted, I don't have a baseline upon which to compare since this is my first air rifle, but it is not something that your neighbors won't hear.

Those things being said, I am enjoying it, I recommend it, and am very glad that I purchased it. I just wanted to let people know what they are getting.

Total cost about 80 bucks. Hangs at a perfect angle and all my shots were deflected down into the dirt but with enough spatter to the sides to ding the support legs on the sawhorse. Below the target and forward of it couldn't find any large fragments of jacket and only tiny bits of the lead core. The target sustained no damage at all in the way of dents, cracks, or chips. I was ~60 yards away, a bit closer than I would have liked but the way the target is hung on bolts made it very unlikely that any fragments would return. I expected some damage to the plate at that distance but apparently the angle means less energy is transferred to the plate on impact. Flourescent orange marker paint works great to touch it up. AR500 is tough stuff, a target that won't get used up at least in the calibers I'm using.  Outstanding!

product_title: Splatterburst Targets - 12 x18 inch - Silhouette Reactive Shooting Target - Shots Burst Bright Fluorescent Yellow Upon Impact - Gun - Rifle - Pistol - AirSoft - BB Gun - Air Rifle
review_headline: Great targets, but there are better ones for pistol practice!
review_body: These are great targets, but there are better ones out there for pistol practice.  First, let me say that these are good.  You can see your shots well from quite far away, even without binoculars.  And the targets are nice and large.  But, only the main body target is practical for most pistol shooting.  From any further than 7 yards away, the little targets next to the head (and even the head target) are too difficult to hit, particularly with a compact or subcompact pistol.  So, for most intents and purposes, you have only the main body target (which is great).  Second, these do not come with pasties for covering up holes.  Other targets on the market come with pasties attached, which allow for more shooting on fresh targets without using up so many targets.  Third, there are self-adhering targets on the market, so you don't need to use a staple-gun or masking tape.  And these adhere well, even in the cold, and resist wind better than staple gunned or taped targets.  Lastly, other (smaller) targets are often better because you can fit more than one of them on a target stand or box (see 8" or 12" targets).  If you do buy these, do yourself a favor and order some pasties, you will need them.

product_title: Ford F150 FX2 Sport Decals Truck Stickers (1997 - 2008) - F
review_headline: Great look!  Accurate sizing and styling...quality: pretty good.
review_body:
I don't regret buying these, but not exactly what I had hoped. The size was perfect, the method of adhesion went flawless and I haven't had any failures with the stickers yet (used them for several months now). There's a couple of things that I'm nervous about that haven't happened yet, but may in the future. At the upper right corner of the "X", the sticker comes to a very acute point. This sharp point (as is with all stickers) may be somewhat venerable to getting caught and peeled back. Again, this hasn't happened yet, but after the truck is washed and dried, I find small fibers from the drying towel underneath those sharp corners (also within the "sport" lettering). If those sharp corners were ever so slightly rounded, it would reduce the chance of peel back. We shall see how it holds up.

Only other thing is the coloring and sticker material could have been a little better. I'm not positive, but is seems to me that the color may have been applied to the exposed side of the sticker, making it more susceptible to the elements and fading over time. I wish the plastic used for the sticker was a little harder and the color was applied to the inside of clear plastic to protect it more.

Overall, I have had ZERO problems with these decals, these are only unconfirmed suspicions of mine. Just be aware, these are Ford "licensed" decals. This only means that Ford has authorized the use of their trademarked "FX2 Sport" wording and styling. These are not necessarily manufactured at the same level of quality as the factory Ford decals.

Bottom line, I've been happy with them up to this point. And as of now, I'd buy them again if I needed them. They are, after all, at a pretty decent price. Go for it...

product_title: Buck Knives 0286CMS13 Bantam Knife, Reaper Black
review_headline: a 5 star knife for what you pay for
review_body:
while this isn't the greatest knife you can get, you do get a 5 star knife for what you pay for.

the blade is 420 high carbon steel that is 3.75 inches or 9.5cm long. blade profile is drop point hollow ground with a beveled cutting edge. this imo provides the best cutting edge profile. it is easy to sharpen, can be sharpened razor sharp but requires more sharpening maintenance.
the knife came shaving sharp right out of the box, but could use a stropping to remove some of the roughness.

the handle is glass reinforced nylon which makes it light, strong, but flexible. flexible is not a desirable trait, but it is what it is. you want stiffer material, the knife will be heavier and more expensive. that's the tradeoff.

the black reaper pattern seems to be no longer available at the buck store. this may be the last run of it, so get it while you can.

the knife has ambi-dextrous utility. i was able to use it comfortably in either hand and open it one handed in either hand. it is however lock-back which requires 2 hands to close. as with other features, the lock back is a trade-off. it provides extra strength for the knife, but you need 2 hands to close it. it also has a springy snap closure so using 2 hands to close it is ideal. there are ridges on the handle which assist in exerting extra cutting force. there is very little play on the blade

the clip is skeletonized steel held by 3 screws. it can be removed but the position cannot be changed. however, it doesn't seem to get in the way in either hand. functionally, it holds the knife well on the belt or cargo pocket. point down. if you prefer point up, look elsewhere. the lanyard hole is generous, but not reinforced with metal. that shouldn't be a problem.

the function for this knife is primarily hunting, trapping, camping and day hikes. it can also be used for carving in a pinch. although if you do plan on using it for hunting, you should probably get the one that has the mossy oak blaze camo pattern or the orange head hunterz pattern.

my hand width is approximately 3.5 inches and this knife fits perfectly in my hand. the balance point is right at the bulge of the clip, directly below the 3 screws (approximately where the forefinger rests on the grip).

i've said what it is, now i'll say what it is not.
it is not a survival knife. don't expect to beat up on it and expect it to last long.
it is not an axe. don't chop wood with it.
it is not a tactical knife. don't expect to get into a knife fight with it.
it is not an edc town carry knife. a blade longer than 3 inches is illegal in most states. carry at your own risk.u should probably get the one that has the mossy oak blaze camo pattern or the orange head hunterz pattern.

product_title: Star brite Mildew Stain Remover
review_headline: Perfect results. You can't beat this stuff
review_body: Believe what everybody's saying about this stuff.  I tried it on some badly mildew-stained vinyl boat seats and it took away every trace of the stains.  What worked well for me was to spray it on heavily, then lay a paper towel over the area and spray that a bit as well, so the cleaner was held wet against the seat for five minutes or so.  Afterward, just a light rub with a rag, and a rinse, and voila.  Perfect results.  You can't beat this stuff.  I just upgraded to the gallon size after great success with it last year.  One thing...this definitely smells like bleach, so the poster who said bleach works just as well might be onto something.  I'd say to go easy though, if attempting to use your own bleach solution.  Might be harsher than this formulation.  One other note:  I've resolved to put protectant on the vinyl after cleaning it, so it is less prone to getting as mildewy again.  The fewer times you have to use something this strong to clean your nice soft vinyl, the longer it'll probably stay that way.  Bottom line on Star brite though...get it.  It really works.

product_title: Kershaw 1556BW Cryo II Folding Knife with Blackwash SpeedSafe
review_headline: Kershaw's Cryo II is a hot one.
review_body:
I carried a CRKT M16-13ZLEK for many years and liked it but never loved it. I didn't like the placement of the clip, the serrated blade and the overall size. Also, the blade opened while in my pocket a couple of times which created some 'trust' issues. Overall it was a good knife, I just wanted something different. I did some research for a couple of weeks on folders and I landed on the Kershaw Cryo II.

I know the CRKT M16 is much different than the Cryo II but my experience with carrying a folder on a regular basis is based on the M16 so that is where I'll draw my comparisons.

It's larger than my old M16 but I knew that and I like the size. It still carries comfortably for EDC purposes. The Speed Assist works well; deployment of the blade is much faster than the M16, which just had a standard flipper. The thumb stud method of opening on the Cryo II is easy for my right hand but I'm still practicing with the left hand. Once open, the lock can be released one handed with either hand after a little practice. The adjustable clip and four carrying positions is what sold me on the Cryo II (after the Kershaw quality and rave reviews). I bought a little precision screw driver set ($6) that included a Torx T6 head. However, I've also used a Torx T5 head from a friend's tool set to change the clip. I don't know why two different Torx heads worked on the screws but my guess is one of the tools was a bit off and it's actually made for a T6. After moving the clip I can now carry the knife tip down and that improves deployment over the M16.

I was concerned about the smooth all steel construction without any texturing/micarta on the body. I actually dropped the knife when trying to open it via the flipper from my left hand. I know knife connoisseurs might get a bit queasy when I say this but I might cut out some skate boarder's friction tape and apply it to the handle. I did that for my CRKT Sting (great boot/neck knife) and it helped. If I can drop the knife under non-stressed, pristine conditions because it's smooth then who knows what can happen with stressed wet/cold/bloodied hands?

The knife came out of the box razor sharp so I haven't had to put an edge on it yet. Build quality is great. The Black Wash finish is nice.

As a side note...While I was in the hardware store buying the precision screw driver set I showed a store employee the knife. He immediately started raving about it and said he wanted to buy one. He had his own Kershaw knife on him at the time and said he loved it but thought it was time to upgrade.

product_title: Browning Spec Ops FHD Camera, Camouflage
review_headline: There's good & there's not so good
review_body:
Average rating for a mixed review. I'm using it for a little security outside the house. Some of the problems are inherent in all cams like this. This is the 1st trail cam I've purchased, so I can't compare it to real world experience with others, but I have read many reviews of others before buying this one. Most of my recording is in 1080p. I did not realize so much was happening in front of & sometimes on my property until I installed this.

Good:

- The camo color is a warmer yellow than the picture appears. This is better in my environment.
- The images are HD much of the time & the colors are usually very good. Sometimes they look great & crisp, other times dulled, even hazy, depending on the atmosphere, sun, speed of subject, glow of lights at night.
- IF it's triggered to record that large elk 70 ft away there's a great chance you will be able to count the number of points. (Problem is there's a good chance it won't be triggered to start recording at that distance).
- The nightvision face pics/vids are pretty good at 20 ft, after that you start guessing but can make out some things.

Neutral:

- It uses 8 AA batteries. The 1st set of disposable alkalines are near 10 % left & they've lasted me 1 month so far. There is a pretty good amount of activity in their view. I'm planning to buy rechargeables soon.
- Using a 16 GB SD card, it actually records 14.8 GBs. Recording in the highest quality (1080p) for 1 min segments my card is full in 3-3.5 days in a somewhat busy area. At that setting I get about 85 videos. I would think that it should last longer in the wilds.
- The closer the subject, the faster & more accurate the trigger speed. The farther away the subject is the bigger it needs to be to trigger the recording & the more likely the cam won't record at all. The other day it failed to record a walking man 30-40 ft away, but started recording when he pulled away in his vehicleabout 60 ft away.
- The sensor to check your viewing field seems to be fairly effective, & it's good for showing you how potentially inconsistant the triggering may be for you.

Not so good or approximately Bad:

- Though I see nothing at night when it is recording, during the day the bright red sensor has frequently caught my eye & sometimes I see a bright red dot on videos/images taken during the day, on a car & such. Given the certain angle or something it's easily spotted during the day because of this red (sensor). I can see how thieves might easily spot one in spite of the camo casing.
- I really wish the trigger speed was consistent & quicker. I've seen the backside of people leaving my property when it never recorded their arrival at all (they walked up to it & past it & it did not record them, but it recorded their backside 15 ft in front of it when they were leaving the property). It seems very rare that the trigger starts in near a 1/2 second. Most of the time the trigger starts recording in 1-3 seconds, usually takes 2 seconds or even more, sometimes it's never triggered. Sometimes it misses a whole person, sometimes it appears the pic or video was triggered by a flying bug, bird, shaking leaves, or a car that went by (I live at the end of a road with driveways) but by the time is starts recording the car is already gone for viewing field.
- Really lame that the night recording is only 10 seconds. It's often too short, & sometimes it records activity at the beginning of the incident, stops after 10 secs, then doesn't start recording again with the continued motion (which I have it set to do).
- Yes, having a viewing screen to check the field of view when setting up would be real nice, which is missing with this cam.
- It took 6 days just to get off the shelf to be shipped to me, which is the annoying norm for me the last 6+ months here. Maybe it's yet another annoying thing that's supposed to make me want to go Prime.

Approx Tips:

- When setting up, make sure leaves aren't nearby to be blown by the wind & trigger a lot of wasted recording.
- When setting it in place remember the subject might travel up to 30 ft before it's caught on cam.
- Recording in HD, your much more likely to get better results with a Class 10 SD card.
- I'm happier with it when I remind myself it's better than nothing. Honestly you can't expect too much when it's technology with many fluctuating variables. I look forward to these being better though.

Both software and hardware versions have updated.

product_title: Highgear Alti-XT Altimeter Watch
review_headline: Altimeter function is inadequate, compass totally worthloess.
review_body: My major reason for purchasing this watch was its altimeter feature.  I had owned a previous model with which I was basically satisfied for a period of about 5 years until the band wore out and I could not find a replacement.  The various timing features on the watch are fine, but the altimeter is less than satisfactory.  It works by sensing atmospheric pressure, and normal changes in atmospheric pressure can cause it to drift off by 200 or 300 vertical feet.  This may be unavoidable for a device that determines altitude based on pressure rather than GPS, but the annoying feature is that resetting the watch to the correct altitude takes a lot of button-pushing and can take more than a minute of holding down the button that scrolls through the value for "altitude in feet" that is displayed.  Even worse, the "altitude" that is displayed typically only updates about once per minute (whereas the older model of this watch updated about every 10 seconds).  Even while hiking in steep terrain (not to mention rapidly changing altitude by other means) this is woefully inadequate.    Furthermore, the compass function is worthless, being essentially stuck on one direction that could be disastrous for somebody who relied on it giving even a reasonable approximation of the correct direction.  I had the option of purchasing an altimeter watch by Suunto (?) and did not do so because those had such large faces.  The High Gear watch is more normally sized.

review_headline: Condor makes great machetes. This Parang is a classic example
review_body: Condor makes great machetes. This Parang is a classic example. A Parang is made with three cutting edges. The top of the blade is designed for skinning animals, the center of the blade is for chopping and the skinny bottom of the blade is for fine carving. It is in reality 3 blades in one. For those who are concerned about the less meaty carving bottom, don't be. This blade will never break in normal use. The design has been around for many years. I have used mine hard and it still works great with occasional sharpening. I actually prefer my Condor Golang to the Parang as I like the way it feels in my hands. If I had 3 blades to take on a trek I would choose those two and a Kabar Full size hunting/combat knife. Can't go wrong with those.

review_headline: It definitely looks like a makeup canister if some sort
review_body:
Got the pink and red set for my daughter for problems she has had with an aggressive male coworker. It definitely looks like a makeup canister if some sort. +1for the potential surprise factor. The trigger mechanism is a wash. The only safety mechanism is the cap/cover. Once the cover is removed it exposes a green button and a red button. The green turns on an led flashlight, the red button triggers the stun. Without an actual safety switch plus trigger to activate it seems as though the user has a greater chance of shocking themselves but it also means that it is faster when needed to pop the top off and defend yourself.
The contacts are the reason that I took off a star. They are flush with the container. That means you almost certainly need to make contact with bare skin or very thin cloth. They won't be penetrating. I advised that if she were forced to make use of it she should probably go for the exposed neck. Secondly the charge does look as though it would be painful but not incapacitating if you touch an extremity. Bare chest, neck or possibly exposed groin (ouch! ) look like the most effective choices. Given the blinding effect of pepper spray that would probably be the better first choice of defense with the stun used if a blinded attacker gets ahold if you.

This mic is made of aluminum and it looks very nice, the shock absorber adds that extra touch of awesomeness too!!

I highly recommend this mic, it is great for both people who record as a hobby and those who are starting out.

product_title: Red Rock Outdoor Gear Assault Pack
review_headline: Great day pack for the price!
review_body:
This is a great little backpack. It fits my 13" work laptop with extended battery and extra gear, and rides well on my back when I bike to work. The straps and buckles are sturdy, and all of the stitching is great. Its slightly smaller than the Maxpedition Falcon pack, and the Large version of the Red Rock assault pack is a little larger than the falcon pack. If you're a prepper looking for a 72 hour pack or if you want something more than a day pack, spend the extra 5$ and get the large one, you won't be disappointed. For the rest of us, this makes a great BOB for the car or just to throw around anywhere.

Pros:
Lots of webbing everywhere. For a pack this size, adding a couple of pouches turns it from a day pack into an up to 32 hour pack.
Compartments all have inner pockets
Stitching is good everywhere
Mesh padding on the back and shoulder straps to help dry out sweat
The nylon is sturdy and pliable, hasn't torn on anything so far (not rolling in the dirt with it though)

Cons:
The webbing isn't Molle spec, but can work with it. You basically have to skip rows
A lot of the webbing is halfway or off center, so you get unusable webs for no reason
As usual, the redrock outdoor logo is stitched onto the bottom row of webbing at the base of the pack, rendering it useless. All you need to do is pick the stitching out and you'll have access to it again. Don't know why they don't just put their logo on the top by the drag handle
The shoulder width of the pack is a little small, so if you somehow burden it with many heavy things it could dig in after a while. It IS a small pack though, so you shouldn't be able to unless you're trying real hard

product_title: Innova ITX9600 Heavy Duty Inversion Table
review_headline: Best Value on Inversion Tables - Period
review_body:
Table is extremely solid and its much cheaper than others. This is a no-brainer purchase.
It also has one of the coolest features I've seen. The limiter bar should be on all of them. I go completely inverted for a while then while still locked in just slide the bar in and screw it all the way down in the lowest setting so I can get the blood flow back calmly before going back to a full upright position. So comfortable I've actually accidentally fallen asleep on it. Whoops.
I saw someone comment about the bar being weak and that it would eventually break. If you thread the bolt down fully every time it will last a lifetime. Mine is nearly past the tab and over the main bar once it's fully seated. There's no way it would snap off. YMMV

Downside is it doesn't stand/store well. It tries to open up and it's still really deep then it's folded. I had to rig up a latch to keep the legs from opening in the standing position because they won't stay and when they separate it gets front heavy and will fall. It's got some weight too so that could cause/be a problem. Make sure you have some strength to move it, if you don't plan to leave it in one place - ready to use. Even folded you need a fairly large area to store it.
still it's excellent and I am more than happy with the purchase! Best value on inversion tables hands down.

review_body:
I think I expected more. I purchased this rebounder because of the weight allowance and because of the stability bar. I used to work out frequently but after injuries and weight gain I needed to try something different to get myself back on the exercise bandwagon. I thought this might do well to preserve my joints and foot, that has never been the same since it was injured. I'll be honest, it was hard to set up. Why, you ask? Because the stickers were swapped. Do not open this end was put on the end that was supposed to be opened and vice versa. Imagine me sitting in the floor trying to pull apart metal that was meant to stay together. The main reason I picked this rebounder was because of the stability bar. It took some work to fashion it on the rebounder but when I finally did I was super disappointed. I need it, because I'm not very sure on my feet on this contraption, but I know it won't hold up very long. I suspect somewhere around workout 10 I will be attacking it with a roll of duct tape.

For now, I am semi-satisfied, but not really, with it. I wouldn't recommend you buy it, but I'm not going to return it either since it's already here and set up. Will I break it? Most likely. Soon? Unless I quit using it, most definitely.

review_headline: I wouldn't go flashing the driver to my friends after hitting one drive with the Poly Max tape on because once there is a ball m
review_body:
I have tested these out the past three weekends. When I use them, I hit all kinds of fairways and I am hitting bombs. Now, I still get some movement left to right but it is about 1/3 the normal curvature. I even played one round without them in the middle and I was slicing a little bit more than with them. I guess if you cut across the ball with the face open the ball is going to slice no matter what you put on the face of the driver. That's my big miss, cut across with the face open. After the round without them on, I tried putting another one on the driver, and wallah, a big difference again. One thing to note, they also act as impact tape on the face letting you see your strikes. I wouldn't go flashing the driver to my friends after hitting one drive with the Poly Max tape on because once there is a ball mark it is pretty easy to tell there is something on the face from closer than a few feet. From further away, it just looks like a nice ball mark on the face. All I can say, is they work.

PROS:
***They reduce curvature by about 66%
***Acts as impact tape as well
***Relatively inexpensive compared to the amount of fun they add to the game

CONS:
***Can see ball marks on the tape within a few feet away indicating something is there
***A little tricky to peel and stick on face
***Precise trimming required with razor so it matches nicely with face
***Must apply carefully to avoid air bubbles underneath. Start at toe end and slowly press it on working towards heel for best results or top-down works too

product_title: Enpassion Waterproof Pouch with Waist Strap for Beach, Fishing, Hiking - Protects Phones, Camera, Cash From Water, Sand, Dust and Dirt
review_headline: It's a great idea but the Velcro makes it tear too easily (so much for "waterproof")
review_body:
I got this for free in exchange for testing it. (Uh oh! I happen to live by the beach!)

Well, let me tell you what works before I tell you why you should not buy this (IMHO). First off it fits your (my) iPhone 6+, as it was advertised to me. It also would fit a sandwich for that matter. It is essentially a thick plastic zippy bag. It is about as durable as an air mattress and made of what looks to be the same material (or 5 quality zippy bags). It has a TWO "press to seal" zipper closures that effectively keep water out - even salt water. How do I know? I put my iPhone in it and I tossed it into the ocean. Please note that salt water won't destroy this bag but it will make it sticky (not a real problem - just wash with soapy water). Wet sand (like you find at the beach) however will cling to this thing like a magnet, as will garden variety dirt. This is important as I was told that this was ideal to take to the beach. Sand (wet or not) however, will play havoc with the Velcro closure. Good luck making this thing look line after one day at the beach, or worse - surfing (see below).

The Velcro closure is completely unnecessary to the functioning of this bag and was its downfall. Not only does it attract every bit of dirt and debris that you come across when out in the real (wet) world, but it is glued firmly onto the blue plastic this bag/envelope is made from. The general idea of the Velcro closure is that you roll down the top (zippy parts) and fold over the top flap to make the bag/envelope more compact. The problem with that is the fact that you immediately lose 40% of your storage. Suddenly your waterproof bag isn't so big anymore.

But here is the killer: The blue plastic is stretchy but the Velcro is not. The hole thing is attached to a nylon waist band. The moment ANY tension is applied to the nylon strap (around your waist) the blue plastic is forced to stretch but the Velcro does not, and you end up with a tear in your blue plastic "waterproof" bag (I found this out the hard way). At this point you could have ten zipper locks and your iPhone (or sandwich) would be ruined. This is a great product if you never use it, or if you gingerly carry it around in the fog or light rain, but it is designed to be submersible so you can scuba, surf, swim, dive, or work in the rain. Being that your bag WILL be around your waist and that the blue plastic is easily torn, you should hope that you had a sandwich in there and not your phone.

I am sorry to be a downer, and I see that everyone else loves this thing, but I have to wonder if they actually gave it a real world test. Buy this at your own risk. Good for extremely light duty except for the fact that the heavy duty "press to seal" sippers are hard to seal for "light duty." If they took the Velcro off this bag would stretch and not be so prone to tearing. Remember, all you need is one small tear or hole and your bag is no longer waterproof. Anyway, thanks for reading. review_headline: This SightMark bore sight works great. I have a tip for those who use ...
review_body:
This SightMark bore sight works great. I have a tip for those who use this to keep the batteries in the sight. I took a paper punch and punched a hole in a piece of paper, then taking the round piece that was punched from the sheet of paper, unscrew the cap of the boresight, remove one battery, then place the small piece of paper between the batteries and screw the cap back on. The sight won't turn on because there is not a complete connection between the batteries.

When you want to use the sight again, unscrew the cap, remove the piece of paper, insert the battery the correct way and it bingo it comes on. No more removing the batteries then replacing them each time you want to use the bore sight.

product_title: Anderson Bat Company Rocketech 2.0 Slow Pitch Softball Bat
review_body:
So the league I play for recently switched to aluminum bats only. I spent quite a long time looking for a good end loaded aluminum bat. The Demarini SF7 seemed like it was the only good slow pitch aluminum bat out there, most everything is composite these days(for good reason, who wants to spend $250 on a bat to have it dent after 10 at bats).

But anyways, like I said, I wanted an end loaded bat. The SF7 is not end loaded, so I looked elsewhere. I stumbled upon this bat, and while there were no reviews on Amazon, other websites had vouched for it. I had never heard of the Anderson Bat Company up to this point, as I only had experience with Demarini, Easton, Louisville Slugger, etc, more common baseball bat names. Well the Anderson Bat Company didn't disappoint. The bat has very good pop for an aluminum bat, comparable to a composite bat, and so far through a few games it hasn't dented or shown any signs of denting*knock on wood*. It feels very solid though, if it does end up denting in the future I'll update this post and say when and how many at bats(roughly) it went through.

I'm giving it 5 stars because it has good pop, feels like a strong bat that won't dent easily, and has exceeded all expectations.

A couple things to note about the bat that I'm okay with, but others might not be. I had an end loaded bat last summer that was composite. That bat you could catch it a little lower than the meat of the barrel and still get a good piece of the ball. If you don't hit this ball square on the barrel it's going to feel like you hit the handle. When I say it's end loaded...I freakin mean it, it's almost like all the weight is in a 5 inch area, haha. But that's what I was looking for. If you have the hand eye coordination to ensure you hit it on the meat of the bat consistently, and feel like you can handle a very heavily end loaded bat, then this bat will be great for you.

product_title: Tippmann Flatline  Barrel for X-7 & X7 Phenom
review_headline: Barrel breaks barriers and with help, not balls
review_body:
Amazing barrel but use it with caution. All flatline barrels are hard on paint due to their curve, the X7 version has shortest barrel and the steepest curve which makes it the hardest on paint.

There are two tricks I've found to make this barrel sing, first of all use midgrade paint. Cheap paint will break in any barrel and high end paint has a thinner shell, so use midgrade for its reliability and thicker shell. Secondly (and I only suggest this when using a Phenom) dial the FPS back to 265. The Phenom has an internal regulator which allows for lower FPS shooting without inhibiting performance and 265 FPS is the sweet spot to almost eliminate breakage.

I'm only posting this bottom section for those who don't already know what the flatline does.

This barrel has a curve to it and a sandpaper like texture inside which forces a paintball to spin backwards while in flight. This backspin does wonders for the projectile, it both creates a low grade lift (similar to the "fastball" pitch in baseball) and nearly eliminates the imperfection of the paintball seam which will otherwise cause inaccuracies. The result is a further flying projectile with increased accuracy.

A bit of warning though, if you do break a paintball in this barrel... the backspin will not work and your accuracy will greatly diminish. You must remove the barrel (which isn't difficult) and fully clean the unit before it will function properly.

product_title: Dog Expedition TC1 Border Patrol GPS System and Remote Trainer, Black Finish
review_headline: Good start, some flaws, customer service is AWFUL!
review_body:
I bought this unit, along with an add-on collar for a second dog, from a brick and mortar store, not here. But wanted to add to what other reviewers have posted. We use this simply as a "fence" at home to keep our dogs from wandering around our rural neighborhood. The battery on the collars does not last for more than a day, but that is ok for us. We take the collars off each night when we put the dogs to bed and charge the collars and then just put them back on them in the morning for the day. The handheld unit generally stays plugged in to the charger most of the time.

It is limiting being able to only create a circle fence using a radius and being able to identify "way points" would be much better but we've made the circle work for us (we have five acres so we've got some room to work with but we have a very oddly shaped lot so that made it trickier). It took me several hours of traipsing around our property and at least five different tries to find the right center point and the right radius distance to create a workable "fence" area.

The antenna is a definite issue but one that they appear to be working on. The main unit that we bought came with the skinny wire antenna that shows up in the picture and others have identified as a problem. But the add on collar we bought have a much thicker, stiffer antenna, more like the antenna that is on the handheld unit. The add on collar is still working great. Unfortunately, in just over two months, the skinny wire antenna had bent, shredded, and eventually broke off entirely, which caused that collar to stop working altogether. I sent it in for repair and two and a half weeks later, the company is still not able to tell me anything about the status of the repair, except to confirm that they received it and that it is in their repair shop waiting to be fixed, and that their turnaround time is 5-6 weeks! When I pay $600 for something and it stops working within threemonths, I expect better service than what they provide and it makes me think that their repair shop must be overly full with broken products if that is how long it takes them to get to it!

Ultimately, we do love the product for what we wanted to use it for and I'm hoping they send me a new collar with the thicker antenna soon so I can get back to keeping my dog contained in my yard.
