product_title: Maxpedition Gear Cocoon Pouch
review_headline: Great pouch for Sawyer and Survivor water filters
review_body:
I ordered one of these pouches from my recommended items list because it had the dimensions of a couple of backpacking water filters that I carry. I received this pouch and quickly test-fit it for my filters, and it both styles fit perfectly. I always carry a Sawyer Mini water filter when I go backpacking, and I also keep one in my bug-out bag. I was using a different zippered semi-hard sided case for my filter previously, but that case was designed to protect a GPS unit or small/midsize electronics device. This pouch is far lighter and a much better use of space.

The Survivor filter (also sold here on Amazon) was the first filter I put in this pouch. The fit was perfect. It even left a little space on the sides so I could put the extra prefilters inside, as well as a modified hydration tube adapter I made so I can process water through this filter and right into my hydration bladders. Next, I put the Sawyer Mini in the pouch with the adapters I've also made for that one. I was even able to roll up and store my 16oz squeeze pouch that came with the Sawyer and fit it in this new pouch as well. Again, I was pleased.

I ended up purchasing 2 more of these pouches. One pouch now houses the Survivor filter, hydration adapter and a 16oz squeeze pouch. The 2nd pouch holds my Sawyer Mini, hydration adapters, and a 32oz squeeze pouch. The 3rd pouch holds 2 64oz squeeze pouches rolled up. I will use those as extra water portage when needed. You could even use one pouch for your filter, and the other for your tubing and squeeze pouch to prevent cross contamination. Get creative.

This cocoon pouch clips to various pack straps or right to molle webbing but horizontally. Some fast adapters would work on this as well, as it does have 3 bands of molle on the back of the pouch for various different attachment uses. The pouch comes with one quick clip that would work, but I prefer a more secure molle attachment.

Instead it uses a simple to use and seemingly durable nylon buckle.

This has great adjustment on the shoulder straps and waist. Although I did not try the smaller version of this safety vest, based on how large this vest (L/XL) is capable of being adjusted, I could probably have fit easily into the S/M/L size of this. I'm 6'2\\", 205 pounds.

product_title: Metal Police 75 Million Stun Gun Volt Rechargeable LED Flashlight & Taser Holster Stuns R Us
review_headline: easy to use and a must have for self defense
review_body: This stun gun is a must have. It looks and work like a regular flashlight but is a stun gun as well.  It is rechargeable which takes about 8 hours to fully charge on the first initial use. It comes with a charger to charge it and the red light on the bottom indicates it is charging.  The red light will not go off when it is through charging so you have to use it when you believe it is through.  The flashlight is very bright and the light has a wide lighting coverage. Now on the bottom of the flashlight is the on/off switch.  Use that switch to power on the stun gun. On one side there is a switch for the flashlight push the switch up to turn the flashlight On. Push the switch Down to cut the light off. Push it down again until you hear a click to activate the stun gun. Turn the flashlight over to the side which reads Police and there is a button to operate the stun gun. Press the button and you will hear the zapping from the stun gun. Only hold the button down for one second or you can burn the battery. To deactivate the stun gun push the switch up once on the flashlight side. To turn the whole unit off and to preserve the battery push the switch to the off side on the bottom of the stun gun.  Now I will admit I was confused on how to use the stun gun part because I didn't push the switch Down far enough on the flashlight side. it also comes with a case to protect the metal and the stun gun. Overall it's easy to use and good self defense gadget.  I received this product for testing and reviewing purposes only and all opinions are mine

product_title: Burris MSR Riflescope
review_body: Bought the Burris MSR 4.5-14x42 223 scope for my 223. I compared this to a Vortex Viper HS 4-16x44lr of mine.  Here is my comparison:  I liked the SF on the Vortex better, the turret clicks on the vortex are definetly more pronounced. However, the Vortex's  magnification ring is harder to turn and I would prefer to have at least all the even powers on the mag ring. On the Vortex I found the paralallax markings to be way off for me by 100 yards or more.  I looked thru both scopes in the direction of bright sunlight and at dusk.  I didn't see a discernable difference between the 2 they are both very clear. The AO on the MSR is not as easy as a side focus but the parallax settings on the MSR were right on the money. The AO on the MSR is rather large which means it cannot be mounted as low as the Vortex if that is your concern. I like how the turret knob is lower on the MSR, making it easier to fit in a gun case. The tracking on Burris seemed  excellent by matching the ballistic chart for my load and returning to zero.  Used it to shoot out to 700 yds. The Vortex is known for excellent tracking as well. With the MSR I could see the splatter marks in the paint on the metal gong i was shooting at 700 yards with my 223. Good clarity.  Both the scopes have a BDC type reticle. the reticle on the Vortex  appears to be thinner,  It also has 2 moa hashmarks for windage hold off which is a cool feature. In  the Burris's favor, its reticle is easier to see as it gets dark. Yea the finish on the Vortex looks a little nicer. I dont like the little screw on the bottom of MSR, looks kinda cheesy.  I paid 1/2 the price for the Burris MSR as I did for my Vortex.  I think you can't beat the Burris MSR for the price. It performs excellent. It's a worthy scope.Burris has a great warranty too.

product_title: Mizuno World Win GXF75 Baseball First Baseman's Mitt (12.5-Inch)
review_body: My son has been begging me for a first baseman's mitt for two years.  He has been a utility player over the past couple of years, so I told him I wasn't going to spend money on a first base mitt until I saw that he was going to consistently play first base.  He joined a 12U travel team this year and he started regularly playing first base in the first couple of games, so I had to hold true to my word.  Since we were already into the season, I wanted a mitt that we could break in easily and quickly.  This glove was the top ranked 1st base mitt at JustBallGloves.com early in the season and was one of the cheapest. However, they still wanted $90 for it.  Boy, was I happy when I found it on Amazon for $60-$65 and since I have Prime...free shipping, too!  Most of the reviews were positive and most everyone stated that the mitt was easy to break in.  This was also true for us.  I broke the glove in according the Lee Chilton's (The Gloveman's) procedure in this article from the LA Times: http://articles.latimes.com/2012/feb/22/sports/la-sp-erskine-20120222.  I microwaved a wet towel and wrapped the glove (with a ball in the pocket) in the towel once a day for three days straight.  After a couple of practices, the glove was ready to go.  My son swears by the glove.  He thinks it's magical.  All I can say is that he has become a ball eating machine at first base.  He had a hard ground ball at him in a blink of an eye at a game last night and he stop it cold in its tracks with the glove.  One of his coaches called him, "His hero" twice--once on that play plus another long stretch and grab put out.  The coaches also said he was their best fielder that night.  We even had an awesome come from behind win in the last inning and my son's performance was largely responsible for it.  My son thinks it's because of his "magic" glove.  The only magic in the glove is that it's instilled a confidence that I never seen before in my son, and it is a lot more fun to watch him play.m play.

product_title: Flatworld® Manual Open & Close Umbrella - Durable and Delicate for Sun and Rain - Volume Light Vinyl Umbrella
review_body:
As we were beginning to pack for a trip to the Islands, we wondered what hats to bring along and whether or not an umbrella made any sense - as the rains are frequent, but usually brief and gentle. Then came this small umbrella/parasol from Flatworld. Just right for Maui - Come rain or come shine!

Gift packaged with style and simplicity, the simple, but light and easy to open and close device fit easily into our suitcase and car. It is great! The flower decoration makes it seem most fitting in the hands of a woman - but I noticed that on Maui, more and more men are carrying what were once quite popular as 'parasols' (sun umbrellas) in the days before anyone knew anything about SPF.

The rains did come while we were there - along with some fairly strong afternoon tradewinds, as anyone familiar with Maui will have come to expect. This petite but effective travelling pal from Flatworld held up quite well. While we watched larger, more traditional umbrellas blow inside-out, our little one kept both its shape and functionality.

A word about price:
This is not the cheapest small umbrella on the market; That is for certain - BUT, there are times when you DO get what you pay for and this may be one of them. It is now a permanent component of the "let's go to Hawaii" bag!

product_title: XYZ Boat Supplies Dual USB Charger Socket for Boat / Rv / Car / Motor-home
review_body: While it is a great idea, it has several design errors that make it a problem.  The first issue I ran into was that it was intermittent (power light would flicker and anything plugged into it would keep resetting).  Turns out that was a double problem - there is an inductor coil inside for the switching regulator that drops the 12v to 5v for the USB - not only was the coil suspended in mid-air by it leads (very bad design in any kind of environment with vibration ... like a mobile installation), but one of the coil leads had not been properly soldered to the circuit board - that was the intermittent connection.  The coil should have had a blob of silicone etc. between it and the circuit board to keep it from vibrating.  Second issue was the base/circuit board was never glued into the main housing and when you plugged something in, the entire assembly slid out the back of the housing.  The missing glue may have been just a random issue with the one I got, but the coil being suspended in free space without any silicone etc. to keep it from vibrating means anybody else with one of these WILL eventually have it fail if it is in a vibration prone environment (car, boat etc.).

product_title: Yurbuds Ironman Inspire Duro Plus Cloth Cords Sport Earbuds
review_headline: Might be a good choice for runner
review_body:
My workout is mostly cardio and these earphones work perfectly for me. I do running and rowing in a gym and outside and I'm pretty happy with the fit and the sound quality.

Fit: the default Apple earbuds almost fit me but they fall out randomly. This pair fits me perfectly, even slight tugs on the chord are not a problem. For example I dropped my phone two times while running and both times the earphones stayed in place and rather the phone and the chord disconnected to let the phone go.

Sound quality: For sport earphones I'm pretty happy with what I get. Categories better than the other sports pair I have. In silent surroundings I would put the quality in line with the Apple earbuds.

I've seen some very helpful reviews with three major concerns, let me address those.

Ambient noise: Yes, these earphones don't filter outside noise a lot which I like very much as it makes them safer for running outside and I even feel better this way in the pretty silent gym I frequent. I don't like to lose touch with my surroundings.

Cord tangling: Actually, I find this material pretty easy to untangle. It is a lot better than the all-rubber ones. With this one you just hold on to the middle fob, shake the thing a bit and most of the untangling is done!

The rubber coating on the ear-pieces does get gross a bit, but with a wet finger you can wipe them clean enough for my taste. And actually, this won't be the most gross piece on you after a good workout anyway:)

You get the idea: before I couldn't, it was time for tendon tenderness, muscle movement and better blood flow. What about that yoga mat of my wife's? Petite and about a hundred pounds lighter, her 1/8" thick mat seems to work great for her. I tried it—several times—before I gave up. The comfort level of her mat? I am being generous here: 'hand towel on concrete.' When I touched the Thrive On mat, I knew I had my answer. Comfort level? Supreme! The cushion and give are just right: comfortable and firm enough to be a secure, stabile base for different poses. Though it's light, it stays put on the floor and does not slide around. The Thrive On mat is an invitation to take care of myself.

Quality shows in two other mat details: the rounded corners and the strap. Two elastic garters with a handle in between, the carry-strap makes for quick, simple storage and transport.
PS: Love the blue color!

review_headline: Does the job - but overall disappointed
review_body: Updated review after vacation use. After a day of using this is the Florida sun in Orlando, I found the negatives outweighed the positives.   1) the screen was nearly unreadable in the sun, the soft material over the screen part degraded the contrast to near zero 2) the no button access was more of a problem than I anticipated. 3) due to the lack of contrast, taking a picture or video was nearly impossible after all, which was the point of the case 4) the screen cover material prevented access to certain areas of the screen for some reason, for instance was unable to swipe Up or Down End of the day, I rather would have not purchased it.  Does the job intended.  The touch side interface is sort of a rubbery elastic surface, so its a little strange to use, but the point is that it indeed seems quite waterproof.  I left a facial tissue in the unit and submerged it in a container for about 2 hours, and not even a speck of moisture.  One downside, no flexible push points for volume or on-off buttons, the only access is to the front button and touch screen.  One other, Touch ID doesn't function as it cant's get a good read due to the material.  Minor annoyances for the intended purpose.  I would have liked a longer lanyard, the one included is a standard length like for a badge, but too short to swing up to like take a picture, the phone ends up be like 6 inches from your face.  Still though overall, very good price for what you are getting it for.

product_title: Swing Extender Golf Swing Trainer
review_headline: Use this as you deem approriate to address your needs....
review_body:
This is a device that may and may not work for you. It can give you feed back to not collapse the trail elbow but you may need to have a means to really provide a means to practice the "feel" to prevent the collapse. Consideration should be also given if it is not an upper body flexibility issue that needs to be addressed or over swinging in an effort to create more club head speed....all of which may need the help of a certified instructor.

Has it helped me...sort of. Created awareness of where trail elbow should be, however you need to (in your mind's eye) know work with your hip turn (proper weight shift), arms / shoulder turn , wrist hinge...don't over swing...then transition properly on the downswing...easy peasy and strive for proper tempo. Using a radar you'll be surprise at the mph you generate via a fluid swing versus an attempt to force the swing.

review_headline: This product came and I was really pleased with the design even if it is just a ...
review_body: I purchased this item to carry my camera during mud runs. Yesterday was it's first try and it kept my camera dry and in working condition. Last year I put the camera in a zipped lunch baggy stored in the waistband of my pants. I almost lost it in one of the mud pits and decided to look for something that 1. could keep the camera dry and 2. that wouldn't float away. This product came and I was really pleased with the design even if it is just a smidge too big, 5"x 8" for my purposes which was too carry one camera. My fellow mudders were excited to see this bag and so I can tell you that it can carry 2 cameras and 2 average size smart phones safely. When you lift the velcro flap it reveals a rolled section of the bag where three separate really tight zips are located. It took some effort to open those zips but that's good because you know they're sealed tight, there are three of them, and they're rolled under a flap attached with velco. Water is NOT getting in there! I've read other reviews saying that the bag was flimsy and would fall apart. The material will degrade over time I'm sure but I think you'd really have to be abusive for the product to fail right away. The waist band is a about and inch thick and adjustable, approximately 30 to 44 inches. I have a 28" waist so the bag bounced a bit but that was not a big deal. Overall, a really satisfying purchase and my fellow mudders will most likely be ordering one for themselves before the next race!

product_title: Truglo Replacement Fibers .060X5.5 Optic, Multiple
review_headline: Great replacements, very long, very bright, fits my XDs
review_body:
Fit my Springfield-Armory XDs perfectly. Very well made so that you don't have to get extensively close to the filament to balloon the tip and lock it in. This is better because you end up with a much cleared filament in the end. Of the set of colors, green is by far the brightest. The orange is the dimmest. Red trails green only by a little and the others are just a mix between the red and orange in the power.

Simple installation, simple working. First remove the old one by cutting it some how and pulling it out of both ends. Be careful to not destroy your front sight because it will look bad! We don't want that. Next, use a flame or heat source to balloon the bulb slightly at the end, at this point, I didn't cut anything off. Be careful to NOT touch the filament to your heat source or it will cook the inside of the filament. This will cause clouding, and that basically means that light will not travel through it, and rather than an fiber optic that gathers light and sends it to the ends, you are looking at green plastic sights. Don't do that. After you balloon one end, slide the whole filament, still uncut myself, into your sight hole. Mark a small amount over the edge of the sight mount. I used about 2 mm or so, it doesn't have to be large, just enough to provide material that will fill the whole once ballooned. You can score the filament at that point, then remove it from the sight. Give it a little more cutting in the score and you should be able to bend and snap it at that point. A flat cut is most unnecessary, when you heat that side it will just round off anyway. Again, not touching the filament, reinsert the filament and balloon the second end, thus locking the filament in place. If it has a little wobble, apply ever so much more heat and do so patiently, or just let it go. Finally, look through the filament and ensure it is bright and not clouded. Then, you are done!

Oh, and I didn't say to clear your weapon to start this thing, but if you don't do that and end up dead, you really shouldn't have a weapon in your hand anyway.tart this thing, but if you don't do that and end up dead, you really shouldn't have a weapon in your hand anyway.

product_title: All-Star Youth D30 Protective Inner Baseball/Softball Catcher's Glove
review_headline: Need a bit more padding for the critical areas
review_body:
This glove fits my boy and his teammates perfectly. They're skinny, tall, 7 to 9 years old, with average growing hands. The teammates, who are a bit huskier/bulkier, larger than average hands, can't even slide their hands past half way.

Pros:
Glove reduces the stinging from fastballs tremendously, especially the hand's web and palm areas.
Provide filler for the gloves, allowing the hands to fit the larger gloves more securely.

Cons:
Thumb and index fingers' padding require a bit more high tech padding. Most of the stings occur between these two fingers, while providing great impact protection around the palm-web areas of the hand.

The two paddings, at the base of the four finger and the palm areas, crease together too aggressively, causing a pinch on the skin at the palm's fold. The gap between these two paddings require a bit more gap. I have to cut out a bit using my dremel tool to increase the glove's gap for comfort, preventing any cinching/creasing. Kids are quite happy using the glove now.

This is a valuable tool to have to train beginners to handle fastballs coming at them, as they adjust to the ball receiving methods, without hurting their hands, which discourage them from playing.

product_title: Polar M400 GPS Smart Sports Watch
review_headline: Better to use H7 Strap + $7.99 Polar Beat App Bundle
review_body: I don't think this is the best exercise companion there is. I have been a hardcore Polar fan since my Polar RS100 saved my life by detecting extremely high heart rate and beeping like crazy. Tracking your heart rate is paramount for anyone with any history of cardiac conditions or anyone willing to track effectively their performance and progress. Over the years, I have seen how my resting heart rate has become better and better. However, we are now becoming obsessed with tracking - we want to track everything. I was thinking on replacing my loyal and hard-working FT7 with the M400, but I see it as a downgrade.  I am not really interested in tracking how many steps I take or if I am moving enough because I already live an active lifestyle to the scope of my body comfort and ability. I don't like to be a couch potato. What I need is a very efficient and dynamic companion to help me understand how my body is reacting during what is most important: a workout. The M400 is not as informative during a workout as the FT7.  My FT7 tells me before I start the tracking what my heart rate is. While I am working out it tells me very key information: heart rate, what am I doing? burning fat or cardio?, how many calories have I burned, how long have I been working out... and if I need to know something very important such as the time... I just bring the watch close to the sensor and voilà, the time shows up for a few seconds. With the M400.... I don't work as happy or informed as I want. If I want to know the time, I gotta stop and press buttons to make it to the time. My heart rate is shown in one screen that also shows me 5 buckets where my heart rate can be working in. These 5 buckets correspond to the Heart Rate Target Zones... I am honestly not that interested in this push Polar is doing into heart rate compartmentalization. I think every athlete or exercises has their own targets. This zones are particularly irrelevant in this model since there is no "Virtual Coach" to guide you on how long to spend on each zone - there are no programs on the watch like the FT80 has that make the Heart Rate Zone relevant. If you are running or cycling, you get helpful and relevant screens for your sports that indicate altitude and speed, but if you are doing "Other Indoor Activity" you will won't get any cardio vs. fat information, nor the calories that you have burnt so far. Updated: You can actually go to the Polar Flow website and create custom training views for your watch - one of which can be Calories burned. I gave a new start for that level of customization. However, I am keeping my FT7 as I will use the app bundle when I need voice guided coaching and the fitness test. My FT7 can received the transmission of the H7 without any problem while it transmits to my phone as the FT7 doesn't uses Bluetooth but a coded signal - thus the information is available to both devices! The FT7 has a move convenient form factor and it is much more discrete.  I am not a runner nor a cyclist, I am a cross-trainer. I do like to follow a Paleo lifestyle - specially in my eating. I try to do with my body the most I can because our body needs conditioning and activity as much as it needs good food and rest. Sometimes, I like to  play "Caveman" and I walk to the supermarket to get food for the day - my version of going hunting... The calories that I burn while "hunting" are like credit cards rewards points that I can use for food. In my mind I have this idea that if I don't move, I don't eat. Period. It may be a corny roleplay but it has been very effective in losing  weight and keeping myself motivated. Therefore, sometimes, I workout with a calories burned goal rather than a time goal. I am pretty sure that if I burned 500 calories under an hour, I worked out well. I tried the calorie counting lifestyle once using MyFitnessPal app and the math doesn't fail. Polar HR Monitors are very accurate at registering calories burned. I did the thing as mathematical as possible and did lose the 2 lbs per week. Caloric deficit is mathematical.  I don't find myself obsessed with tracking everything I do. I just need to track what is important on a workout and the FT7 does that very well. However, there is a helpful alternative to a watch. If you get the Polar H7 Bluetooth enabled strap, runs about $50, you can then use your smartphone with the Polar Beat app to track your workout. The best part is that Polar offers a bundle for $7.99 that enhances the Polar Beat app to include: Benefit Target, EnergyPointer (fat vs cardio), Fitness Test, Running Index. Those are solid features as the apps already tells you how many calories have been burned and gives you GPS information using your phone. Not just that but all this syncs to the Polar Flow website and you can even see a pretty cool EKG-like graph of your heart rate during the workout!  H7 + App Blunde = $60 with tax. Much cheaper than getting this watch to track your steps and your sleep. Seriously, sleeping with this is VERY uncomfortable...  The watch is big. It is very good looking but it is very big too. I could not sleep with it. While I sleep, I want my body to be free of constraints. My bed is the place where my body rests from everything - mentally and physically. I don't sleep naked... but I do sleep with very comfortable sleepwear. The size of the watch will create pressure against your arm. Those people who like to tuck their arms under the pillow or face will feels its presence. The strap locking mechanism will dent deep into your skin as your arms rests against anything... which brings me to one thing I really really dislike about the watch... the strap. The strap is bulky and you have to wrestle it to take of the watch. The watch is not very easy to put on... but it is very difficult to take off.  I will order an H7 and use my smartphone to track my heart rate when I work out at home. I may even use my tablet. I will continue using my FT7 for anything else.

product_title: Sea Striker HS8 High Speed Planer 8oz
review_headline: Great way to get to deep fish
review_body: I've been very happy with this planer so far.  I live in Hawaii and have used it both on inner reefs (40-60 ft) and on the 40 fathom ledge.  On the inner reefs I used to use a deep diving Rapala but it put a lot of stress on the rod due to the resistance created by the big lip and never got as deep as advertised.  With the planer all the resistance is on the planer's line which attaches to a cleat, and very little is on the rod.  I've found that it gets my lure deeper (around 20-30 feet) and has consistently outperformed my old style of fishing.  Last week I tried the planer with a skirted jet head on the 40 fathom ledge and was worried that the planer wouldn't work at the 7 to 8 mph that I normally troll at.  It did fine and I had 2 Ono (Wahoo) strikes, and landed one of the fish which was a 40 pounder.  That fish alone made the cost of the planer well worth it.  The only caveat is that it is a bit of work to deploy.  You need to slow down at first until it engages and an extra pair of hands helps.  Also, you can't pull too big a lure or the rubber band will break. All in all I'm very satisfied.  I've been catching fish that I wouldn't normally get, so that makes it a great addition to my gear.

product_title: Nautilus 5 Position Bench
review_headline: Save $50 and buy the identical BowFlex bench
review_body: I ordered this weight bench through Amazon Vine and was surprised to see that it's identical (except in color) to a weight bench I had previously bought through Amazon-- the BowFlex SeclectTech Adjustable Bench Series 3.1  http://www.amazon.com/dp/B000BH7CB2/ref=pe_309540_26725410_item  I wanted to replace the BowFlex bench because my dog had chewed parts of the foam leg supports. Since Nautilus makes BowFlex equipment, you can save yourself $50 and buy the BowFlex bench. Because the benches are identical, and I've owned the BowFlex for over 2 years, I can tell you that if you want to buy either one, you will be pleased with your purchase. The bench is very durable and is a great addition to a home gym. After 2 years, there is not one crack in the vinyl, and we use it almost daily. It's very easy to assemble and easy to adjust. Note: To adjust to decline, just fold the adjustment arm up next to back of the bench and lower the upper part of the bench to be parallel with the angled back leg. Several other reviewers have commented about the gap between the seat and backrest, but I have never noticed it. I do agree with other reviewers that the leg braces are at a bit of an awkward angle, but it's not bad enough that I can't do decline presses or crunches. My husband and I are both 5'9" and my son is 6' tall, and the bench accommodates all our heights. I highly recommend this bench or the BowFlex SelectTech, but check the prices on both as you may be able to save some money by buying the BowFlex.

review_body:
The “point” of a multi-purpose knife is to be a well balanced and reliable tool. This multi-purpose folding knife is exceptionally well balanced, in its ability as a tool and in weight, and is a respectable tool for its various jobs. This knife will allow me to be able to explore with my friends…I can go anywhere from the beach to the park to the woods because I don’t have to stress about not being able to eat or drink in the great outdoors.
The only thing about this knife that I found to be problematic was that the positioning of the cork screw was such that the tip of the screw, when closing it, had chipped the very tasteful matte finish red paint. However, if you open the knife with care, this shouldn’t be a problem for you. Even with the chip, the features of the knife are all aesthetically pleasing and make me excited about sharing it with those around me. No matter if you’re a straight edge person or if you cut things close to the edge, get this knife!

review_headline: You get what you pay for.

Seemed too good to be true, and it was. They are about 1/3 the cost of other urethane-coated dumbbells. The urethane coating is actually great. The problem is they ruin it with the handles. Basically, they took great weights that could compete with gym quality products and put the worst handles ever on them.

product_title: Frogg Toggs Men's Firebelly 2-Tone Jacket
review_headline: Can't make a silk purse from a sow's ear.
review_body:
I purchased two Firebelly jackets. First I purchased a medium based on Frogg Toggs sizing chart. It turned out to be too big. This jacket looked so nice that I kept it (with the intent of gifting it), and ordered a small for myself. The small arrived, it didn't fit that great. It appears they size these for tall slender people with long arms.

But the disappointing part was the wrinkles. Once this polyprop material gets wrinkled, it looks awful. Worse yet, how do you get the wrinkles out? So I washed it. Big mistake. I used the gentle cycle on warm, and the black bled into the red. Had I used cold, it might not of bled. Regardless, the wrinkles didn't go away. So I dried it. Bigger mistake. Now it looks more wrinkled than the cheaper Frogg Toggs. The only thing good that happened is that the arm lengths shrunk a few inches, and the jacket now fits snuggly.

The material is polyprop. It is cheap, uncomfortable, not durable. They put a lot of sewing workmanship into the jacket, but you can't make a silk purse out of a sow's ear.

My recommendation would be to avoid the higher-end Frogg Toggs and go with the cheapest disposable Toggs; knowing the material is cheap, and is really more functional as a back-up plan stored in the bag.

Note: Since writing the above review, I've had time to use the jacket in rainy conditions. Now I even like the jacket less. It is very restrictive toward movement. Poor design, with some superficial perks (e.g. pockets & adjustment straps) to distract the buyer. DO NOT RECOMMEND THIS PRODUCT.

product_title: Your Jiu Jitsu Gear Brazilian Jiu Jitsu Uniform White,Black,Blue & Grey
review_body:
I bought this gi because I'm new to the sport and didn't want to blow a pile of cash right out of the gate. Also, I tend to not be great at sports so I don't feel the need to buy top of the line equipment.

I'm 6'-1" (185 cm), 225 lbs (102 kg), 30" (76 cm) wrist to collar, 44" (111 cm) chest, 42" (106 cm) waist, 38" (96 cm) hips, 32" (81 cm) waist to ankle. I ordered the A4 and it was roughly half an inch long at the sleeve and leg. I did an initial wash, double checked the length of the sleeve and leg and did one run through the dryer on low heat (I did not dry the belt). It shrunk up perfectly. The gi top is a little loose in the shoulders but fits well as long as you have the right size top. The top is pretty stiff so if you try to close the jacket too tight the shoulders don't lay properly. The pants are a little light and a little baggy. The belt shipped with the gi was marked A4, but was cut at an A3 length. I contacted amazon (or the seller, I'm not sure which one answered my e-mails) for a replacement but was offered a partial refund instead.

My complaints are that pants too light (the fabric is about the same weight as cotton pants) for me and the belt is too thin and as result not rigid enough. If I had to guess it's the pants and the belt where they cut corners to save on costs. All in all, is this the same quality as a $200 gi? No, but it's also not a $200 gi. Is it a good deal? Definitely.

product_title: Louisville Slugger EB 2014 Series 5 Rig Baseball Bag
review_headline: Good value for basic bat bag
review_body:
This bag (Series 5 Rig) is a good value, but here are the pros and cons:

Cons:
Not many pockets/compartments - one main area, one top area called "game day pouch" which is the a bit larger than the size of a batting helmet, one long side pocket, and one compartment for your bats. This means your cleats must be stored with your gloves. And the bat compartment has no separation, so your bats make contact.

No stiff bottom so your bats add the rigidity along the bottom.

Pros:
Appears well made (I haven't used long yet) and worth the price.

Good size for non-catcher - holds 4 bats, 2 sets of cleats, 2 gloves, batting helmet, misc items (ie sunscreen, batting gloves, neoprene braces, etc). However I needed to separate items into bags so that they would not merge together in main or side compartment.

This bag is a good value for a basic bat bag, as it is laid out better than most basic bags. I would prefer to have spent more to get the same size bag with more organization. But for most players, this bag will do the job. It wouldn't be fair to rate it a 3 out of 5 stars because it is a good value. But if I were to rate it on only it's merits, I would rate it a solid 3 starts.

product_title: Bowflex Max Trainer M5
review_body:
I bought the M5 back in September 2014. It only took me about a week to get mine but due to demand I guess a lot of people are having to wait a lot longer. Is it worth the wait? Let's dive in. I'm going to be completely honest so bear with me. The machine arrived and I assembled this beast by myself. Some people are having a really difficult time putting it together, others are having no trouble. The machine is assembled with hex screws and hex wrenches (supplied). If you have a drill with a hex attachment it would make assembly MUCH easier. I didn't so I used the supplied hex wrenches and it wasn't difficult just very time consuming. About two hour time consuming if you're doing it by hand. But assembled it was and time to hop on.

I hopped on the max trainer and the movement is fluid and pleasant to perform. Then I did the assessment and that alone kicked my butt. Then I decided to do the max workout on level one. I made it three minutes and had to quit. This machine is NO JOKE. If you're as out of shape as me then this machine will destroy you in no time. After a few days I started playing around with the various programs and decided that honestly, I got the best and most pleasant workout just by getting on the machine and pressing start and doing a manual workout. The varied workouts are great but I like being in control. On the manual workout I can adjust the resistance during any time of my workout. I now usually do a whole fifteen minutes on the highest level (16). I vary the speed and usually burn about 250 calories in 15 minutes. I do this twice a day. Once in the morning and once at night for a total of 500 calories burned per day. I usually do three days a week, if I feel like it I do four or five days.

After about three months I went back to the max routine and I blew through the whole 14 max workout on level one with no problem. I still burn more calories in manual mode so I've stuck with that. Other things to note, the machine is sturdy. Built like a tank. The electronics are first class all the way. It comes with a chest strap heart rate monitor but I've only used it once. It's just easier for me to place my hands on the built in heart monitor to see where I'm at. It also has an app you can download and sync to the machine but I have yet to do so. I don't need an app to tell me if I've done well or slacked off. I'm sure many people would find it useful. You can also put a water bottle in the back of the console but I've not used that either. I have never had time to read or sip water while on this machine. The machine is heavy but easy to move with the attached wheels. It's also very small and takes up minimal space. It's roughly two feet wide, four feet long, and five feet high.
It's also quiet in motion. Going full steam it's about as loud as a window air conditioner. I live in an apartment and none of my neighbors have complained about noise.

And now, there are a few negatives that fortunately I have not experienced. A lot of customers have complained of squeaky wheels. My advice is to contact Bowflex customer service and from what I've heard they have been able to resolve this issue. I guess I got lucky, I've had my machine for six months now and I've noticed no squeaking. Another negative is that people are scared it might be too hard and they're right. This thing is a monster. If you're like me and the max workout proved too difficult than just do the manual workout instead. Stamina and strength will come with time. It did with me...and very quickly.

And now for the honesty part...have I lost weight? When I got my M5 I was 203lbs and I'm only 5'7. Six months later I'm at 183 so I've dropped 20lbs. as I wrote...I'll be honest... I LOVE food!! I love cake, cookies, chips, chocolate, beer, vodka. At 40 years old it really is a battle. I've also accepted that I'm not going to give up all the things I love for a six pack. Not happening, sorry. I try and eat wellSun - Thursday with salads and no junk food but come Friday and Saturday...forget it! Bring on the brews, the pizza and anything else I can get my hands on. I try my best not to cheat during the week but it does happen. My goal is to get back down to 160. I'll get there. It took me thirty years to put on 50lbs. I was 210 at my heaviest. I'm about halfway there and it's only been six months so I'm pretty happy. I expected to be back to 160 in about three months. I think that goal was a tad unrealistic especially with the holidays being only a few months after I got the machine.

I'll update any pros or cons as time goes by or when I finally reach my goal body. My final thoughts are this. The Max Trainer is as beautiful as it is functional. It will kick your butt if you want it or you can take a leisurely little hike on it if that is what you're after. With a ton of programs and a manual one you won't get bored with it either. Half a year later I'm still thrilled with my purchase. Unfortunately there isn't any way to test the Max before you buy it but if you don't like it you can return it. (Check with Bowflex, I don't know the return policy off the top of my head.) I've also noticed that my bad feet and knees are not impacted negatively by the Max. So, there you go. This thing is a low impact calorie torch. Built well and is as nice to look at as it is to work out on it.
Recommended.

product_title: Pistol Metal Snap Caps 380Auto 5pk
review_headline: These Snap Caps are useful in working with a Taurus 380
review_body:
These Snap Caps are useful in working with a Taurus 380. They do cycle through the pistol and give you some insight into the operation of the pistol. I was pleased to see that these did actually load and eject. The plastic ones that I have tried did not. Those often got hung up in the pistol. I think the problem of those was due to the extra friction of the plastic nose compared to the metal nose of these simulated cartridges.
At the shooting range, the Taurus fed the actual cartidges without a hitch. It fed jacket rounds and jacketed hollow points with no hiccups. That surprised me because of the difficulties with plastic Snap Caps.

product_title: DGA Mach 2 Disc Golf Basket – Portable Heavy-Duty Outdoor Galvanized Steel Disc Golf Target
review_headline: This DGA Mach 2 or the Disc Catcher are the best if you can afford
review_body:
I bought one of these from a guy who had his own private course but sold his home and sold 18 of these for half price. That was ten years ago. With my Golden Retriever "Amber" we are in the backyard several times a day with a dozen discs to practice putts. Unless you have 300'plus distance use this basket for putting practice. I you are serious about really better play and fairly consistent winning putting 50 plus times most days over a couple years and 10 out of 10 putts will go in from about 35'. It is rare I can't get my "up" within 30', any drives within 30 to 40' means tournament wins if you can putt decently. It is long and complicated but in short good putts mean doing the same thing absolutely everytime with a chance to literally aim during the motion of putting when you hand passes in front of your eyes. Stand sideways with disc in hand and hand directly in front of disc toward basket. To "fire" the putt hold hand out and pull back SLOWLY to waste then quickly always with hand PULLING IN FRONT OF DISC TOWARD BASKET. Always hold disc level, few do, or slightly tilted down toward basket. Slow back and with speed fire LEVEL disc toward basket through the line of your eye and basket with wrist roll and out in front of released disc rolling from elbow down to hand so it "feels" like your throwing over your palm UP hand at release. When you get tired you will start with your hand too low and bad habits will creep in and wreck your putts. Absolute consistency repeated over every time or it all goes away and the "muscle memory" is ruined. Any tiny deviation in your putt should be tried at least a thousand times and clearly understood why it benefits and not because it "works" temporarily. If you understand what I just wrote you have a large portion of what at least a million putts have taught me. And you still need the basket to make the putt consistently yours.
Tomorrow I play doubles in our weekly game for 16yrs.
Happy Trails

product_title: BottleBand
review_headline: Helps keep water bottles at hand on walks, hikes or runs.
review_body:
The bottle band is a great tool to help those active individuals carry water with them without extra effort.

The bottle band is a thick elastic band that attaches at the top and bottom of a bottle. It allows for minimal effort in holding a multitude of bottle sizes while you walk, run or hike. I like this band because when you have to hold onto your water bottle when walking, hiking or running you have to switch hands back and forth because keeping a tight grip around a wide diameter bottle that is wet takes a lot of hand strength. After walking your hands feels like they got more of a workout than you did. I think that this band is perfect for those who keep active but have arthritis problems that may limit their hand strength.

I usually carry more water than I think I need so the containers start to get quite large. This bottle band will fit around large Nalgene bottles, the max I have tested is 1.5 liter bottles but the band is limited by bottle diameter not the weight/volume of the container. I tested the minimum sized bottle this could carry and I would say that the 16.9 ounce water bottle is about the smallest you can fit which is not bad. I like that I can carry Gatorade, Powerade or water bottles than are readily available at conveinence stores or reusable bottles if I want.

One use that I found was that this band is great for holding grocery bags. I just slip one end around my wrist/forearm slide the bottle band through the plastic bag handles and then slide the other end around my wrist. I can carry many bags and have my hands free. This is not what the bottle band is intended for but I think this is a great alternative use for the bottle band. I like that the bottle band comes in different colors and has some great wording on the product.

I would recommend that if you have problems with carrying your water (or are just tired of doing so) with you on walks, runs or hikes you should consider buying the bottle band. It helps you keep water with you without requiring extra effort on your part.

The fit and finish rival most of my center fire rifles. The bluing is excellent and the woodwork is out of the park. The most important thing of course is accuracy. After zeroing my optic, this air rifle has proven itself a tack driver out to 25+ yards! It has also worked very well for varmits. It will drop a squirrel in it's tracks with a well placed shot every time. The only drawback(s) is the weight. It's pretty heavy to tote around in the woods all day and there's really no place to attach a sling to alleviate the weight/carry issue. That being said, the quality of this English made rifle make it an one you can hand down to your kids.

product_title: Ultra-bright LED Frisbee Multi Colored Fiber-optic Array Illuminating Ultimate Flying Disc
review_headline: Awesome frisbee that can be used in the dark! Many flashing different colors! Great for any age!
review_body:
So when i received this frisbee the first thing i wanted to do was go pass it around with some friends, but it was still day time. Later on a couple friends a i went to a dark field with no lights so we could see how bright it really was. When we got there and started throwing this frisbee around it was incredible. I could be on the opposite side of the field and still clearly be able to see it. The light was just so bright. We had so much fun throwing it around barely being able to see anything but we could see the light of the frisbee. The way the colors flash is pretty cool, they flash slow and sometimes they flash fast. At first i thought it would only display a couple of colors but then i realized it has a wide range of colors that are display.

The battery is underneath in the middle of the frisbee, it being there doesn't change anything from a normal frisbee. It is still light weight, and doesn't effect how it flies. The only difference that is noticed is that it makes a faint whistle sound when flying around. Its great too because the battery is changeable so when it goes out you can replace it and not worry about it never lighting up again. Where the battery is located is also where the lights are, but throughout the frisbee are 5 fiber optic wires so that the colors go to the edge of the frisbee, and this helps the frisbee look like it is lit up much brighter, it helps to see light throughout the entire frisbee.

Overall i think this is one really cool frisbee, and is great for playing with at night when you can't throw a normal frisbee around. Anyone can play with a frisbee, kids, college students, and even adults. I would and definitely will recommend this product to everyone. I especially recommend this to parents to buy as a gift for there kids because they will definitely love it.

product_title: Mio FUSE Heart Rate Training + Activity Tracker
review_body: I'm actually reviewing two different things here:  The Mio Fuse and the Mio Go iphone app. The Mio Fuse is great!  I love it. The Mio Go app can go suck it.  First of all, I'll clarify something.  I bought this mainly as a heart rate chest strap monitor replacement.  The activity tracking is less important to me.    The Fuse as a heart rate monitor: It's comfortable.  It's accurate.  I think it's kinda cool looking.  It's a bit bigger and more serious looking than a Fitbit Flex, but doesn't look like it's trying to be something it's not (think smart watch).  Normally, I wear it loose.  It's still secure.  When I go for a run I cinch it down and put it into heart rate mode.  It grabs my heart rate in under a minute and keeps it.  Tap it again and you're in workout mode.  Even when my heart rate is at max (185 bpm for me) it's got a reliable reading.  Bouncing around while mountain biking, it's got my heart rate.  Shower?  Yep.  Pool?  Yep.  Try that, Basis/Fitbit!  Neither of those ever could hold my heart rate when I was running really hard.  I even shaved a patch on my wrist so they could get a better view to no avail.  Psshhh...  Activity Tracking: The step counting is a tad low, but mostly accurate.  I've compared against my iPhone and a Fitbit Flex.  It reads distance a bit off as well, but what can you expect from a wrist based activity tracker.  You enter your height into the Mio Go app and it figures out your distance according to an averaged stride length I guess.  Well, my running stride is longer than my walking stride.  The distance calculation when walking is spot on (verified against Google Maps/Earth) however when I run it falls behind.  I use Endomondo to track my runs anyway.  No biggy.  The calorie burn calculation SUCKS!  I don't know if this is due to the Mio Go app or what.  According to this thing, some days I'd be dead.  I don't even get up to my Base Metabolic Rate!  The only good thing I can think of to say about caloric burn is that it's consistent.  Now, the Mio Go app.  Simply, it's a POS. 1)  The interface sucks.  It's cludgy.  No good graphs to compare your workouts, steps, distance, caloric burn over time...  NONE!  Mio please take a look at Apple Health, Fitbit, Withings... 2)  The distance calculation is WAY OFF in the app.  Let's say I start heart rate mode on the Fuse then I start a work out in the Mio Go app (you can start a workout on the Fuse OR in the app. Handy).  I'll enable GPS in the Mio Go and go for a run.  The other day I ran 6 miles.  Endomondo said I ran 6 miles.  Google Earth (I plotted it) said I did 6 miles.  Mio Go...  5.46 miles.  WTF  Another day I did a 5 mile run.  Endomondo and Google both are spot on.  Mio Go said 4.59...  using GPS!  On the same device as Mio Go!  I looked at the map in Mio Go and compared to Endomondo and Google.  It's exactly the same.  Mio must count miles differently than the rest of the world.  I took my dog for a walk the other day.  I started a workout on the Fuse AND in Mio Go.  I walked 2 miles exactly.  The Fuse reported 2.02 miles.  Mio Go reported 1.86.  Gawd.  FIX IT, Mio!  Unacceptable. 3)  It counts calories VERY low.  It regularly comes in several hundred calories behind Endomondo for single work outs and thousands of calories low daily compared to Fitbit.  Some days I don't even get up to my Base Metabolic Rate.  Guess I'm dead, then? 4)  I wish I had more control.  I wish I could edit my workouts (fixing time/distance).  I wish I had more choices for workout type (weights, treadmill, snowshoeing).  I wish I could edit my walking/running stride length.  I wish that I could set my goal for total calories or maybe just do away with the goal completely.  I wish I could enter a Base Metabolic Rate to assist it in the caloric burn calculation.  Final thoughts...  I love the Fuse.  I hate the app.  I hope they read Internet reviews and fix fix fix.  I hope they re-work the interface.  If they do, they'll have a stellar product.  For now, an awesome hardware product is hampered by horrible software.

product_title: Spyderco Endura4 Lightweight FRN Flat Ground PlainEdge Knife
review_body:
I won't get into the specs of the knife since that's been reviewed at least 60 million times by now but here's my thoughts on the knife.. I recently retired the tenacious I'd been carrying for over 2 years and decided to step up to the endura 4. I'll be honest, at first I wasn't too sure.. Don't get me wrong it was an excellent and well made knife but when you've been carrying something else for so long it takes a while for your hand to adjust to the feel of a new knife. The handle is noticeably thinner, I wasn't used to having the finger grips, and it definitely doesn't deploy as fast as the tenacious. Having said that, it's been about 3 weeks now and this knife is just awesome. I'm used to the feel of it now and it fits my hand like a glove. On top of that the deployment is much faster and smoother after breaking in. So be aware, if you've been carrying something else a long time you're going to have to give yourself a few weeks to adjust to this one but it's well worth giving it a shot.

A lot of the reviews talk about the stiff deployment and being hard to close one handed. This is simply not the case for me. I loosened the pivot pin just barley, and opened the knife a lot to break it in and it flies out as smooth as butter. Closing it is also very easy to do one handed with a little practice so I think a lot of these people just haven't carried the knife long enough to figure it out.

The nicest thing about this knife is the blade steel. It came razor sharp and after 3 weeks it still shaves hair. I've used it mostly to open boxes at work and cut up fish for bait as well as skinning several catfish and still haven't actually sharpened this knife. It will lose the ability to shave hair but will still have a nice working edge, and a few swipes on the finest stone of my sharp-maker and it's back to shaving again. That's all I've had to do. I can promise you a lesser steel would've required a complete resharpining by now after cutting through fish bones. Also I've gotten it wet plenty of times and have had zero issues with rust. The size, edge retention, and rust resistance have made this knife an ideal fishing companion.

This knife is a big a folder.. Everyone knows that. I personally prefer big folders due to my job, outdoor hobbies, and living on a farm but be aware, if you don't like a large manly man knife then this is not for you.

The only con I can think of is that I had scratches on the pocket clip the very first day so I went ahead and sanded all the black paint off of it and I think it looks even better that way. This isn't really a hit on the knife just something to keep in mind.

Overall this is just one awesome edc knife and I've owned just about every brand. It deploys fast, locks up tight, feels great in the hand, has the size to tackle just about any job, holds an edge very well, and offers multiple carry options.. The list goes on. review_headline: This ball is torture!!! DO NOT BUY if you want to preserve your brain cells.

The plastic blue hose frequently detaches itself from the pump and creates the most annoying high pitch concentrated sound you can ever hear - I think that is how demons cry in the seventh circle of hell.
That is not all... the hose has a white nozzle to go into the ball that is not very tight and as the ball gets fuller, you can hear air escaping it... it may come lose and create an even more annoying cringing sound that I am pretty sure is how the demon boss of hell cries for help trying to inflate this ball.
Overall... I may only keep this because the half-ball is more expensive on its own on Amazon than the bundle.

product_title: Striiv Touch, Black
review_headline: Probably not for the fitness hero
review_body:
Let's just begin with the fact that I didn't have high expectations for this product to begin with. I'm moving up from inaccurate and unreliable, dedicated pedometers. This product is definitely better than anything else I've had. Also, I knew going in that I would not get a Ferrari for the price of a Saturn. (The band was on sale when I purchased it.)

I'm not a fitness pro; just trying to transition slowly from decades of the couch potato lifestyle. But, I need incentive. My phone can track steps, but even I'm not geeky enough to rock a phablet strapped to my arm all the time. Touch gives me freedom from my phone, without missing important calls or texts - love the optional notifications feature. Step accuracy? Not the greatest, I'm sure, but I just need a ballpark figure for encouragement. It syncs with My Fitness Pal on my Android phone, which is pure entertainment!

Pros:
Syncing with other apps
Notification toggling
Display toggling (display can be flipped, so no worries about how to put it on)
Tracks stairs
Cost efficient geek fitness toy
Manual toggle for sleep monitoring (don't trust auto tracking)

Cons:
Setting up sync to MFP can be a challenge if not approached with sense of adventure (and humor)
Step tracking not much better than other low end gadgets I've tried
Manual toggle for sleep tracking (I don't trust auto tracking, but it would be nice if I could!)

review_headline: Secure Case with Small Design Issues
review_body:
The case itself seems quality enough, but the unit I received already had cracks on the closing latches. It latches and stays closed just fine, but I'm also a little more careful with it because of the defects. In terms of holding cartridges, it works great. As others have mentioned, you have to load 9mm (and I'd imagine .380) primer-side down or else you will have wobbly and messy rows of cartridges. Flat-point or hollow-point projectiles actually balance a little better and can be seated nose-down, but still don't stay perfectly straight.

It is also a little difficult to extract cartridges from their places when the case is full as the spacing is tight and you have to grab the cartridges by the rounded top of the projectile. Making it even more difficult, the rearward sides of the case actually rise to meet the rear hinge, meaning grabbing cartridges from the rear edges is quite difficult without first clearing out cartridges from the adjacent rows. These are nit-picky critiques but I think it's worth mentioning.

Not sure why everyone rates this knife so highly. I have about 18 knives, from Chinese Kershaws to Black Class Benchmades. I purchased this knife to take to Costa Rica on vacation. I wanted a cheap knife in case it was lost or confiscated. I think the cons outweigh the pros and I agree there are better knives with similar characteristics.

The Pro's
- Its inexpensive
- Great carry size for EDC light duty
- Multi-functional (it's not a leatherman, but the tools it does have work well)
- The cheap Chinese steel does well for this price point

The Cons
- The knife was difficult to open when I received it, nearly to the point I had to use something to pry it open. I disassembled it and oiled it up. This helped a bit but its still difficult to open compared to other Kershaws I have.
- The bottle opener can digs into your hands and gets caught in your pocket
- The screwdriver sticks way above the "deep carry" clip making it more conspicuous.

product_title: Smith & Wesson 327 TRR8 CO2 BB Revolver, Black
review_headline: Realistic looking with heavy all metal construction and Smith & Wesson logos makes for a great co2 revolver.
review_body: I have a small collection of BB guns and I wanted to get a revolver. I considered the Colts and Dan Wessons and decided for the price this would be a good choice. I was right, it's fun to shoot, accurate and realistic. The rear sight is adjustable for elevation and windage and there are fiber optic rods in both front and rear sights. I used the rails for a flashlight and red dot just to see how crazy I could make it look, I should have taken a picture, it was a bit much. I decided to go in the other direction and remove the top rail. The instructions tell you how to install it but it comes installed on the gun. It has a pin that can be pushed out easily with a 1/16" pin punch or the blunt tip of a drill bit. When the screw through the top of the rear sight is removed be aware there is a small compression spring pushing it up, don't let it get away. Use a 1.5 mm hex key to loosen  two set screws on the top of the rail before the rail will slide off to the rear, they will leave barely noticeable marks on the top of the barrel. I think the gun looks much better without the top rail. Other good features are the box it comes in and the speed loader.

review_headline: Exceptional flexible running gloves for cool weather, great moisture-wicking properties, light and soft
review_body:
These are very exceptional running gloves. They are made of a mixture of nylon, polyester, and spandex which have an effective moisture-wicking effect, perfect for the occasion while you're exercising, whether in colder weather or whether it's mild. The material is lightweight and flexible which does not prevent your hands from losing any dexterity or mobility when you have them on. I was impressed how nice and unrestricted I felt when I put them on. I ordered a Medium, and the size is as expected and even stretches to fit (due to the spandex factor) for those with hands that are in between sizes.

I like the cuffs on the gloves so they don't slip off when you're waving your arms and hands around, and I especially like the combination of bright neon pink and black. The bright pink mesh serves to outline the black of your fingers and gives it a splash of an otherwise dark color. I recommend these light weight gloves for running on cool days, but I don't suggest using these gloves as exclusive cold-weather gear, as it is not really made for that. Overall, the workmanship and the quality of these gloves are exceptional. I received these gloves at a discount in exchange for my honest and unbiased review.

product_title: Exerpeutic Folding Magnetic Upright Bike with Pulse
review_body:
I really liked this bike at first; however, with time, it is proving to be of shoddy construction.

When I first received the bike, one of the connectors holding the two plastic pieces around the spinning belt was broken. This caused the two plastic pieces to come apart slightly, but it was too much work to return the bike to Amazon over what I deemed to be a cosmetic flaw.

After about 6 months of non-regular use (1-2 times per week), one of the pedals started to become wobbly. I got a wrench, tightened up the screw and started riding again, but within 5 minutes, the pedal was wobbly again. Now, no matter how tightly I screw on the pedal, it always becomes wobbly after about 5 minutes or less of use. I investigated the pedal and it appears that the hole in the pedal does not fit correctly onto the axle, which causes the act of moving the pedal to loosen the screw and cause the pedal to become wobbly.

product_title: Mueller Quick Shot Rifle Scope
review_body:
I originally ordered this for a shotgun but found it made the weapon hard to use so I shelved it for about 4 months. In January I purchased a DDM4V11 and put some Mbus Pro sights on it, and called it finished. So just outa curiosity I placed the Quick Shot on it and what do know Perfect co witness..........

Overall build quality is about an 8/10, I've seen much better from companies like Vortex but those are $160+ this was $99. The brightness has to be maxed out for daytime use and the small Dots are almost impossible to see however the "kobra" type sight with the small dot and a "T" around it is in my opinion the best option. the next is the "holo" type sight which is okay but not as accurate in my opinion due to its size and amount of space in the middle.

Now on to the reason I only gave it 4 stars, the battery life is sub-par it lasts two weeks while turned on all the time cause from what I've seen there is no off switch and the only way I've found to make it last that long is turn it down while not in use. This is a great sight for $99 probably the best for this price, mine has taken 300 rounds of 12 Gauge and around 600+ rounds of 5.56 and still going strong.

Though back to the battery life I've used the 2 it came with and bought some Duracell Lithium Medical Battery, 3V, 2032, 6/Pack on prime right here on amazon for around $8.50 is my personal favorite, they are medical grade batteries and last a little longer.

After all its been through I'm still happy with it, a decent alternative till I can afford an AimPoint.

product_title: Snugpak Special Forces Bivvi Bag
review_headline: Fine lightweight backup bivy; however this is a poor choice for tall users and there are much less expensive alternatives.
review_body:
Beware tall users! This is advertised as 220 cm in length (86.6"); however, this is laying flat (as pictured). In order for this to work as a true bivy you have to cinch down the cord that runs around the inside of the bivy's hood. This dramatically reduces the interior length, so much so that my long length mountain hardwear sleeping bag is longer than the bivy sack when the hood is cinched down. Therefore I am unable to use the bivy sack as it is intended with the cord cinched down around my head and sleeping bag hood (think how a mummy bag cinches around your face). Instead the entire top of my sleeping bag is left unprotected. This would be fine if I was using the bivy in a tent, but I purchased the bivy to allow me to sleep outdoors while providing at least moderate protection from moisture and rain. The restricted length makes this impractical. I also don't like how thin and fragile the material is. I understand that this is necessary to achieve the bivy's light weight, but a ground sheet will be required to prevent sharp rocks and sticks from cutting or rubbing through the thin bivy.

Instead I find myself using my MSS woodland camo bivy (a full pound heavier) which I intended to replace with this lightweight alternative. The MSS bivy provides plenty of extra length so that I can fit excess gear or clothing that I want to keep dry down by my feet. In addition, the MSS bivy's gore tex fabric breathes better and is far more robust. I find there is less condensation in the MSS bivy after a night's sleep, even with the MSS fully closed and the snugpak wide open at the head. Finally, a brand new MSS bivy can be found for one third the price of this bivy. The one pound weight savings is outweighed in my mind by the benefits of the added length, durability, and comfort of my MSS bivy.

Final Thoughts: This is great as a lightweight emergency cover for your sleeping bag (if you're 6'00" or under); however for regular use there are better options out there (check out the MSS bivy which can be purchased new for one third the price).

product_title: Musashi - Bamboo Full Tang High Carbon Steel Katana
review_headline: Minimal damage under the guard after testing, it was an easy fix though with some hot glue. Good sword overall.
review_body:
Hello. I'm anonymous.
I bought this sword a few days ago and happened to conveniently get it a few days later, a mere exact timing that was given.
It came in a big 3 foot long box, so you would kind of 'obviously' perceive what it is. Especially if it noted "Marshall Arts" on the company stamp.Of course, this was not a real big deal to me as I bought this for myself.
As stated by other review[s], it slices through household objects easily, such as cardboard, and water bottles too.]

When I first got it, it definitely had a bit of a dull edge on it; it was easy to tell that it was made in a factory. Some parts of the blade's edge was very sharp, others were very dull. Still, even without sharpening it, it managed to decapitate a poor innocent water bottle.
The sword itself is very ornate, measuring 3 feet. The bottom of it did happen to snap off with my first swing at a brick wall [on accident], but with some hot-glue it was in marvelous shape once again.
Speaking of hot glue, the cotton-ish raveling past the guard is hot glued on for mere decor, and doesn't take much of a beating to get something loose down there. Again, hot glue does the trick very well.
Aside from minimal damage after a few water bottle beat-downs near the bottom past the guard, it held very well.

PS: The blade was very oily when I got it and dull too. We're going to give it a sharper edge and a little bit of cleaning on the blade, and the thing would be as good as a semi-professional training blade.

Best regards,
An Amazon Customer.

Had this nasty little trait occurred while I was carrying in public, I probably would have lost my magazine and been left defenseless.

product_title: Fixed Legs Meditation Bench Premium Ultra-Light 3 Sizes Many Colors Made in USA
review_headline: Not Flexible? Over 5' 8''? Get the size Large
review_body:
I order the medium bench based on my height. However, I am not very flexible, which made the size medium uncomfortable at my ankle joints. For this reason, I should have order the Large bench. I called the seller directly from the phone number provided on their website "Joy is within you" and spoke with the gentleman who actually makes the benches by hand. He was very helpful and actually offered to make me a customized bench! I just received it yesterday and it's perfect. The size large probably would have been fine too. If you are over 5' 8'' and not flexible, I would recommend that you get the size large bench. Here are some other things that made my ankles more comfortable on the bench:

1) Roll up a towel and put it under your ankle joints for support, or...
2) Angle your toes slightly inward, so that your toes slightly overlap but your heals remain distant, or...
3) Sit with your feet parallel and develop some flexibility in those ankle joints!
4) Put some form of padding beneath your knee's (obviously not an ankle issue, but still)

Initially I wanted a bench that folded (for convenience) but am now glad that I got this one instead. I can focus on my meditation and not wonder if the bench is going to collapse beneath me if I move the wrong way.

Lastly, they have some free instructional videos on their "Joy is Within You" website. I found these to be helpful as well.

product_title: ALPEN Shasta Ridge Waterproof Fogproof Binoculars. Fully Multi-Coated with BAK4 High Index Silver Metallic Coated Optics and Long Eye Relief. Model 381SR 8x30 featurers a Super Close interpupillary distance (IPD).
review_body:
In a rare show of restraint, I forced my self to go for the Alpen Shasta Ridge binoculars instead of some more expensive version made by a bigger manufacturer with wider distribution and more advertising. These are at or near to the lowest price point for entry level, high-quality 10X42 binoculars, but, in my opinion, are easily comparable if not superior to most of the analogous models made by manufacturers like Vortex, Bushnell, and others. If you want to split hairs about extremely high degrees of clarity, then you should be looking at $400+ binoculars.

I bought these to hunt, watch birds, and take to baseball games, and I couldn't be more pleased. Just got back from Spring Training in Mesa, AZ, and they enhanced my experience hugely. I'm not an optics expert, but I have good vision, and these things have beyond sufficient clarity, even in low-light conditions. The fit and finish is great, the rubberized coating feels great in my hands, the camo pattern looks awesome, their weight is competitive for the price class, and the warranty guarantees free lifetime repair or replacement of the original binoculars for defect or damage of any kind if you return them (so, not if you lose them)--all for $50 less than the competition.

There are higher-clarity 10X42's on the market, but not for anywhere near this price, and frankly, if I miss any animals with them, it will be my fault, not the binoculars'.

product_title: Windy Thai Style Training Gloves
review_headline: pros & cons, very detailed and informative review/breakdown
review_body: Absolutley love these. I have the natural leather (brown) color and it is absolutley gorgeous! The leather quality is top top notch! It is supple and smoothe and even after 2 months of hard training still has that fresh leather smell. The stitching is very consitant through out, the liner is comfortable but absorbs and retain alot of sweat however not a huge deal because of the cuff being naturally circular they air out almost automatically just leave them out for a few minutes and they will be good. Speaking about the cuff, it has very good padding for if you have to block hi kicks or if you shell up and I must say the wrist support it leaps and bounds over any other thai glove ive ever worn, which was always my gripe with thai gloves (I have weak wrists). The most important part of the gloves and actually the best part of the gloves are the padding. The padding is excellent it absorbs very hard punches, and intense bag work with no hand pains what so ever. Also you can make a very good fist with these for a thai glove (traditional boxing style gloves tend to greatley excel over thai gloves in this category due to design, no open palm and thumb placement allowing you to make a perfect and proper fist everytime, provided that they are quality gloves). Now the only reason that I did not give these gloves 5 stars are becasue of stiffness and break in period as well as pinching. When ypu first get these gloves they are rock hard stiff! I DO NOT suggest you spar with these right out of the box because you will hurt your partner. Due to the stifness and rigidity of the gloves as well as the hard padding. Now because they are so stiff at firts you will notice that your fingertips will be pinched and it will be uncomfortable especially and mostly your thumb. This actually made me hate the gloves at first but after a round or two on the bag I stoped feeling it (or just didnt focus on it and forgot about it). How ever those negatives go away once the gloves break in becausethey break in so well almost like they were custom made for your hand! Only problems is that this takes awhile. While most gloves only need about 20 rounds of proper and intense heavy bag work to break in (roughly 3 days to 1 weeks depending on how you train) these took about 33 rounds of proper and intense heavy bag work to break in (just over 2 weeks for me) wich is considered extinsive. I feel like the break in period is worth it because they feel so amazing once broken in but c'mon that has to be a design flaw, I know windys are built tough to last but 2 weeks of consistent bag work is a little too much for a break in period. But again like I said once broken in they feel like they were made just for you and are as comfortable as wearing clouds on your hands (oh yeah i forgot to meantion that I have the 16oz pair and they feel pretty light which I like but thats personal preference).  If they wouldnt have broken in so well I would have rated them 2-3 stars because they would have lacked heavily in comfort but this is not the case. I personally use these gloves for sparring and seldomly for mitt work, but while occasionally using them for some very light bag work just to break in the padding a little more and make it softer (I have actuall bag gloves for bag/pad work so again this is just personal preference and you wont have to do that if you dont wish to do so). I would say that these are an excellent sparring glove at 16oz and would make a decent-good bag/mitt/pad glove at 10 oz -12oz (depending on your weight and hand size would decide the size ie. Heavier with larger hands=12oz, lighter with small/regular size hands=10oz). But if you are person that can only have one pair of gloves or prefers to only have one pair of gloves than the 16oz pair also make a great pair of "work-horse" gloves. All in all great pair of gloves, high quality, built to last, great construction and made by a brand that is trusted among fighters, if you can deal with the stifness and pinching in during the break in period than you should totallt buy these gloves. I hope you enjoyed this review I know it was very long but I hope you found it informative. Good luck, train hard, have fun and never give up. Oss!
