product_title: Rubber-Cal Tuff-N-Lastic Rubber Flooring Runners
review_headline: Great Product But Not Sure About Rubber Cal's Customer Service
review_body:
Originally I contacted Rubber Cal directly and had them send a couple different samples so I could choose the best for my application. I build and maintain props for my daughters dance studio. We have two 2' x 11' wooden ramps that are part of a stage production set. Dancers were slipping on the painted plywood surface in tap shoes (including my daughter) and I needed a safer surface ASAP.

I ordered 15' x 4' of this material on their web site and two days later, received an email stating they are out of it and will be 12 weeks or so before they have more. I was not happy that it took two days to let me know they were out . I starting searching for similar on the web and what do you know, Amazon had a bunch of it. Not something similar but Rubber Cal's material I attempted to purchase. Apparently they sent it all to Amazon. What I don't get, why didn't Rubber Cal advise me to check Amazon to solve my time sensitive problem and retain me as a customer for future purchases?

Ok, now I have the product at home, out of the box and breathing because it does stink like a tire factory. I needed to glue to the plywood ramps so I tested a sample piece with Gorilla glue. It seemed to hold so I proceeded to spread it all over one of the ramps and placed the rubber over top. I put all kinds of heavy object on top of the rubber while the glue was setting and activated with water like you are supposed to. I use wood glues and Gorilla glue all of the time in my workshop.

Two days later I removed all of the hold down objects and tested by gently pulling the edge of the rubber to see how effective the hold was. The entire sheet pulled right up. Yes, I have a heated workshop and plenty warm. I called Rubber Cal and asked for glue advice. They sell a two gallon structural poly urethane adhesive for $125 plus shipping (I live way on the other side of the country from CA.). I asked them to advise on something similar I could get locally right away and not break the bank. They had no advice, kind of disheartening.

Anyway, I bought some acrylic rubber gym floor adhesive from my local flooring supplier and it seems to be holding but I'm not confident it will hold forever. The rubber product itself is very nice, just can’t get anything to stick to it well.

product_title: VT Airsoft Valor Target / All-in-one Professional Shooting Target & BB Trap
review_body: This is so much better than the homemade cardboard traps I had been using for airsoft. Cardboard was always very noisy, where I don't hear impact on the Valor Target at all. The target absorbs airsoft bb's and the only sign is the hole appearing on the paper. It's so stable, I use the box that it came in as an improvised stand and it doesn't budge no matter how many full-auto bb's @ 450+ fps I put in it (and from only 15ft away). The trap uses simple but ingenious fiber-strands (sort of like an industrial mop head) to stop the bb's without damage - wonderful to be able to recycle bb's (before you can reload the used bb's you do have to rub or blow off little bits of the fibers and remove those few bb's that hit the interior walls and broke apart). Would definitely recommend some sort of extended backstop (e.g. big sheet of cardboard) if you're using indoors, just in case you miss the target completely (it happens, and I have the dents in the wall to prove it), and if you hit the hard edges, bb's will break and ricochet, so of course wear eye protection.  Have not tried it with paintball training rounds or used the dart-board, which is smaller and much lower quality that a real bristle board (which cost more than this target), but arguably better than the cheapest of toy-store dart boards. I'm only using this for airsoft, and it's proven to be perfect for my needs.

I gave it five stars because it works perfectly well for her to practice on, it has Velcro along the side so she can attach the two mats together to enlarge the surface area, it's easy to take them apart when finished, folds up in a jiffy, and she can use the handles to easily put them away when finished.

Never content to simply see an item as we adults would see it, she and her little friends have cavorted and tumbled for hours on end on these mats, then used them for sleepover mats, made play forts with them and even tents! Who knows what their creative minds will think up next?

product_title: Tactical Tailor Fight Light Magna Double Pistol Mag Pouch
review_body:
Despite reviews to the contrary these DO fit Glock magazines, and the rare earth magnets will hold the Glock mags in place due to the steel lining in Glock magazines. I have two pairs of these and use one set on my plate carrier everyday at work. No problems and I like how you can cover the magazines with the velcro strap when immediate access is not a priority. The pull tab on the velcro strap makes it quick and easy to get to the magazine when the need arises, or you can remove the strap ahead of time and rely on the strong magnets to hold the magazines in place (which they do). I've placed two loaded Glock 17 magazines into these pouches, turned my carrier upside down, and shaken it and the mags did not fall out with only the magnets holding the mags in. The durability has also proven fantastic as they have stood up to tremendous abuse both while wearing my plate carrier and sliding around in a trunk. Its worth noting that the fit is a little tight with Glock 21 magazines; however, you can still fit them and place the velcro strap across the top.

Overall these are the best magazine pouches for a plate carrier or tactical vest.

I bought this for a few reasons, (1) I live in a tiny NY apartment and don't have a lot of room for any large equipment, (2) it's been a rough winter so I haven't been able to go out for runs/walks, and (3) the cost of a gym membership here is obscene. I really like this product. As some of the others noted, it takes a bit to get used to the short stride but I haven't found it to be a problem after the first couple of minutes I was on the machine. I also like the fact that you can change up the tension as well. It was super easy to put together and it is light enough to move to a corner or under a table to get it out of the way each morning.

There are only two downsides in my opinion. First, when using it sitting down, you really have to be sitting at a precise height. Otherwise it will be awkward to use because either the angle will be off or your shoes may rub on the back of your foot/ankle. Second, the digital readout that shows miles, steps, etc... is completely off. I have been using a fitbit for two years and have found it to be very accurate so I was surprised to see how different the calculations were on the machine. Because of that, I just use it based on time, nothing else.

Overall, I love this product. I have been using it for a few months now and have no regrets.

product_title: Cressi Comanche Speargun, Ruber Sling Spear Gun
review_headline: Fun speargun but check the crimps on the line before using
review_body: I gave this 3 stars but might possibly give it 4 stars.  I really like this speargun but there are a couple quality problems that I think Cressi should address.  First of all, the shaft was very difficult to load. It took several attempts to get it to lock in place and that is very annoying when trying to reload while in the water.  Through trial and error, I found out that if I insert the spear and then push and release the trigger quickly (flick it with my finger), it will lock in.  Another problem was the crimp was not crimped tight enough where the line attaches to the muzzle end of the gun.  After about 20 shots, the spear came off the line and I lost the spear.  It was a short fishing day that day.  I eventually bought a bungee cord (http://www.amazon.com/gp/product/B00G8IY6WQ/ref=cm_cr_ryp_prd_ttl_sol_2) and it makes it soooooo much easier to load the gun. Trying to lock the shaft in place while holding the line in place around the rear line holder is very difficult, especially with gloves on.  But, with a bungee cord, you can lock the shaft in place first and then pull the line around the rear line holder.  This is the only speargun I have ever used so I don't know what to compare it to, but overall I like it and I would probably buy it again based on price.  If you need replacement shafts, it uses 130cm shafts with the European ends.  For $56.32 (including shipping), I ordered two Coralign Tahitian Spear 6.5 mm Heat Treated Inox 17 / 7 Ph shafts from scubastore.com (http://www.scubastore.com/scuba-diving/coralign-tahitian-spear-6.5-mm-heat-treated-inox-17---7-ph/618039/p) and they fit like the original.

product_title: Viper Specter Bilingual Electronic Soft Tip Dartboard
review_body:
Fun dart game that's great for a beginner especially. The unit features 50 different games with variations and allows up to 8 players at a time. Features electronic scoring and a small booklet with directions to get you started. Mounts fairly easily on a wall and the directions provide the user with information on space needed for the correct distance each player should stand from the target. Uses either batteries (3 AA not included) or a power cord for power. Buttons on the right side control on/off, type of game, number of players, etc. and the bright score pad at the bottom does a good job of keeping score automatically.

The 6 darts (3 red, 3 blue) are plastic tipped to avoid any problems with marring a wall or other surface and extra tips are provided. Still would not want really young children nearby or playing without close supervision. Mounting screws are provided as well. The grill on the board is flexible enough that the plastic tips almost always adhere to the face. Actual metal tipped darts should not be used by the way.

Two things I did not like. The voice indicating score and next player is annoying (there is volume control to turn the voice down) and the darts really stick in the board and must be removed with a some effort. It does not take any extra effort to throw the dart and, in fact, a soft touch is preferable anyway. However, once they are in the board, they hold tightly.

But overall the unit is terrific and a nice way to learn the game.

product_title: Titan Power Rack Squat Deadlift HD Lift Cage Bench Racks stand cross fit pull up
review_headline: EASY assembly. The fit and finish of the final ...
review_body:
I bought this rack to replace an Olympic bench, squat rack, and powertower for pull ups. As an all-in-one, it fit my needs perfectly. I lift alone and as my squats pass 350lbs, the safety catches really sold me. I'm an experienced lifter with over 2500lbs in free weights and multiple weight stations in an extensive home gym I've used for the past 14 years. This is my first cage.

The review:
First of all, it shipped the day I purchased it and arrived the next day from two states away. I also bought two extra j-hooks from Titan on a separate date and again, they immediately shipped and arrived the next day. Titan ships quick. Second, assembly was a snap. The instructions suggest a two-person assembly but I did it myself without difficulty in an hour. Just remember, don't snug any of the bolts until you get the entire thing together, put in the 1 inch silver safety catches then snug the bolts. I prefer snugging the base LAST to prevent it from pulling the uprights left/right or forward/back. Otherwise, tightening the bolts without safety catches in place can pull it out of square and the safety catches don't want to slide straight through. Otherwise, EASY assembly.

The fit and finish of the final product is very good. If you spend twice as much or more you might get a better finish but in this price range, you won't find better. It's very sturdy so far and I can easily do weighted chin ups without tipping the cage. Some online reviews suggested that dropping heavy weights at the end of your set might make the cage move. I have not experienced this but mine sits on carpet and my floor is completely level. I do not have this cage bolted down and it does not come predrilled to bolt down but it hasn't moved so far. If it does, I plan to drop some 50lb sandbags on the base.

PROS: Fit and finish, sturdiness of frame, ease of assembly, PRICE, small space footprint, fast shipping, cheap extra j-hooks and dip accessory if you need one.

CONS: The weight plate posts at the rear of the frame mean that if you want to use them, you need this a good 18 to 24 inches from the wall. I don't have the space for that so I don't use them. A low horizontal post off the upright would have been preferable./>

product_title: Neewer® 3P Comfortable Waterproof Assault Pack Tactical Backpack Molle Bag (Khaki 20L)
review_headline: I am very happy with the pack
review_body: I purchased this Pack for a trip from Green Bay, Wi to Magnolia Springs, Al. I didn't want to deal with luggage at the airports so I bought this pack hoping that it would be large enough for me to pack enough for a week (planned on washing a small load of clothes). Other reviewers have complained about "loose threads" and "un-tight" seams. My pack had no seam issues and a couple of thread ends that hadn't been trimmed but a quick snip with a scissors and done.  I packed one pair of jeans, one pair of flannel lounge pants, five tee shirts, five pair of socks, five pair of boxers, toothbrush, deodorant, toothpaste, medications (had open heart surgery last Nov), camera, small hair brush, electric razor with charging stand, earbuds, eyeglasses and and ipad. I've included pics of the pack fully packed. The tape measure case adds three inches to the measurements. Fully packed the pack measured 17" tall, 12" wide, 11.5 inches from front to back and weighed 16.4 pounds. I took a total of five flights and it fit in the overhead on all of them. I was able to grab the pack and go while others had to wait because their "carry on's" were too large. I was very happy with the pack. The only issue I had was slippage with the strap buckles occasionally but that was easily solved by adjusting the strap and then doubling the strap end back through the buckle. For the price this pack would be hard to beat. Would it hold up to a serious day to day beating? I can't say but for my occasional travels and around town uses I'm sure it is going to serve me well.

product_title: #6 Opinel Carbon Steel Folding Knife w/ Beechwood Handle and Leather Sheath
review_headline: There is a good youtube review on Opinel comparison of sizes for a ...
review_body:
There is a good youtube review on Opinel comparison of sizes for a visual tutorial. This No. 6 size is the smallest size that comes with the twist ring collar lock. In person this knife is about twice the thickness of a gentlemen's 2 or three blade pocket knife but smaller than a Buck knife.

The blade is a flat grind and for a folder it is similar to one the best kitchen paring knifes you can readily find. In fact the No.6 size handle fits all four fingers comfortably (average size hands) Right out of the box it is scalpel sharp and the spine will throw a spark from a fire steel if need be.

For a first choice buy it might be better to pick the No.8 or No.9 size if you are used to fixed blade handle grips as those two handle will afford purchase for both small paws and larger ones too.

On the Opinel USA website you can still find the No.2 and No.4 sizes available and while they are so small to be considered 'novelty' knifes they are by no means chinzy. They to are razor sharp and can slice or poke quite deep. The site suggests the use as letter openers. They could be used as box openers just as easy. Only thing is on the No.2 is that the handle has just enough room for two fingers at best and the No.4 three fingers tops.

Any size smaller than the No.6 will not come with the collar ring lock due to them being so small that strenuous work/force is not practical with them. They are simply small cutting tools with no bulk in the pocket. From the No.12 on down I like them all.

product_title: Elk Ridge ER-507 Machete 17-Inch Overall
review_headline: Great when it works...otherwise, not so good
review_body: Bought one at a gunshow to see how I liked the "Woodsman Pal" blade design. Liked it a lot and the Elk Ridge is thinner metal so it's lighter to carry. Sheath was okay, fit well, plastic liner protected from blade edges. Machete needed a little sharpening but was okay. Handle is very square and painful if used much or hard but a minute with a file or sander and the rubber can be made very comfortable. Liked it so well I bought a second one to put in my truck. Used it for 20 minutes clearing a trail of cedar limbs. Cut a 2" thick vine against a tree trunk and the blade snapped cleanly about 1" from handle. Twenty minutes of light use...ouch. Gunshow dealer ("sorry it happened but I didn't make it") referred me to the manufacturer. Contacted them and left a voice mail for their customer service department. Will post results if and when I hear from them. Quality of Chinese steel seems hit or miss. Great when it works...otherwise, not so good.  A month later, after NOT hearing from them I contacted their customer service by email and got a quick response. They offered to replace it (without returning the defective one) if I paid "shipping and handling". I agreed and received a new machete that I have worked with for several hours. This one matches the first one in that it is lighter than a Woodsman Pal but does very well in the woods around my place for the trimming of limbs and low growths. I am pleased enough to put it in a truck for light tasks afield. The company did okay by me. Only way they could have done better would have been free replacement but I'm satisfied with their efforts to make it right.

product_title: Full Size Link Hylian Zelda Shield with Grip & Handle
review_headline: Good shield, be ready to repaint
review_body:
As others have mentioned, the paint job needs work. It's presentable enough if you're just going to a dimly lit halloween party, but if you are a cosplayer, you're going to want to paint it. There are just silly spillovers of paint everywhere. There's even hair embedded in one part, seriously. And the paint isn't sealed all that well, so it might wear off if you're not careful. That's fine, you're probably used to repainting everything anyway if you make costumes.

It looks pretty sturdy, looks the correct size, feels light weight, and has enough detail to feel worth it. As for the wacky strap stuff on the back, yeah, some instructions would have been nice. The handle is at least solid metal with a foam cover, so you shouldn't get too fatigued if you have to hold it for a while. And yes, it's a shield for your left hand, so it will be uncomfortable if you're trying to play an accurate southpaw Link. The hardware is screwed in, so you could possibly convert it to a right hand shield with some work and a drill though.

As mentioned in another comment: if you buy from Top Swords, you will get the shield featured in the picture.

Other details:

-On my (not the most accurate) scale it weighs 6 lbs.
-Made in China in case you were wondering.

product_title: Browning Trail Camera - Dark Ops
review_headline: Browning Strike Force & Dark Ops Models are the Highest Rated Cameras on the Market for Their Price Point
review_body:
UPDATE 2/5/16 - I wanted to update this review, since my issue mentioned later in my original review has been has been completely resolved. I mailed my camera to Browning Trail Camera's service center. Incidentally, I was happy to see that their service center is in Tennessee. Even though my camera was technically past the one year warranty date by almost two months, they immediately sent me back a brand new (still in the packaging) Dark Ops. I had a brand new camera within two weeks of mailing it them. I guess since I contacted them and explained the issue had started months before (but took a while to ensure it was the camera and not bad batteries), they fully warrantied the camera. It is very refreshing to deal with a company that stands behind their product. Browning is two for two in my experiences with their customer service. I am incredibly pleased. They have ensured they have a loyal customer in me. I have no reservations recommending either the Strike Force or the Dark Ops models.

ORIGINAL REVIEW:
See end of review for updated comments after one full year of use. When I first starting researching buying some new trail cams, I was a bit skeptical of Browning, since it seemed like a situation where a well-known company was sticking their name on something outside their area of expertise - but it turns out these very well may be the best trail cameras on the market. Browning has two cameras in their sub-micro series currently, the Strike Force & the Dark Ops. The Browning Strike Force was the highest rated trail cam for 2014, as it essentially changed the market and price points for trail cams, with a debut at $150 and features only available at the time in the $300 price point with other manufacturers. I initially purchased the Browning Strike Force model since it was at the top of the rankings, and I was so pleased with its performance that I eventually purchased the Dark Ops model, as well. I have been just as pleased with the Dark Ops model as I was with the Strike Force, as both models have identical features with the exception of the flash (Strike Force is a visible IR flash and Dark Ops is dark IR flash). (More on the specifics regarding the differences between IR & dark IR flash technology later in the review). The bottom line is the next trail camera I purchase will be another Browning Dark Ops.
Dark Ops - The Good:

1. Terrific Daytime Picture Quality - 10MP
2. Terrific Battery Efficiency (*this declined after several months)
3. Dark IR - No visible flash to alert nearby humans of the camera's presence
4. Good Night Quality (Black & White) & Good Flash Range (Comparable to Strike Force)
4. Great Versatility & Options - The burst mode and timing adjustability are very handy
5. Lightning Fast Trigger Speed
6. Great Detection Range
7. Display for Battery Life* & Remaining Photo Memory (Battery life indicator doesn't work well with Lithium batteries)
8. Connection Port - Camera works as SD card reader by connecting to PC or TV
9. Good Customer Support - Emailed the company, and they sent spare latches free of charge (see below)

Dark Ops - The Bad:

1. Cheap Plastic Latch - The plastic latch that closes the cover over the bottom half of the camera (control buttons, display, and SD card slot) is really easy to break. You really have to consciously make sure everything is lined up correctly or this latch will just snap. Several other reviewers for both Strike Force and Dark Ops have complained of this exact issue. (Update - I contacted the manufacturer, Prometheus, and they sent me some spare latches at no charge. The latch is simple to replace if it breaks.) This is the only real complaint I have so far with either the Strike Force or Dark Ops, so it really would not deter me from purchasing another - but it is something the manufacturer should correct on future models. All the other items I couldlist are really more of a \\"wish list\\" type item that would make the camera ideal, but in reality are not offered in other models in this price range yet either.

Other Comments on Features:

1. No Field Viewer - There is no viewer to preview photos in the field, or to check alignment (although for alignment purposes it does have a test mode which flashes as the camera detects motion within the detection area). This would be a handy feature to check your alignment from the get go, but most cameras with this feature are quite a bit higher priced.

3. Motion Range - The range of detection is slightly greater than the camera view, and coupled with the lightning fast trigger speed this can mean the first photo may go off before the subject comes into view. I usually utilize the 2 shot burst feature, and by the 2nd photo your subject will be in view. By the same token, because of this combination of features I have caught animals at a full speed run that otherwise would not have been in view with narrow detection & slower triggers.

4. Digital camera USB connection cable for connecting the trail cam to a PC or TV is not included. The connection cable for my wife's digital camera fit the trail cam, but I have used this feature a lot less than I thought I might.

5. SD Card Slot Access - For those with big fingers, the SD card can be difficult to remove from this camera; and it is virtually impossible to do with gloves on. I often have to carry some tweezers to assist in pulling the SD card out far enough until I can get a good grip with my fingers. This issue really would not deter my purchase of this model, but it is certainly something the manufacturer should address in future model updates. It really just needs a sturdier spring to push the card out further when ejected.
Comparing Dark Ops Model versus Strike Force Model

1. Both are easy to use, have great daytime photo quality, and have terrific battery efficiency. The only difference between the two camera model is the flash type, so the remainder of the comparison is basically a contrast of traditional IR versus dark IR flashes.

2. Night Photo Quality - The only area in which the Strike Force has a slight edge over Dark Ops, but it is really not much of an edge at all. The Dark Ops night photos are necessarily somewhat darker with the dark IR flash, so the clarity level is slightly affected. Still the range for night photos for the Dark Ops, although slightly less than Strike Force, has been fairly impressive just the same. Generally, I can only tell the difference between the flash ranges of the two models when they are set up in fairly open areas, i.e. they are nearly identical in thickly wooded areas.

3. Flash Visibility - Strictly for deer trail camera purposes, the dark IR technology does very little, as although the deer can see the IR flash on the Strike Force, they become accustomed almost instantly. The real difference for flash visibility is as it relates to humans. Obviously, if you intend to use for security purposes, you should purchase the Dark Ops model. Furthermore, if humans are likely to come within your hunting area, the dark IR prevents potential camera thieves from being alerted to the presence of the device at night. The one usage related to hunting in which dark flash would be mandatory is for predator photography. If you intend to use the trail cam to pattern predator movements for foxes, coyotes, and bobcats; then the dark IR is a must have. I have captured three times as many predator photos on the Dark Ops model as I have the Strike Force. When I have caught coyotes in video mode on the Strike Force, they immediately turn and run away from the light source; and when in trail cam mode they are always looking directly into the camera for the initial photo and gone from view in subsequent photos. Whereas, I often catch both bobcats and coyotes in multi photo sets with the Dark Ops cam, and they usually do not show signs that they are aware of the camera at all.

Tips
Here are few tips for new users that I have picked up from my experience with this trail cam:

1. Purchase Lithium batteries - I had read that tip on a trail cam review site, and was wary at first since Lithium (AA type) are not rechargeable and are not cheap either, but I have had one camera in the field for over two months straight and the battery display still reads 100%. Update 1/11/16 - It took me a season to figure out that the battery life indicator doesn't work with Lithium batteries. It pretty much goes from 100%, to 90%, then batteries are completely dead shortly after a 90% indication. The indicator works fine with alkaline, and seems to work with rechargeable NiCad. That said, lithium batteries last much better.

2. Purchase two SD cards - 8GB is plenty, even in video mode.

3. Buy a Cable Lock or Security Box - I have traditionally used a Python lock, but they can be cut with bolt cutters and I have had issues with keys breaking off in the lock. Also, a trespasser still has access to the SD card when using just a cable lock, so a trespasser could simply steal the SD card to prevent from being recognized. To protect from this, you would need to purchase the Browning security box.

4. Field Set Up - A strap is included with the camera, which will secure the camera to trees of probably 24 inches and under. Keep in mind the height range for the intended target when securing the camera, as a trail cam set at 6 foot from the ground is not going to catch many deer or turkeys, but a camera set too low will probably catch more squirrels and raccoons than you want to see. I recommend a height of approximately 30 inches for deer (depending on the topography), and slightly lower for turkeys. Clear the ground immediately in front of the camera and remove limbs, tall grass, etc. out to at least 15 feet to minimize false triggers during windy conditions. Limbs and other vegetation that are within a five foot range (directly in front of the flash) will also reflect light from the flash, and can slightly hamper photo quality. Another consideration in winter is overhead limbs in case of icing. I had one of my cameras to be completely blocked by a sagging pine tree for nearly a week after a recent ice storm.

5. Face it North (whenever possible) - Unless you have a spot in which you know you will be looking for either morning or afternoon photos, then you will want to aim the camera looking North (for those of us in the Northern hemisphere). Shadows and glare will be much more manageable when the camera is facing North.

6. Settings - If you plan to set the camera up over an area that the animals may tend to linger, you probably want to minimize the burst mode (or don't use burst mode at all), and keep the delay duration at five minutes (or longer). On one occasion I set the burst on 3 photos, with a one minute delay, and ended up with nearly 2,000 photos in less than a week - which does pretty much guarantee you will have good shots of every animal that walked through, but makes for a long sorting process when trying to establish patterns. A two photo burst will capture most targets that were essentially just quickly walking by, and a five minute delay is pretty good timing for deer, which tend linger for a maximum of about twenty minutes in any single interval.

Update 1/11/16 -
This camera stayed in the field from late November through mid January, then mid February through mid May, and finally late August through early January. I noticed starting in October that the battery efficiency went way down. I switched to rechargeable batteries this fall, and thought it was just the batteries at first, but when I went back to Lithium, I was still only getting a couple of weeks out of brand new batteries. That contrasts against getting two months with the same settings when the camera was new. I tried Alkaline batteries as a stop gap during the season and they only lasted two days. Not sure what has happened, but the battery efficiency has plummeted. My Strike Force model has not had anywhere near this severe a decline in battery efficiency. Not sure what has happened to the Dark Ops model, but I may need to contact the manufacturer. Up until this issue, I had been thrilled with this camera, and thought it was the best value on the market.

Other Tools for Trail Cams
As an aside, there are several new web-based software applications coming on the market to help trail cam users garner useful pattern info from their trail cams. These applications allow users to select trail cam locations using GPS & aerial satellite photos, and upload photos from each cam site. The application then downloads local weather data for each site, and matches the photo time stamps with local weather conditions. Specific animals can be tagged by photo. This allows the application to utilize predictive algorithms to pattern a deer's movements and predict your most likely areas for success based on predicted or current weather (and moon phase) conditions. I have long complained about the significant gap between the information trail cams provide, and a simple way to fully utilize that information to determine the end means for most users (patternable deer movements). product_title: Spyderco Triangle Sharpmaker, 2 Medium/2 Fine
review_headline: Spyderco Triangle Sharpmaker is excellent but take some wee bit of effort to learn to use.
review_body: I bought this because so many I know have recommended it.  It works very well in my opinion and is easy to use but there is a learning curve that a new user will have to overcome. You have to have good hand to eye coordination  and common sense to get good results.  Once I got past this learning curve I really love this knife sharpener. You have got to be able to consistently  keep the knife vertical for it to work properly.  If your knife has not been sharpened in a long time or it was sharpened improperly prior to using the Spyderco Triangle Sharpmaker it going to take some extra back beveling with the course stone and or extra work with the 40 degree stone to bring the shape of the edge into its original specifications. Once you have re-established the original edge template the subsequent sharpening's become very easy and fast.  Compared to the other sharpeners I have used Spyderco Triangle Sharpmaker is the easiest to use to get the original knife template re-established.  Another thing I found that is useful to make sharpening faster is to clean the stone with a wet rag to remove the metal filings that build up on the stones.  I have sharpened a lot of scissors and knifes with regular and serrated edges and got very good results with the standard stones that come with it.  The good thing is this sharpener does not wear the knife out by removing to much metal the way some of the electric sharpeners do the only down side it  takes longer but give you a better result and you can sharpen your knife without needing an electric outlet.  I am very happy with my purchase and would recommend this sharpener to people with good hand to eye coordination and some patience for the learning curve that some people might experience.  So if you buy it and you think it does not work I can guarantee it's not the knife sharpeners fault so be a some patience because it has worked for every time for me. I give it five stars.

product_title: HIVIZ Ruger P-Series Fiber Optic Sight (Green)
review_headline: Great replacement for the factory sight
review_body:
Got this sight to replace the bland and hard to see factory sight on my Ruger SP101. While I LOVE Ruger's durability and quality I will never understand what they were thinking when they designed the stock grip and sight on the SP101.

$39 price on Amazon for the Hi Viz RG2006 was the best I found anywhere. The product arrived before the projected delivery date, and the package was in good condition. No problems there..

Hi Viz recommends hiring a gunsmith to install this sight, but if you are a little bit mechanically inclined that's not necessary. The sight is just a little bit thicker than the stock sight so it will need to be filed ever so slightly. (..I used the coarse side of a Tri-Hone sharpening stone and it took about 10 moderate passes on each side..) The sight also needs to be drilled in order for the roll pin to go through and hold it securely in the gun. There are plenty of tutorials on YouTube that explain how to do it and what tools you will need. Take your time and you will be fine.

Target acquisition with this sight is MUCH better than that of the factory sight. Daylight visibility is great and low light visibility is reasonable; however, this is not a glow in the dark night sight. (..those cost between $60 and $70..)

All in all I love this new sight. It's easy to see, and it only took me about 30 minutes to install it on the gun.

review_body:
Im going to list pros, cons, and shipping, and explain them afterwards.

PROS:
*lightweight
*thin, not bulky
*not heat absorbant
*silicone isn't a bother, does it's job

CONS:

SHIPPING: From Sports Authority

For this perticular item, I got it a day earlier than expected, but I bought another item from the same seller, and didn't see that with the package when the reciept said both were delivered as well as my email from amazon did. If it comes within the next few days, then it will be on time as notified, but reciepts should be absolutely correct when the ordered item is shipped. That is critical information to clearly identify if the item(s)
Has/have been delivered. I have contacted the seller and notified them of the issue. I will update the review as I get Customer feedback and whether or not my item was delivered on time or not.
The packaging for the item was a little underrated, it was just in a USPS cardboard slip, no perticular protection other than the plastic wrapped and taped around the item, Nike Fury Headband (Black/White), with the INCORRECT information on the reciept as to which items were in the package. I expected a little better packaging, the reason being the product can still be damaged, such as water damage, a rip or tear in the fabric, or possibly be dirty. I expect $9 shipping to be of excellent quality shipping, which includes appropriate protection and delivery speed, and only 1 made the criteria. The delivery came from California, but made it just fine. Overall im happy with the delivery speed, but packaging should be better.

Ok, now for the product details

The Product PROS; Explained
The product overall is great. It's lightweight, thin not bulky, looks great, the silicone whichis inside the headband isn't uncomfortable, it does not retain massive amounts of heat, which in my case is good as I'll use it for running and basketball, but does help keep the ears warm (if you cover them with it) depending on your taste in style. In my case, im looking for fashion and performance. Now the important part; the headband doesn't fit to tight, nor to loose, just right. My head is a medium in terms of size, to a snapback, with all holes or 1 stud not used, and a perfect fit for a revolution/speed helmet for American Football. The stretch for the headband is very good, and conforms well to my head. There seems to be just the right amount of spandex. The fabric is a rough silky plus polyester feeling

product_title: Lee Precision 4 Hole Turret (Silver)
review_headline: Doesn't seem like a genuine Lee part.
review_body:
Unless Lee has changed their manufacturing process, I have strong reason to believe that this product is counterfeit. I have another Lee 4 hole turret and have seen many of them. This one is definitely not the same as all the others. First, if you look at the picture for this item, you'll notice that there are four large holes on the top side of the plate and that is it. That is consistent with my other turret and with all of these turrets I have seen. However, on the product I received from this company, the center post hole from the underneath side goes all the way through to the top side. It is also a very ugly and non-cylindrical hole. Second, the treatment on the side of this one differs from my other one (which I believe to be bead-blasting) . In addition, the thread work in the dye holes is really shoddy. Finally, there is a large lap (resembles a crack) on the bottom side of the turret, and that is my main reason for the return.

I currently use and operate several products from Lee Precision and have been very pleased with the products and extremely pleased with the value of the products. Like I said previously, unless Lee has redesigned this part and quality has absolutely taken a nose dive, I have reason to believe that this part is counterfeit.

UPDATE!!!!! I contacted Lee. This part was redesigned and began to be distributed last year. Lee took responsibility for this part and apologized for the quality. THE PART IS NOT COUNTERFEIT.

product_title: Weslo Cadence G 5.9 Treadmill
review_body:
One review on this really convinced me to wade through the negative comments and take the plunge with this treadmill. When shopping for such a large, expensive, item it's hard to sift through the cheap options and pick one that will actually work. With big decisions like this it can be easier to just buy an expensive one because you can be more confident that it will work. Less anxiety. $300 is cheaper than most treadmills, but it's still not a small sum of money. The idea of taking a risk on a product that doesn't work and basically throwing away $300 is almost enough to make anyone run to a more expensive option. I am SO glad I bought this treadmill. It works perfectly fine, can handle running without breaking or skipping and must have a reasonable weight limit. For somebody just looking to do some walking or running from the comfort of their own home, this will be great.

I will say: this was NOT easy to set up. I don't know what the other reviewers did--maybe mine was a little wonky, but this was HARD. Connecting the handle and upper feet area to the track took two people, some muscle, and some WORK. We almost stripped everything clean trying to line these up. All that said, it was doable, we got it after a few hours.

product_title: SKLZ Super Sandbag - Heavy Duty Training Weight Bag
review_headline: Good quality, but not really a good sandbag
review_body:
Used the SKLZ sandbag for about a week now. I did others did and used large zip locks inside their bag. My wife uses 1/2 the weight I do, and we haven't seen any leakage. Overall seems to be a well constructed bag.

But for me and my wife, it just isn't a sandbag. When full, it is like a padded brick with handles. I can drop it, toss it over my shoulder with no pain. But the sand inside doesn't actually shift. I thought a sandbag would shift around, forcing my body to compensate, and use small muscles. But instead it just lifts like any heavy weight. It does fold a little in the middle, but that wasn't really the effect that I want in a sandbag.

I think I am going to make my own internal bags that will be less rigid. The only other real complaint is that there is no middle handle.

So if you know what you want in a sandbag, this seems to be a well constructed piece of gym equipment. I guess I need more time, but I just don't see it breaking any time soon.

review_body:
I recently have taken up the lovely game they call golf. I have played one summer and really enjoy the game. The only problem is that I am terrible. The last round of the year I was able to have my best round of the year, shooting a 109. Needless to say, I have a lot of work to do.

Upon first starting out playing the game, I received many recommendations about taking a few lessons with a pro. I took a few lessons with the local pro and he helped to give me a decent foundation to start with. As I live in the Northeast, I will have to wait until the snow disappears in order to practice, or so I thought. That’s where the Rukket RukkNet comes into play.

First point I am happy with is delivery. Not sure who gets the credit for that, Amazon or Rukket. I ordered the net on Wednesday at 4:30PM and received the net Friday morning (I have Prime). I have never before been so happy to see the UPS man. Upon opening the box I pulled out a large circular bag that I would guess is 36’’ in diameter.
Upon opening the zipper, I noticed two things that caught my eye that I could really appreciate. First thing is the case for the net is slightly larger diameter than the net in its closed position. You know the feeling of trying to put the Christmas tree back into its original box? That will not happen with the Rukket net. Second thing I liked to see were the instructions for opening and closing of the net were sewn into the side of the case. Instructions are the first thing I often lose. You will really only need to use the instructions once to open and close the net, it’s very simple, however, if you let someone borrow the net the instructions will prove valuable.

Like the everyday Joe, I don’t have a room dedicated where I can keep a permanent net up at all times. To the dismay of my wife, I erected my net in our family room. When I opened the net on carpet it was very easy to get the net up, however it is a little more tricky on carpet as the legs want to move on you. Either way, once you get it up, it does not move.

The net also comes with a driving mat with three different terrain types. The fairway lie is the same as hitting off the deck at a driving range. The middle lie is similar to hitting in the rough, however the rough grass would only be about 1.5’’ high. The last lie is extremely dense , almost like a Brillo pad. This lie is the closest feeling to grass of all thee. If you hit it fat, you club head wants to stop and dig in.

After using the net roughly 10 times, I am extremely happy with the build quality. I’ve used every club in my bag, sans the putter and the net is holding up fine. Being that I am a terrible golfer, I have hit many miss-hits and worm burners and the net stops them all. I can build and take down the net in literally 3 minutes, you simply cannot beat that. review_body: I attended Purim as a guest of Jewish friends two years ago. product_title: Smith and Wesson M&P Pro Series Tactical Range Bag, Black
review_headline: Nice size, not too small-not too big
review_body:
Very well made bag. Nice size, not too small-not too big. I have more than enough room form my Glock 19 and .380, plus 400+ rounds of ammo, ear protection, safety glasses. Plenty of room left over for tools, cleaning gear and any other items you may need at the range.

I gave it only 4 stars because to me, 5 stars means "perfect". and unfortunately this bag does have one negative. The description states that the bag has locations for holding 10 mags - this is deceptive. What it has are two pieces of elastic bands in two different compartments that are stitched down at different points along their lengths for you to push your mags into. However, the stitching was done very poorly so that the space between stitch points, where your mag is suppose to go. is inconsistent in width. My Glock mags fit in some of these slots, but not all. For a high quality bag like this to resort to such a cheap and poorly executed method for holding mags is incomprehensible, which is why I gave it 4 stars.

Even with the above negative, I would still highly recommend this bag. There are plenty of other pockets to hold your mags, so you could use the elastic to hold tools and such instead.

review_body:
The zipper fell out after a few days. I sewed it back in, but the fabric is a stretchy knit that snagged and separated when I mended the zipper. The repaired zipper lasted about a week.

It had a funny smell when I opened the package so I washed it before I wore it. I handwashed it and let it air dry because it didn't look sturdy enough to withstand the washer and the dryer.

The fabric is soft and feels like the cuff of a sweatshirt. Until the zipper came out a few days after I started using it, it held small objects, like a Fitbit and my house key, just fine.

I order the red one, which was more of a red-orange rather than the bright fire engine red in the picture on my screens -- I viewed it on my computer as well as my phone.

The manufacturer itself, Suddora, sends unsolicited email after the sale, continues to send unsolicited email after being told it's undesirable, and removes negative feedback from its page, falsely claiming that the feedback is about the product rather than Suddora. For example, this is the Suddora-specific feedback that I left on Suddora's feedback page: "Seller spams after the sale and continues to send unsolicited email even after being told to stop. Seller contacts Amazon to have poor feedback removed, saying that this feedback is against the product rather than the seller. This feedback is definitely about the seller, not the product."

Overall, I wish I had not purchased this Suddora product. It's either designed badly and from from shoddy materials or it's defective. And since the manufacturer behaves defensively and deceptively, I don't see any point in returning the item. I should know better than to pay $8 for the cuff of a sweatshirt anyway.

The blades are very sharp, not face razor sharp but each will take the hair off your arm. However the blades are not polished so there were spots of corrosion starting to form. The handle and brass have only the smallest of flaws and it's really me being overly critical. The buck plate has a small space around it so there is a gap as well as roughness where the brass meets wood.  I rate the knife 9/10.  A great buy for classic look and functionality.

product_title: ADVANTUS Super Stacker Index Box, 3" x 5", Clear, 1 Box (40307)
review_body:
I had been spending countless minutes over the past month trying to improve my index card file box since I don't have a PC, only an iPad from 2011. The iPad is very helpful but has come up short in various tasks. So I wanted to sort my index card file setup into a few separate containers. Like I said, I spent much time and bought a few boxes but nded up returning them because they were deficient in various ways.
So when I scanned the products on Amazon, I liked the description of this one, SKU -AVT40307 Super Stacker Storage Box, clear, removable lid. One thing I like also is that they stack because they are constructed so that the tops and and bottoms are made to nest. This will make it possible for me to have all 5 boxes (from the 2 orders) stacked in the corner of my office desk with a label on each identifying the category.
I have only one very small negative suggestion: The next redesign should give the vertical dimension a very scant 3/8 inch or 1/2 inch higher dimension to allow that the maximum capacity of cards PLUS the divider cards fit better. But overall, it's a real bargain at just under $5.00 each and should last for years. It came directly from BIC in Broolyn NY via Priority Mail 2-day. I was surprised that they were shipped in a plastic shipping bag rather than a cardboard carton with packing material to protect the contents, but the boxes are definitely in good condition.
Now on to the next 60 products I've ordered.

product_title: Compact Dumbbell Rack
review_headline: Heavy duty and solid, shipper needs to learn to protect contents of package.
review_body:
So, it's heavy duty. Super. Seems very sturdy. However, there was absolutely zero packaging in the very ample box. Lots of air, but no foam, peanuts, plastic bubbles, or anything. As such, nearly all of the components banged against each other (or external forces), and they all have significant paint chips and some have minor dents/dings. The dings I can live with, but the paint chips are unfortunate. I'm guessing this isn't stainless steel, so I'll probably be dealing with rust issues in ~6mo or so.

Aside from that (and, assuming I can touch up the paint), it's a solid product. All metal, all the time. The L shaped hooks (to hold the weights in place) are a bit tall for smaller weights and can pinch fingers (20lb and below). Not a problem on 30+lb weights, though you won't fit many on there. I managed 4 pairs with just a bit of space left on the smaller rack: 12, 20, 30, 40.

product_title: Schrade Viper 3, OTF, Black Handle, Black Blade, Plain
review_body: Weird.  It locks up solid, It's substantial and heavy, it has a dagger-style double-edged blade, but: it's single-action, which is OK, but the resting position of the trigger is back near the glassbreaker, at the butt end of the knife. in order to fire it you can't hold it solidly and push a button or a conveniently-located slide with your thumb; you have to either hold the knife in one hand while urging the slide-trigger forward with the other hand, or develop a sleight-of-hand method of gripping the butt of the knife while also pushing the slide forward. Maybe I'm being picky, but I have only one opposable thumb on each hand. There may be a way of learning to operate the slide with the heel of my hand, but the bottom line is: out of the box, there's no obvious way to both grip the handle of the knife and open it-without either using both hands or a lot of practice. On the other hand, for the price, it's solid, double-edged, and it doesn't rattle.  After a month of using it, this knife is more impressive than I first thought. The trick to opening it properly, for me, is to hold it between thumb and forefinger with the slide on the undersurface, i.e., with the slide pointing at the floor, then use the middle or ring finger to start the slide moving. That may sound awkward, but the solidity of the lockup at full extension makes it worthwhile to learn some way of deploying it. For the price, that solidity (the handle tightens onto the blade at extension) is  unique.

product_title: CAP Barbell Soft Kettlebell
review_body: I was originally looking for kettlebells, but after a little shopping decided against them because I'm very clumsy and I can just see one of those babies crushing a foot or breaking something in my house. I'm also recovering from injuries to my arms and hands (thanks to an idiot drunk driver) and have a lot of pain, plus I bruise very easily, so a real kettlebell seemed less attractive once I found this. This looked to be a great option as I can still get similar benefits to a kettlebell workout. Granted, these don't come in more than 20 lbs, but my arms may not be able to handle that much anyway. We'll see. I have the 15 and 20 lbs sizes. They look a bit awkward, but they can do the job! They can swing, not quite as gracefully as a kettlebell, but I don't have to worry about breaking any bones, bruises, cuts or scrapes, either! Of course, you can still pull a muscle if you don't pay attention, but that's probably it. I can do a lot of other exercises that are done with kettlebells just fine. The handle is metal covered with neoprene and is comfy and has room for two hands for medium to small hands, anyway. You can't park it like a real kettlebell as it will just fall over, and for a short person, doing figure 8/lunges are not optimal. But everything else is good. There is nothing wrong with cast iron or steel kettlebells, if that is what you want. There is nothing wrong with these, either. Both are very useful, it's a matter of what your needs are and goals are. They're certainly a nice kettlebell alternative. So if you want the benefits of a  (lighter weight) kettlebell, and don't want the risk of one, give these a try or look into sandbells or steelbells.

product_title: Revolution Carolina Team Disc Golf Bag
review_headline: Great bag in 2007...but i cant speak about the current company
review_body:
I got into the sport around 2003. back then, Revolution was the Cadillac of disc golf bags. If you were competing, half of your competition had Carolina bags. I got mine for a Christmas gift around 2007 and has stood the test of time and punishment through literally hundreds of rounds, rain, snow, heat and cold. I haven't had a single issue with the stitching. i have absolutely zero tears or holes. I have the backpack style straps and it wears comfortably and I've had no issues with even the steepest of courses.

Pros:

Storage. Between the two side compartments, you should be able to carry whatever you want with you. towels. extra towels. scorecards, cell phones, snacks, i've even stuffed a rain jacket into the side compartments. For a round on the course, and even a two day tournament you should be set. There are two water bottle holders, perfect for nalgene bottles and gatorade bottles. The putter pocket can hold two putters easily. The main disc compartment is plenty large enough for me, but i don't carry around spare discs for my spare discs. I can get through most courses with about 10-15 different discs for any situation, and of course a few spares thrown in for good measure.

Durablility: As i've said above, i've had mine for about 8 years and put it through hell. not one tear, not one hole. even my color isnt horribly faded. I understand that revolution's quality has been iffy since 2010 or so, but now the company is back under new management and i hope the quality is back to par. I have had no issues with mine. The bottom of the bag is almost like a composite EPDM waterproof material so it can be placed on wet grass and mud without any seeping and of course, easy cleanup after the round. The "rain-fly" as i call it is a good feature that i have used in rainy tournaments but i usually just keep it stuffed into the rear compartment which can also, of course, hold extra discs.

Cons:

The price. The bag design hasn't changed in years (other than new colors) and doesn't even come with backpack straps. you'll have to order those separately unless you want to carry your discs around like a messenger bag.

Lack of backpack straps: As i just said above, but i feel it deserves a bullet point of its own. The bag comes with a messenger style strap, but is fully designed for backpack style straps.

The brand: Revolution was on top of the disc golf world in the early 2000's. then out of nowhere, the quality dropped, the customer service was almost nonexistent. And then Grip took the reigns. As of February 2015, i received an email that "REVOLUTION IS BACK!!" and under new management and is working tirelessly to win over the disc golf world all over again. I, for one, welcome them back and hope for the best.

Bottom line - Wait and see. i absolutely love mine and got my money's worth. I havent seen another disc golf bag yet where i was in awe and wanted to switch to a different bag. It's built like a tank and has NEVER failed me. But the company is under new ownership and will probably (i'm not certain) roll out some new products to compete with Grip (a bag that has great storage, wear-ability, good reviews and comes with backpack straps).

review_headline: OK, but not what I was looking for

This DVD was OK, but not exactly what I was looking for.

There are 3 ten-minute "workouts". The first one is very aerobic, led by a man, and uses a jump rope - although one of the two women in the background is doing the workout with modifications, not using a jump rope and slightly lower impact.

The second workout is led by a woman, using a kettlebell, although again the 2 people in the background are doing the workout with modifications. One is using a regular hand weight, and the other is not using a weight.

The third segment is yoga, and is just one woman alone. It would have been helpful to have other people doing modifications; I could do very few of these yoga poses the way she did them, since I have bad knees and wrists, and almost all the moves are on hands and knees, with an excessive number of planks! product_title: Specter Gear MOLLE/PALS Compatible Modular Double Universal Rifle/Carbine/SMG Magazine Pouch
review_headline: One set of field gear for two different rifles
review_body:
One problem if you have two very different rifle systems, like an M1A and Armalite Rifle No 15 for example, is the magazines are VERY different. When trying to get some kit together, this produces a problem. Since overloading yourself really isn't an option, you'll have to spend more money then you'd like on two different sets of field gear to support each rifle. These mag pouches solve that problem. One set of field gear, with all your supporting items, that will support two different magazines. Just grab the mags you need depending on the rifle in hand and stuff them in.

I ordered two of the Foliage green due to the price. It was like getting two pouches for the price of one. The molle straps are top notch, everything about these things seem well made. I'd prefer snaps over velcro, but velcro seems to be the things these days so there's no getting away from it.

I have found that one these double mag pouches will:

product_title: Spyderco Caly 3.5 Black G-10 PlainEdge Knife
review_headline: Great blade...but some improvements could be made
review_body:
I love my Caly3.5 G10 despite the list that follows:
1.) It is not made in the USA. I buy plenty of overseas produced products. This comment is meant to highlight the fact that Golden, CO produced Spydercos are at a quality level above those coming out of Seki City, Japan.
2.) There either aren't bushings or the bushings used are lower quality. They do not make for a smooth deployment. While things have improved since using some knife lube on the pivot, there is a detectable amount of grittiness when opening the blade.
3.) There is slight side-to-side blade play with the pivot adjusted as tight as possible to still facilitate fast, one-hand deployment.
4.) There are scratches on the ricasso (probably because there are no bushings) and the jimping isn't as grippy as the Golden, CO jimping.

Overall this is a good knife. It's long blade for relatively compact size is impressive and it is certainly a beautiful design. If they could smooth out the deployment and improve the locking mechanism, it would be a 5 out of 5. If you are a total stickler for these things, know that I have a Delica and an Endura (both cost half as much) and they have super smooth deployment and amazingly solid lockup. The Caly3.5 is more like knife art in my opinion. It is a gentleman's folder and thanks to the G10, has enough traction for tactical use. 4 out of 5.

product_title: FOCUS T25 Shaun T's NEW Workout DVD Program—Get It Done in 25 Minutes
review_headline: Already fit? No problem. This gets you even stronger.
review_body:
Background: I'm a very healthy person, 22 year old 5 foot 10 female 150 pounds, very lean and toned, I eat a completely clean diet free of processed foods, commercially processed meat and eggs, dairy, all gluten and most grains. I do Zumba and kickboxing most mornings for about 30 minutes in front of my Xbox Kinect. I got really tired and bored of these workouts, though. I needed something new, and I had reached a plateau in my fitness level. I wasn't going anywhere and something needed to change.

I saw T25 on an infomercial. I always take infomercials with a grain of salt, and am very suspicious about them, but the more I watched the infomercial, the more legit it seemed. I've worked out my whole life and it seemed like the workouts and results from this program could be real. After doing a little more research and reading reviews on here, decided to order it.

Pros: The workouts are HARD. Even at my fitness level, I was using the low-impact moderator a few times. I guess that could go in the cons section too, but I got my sorry butt kicked the first day. Zumba and kickboxing are nowhere near this level. The only time I could remember working out this hard was back in high school for sports practice, and in college when I worked with a personal trainer to keep the freshman 15 off. But don't let that scare you away...I felt GREAT after!! I had an exercise high like no other. The program, calendar, and nutrition plan are very straightforward and easy to follow. I didn't really need the nutrition plan since I was eating like that anyway but I did gain a few new recipes out if it, so score! Shaun is a great motivator and you really connect with him through the screen. And before you know it, the workouts are done! It goes SO fast and you feel so good after.

Cons: Again, the hard work. Do not do this if you are not prepared for a boot camp-like experience. And be prepared for soreness after. I wasn't very sore after most workouts (although I did have to go to the chiropractor at the end of the week to fix my neck, an old injury got aggravated from working out--another thing to keep in mind if you have previous injuries) since I was already in shape, but it felt good to work muscles I hadn't worked in awhile. The second con is that these workouts aren't *truly* 25 minutes to the T. Shaun included a 2-3 minute cooldown after, which I highly recommend you do. I then like to stretch more after that, for a full 30 minutes. So just ensure you have 5 extra minutes after T25 for stretching. Also, these DVDs *do not play well in an Xbox One* so use an Xbox 360 or DVD player. I don't know about PlayStation systems.

Overall: T25 was one of the best decisions of my life. I'm not trying to lose weight so I can't tell you about my weight or measurements or anything, because again this was purely me trying to change up my fitness routine, but I think next I'm going to try P90X3 or something else because BeachBody is a very respectable company and I feel like my health just took on a whole new level.

product_title: M-Clip Ultralight Aluminum Money Clips with Black Urethane Rubber Accents
review_headline: Minor design flaw with major implications
review_body: I bought this as a Christmas gift for my father upon his request.  Before wrapping it, I had to open it up to see what an $80 money clip looks like.  While I still feel it is overpriced, I couldn't help but notice the quality.  It definitely seemed solid and well-constructed.  Overall, it had a very classy appearance.  I then decided to try it out with a few credit cards and some money and quickly discovered a fatal design flaw.  On my sample, the money clip didn't squeeze together strongly enough to prevent the cards and/or money from easily falling out (even in the closed position).  Unless you plan on carrying a lot of money and many credit cards, I don't see how this product will retain your money as it should.  A product of this price should be able to securely hold a single dollar.  Despite my concern, I wrapped it anyway since it was, after all, a gift.  However, when my dad opened it he quickly arrived at the same conclusion.  There was just too little tension to be useful.  So, of course, this item has been returned.  Good idea...poor execution.  If they designed the money clip with sufficient tension it would be a quality, yet overpriced money management solution.  As it stands, it's overpriced and has very limited functionality.  Sadly, they're a minor adjustment away from a decent product.

review_headline: Long Shaggy Dog Story, All Negative
review_body: Originally I was giving my first impression on opening the box, and gave the Polar FT7 a 1 rating because I couldn't get it to work.  Later, I increased that to a 3 because the Polar FT7 has some good capabilities but in my case doesn't work and has lousy instructions.  Now I'm returning to a 1.  See below.  This was not an Amazon purchase, but rather was from a sporting goods store.  I used to have a Polar Pacer, but the batteries have long since gone dead from accumulating too many knee problems after turning 60 and having to cease jogging about five years ago.  The Pacer, also with a chest strap and wrist unit, was simple as pie to understand and operate.  I am trying to figure out, on a gym treadmill given what a medical technician told me, whether I can get my heart beat up to a specified rate at a specified treadmill speed and incline, to get a good stress test reading without having to break into a jog and very possibly re-injure the knee with known meniscus issues.  So, my issues and history so far with the FT7 are as follows: (1) They design something fancy with lots of new high-tech gizmo features most people don't need, and then, as is the case with almost all electronics, assign, as a throwaway follow-up project, to some flunky who couldn't explain how to turn on a water faucet, the writing of the associated little instruction booklet. (2) I returned to the sporting goods store and consulted first with one sales rep and then with a second sales rep who was a very experienced expert on various heart rate monitor models and their idiosyncrasies and set-up procedures.  In brief, the first sales rep couldn't get a heart rate reading, either, nor could the second, expert, sales rep.  (3) The first rep after various lines of analysis and solution attempts finally resorted to replacing the chest strap battery.  That didn't work.  (4) The second, expert, sales rep, among other things, did a printout of the more detailed online instruction manual and found a discrepancy between it and the cheapo little instruction booklet that came with the product.  Very basic.  One said chest strap battery right side up, and the other said chest strap battery upside down.  We didn't determine definitively which was correct.  Packaged, the chest strap battery in product came right side up.  (5) He retrieved a second Polar FT7, the last one he had in stock, from the back of the store, and after more effort couldn't get it to work, either.  The wrist unit for both the originally purchased product and the one from the back of the store kept searching unsuccessfully for a signal from the chest strap, even after better moistening the chest strap, checking its positioning, and whatnot.  (6) Today was a holiday, and the sale expert rep is off the next three days, so after that we call a Polar HQ troubeshooter number retailers go to for solutions.  I may edit this review further, then.  (7) That said, the Polar FT7, if functional, is, according to the second, expert, sporting goods store sales rep, better than comparably priced heart rate monitors, and better than a cheaper wrist-only Polar pulse-measuring model, because the others do averaging and the Polar FT7 is closer to a miniature EKG.  (8) He said I could not have avoided the complicated set-up by buying something else, Polar or non-Polar.  He redid the set-up for me, and went through the button procedure if one gets it working and straps on the unit and goes out exercising some future day.  His explanation was that it was more than just a case of hitting the middle button on the right.  (9) My preference would be for Polar to make a miniature EKG-quality wrist-chest combo unit that doesn't have all the bells and whistles necessitating all the set-up.  And that has instructions by somebody who has strong abilities in explaining things.  I say that as somebody whose pre-retirement career, for 30 years, consisted basically of explaining things.  (10) Postscript: A few days later, I returned to the sporting goods establishment.  The sales rep called the Polar help desk, and got through.  He got put on hold, but began fiddling with the wrist unit, and suddenly got a heart rate reading without knowing how he'd done so.  That lasted until I went to bed, although it was too late on a Friday to do the trial walk on the gym treadmill.  (11) The next Monday, I again could not get a heart rate reading, pressing buttons in a panicky mode.  The little instruction booklet is absolutely horrible.  Instructions intended to explain a product need to do that in a square one, square two, square three, etc., sequence building the user's education.  This doesn't.  I called the 800 number at Polar, got a series of options none of which related to heart rate monitors, picked something else, and ended up on hold for a long wait.  I hung up, returned to Amazon, and downgraded my rating from a 3 to a 1.  (12) I tried the 800 number at Polar again, got a tech rep named William.  He sent me a new sensor to fit on the chest strap.  (13) It arrived four days later, and had a batter in it.  I tried it.  The product still does not work.  (14) I called the 800 Polar number, and got put on hold for upwards of 15 minutes without getting anybody.  Their help desk people according to the recording had a high caller volume.  Yes, I very well can imagine.  I'm headed back to the retailer to see if maybe the wrist unit is what's bad, despite appearances. product_title: Talley 1in Model 110-111-112-114-116 Extended LowFlat Rear
review_headline: Functional Product that Looks Good Too
review_body: I use Talley or Warne products for all of my scope mounting. After having screws break on rings with only two screws each in heavy recoiling applications, I have for the past 7+ years insisted on rings with 4 screws each. The product in reference, extended ring/bases - low height, worked great to put a Leupold 2.5-8 on a flat receiver style Savage 110. These are the best option out there for mounting shorter, lower/mid power range scopes on long actions with wide mount spacing such as the Savage 110 and Remington 700; they look nicer and are far sturdier than STD or dovetail designs that necessitate  offset rings to facilitate mounting many styles of scope on a long actions, and they don't protrude too far into or entirely over the action opening like extended or 1 piece baces do, which effectuates easier loading and, more importantly, jamb free ejections/feeding in adverse conditions and positions. One consideration when selecting this product: These particular ring/mounts work well with scopes that have 4\\" eye relief and a non-critical eye box, as the front ring position/base thickness will not always allow many scopes with lesser eye reliefs to be mounted far enough back to instantly obtain a full view on all magnifications. Shouldn't be too much of a concern, as 4\\" of eye relief and a non-critical eye box are excellent features to have on hunting scopes anyway.

product_title: SABRE Red Pepper Spray - Police Strength - Spitfire- Most Advanced, Compact & Fastest-Deploying Key Ring Spray with Refillable Case
review_headline: Comfortable to carry, easy to use
review_body:
From my wife Sarah: I bought this to take with me to places like the parking garage at the mall, etc. Although I have not tried to expel the pepper spray yet and hope to never have to, here's why I like it so far:

- It's extremely light and compact, which makes it easy to carry around.

- It's convenient that it attaches to my keys, especially since I always have them out when I exit a building. I don't have to remember to take it because it's on the key chain.

- The pink color makes it easy to spot in my bag so I can grab it quickly.

- It's extremely simple to use.

- I see that another reviewer said that it's easy to discharge this in your purse. I haven't found that to be the case. I think it would be very difficult to do by accident and I haven't done that so far though I take it everywhere.

- Because it's a small hot pink object, it's not going to look very intimidating, which could be a negative. On the other hand, you'll have the element of surprise on your side because it doesn't look threatening.

I gave it 4 stars rather than 5 because I see consistent reviews stating that the spray itself does not go a full 8 feet away as the directions state, and that it's a mist rather than a strong spray so it's just as likely to hit you as the attacker. As I said, I haven't sprayed it, but if a lot of people say this same thing, it's important to take that into account.Lastly, I feel that it looks rather phallic, and I find that a bit embarrassing to carry around.

product_title: Barnett Predator 375 CRT Crossbow Package Arrows Scope
review_headline: Get a good target, I started with a bag of corn
review_body:
this thing is sick. after a crash course in the basics of crossbow and learning some hard lessons. this thing is really accurate, bolts touching at 30 yards. some problems....
1. Get a good target, I started with a bag of corn. blew right through that, hit a metal target and ended up 40 yards in the field with damage to the bolt from impact with the metal target (side of bolt from impact with target and rocks) definitely not a bolt quality issue but the amount of force it hits with and how it hit...totally understand. ended up using two bags of corn and a travel bag stuff with rags and old clothes as a target. well that finally stopped it from blowing all the way through but the fletchings were getting messed up. this affected accuracy. New bolts and accuracy was back on. got a real target with heavier bolts and still sinking in to the fletchings...
2. scope- the scope i received worked just fine, had a flaw in it though, with the illumination feature. it would illuminate but the light would bleed out from the aiming circles making it impossible to see in low light. Amazon and Barnett very quickly made it right and despite this flaw am very happy. i am sure there are better fancier scopes out there, but this one does the job just fine. when mounting make sure the crosshairs are truly leveled with the crossbow otherwise and distances it will be off to one side or the next.
3. Bolts- buy extra bolts.... you will most likely damage the ones you have. the bolts are just fine, actually seem very high quality, but this thing is a beast. i bought heavier bolts to slow it down some which seems to help with depth of sinking into he target (enough to not damage the fletching) but it literally knocks the target around and have to fix/re position the target.
4. not an issue just some tips and tricks i learned the hard way.
a. when putting together be meticulous in following directions. even do some research, its not very hard but can be easily screwed up. Use lock tight on the bolts for assembly and be sure to re-tighten after some usage.
b. Lube it religiously. rail lubing even more then it calls for. as I became accustomed to it, if you lube it consistently the same way it will be a tack driver.
c. buy extra lube, it goes quickly
d. Keep crossbow level when firing... really important for accuracy
e. mark your string and ensure it is centered every shot....again really important for accuracy
f. do some research on general crossbow usage and care, there is alot more to this then I thought
g. get a sling

In summary, you may be able to get a better crossbow with higher quality, better reputation etc etc. but for the price this thing will be hard to beat. its accurate, its powerful, it seems pretty high quality and the customer support is really good in my experience. it might be kind of big in comparison to others but not by much and I don't see it as heavy.
