review_headline: Maximizes space for fabric storage as "mini-bolts".
review_body: I bought two sets of these to organize my sewing fabric stash, and they work wonderfully. I had a fairly organized collection of fabric before, but the amount of ironing I needed to do to get the random wrinkles out before sewing was wearing me out. I am also limited on space for storing, and found that I was buying fabric that I already owned, or very close to what I already owned, because I couldn't see what I had. YouTube has great videos out there for how to fold your fabric onto the board depending on the length. I have fit everything from a fat quarter to 3 yards of fabric with no issue or compromise to the finished "mini bolt" uniformity. I have to double up the boards if I want to fold more than 3 yards- I have done up to five yards with two boards together. After folding all the fabric in my stash, I got so excited that I actually cataloged all of it by taking a photo with my phone and storing it in an app I bought so I have a digital photo database with me when I go to the fabric store that reminds me all of the fabric's details including what it's made of, where I bought it, what I paid, and how much I have. Sounds super nerdy, but it really renewed my excitement about sewing. I have also read blogs where women will store their vintage patterns on a comic book board, then in a comic book clear plastic bag and file it in an ikea storage box, which lends itself to cataloging your pattern stash in a database again.... I digress. Organization is great- and these boards help a lot.

product_title: KA-BAR 1258 Short USA Clip Point Knife-Hard Sheath
review_headline: Great knife.  Great sheath with multiple points of attachment and fastening options.  Allows for quick release.
review_body: This knife with sheath is exactly what I was seeking.  Smaller diameter of the handle so my not-very-big daughter can get a good grip on it.  Very good Kabar standards for the blade.  The sheath is pretty amazing.  Other knife manufacturers would do well to copy it exactly.  Why?  First, the friction grip holds the knife in place well and makes for easy extraction.  Second, as if that was not enough, they provide a snap closure on the top.  Third, if that was not enough, they provide a third snap enclosure that crosses diagonally from the back to cross the lower part of the handle.  So now you have three points of contact to secure the blade when bushwhacking through dense brush.  But you can also release the extra snaps when walking in more open terrain for those occasions when you want a quick release.  The kydex (sp?) sheath also provides numerous options for attaching to a belt or harness.  Use the standard hang-from-your-belt option when you need it.  But with the numerous holes placed on the edge of the sheath you can also attach the sheath to an H-harness or the shoulder strap of your backpack or fishing pack.  The numerous points of attachment and fastening options make this the perfect knife to have on your person when moving about in the mountains alone when you might need quick access to your knife.  Just a great product.  Perfect for my daughter.

product_title: SKLZ Super Sandbag - Heavy Duty Training Weight Bag
review_body:
For me this bad was not worth the difficulties I encountered. I will stick with kettle bells in the future. I started with sand... yes I know rice is probably the the way to go, but heck its a sand bag. After using way too much spatial reasoning and geometry skills, I got the bags in there, and then weighed the whole thing: 38lbs. I'm not sure there is anyway I could feasibly fit more sand into those bags short of somehow stretching them out.

After several workouts the bag is still holding up, though there is some pulling on the main of the stitching on the top handle.

I look at this duffel compared a patagonia black whole bag I have and I think they did a pretty good job on a bag is 1/3 price. But the using it part, and the part that it doesn't get the advertised weight, and all the trouble with it just seems like its not going to be worth the hassle for my needs. I looked up some things you can use this for that you couldn't use a kettle bell for and that a medicine ball wouldn't be quite enough and it does have a few uses, especially with a partner. I also put it in by back pack for a hike that I wanted to do in lieu of legs and it worked much better than I'm sure a weight would have worked, but I also could have just put gear in that pack.

So for me this is one of those workout items that I can will do without. Between the hassle of filling it and getting in there, the fact that its still a little underweight, and the fact that other people have sand leaking problems, I will probably just stick kettle bells and medicine balls.

Still SKLZ I think came close with this product, if they just get the manufacturing a little more squared away it will be a real winner for some people.

product_title: JumpStart 180 Fitness Low Impact Workout Videos with a Workbook(4 Dvd's)
review_body:
I keep talking about things that would help you make a change in 2015. I'd say I'm sorry but I'm really not. If I can inspire just one person to make a positive change in their life, I would feel like I have done some good. When this product, the Jumpstart 180 exercise system, was being offered for a product review, I was very interested because it seemed like something that could interest many of my readers in helping them make a lifestyle change in their fitness for 2015.

This is an 8 Week Low Impact Exercise System (created by a doctor of physical therapy) is specifically designed for men and women 50+ who are beginners to exercise. They may also be in pain, recovering from surgery, need to be more active, need to improve their balance, get strong, be more flexible and MUCH MORE! Exercises can be modified to fit your current activity level, or any physical limitation you may have.

This beginner friendly product contains 4 DVDs
-There are 7 different follow along 30 minute exercise routines
-An advanced exercise routine
-A FAQ video of the top 20 question/answers most men and women 50+ ask
-A workbook to track your progress and a calendar to tell you what routines to do on each day

The workbook included with this system outlined the ages recommended for this program -50 to 80 years old. Since my father is 85, we first put the video in to try out ourselves to make sure it wasn't too physical for my father. Thankfully, it was perfect for my father so we initially worked on the upper body and it was a nice stretching exercise for us as well.

Then, once we were certain my father would be okay using this system, we began the exercises with him, starting out with the first video. My father actually seemed to enjoy the video workout, which was very surprising. I never thought he would actually go through with using the workout system, but he surprised us all!

When we realized my father was taking it seriously, we stepped it up a bit and put in the DVD that addressed his balance. He said he had been having problems with his balance so we wanted to see how this would go. The nice part about the videos is that they offer a modified version of each workout so if you aren't healthy enough to do the full routine, you can still follow along in a modified fashion.

The exercises in each workout are simple but very effective. You don't need any expensive equipment, just a pair of light-weight dumbbells is all that is needed. Though the workouts are intended for older adults, anyone at any age or fitness level can enjoy this workout program. You can follow-along with the 4-DVD set that includes 7 different 30 minute routines along with a FAQ video. This is a good low impact workout. review_headline: Didn't fit over my prescription glasses
review_body: Description says they fit over "standard prescription" glasses.  With all the styles that exist today, what is considered standard?  I have slightly rectangular prescription glasses.  When lying on the table, I can place my prescription glasses inside the Champion Ballistic glasses.  However, when I try to actually wear them over my glasses, they won't fit.  I determined the problem is with the temples.  You may want to measure the temples of your prescription glasses.  Mine are 6 inches apart.  However, when I wear them, my head spreads them slightly further apart.  This results in the Champion glasses to not stay on my head.  Instead, they keep popping off/forward, rendering them useless with my prescription glasses.  If the frames of these glasses were a little wider, they would fit perfectly over my glasses.  My recommendation is to make sure to measure your glasses from temple to temple to avoid the problem I am experiencing.  Maybe I just have a big head?  Build quality, they seem to be fine as far as plastic framed glasses go.  Gave it 3 stars for the quality, had to knock off 2 stars for the fit.

product_title: Mossy Oak Men's Briefs (3-Pack)
review_headline: Mossy Oak Men's Briefs - 3 Pack - Nicely constructed but lack a bit of quality control
review_body:
I recently went on a waterfowl trip to Maryland and had a very good time, but wouldn't ya know that I forgot to pack underwear! That never happens, but it did this time. We arrived with enough time to pop over to the local Walmart, and these caught my eye. Interesting concept; and since we were there for a hunting trip...

These briefs seem well constructed, and I really like the waist bands (wide and hold snugly), but there are two things that were a bit of a bummer:

1. The three briefs were packed in their bag in a manner that the one camo brief wrapped around the other two. I thought that all three were camo patterned, and it was not until I got back to the hotel and opened the package that I realized the was not the case. Am quite sure that they are packed inside their plastic retail bag like that on purpose.

2. The two non camo briefs fit perfectly. They are very comfortable and fit exactly right. However, the camo brief has a different cut and the back is about 1.5 inches shorter than the back on the two non-camo briefs, so when I wear the camo briefs i have a permanent case of plumber's crack (even when just walking around). made me wonder if the camo brief was made in a different plant than the non-camo briefs.

I really like the fit & finish of the two non-camo briefs and my wife gets a kick out of the camo pair. I'd buy them again if needed.

Go for it.

product_title: West System 105 Epoxy Resin (.98Gallon 10.3-Pounds)
review_body:
This truly is a miracle glue. I've never seen a better one. Check out some of the projects done with it, primarily boatbuilding.

I bought this glue primarily for wood cabinetry; dovetailed drawers, faces, and less critical boxes. I even glue up thin strips and glue them on the drawer bottoms to help support the contents, and they don't sag a bit. If that seems obsessive, I used to do this professionally and my customers were wowed. The glue system performs flawlessly. You have almost an hour fit up time, and the cleanup is spotless and easy with alcohol. My joints are perfect.

I did an entire staircase with this stuff, and while the clamping was a pain (I didn't use a single nail or screw to see how it would do), it turned out beautifully; structurally ultra-solid; NO wiggle at all. I've never seen another this rigid.

I've also used it for a variety of other jobs, and the performance is always the same; solid performance you can rely on.

Don't skimp and get other brands; your material costs and time simply aren't worth the trouble.

Oh - and get the pump; better results, and you won't end up with extra resin or hardener.

product_title: Saucony Women's Bullet Tights
review_body:
I ran in these yesterday and am reviewing them based on my experience. First, the good. The fabric is smooth and on the thinner side, so they're not very compressive and they breath well. The wide waistband is flattering and doesn't create a muffin top. There are large pockets on each leg. I had my Samsung Galaxy S4 in one, it stuck out just a bit at the top and didn't fall out or move around when I ran. There is also a zippered pocket on the back. There are zippers at the ankles to make them easier to get on and off.

Now the bad--they kept sliding down while I ran. I'm 5'1" and 108 lbs and ordered the extra small, so I can't go any smaller. I never use drawstrings in my running tights or capris. These do have a drawstring, and maybe I'll try them. I do prefer my tights to fit without needing to use the drawstring.

Overall, I'd recommend them if the sizing works for you. The pockets are tough to find and these are a good size, so very useful. Also keep in mind that these are thinner, so not great for really cold weather. I wore them on a 40-ish degree day and they were adequate. I think they'd work down to 30 or lower, but wouldn't be enough to protect you against wind.

product_title: FitDesk 2.0 Desk Exercise Bike with Massage Bar
review_headline: Overall pretty darn good.  A few little changes would make it great!
review_body: Overall I really do love it.  It is comfortable, feels sturdy, and a nice quiet ride.  It's pretty easy to do things on my computer while I get some exercise.  There are some changes I would like to see in the product.  If you want to count down your minutes or miles or calories, there is no beep of any kind to let you know you reached your goal...it just goes to zero and then starts counting up.  If you are using a laptop, it completely blocks the electronic display monitor, so it would be nice to know when you reached your goal without having to keep checking.  It also has an odometer that doesn't seem to be able to reset.  It does track your miles per ride and this is able to be reset, but a feature that would allow you to track all of your miles for a week or a month and then clear it off would be really nice.  Or even better, a device that allowed for more than one person to track their miles would be even better.  The arm rest / massage bar really is not easily adjusted.  This isn't a big deal because I found the most comfortable position and just leave it there, but if you do want to change it to another position, it's not really easy to do.  A cup holder would have also been really nice!  I do think the price was a little high for it, but I have not seen any other similar products on the market...so it was worth it to me.

product_title: IRONMAN Gravity 4000 Highest Weight Capacity Inversion Table
review_headline: Works great for me and my family.
review_body: I'm not all to keen on what the Doctors say about these devices, but personally, I have noticed remarkable improvement in my lower back pain. This device is HEAVY, roughly 80 lbs, and requires a good amount of assembly. It also takes up a good amount of space, even disassembled. Ensure that you inspect the item thouroughly when it arrives for both parts and damage. The one I recieved had 100% of all parts, however there was a small dent within the framework in a benign part of the system, so safety-wise, its good to go. There's an adjustment strap which will allow you to choose how much inversion you require, ensure you adjust properly before using. I will say though that you will probably need pants on or socks at a minumum for ankle support. The ankle end that holds your feet can cause a little bit of pain in the ankles regardless of how tight you close it on your legs. When you invert, your body slides slightly down the mat, which now your body weight is solely rested upon your ankles. If you have ankle issues, be warned, and you may want to talk to your doctor before using. I'm 6'0, and 188lbs, and in good shape. This works great for me. If you are clinically obese, you may want to consult your doctor before useage of this device please read the item description for weight capacity. This device is very easy to manipulate, so, getting back up from an inversion requires little arm strength, just grab ahold of the bars and "sit up". It's worked well for me, and I have noticed improvement. Look at the YouTube videos concerning this device and the website for Ironman before purchacing. Good luck!

product_title: Quarrow Turtle8 8-in-1 Pocket Tool
review_headline: Take the cash out of your wallet and light it on fire. Watching that would be more worthwhile than buying this.
review_body:
You could probably use two sticks and a rock more effectively as a multi tool.

The good -- The plier head portion seems solid. If you weld some real handles too it, you could have a mediocre to low quality mini plier.

The bad -- Pretty much everything

--The plier handles are made of extremely thin sheet metal that flexes. The handles are warped and bent straight out of the package. One very small screw is all that attaches each of the thin sheet metal handles to the plier head. Any actual use of the pliers (even minimal) will bend and flex the handles. I would not be surprised if the screw pops through the handle with any kind of real pressure. Even if the handles and attach points were built well (which they are not), they are very awkward to use because of the shape.

-- The "tools" do not lock in place. They don't even have springs to hold them open like basic old non-locking knives. They just swivel on a rivet, no positive hold open at all. Once they loosen up, they'll be flapping around freely. Now, it does have a spring tensioner built in but, it is so poorly made that the spring doesn't even contact the "tools" at any point. Useless.....

-- The knife has about 3/4" of blade that is sharpened so roughly that there is about 1/32" of burr on one side. The File actually has a decent little bit of rasp to it, that is, on the 3/8" length of useable area. The Phillips driver is literally twisted. The four divisions swirl up to the tip and the sizes of each is different. They obviously hit this thing on a polishing wheel so it looks nice and shiny. Unfortunately, that also happens to round every single part of the driver making it 100% completely useless. The flat driver is again completely rounded, even the tip. There is no flat part on the flat driver to speak of.

No offense to the guy that put this in his PSK (personal survival kit) and in fact good on him for even havingone but, this thing is a joke. If you had to rely on this in a real situation you'd be up the creek without a paddle. Just because it's small, shiny, and has a couple extra "tools", doesn't mean it's worth using in a kit that you may have to rely on to save your life. Get a leatherman squirt or at least a decent small knife.

I understand that this is cheap so I shouldn't expect much but, like I said before, I could use two sticks and a rock more effectively than this and those are free.

It was a gift or I would return it immediately.

review_headline: Very Light Weight; Seem To Draw Sweat Away From Your Body
review_body:
It is good there is a notice on the Amazon product page that you should order one size larger than you normally wear. The shorts run a little small. When I took them out of the box and held them to my waist I was afraid even one size larger might not have been enough, but there is good elastic, so they fit fine.

These shorts are good looking and very comfortable. So lightweight it is hard to believe you have them on. And the legs don't go below the knees. The long \\"shorts\\" I see young guys wearing at the gym are not for me.

The shorts are very comfortable even in the hot weather we have in the Dominican Republic where I live. Besides being very lightweight, they seem to draw the sweat away from your body

The drawstring is thick enough to last, and it's length is about right. Also, the ends are sealed so that the drawstring will not unravel (like the ends of shoestrings are sealed). That is nice touch that I don't have on my other gym shorts.

I don't want to over state concern about the lack of pocket, but it is a problem for me. Without a pocket, I have to carry my cell phone in my hand from machine to machine when working out. Not the end of the world, but a nuisance. If I was accustomed to keeping my wallet in my pocket while working out, I would be even more concerned.

Because the shorts do not have a pocket, I am giving them 4 stars. I think most people would prefer a place to put a wallet, cell phone, keys, etc, when wearing them.

I was sent these shorts and asked to try them, then write a review.

review_body:
first off, this unit is pretty solid and holds zero with no problem.
pros- compact, light weight, has ir pointer, clears front sight base on my ar15 mounted ontop the handguard, its very solid, remote switch works great. both lasers are very bright. it comes with velcro to atach switch to what ever u want. the top rail would be perfect for a mini red dot sight to be used, side rails are worthless tho. it does what the description says!

so if you want an ir laser without spending a grand this works really good, the green laser is great as well, if your looking for a peq or dbal clone, this isnt it, its too small and square to pass off as one. oh and when mounted ontop it clears your front sight tower on an ar15. so yeah for the money its worth it. id go with one of the HFIRE lasers sold on here, i had one and it worked great and looked alot like the dbal lasers.

product_title: Basis Peak - Ultimate Fitness and Sleep Tracker (Matte Black/Black)
review_headline: Best health analyzer - however not a real sport watch.
review_body:
I upgraded my FitBit Force to the Peak. So far I like it (2 weeks of use). I like the accurate and constant heart rate reading. The sleep record pattern is much more elaborate than anything else I have seen before and "seems" accurate.
What I don't like:
- Although the web interface is cool, it doesn't connect with anything else so your datas sit there but you can't sync with MyFitnessPal or any other health app.
- No sync with the iOS Health app.
- The bluetooth link was finicky at the beginning, keep dropping but it seems fine now after I reset the Peak thrice.
- You can't stay on the heart rate screen, it automatically come back to the time after a few second so it's not great for exercising.
- The Peak sometime think I am sleeping when I am just seating on my couch watching TV.
- The automatic detection of walking is heratic at most. It's whenever it feels like. I haven't tried the biking option yet.

Conclusion: I like the peak and I think it's the best of his kind currently on the market. I can't wait for the extra features promised by Basis. However I also own a Suunto Ambit and I keep it for real exercise as it provide features the Peak doesn't have. the Fitbit is gone.

product_title: BARSKA 6-24x50 AO Varmint Mil-Dot Riflescope
review_body: This is a good scope for the money.  It is a varmint scope...ok, this means it is meant to be used with smaller calibers, like the .22 family, .17, maybe a .22-250.  Don't put this on a .308, it won't hold a zero, or will crack the glass. It's not meant for the bigger calibers!!!  It can be a bit blurry at times just mess around with the Adjustable Objective, if you are shooting on 24x make sure your parallax adjust is spot on or it will be blurry.  Other than the parallax adjust being a bit finicky. Make sure you buy higher scope rings so that 50mm objective can have clearance between itself and the barrel.  I had it zeroed in 2 rounds and held a nice zero.  Zeroed a Ruger 10/22 @25yds shooting 40gr Remington .22lr. Dead-on @ 25 yds. Dead on @ 50yds.  about 8 moa hold @ 100 yds (last mildot on reticule) about 8" drop at 100yds with the rounds I was using.  There are two little screws that hold the adjustment knobs on.  You can reset the turrets to zero if you wish, and just adjust for target distance that way.  Honestly, its a $60 scope, so I am afraid to do this, I'll let ya'll know if it works.

product_title: 30 Caliber Aluminum Gas Checks (.0130 Thickness)
review_headline: Effective but ugly, you get what you pay for.
review_body:
I ordered a sample pack from VulcanChecks of all the three types that they make (.0130 and .0145 Aluminum and .016 copper) I applied them to Lee C309-200-1R bullets. My previous experience was with Gator Checks which snap right onto the base of this bullet.

First off, I grabbed my calipers and could not discern any thickness difference by measuring the rim of the 2 different aluminum checks. They appear to be identical, and they seat exactly the same. The outside edge (bearing surface during firing) of the check is pretty rough until I run it through the sizer, then it cleans up pretty good. For whatever reason, every single gas check has a little "chunk" taken out on one side of the rim. It doesn't seem to affect anything, but cosmetically, it's a detractor. The copper checks are the same way. My Gator checks are nice and smooth and pretty, these are rougher and have this little "bite" taken out of the rim. It's very small and I can't say if it would cause any instability, probably not, but it's there for better or worse. You can see the "Bite" mark on the checks in the picture on their website, but it seems smaller than on the ones I got.

Seating: I had to push each check onto the base to start it, then tap-tap-tap it on my press frame to fully seat. They don't snap on like Gator checks. Once applied, the seat is good and they don't seem loose. The copper ones were the hardest to apply since the metal is harder.

Conclusion: I will buy more of the aluminum ones just because they're so cheap, but the quality could be better. For copper, I would stick to Gator or your other favorite gas checks. I think Vulcan has room to improve quality control. I have not shot these yet, I haven't had a chance to get to the range yet.

review_headline: Broken after 20 shots... go with Aim
review_body:
Broken after 20 shots... go with Aim's scout scope which looks very similar to the non-illuminated NCstar scope... in fact might be the same thing. Mosin 91/30 with a universal brass stacker mount (see my aim scout scope review for a much more positive experience).

Optical clarity: Surprisingly clear... has a slight yellow haze when u compare to higher end scopes (my vortex viper PST FFP $900 scope). But pretty darn clear.

Turret adjustments: This is where this scope got 1-2 stars. The windage adjustment would not hold up to the Mosin 91/30 recoil. I noticed after I zeroed (5 shots), that my group really started to open up. I'm a 0.5 MOA or less shooter with my remington 700 308 so I know i'm steady as hell.
I kept trying to shoot and noticed it kept migrating and migrating. I noticed the turret was loose and when I had to readjust to get it to catch again, the zero was WAY off to the right. I could not adjust anymore. That too me is unreliable and deserves a return...

Durability: See above...

This scope gets 3 stars only b/c of the optical clarity but easiliy 1-2 stars for durability.

review_body:

product_title: The GunBox Biometric Hand Gun Safe
review_body: I gave this 5 stars because it's the best mass produced biometric small gun safe you can buy. Unlike all the others you commonly see, it can't be bumped open because it has opposing latches. It's very well constructed and is nice looking without screaming I'm a gun safe. The fingerprint scanner works well, it doesn't require you to slide your finger you just touch the pad, press, and HOLD your finger there until it opens. Holding your finger there greatly increases the chance it will open the first time. I programmed all my fingers a few different ways and would say it's 95% accurate. I suspect the people having problems with the finger print scanner are just clicking their finger on the pad. With the RFID scanner it opens every time. The purpose of these type of safes are to keep kids out but allowing your weapon to be accessed relatively quickly and this job it dose well.  That being said its not perfect it could use more interior height, thicker full size pistols will need to be placed in just the right place for the lid to close without the gun touching.  I was abLe to get my sig p227 and an extra mag fit once I found the best spot and my Ruger sr9c fits with the grip extension on and 3 extra 10 round mags. In regards to the recall mentioned by others I believe the first generation was able to be bumped open like all the others on the market. This basic means if you bang the safe hard enough in the direction the latch opens the safe will pop open. The new model they are selling now can't be bumped open because it now has two latches that apose eachother. Keep an eye out when purchasing this so times the company has coupon codes available for purtchasing it from they're web sight. I purchased it on amazon because they wouldn't allow me to use a coupon code that had just expired. They are a small relatively new company with one product but they wouldnt extend the discount to me. They did however inform me that they would give me a discount if I were law enforcement or military. Now I agree with the military discount but law enforcement? They don't get paid to do a job like everyone else? Bottom line is if your looking for a small digital pistol safe this is your best option it's a little pricy but it's cheaper than the pistol your storing in it and just as important.

product_title: 5.11 Tactical Rush 72 Back Pack
review_headline: Great bag. Tried both the 24 and 72, and the 72 won!
review_body: Great bag. Love the quality on both the Rush 24 and 72.  I'm a huge 5.11 fan, being made in the USA and all.  The 24, being not as big as I wanted, I returned it for the Rush 72, which I'm much more pleased with. I work on film and TV sets, so I need a pack for my daily gear, plus rain gear when on location, "just in case". The 72 is not much bigger when not fully packed, it tightens up well, but the extra room is enough to make a huge difference in what you can carry.  So for me, it's a no brainier. That said, I found the 24 slightly more comfortable to wear. So, if all you need is a lighter pack, and you are traveling longer distances, then maybe the 24 is the better choice. Thankfully, Amazon has a great return policy, and I was able to swap them very quickly.  I even had both at home to try out back to back for a short time. If you're not sure whether you want the 24 or 72, go with the 72, you won't regret it. I wish I could afford to keep both.

product_title: Onyx-Arctic Shield-X-System Men's Arcticshield Boot Insulators (Real Tree)
review_body:
I purchased these on 10/27/14 for the deer hunting season. I used them every time I went out and the temp was below 40. They work fairly well, but even better if you slide in a Hot Hands packet to keep you warm. I wore them with 800g insulated boots in temps down to upper 20's and my feet were always pretty warm and toasty. That being said, I wear a size 10 boot and a size large was too small in my opinion. I could zip them up, but not easily, and during the coarse of the season, one cover had the zipper pull break off, and the other boot had the complete zipper assembly becoming seperated cover from the bottom. I only put them on/off when getting into and out of the tree stand. Had I ordered an XL, I'm not sure this would have happened, but hard to say. I just sent an email to Onyx, to see if they can do anything for me, given the covers are only 2 months old. I'll update my review if they respond to help me out. Otherwise, I can only rate these a \\"3\\" because they work decently well, but have issues with holding up.

1-24-15 Edit: This is a follow up review to the original 3-star review above. Through email, I contacted the company, provided proof of purchase, pictures, etc of the problems I had and they sent out a brand new pair free of charge. AWESOME customer service! Would definitely buy again!

product_title: FitDesk 2.0 Desk Exercise Bike with Massage Bar
review_body:
Yes you can cycle and type at the same time but it will take time getting used to it.....

Parts
The drawer was broken in the package. I will probably return it but it is unlikely I will ever use the drawer so will save myself the headache of the whole returning process.

Saddle Comfort
I found this to be very comfortable - early days yet as I have only spent 30 minutes on the bike

Back pains
My back was feeling uncomfortable after a few minutes and I do not have back problems. Ergonomically speaking I don't think I will spend more than an hour on this bike without taking breaks

Cycle Meter
It would be nice to have a sensor one can use to sync to an iPhone or Android. As the wheels are covered you can use a normal cadence sensor like Jarv or Wahoo - but I am trying to see if any of these can be adapted to us. I some how don't trust the cycle meter for accuracy. I did place my Fitbit to the pedal and I was able to count my cycling activity as steps. Each pedal counted as a step. This will have to do for now. Though I would like to sync to Strava and get some cycling miles in.

Massage Bar
This keep on coming off and we did screw it in. The left attachment looks bent. I will contact Customer Care and see what they say. But you do need this as a rest.

Laptop
The table is a bit low. I have had to put some books under my laptop to raise it to a level that was comfortable to use.

Assembly
Fairly easy to assemble. A friend came over and it took about an hour. We came unstuck when one of the screws on the saddle seat will not come undone. I had to take it to Home Depot the next day to have the screw loosened.

review_headline: ... a different one before and the quality was very good.. Now for my review of the ER-064
review_body: I bought this Elk Ridge knife because I had purchased a different one before and the quality was very good..  Now for my review of the ER-064..The quality of this knife if not what I expected, I have been a woodworker for over 35 years and when you work with a hardwood and the moisture content is above 7-8% you will get some shrinkage..and that's what happened on this knife handle, the rosewood colored part of the handle shrank .050 leaving .025 of the steel shank exposed above the handle, top and bottom and created gaps between the brass inlay, also all of the rivets stick out above the handle, not flush.  Now if you have the equipment to grind and remove the expose tang and give it a polish finish and can accept the reduce diameter of the handle, you may have an ok knife.  BTW I saw it yesterday for under 10 bucks, today it was almost 18??  I am going to try and contact the sender..not sure if it will do any good.  I will try and get a few pics later    UPDATE: Contacted Amazon..GOOD NEWS :They quickly sent a replacement, saw the package when I got home..opened it, BAD NEWS : only to find the replacement had the same issue only this one the handle was cracked on both side at the brass grommet.  The finish was not as nice as on the 1st one..and the rose colored handle had shrunk the same.  Now I have 2 to send back..  I will update if the third is any better, may just keep it..spend a few hours and replace the handle.  It is an awesome looking knife.

product_title: Arachnid Cricket Pro 800 Electronic Dartboard
review_headline: Good enough for home use but definitely not what I would consider "solid"
review_body:
[[VIDEOID:1e71eb076dcdd39ffcadc1864d6cd60b]] This is a review of the Arachnid Cricket Pro 800 dart game.

In days gone by I used to play electronic darts with my buddies for hours on end. I was really intrigued by this Arachnid Cricket Pro 800. With all the game play options, it really was a lot of fun to get back into darts.

This came with two sets of darts (3 darts/set) The shafts were already in place, I just needed to attach the flights and tips to the darts. Once I started playing, I immediately realized that these were not very good darts.The provided darts are quite light and for people with poor technique, you get a lot of bounce outs. Even I had what I thought were way too many bounce outs. The plastic tips are not very good quality either. In just my first 15 minutes of play I went through 2 tips. Just a single bounce-out can bend the tip to the point where you have to replace it or you will get a bounce out every time you throw that dart with the slightly bent tip. Fortunately for me, I was lucky enough to actually find my good set of darts that I used to play with years ago. I used those with much better results.

The row of buttons along the bottom edge of the board are kind of cheesy feeling. I really thought that at this price point a better quality button should have been used. I don't have any problems with them, it's just that they feel really cheap. Game selection is done by pushing the game button. Unfortunately you can only go through the games in one direction so it requires a lot of pressing to get to a high numbered game. For the popular games of Cricket and 301, there are dedicated buttons to immediately get to those games. The other buttons are for solo play, options, number of players, volume control, miss and bounce out amend and select bull.

The Heckler feature is fun for a while but it does get repetitive. Now that the thrill has worn off, I leave it off.

Game play was pretty good. I really don't have too many bounce outs. I do get some miss calls though. I'm still not sure why that happens but it does get irritating when you don't get credit for a properly placed dart.

The fun factor is great with this. I'd like to see higher overall quality of the game, particularly the buttons since this is not an inexpensive game. Given the overall quality and price I've got no alternative but to rate this 3 stars. If it were priced lower, or of higher quality, it would have gotten a higher rating. But I'm having a lot of fun playing darts again.I really don't have too many bounce outs. I do get some miss calls though. I'm still not sure why that happens but it does get irritating when you don't get credit for a properly placed dart.

The fun factor is great with this. I'd like to see higher overall quality of the game, particularly the buttons since this is not an inexpensive game. Given the overall quality and price I've got no alternative but to rate this 3 stars. If it were priced lower, or of higher quality, it would have gotten a higher rating. But I'm having a lot of fun playing darts again.

product_title: Seamax Blue Portable 12V Electric Air Pump for Inflatable Boat, Inflatable Kayak and More (No Battery)
review_headline: A bit pricey but worth it.
review_body:
August 7, 2016 Update
I did contact the pump company. They sent me (for $35) a replacement hose and some fittings to fix the old hose. The first time we tried to use the new hose it blew off the pump fitting, then on a second try the hose blew off the stand up paddle board. We ended up having to hold the hose ends to get the job done.

As I said before the pump is fine. It switches from high volume / low pressure to low volume / high pressure automatically. It inflates the SUP quickly and firmly. The problems are with the hose.

One problem Seamax related is the hose gets hot near the pump, and if the ambient temperature is high (perfect for SUP use), and if the pump is in the sun (where else!) it may overheat the hose. The new hose came with some black tape wrapped around the end. It seems the company did a fine job on the pump but failed to match the hose to the pump and operation.

I will now be going to the hardware store to see if I can find an alternate hose that can withstand the heat and pressure.

June 20, 2016 Update
We've now used this pump perhaps five or six times to inflate the SUP. It works fine and I wouldn't want to be without it. There's no way I'd want to use a foot pump after seeing how hard this pump works for five or more minutes to fill the SUP. We run it off a portable battery, which we purchased years ago as a jump box for our boat. That portable battery box has a motorcycle sized battery built into it.

The only problem we just had was the yellow hose blew out. That is a bulge developed in the hose and just as the SUP was at peak pressure the hose parted at the bulge. I'm on a trek to contact the company and obtain a replacement hose.

Original Review:
I bought this Air Pump for my wife's new Inflatable Stand Up Paddle Board (ISUP). The board has a maximum inflation pressure of 15 psi. This pump only inflates to a maximum of 11 psi, but that is more than adequate.

One complaint, which I was already aware of, is the digital display shows kpa instead of psi so we had to convert. Not that big of a deal, especially as the only use we have for the pump is for her ISUP for which we set it to maximum. Set it to 80 KPA and let her rip. No stars off for this.

It was a little difficult to get a sense of the size of the pump given the pictures included. The best indicator is the photo with what appears to be a standard car battery next to the pump. Upon receipt I was pleased with the small size of the pump, and how light it is for my wife to carry.

Even though it is only January and the ISUP won't be used until about May we decided it would be prudent to blow it up with the pump now to ensure everything works properly. We did that in the kitchen. The process was easy with one small issue.

Included was a small zip lock package with the hose fitting for the end that twists into the ISUP. The package label said there would be 4 gaskets but only 2 were included. I selected the larger gasket but it wasn't thick enough so I had to hold the hose and push it onto the ISUP fitting to make good contact. One star off for this.

We used a battery jumper box as the 12V power source for the pump; the same booster box we will use at the beach.

The ISUP began to fill quickly when we turned the pump on. I didn't measure but it seemed to take about 5 or 6 minutes, certainly well under 10 minutes, to fully inflate the board. With 11 pounds of pressure in the board we were surprised how hard the board was. The pump shut off automatically when the pressure reached 80 KPA as we had selected.

We then switched the hose from the left side of the pump to the right side and attached the other end to the board to deflate it. It only took a couple of minutes to deflate the board well enough to get a tight roll so we could slide the board into it's duffel bag.

These pumps are expensive but I read quite a lot of reviews regarding manual pumps to know this is the preferred method. Besides the combination of the inflatable board and this pump were still priced under the cost of most rigid boards. Now we can transport the ISUP in the trunk of our car, and take it on our 21' boat too.

As we've only used it once I can't speak of the long term reliability. Otherwise I highly recommend this pump.is pump were still priced under the cost of most rigid boards. product_title: McDavid 195 Ankle Brace with Stabilizer Straps
review_body:
I ordered this brace because I injured my ankle while training and lifted some heavy weight off a squat track wrong which resulted in some prolonged ankle soreness.

I've had bad ankles from playing offensive line in high school and having level 1-3 tendon tears in my ankles from those years past, I used to have two of these back then but lost them when I moved out of my parents house way back when. I can say that this is by far a great brace because the fit is snug and during my most recent injury my ankle has pain in the front that gives me pain when I'm on my feet for too long or walking a lot (live in a metropolitan city so I do a lot of walking). Since using this brace it has mitigated that pain because it is snug enough that it isolates where my pain is and allows me to walk normally and without a limp.

Comfort wise the brace is snug. I usually run a 9.5-10 shoe and in my walking shoes it fits fairly well an 8/10 fit, in my dress shoes for work it fits very good 10/10 but I do need to use a shoe horn to slip into my shoes. I ordered a medium in this case.

Practical usage of the brace when I'm walking home or to work it gives me maximum comfort and helps me forget that my ankle even hurts. When I'm training I don't feel any pain either but I'm not lifting with as heavy weights until I heal up. The support given in my opinion is around the 9-10/10 mark just because of the isolation during walking motions and the stability offered on the sides. When I'm on the bus standing up I can balance myself if there's weird motions as opposed to hopping about looking to grab onto something for support, and I can also jump 2 stairs at a time without worrying about pain from stressing it in different motions.

As far as putting the brace on or taking it off it is fairly straight forward. The side bands that form a figure 6 (I think it's mentioned in the description) help to provide that motion stability I mentioned previously, and the top bands that secure around the laces are all straightforward in attaching and removing. The laces and brace itself does run slightly tighter and more snug than any other brace, so you'll need to spend some additional time with that portion of it. If you have swelling then this could be good for mitigating the swelling (not a doctor or health professional) but if you're pain adverse then I'd exercise caution just because of how snug the brace can be.

product_title: Tops Knives Brothers of Bushcraft Beadblast Finish
review_headline: An overpriced 50$ knife that I wouldn't stake my life on
review_body:
I have had this knife for 6 months now, and I have put this thing through the ringer.
1. The sheath
A. This sheath is horrible this may be in large part to the fact that I hate kydex. If i want to announce my presence in the middle of the woods I wear kydex. This being said I've worn cheap kydex sheaths that blow this sorry excuse out of the water.
B. When sitting in the sheath the handle sits way to high to the point that if I fall there is a potential injury. The sheath does give you the option that you can rotate the knife and allow it to ride at a angle on your belt.
C. The ferro holder on this sheath is obviously made the magnesium striker that comes with the knife. As the above reviews states it's pretty sorry. I as well changed it out for the exotac however that or any other ferro rod does not fit well in the ferro holder.

I used the sheath twice then tossed it in the drawer since then I've switched to a leather bush style.

2. The knife overall is a well built knife.....somewhat.
A. The handle on this knife is phenomenal minus that stupid ferro rod striker on the pommel that doesn't work.
B.If you want to strike a ferro rod with this knife you have to either use the edge or the back of the tip of the knife. I have since used a grinder and ground down the spine of the knife to create useful tool in the bushcraft world, the 90 degree edge.
C. When it comes to batoning this knife does extremely well I have no complaints other that the fact that I wish that it held an edge a little longer. D.Feather sticks when sharp very well!
E. Skinning not so much. It got the job done but it took a lot more work than I expected. If you look at the tip of the blade you can see that it has a slight drop point design. Although this ideal for batoning the wood when cutting through the skin on the belly of an animal you use a two finger method where the spine of the knife rests in the palm of your hand and the tip falls in between your middle and forefinger. This is done so the tip does not pierce any digestive tracks and taint the meat. This knife is extremely cumbersome! I had resharpen the knife twice while processing a small game animal....
F. Fine carving tasks not so much.

Wouldn't stake my life on this knife!!!!!! It's backup knife if something was to ever happen to my main.
I don't hate this knife but I've held 40$ condors that do a better job. The only reason I'm giving this knife three stars is because I know that with some work and customizing I know that I can turn knife into a decent knife.

product_title: adidas Fit Smart - Fitness and Activity Monitor Wristband
review_headline: The Best for My P90X workouts
review_body:
After much research on getting a workout watch with heart rate monitor for my P90X routines, I decided to get this one. I was reluctant to buy it at first because of the total rating was only around tree stars or less when I was shopping for it.

However, when I read the negative reviews, they were all complaining about the initial set up process, rather than the quality and functionality of the product itself. So I took the plunge and, boy, I am so happy that I did. I have to thank the negative reviews because it drove the price down to far less than half, and now it's back up after I bought it.

The set up is a breeze for me with my phone and tablets. I guess one must have the concept that this is not a watch, but a computer accessory for you to wear in order to let it monitor your activities. If you treat it as a watch, you'll be disappointed because it's not that simple, yet it's not hard if you treat it as a computer accessory.

Even though I already own ([[ASIN:B00I6TUZJ8 adidas miCoach Heart Rate Monitor]] which is to be worn around the chest, I like this Fit Smart because it's rechargeable and the other one needs button type batteries, and I hate button type batteries because they are not commonly used like AA or AAA batteries that I have a lot of them (rechargeable) at home all the time.

As for usage, it takes a little bit to get used to, but nothing unreasonable. For example, I tend to start the workout and think it has begun but later I found out that it has not started recording because I forget to press \\"Go.\\" After the exercise, I tend to forget to press stop, which requires you to push the button for 3 seconds. Within a few days, I got used to it.

After exercise, all I need is to open the miCoach app on my phone or tablet and click sync to retrieve the data from the watch (note: it won't sync if the watch is not on, i.e. not showing time.) Wallah! All my workout results are transmitted: every heart rate, calories burnt, etc.

Please note that I only use it for P90X and mainly for monitoring heart rate. For that purpose, this watch is perfect for me. I am sure this watch is also good for running, but there are many devices made for running. Only this one gives me accurate heart rate with much lower price range.

I recommend it!ase note that I only use it for P90X and mainly for monitoring heart rate. For that purpose, this watch is perfect for me. I am sure this watch is also good for running, but there are many devices made for running. Only this one gives me accurate heart rate with much lower price range. I recommend it!

product_title: Versacarry Inside the Waistband Ambidextrous Gun Holster for .40 Cal Barrels
review_body:
I had been looking at the Versacarry for a while before I decided to buy 2: 1 .40 and 1 9mm. They are good at retaining the gun, but I think my most glaring problem can be summed up with a single word: Cant. No, not the contraction for cannot, bit the fact that the gun is 100% vertical with no adjustable cant fpr draw angle. If you love drawing your gun straight up, be my guest, but I like a little forward cant in my holsters. It's not UNcomfortable, but since there is nothing protecting your body from the gun, it can rub you if you aren't careful. Overall, I am glad I bought it, but it will definitely NOT replace my Crossbeed which blows this away for comfort and carry endurance.

Pros:
Inexpensive
Lightweight
Incredibly strong
Excellent weapon retention
Fits multiple weapons

Cons:
No adjustable cant
Fixed ride height
Generic design may not work for every gun
No inner trigger guard (safety issue)
Annoying break in period

product_title: Spyderco Southard G-10 Black/Titanium Plain Edge Knife
review_headline: Amazon is selling FAKE Spyderco Southards!!!
review_body: Amazon sold me a FAKE Spyderco Southard! I just received mine and several things didn't seem quite right. The blade is not black. The clip is not black. The titanium is not stonewashed, it's a smooth continuous finish. Screws are not completely countersunk. I went on Google and researched how to tell a fake and this is absolutely 100% a counterfeit Southard. I'm sending it back and ordering a replacement. If the new one is also a fake then I will buy one somewhere else.    This was not bought from a third party seller. It was sold by Amazon directly. If you have bought one from Amazon, please check your knife and make sure it's authentic. The fakes can be actually pretty difficult to recognize and are quite well made. Also the manual and box are spot on. It's possible this was a return that someone switched out with a fake, but the box was taped shut at both ends with no sign of tampering. I saw someone also received a fake brown Southard from Amazon. I don't know how this is possible -- I'd assume Amazon is getting these knives directly from Spyderco if they are the seller.    Anyway, be careful. Search Youtube. There was a very good comparison between a fake and a real Southard that went into great detail. It was about 24 minutes long. I suggest you watch it to make sure of what you have.    If I get a real Southard with the replacement order, I'll modify the rating to reflect the genuine product. But what I received only deserves one star.    ___________________________    I got the replacement yesterday from Amazon and it's a genuine Spyderco. I'm changing the rating to 4 stars. It's nice. Well built, but still not quite as nice as the Spyderco Manix 2 (which is so far the best built Spyderco I have seen). The action is pretty smooth, but using the two side by side, the Manix feels better to me. Also I think the Spyderco Rubicon flipper has a nicer movement than the Southard. One minor complaint about the Southard... the tip almost protrudes from the handle whenclosed. I can definitely see that being a problem if you reach for the knife in your pocket and catch a finger on the tip. Anyway, it's very nice but not quite 5 stars for me.

This combination works perfect. the bottom of the scope just clears the top of the rifle. I was able to leave the front iron on with no interference with the scope. The irons were way off on my mosin and sure i could Kentucky windage it in, but with this scope I was able to dial it right in at 100 yards. In low 2x this scope is great for fast target acquisition and maintains good eye placement forgiveness to around 4 1/2x, from there to full zoom it does get a little more picky on where you put your eyeball but manageable. Very clear lens provide excellent sight picture for a budget scope. Ive already tossed the packaging but this scope is made in either Korea or Taiwan either way its much nicer than the China scopes. I have one friend that also put this scope on his mosin after shooting mine, he is older with bifocals and had a hard time shooting the irons. And another friend has it in the plans for his. My goal was not to make my mosin a precision super long range rifle I just wanted to have the confidence that i was going to hit what i put the sight on reliably and cost efficiently and this scope met my needs. The only lame thing, I have seen the price bounce all over the place for this scope. I bought mine new (not a return) for $76.77 free shipping from Amazon themselves, not just a deal from a seller. But even at the current price I would buy another one if the need arises.

product_title: Leather Accessory Bands for Fitbit Flex
review_body:
In order to understand my review and thought process, I will write a few details about myself:

I'm a female with small wrists who has been wearing a fitbit flex, with the rubber bracelet for a year. I do not go to the gym, but I always walk 10K steps a day. I take the bracelet off when I sleep, shower and when I type/write stuff by hand. I wear it on my left wrist and is right hand dominant.

I get a lot of compliments, but the main one is "Cool! It looks like a watch!" And I think basically sums up my reviews of it (long and short are included).

The short review: It does everything a fitbit band would do and it has the glamour of the Tory Burch bracelets. But as a band, I would treat this band like you were wearing a watch. I don't think you would want to wear this to the gym or in a pool or even in the shower since it might wear and tear the leather, but if you do, it will be accurate in steps and everything else. Would definitely this to anyone that works in a professional setting and that wants to look like they are keeping fit while looking classy.

-------

The long review: I was torn between upgrading my flex to the charge, going fancy and getting a Tory Burch metal bracelet, taking a gamble and purchase a handmade "fancy-looking" bracelet on Etsy or just buying a new color rubber bracelet. While searching on the internet, I came across this product and thought I would try it out. In theory, for the price of three bands from fitbit, it offers both functionality, while it offers style and sophistication that the Tory Burch price tag could rival. So I bought the white one.

Immediately, I opened the bracelet and tried it on. First impressions was that it was light and looked stylish. The bracelet was hard to put on at first since you are trying to break fresh "genuine leather" holes, but for me, once I put it on, it stayed on. Also, the tracker compartment for me was really impressive. It opens from the front and has two magnets on each end which keeps the cover on. You can have the cover off using one hand, but after trying to jiggle my wrist in all directions and purposely tapping the bracelet to get the tracker out, I could not get the tracker to leave the bracelet- which is good since I never dealt with a front open tracker compartment.

I decided to test the bracelet out in the same situations I would with my rubber band.

Sleeping: it sort of felt the same as the rubber band. On some instances, I could feel the hard compartments but it wasn't painful- just weird feeling.

Getting it wet: I wore the bracelet while washing my hands and accidentally in the shower. The band seems okay and the tracker is fine. My only worry is that if too much water gets on the leather, it might get tough feeling, but I'm not at the point yet.

Being accurate: I tested both bracelets by counting the amount of steps in a small distances and to see if it would match. For me in that experiment, the numbers were accurate when executed. I did not have to worry about inaccuracies with the new bracelet.

The only future issue I can think of is how I can keep the bracelet from "breaking". What I mean is that the holes that clasps goes into "breaks" the holes and that the more times I take it off, the more "torn" the hole looks. I only have a fear that if I keep taking the bracelet on and off, I would make the holes looser and at one point, might have to worry about having the bracelet fall off without warning. This hasn't occured yet but I'm sort of sure it could.

With that being said- I really like this bracelet so far (I had it for about 2-3 days so far). I think it's a great look and material for the amount of money you are spending. I have been getting compliments left and right and it looks professional.

Definitely would recommend this to ladies who were thinking about the Tory Burch bracelet but has small wrist since that bracelet is one size fits all (meaning if you use the small bands, that bracelet would be a bangle and might not be as accurate as your rubber band)

Hope this helps!

product_title: LifeSpan TR4000i Folding Treadmill
review_headline: 4.5 Stars! STURDY/QUIET Easy assembly + No static with TrippLite Surge Protector.
review_body:
I would give this treadmill 4.5 stars if I could. My wife and I are very happy with it. Very minor issues. See bottom of review for suggestions on lube, surge protector & pad.

My situation: Upstairs treadmill, limited space, I am a work from home dad with a 4 month old kiddo so lots of short workouts, TV already accessible near treadmill, and it's on carpet. My wife and I both play soccer and go to the gym but use this treadmill as convenience for off days, rainy days and MONDAYS! LOL

After reading and researching for a couple of months I found this to fit what we needed comparing about a dozen treadmills. I specifically wanted a treadmill that was quiet, reliable and sturdy (in other words the handles/console didn't wobble excessively while you run).

Pros:
- Quiet & Sturdy - no wobbling handles/console. We have ours upstairs and it's still VERY quiet below 6.0 running speed. And even at 6+ the sounds you hear are thumping shoes and not the treadmill itself. Solid, stable deck!
- Very easy assembly that I should have probably used my own tools for 'cause the ones provided were a tad awkward.
- Easy console to use. I do manual workouts mostly anyway. Just push a button or two and incline or speed. Easy.
- Great incline - 15!
- LOVE the Speed & Incline Shortcut buttons. You can jump from 0 to 3.0, 4.0, 5.0 or 6.0 speed with one click... no endless up, up, up clicking on the arrow acceleration key. This is also true of the incline with preset option buttons not endless click, click, click... up, up, up.
- Console is simplistic and easy (also a con for some as mentioned below)
- Handlebar quick access buttons are great for incline or speed adjustments (although easily bumped as mentioned in cons)
- Aside from lube, the treadmill was ready to use as soon as assembled which was easy.
- Heart rate handles are quick and easy

Cons (minor to my situation but possible heads up for future owners):
- Heavy to get upstairs (we kept it in the box while moving). It is one solid piece that is not worth disassembling to move. Just find your strongest, most ambitious neighbor. And beer as incentive. :-)
- Console is a little simplistic. I am perfectly fine with it 'cause I don't need much but this is where I believe I should get a little bang for my buck or a lower price. I don't use the speakers or need fans. But the console could use an upgrade considering I spent $1900 and my friend spent $1500 (after tax) for a better console on another brand. Although I like my friend's console I didn't like his treadmill! Its a Proform 4500 I believe.
- Handlebars seem short. At the gym I feel like I can use the handlebars for support or for leaning on hard workouts. With this treadmill I feel like they're about 6 inches short and not as supportive. They are still sturdy however and I manage just fine.
- Handlebar buttons are bumped easily but as mentioned above they're also a pro.
- Deck is slightly narrower than what I'm used to at the gym, but most treadmills in this class were the same or only better by 2 inches.

To conclude, I think its a 4.5 Star that should be priced at $1600-1700 or have a more modern console (I paid $1799 + tax). The sturdiness and overall simplicity make it worth the money. I don't see much use for the speakers and the USB user setup is just OK. I don't even bother with it since I have a Fitbit and use myfitnesspal.

product_title: Rubber Cal Eco-Sport Interlocking Tile-Pack of 5
review_body: This product is aesthetically pleasing, durable and thick enough to provide protection of floors. However, they are not well manufactured. I purchased to cover a large area (~15x15').    The first problem to note, is that they are not actually 20\\" tiles, but instead 19.5\\"; this may be important if you are trying to buy enough tiles.    The manufacturer decided to use pins to secure multiple tiles together; this is a huge mistake. Besides being extremely difficult to get them together (when laying over a large area) without breaking the pins, the pre-drilled holes were not always made. Trying to do this yourself with a drill is more challenging then you might expect because a wood bit moves all over when trying to go through the rubber.    The tiles are not cut perfectly straight, so when you lay a large floor you end up with gaps ranging from 1/16\\" to 1/4\\" all over. This means any spills would require completely disassembling which could take hours.    The quality is great, but the flaws in design and manufacturing do not make this product suitable for a large floor cover. Had they stuck with the dovetails on most every other exercise mat, it would probably fit better and get a 5 star rating.    Another note about these tiles, they are slippery when wearing rubber shoes. This may be an issue as in my case, when you are using it for a home gym. Anytime you need leverage (stretching or certain exercises), you will lose traction. Another example, when I use my rowing machine, I have had to put another mat between otherwise the rower slides across the mats with every stroke.

product_title: Polar Loop Activity Tracker
review_body:
I've had my Polar Loop for about a year. I wear it daily and use it to be sure I am getting up and moving around throughout the day. I work at a desk - so it is easy not to. I love that I don't have to take it off to shower or when I go swimming. It tracks several things - your steps, your daily activity, and calories burned - those are the basics that you can actually see on the watch (it shows time too) when you are wearing it. If you install the Polar software on your computer, you will get more info and have the information personalized to you by entering in your age, gender, weight, height, and usual activity level through the day.

The activity portion of the tracker tells you how long you need to jog/walk/get up to meet your daily goal. So as of right now I've walked 7740 steps and to complete my activity goal I need to either jog for 17 minutes, walk for 40, or get up and move around for 2 hours, 13 minutes.

The biggest flaw for me is that I have never been able to get the Bluetooth to work with the tracker, the app will not recognize it. However, I do use the info that is uploaded to my computer each time I sync and charge the tracker. You can also see the hours you spend sleeping, which is a nice addition because you can add notes to the diary, and track why you were or weren't feeling hot that day. (Usually it's the sleep part for me.)

You can also get a polar heart rate strap and sync it with the loop for even more workout info.

product_title: Upper Bounce Indoor/Outdoor Classic Trampoline and Enclosure Set (7-Feet)
review_headline: There has to be a better way of doing this!
review_body:
Very difficult to install: I am pretty savvy with this sort of thing. They haven't made a piece of Ikea furniture that I can't assemble, but the part of the installation where you put the round part of the frame together was a real challenge! It took a couple of pretty strong guys and a wall to press against to get this thing coerced together. Even then it was out of round until we massaged all the joints with a rubber mallet. I would have sent the thing back if I wouldn't have trashed the box so badly getting it in the house.

Bad and incomplete instructions: The parts list didn't show the sleeves that go over the top enclosure or the little caps for the feet. Half of the screws for securing the top enclosure were self-tapping. This was not mentioned at all in the book. We had to use an impact driver with the self-tapping screws to attach the top poles to the bottom poles because the holes were on the wrong side! They include this hilarious little screwdriver with the kit. I would love to see someone use that to get those screws installed.

All that said, once we finally did get it together it seems pretty solid, and it is attractive, and my kids love jumping on it.

product_title: Fortress Alarming Quick Access Pistol Safe
review_body:
1) The safe I purchased was defective. It accepts my code but wont disengage the lock with 4 brand new batteries and no problem with the key override.

2) I receive a series of 5 beeps with flashing red LEDs but no mention of what it means in the instructions or their webpage.

3) Search for this safe on YouTube and watch someone pop it open with a screwdriver in less than 5 seconds.

4) The "bolt down package" means there are a couple holes in the bottom and a couple wood screws included. What a joke.

5) Thin enough metal I'm sure I could flatten with a hammer. 4 digit code ONLY. No more, no less. Gigantic barrel keys that only require about 1/8 insert to disengage.

6) The alarm, though annoying, is quieter than the input beeps and easily muffled.

Even at half the cost at the big box store, this toy wasn't worth the gas to buy and return it. Avoid this thing. Buy a cashbox with a keypad since the "security" is about the same.

product_title: TrailHeads Elements Touchscreen Running Gloves
review_headline: comfortable and warm (especially for their size)
review_body:
First off, the gloves are just what I could have most expected: light, comfortable and warm (especially for their size). They are tight, but in the way you want: they wrap your hand and keep in the warmth while, at the same time, conforming to your hands. They look good, but that for me is secondary.

The other great thing is the customer service. It would be a red-flag (and rating deduction) to say that my initial pair tore a bit along a seam within a few runs, but when I let them know they said that they had an issue (since corrected) with a Fall production run, and sent me a new pair for free (while having me keep the old ones... which I'll use if it gets really cold, or give to someone else) in a matter of days. And this new pair really does hold up, and seems clearly more substantial, so I expect them to continue to do so. That, to me, defines customer service.

I have heard that some companies fake reviews, but if there is anyway to check that I have ordered a ton of stuff from here on my own dime, and never written a review until I was impressed enough to do so now, I hope Amazon can show that this is legit.

For $20, my hands are completely warm even in wind, and what else could you ask for in a (now) durable glove, from a company that makes things right immediately when an issue does arise?

product_title: MIRA Stainless Steel Vacuum Insulated Water Bottle | Leak-proof Double Walled Cola Shape Bottle | Keeps Drinks Cold for 24 hours & Hot for 12 hours
review_body:
Purchased this recently for $15 after a $5 discount. I'm very impressed with the ergonomics and stylish shape of this double-walled stainless steel insulated beverage bottle. Very easy to open & close cap - no leaks, secure fit. Lightweight, good grip, easy to handle and drink straight from the bottle. Easy to clean as well - just use a long-handle bottle cleaner. Outside surface does not show any condensation either, but then again it's winter at the time of this writing. Now, size is a bit large but, as I mentioned, the ergonomics makes it comfortable to handle and drink from. Think of it as a large mineral water bottle with a wide mouth (like that of a Gatorade bottle) -- no issues there. Fits nicely in my cup holders, but I can see how it'll be too wide for the smaller cup holders (i.e. built-in cup holders on doors). I find myself enjoying my cold drink longer that I'm actually hydrating myself better these days, so ontop of all the good points with how this bottle is made, it's actually helping me health-wise as I tend to either be too preoccupied at work (or too lazy at home) to get up and get something to drink throughout the day and actually finish the drink by keeping the temperature relatively constant.

I didn't give it 5 stars only because the surface of the bottle gets either a bit cold or hot, depending on the temperature of the liquid inside. This means there's enough heat exchange getting through the double-walled structure. I don't experience this with my Nissan Thermos - http://www.amazon.com/gp/product/B00009V4FM/ - but then again they're not exactly the same type of products. However, for most of my own personal uses, this bottle provides enough insulation that my cold drinks stay cold enough for several hours. For example, I poured cold iced tea and added several ice cubes inside the bottle; it kept the iced tea cold although all the ice melted by the time I woke up and checked. This was about 12+ hours later. I have yet to do an extended time hot beverage test, so I'll make coffee tomorrow morning and update this review.

Please read the other reviewers' comments as far as how this product fares when left inside a vehicle in either a hot or cold day so you can gauge how this will do based on your lifestyle. review_headline: Great Value for a Indoor Biking
review_body:
Personal background: ride bikes indoor and outdoor, 160 lb - 5'11" - male

Order and shipment: the default shipping selection is the Standard which will charge you. make sure you select the Free Shipping. received it in 3-days.

Assembly: the bike is assembled to ~80 percent out of the box, the instruction is easy to follow, and the parts are made precisely for put the parts on the position and tighten up. Just follow the instruction step by step. Some improvement can be made.

First Feeling: the bike looks very good for this price, stable on the floor and sturdy while riding, easy to adjust the high of the handlebar and the high/front/back of the seat, adjust the force resistance and braking are linear and smooth

Fit rider height: My wife is ~5'2", and the lowest seat setting, line 1, seems still a little to high for her, but set to the lowest bottom position made her satisfied. I'm riding at Line 6 and the highest setting is line 10 for at least 6'5" and taller.

Noise: This entry level chain type bike does have a little noise while riding hard. I didn't readjust it due to the noise level is relatively low and tolerable for us.

Conclusion: Pros: great value for a basic full function indoor station bike. Corn: Slightly improvement on the instruction manual. I still have four hexagon flat round head screws, parts #34 M10x25, left after put everything together.

product_title: Bl Force Vickers 2-Pt Cmbt Slng Brwn
review_headline: Possibly the best AR15 sling available. Very versatile, very simple.
review_body:
The Vicker's Combat Application Sling (VCAS) is possibly the best on the market. At the very least, it is a front runner. I have previously used a BLACKHAWK! three point sling, a Troy one point sling, a MagPul MS2, a few different home-made contraptions, and most extensively and most recently the Viking Tactics sling.

If you are expecting something "cool", this sling is not it. The biggest advantage this sling has is simplicity. It works. It is a strap to secure the rifle, and can be tightened to help stabilize the rifle. That's what it does. Whereas other slings have complicated features that offer supposed advantages, when you're focusing on trying to get rounds on target and maneuver they tend to just get in the way. The VCAS is lean and sleek.

My two favorite things about this sling when compared to competition is the lack of a "tail" of webbing hanging free whenever the sling is tightened down, and the material the sling is made out of. The webbing is more rigid than the competition, and much less resistant to rolling and twisting. It also has less tendency for the adjustments to change unintentionally due to the nature of this material.

Comparing this exact product to the other VCAS slings, I really like the lack of padding. While the padding is comfortable, it means that a rather large section of the sling cannot be adjusted- it is fixed length in that area. With the model being sold here that is all webbing you have a much wider range of adjustment, particularly when trying to make the sling smaller. Why would you want it smaller? The obvious reason is if you are a smaller person. The other reasons are if you are not using body armor and want to be able to snug the sling in tight to act as a shooting aid. Most of the AR15 slings on the market are intended to be used with rifle plates, and are sized appropriately... if you intend to shoot with only soft armor, or without any armor at all, it is very easy for asling to be too big.

Overall, this is an awesome product. The build quality is exceptional, and the design is simple, effective, and very intuitive.

product_title: Sentry Solutions TUF-CLOTH
review_body:
Performs as advertised! The TUF-CLOTH comes saturated with Sentry Solutions' TUF-GLIDE.

Wiping down the clean metal components of your collectable knives with a TUF-CLOTH rewards you with a satiny shine that does indeed dry without an oily film. The treated metal resists stains from fingerprints and rejects dirt and dust. From the research I've done, the rust inhibiting performance of this stuff is about as good as it gets! For marine environments use the marine-grade TUF-CLOTH, as used by Navy SEALs.

For routine light cleaning I just use canned or compressed air, and a microfiber cloth to remove finger prints.

For more thorough cleaning, I blow away any debris with canned air, then use 90% alcohol, paper towel or cotton balls, Q-tips, and/or gun cleaning patches. I then thoroughly dry the surfaces with more canned air. Finally, I apply a coat of TUF-GLIDE to the blade, bolsters, and exposed metal surfaces. For some knives, I apply a layer over the entire knife--grips and all. Let the knife air dry for maybe a half hour, and it's good to go, though I'll sometimes apply a second or even a third coat to brand new metal.

This stuff gives a nice, even, satiny glow to my knife blades--even the black-coated blades. New black-blades may require two or three applications for an even finish, but after that, one occasional application will suffice. Here too, the blade will resist fingerprints and dirt. Let surfaces dry thoroughly between applications.

TUF-GLIDE makes the details in my Damascus blades pop! I condition these as I do my black-coated blades.

TUF-GLIDE also brings out the richness of bone, horn, and wooden grips, offering protection from water, skin oils and acids.

I apply TUF-GLIDE Lubricant via their Needle Applicator Bottle to all moving parts. A little goes a long way, but if a folding knife is stiff, I'll use a few drops, and once the assembly moves easily, I'll blow the extra lubricant out with canned/compressed air, and wipe it off. Be sure to shake the bejabbers out of the bottle before dispensing TUF-GLIDE, to ensure that the proper lubricants are getting where you want them.

The scent of TUF-GLIDE is not at all objectionable, to me anyway. It smells a lot like turpentine, which is something I grew up with. The smell dissipates quickly, and most of it will be coming from your cleaning patches and cloths--and the TUF-CLOTH itself. I seal the disposables in a plastic grocery bag, and return the TUF-CLOTH to its plastic jar. Easy-peasy.

If you don't use your TUF-CLOTH for actual cleaning, it will last indefinitely. You can occasionally revive the well-used cloth with TUF-GLIDE spray; just be sure to shake it well before dispensing it.

I presently don't use this product on my guns. I use Hoppe's Elite Gun Cleaner, Hoppe's Number 9 Oil, and the traditional silicone cloth. But I'm beginning to question that policy...

I give the TUF-CLOTH and TUF-GLIDE Lubricant a full 5-Stars, and readily recommend it to others!
