product_title: Windline FDL-4B Marine Removable Folding Pontoon Boat Ladder with 4 Plastic Steps
review_headline: Good ladder but there is a catch
review_body:
I have owned this ladder for two seasons and used it every other weekend April through September on a pontoon boat. The ladder will hold up fine if it's only used for ingress and egress. I had a teenager on the boat that used it as diving platform, diving off the bottom step, which sheared one of the aluminum straps that hold the top and bottom together. I was able to fix it by making another strap but for many that would have been the end of the ladder. Also the top of the ladder sits too deep int eh cups and caused them to tip outboard putting a heavy strain and distorting the plastic. The fix was it insert pieces of PVC pipe in the holes and secure them with SS screws to limit how deep the ladder inserted in the cups.

For the current price on Amazon $65ish its worth it but I would look else where if the price increased much. There are ladders that appear to be better quality and have different mounting methods for just over $100.

product_title: CFF Post Landmine Trainer
review_body: I love this thing.  My gym doesn't have a landmine so I have to put the barbell into a corner where it punches a hole in the drywall.  With this thing, I put a couple of 45 lb weights on the floor, and I'm good to go.  I'm taking a core class, where a hot chick teaches it (I would kill for her abs).  The class is more of a body weight core workout for thirty minutes.  On the off days, when I don't take the class I want to do some core exercises that are different from those she does in the class.  This is great for that.  I carry it in the bottom of my gym bag and use it every other day.  I'm seeing good results in my abs (partly from the core class, but also from using this on my days off).  The morning after I use this, I can feel it in my obliques (sides).  They are sore and tight.  I'm 60 years old and I might not have big arms and legs, but I don't want to have a belly like so many guys my age are getting.  It's working.  I've pulled my pants in and gone in two belt holes after about two weeks of working with it.  No weight change, just tightening up my gut.  If someone steals this, or if I lose it, I'll definitely buy another one.

product_title: Viper Dart Accessory: Soft Tip Darts Tune Up Tool Kit
review_body:
I ordered this kit just before the new season of my local dart league stated to refresh my darts. Overall, I like the kit, but I want to review each part individually.

TIPS
The 150 pack of tips are great. The tips are high quality and stick in the board well and consistently for the life of the tip

SHAFTS
Both of the shafts that come with this kit are longer than the ones that are on my darts, so I continue to use the ones I had. I tried the spinning shafts and they are much thicker than the normal ones so they mess up my throw. The aluminum ones are identicle to the ones that came on my darts, the only difference is they are about 10mm longer.

STEEL TIPS
I do not use the steel tips so I cannot comment on the quality of them.

FLIGHTS
The quality of the flights are the one downside to this kit. The are horribly thin, and if your dart doesn't stick in the board it will fall to the ground and break the flight. It comes with 12 flights and I have 2 left after about two weeks of playing.

O-rings
These are a must if you have aluminum shafts because they allow you to tighten the shaft enough that it wont come loose after every couple of throws.

DART ROSIN
I have never used rosin until now and I like how it makes my fingers feel when I hold the dart. It makes it feel like I have a much more consistent throw and less chance of slipping while I throw.

DART TOOL
The tool that I received with the kit was not the one that was pictured on amazon. The one I received is a better quality with more uses.

FLIGHT SAVERS
The flight savers are a waste of time in my opinion, they do not save the flights from anything and just get lost quickly.

overall, this is a good kit but the biggest disappointment was the quality of the flights.

product_title: Forgan F3i Hybrid Iron Golf Club Set 3-SW Mens RH Reg Flex STEEL
review_body: Never heard of the Forgan name brand before, but picked them up because of the great price and decided to give them a try. I'm a high handicap golfer who usually posts about a 90-95, so I was looking for a good set of hybrids to add consistency to my swing. Bottom line is they work. First time out with them shot an 86, just absolutely easy to hit solid and straight with a high ball flight. They completely eliminated the fat/chunk shots and the rolling/thin topped shots that used to be 20% of my swings. If your a scratch golfer who hits draw/fade on command I don't think this would be for you, but if your in that 90-100 range trying to add consistency and confidence I would highly recommend these clubs at a great value. In the past I've played nike, cleveland, taylormade, adams and go figure the cheapest set I've ever given a try has produced the best results for my swing. Truly surprised in Forgan clubs on 1st impression.

product_title: Training Mask 2.0 [Black Original] Elevation Training Mask, Fitness Mask, Workout Mask, Running Mask, Breathing Mask, Resistance Mask, Elevation Mask, Cardio Mask, Endurance Mask For Fitness
review_headline: Can cause you to inhale CO2 if worn while working out
review_body:
I wore this mask after running, while stretching, and in-between sets, for about a 2 week period (10 workout days).

When my heart rate is elevated, I breath harder and faster. If I wore the mask while my heart rate was elevated, I noticed that not all of my exhale was fulling expelling from the mask, and I was inhaling a portion of the air I was exhaling. I started to notice that I felt very lethargic, and somewhat nauseous, after working out when incorporating the mask.

I did not feel this way, doing the same workouts, without the mask. One could summarize that I felt lethargic and nauseous because the mask was intensifying my workout. I disagree. I think the mask was making feel lethargic and nauseous due to it increasing the amount of CO2 I was breathing in.

This mask should not be used while working out. If you do slow, deep breathes, with this mask on, while not working out, it will work as it was designed to. Slow, deep, breathes will better expel the CO2 from the mask. It does not mimic elevation. It restricts your air, and makes it harder to inhale.

I recommend doing some research before deciding whether or not this mask will increase your stamina. In my opinion, it does not. I would not recommend this mask.

product_title: Revolution FIT 3-in-1 Exercise Balance Board Training System
review_headline: Versatile training and rehab tool for runners
review_body:
This is a really awesome set of bases for a high quality board. I had just read "Anatomy for Runners" (highly recommended for any and all runners serious about improving form and biomechanics), and Jay Dicharry (the author) talks about the place for rocker boards/ balance boards for improving strength (and of course, balance). The board pictured in the book is the Vew-Do Zone, which was where I started my hunt for a balance board. I loved how it had three bases.

Vew Do is however out of stock of the Zone board until next year, and I was very eager to get started on implementing this supplemental training to improve my runner. I spent over 6 months this year sidelined from running because of a knee injury. I thought I just had bad knees, but reading Anatomy for Runners helped me see it was more about my form and underlying weaknesses. So investing in a high quality training tool was very worthwhile to me.

This FIT board I have found to be a high quality product. Unlike some boards (like for instance those by Vew-Do), the bases do not lock onto a railing system under the board. This makes it more versatile in my opinion.

I use the rocker base for ankle strengthening as well as squats, the wobble platform also for ankle and foot strengthening. The rolling platform is really a blast, and has already improved my balance a lot.

You can really get a great workout with this board as well. I haven't fully explored the uses of a balance board outside of those specific to runner strengthening, but I know there are many. It would benefit any athlete I am sure.

This company has really great customer service. I highly recommend this product, and think you get your money's worth with the three different bases. Most boards only have one, but truly all three are useful!

product_title: Primos Bow Hanger
review_body:
This is a stout rifle and bow hanger. I've hunted it with both my Bear bow (only 4 lb) and my Rem 700 30.06. It holds both, as well as accessories (grunt call, range finder, binocs, etc.)...with no issues. Screws easily into the tree. It also folds up very nicely, with the hook helping it stay closed. I simply strap it to the front bar of my climber and climb the tree.

The only complaint that I have is the arm itself does not swivel at the "elbow". When properly installed, it sticks straight out from the tree. It won't articulate to put your bow right at your left hand. That was kind of an unexpected bummer. Something I'd have probably known if I'd checked it out at a store first.

All-in-all, I like it and will continue to use it. I'd also recommend it to others with only the caveat I've stated above.

product_title: B-Square Bubble Level-Weaver rail
review_body: I really like this level. Other reviewers have indicated that it is made of inferior materials. I took  this into consideration when ordering it. Mine appears to be made of decent quality aluminum. The spirit level is apparently made of a type of plastic. The indicator in mine was very well affixed and did not require regluing as some others have noted. The base was flat and made for a nice mounting surface. I used a drop of blue Loctite and tightened it appropriately and it neither bent or broke as some other reviewers have stated. Once it was mounted I checked level using a small Stanley level and they both agreed. Mine is mounted behind my Bushnell AR22 2X7 scope. It is not easy to see the indicator because of the scope size. I did not lower the score for this since each application is unique. For leveling a scope or as an anti-cant device I think you would be hard pressed to beat it for the money. As mine is mounted on a Colt M4 Ops 22LR I doubt recoil will be a factor at all. But even on higher recoil weapons I feel based on mine that they will stand up to a fair bit of use. For the money I feel like it hard to beat.

product_title: BeamLOKR Shotgun Flashlight Mount, No Rail Needed, 1 Second On/Off Magnetic Quick Release, Ideal for Home Defense, Multiple Guns
review_headline: A Must Have Product for Any Shotgun Owner.
review_body: I have owned one of these for over a year now, both the Shotgun unit and the Rifle unit.  I recently purchased a number of these for Christmas gifting.  They really are one of the most innovative and useful gun gadgets you will ever own.  Simply stated, the BeamLOKR allows you to attache a flashlight to virtually any long arm, with a simple snap of a magnetic mounting bracket.  This particular model is for 12 ga. Shotguns and comes with a pretty nice little light....however, you can easily snap in your own flashlight if you own one. (Any one inch diameter flashlight will fit, I usually use a mag-lite XL50, but virtually all flashlight companies make a one inch light.)  This device allows me to use my basic Ithaca 12 ga. bird gun for home defense purposes...However, I have friends who use it on their home defense style shotguns just fine (like the Remington 870 series).  This system is mounted on the barrel, and it handles recoil just fine.  (Just be certain not to mount it in the magazine tube, it is designed for the barrel.  The magnets never touch the barrel so no scratching will take place, they float just off the metal.  I like being able to move it easily from weapon to weapon.  The 12 Ga, Unit fits many thicker barrel long guns. For example I also use this on my Marlin .357 lever action rifle, my grand daughter's Red Ryder BB gun, and even my bull barrel Ruger MkII pistol.  It is very versatile and you can not beat the price.  Once your friends see this, they will all want one, Trust me!

product_title: Bushnell PowerSync SolarWrap Mini USB Charger
review_body:
This is a very portable device that will give you a little charge for your USB devices. It is light and rolls into a small roll (a little less than 6 inches long) that easily fits into a purse or backpack, though when it's unrolled the solar panels are sizable, about 11" by 3-1/2". While it is easier and more reliable to charge this device using a physical connection, you can also build a charge using the solar panels, though this requires a hefty time investment and good weather. Still, if you're out and about it's easy to have this charging, or if you plan ahead you can plug it in on your off hoirs and have a quick charge ready when you need it later.

If you're smart about using this it can be an excellent source for an energy boost to your USB devices. It would be a decent addition to an emergency kit. But it is not a super tech device that will be effective if you don't consciously plan and use it.

review_headline: A Worthwhile But Not Essential Piece of Equipment
review_body: The perfect Fitness Ab Carver Sport does give a good abdominal and core workout and it does, in the process, work out your arms, some of your chest, and your back to an extent. It is easy to transport so it could add to your fitness routine when traveling. However, whether or not it does a better job than a non-equipment abdominal routine is a toss of the coin. Also, if you don't have good form and roll to the left or right you could potentially injure your back. If you need this equipment because you find an abdominal routine onerous then by all means get the Perfect Fitness Ab Carver Sport. It won't break the bank and if it motivates you to work out then it is all worth it. However, don't expect it to do a better job than a good abdominal routine. Instead let it serve as both a reminder and an effective ab toner.

review_body: We bought two combos, one for me and the other for my wife and we absolutely love them. While the reels can't be touched in my opinion the rods need some quality improvements. While frustrating as it is, I still think these Penn inshore reels are the best. Hopefully the Squadron rod will not falter. I did contact Penn and they said I could send back and I would have to pay for shipping at $19.95 per rod. While I can get a new rod for $40-$60 bucks its not very cost effective to send back for repairs. All I ask is to improve the quality of the rod guides you use!! Fish ON!!

product_title: Mpow® Dolphin Smart Bluetooth 4.0 In-car Speakerphone, Hands-free Car Kit, with NFC, Voice Commands, Motion Detection, Noise Reducing for iPhone 6 5S 5C 5, Samsung Galaxy S5 S4 S3, Cell Phones and Other Android Apple Devices
review_headline: Nice Speakerphone, good Battery life with auto OFF & ON functionality
review_body:
In the box, you get the hands free speakerphone and a microUSB charging cable. The speakerphone is built very well, the button control surface is glossy finish plastic with the speaker area covered with perforated nylon cloth over a plastic grill. Rest of the body including the clamp shape and rear side is made of rubbery plastic for a firm grip with the car's sunvisor.

It features Bluetooth 4.0 with EDR profile for quick and efficient connection. I had no trouble in pairing and connecting it to my Nexus 5 phone. Coming to the features, the speaker has power ON/OFF button, volume control buttons, mute button, and dial button. It has a standard microUSB port for charging its battery. It gives a indication voice when powered on and when connected to phone. The speaker gets fully charged in about 2 hours time, and during this time a red indicator glows until full charged. During my test I got a total operating time of around 12 hours. It features auto shutoff function when not used for long duration. But the thing I liked about this set is the ability to turn ON automatically when I get into the Car. Yes, this set turn ON automatically when a vibration such as door opening is detected.

It has all the standard functions for operating as a handsfree speaker phone such as redial last call, mute function, voice dialing (depends on phone support), answer, and rejecting calls. My Nexus 5 supports voice dial, so I had no trouble in dialing call via voice. It can also play music through the speaker phone. The only hitch I can think of that there is no backlight control buttons, the device's control buttons are not visible during the dark.

Overall, I am impressed with its performance and happy with it.

review_body:
First, assembly instructions: Note that kit includes a piece of floss/string. (1) orient sling to grip so the sling basket is oriented forward, and you see which tube goes to which grip hole (left: top, middle, bottom; then right top, middle, bottom). (2) for each rubber tube, fold the floss in half and slide the loop a little through the respective grip hole (3) for the specific grip hole and matching rubber tube in turn, put about a half-inch of the rubber tube end through the floss loop, and pull the floss (and rubber tube) back through the grip hole. Repeat five more times for each tube and matching grip hole. (4) with all tubes through the grip, pull back on the sling basket slightly to match the tension for each rubber tube. You should leave approximately 3/4-inch of tube out the end of the tubes. (5) wet and slide a small BB into the end of each tube. (6) Do final adjustments on tube length/tension and adjust BB depth to match. (7) Pull sling basket to full tension to seat tubes. (8) Install brace referencing picture.

Now, the review. The slingshot arrived on time and is exactly as depicted here. I have a medium build and find the grip, brace, and tension comfortable. I'll follow up later with a longevity review.

product_title: LifeTrak Move C300 24-hour Heart Rate Watch, Black/Woodland Green
review_body:
I did not like this product one bit. I'll admit. It looks a little cool but here's what I have determined from this product.

Pros
-Waterproof (Went swimming with the tracker and it works just fine)
-Heartbeat monitor is accurate
-You can set goals to reach (Calories Burned, Steps Taken, Distance Traveled)
-The watch keeps track of your progress of the last few days (Calories Burned, Steps Taken, Distance Traveled)
-The strap doesn't come off easily. I've read on some other fitness trackers that people had trouble with the straps, the strap for the C300 is very good and very comfortable
-Battery life is nice because it uses a coin battery like a watch
-Displays time and date
-You can select what you would like to display below time and date (Calories Burned, Steps Taken, Distance Traveled)

Cons
-App only for iOS. It tells us this in the specifications but with android phones becoming a large percentage of smartphones on the market you would think they would try to gather as much of an audience as they can.
-No syncing to PC/MAC. This only syncs to an app so you either need an iPhone or iPad
-Tracking is wildly inaccurate. I some how managed to gather 200 steps in my sleep and 300 steps while showering and 2000 steps while swimming
-Getting the display light to turn on requires you to press two buttons simultaneously. Could be a pro for some people, I find it a con especially since it's light has such a short duration.
-The display is dated. Granted I don't care so much about the display of a fitness tracker as long as it performs well but this display is similar to that of a Gameboy.

Over all, this product did have a few more pro's than con's but the con's really hold the product back. I recommend the FitBit or Garmin Vivofit if you have the budget for it. If you just want a fitness tracker to roughly track your activity then this product may be for you.

****UPDATE****
I have now tried this out for a few months and have had the Android App since I became aware that one existed and it has earned an extra star in my opinion. The application is really handy and helps you keep track of your progress long term (super helpful). There is still no interfacing with PC or Mac but they may develop that too by having the app's device connect to a program on either the PC or Mac. Overall I find this product to be worth the money. It's not the best out there but definitely gives the competition a run for it's money considering how much is it.

product_title: Polar Loop Activity Tracker
review_body:
Needing the extra "push" to get my self moving and hopefully fitter I purchased the Polar Loop. Aesthetically it is great, neat and modern with a readout that is on only when you want it, as a piece of decorative jewelry it scores pretty high.

That's the good news, and that's all there is on the good side.

Having worn it to bed I found that it had recorded 72 steps while I was asleep, odd, over breakfast I reviewed and answered half a dozen emails, another 1400 steps added. Drove to the mall and we were almost at 2000 steps. At this point I took it off my wrist in disgust and stashed it in the cup holder, when we returned home we were at 2000+ steps.

This prompted me to write to Polar and explain what was happening, they responded in one day as follows:

"Polar Loop has a 3D digital acceleration sensor and it measures your wrist movement. The frequency, intensity and irregularity of your movements are registered and utilized in the estimation of steps. Therefore you’ll accumulate steps even if you’re swimming for instance and not actually taking steps at all."

Something that records steps when you are typing, or driving or is not even on your wrist is as much use as an ashtray on a Harley in terms of an aid to health improvement and activity tracking.

Polar should be ashamed of themselves for asking for payment for this so called activity tracker.

review_headline: It made a good first impression. Fits Kahr CW9, as well as Glock 19.
review_body:
**This is a "First Thoughts" review. I will update as needed.

I ordered this product on the 19th of November and was told that it would arrive sometime between the 21st and the 26th of November. Shipping from California to Georgia, it arrived on the 24th of November.

I had several holster options that I was trying to choose from but this one "spoke to me." The attractive displaying of the product caught my eye -- showing the company's knack for marketing -- and the quality of the product photos allowed a better look at the quality of the materials and construction which, thus far, seem to be quite high.

The first thing I noticed was that it smelled like Campbell's Chicken Noodle Soup. I like soup, so this is not a problem for me, although it does make me hungry....If you do not like soup or have problems with overeating, this may not be the holster for you and I advise you to keep looking. The holster, having been squished sometime during shipping, has spent the day holding a Glock 19. I showed the holster to my dad who promptly slipped it over his Kahr CW9 and seemed quite impressed with the fit. The holster provided adequate retention for the Kahr, as well as the Glock.

I am impressed at how well the holster maintained its molded shape despite its being squished. So far, I am pleased with this product, and so -- apparently -- is my dad. I foresee another purchase from this company in the future.

review_headline: Defective from day one plus lousy service and support from both the retailer and manufacturer!
review_body:
I am unsatisfied on multiple counts. First was that LG Outfitters certainly took their sweet time on actually shipping the product. They also didn't not make sure the package came with a owners manual or other product information, including any warranty papers. The only thing in the box was the air rifle! Also considering that I had to pay nearly $30.00 for shipping, they shipped me a torn box. It looked like somebody had previously opened it in a very excited fashion.

The issues listed above are minimal but only small in comparison to the real issues. When I finally received the air rifle I tried it out and thought there might be a problem because the pellets merely bounced off of anything other than paper type targets, at a distance of no more than 40 feet.
I had read about air rifles a bit before the purchase and many people seemed to indicate there were \\"break-in periods\\" so I though maybe I need to shoot more pellets through it first.

At the time of receiving the rifle I did not have a lot of time due to work related priorities so I put the air gun on the back burner for a couple weeks. When I next had time to play around with it I continued to have consistent low power problems so I contacted lg outfitters and at that time they said my 15 days are up and they would not do anything for me(period). The person I spoke with on the phone was actually even rude about the whole thing and in the end I was told flat out to contact the manufacturer.

I contacted Uramex only to find their customer support to be even more unpleasant to deal with. The guy on the phone repeatedly cut me off while I was explaining the problem with the rifle. He simply wanted to tell me that there wasn't anything he can do aside from me having to mail the rifle to them - at my expense! I remind you that I have only used the rifle twice now and it had been only one month since the purchase. After arguing with the jerk on the phone I had gotten him to give me a few things I may check and where I could find a manual on the rifle so that I could understand what he was telling me to check.

In the end the rifle came shipped with a defective breach seal !! I called back and they would not send me a new seal unless I paid for it plus shipping fees so I went to the nearest auto parts store and got a new seal that doesn't leak for $1.30. The rifle now pushes standard dome shaped lead pellets into trees upwards of about a half inch. I'm not certain if that is normal or not for this air rifle but it is definitely better than merely bouncing off of them.

I would not recommend that anybody purchase products that are sold by LG Outfitters (even though it is through amazon). The RWS air rifles seem to have good ratings and overall quality, but if I were to buy another air rifle it would not be an RWS and especially not from LG Outfitters.

review_body: I bought the Soffe running shorts (which are awesome, but EXTREMELY short) and needed some tights/leggings to go underneath them because I run outside during lunch and its cold. Oddly enough the inside orange stitching has retained its color, so I just turn them inside out and I feel as if I look less silly. review_body:
--I don't do reviews, but I thought I'd chime in because I saw so many fake reviews all over the internet concerning treadmills and exercise units in general; it took me awhile to decide on this unit. It was unnecessarily a difficult process; I even got a online CR subscription to try to figure out fake reviews from good ones, and found out that CR isn't quite what it used to be 20 years ago. Amazon reviews seem more spot on.
--Anyways, background - I've bought 3 treadmills in the last ~20 years or so. One cheapy that went in the trash. One very good Landice that was like $2000/~15 years ago which I loved but my nephew burnt out, a refurb Precor commercial which my sister still uses that I bought perhaps 8 years ago. And also various ellipticals of varying price ranges. My point is, I'm not a total dummy when it comes to exercise equipment, but I'm sure there are more expert people as well. I'm a 43 year old guy, weigh around 160lbs and when I do get on an exercise binge, I probably jog 3-10 miles a day 6 days a week, at around 5 to 7 mph, and I'm short, so my gait is very short too. I wanted a no nonsense unit. I don't care about bells and whistles. I wanted as low a cost a unit as possible that would still function well and reliably for at least a few years to get my money's worth, and also because I don't know if I will be moving soon(moving+cardio equipment=BAD), and I didn't want to go all the way to buying a commercial unit again. So, I wanted as cheap as possible but still reliable and built-well unit - not like the rip off brands you typically get for under $1000 from big box stores that are good for walking the first 5 miles and has all sorts of useless whirligigs and then either sits there or breaks within a week with any sort of real exercise(including rattles, tread slippage, motor burnouts, console computer problems, etc. and good luck getting warranty) The reviews on this unit seemed promising and the price was good. I went for it.

1. Assembly- The box came with a rip on one side. I took a pic and prayed. Inside, the unit wasn't damaged. Hard styrofoam packs(versus the better soft). The packaging itself was meh. I'd give it 3 out of 5. I think the fact that the unit comes with mostly important stuff already assembled saved it from a lot of possible damage. The unit was very easy to assemble and I've assembled lots of c*&^, and took me 2 hours, alone. It was one of the easier if not easiest assemblies I've had of a cardio machine. I could have done it in 30 mins I think but I took my time and took calls and stuff in between, had a quick bite, etc. and tried to do it perfectly. Personally, my preference is to assemble anything like this myself cause I'm pretty good with my hands and I don't trust those \\"expert installers\\". I always think those \\"expert installers\\" are the same ones that assembled the run down and broken c*&^% that you see on display at the onsite stores with pieces hanging off. Pay $300 extra for that? No thanks. Anyways, the big pieces of the unit come pretty much all already attached/assembled. Personally, I put the unit on the side and walked it out of the box, cause I didn't want to destroy the box in case I wanted/needed to return it. I had no trouble and was ultra careful to follow the instructions which also I rate as good enough, 3 out of 5. I noticed some reviewers had trouble with the screw holes on the arms. I had ZERO trouble with that portion. Maybe Lifespan fixed that issue. What I did have trouble with was the very last step of assembly. The screws come already screwed into the holes of this unit. The very last step is to put a plastic piece on the back of the display console. It just covers up the wires on the back. I found the four screws were frozen on the metal and wouldn't unscrew. I needed a vice grip to twist out one of the screws, and rounded out two screws in total trying to unscrew them out. It isn't an integral piece,and I didn't mind so much, but still, bad is bad. I did manage to get the plastic-trim on, but one of the screws will not screw in all the way and juts out a bit, it's nowhere that it can snag or endanger anyone, and it's function is largely cosmetic, so, I just left it and the plastic piece does not wobble or rattle so, again - good enough. Hence, I can trust the earlier reviews that note the problems with fittings, is possible, but for me at least, I didn't experience any of the big issues they reported(maybe they fixed the big issues in the generation I received), but rather just that single minor problem with that trim piece, which admittedly is annoying but not catastrophic. All other pieces I have to note, to be fair, fit perfectly and easily for me, so, actually it was doubly surprising that those last screws gave me trouble since all other pieces fit so well. Afterwards, I sprayed the deck, took off the red zip tie, put in the safety pin, and turned it on. It worked fine.
2. Console - Admittedly, I really don't care for music or entertainment when I exercise so much and I didn't want to pay for stupid doodads like fans and a tiny 5 inch lcd screen. I can get a tablet to watch movies if I want. To me all of those are gimmicks that tell me the manufacturer spent money on useless things that should have gone to paying for a better motor, frame, deck, shock, and tread --- and after-service(unless ofc the unit is like multi-thousands in cost, then I expect all the doodads). To me, those are the important things - the structural things. This unit doesn't have any of the nonsense really. Also, I'm the only user, so personally, I have no trouble with all that internet nonsense myself. As I said, these are MY PERSONAL PREFERENCES, not saying people who like those things are wrong. But I don't bother with them myself so, that aspect of the review, ignore me, if those things are important to you. What I did care about was the quality of the buttons. It has nice big silicon covered buttons that I prefer FAR over the bubble ones which I hate pressing and seem to stick after awhile and cause all sorts of trouble. I had those problems before in an elliptical(an older Precor of all things). I like the buttons on this unit; they are very responsive and easy to push. I would have liked as other reviewers mentioned, quick buttons that go all the way to 11 miles per hour for easier interval training; the unit comes with quick buttons up to 6mph. But to me, again not a biggie; I can just press the up/down buttons to get that speed I want and as I said, the unit responds fast and smooth enough to me, so I don't see what the problem is at least for myself. Others may disagree. What I do appreciate is that the unit speeds up smoothly and quickly and slows down likewise, and without hassle. It does. Call me old fashioned, but that's more important to me. One time, the incline at 10 degrees made the machine shake. But I tried to replicate it, and was unsuccessful. Maybe the machine settled down? I don't know. The heart rate thing doesn't work. I have had heart rate gizmos that did work with moist hands. This one just doesn't work - AT ALL. I don't care. I've worked out enough to know what my heart rate is by feel and I think anyone who's done maybe 10-15 miles of jogging does too. I don't, hence, plan on getting a polar strap or anything like that. I used to have one and never used it after the first 20 miles of working out; it was too much of a hassle to put on for me before every workout. I give the controls/console an average 3.5 out of 5(considering the price of this unit, that is, and that I wasn't expecting anything miraculous in the first place), just because the buttons work well and speedily and seem sturdy. To me, that's important above everything else. Simply, there isn't too much to the console, but what there is, seems to work very well. I'm admittedly biased, because I like that kind of simplicity. For example, I press start, press desired speed, voila! You know the calorie thingie in every treadmill is wrong. You know the HR reader isn't worth it. You know the speeds are approximations. You know the inclines are approximations. You know the step function is useless. You know if you are watching tv, you probably aren't working out as much as you should be, and you know those CPU fans will get dusty and break on you. Putting in weight and height - really you think that makes the calorie estimate anymore accurate? Really? :/ Mmmm.. No... Every human being is VERY different. The fact that the numbers go up as you run is enough for motivation. But trust me, there are no accurate calorie counters on these things. For me, I like to - press start, press speed, and run! If I can get a decent distance reading that's sorta accurate, I'll be happy. Basically I burn like 110-130 calories per mile, or I'm supposed to, who knows? And any difference(inaccuracies) in calorie burn is whether I put cream in my coffee in the morning or not. Heart Rate? If you can barely talk, you can run that speed for awhile. If you can't run that speed for awhile, guess what? Slow it down! Simples.
Point is, I just don't hold to gadgets on these things. To me, they are useless. As I said, that's me. If you have different opinion, no offense.
3. The treadmill itself: The important part... I was apprehensive because, yes, the box is heavy, etc. sorta, but actually comparatively this treadmill is far lighter than any other treadmill I've ever had before excepting the really cheap ones, and it's the first FOLDING treadmill I hazarded to purchase. I was hesitant to buy a folding one at all to be honest. I just don't trust them nor do I trust lighter treadmills, and it's not like it saves that much space, really to be able to fold. I don't ever plan on folding it. It's a hassle to unfold and fold machines in general to me. I think of folding treadmills as again a gimmick. So keeping my prejudice in mind --- Anyways, I assembled the whole unit myself and moved it with the wheels etc. and it seems at least to me, to be totally honest, NOT as tanky and substantial as some of the other reviewers seem to describe and I, hence, was hoping. Honestly, I wish I would have paid the extra $500 for the 3000 unit that is one grade up. That said, however, after assembly and trying it, I have very little reservations that it is just about what I NEEDED and is practical. Now, I'm not training for a marathon; if you are serious, look at the $2000+ range, maybe a refurb commercial unit or something, I don't know. But as I said, I'm 160lbs and looking to go down in weight 10-15lbs which is my comfort weight before I got fat(lol), and so, I'm saying I don't expect I will really abuse this machine, and I'm short, so the shorter deck is fine, and I only plan on doing average of 3-5 miles a day, 6 days a week alone, maybe a 10 miler once a week. I think in those respects, this is one of the better treadmills I have tried out in the $1000~ range. And believe me I've broken many a under $1000 treadmill just by using them (and I mean within a week!). Admittedly, I've only tried this mill for a couple miles barefooted in my jeans tbh, literally like 20 mins ago, right after assembly, just to get the silicon deck spray evened out. But there is no slippage and the unit seems solid enough. The deck is a bit too springy to me, however, and not like cushioned springy as much as like the deck feels too thin springy, which isn't comforting. I'm thinking if you are on the heavier side, if I was you, again, I'd go with the heavier more costly unit with the thicker deck. Having said that, I'm middle-aged and my joints not the greatest, and the cushioning itself comfort-wise seems surprisingly good to me. It's springy, not spongy. It does have enough firmness to strengthen your joints but at the same time, not feel too uncomfortable.In some commercial units with lots of padding, I found, I usually ended up having joint problems because you don't get enough shock for your body to heal back up to compensate, and I mean the spongy feeling ones with spongy treads, like Life Fitness commercials. Spongy treads always made my joints wear out, but didn't have enough impact to prompt my body to recover the joints, causing more joint damage for me in the long run, not less. This isn't that. It's springy, not spongy. I like it, personally. But again, ofc, that's totally a matter of taste and preference. Like I said, I did a fast 2 miles and my joints don't feel as if I did anything. I usually felt it on my commercial Precor which my sister still has at her house which was probably a ~$5000 unit new and to me was too firm a ride. This unit's deck is like I said, springy but hard feeling too, and to me just about right, altho I'd prefer it to be just a tad less springy. To me, it vaguely reminds me of my old Landice L7(which to me had a perfect ride) in feel tho albeit, as I said, a tad too springy. I'd give the ride a 4.5 out 5, which genuinely surprised me. Just keep in mind ofc, that everyone has different tastes in this regard.
4. The bad - First, I saw reviews that complained about the plastic motor hood. And yup. It is cheap and juts out too far. I'm short like I said, and I do try to keep my feet under me and back, not front of me, but still, I can see someone with a longer gait having trouble with this. Probably, I would hazard to guess, if you are taller, you could get problems with your feet hitting it. I don't have a very big problem with that part of it. It's ok to me. The part that I do have a problem with is, that the cheap plastic motor cover rattles obscenely against the metal base. Don't get me wrong, the cover LOOKS nice enough, just feels cheap. I fixed it with some double sided sponge tape I pried in between the plastic and the metal base. Problem sorta solved. The noise is definitely a lot less - and verging on quiet. Why the manufacturer didn't already do that? Or even just simply screw the cover on in the front with a rubber washer? I don't know. Second - maybe I'm spoiled with better, more-costly machines, or maybe it's related to the bad plastic housing up front that I unconsciously try to avoid, but I found I do reach the end of the deck at the back too often, and like I said, I'm short. 5' 4\\". But having said that, it's not horrible to me. It's ok, and I'm a bit nitpicking for a ~$1000 machine. Definitely not enough to want to keep me from using the machine in any sort of way. Third-as mentioned before, the bad screws on the back plate of the console and the somewhat thin feeling hollow sounding deck, plus the heart rate monitor that doesn't work. All those things are nitpicking again at least TO ME, because I sort of expected a lot of those issues having read the reviews and knowing what $1000 machines typically feel like.
--Conclusion- It's worth $1000. I've been on a lot of under $1000 and even slightly-over $1000 treadmills that didn't feel half as sturdy. I like that it feels sturdy for me. But then again, it could be sturdier; I wouldn't mind. And if I weighed more or was taller, I would consider a more substantial pricier unit. Actually, I do wish in retrospect that I had gone with the tr3000 model of this myself, tbh. But as I said, I plan on moving in the future and perhaps this unit was just right for me. I don't want to have to worry that it will break after the move(that's happened to me on a lot of expensive treadmills and ellipticals) and for $1000, I kinda don't because I plan on getting $1000 use out of it before I move(not that I think $1000 is not a lot of money). So far, just initial impression is that it will not break down on me with regular use. It is just right on that verge of being sturdy enough and no problem enough for me to have good workouts without hassles or worries. Is it a pricy $2000+ unit? No, it isn't. I think it is, however, probably one of the better ~$1000 units out there for anyone who does more than a couple miles of walking a day. I would say about on par, comparable to, let's say, a late 1990's Keys unit(as in off-brand treadmill but still decent since they are trying to compete with the big boys). As I keep saying, however, reviews are just opinions, and ofc this is just mine - I'm pretty happy with the unit! I tried a Spirit and a BH unit at a local exercise equipment store that were around $500 more, this unit compares slightly better mostly, again, in my opinion, to those but $500 less, (perhaps a little less sturdy feeling than the BH though and def sturdier than fold-up Spirits). I also tried a Sole at DS locally and found although the unit was solid(even more so at least in feel than this unit)the ride felt ultra hard for me and unforgiving. As comparison, I didn't run but 1/4 mile on the Sole and my knees were uncomfortable(ofc not painful but still..) as I walked to my car. As I said, the ride is personal preference, however. I mean to say, personally, it was the reason why I didn't go with a Sole.

Hopefully, this unit lasts 5 years; I'd be happy with that. I mean, this IS, keep in mind, my FIRST impression only. I'm glad for a unit at ~$1000, that it just works at all, to be blunt(if you know treadmills at all, you know that $1000 is the very very least cut off point for a reliable unit vs. junk). If I wasn't planning on moving in the future tho, perhaps I would have anted up and bought a $2500 True or even a $3000 Landice or a $2500 refurb commercial, if not the tr3000 of this brand. But as is, seems a great bargain for a ~$1000 unit. :D As others have pointed out, don't forget the silicon deck spray and I do recommend a treadmill mat for this treadmill because the one I ordered seemed to help it feel a lot more settled than on my bare garage floor.

I also wanted access to the various programs, etc., and I believe I needed to make the usb for that. Nothing told me how to access the programs when I did(not in the manual and not on the website). I had to sorta figure it out. You have to press up or down before starting the machine(which I guess is pretty standard on machines but still). The other thing is, if you are going to use a usb, keep in mind that putting in a usb and taking it out constantly(i.e. every day) doesn't imo bode well for the life of the usb socket on the machine, but to use the website features, you would kinda have to keep putting the usb in and out. I work with computers in my work, and mechanical things like that tend to break easy on computers. It's just not well thought out to have to constantly stick in a usb and take it out, etc. I plan on leaving my USB in and never visiting their website again, but for people with 2 users etc., I mean, I wouldn't buy this machine if you plan on having more than one user who wants to use the website and computer related functions - having to pay money for that sounds frankly dumb. The website is pretty slow too and pretty darn awful - Probably took a programmer a week to make. The website also asks you all sorts of personal questions, as if data mining, I just don't appreciate that - and on top the website quality makes me wonder what the rest of their website is like and question their security. I just wouldn't feel comfortable in supplying the website with any sort of vital/personal info. i.e. credit card or what not. The \\"whir whir\\" of the motor is the biggest concern, the unit still functions decently, and I do still like the cushioning of the machine. I don't really want to contact their warranty to fix these issues because I'd rather just live with them than bother with all the headaches of tech support, etc. Still, I have to knock down a star for these issues.

product_title: Tactical 5.11 Unisex Adult TMT L2 Flashlight
review_headline: Beware of the twisting lockout switch: comparison with previous model
review_body:
I bought the 5.11 ATAC L2, the predecessor to this model, in October 2013, about 13 months ago. That light has since been discontinued. As this light seems to have a very similar design, I wanted to point out the problem I am experiencing on my L2 as something to watch out for on this light as well.

Both the TMT L2 and my ATAC L2 are provided with a twisting switch on the back of the light, just under the thumb activated button that turns the light on. The intent of the twisting switch is to "lock out" the light, in other words, to prevent the thumb button from being activated and turning the light on when you don't want it to be turned on. An example would be when it is in your pocket or attached to something where you might press the button by accident.

The problem I have experienced on the ATAC L2 is that, after 13 months of non-daily use, the light will randomly switch between modes (high, low, strobe) once it is turned on. More specifically, once the lockout switch is turned to allow the light to be turned on and then the light is actually turned on with the thumb button, the mode of the light will switch randomly. Most often, it will change from high mode to low mode just by holding the light.

After experimenting with the light some, I noticed that the problem seems to occur when the area just around the lockout switch is touched, tapped or held. This is likely because the switch itself has loosened from (little) use and now has some "play" in it when the switch is turned on. Thus, it appears that the circuit to activate the light is momentarily interrupted by the gentle touching of the switch and the light responds as though you had just tapped the thumb button one or more additional times.

I am hoping that 5.11 has resolved this issue in the TMT L2, but I wanted to point it out so that buyers are aware that, given my experience, such a problem is possible in only a year of use a few times a week. The ATAC L2 is otherwise a great light and I am sure that the increased light output on the TMT L2 is a welcome addition to an already nice package.week. product_title: Horseware Amigo 1200D Hood 150g
review_body:
The 150g fill hood is a great addition to an Amigo medium turnout blanket for extra cold/wet/windy days. Like all Rambo products, it's very well made. The velcro attachments on the Amigo blankets are easier than those on some of Rambo's other product lines. (Before you buy, make sure you have an Amigo--the mechanism attaching the hood to the blanket is two horizontal velcro strips on each side that loop through rings on the blanket, rather than a single long vertical strip of velcro on the hood that fits between velcro strips on the blanket.)

As for sizing, I bought a large for my well-muscled 17 hh warmblood who wears an 81. I had tried extra large before because his neck is so long, but it was huge around (definitely for draft horses) and would have let too much cold air in. The large is a little short for him like all hoods, but the perfect width. I would say it runs true to size.

I did think that the $10.95 shipping and handling was excessive for such a compact and lightweight product, but I looked for two winters to find a solid black hood to match my black/red blanket, so I decided it was worth it.

product_title: Foundation Training DVD Set
review_headline: Foundation training is absolutely amazing. My back used to always hurt at least ...
review_body:
Foundation training is absolutely amazing. My back used to always hurt at least a bit and I thought that was normal. After the first foundation training workout, my back began to feel better. I have been doing foundation training for about 8 months now and my back is rock solid. I used to lift very heavy weights for many years and it took a toll on my body. For the last five or six years I have primarily done various types of calisthenics. A few weeks ago I was curious to see what the heavy iron felt like. I had not deadlifted in about 7 years. Years ago I did a bit of competitive powerlifting and the deadlift was always my weakest lift by far. I am now 55 years old and was able to deadlift 365 like it was a bag of groceries. I probably could have done 5 to 8 repetitions. I am sure I could have done 400 plus maybe even 500. The point is foundation training has made my back super strong without training with heavy weights.
I am an MD and frequently do spine injections for pain management. I have been recommending foundation training for many of these patients because I believe in it so strongly. Most people with back issues are weak and tight. Foundation training solves that.

product_title: Daiwa DXS862MHXS 8-Foot 6-Inch DXS Salmon & Steelhead Spinning Rod, Medium-Heavy Power, Black Finish
review_body:
I'm about to purchase a second of these Daiwa rods, since a family member claimed the first one as hers. These are great, if plain, rods, perfect of for bank fishing for salmon.

I can't say I'm a fan of the matte finish, but it doesn't seem to matter to the fish.

I like that it's IM7 and slightly less fragile than the newer, higher modulus graphite composites. It's as sensitive as much more expensive rods, but marginally less fragile. That's important if you're excitable, and fishing from a rock and gravel bar.

It has an nearly ideal action - Medium Heavy/Extra Fast - for tossing bobber and bait rigs a surprisingly long distance, and for tugging-on a large fish until it agrees to come to the bank.

And it has an agreeable price.

It's not a Lamiglas or a St. Croix or a Loomis. It's not a five star rod. But it's the best sub-100 dollar rod I've come across.

If you understand "extra-fast" action, I highly recommend these rods.

product_title: Conquest Scents EverCalm Deer Herd Scent Stick
review_headline: Must have product for hunting whitetail
review_body: I was fortunate enough to spend a solid week of hunting whitetail in WV last week.  These are high pressure deer with eye on top of their heads and adrenal glands 2X the size of most deer.  Here's what I can tell you about ever calm.  I saw 10 deer in a week and had shot opportunities at 8.  The two bucks I took both walked under my stand before I shot them.  One was on high alert and stomped all the way in but veered towards my tree and under (under meaning I could see him through the slats of my stand) it before I eventually took him at 12 yds.  The other was a bench below me and as I waited for the nice 3 year old to come around the other side of the cedar for a 32 yd shot it never appeared.  Looked around and there he was under the cedar tree I rubbed with evercalm  and shot him at maybe 10 yds.  Deer went maybe 35 yds before expiring.  After finding him I walked back up over the bank and there was a doe standing over my bow and next to my climber that I had left not 15 minutes ago.  I watched other deer that came down wind and you could see they became cautious but never left the area.  in fact they seemed to want to stick around despite a whiff of human odor.  One thing that I believe helps is this is not a rut scent.  That can be very hit and miss often scaring deer away.  This stuff does not seem to spook anything and even though your scent is present this seems to override the natural alert reaction and settles them down. Go look at Cabelas, Gander, Bass Pro and whatever other site you can find.  When you see 4.5/5 consistently in every site you know something must be working.  Great stuff and not expensive especially when you consider a stick will last all season.  You will see more deer and get more shot opportunities with Ever Calm Update 10/10/15:  This stuff continues to amaze me.  Used the same stick left over from LY.  2 Doe come cross down below me, hit the trail from rubbing this on my boot tips and they turn come straight up the hill and stand next to the tree I rubbed at 10 yds.  2 Bucks came up to follow and the big doe spooked and blew when I drew on the largest one.  HOWEVER>> they did not run off.  Moved about 10 yds but just stayed in the area including the doe.  When hunters catch on about this stuff it will be in every pocket before heading out to the stand.  Amazing stuff!

My two hobbies are writing amazon reviews and working out, an combination but it works for me. When the opportunity comes up to combine the two I will rarely pass on it. I was offered this product in exchange for a fair and unbiased review and I intend to do just that.

Service: Henrik is personable and cares about his products. I grade service and durability as the two most important factors when evaluating a product. Service is a no question 5/5. Out of every person that i've spoken with about reviews (and it's a lot). Unlike some appointed "marketing specialist" reading lines off of a cheat sheet Henrik stands out as someone that truly enjoys his job.

Durability: I'm at the gym 5-6 days a week but I really only need straps during back (Deadlifts) and legs (Romanian deadlifts) days. I typically rotate these off but in the interest off writing a fair review I stepped my game up. Quality is a tough thing to rate on a few lifts but I see no cause for concern. In my 2 month experience I am quite satisfied with the durability. 5/5 - - - Note that if I notice quality deterioration I will be sure to come back and adjust my review.

Intangibles: Packaged better than the competition. Easy to read instructions. I can't tell you how many products I've received that are puzzles to figure out. From car top carriers to bluetooth headphones it seems like most companies are okay with you trying to youtube the one lucky guy/girl that figured it out. Nordic Lifting bucks that trend. All of the lifting accessories that I've used by NL come with clear and detailed instructions. They were properly thought out. 5/5

"Style" -. I don't hate Yellow. I just moved from NY to Pitt and that means black and Yellow is my new thing but it's just not a color scheme that I own. Given that style doesn't matter when lifting i'm not deducting any stars.

Do you need them? For the price, I see no reason why you shouldn't give them serious consideration. These straps will help you on the heavier of your lifts. I would recommend using them on 1-2 sets of your D-lifts. I've seen people use them for pullups but personally don't have any experience.

Like ANY other lifting supplement I strongly suggest that you research how to properly use these wraps/straps. Not just how to properly put them on but rather the generally accepted use of them. Most agree that they are useful but almost everyone will caution not to become reliant on them. You need to constantly allow for your grip to battle your target muscle group. This means that you should always want to have the ability to grip the weight your lifting without assistance (I.E. these straps/wraps) but at the same time you should be trying to lift more than your grip can possibly handle. No, you can't have it both ways but having the right products at your disposal can help you continue to maintain that balance.

review_headline: you get what you pay for
review_body:
I purchased this call based off of the reviews I read here.

The tone on this call isnt even close to realistic sounding. It sounds more like a kazoo than a mallard hen. The uncle si has Zero rasp, its very hard to put any inflection in your calls, and it sticks very bad in the cold when it gets wet. This uncle si has done nothing but send ducks the other direction everytime i have been out.

After taking it out 5 or 6 trips on the water with me i realize now that this is nothing more than a stocking stuffer for your kids. It has become blatantly obvious that the duck commander company has realized that they can put any crap out there and people will buy it based on the families popularity. The uncle si will no longer touch my lanyard and the only use i can see getting out of it is keeping it in my truck to tool around on back and forth from work.

Please remember what you are reviewing when you write a review for a product. Giving a subpar product a 5 star rating because "you stand with phil" does nothing but make actual duck hunters waste thier money on toys like this call. I would be interested to see what phil actually has to say about his companies low end calls. Dont waste your money if you are planning on using this to hunt ducks. Spend a little extra money and get a quality call.

product_title: Perfect Fitness Pushup Stands
review_headline: A nice addition to anyone's training equipment collection
review_body:
Except for working my back on my chinning bar, I don’t do much with body weight exercises. One reason why is they generally don’t give you the intensity you need for the adaptive response. Some body weight exercises are great finishers, for example doing slow, deep squats with body weight only after finishing a front squats/sissy squats routine.

For the pecs, I have tried push-ups as a finisher but I don’t get the range of motion. Normally, I do the bench and then flyes in the morning, and then in the afternoon I hit flyes again with 55lb dumbbells. I keep doing short-interval sets with as many slow reps as I can until I can do only one rep. Then I switch to 40-lb dumbbells. With the lighter weight, I stretch the pecs back and then squeeze slowly up; usually 3 or 4 sets of 2 or 3 reps. This works well; I have a 44 inch chest despite weighing barely over 150 lbs.

But even this brutal workout doesn’t recruit all of the fibers. That means I’m still giving up some potential muscle growth. Push-ups at this point have not worked well for me. The main problems are the range of motion and the effects on the shoulder, hands, and wrists.

These push-up handles solve these problems (and several others). For example, one reason I don’t like push-ups is the negative effect on my palms and my wrists. These push-up aids put my wrist at an angle that prevents stressing the connective tissues and the pressure on my hands is spread out over more area. One reason I hadn’t used a push-up device previously was I thought the surface area would be much less, but actually the opposite is true.

OK, so any decent set of push-up handles will solve the problems I just discussed. So what makes these different?

One really nice feature is they are stackable. I have my own Olympic weight set, which, even with an Olympic weight tree, takes up considerable space. Add to that the weight rack, triceps bar, etc., and the idea of addingmore equipment quickly loses appeal. Anything occupying space in that training area has to really deserve to be there. These don’t take up much room, and in fact I’m able to store them on the little cart that also holds weight collars, bar pads, and other accessories.

The handles come with a booklet that warns the user not to use these on linoleum and similar surfaces. The reason is if you are exercising the way most people do, you are likely to slip. Most people exercise with the goal of completing reps and sets, rather than working the muscles around a given joint (or set of joints). With proper form, you are not going to slip. But most people are nowhere close to proper form.

So I decided to see how much force it would take to slide these across tile. It seems to be a little less than 10 lbs of lateral force. I would never generate anything like this doing push-ups, but that’s because my form pretty much eliminates lateral force. I’ve watched other people do push-ups, and most of them are focused on counting reps and that focus leads them to recruit their front and medial delts into what should be a pecs, biceps, and triceps exercise. This means they will slide on a tile floor.

The same poor form exists in the bench press. Normally, when I correct the form of some guy who thinks he is bench pressing 220 because that’s what’s on the bar he can no longer lift it off the rack. When I drop the weight to 90 lbs, he has to struggle to do even one rep.

The instructions also advise getting qualified instruction on how to use these training aids. That’s very good advice, given what I just said about the bench press.

My first introduction to qualified instruction was when my grandfather showed me the right way to train pecs using the only device he trained pecs with. It was just a wheel with handles on it. Very brutal workout if you are working the muscles instead of just rolling it to say you rolled itX number of times. He had fairly impressive pecs even into his 70s.

If you don’t have weights, I think you could use these push-up aids for most of your upper body work. If you train to work the muscle and do slow reps with these, something else you will notice is your testosterone will be elevated for several days after your workout. That’s because the push-up is a compound exercise and when done correctly it takes a great deal of energy. That elevated testosterone signals your body to store calcium in the bones, burn fat, and build muscle. I don’t know of anybody who objects to those three benefits.

product_title: Innova Fitness ITX9250 Deluxe Inversion Table
review_headline: 10 stars for Inversion Therapy, three stars for this table
review_body:
Inversion therapy has improved my back pain and pretty much negates any damage I do to my herniated disc from hours of sitting and/or straining. It's incredible. I find that the best time to do it is right before bed so as not to undo the pressure relief you've just worked so hard for. Yes, it's difficult to handle the inversion position for a long time. I started at 2-3 minutes and felt like my head was going to explode. Now I can do up to 10 minutes and find that my back feels ten times better the next morning after a session.

Keep in mind that your ankles are going to be uncomfortable. It's going to hurt and it's not doing any damage to your body, but it will lessen a little if you wear proper shoes and socks. I found that ugg style boots are particularly good for increasing my ankle comfort. Just be prepared for it to be annoying: your entire body's weight is being held up by your ankles.

This particular table was not as easy to put together as the last one I owned. I would wholeheartedly recommend the Body Champ IT8070 Inversion Therapy Table which Amazon also sells for just a little bit more than this one. The "feet" on this particular piece of equipment are rather annoying. Since I have to fold it up after each use, I find that those plastic feet pop off as soon as you start moving this thing around. It doesn't feel as secure, but that isn't too big of an issue. I believe regardless of its feel, it is in fact secure enough to prevent you from falling and I haven't had a problem with that. There are also more options on the Body Champ for those who are not an average height/size that allow you to play with the adjustments. You won't go all the way upsidedown if you have the settings wrong. You'll have to check them several times to get it just right if you're not the average height. If you're on the fence, go with the Body Champ.

product_title: ProSpot Fitness HG-6 Home Gym
review_headline: Best Home Gym On the Market - Owned since ~2007
review_body:
First off, I see there are some suspect reviews... Well folks this one is real. I bought the HG-6 in Chicago around 2007 (if memory serves me correctly). I was just telling a co-worker about this thing, which, interestingly enough, was not being made for a number of years due to the owner spending all the cash as soon as it came in and thus the business collapsed (or at least that's what they told me on the phone when I called the company back in 2009 looking for a part I thought I lost during a move... They said another company was looking to buy the business and looks like that has happened). So anyways... I Googled the ProSpot simply looking for a picture and was excited to see that it was listed here (among other websites).

So let me tell you what this thing can do.... Everything. Period. The bench bar is the coolest feature. It hangs on a resistance-free cable and there are sensors in the bar. Whenever you let go of the bar, the cables lock up. This means you can safely lift some pretty heavy weight by yourself in a safe manner without a spotter. I show this to everyone who comes over to my house. Awesome party trick. When you're done, do a few curls then store the bar at the top of the unit and do some chin ups before you leave. Note: You can use plates (which I do) or hook the bar into the track system. The track system is nice, but then you lose the 'free weight' feel.

The bench is another engineering feat. It does the standard incline, but it is also on a track system. You hook a cable into the bottom of the bench, unlatch the lock, raise the seat portion up 90-degree, and you can sit facing the machine to do leg presses. Lock the track system again and you can do seated rows. Turn around and work your quads with some leg extensions. Bring that bench bar down and do some squats. Getting tired, let go of the bar and it locks in place!!

As far as the rest of the pulley system, you can do any pulley exercise you can think of. What I consider the 'main' tracks on the left and right can be raised and lowered to do whatever you want. There are also inserts that you can use to do dips facing the machine or leg raises when facing away.

Lastly, the thing just looks sharp. The neon light really sets it off. Much better than the standard machines that just look boxy and have no class.

You may also be wondering what the difference is between the HG5 & HG6 - From what I remember, the main thing is the HG5 only comes with 200lbs of weight (2-100 stacks). The HG6 has 400lbs (2-200lbs). I THINK they're pretty similar after that. 400 sounds like a lot of weight, but consider that you'll be doing some exercises on only 1 stack, so 100lbs might be a little inadequate.

So down to brass tax:

PROS:
- Space saver
- You can do ANY exercise you can think of on this machine
- Super cool looking
- No spotter needed
- Engineering masterpiece

CONS:
- Sometimes the "Grab-N-Go" system is a little sensitive and locks up when you don't want it to.
- No matter what I try, the pulley system always seems to have "ghost" resistance, like the wheels are not oiled enough and the cables don't run as slick as I'd like them. It make the weight seem 'lighter'. It's not enough to knock a star off, plus maybe they improved the wheels or something since I've bought mine. Even so, it's not a huge bother and the other PROS outweigh this minor annoyance.

NEUTRAL:
- The weight stacks increase in 10lb increments. When I bought this, I had to pay extra for the 5lb blocks you can rest on top of the stack to do a more gradual increase. Depending on what you're doing, going from 20lbs to 30lbs is a big jump.

Note of caution: The picture at the time of the review has the 2 blue speakers near the top of the unit. I'd question whether or not these are actually included as these were optional upgrades (along with a built-in TV) when I bought my unit.

review_headline: Get back to where you once belonged
review_body:
I just got it today so I don't have tons of time on it but I will say I like it a lot. It's exactly what I need without going with a more expensive GPS with unwanted downloadable maps.
The actual set-up wasn't that bad and the instructions are easy to follow. I had to read it a few times to get a better grasp but that's my preference. Younger folks won't have a problem with it.....older guys like me will wonder where to put the 5\\" floppy.
A note to older guys: Yelling at it won't make it better.

PROS: The size, weight and ease of use. Functions are exactly what I need so no excessive BS. AAA batteries are cheap and the coupon for better batteries was included. Construction looks to be good but I don't intend to go crazy with it. The Back Track app was easy to download and works great. If you're familiar with Google Maps, then you'll like this feature. The tracking is really accurate and showed the route I took going through me yard, into my car and a quick 3 mile drive around the neighborhood plus a turn around in someone's drive way. You simply can't out run thing.
I also got the Case Logic pouch as mentioned in the \\"frequently bought together\\" section. Great pouch and worth the $5.

CONS: The back light isn't the greatest and the ambient setting could be better. The rear cover \\"twist lock\\" for the battery compartment is an antiquated design and could fail. Also, the batteries need to be pressed in more than you think or the rear cover creeps up a bit. Battery door feels uneven. Opening it up again and reseating the batteries will fix it. The altimeter doesn't seem to be accurate and it if it's not I don't care. Compass & temp work great.
Coupon for batteries as noted above expired 9 months before I got it. Nice to have but useless.
As A personal gripe. I can't stand Bear Grylls' pretentious ego. Owning a product associated with him bothers me but since it's the best one out there, I had to get it.

All in all I like it a lot. This is my first personal back track type device and it's a great entry level unit. I would recommend it to anyone who wants to get a highly detailed look at their hikes and or every day travel.

review_body: I have this Well Airsoft MP5 (6 mm) and the H&K CO2 PDW version in 4.5 mm steel BBs. They are both about the same price and size but the H&K is much higher quality than the Well. The Well MP5 runs on green gas.  The H&K runs on 12 gram CO2 cartridges. Green gas is much more expensive and less available then CO2 but less susceptible to temperature variation than CO2. You can buy a propane adapter and run the Well MP5 off propane which would significantly reduce your operational costs but you need to add some silicone to the propane.  The H&K is the most realistic looking MP5 but it  only comes in semi-automatic. The Well has semi-automatic capability as well as fully automatic capability, which mirrors operationally the functions of the real MP5. Additional magazines for the H&K are cheaper because they do not serve  dual functions like the Well magazines (Well Mags hold rounds and hold gas/ H & K mags only hold rounds). Overall though - both are fun as hell and I would recommend either for your air gun collection!

review_headline: Poorly packaged but good for the $$
review_body:
The box was pretty much destroyed upon arrival, with a large section of missing cardboard patched over with packing tape. The contents were certainly serviceable but a bit scuffed. Like another reviewer noted, it's for lifting weights so not a huge concern for me.

Otherwise, once assembled, it seems fine. It is a tidge wobbly and a little bit more flexible than one might like, but not terrible or to the extant that it seems unsafe. For a home gym with limited use, and using less than the manufacturers recommended 300 lb max, it's more than sufficient. Also, our exercise room is small and it tucks nicely against the wall. I've been using it for standard bench press, squats, and military press. The pull up bar easily handles my 200lbs, but I already have a wall mounted unit.

You will want a separate rack for your weights, as the small ones that attach to the bottom of the cage don't hold much and, if used, will block access to the bottom attachments for the spotter arms.

If you want something that's rock solid and can easily handle, say, 400+ lbs, you will unfortunately be spending a bit more money and will likely need something larger.

product_title: G96 1055P Complete Triple-Action Gun Treatment
review_body:
This was one of the first gun cleaning products I ever bought, and it's definitely good stuff. The first thing you'll notice is the smell, it's very pleasant, a bit like egg nog or some kind of spice blend. It's a bit of a toss up between this and Break-Free CLP as to whom is better. After the solvent evaporates it appears to be on the thin side; but I haven't noticed any increase of wear on action slides or AR internals, so it seems to be doing a good job. Removes carbon and rust VERY well, no chemical effect on copper however.

This is also an excellent product for inhibiting rust on tools and other ferrous items. Long after treatment, water will appear to bead up on the metal. If those around you are sensitive to the odor of your firearms cleaning products (Wife, Girlfriend, Kids) this is possibly the best available product to use.

I've never had to use it in a defensive situation since I've gotten it (and hope to never have to) but I can tell you it will leave a mark. I did however use it as a window punch recently and it preformed flawlessly. So over all I'm impressed and will keep it part of my EDC. product_title: Blue Sea Systems ST Blade ATO/ATC Fuse Blocks
review_headline: and bad wiring. When adding lights
review_body:
I've used several of these in putting together old cars that originally came with very few fuses, and bad wiring. When adding lights, gauges, and other equipment, I've loved the simplicity of these boxes.

Things I like:

1) The plastic covers come on and off very easily, and are secure when on.
2) Most other fuse panels I've worked with have not had internal busses; on other units, to power 10 fuses, you first need to split your power source 10 ways. With this unit, I can run a single #10 or #12 wire to the fuse block, and then run smaller gauge wires out to the various accessories.
3) The included ground bus is a nice touch. It sure beats trying to sink sheetmetal screws with wire lugs to find a ground, or installing a separate ground bar. With this unit, I can run a solid, known-good ground from the battery, and know my grounds are solid and not affected by a rusty body panel.
4) The body of this thing is completely solid, not flimsy in any way.

I've been really finding these blocks, and in general, much of the blue sea product line to be well made, solid, and easy to use.

Also, for one of my similar fuse blocks, I had lost a few of the terminal screws. They are very nice screws, with a captive star washer, and I don't know where to find them. I emailed the company for info about where to source some more, and they simply sent me a baggie with 10 or so of the screws. I love good customer service!

And so this is my experience with this item that hopefully others could gain some insight from and make up their own mind.    Pros:    * Great design  * Is compact and doesn't protrude beyond the muzzle  * Extremely bright laser.  (These are the only reason why I gave it 2 stars)    Cons:    * Unbelievably frustrating to screw in the cap for battery. It will take you a while to do something that should be so simple thanks to poor design. Plus there is extreme stress created from not trying to cross-thread the battery cap, as once it's ruined; the light/laser is no good permanently.  * It has 6 modes of light only, laser only, laser in strobe mode, strobe light only etc. But this mode is set in stone in a particular order. And so you have to cycle through the modes in a set, particular order. In other words if you want to go from laser only to light only (which you should be able to do with one switch) you cannot. You have to cycle through some 5 modes which cannot be changed according to Viridian. (I called them.) Cycling through all these modes takes a long time and requires pressing 2 separate buttons at the same time. This is no good in an emergency scenario and is again a result of poor designing. Frankly, it's a deal-breaker for me.  * Very difficult to adjust the windage and elevation. Frustrating.  * When I fired my gun with this laser/light attached, the laser would turn off about 30% of the time. I think the recoil shock of the gun de-connects the battery, as I had to take out the battery and put it in again for it to work. And so I don't trust it in a life-or-death scenario.  * Incredibly overpriced. The Streamlight TLR-4G green laser/light combo is better and you can get it for around $200.    One other note about lasers in general: I have also owned both a red and green laser. Frankly, I don't see a huge improvement with a green laser. Yes it is easier to see, but not by much. During the daytime if its sunny, it's difficult to see any laser whatever the color: a green laser is not that visible. Otherwise, I can see the red laser just as well as a green one in my experience. To whatever degree you can see a green laser better, they are so much more expensive that in my opinion the green lasers are not worth it. As a result, I'll be sticking with a red laser.    I would recommend the Streamlight TLR-4 red laser which is their red laser/light combination which you could buy for about $110 or so. It's still compact, doesn't protrude much, reliable, you can switch from laser only to light only and so on, and its laser is as bright and powerful as the Viridian as far as the eye could see.
