product_title: Meprolight Ruger Tru-Dot Night Sight for SR-9 & SR-9C. Fixed set
review_headline: Excellent night sights for the Ruger SR40/9 and SR40c/9c
review_body:
These are excellent Tritium night sights for the Ruger SR9c/40c and SR9/40 pistols. I put a set of these sights on my Ruger SR40c and they have performed superbly.

The Tritium dots are adequately bright such that they enhance visibility of the sights in dimly lit rooms and the like. The front sight dot is large enough for quick target acquisition but small enough for accurate shooting. While some shooters prefer a larger front sight dot than these sights provide, in practice I have found that I shoot very accurately with these Meprolight sights on my Ruger SR40c, one of my primary carry pistols.

These sights do not allow for elevation adjustment as do the stock Ruger sights. I was initially concerned about this, but as it turned out these sights were perfectly sighted for both windage and elevation and this is accordingly not an issue.

I have in the past been a skeptic of night sights on the theory that light dim enough to allow the Tritium glow to enhance the sight would be light too dim to allow proper target identification. In practice this is not so. In dim but perfectly visible indoor light the glow from these sights makes for brighter sights than the stock ordinary white paint sights. This is a good thing.

Overall, I have five-star satisfaction with these Meprolight sights. RJB.

product_title: Aurorae Printed Extra Thick 5mm and 72" Long Premium Eco Safe Yoga Mat with Non Slip Rosin
review_headline: Slippery, slimey, and squishy. But pretty!
review_body:
This mat has great quality and looks pretty, but there are several core flaws which make it unusable, for me anyway.
I've had this mat for several years and have been giving it chance after chance, but to no avail.
The product looks great and is constructed nicely, but the two major issues are that it is too slippery and behaves more like squishy memory foam than a mat.
After reading other reviews that others also found the mat slippery, I purchased the (rather pricey) yoga mat wash from Aurorae, which I actually think worsened the problem. The wash smelt great but the content include oils which I think further lubricated the mat. I could not even hold a downward dog without sliding all over the place. So I ran the mat through the washing machine with all natural unscented detergent, which helped the slipperiness a little. I also read that "continues use" would "break the mat in", and I put myself through many many awkward practices where my concentration is broken by repositioning my hands and feet every time they slide into an uncomfortable position. So I also washed the mat with diluted vinegar, practiced on it some more, and no luck, then tried highly diluted baking soda, no luck, and then just hot water and a washcloth. Over time the slipperiness got a little better but this mat just lacks grip. I was still unable to hold poses like Prasarita Padotanasana without the risk of injury because my feet just could not GRIP the mat - well after a year of "breaking the mat in" and trying various washing techniques, including the recommended name brand wash.
Furthering the issue of not allowing my feet to grip the mat, is that this mat behaves like squishy memory foam, and holds indents of hand/foot impressions far beyond releasing the pose. I personally prefer a mat that provides friction and "push back", and this mat provides neither.
Perhaps this is just my personal preference, but this mat was just not for me.I read the aggressive responses from the company to all the negative reviews, and I'm sorry, but your product is just not for everyone.
I will say the durability of the product is great, provided I tried so many different cleaning regimens and it still "acts like new", which for me, is unfortunate, as it is nearly as slimey and squishy as when I first got it.

These pair of bins weigh exactly 3 pounds 2 ounces i.e. with neck strap attached and optical caps on. Whereas the Celestron Skymaster 15x70 binoculars weighs exactly 3 pounds 1 ounce, just one ounce difference.
The best way to view from these bins is to roll down the eyecups then you'll really have a better viewing.
One thing to be noted once you roll down the eyecups the caps provided fits perfectly.

Today I received my bins right on time and in great condition. Opening the package I saw the exact same items like the [[ASIN:B00008Y0VN Celestron Skymaster 15x70 binoculars]] nothing different other than the binoculars itself.
I'd personally recommend it for a single user; reason: Once adjusted to your specific setting for your eyes it will not necessarily work for another person. To go back and adjust to your settings is quite time consuming especially if you already set it to view at a particular distance.

It takes a little time to get it focused properly, once you get yourself familiar with it then its very easy to use. Don't get frustrated, take your time and get the feel of it especially if you have it mounted onto a Tripod, it makes it even more simpler to use.

Now that I own both 15x70 and 25x70 binoculars by Celestron, I can definitely enjoy myself.
Looking through these bins in comparison to the 15x70 is seeing everything 25x which is 10 times closer that the 15x70. I still have to test it out at night for celestial viewing to give further info.

review_headline: You get what you pay for. And a little less.
review_body: Ok. So yes, it's a behemoth of a knife, so you'll get the "that's not a knife, this is a knife" feeling when you first pull it out,  but the quality is mediocre at best & the novelty soon wears off. It will not go all the way in, there's still a half inch of blade visible(pictured). And once again I'm afraid to force it cause I think it'll just pop off into the sheath. Also I'm not too crazy about the design of the clip(it's not attached to said sheath so you can't rely on it being in one place). All in all it's still a huge knife and I like it, but I feel like I bought a chore with all the tweaking and sharpening I'm going to have to do. Now I can't say for certain if a little more expensive one would be any better,  but I still think I got cheated for the amount I did pay.

Disclaimer: I received this product in exchange for a fair and honest review.

This is the sort of item that anybody can benefit from having around. It onviously has a lot of handy features, and since you can wear it, it also has supreme portability. That said, if your wrists arent very big, this will be quite loose, so be aware of that.

Paracord: I did eventually unwind the bracelet, and it measured out to exactly 9 feet. That was nice. You can further separate the strands to get even more out of it. An excellent addition, especially since both are part of the clasp. No wasted space, as it were.

Knife Cutter: This is not the greatest knife cutter in the world, but it is functional, and considering the item as a whole, the cutter provided is perfect. I tested it on the paracord itself, in addition to using it on the fire starter.

So, that's basically it. There are tutorials on youtube for putting these back together after unwinding them. It isnt easy though, so only unwind this if you really plan to use the paracord and have no intention of wearing it ever again.

product_title: Zero Tolerance Unisex G-10 Folder Knife - 0350Sw
review_body:
Received in about 48 hrs as promised. Thanks Amazon!

The ZT0350SW is a handsome knife.very clean,simple and all business.has beautiful high quality G-10 grips with a denim like texture very similar to type used on some Spyderco models.and the stone washed blade really shows off the unique facets of the blade grind.really sharp.

Its really put together too with thick full steel liners approx .080" thick,a large blade pivot shaft and (3) good sized build screws. Like other ZT models the 0350's thumbstuds do double duty as the blade stop as they contact the frame up near the thumb ramp. The 3.250" blade is .125" thick and is made from excellent CPM S30V.as delivered it is very,very sharp. Aided by the sexy,swoopy re curved and flat ground blade,it glides through the paper test and breezes through multiple layers of cardboard. Edge geometry is really good and the knife will make an excellent utility,outdoor/camp or even hunting/skinning blade .and of course would be a masterful self defense blade.The blade is nicely centered and the pivot is very smooth with no play. Deployment via the thumbstuds or flipper is very fast living up to the "SpeedSafe" moniker unlike my Kershaw Cryo 2.

Blade lockup is very tight with zero play in any direction with the heavy liner lock engaging the blade to about 55% of the blade thickness or about 85% of the liner thickness.just about perfect IMO, taking advantage of the full strength of the lock design and quality materials while still allowing for many years of wear compensation. I do not abide by the idea that very early lockup is a sign of superior quality and craftmanship. Yes it does require great skill and excellent materials and heat treatment to set a lock like that and yes it will outlast a deeper engaged lock. But it also makes it much more susceptible to inadvertent unlocking due to rough handling or heavy use as the liner lock is perched precariously close to the edge of theblade tang. Ill take about 30%-60% engagement depth thank you very much.Besides,this lock will likely last a lifetime as is so what exactly are the advantages to a lock that is hanging by its toenails anyway???

The balance point is right in the finger choil and although its not what id call a lightweight,it handles very well and is quick into action. Operation is smooth smooth smooth.from blade opening to unlocking and closing it just oozes solid smooth quality. Ergonomics are spot on.This has to be one of if not the most comfortable knives i own. The handle is just under .500" thick but is quite wide and hand filling at about 1.250" at the ring finger. Its just about perfect for my fairly large hands. The handle length is a little short as i can just get all four fingers on board but this allows the handle butt to nestle into the fleshy part of my palm and giving an extremely sure grip .the heavy but smooth jimping and the relatively shallow finger choil works together to really lock the knife in to my grasp and it does so very comfortably. Its actually a revelation bringing to my attention how incredibly uncomfortable some other knives are. The ZT0561 comes to mind here. Compared to this knife it is like gripping a cleated bicycle pedal with all the sharp edges and aggressive jimping. Overall this knife is just RIGHT.even the pocket clip is completely unnoticed in its stock position set for right hand tip down. Although i prefer tip up carry,because its so comfortable i plan to leave as is and adapt. Speaking of pocket clips,this one is very plain and boring looking but does a good job of securing the knife with a med deep carry.

All in all i am in love with this knife. Its muscular and athletic.at once powerful and nimble.rock solid yet graceful.a bit intimidating but beautiful. And did i mention comfortable? This is now my favorite EDC out of dozens of knives ranging from budget to high end. I really wouldnt change much about thislittle beauty. Thanks ZT! 5 stars and 99/100. Really great knife and extremely highly recommended. Definitely one of about five must haves.Buy it!

I'm not sure they still sell this on the Safariland site, the ALS has changed somewhat, but for me this is the perfect retention holster, natural draw disengages it. product_title: ProSource Puzzle Exercise Mat, EVA Foam Interlocking Tiles, Protective Flooring for Gym Equipment and Cushion for Workouts
review_headline: because we wanted to cover a good chunk of the 10x10 ish room
review_body:
Bought these to cover a pergo floor in an upstairs bedroom-turned-gym when we bought a punching bag on a stand. We bought 2 packs, because we wanted to cover a good chunk of the 10x10 ish room.

These are exactly what we wanted. They were super easy to put down, fit together perfectly, and were easy to cut to allow the heat/ac vents to flow. They're not super thick, but they're not as soft and spongey as the ones they make for kids' playrooms in primary colors. They also seem to have better grip than the kids ones; these don't slide around under you when you work out, at least not with the weight of the bag in the corner holding them down. They do cut down the noise a little bit too, which is nice. They look a little brown to me in the pictures,but they're actually a slightly grayish, sort of shiny black. Didn't really matter to us, color wise, but we do like the black.

As for working out on them, I spent an hour on the bag barefoot yesterday, and my feet felt great afterward. The mats are grippy enough so you don't slip, but not so grippy that you can't pivot a foot when barefoot when you want to. They're also comfortable to do floor exercises on; planks didn't make my elbows sore, and they gave a little cushion under my back for crunches. They're not going to make it not hurt if you take a spill, and they're certainly not going to protect against dropping huge weights on them, but they do offer some protection against scuffing and scratching. Overall, for the price, you can't find better.

product_title: Hip Hugger - The Big SheBang® - Women's Holster for large firearm Concealed Carry
review_body:
I will first say that this holster did not fit the niche that I wanted it to but it is in fact an excellent holster. I carry a Glock 19 and occasionally a Ruger LCR 357. I originally wanted something that could conceal my Glock in the 4:30-5:00 position low on my hips. Well....I've come to realize that just isn't practical for someone shaped as I am. 5'4. 140, very hour glass shaped with zero butt. Nope, nothing is going to work the for me. HOWEVER, this holster does work pretty nicely at the 5:00 position higher up on my waist, concealed in the indent under my ribs the narrowest part of my waist. Of course there is a slight print but most of the bulk of the gun is pretty well obscured. This works especially well when I'm wearing tight jeans and have no hope of stuffing a gun and a hybrid holster between myself and my pants. It also works nicely with yoga pants because it does not require a separate gun belt.

I actually bought mine from Can Can Concealment's Etsy shop because they had a purple version and I originally ordered large with a size extender because I have recently gained weight (boo!) but I had to return it and get a medium. Both belts I received are of excellent quality and are very sturdy. They do tend to loosen up slightly but are extremely comfortable. product_title: Bushnell 6MP Trophy Cam Essential Trail Camera with Night Vision
review_body:
The Bushnell 6MP Trophy Cam with night vision is an amazingly useful camera with its 60-second audio record, YesPIR sensor, adjustable (low/med/hi) AutoNight Vision Flash and more. It takes 8 AA batteries with a life of up to one year and can use standard or rechargeable batteries. It has a 32GB SD card capacity, a 60’ LCD display and comes with an adjustable web belt which we used to secure to a tree at various locations around our property. It is relatively waterproof as well.

There’s a settable time/date stamp which took a little figuring out, but we finally managed to set it and keep the setting. Some reviewers complained of needing a firmware update, but this camera which we received this month (Oct. 2014) was among those with the upgrade included.

The motion sensors use heat and motion to capture black and white images, while in daylight the images are in color. Also, the video length is programmable from one to sixty seconds. In our trials we were able to detect images beyond the 45 foot limit suggested, however, in low light they are not really clear. We live in a fairly remote area and were curious to see what visited our property at night, so we set up the camera near a birdbath, a gate onto the road at the edge of our property and near our hen house. At the birdbath location we clearly saw a skunk—didn’t have the time/date set for this one. However, for the others, we recorded images of a cat, a dog, a buck and two does in one location and a single doe in another.

We’re very pleased with the operation of the Bushnell 6MP Trophy Cam and have set it up near a wire fence where we’ve noticed some human traffic.

The camera was simple to set up and very intuitive. The instruction manual is as detailed as it needs to be and easy to read (larger type for our aging eyes would be a plus).

The only negatives would be that to use/test this camera, you need to provide both the batteries and an SD card as neither is included. review_body: I bought these after trying a different grip pad product that tore up after the first few uses. These looked to be a little more stout and that's proven true. I've had maybe 10 training sessions on them and they're still holding up.    I'm 225 lbs and do CrossFit. When someone of my size does a lot of reps of butterfly chest to bar pull-ups there tends to be a lot of friction/torsion on the hands. I was in need of something that would let me train harder and more often, since my hands were tearing and limiting my effort. The pads have allowed me to keep training without any tears so far.    The soft and firm pads work well, but the foam pad isn't useful for my type of training. I prefer the soft (thicker) pad because it's a little more forgiving.    The two things I would change if I could would be to have it shaped so that there was a more natural spot for your thumb and a light strap on the back to keep them on your hands when you let go. I could just as easily cut a corner off for my thumb, but really it's not that big a deal.

product_title: Zebco 33PL Platinum Series Spincast Reel
review_headline: User error doesn't make the reel bad.
review_body: I've read many of the negative reviews of the Zebco 33 Platinum, and couldn't disagree more! I've been using these reels exclusively for over twenty years and have not had the problems stated. I've caught fish as small as bream to fifteen pound redfish, and even a few twenty pound manta rays and a twenty-six pound catfish; as long as the drag is set properly, it's no problem. I use a one piece, medium action, seven foot Berkley Cheerywood Graphite rod exclusively for these reels. Recently, before the release of the newly redesigned Zebco 33, the factory starting shipping with the red, Cajun, 10lb. test line; I've found that it is coming with too much line and cut some off before I use the reel. I have had the line go under the drum a few times, but this is due to reeling when there is slack in the line under the cover. As stated earlier, I use these reels exclusively and have done so for over twenty years; consequently, I have adapted the way I hold the reel to prevent the slack from forming-- I palm the reel and hold my index finger over the hole and apply slight pressure to the line- I originally started doing this while bass fishing to better feel a bass pick up my worm, and now it's second nature. Don't let the bad reviews deter you from buying one of these reels. Also, and this may come across as pretentious, but two of my criteria for deciding how much I believe and accept a review are spelling and grammar. If the reviewer does not know the difference between your and you're, can not conjugate verbs, and/or use spellcheck, I can't find the review trustworthy. It's not that hard to proofread your review before posting it, and if what was posted WAS proofread,...need I say more?

product_title: Zepp Golf 3D Swing Analyzer
review_headline: No regrets in buying this one!

As a newbie golfer, I bought all sorts of training aids and even signed up for private lessons where they record your swings in video. But this Zepp Golf 3D Swing Analyzer is one training aid I don't regret buying and am definitely keeping. By using it when I'm at the driving range, this gives me immediate feedback on what I could be working on, instead of just swinging at the golf ball numerous times hoping it goes where you hope it would go, and not knowing what to fix when it doesn't. I use this with my I-phone. I have the phone right at my feet so I could see my swing stats right away.

I definitely think this is helping me in my learning process and I'm glad I decided to take the plunge and bought it.

product_title: Sniper Flip-up Rear Sight with Dual Aiming Aperture
review_body:
This is a beefy, solid rear sight. It's hard for me to imagine iron sights that cost several times this being any better. I was afraid it would be flimsy or have some play but it feels very heavy duty. Takes a good bit of force to flip up and down. Bit of lube helped that, but I think what it really needs is to be used a bit. Takes even more force to flip from the large aperture to small...well it feels like a lot of force because you can only use a finger. I'm sure that will become easier over time too.

I haven't taken it out shooting yet, but I have it mounted and I'm pretty happy with it.

The screw on the side is very beefy indeed. I guess it's made to be easy to install without tools. Personally I'd rather get the space back and have to use a big hex tool or something to install it, but this works too. The bolt doesn't come out completely, so no worries about losing it. This made it a little difficult to put loctite on, but I managed.

Overall a great little purchase. No regrets here.

review_headline: Excellent Floor Protector, Mediocre Exercise Mat
review_body:
Durable and feels solid, provides protection to hard wood floors. Mainly purchased to protect my hardwood floors for my home gym. While this floor mat does protect my hardwood floors, it is not quite suitable for home gym workouts like P90X. The mats are just too slippery and do not provide any traction for a safe workout. Even changing to various shoes, I am unable to find any shoe that can stand on the mat without slipping and sliding around. The whole mat even moves sometimes when I do workouts, which is quite frustrating. I suppose I could put some sort of tape on the bottom to prevent the mat from moving around, but that defeats the purpose of this mat.

The mats are also lacking in finish as well, I ordered two sets of these mats (black with gray flecks), the color from both boxes vary greatly. Some are dark black, while some other pieces are a lighter black. It really stands out when you're looking at them.

In hindsight, if you're looking for a good exercise mat, it's probably better to buy one that is one whole piece instead of it being in sectional pieces. That is what I should have purchased in the beginning.

review_body: I've owned this knife for over 18 months and use it nearly daily (my EDC) and I absolutely love this knife.  After using it on a 9 day camping trip I was compelled to write this review. I went 20 some years a very old EDC buck knife from my grandpa and replaced that with this and don't regret it for a moment.  It fits my average sized hand perfectly, and I can open it one-handed when necessary though it feels more comfortable using two hands for safety reasons.  I have the newer CPM S30V steel version.  And mine shipped directly from Golden Colorado (the shipping info manifest showed this.)  The blade is still as sharp today as was new.  About the hardest I've been on the blade is cutting shavings off a branches though its more usually used for trimming rope, breaking down boxes and trimming up shipping related things.  The blade barely looks used with no staining or scratches even with abusive use.  I just clean it well after each use or before I go to bed.  This knife is large enough you know its in your pocket when its laying loosely so I like to clip it to my pocket so a small part hangs out but it doesn't bother me a bit.  The clip is quite strong and I never fear its slipping out of my pocket.  I have considered getting a smaller knife for dress trousers or a suit as it does feel somewhat awkward in nicer clothing.  But I've not found a smaller EDC knife made in America that caught my attention yet.  I had many people recommend the Manix 2 G-10 as my first modern knife and I am completely satisfied with my purchase.  My only real desire with other knives are for other applications this knife wasn't intended to handle.  I would absolutely recommend this knife to anyone for any reason if a folding medium-sized knife was desired.  And this being made in America with high quality materials is all the better.

review_headline: Circumference too big for small hands on 12-lb bar.
review_body:
The bar was okay. I am still giving it 4 stars, even though I returned it, because I don't think everyone else will have the same problem I did.

PACKING: The bar arrived wrapped except for the capped ends, which were outside the packaging (loose plastic wrap and brown paper). The caps were grubby, but looked like they would clean easily with a damp paper towel.

THE BAR: The bar had no detectable rubber odor (a plus over some workout equipment I have purchased). The bar was heavily padded, which is both a pro and a con. It made for a squishy grip, but also a large one.

MY PROBLEM: My main problem, and the reason I returned it, was the circumference too big for me to easily grip. I am 5'6'', but have a slender build. The bar was 5 7/8 inches around.(~15 cm). I had a hard time wrapping my hands around the bar comfortably.

MY SOLUTION: I returned the bar and got a [[ASIN:B001QTPWKW Champion Barbell Reactor Work Out Bar, 12-Pound ]], which was a couple of inches shorter in length (still over 48 inches), but only had a circumference of 4 3/8 inches (~11.1 cm). That 1.5 inches may not seem like a lot, but it makes all the difference in how well I was able to grip the bar.

product_title: Bundle - 2 Items: Morakniv Fishing Comfort Fillet Stainless Steel Knife with 6.1" Blade Length and Morakniv Companion MG Carbon Steel Knife
review_body:
UPDATE: I stand by my original review. I guess I didn't make it clear enough that I like the knives very much, and the negativity is due to the fact it's an illogical pair of knives to bundle together (even though it's in the title and repeatedly stated in the review). I own both knives, purchased separately at full price. I had already owned and regularly used the Companion in high carbon steel and needed a better fillet knife, and would have been thrilled to have a mora STAINLESS companion for the tackle box as well (I ended buying a Mora Top Q Stainless Allround separately, it's great, a few spots but zero rust in heavy saltwater use). I'm gonna bet a lot of people who take offense to this review are armchair outdoorsmen, because no fisherman in their right mind would use a carbon steel knife, salt or freshwater, and any outdoorsman who knows anything would understand the nonsense of this combo. Why would Mora package a fishing knife with a Companion useless for fishing? They know fishing in Sweden, and they make a stainless Companion and many other fine stainless knives, why not offer any of those in the bundle? It's pretty dumb, and judging by the four total reviews, this bundle isn't exactly jumping off the shelves. For those MORA FANBOYS who still might take offense to my criticism of the great Morakniv company, PLEASE READ THIS CLOSELY: I USE AND ENJOY AT LEAST 5 MORA PRODUCTS ON A REGULAR BASIS for fishing, camping, and around the home. It's a GREAT PRICE for two fine, UNRELATED knives, but THIS PRODUCT BUNDLE MAKES NO SENSE AND COULD EASILY BE MADE BETTER FOR FISHERMEN. It is amusing that people are actually steamed about this review (It looks like the reply where someone actually called me names has been removed). For those who think this is a great bundle, perhaps I could interest you in welding mask/wood glue bundle? On a trip to McDonalds do you order a quarter pounder and a roll of toilet paper? Come to think of it, those last 2 are more directly related and useful than a fishing knife and a high carbon steel knife…

ORIGINAL REVIEW:

This may be a little unfair since I have not purchased this item, but here's why I won't purchase it. I own the mora carbon steel companion MG, and it is a great knife. But it is useless in a saltwater environment, especially if you don't have access to freshwater to thoroughly clean the blade after it touches salt water. Salt water begins rusting carbon steel immediately. Not a huge deal, it can be cleaned off with steel wool if the blade already has a patina on it, but stainless steel is much more useful in salt water, and frankly will save you a lot of headaches with freshwater too, carbon steel is just not a great material for use in constantly wet environments. So here we have two great knives, but not a great combination. I'd venture to bet that a combo of the two fillet knives would actually be pretty good, the shorty would probably be great for cutting bait, line, and gills when you're bleeding the fish out etc, but I personally use the Mora top Q all-around for grunt work around salt water, highly recommended. I believe the companion comes in stainless too, why they wouldn't offer them as a combo for fishing use is beyond me, what else are you going to use a long fillet knife for?

product_title: Conquer Dual Bike Storage Stand Aluminum Telescopic Floor to Ceiling Pole - 2 Bikes
review_headline: sturdy, well made, easy-install and just what I needed
review_body:
I have a couple of single-bike floor stands from Feedback Sports and they’re great but I now have so many bikes that I needed something that would hold two bikes up and out of the way but still make them easily accessible. I agonized over what storage solution to go with because there are so many options. You have pressure pole racks like this one, stand-alone racks for two bikes, floor racks for multiple bikes, racks that attach to a wall, and racks that hang from the ceiling. And I’m probably missing some. A ceiling rack seemed difficult to install and a wall mounted rack would involve the complete rearrangement of my garage so I narrowed it down to a pressure pole or a stand-alone rack. In the end I went with a pressure pole stand because it appeared sturdier and to take up less place. I chose wisely by going with the Conquer Dual Bike Telescopic Floor to Ceiling Pole rack because the only complaint I have about it is that it doesn’t come with instructions. I thought the lack of instructions was a mistake but when I contacted the seller (CyclingForLess) they said that’s how it comes. CyclingForLess was kind enough to give me their phone number and say they’d give me a walkthrough if necessary but as it turns out that wasn’t needed. The stand comes mostly assembled and it’s fairly intuitive to put together even for someone like myself who normally has trouble with this sort of thing. Just by looking at it I was able to figure most of it out but looking at photos online helped too. You can’t really break anything or screw anything up permanently during assembly so that’s a relief. Once assembled and put it place I had to tweak the space between the two holders so that my two bikes wouldn’t overlap. But I didn’t want the top bike being up so high that it would be difficult to grab so the longest part of the assembly was just adjusting the spacing and tilt of the holders. It took about 45 minutes to get it just right but I’m kind of OCD about these things. I had to have the space and tilt just perfect. Once you have the bike holders placed correctly then you can go ahead and tighten everything to the max.

As a safety precaution, you’ll probably want to line up the top piece of the pole with a stud in your ceiling because you’re going to want to tighten the pole as much as it will go and that applies quite a bit of upward pressure. You tighten the pole in three places; at each telescoping junction and at the bottom of the pole. You tighten at the telescoping junctions first and then at the base. I found it helpful to have my wife tighten and lock the telescoping junctions while I applied upward pressure on the pole itself. The base you can tighten by yourself but keep in mind you’re going to turn the knob for a long time until you can’t tighten it anymore. Once the pole itself starts turning you know you’ve tightened it as much as it will go. Once tightened to the limit you’ll probably still feel a little bit of give when you shake the pole because of the spring at the top. That’s just the nature of the design and since it’s a pressure pole it’s never going to be unmovable. If you push on the pole enough or shake it violently yes you can dislodge it. But for holding two carbon road bikes this pole is more than sturdy enough. I wouldn’t hesitate to put two mountain bikes on it or even more two Electra Townies and those bikes are really heavy. The stand is a great space saver. It’s profile is minimal and I placed it right in the heart of my bike area for easy access. The construction of the Conquer pole is surprisingly good. All parts are thick, well made and solid. That’s one of the things that attracted me to this stand. From the photos it appeared better made than the other stands I looked at. I also liked how much thicker the pole is than some of the other pressure poles. Maybe it’s psychological but I feel better about it being bigger. In summary, I really think this product is the best option for a two-bike storage rack. It’s priced competitively, it’s trustworthy, easy to install, portable, and easy on and off for your bikes.is product is the best option for a two-bike storage rack. product_title: SA Sports Fever Crossbow Package 543
review_body:
Although I didn't buy this one from amazon, I bought the exact same one from Dick's sporting goods on a black Friday special for about $130. It was a Christmas present to myself so that I could get back into archery hunting. (PA allows crossbows for archery) I followed the directions for assembly with no problems.

Its fairly easy to cock with the string/assist pulley like device. The trigger isn't great, but its not too bad either.

I can hit very accurately out to 40 yards. I use the various marks on the scope for different ranges. I even printed a diagram of the scope reticle and wrote which mark was for which distance. I taped that to the stock so that I would never forget where to shoot at a particular distance target.

I chronographed the bolts with 100 grain tips at about 200 fps. It's not the advertised 235fps, but still not too bad. If you use that speed and weight bolt, you get an energy that is good enough for deer hunting.

I took it for archery season last year and got a doe on the last day of the season from my treestand. I was about a 30 yard shot, went through both sides of the deer. I found her about 40 yards from where I shot her.

Small drawbacks: the scope is not the best quality. It does work OK, but there is some distortion at the edge of the field. My first string frayed and began to unwind after only a few shots. I emailed the manufacturer and they sent me 2 free replacement strings in the mail. The bolts are crap, throw them away and use better ones. Even with there cons, I think its a great deal. I thought about buying a more expensive one, but this one works fine, I might just use it indefinitely.

product_title: Buck Knives SpitFire Folding Knife
review_headline: It's a piece for American made, don't buy.
review_body: This knife is a piece. Do not buy it. The handles have been sloppily cut and the edges are sharp, the holes for the bolts are too big and allows play in throughout the whole knife. The rear frame support is also sloppily cut and doesn't align with the handle. The lockback piece is cut too thin causing a wobble, also cut too short causing the blade to cross the 180* center, putting the blade at a 185* angle when cutting or applying force. Also the picture of the serrated knife on the internet or on the website is fraud; the photo shows the serrations protruding from the blade, whenever the actual out-of-the-box product is recessed into the blade, causing severe snagging whenever cutting. The sharpened edge of the blade is sharp but was also cut sloppily, causing an unevenness and curving along the entire edge of the blade. For such a high price on the knife, this is very unprofessional and says a lot about the character of Buck Knives: disappointing. Maybe knives should be made in China because then they'd at least be cut right, seems like Americans and their companies are getting sloppy and careless. Buck Knives needs to improve their quality. I have high hopes for their knives and I personally feel let down by the quality of the 2 knives I purchased from them.

product_title: Dead Ringer Trauma 100 Grain 2-Blade for Broadheads (3-Pack), 2-Inch
review_headline: Left a very good and short blood trail
review_body:
I purchased the Trauma 100 Grain along with the Rampage 1 1/2 inch cut (2blade). I shot a doe with the rampage and it dropped within 30 yards. Left a very good and short blood trail. Both the entrance and exit wound were as advertised.
Then I tried the Trauma on a second doe. Unfortunately, I made a poor shot and wasn't quite sure where I had hit her. The blood trail was unbelievable!!! I mean, blood was spraying on sapling's and brush! Upon observing this, I began to change my thinking that I had made a better shot than thought. I found the deer expired within fifty yards.

I had only waited about 20 minutes, as I had work in the afternoon and it was too warm to wait until the next morning. I was completely in awe when I observed that it was a gut shot and half of her intestinal tract was hanging out of the gapping wound. Upon field dressing the doe, and clearing the intestine from the wound; I observed an exit hole the size of my fist. All this was achieved with a 60 pound draw weight.

In the past- I have used Wasp, Cabela's Muzzy, Slick Trick, Grim Reaper, and Rage broadheads. None of them have ever caused this devastation. I mean none and I have shot tons of deer. The name Trauma is truly fitting. After 29 years of bowhunting; I have found a broadhead that I am completely satisfied with. Just amazing!!!!

Normally I tend to not trust these as much as some people, but after shooting this out to 500 yards, I am thoroughly convinced that this particular BDC reticle is wicked accurate! On a side note, I have never had to use the vortex warranty that came with this scope, but from what I've heard it is amazing. Vortex apparently really takes care of their customers. My skin stayed nice and firm as I lost weight, so I look great as well as feel great! (None of that flabby hanging arm skin I have seen on others who loose weight).

Rebounders have been in my family since the mid 80's, so I am familiar with them, and even tried all the various types that claim to be the best. (Several family members sold different ones over the years -:)

All my family members and friends who visit me, love my JumpSport rebounder, some even try to take It when I'm not looking (-: (Like my Nephews who, swipe it every chance they get, they love to do gymnastic stunts off / onto it)

I have also left it outside in the Texas dessert sun for 6 months, since I love to rebound outside in the early morning, and under the stars (-:

All this and it still works great!

Many of my family and friends have now given away their spring rebounders and replaced them with the silent JumpSport rebounders like mine (-:

One of the main things we all love about them, is that they actually get used!

No noisy springs that wake up kids or others resting / watching a football game!

product_title: Fiebing's Pro Dye
review_body:
I found two free leather sofas on Craigslist that were faded very unevenly by the sun. They were also a burgundy color. I deglazed the sofas with an alcohol/lemon juice mixture and then dyed them with Fiebing's Professional Oil Dye in chocolate. The dye did an amazing job with consistent color on each area, both sun-faded and the original color of the leather.

I also used the dye on an old braided synthetic fiber rug. I didn't want a crunchy texture of paint, so I decided to experiment with oil dye. (Rit dye did nothing, as if I had painted it with water color.) It was a mess, and it took an insane amount of dye for a 6x9 rug (about 48 ounces total) but it worked, as a first step. The biggest problem was that the dye wasn't color-fast as it is on leather. It came right off on my hands, even after 3 days of drying. Makes sense, since it's a leather dye, not a fiber dye, right? I ended up sealing the dye on the rug with watered down paint (again, to avoid crunchiness) in a color that closely matched the dye. If I hadn't used the dye, the paint wouldn't have had enough coverage in the water-down form (I checked on the side I didn't dye. No good.) I don't recommend this crazy project, it was way too expensive and one heck of a mess, but I do have a lovely brown braided rug under my kitchen table now. Bottom line, the dye is good stuff.

product_title: Benjamin Marauder Synthetic Stock Pellet Air Rifle
review_body:
The Benjamin Marauder .25 is my second PCP air rifle, the other is an Airforce Condor in .22. I try to buy \\"Made in America\\" as much as I can!!!

I have been into airguns for many many years. I still have and use a 30+ year old Benjamin 342 multi pump. PCPs are a whole new level.

The Marauder is relatively powerful, quiet...and can be made quieter with some legal aftermarket products. Accuracy is excellent, with no need to develop special holds like the \\"artillery hold\\" that is popular with spring or nitro guns. Just shoot them like any other \\"real\\" rifle you have experience with. Aim small, miss small. With ammo scarce and expensive, this rifle is good to keep your skills up. Fundamentals are the same. Breath control, squeeze, bang...or pop as these things go.

8 round magazine is nice, as my Condor is single shot. Having a quick follow up shot is nice if you use it for hunting...and this rifle can be used for hunting. Game as large as coyotes have been taken. Personally I would not be comfortable taking a coyote, but if my skills were better and I could be assured of a humane kill I would if I was hunting coyote. Some folks have the skills and have done so.

Now I haven't shot anything but paper with my rifle. This is just to inform about the power level of this rifle. It is not a toy, but an adult air rifle. Make sure you have a good backstop and be aware of what is behind whatever you are shooting at. I have read on the forums of guys taking ground squirrels and birds at 100+ yards.

The barrel is a high quality American product. I have heard the .177 and .22 barrels are a bit of a hit and miss. Some are great others not so good. There are folks making aftermarket barrels for those rifles though if you buy one of those and get a lemon.

I recommend a Hill or FX pump if you are going to hand pump. It is not hard, just use your legs like doing shallow squats. I pump mine up during commercial breaks LOL. Heat is the enemy of pumps, so just take it slow, pause at the top of the stroke as well as the bottom. With all the valving, you want to make sure each chamber has a chance to fill before pumping.

You can use any rifle scope you have as well. Springers or nitro guns need airgun rated scopes as the double recoil will kill even the most expensive rifle scope. These guns are safe for any scope you have laying around.

I recommend this rifle if you are doing pest control or small game hunting. It uses more air than a .177 or .22 so if you are just punching holes in paper you might consider another caliber. product_title: Jaco Guardian Protective Cup System (no pads)
review_headline: not recommend for something like Krav, where groin strikes are common.
review_body:
I started doing a lot of ground work recently, where I am laying on my back.
My fight shorts are loose, and would drop to show everything up to my underwear.
So… I needed something to show a little modesty, but offer protection.
I bought 3 Compressions shorts with Groin protection.
Shock Doctor Ultra 232 in Medium, The Shock Doctor Core Compression 221, and the Jaco Compression shorts with Cup System Size L.
My measurements:
87cm waist 34.2in.
102cm hips 40in.

The Jaco Compression shorts have an external strapping system to allow you to perfectly place the cup where you want it.
The issue I have, is they both use the same shaped cup as Shock Doctor.
Most of the newer cups are going for this narrow, longer cup, but if held in place correctly, they do a good job.
The straps the Jaco uses use actually attached directly to the cup, and they are non-stretchy. They rely on the stretch of the pants.
The strap I do not like, is the G-String strap. It is totally necessary for keeping the cup in place, but it has a bump
where the strap attaches to the cup, so it’s like sitting on a knot, if you sit down.
I ride a Cycle to the gym. Takes about 30 minutes. It was the biggest mistake of my life to put my groin protection
on at home, then ride. Every bump, man-hole, and pot-hole, would feel like someone smashing walnuts on my pelvic bone. Breaking was the same.
It really made me appreciate the Shock Doctor Titan with the soft rubber edges. 3 days later, my taint is still killing me.
The edges on the Jaco are hard, so even though the blow is dispersed, it is dispersed local to the blow, not spread over the whole surface of the cup. This makes for a shocked experience every time someone hits you.
I would not recommend these for something like Krav, where groin strikes are common.
These shorts worked well for stand up, and the length is the best of the bunch, but for overall protection and comfort, I’m sticking to my other selections.

The Shock Doctor Core Compression 221,is criminal. Someone should loose their job on that one.
First the cup rides high, so the pointy end of the cup does not sit on the … taint (look it up).
If I stand next to a chair and place one foot on it, the cup will drop away, and line up with the shorts.
The drop is roughly 1 inch.
That is EASY enough space to allow ‘something' to get between the cup and your pelvis bones.
If someone kicks you while you are in this position, you will get pinched… and probably end up going to the hospital.
The Shock Doctor Ultra 232 is different. It has an internal band that pulls the bottom part of the cup to your skin, no matter what position your legs are in.
The thing I like more about the 221, is the length. It comes almost to my knees, the 232 stops like short boxer briefs,
giving you that muffin-top look as your skin puffs out.
I replaced the standard BioFlex cup they put in the Boxer Compression shorts, with the ShockDoctor Adult Titan Alloy Flex Cup, XL.
I removed the cup from the 221, and use my BadBoy groin guard Size M under it.
The Compression short is still good, and light weight, and allows for more legs-in-the-air without feeling embarrassed.

The standard ShockDoctor Cup is too narrow, unless placed exactly correct, but the 232 does a good job of keeping any of the cups you choose to put inside, in the correct place.
The Jaco, can only use the cup they provide.

product_title: 5.11 Tactical.56003 Adult's Side Trip Briefcase
review_headline: A must buy.... don't even bother reading the review, just add it to your cart and pay for it.
review_body:
Wow, what a GREAT bag! I have a conceal carry permit and my EDC is a Springfield XDs or Glock 27. Pretty much any firearm will fit in the padded slot and of course I use a kydex trigger guard to keep things 100% safe. It's really a "hidden" pocket that runs the width of the bag and it's lined in a fleecy material with a velcro closure. It would be better if it was not velcro because the sound of opening a 15" velcro strip isn't very stealthy but it is secure and a laptop bag isn't exactly an ideal concealed carry solution. I like having a firearm with me so it's far better than not having one when I'm wearing scrubs and can't conceal carry on me. On the plus side, nobody would know the compartment exists. It basically looks like a seam.

Outside of the velcro closure on the dedicated pocket, I have to say it's an outstanding laptop bag in every other way!

- Super roomy pockets
- Great handle that is leaps and bounds better than your typical velcro keeper. This has a 2 piece molded rubbery handle that mates together to form a very comfortable grab handle. Great idea 5.11!!!
- Super wide unidirectional strap with grippy underside that keeps the bag from sliding. Another great feature I've only seen on nice camera bags.
- Roomy edge pockets. I use the back pocket for a water bottle and the front pocket for my Fenix PD35 and Benchmade Griptilian.
- Main compartment is HUGE. Big enough for my MacPro 15" and a couple of 1" binders. Still leaves 2-3 inches of width for a small pouch with pens, cables etc.

I've had many many bags from Samsonite, Tumi, etc and strictly speaking about it's merits as a laptop bag.... this is the nicest one yet. Tempted to pick up another to keep as a backup when this wears out in 50 years. LOL!

review_body:
Model Number: Teeter Hang Up EP-560

"How could this product have gotten so many great reviews? It's completely unsafe! As you try to get on and secure your feet between the upper and lower rollers, you can fly backwards at an alarming speed and nearly fall out onto your floor (my floor is Travertine stone). If you manage to get your feet secured with the lever which is very hard to operate, you still go back way too fast and you may not be able to get back up. My husband couldn't get up and he's athletic and in fairly good shape. I almost couldn't get up and would have been stuck for over an hour upside down. It's also hard to get your feet in between the pads and to secure to the notch that keeps your feel from allowing you to slide out when upside down.

The inversion table is huge and takes up a large foot print in your home. Yes I think inversion tables work and the material is definitely sturdy, but I've tried other brands and have not had these problems. I STRONGLY RECOMMEND YOU TRY THIS BEFORE YOU BUY IT AND NEVER USE IT ALONE!!!"

product_title: Ontario Knife 8862 Folding Knife, Pink
review_body:
First of all, I did not get the pink one, I got the black one, my comments however apply to both. After researching what knife I should get, I settled on this one due to reviews, and I am supremely impressed. I have owned many knives, and this one is king.

Pros;
1) Perfect size for carrying in any pants from gym shorts, to Jeans, to dress pants.
2) Great weight. Just light enough to be unnoticed in your pocket, yet not light enough to feel cheep.
3) Quick opening. It is, in fact faster than many of my spring assisted knives, and that is with no wrist flick.
4) Extremely solid. When it is open, it has the feel of a fixed blade knife.
5) Ambidextrous. With four (yes that's 4) clip positions, and dual thumb studs, this knife is ambidextrous.
6) Sits low in pocket. For not having a fold over clip, this knife sits very low.
7) Razor sharp. I was shaving out of the box.

Cons;
1) Made in Taiwan. As far as quality goes, Taiwan is great, I would however prefer my money go to America.
2) The liner lock is a slightly too small, making it take a few milliseconds longer to close with one hand.

So all in all, this knife was worth twice the cost, and I would advise it for anyone.

product_title: The GunBox Biometric Hand Gun Safe
review_headline: Ideal for Parents of Young Children
review_body:
This seems to be the ideal gun safe for responsible and prepared parents.

We like the biometric only option to open the safe. Curious two-year-olds can find keys, both mechanical and the RFID kind, and gain access to guns. By requiring a fingerprint we are assured that they will not be able to open it even if they find the key.

We were concerned about the reader's speed and reliability using the fingerprint reader. We swipe our fingerprints to access our laptop and phones. This can be infuriating and would be unacceptable during an emergency should we need to access to guns while under stress.

Reading our fingerprint is not instantaneous. It takes a second to identify our finger and release the spring loaded clam shell. We are able to have gun in hand in under two seconds. This is acceptable to us. We rely on a home alarm to alert us to an intrusion if one were to occur. We should have ample time to respond.

During the first month of ownership, we thought the biometric reader would prove too unreliable for us. It only opened for us about three quarters of the time. We discovered two possible culprits, dry fingers and relying on the battery. The first is solved simply by moistening our finger before placing it on the reader. The second is solved by leaving it plugged in. We have had no problems since.

We would like to see a larger model offered. It will not hold two full sized semiautomatics and related accessories. We would like to store two full sized guns and four magazines. As it is, it holds one 4\\" Springfield XD and one Walther P22 with only enough room in between them for one spare magazine. The width is fine, it is just not deep enough.

The interior is lined with a rubber like material. But not all surfaces are covered; there is exposed bare aluminum. When we go to move the safe, our inclination is to carry it like a laptop. The guns move around and their finish has been scratched as result. We would prefer high density foam found in virtually all gun cases to secure them from movement and damage. We would also like a handle or some grippy surface treatment to make it easier to handle.

The safe looks like some sort of electronic device and our non-gun owning friends probably just assume it is a WiFi router or cable modem. Their presumption is enhanced by the two USB ports in the rear and by the fact that it sits next to the laptop during the day on our kitchen counter. This is fine by us. It saves having uncomfortable conversations.

We withheld a star reluctantly because we like it so much. There is nothing on the market that matches it. review_body: The vest is very low profile, The shoulder straps are on the thinner side than most vests and wont dig into your neck. The vest, except for the reflective material and black material at the bottom, is a lightweight breathable nylon mesh. (The Mir Vest looks similar to the discontinued \\"Brooks RV610 Reflective Vest\\") It's bright and very reflective. Only the white/gray portion and \\"MIR\\" logo reflects, the neon yellow does not. And of course the back of the vest reflects too. The entire strap adjustment system runs along the vest at the front and rear reinforcing it to prevent the mesh from pulling or distorting as you snug it up. The lightweight vest doesn't bounce around when running and the low profile and mesh and helps keep you cool.     It seems the only size for this vest is medium/large and no small. I have a 32 inch waist (with shirt) and the vest fit loosely even when set at the smallest position. I cut off just under 3 inches of the excess velcro strap because it just stuck out in front of the vest. This left about 3 inches of velcro remaining. The excess velcro is easily cut and has no stitching to unravel. After wearing it after a run I decided it was still a bit too loose when my arms rubbed against the side of vest. I folded the elastic strap over itself and hand stitched it making a neat looking quick alteration. With the velcro trimmed and elastic shortened, It still fits over heavier running jackets with little change to the velcro attachment point. I can easily undo the stitching if I ever needed to make it larger. So for women with small waists keep in mind it will be a bit baggy around the waist. You can shorten the elastic like I did to make it more snug. I posted some photos as well.    Hint: To best view how reflective the vest is, use a flashlight and don't hold it at waist level. Hold it at eye level or on your forehead and shine it at the vest. (This is similar to what car headlights would do)

product_title: Daiwa Ballistic Spinning Reel
review_headline: Spend a little more get alot more
review_body: I fished all of the major brands of spinning reels hard....you name it: Shimano, Pflueger, Quantum,  Mitchell, etc....but my favorites are the older Series Shimano Stradic FG Series and definitely this Ballistic 3000. Granted both Shimano and Daiwa are trusted names in the fishing game and they have both made improvements to their product lines over the years. I fish the older Daiwa Millionaire CV-Z and CV-X left hand casting reels and adore their smooth, dependable, rock solid performance in both fresh and salt water. These Millionaire CV Series reels are built like a bank vault with frames CNC Machined from Aerospace grade Billet Barstock Aluminum. The Millionaire CV series has been superseded by the Luna model which is basically the same reel as the older CV-Z Series with an exterior magnetic backlash adjustment instead of an internal adjustment dial. Long story short I had become disenchanted with the Shimano product line sans Stradic Spinning Reels which prompted me to try the Daiwa's. I have never looked back. Salmon and Steelhead from as small as Jacks to Chinook over 30 pounds have been caught by my Daiwa Millionaire CV's and hopefully this Ballistic in time. I have several less expensive reels that I have for use in saltwater as basically throw away reels. However, the smooth solid performance of this Ballistic is amazing in salt water. The drag is smooth and solid. Casting and retrieve are the same.....smooth and rock solid. No hiccups or other detracting performance Gremlins to report after two seasons. If smooth, rock solid and dependable performance on the salt water from a spinning reel is what you seek look no further. I am very skeptical about any new equipment that I purchase and tend to gravitate toward my proven old favorites. The acquisition of this Daiwa Ballistic 3000 has been worth every single penny. Can you get by with less? Definitely. However, if you take your salt water angling any type of seriously and want a reel that performs without complaint day in and day out from sunrise to sunset get the Ballistic. I have been amazed at the performance of this reel on the water. Sure, my less expensive Daiwas, Shimanos, and Pfleuegers are hanging in there for now, maybe one more season or two and they are going to start dying. Yes I had spent considerably more money on this Ballistic than the common Department Store Bargain models in the Daiwa, Pflueger line of spinning reels in the plastic retailer blister pack. They are showing signs of mechanical deterioration that spell death soon. Salt water is especially hard on fishing equipment especially reels. There is no more punishing test for fishing reels than salt water. My Ballistic is performing like new into the second season without any issue. That is the pinnacle of peak performance in my book....to be able to fish the reel hard in salt water cast after cast and fight fish after fish while maintaining rock solid, silky smooth performance the entire time without a hitch. My Daiwa Ballistic 3000 spinning reel is nicely mated to my 9'6" Lamiglas Si spinning rod equipped with titanium frame line guides, carbon fiber handle and reel seat. This is the ideal light tackle float rod or light spoon and spinning rod for salt water. Sure this is a stellar combination for Summer Run Steelhead and Coho Salmon. The Ballistic is right at home in Mother Nature's ultimate proving ground for spinning reels....the salt water. I have less than zero complaints regarding my handsome stalwart performing Ballistic 3000. Definitely recommend!

review_headline: Good Distance Finder but Older Model
review_body:
This is a great product for measuring distance to the green. It is easily operated and needs little updating or downloading of course information as it has stored 50,000 courses on it. However, this is one of the first generation models. I am not sure what the next 3 models which are newer (voice +, vt3 or vs4) can offer but I noticed this when I was at the Pro Shop of my Club and saw the newer generation and the pro told me the one I had and just bought the day before was the first model they came out with. With that being said it was $50 cheaper than the newer models.

Positive -
-Easy to use, turn on and use
- bright, lighted display
-volume control

Negative -
- only displays to the center and to get the front and the back you must hold down the button
- does not assist with lay up shots
- one of the 1st generation models

UPDATE: I bought the newer model vs4 and it displays the front middle and back on the screen without having to hold the button down. I do prefer this feature on the newer one as it takes less time and is easier to get your distances. The newer one also snaps into a cradle which becomes the belt clip as opposed to this one which has the belt clip attached directly to the unit. Even thought I have not had the newer one fall out of the cradle, I do believe the older models clip style is more secure. The older one also comes with a plastic cover which in direct light was sometimes difficult to read but did provide protection and the newer model does not have any kind of protective cover.

product_title: Coleman 1000 Lumen CPX 6 Lantern
review_body:
As other reviewers have noted, it is BRIGHT. No idea of how impact resistant it is and the battery pack and it's contacts area do not appear to be at all waterproof but seeing as how I bought it primarily for power outage use that is not much of a concern. I also have the older Coleman Twin LED lantern and there is no comparison in output. This is the first LED lantern I have seen that can compare favorably with a double mantle propane lantern. A lot safer for indoor use though.

This is a large lantern. It is similar in size overall to the 8 D cell Coleman Twin LED lantern but is a lot lighter due to using only 4 D batteries in the removable battery pack. About a foot high with the bail folded down.

If you want to use rechargeable batteries I suggest using D size NiMH such as Tenergy Centuras or using 2AA to D adapters or 3AA to D parallel adapters, both available here on Amazon. Load the adapters with rechargeable NiMH batteries like Eneloops and go for it. This is due to the Coleman rechargeable battery being sealed lead acid technology and if you read the reviews on it about 1/3 are ONE STAR due to early failure. review_headline: Cuts through weeds, tall grasses, and thin branches, like Buttah!
review_body:
I have been looking for a machete that was useful for around my property in the mountains. There are a lot of tall weeds, and some thin branches that get in the way, along my trails.

This has a CroMoly blade which has been durable for an afternoond of cutting through tall grass, and very thin tree limbs. I cut through wet and dry grasses without any problems. A quick strike through is all I needed to cut.

The saw blades are actually functional, unlike some other "Tacticool" blades on the market. The handles are a polymer and are quite comfortable for handling the blade. The weight and balance are excellent.

It is accompanied by a canvas handle with a belt strap for hiking or long walks (where legal).

After cutting for an afternoon, I checked the blade edge for dull areas or bends in the blade, and I found none. I sharpen it using my Apex Pro Edge knife sharpening set. It's too cumbersome for a Lansky system.

Overall, I'm pleased with this general purpose machete.

She nearly ripped them away, with much Ooooooo-ing and Ahhhhhh-ing.
I wanted to use them as line handling gloves on a newly acquired Catalina 320, she had other ideas. She has two beautiful Newfoundland dogs. They are HUGE. One is a typical Newfie, never pulls on a leash, always regal. The other, a rescue, is young and sometimes pulls.
So she tested them first. She says she felt more secure, no slipping. I think she was setting me up to let her keep them!
But I really wanted to try them on the lines. They worked out really well, protecting my hands, and gripping even when wet.
Even after a full day, the compression made for very little fatigue.
You get more than enough dexterity to handle lines, and I like that they are so visible.

Then, they got the ultimate test. We have a friend, in her 30s, in a wheelchair. She is fun and a little wild in terms of style. She always wears gloves as she rolls. She tested them with her racing wheelchair.

Needless to say, we never got these wonderful gloves back.
Once she gets rolling, no way can you catch her!

I received a sample to review...and will have to buy another pair.

review_headline: decent for the price, but some serious complaints
review_body:
A very nice little bag, well made, comfortable, and larger then I thought. that said there are a few major issues holding it back. the straps are very difficult to adjust, so much so that you basically have to take off the bag to change the strap length. the water bottle pouch is a great concept, however it needs to slightly larger, its about 1/4 too small limiting what size bottles you can use. The strap that goes across the waist is perhaps that biggest disappointment. I am a 32-34 waist and the strap is just large enough for me to use, however, as you use the bag the strap slowly loosens with no cap at the end it has completely undone itself several times and as I have mentioned it is terribly annoying to tighten.
I don't want to give the impression that this is a bad bag, its pretty solid for the money, but the affore mentioned complaints will probably have me upgrading to the maxpedition monsoon sling eventually. but at ~120-140$ it might be a little bit and this bag should tide me over

product_title: Aqua Sphere Kayenne Swim Goggle, Made In Italy
review_headline: Very poor goggles if you're near-sighted.  Massively distorted view.
review_body: Very unhappy with these goggles.  I was excited to try these out, given all the positive reviews.  When I put them on, they were comfortable enough.  However, as soon as I went underwater I was surprised at how fuzzy/distorted everything became.  I am very near-sighted (wear contacts, one eye is a 7.0, the other is an 8.5), so I thought maybe it had something to do with the interaction between my contact lenses and the curved lenses on the goggles.  So, I swapped these out for my daughters' goggles, both of whom have Speedo googles (one has the Speedo Vanquisher, the other has a Speedo Hydrospex).  It was like night and day.  The Speedos (which have a completely flat lens surface in front) provided extremely clear underwater vision.  I eventually sent these back, and replaced them with a pair of Speedo Bullet goggles (also with a flat front surface), which are great (i.e. extremely clear underwater vision).  As a final note, the Aqua Sphere's also fogged up very quickly.  My conclusion: if you are very near-sighted, there is some kind of bad interaction with swim goggles that have a curved lens, so stick with something that has a flat front lens like the Speedos.

review_headline: Great gloves, good support, breathable - fits a bit big overall
review_body:
What is it:
GEL Wraps / gloves

What I liked:
I wasn't sure how much I'd like velcro (and gloves overall) compared to traditional wraps, but this has been great so far.

Padding: The gel padding is great - really softens the blow and protects where it should on the hand which is super helpful.
Support: Tightens around the wrist perfectly for support which is critical.
Material: Good quality material that's thick enough to be resistant to day to day use/damage, but also breathes which is super important ('cause lets face it, if you're not sweating when you use these, you're not working hard enough!)

What I didn't like:
Sizing was a bit difficult to figure out (couldn't find a size chart anywhere in the listing or on the web...)

If you fit a large in Everlast gloves (the ones you put under your boxing gloves), you should fit a large in these; the sizing seems to be close, but this brand does fit/feel bigger overall, IMO.

A word of caution - from what I can tell, Small is actually juniors - so unless you have very small hands, go with Medium as the smallest IMO.

I wear these under boxing gloves (Everlast Gel ones in a L/XL 16oz) and it works quite well for fit; snug, but not overly so.

Would I buy it again/recommend it?
Great gloves, a bit more expensive than other alternatives, but worth the extra cost IMO, once you get your size right! :)

product_title: Okuma SLV Graphite 4-Piece Fly Rod
review_headline: An awesome value. The action is MEDIUM FAST
review_body: An awesome value. The action is MEDIUM FAST, a tad on the FAST SIDE. As to the other reviewer, I honestly don't think most people know what medium action is anymore. TFO FINESSE line is Medium action. I generally don't like anything other than medium action, and I've been at this awhile. However, when we get into eight weights and up in fresh water, we are in big, heavy water and big fish - DISTANCE and DEPTH  FISH SIZE AND WEATHER are important. I lived in New Zealand for 10 years and a 9 1/2' , 7 wt. was my \\"go to\\" rod for medium and large rivers - a medium action. There are spots where an 8 wt. would be handy. ( there are many places where 4, 5 & 6 are perfect too)    As to this product, you are getting a custom length rod at 9 1/2 feet, with very sound hardware and construction. The 8 wt. has an extra layer or three of graphite at the base of the first section. The fighting butt is, I must say, very well designed for optional two handed casts or roll casts.    Even if you are hooked yourself on the big three or four high ender companies, you should consider this rod as a backup. Your 25 year warranty is useless on the shores of lake Stroebbel when you've snapped a tip.    Click click click!!!

product_title: Wild Sports College Leather Office Chair
review_body:
This is the worst office chair I ever had! I am working from my home office on a daily basis, so having a decent chair to work is essential to me. This chair looked comfortable and well made and another plus was that we are actually "bleeding blue" in our house ;) So our team's logo on the chair was definitely a plus.

The first trouble started already at assembly. As a previous reviewer mentioned, the chrome looking plastic covers for the curve of the arms are so ill-fitting they fall out of place the moment you move this chair. Since these parts are very thin plastic, there is no way to "bend" them in position, let alone hit them with a hammer to make them stay put. I have been having this chair for about 2 years now and the hydraulic is shot. Even though I am 5'5" I have to adjust this chair to the highest position, to be able to sit correctly in front of my computer. This position holds for about 3 minutes and that the chair starts softly sliding down to the lowest position. Aside from the material that covers the chair, which still looks like new, this is a cheap made chair that is definitely not worse the money I invested in it. I have had chairs between $50.00 and $120.00 before that gave me less grief than this one.

I would not recommend buying this chair. I am certain that one can find a better quality product in this price range.

product_title: Gamo 611009654 Whisper Fusion .177 Caliber 1300 FPS Air Rifle
review_headline: Good rifle, accurate and repeatable, scope is junk
review_body:
This is a very good rifle for plinking or small varmint control. Its performance varies greatly depending on the size and material of the pellets used. It is nowhere near silent, but with a heavier, lead pellet, is very quiet. With a lighter pellet, the pellet will be pushed supersonic, with a loud crack as a result - and no suppressor in the world will stop that.

The fiber optic sights are extremely bright and work well. The scope that comes with it is junk, with limited range of eye relief that gets quite narrow at higher magnification. The scope is ill-suited for this rifle, as it cannot be properly adjusted to suit the rifle: At 50 yards, with the scope's elevation adjusted as far down as it will go, the rifle is still shooting about 2 1/2 inches high. There's no way to fix this, as the scope is at the limits of its adjustment. I will have to replace the scope with a different one in order to make it usable. The scope mount is also not of the highest quality, I used some low-strength Loctite on all of the fasteners (including the rail mount) in order to keep things from getting loose moving around. I suggest the first thing a new owner do is the same - remove the rail and Loctite all of the fasteners. Two of the rail fasteners were finger tight on my gun.

Also, when tightening fasteners, use a quality steel Allen wrench. I was using the included Allen wrench at first and it sheared off inside one of the scope's Allen screws. Throw it straight into the trash when you get the gun.

Grouping however is excellent, with 1/2 to 1 inch groups at 50 yards, so the actual repeatable accuracy of the rifle is quite good. Once I get a decent scope on it, I expect it to be quite usable. The rifle is comfortable to hold, although will be big for smaller users (i.e. children will not be able to properly fire this rifle).

Beware of the cocking force required - at least 40 lbs of force is required to cock the rifle, people with less upper body strength will have difficulty cocking the rifle. After putting a couple hundred pellets through it (attempting to get the scope to zero), my left arm was definitely letting me know that it was appreciative of the exercise.

product_title: Corflex Thumbster Pediatric Thumb Splint for Kids
review_body:
I ordered this for my 4 year old daughter about a month ago; She has Trigger Thumb and my husband and I were looking for an alternative to surgery. Her doctor told us that Trigger Thumb in children often goes away on its own, but after almost a year, her thumb is still bent. My daughter has been using the splint nearly every night since we got it and we are really starting to see improvement. The thumb seems to be straightening out a little bit each night. We're really hoping that it will \\"pop\\" back into place soon. However, we're still going to follow up with her doctor and consider the surgery if the splint does not work after a few months.
The splint unfortunately did not come with any instructions or recommendations, but we were still able to figure out how to put it on her hand. The material is very durable and the part that holds the thumb in place is pretty stiff, providing adequate support. She seems comfortable wearing it and leaves it on all night. It is even washable, though we haven't had to do so yet. I will post a follow up review after she has worn it longer. We're keeping our fingers crossed that this is the solution for our daughter's Trigger Thumb!

product_title: Bushnell 8MP Trophy Cam HD Wireless LED Trail Camera with Night Vision, Black
review_headline: This cam is far more than meets the eye
review_body:
Bushnell is a well-respected manufacturer of outdoor products that for over 60 years has produced binoculars, scopes, rangefinders and now trail cams. One of my favorite pairs of binoculars is from Bushnell. While I am not a hunter the idea of owning a \\"good\\" trail cam has been on my list for a while and this one seems to tick all the boxes.

* It is rugged, weather-resistant and has a wide temperature tolerance
* It has good video and still-image resolution - not the best but very acceptable
* It has ridiculously long battery life (so the manufacturer claims). I'll let you know.
* It can send you images in real-time from any reasonable location

Being a professional photographer/videographer but not a hunter my application is more nature study and location photography than to \\"bag a trophy\\".

The concept is actually very simple ... put it somewhere (many users will tie it to a tree) and it senses approaching wildlife and will send you an instant text message to tell you it has been triggered. It will then permit you to view the activity in real-time as well as record it to an SD memory card.

I have tested it in a variety of conditions and now I want two. One for portable use and one to monitor my front door against someone stealing all the stuff I buy from Amazon. It is perfect for that use being weather-resistant, not requiring external power, and sending an instant alert to my phone to let me know an uninvited guest is at my door.

I have numerous uses for another portable unit but I will detail one interesting one. I am an avid tent camper and have often camped in areas where there are bears, wolves, cougars and the most dangerous predator of all - other humans. I know my tent has been approached at night several times. Going forward I plant to point my trail cam at our tent to detect critter movement during the night and set it to send an alarm (audible or vibrate text) to my cell phone next to me in the tent. In a flash I can see what's out there and take whatever action is necessary.

The only downside to this product is that what makes it special is also its weakness. It is designed to be used in the wilderness and that is where you are most likely to have weak or no cell service. It appears Bushnell choose AT&T because they may have more coverage in the U.S. than their rivals. I don't know if that is a fact but the map Bushnell provides does reinforce that many wilderness areas should have an AT&T signal.

One other thing to be aware of is that when used for its intended purpose the lens is going to get dusty, muddy and rain-spotted. That's not a fault of this specific unit, it's just reality. While it sounds great to be able to leave this camera in some remote location for months at a time, the cold hard facts is that over time the quality of the image will be affected by stuff on the lens. The lens does have a small \\"eyebrow\\" above it to help shield it a little from drizzle and some sunlight. No points lost for Bushnell here because this will happen with all cameras.

I don't think the cam itself is overpriced, but I am not fully satisfied with their plan choices. $120 per year seems a bit steep for the basic plan (there are two cheaper plans but they are only for basic camera maintenance not for sending images). There are also pay-as-you-go plans that seem REALLY expensive.

Note that there is a bear cage available for this camera Bushnell Bear Safe Security Case for Trophy Cam Trail Cameras a wise investment if you plan to leave the camera in the wilderness for an extended period. It is also ideal if you plan to mount the camera as a security monitor at home, you can put it in plain view right at the front door but secure it from theft.
