product_title: Bushnell 8MP Trophy Cam HD LED Trail Camera with Night Vision, Black
review_headline: Great In Bright Light, Not So Great In Low Light
review_body:
I've been testing the Bushnell 8MP Trophy Cam Trail Camera for about the week now. I have it set up above my front door to detect any solicitors that come by (we have quite a few in our neighborhood.)

The camera works during the well it daylight hours. The image quality is pretty clear and faces are recognizable, even up to about 25 -30 feet away. The sensitivity of the trigger seems fine too, the camera is triggered from the end of my driveway which is approximately 65 feet away. In low light situations, I was very disappointed though which is why I only rated it at 3 stars. Once the sun gets low on the horizon, the image quality quickly degrades. Images are in black and white and pretty grainy and pixelated. In the night vision captures, faces were hard to recognize.

The build quality on the Trophy cam is good. It's unit feels very sturdy and seems like it could withstand being outdoors for a long period of time. My unit is mounted where it's open to the weather so I'll udpate this review if there are any issues over time.

product_title: NFL New Orleans Saints Wall Border
review_body: I bought this boarder to install in my son's room after painting it with New Orleans Saints black and gold colors.  I used it as the chair rail border between the two colors.  I was a little leery about peel-and-stick wallpaper, as I had never used it before.  The border installed easily on the new paint and I was able to peel it back off to align it just right before pressing it firmly into place.  This was much quicker, cleaner, and easier to install than regular pre-pasted borders which needs to soak in water before applying.  My son's walls are finished with a hock and trowel plaster, so the walls are not smooth by any means.  I was also concerned that the border may bubble or start peeling off the walls since they aren't completely flat.  A month after installation, the border looks great and the edges are still firmly seated in place.  I first thought the cost was a little pricey.  But after seeing the durable, thick vinyl border, and the ease of installation, I felt it was money well spent.  I would highly recommend this, or any peel-and-stick border, to anyone wanting a better way to hang a paper chair rail.

product_title: Spyderco Dragonfly 2 Plain Edge Folding Knife
review_body:
I'm a convert to smaller pocket knives and the Dragonfly hit my radar recently. For a small knife, the DF manages to fit my large hand well. The models with the unlined FRN handle are very light in weight and just disappear in you pocket. But the G10 model is a step up. I like how it adds a more substantial feel to the little knife. I like the grainy texture of G10 and I like the steel liner. Is it worth the extra cost over the model with the FRN handle? The customer has to decide for himself. In my opinion, it is for me.

Is there anything to dislike about the knife? For my use, the pocket clip is extraneous. I removed the clip and I just carry the knife deep in my pocket where it feels nice and secure but no more intrusive than the lighter FRN model. It's also a little too small for my aging fingers to always manipulate one-hand opening. No matter, I'm not about to whip it out and flick the blade open to impress anyone or fend off an attack of raging pit bulls or invading hoards of Russian troops. This is a small utility pocket knife and I use it accordingly.

The only fly in the ointment for the individual Dragonfly G10 I received was the edge grind was not symmetrical or smooth and it simply wasn't as sharp as the usual Spyderco. This is not a major issue for me because I know how to reprofile and sharpen knives and I don't mind doing it. I simply used the Spyderco Sharpmaker (you really should own this simple device to sharpen all your knives) and went through the whole assembly of stones, from the diamond through the ultrafine and finished with a leather strop and polishing compound. The result is a better edge than you usually get out of the box from any manufacturer. Love the Sharpmaker and I also love the VG-10 steel Spyderco uses in this knife.

Other than the poor edge profile, this was an outstanding knife. I can't give it 5 stars but I do recommend it.

product_title: Barnett 78210 Razr CRT Pkg Quiver
review_headline: Not as awesome as it looks by a long shot.
review_body:
This is the case of a golden turd.

Pro's
1. Looks Awesome
2. The armpit guide does help to get a solid cheek weld
3. Fast
Con's
1. The fit and finish is horrible.
2. The knife compartment is impossible to open without a knife or other tool.
3. DANGEROUS... Everytime you cock/load this crossbow the safety is supposed to be engaged. However due to the horribly poor design of where the safety is, during the process of removing the rope cocking hooks from the string, the hooks move the safety to fire. (i would consider this an absolutely massive product design failure.
4. The plastic bolt hold down device broke in less than 20 shots.

If this were a $300 i would be a little upset with the massive design flaws. However this is a $1400 product and should be top notch. It is far - far from it. Now I own a $1400 dollar horribly made cross bow. This is not my first cross bow by any means and I am very familiar with them. Do yourself a favor and look at another brand of bows. Ten Point or Excalibur make substantially better products and I regret not getting one of theirs. I will list this item on craigslist and try to recover some of my investment.....

product_title: Amphipod Micropack Satellite
review_headline: Good for everything except for running
review_body:
Bought this for a hospital worker who wanted a way to carry her keys and phone at work because her scrubs pants don't have any pockets. She likes having a zippered pocket as well as the unzippered main compartment, and was impressed with how strong the metal clip is.

So I imagine that this would be good for a day at the beach or pool, and for backpacking/travelling as well, esp. to guard against pickpockets.

However, I borrowed it and tried wearing it to carry keys and gels for a run, and found it much too heavy and bouncy...a running belt pocket is still superior (Amphipod makes 2 that I already own and am quite pleased with) as is a handheld water bottle that has a zippered pouch (Amphipod also makes these which I use).

Amphipod also makes a smaller version called a Micropack Landsport that I own, which being smaller does bounce less, but being half the size limits its capacity and usefulness.

If I sound like an Amphipod groupie that's because I am, lol. Would be nice if they could pay me for it! :)

product_title: Benchmade - Rift 950 Knife, Reverse Tanto
review_headline: What does " Reverse Tanto " mean, and/or do????
review_body:
I've got a number of Osborne-influenced " reverse Tanto " knives. All BenchMades. 940's, 950's, 810's, etc and etc. my first Tanto-blades knife was a Cold Steel Shinobu folder in April of 1987. I am not being arrogant, facetious , etc etc, but I do have a valid question, I think. I know what a non-reverse Tanto is. The knives that I mentioned-940, etc, with " reverse Tanto blades ", can you tell me, what does the " reverse Tanto " do exactly? It doesn't cut. It may add strength to the point, I don't know. I use the upswept part of my
Non- reverse tantos all the time. Does the reverse Tanto name imply a cutting edge ? What IS a REVERSE TANTO??? I don't know. If you will hold a 950 or 810 in profile with a BenchMade 420, a 710, a 730/735, etc, you can see that the CUTTING EDGE of the 950/810 is the exact same as the CUTTING EDGE of the knives that I mentioned. I can not see that the " Reverse Tanto " feature is Anything but an advertising ploy-it does Nothing !
If I am wrong, please correct me. I have no problem admitting any mistake. If there is some hidden useful feature in all these
"reverse Tanto " knives, I want to know so that I can use it also! I just do not see it or understand it.
Thank you,
John K. Benfield, III

I'm built like a bear and on the larger end of a 2X and often a 3X, depending on the brand. So I bought these in a 3X black and the fit is perfect for my needs. Comfortably snug. I'm not looking for anything excessively tight. And that's what I want for gym use. Though I think they would fit me even if I were a size larger (or smaller). They seem close to true to size as far as my body goes so I'm glad I didn't order any larger. The material is not super thick. Not going to hold in every bulge by any means, lol. But it's not super cheap thin either. Still better than my regular shorts and will stop me from getting cherry burns during repetitive cardio, which is my goal.

After not finding anything in close by department stores, I bought 3 different brands of spandex type shorts this week off Amazon and these are the only ones I will actually wear. The others came much too small. It's been hard finding these kinds of shorts that are true to size, or somewhat close. It's nice to find "plus size" that are ACTUALLY plus size.

2/9/15 Update: I've been wearing these weekly to the gym since last summer and they've been washed a million times and still like new. However, I NEVER put them in the dryer. I hang dry and they stay like new. Love these so much I ordered 7 more pair after using them a few months, including in the two other colors in blue. All fit perfect. I hate it when a good fitting piece of clothing that was hard to find suddenly isn't available, so I stocked up! :) I am extremely pleased with this purchase!

product_title: Titan Power Rack Squat Deadlift HD Lift Cage Bench Racks stand cross fit pull up
review_body:
The good,
Easy to assemble.
Sturdy(see bad).
Comes with safety pins and j hooks.
Has built in pull-up bar.

The bad
Has slight left to right movement(sway).
Pull up bar has odd knurling some may find uncomfortable.
Is not as heavy as expected(but in all fairness is very sturdy when fully assembled.)
The safety pin on one side is difficult to insert and remove due to some twisting/misalignment on one if the pillars.

The fixes
Re-torquing the bolts after a day or two of use takes a lot of the sway out, a permanent fix I plan to add is a k member on the non pull-up side.

Pull up bar could easily be wraped with some webbing, but in all honestly it dosnt bother me.

Do yourself a favor and bolt the rack down. My method was to put the rack on a3/4 4x8 sheet of ply and drill 4 holes and screw it down.

Lastly the pillar that seems to be twisted....I found the pillar that seemed to be the most twisted, loosened the inner bottom bolt and slightly loosed the outer, then I inserted the safety pin(into the twisted pillar only) and pulled the pillar square, held it in place and retightened the bolts. Safety now slides in fine.

This is a well made piece by Denix, a company from Spain. The design on the barrel and butt are rather ornate and it looks great on a wall or hanging from a belt in a pirate costume. The gun will not fire and cannot be made to do so. If you pull the dog head back you can pull the trigger for a successful "dry fire," if this is done rapidly and constantly the gun may break - just a warning.
I think it is a beautiful piece. Any collector should be happy with it for a conversation starter.

review_headline: Great scope for not alot of money.
review_body: This is a large, full-sized scope that appears well made and is also airgun rated for Spring and Gas Piston guns.  The adjustable objective allows focusing from 10 yds to infinity.  At 10 yards both the target and reticule (mil-dot) are in sharp focus.  Comes with plastic lens covers, one clear the other yellow.  The sharpness isn't great with the see-through covers, and I take them off when it comes to fine focus shooting.  It's a 3-12 zoom and the focus and point of aim is consistent throughout the zoom from 10yd out.  The mil-dot is easy to use for hold overs and shooting from different distances once you've learned through experience how many clicks/dots to hold for a particular range.  The scope is not illuminated, but I find the clear sight picture and the nice mil-dot reticule to be all I need.  The elevation and windage are both adjustable without tools and have held zero so far.  It also have an ocular adjustment to set the scope for your vision.  Works well for me.

The Gaiam Grippy Yoga Mat solves all of the issues I have with sticking to the regular mat, and I no longer have to wear socks and keep a standby towel for backbending postures because if you're like me, you're not wearing a shirt because its super annoying in downward dog at the very least. It stayed directly over the regular yoga mat and made today's practice perfect.

I know this is marketed as "for hot yoga", but I will only be using this for Ashtanga so my mileage will vary from anyone who is doing Hot Yoga. I expect the backing to have issues after I wash it hundreds of times, but I also am used to fair wear and tear on items such as brakes and clutch disc material so you won't find me too upset when the time comes to buy another.

Solid product, thank you Gaiam.

product_title: Condor Recon Chest Rig (Tan)
review_body:
Excellent product for the money. I was looking for a practical, lightweight, basic chest rig to simply amplify how much ammo I could carry to support an AR15/sidearm system. Looking at the pictures, I was worried about the strength of the clips, but I've now proven that they hold up under normal to extended abuse. There's extra room on the left and right sides of the rig to attach whatever MOLLE items you want and the straps are adjustable for quite a large range of users from the extra thin to the extra large operator. I've always found the kangaroo bungee retention straps to be extremely useful and easy to extract magazines, although the kangaroo system does potentially cause issues when trying to insert empties back into the pouches, but that's what a dump pouch is for. AR15 magazines fit extremely well, metal-bodied or larger PMAG-style, and even though I haven't tried AK mags I'm sure they'd probably work just as well.

The inner part of the rig is lined with a mesh retainer for documents, extra mags, tactical bacon, or whatever else you want to cram in there. Pistol mag pouches each hold two single-stack 1911 mags or one double-stack mag pretty nicely and feature adjustable flaps so you can adjust for whatever length the magazines are.

Definitely recommended for the guy looking to attend a basic carbine course, the prepared citizen who wants to amp up his capabilities in possible times of duress, or something to stow away as a vehicle rig.

The only functional downside is the mag pouches are sewn in and non-movable so if you like where they are, great, if not you don't have options. Another issue is when in the prone, you will be lifted off the ground, especially if you load up the pistol mags all around the rig, but all double-stack chest rigs suffer from this.

Lastly, the quality of material seems to be able to hold up to casual to decent use, but extended use in austere conditions (deployment in a forward area) would not be recommended, I don't think it would survive something like that. I'm sure it's good enough for just about any civilian or LEO.

Bottom line: for the money, this does what other rigs can't do. Lots of gear competes for your system's dollars, but this is definitely a value-based solution to attain some serious capability.

review_body:

I did notice, however, that the padding wasn't sewed down around the very edge (like the Canari brand was) so that may be why the other reveiwer had some rubbing issues when wet. I also liked the matte on black Celtic-like design on the side. It kind of gave it more character, in my opinion. I rated it only 4 stars because I don't care for the design of the two front seams that remind me of bathing suit lines, but I suppose I shouldn't be surprised though as TYR is a major player in the swimming industry. I did like the fact that it had a small pocket on the back waist band for holding my phone (2.5\\" x 4.75\\") or some keys during training. A perk that the Canari shorts didn't have.

UPDATE: I have worn them during swim laps (600 meters) and they stayed put! So far, so good...

product_title: Cold Steel Pocket Bushman with Stainless Handle
review_body:
This knife is about as close to a fixed blade as you can get with a folding design in terms of sturdiness. It is also about as big as you'd probably want to go with a folder. The blade and construction is of the CS quality you would expect. The all metal construction makes it a fairly heavy knife for a folder. Everyone either hates or loves this release system Yes, you do need both hands to open and close this knife.
Which means that if you need to open and close it frequently you won't be happy. If you want a knife for quick draw for self defense/tactical purposes, get a fixed blade. But if it's a substitute fixed blade to keep in your backpack or waist pouch, it's fine. Some users say that the operation is dangerous as your grip on the handle may "slip", which is possible under certain conditions, but I don't feel any risk. But then I don't normally operate a knife this size with my hands or grip completely wet or otherwise covered in a slippery substance. I suppose if I dressed a deer with it, that would qualify, but I'd sure be washing that knife off before putting it away. Any knife.

product_title: Galco KT652B Kingtuk Inside the Waistband Gun Holster for S&W M&P Shield 9/40, Right, Black
review_body:
This holster works great for the 9mm Shield. It has solid retention; normal activity including running poses no danger of accidental loss. I wear this comfortably for twelve hours at a stretch. It felt fine when it was new, but now that it's conformed to where I keep it (4 o'clock), it's better still.

Yes, you can tuck any shirt over this holster. Dress shirt, t-shirt, whatever. It's nice to be able to do it when the wind comes or you need to tuck for any other reason. It's also easy to put on and remove this holster after you're already dressed. I find I have to undo my belt but that's it. Once you pick the right spot for it, just index the forward clip to the same place each time and it's quick to put on. I find it easier to put on without the pistol in the holster.

Once in a while I get a little sensitivity because I feel the stitching on the back pressing into my skin. But I've tried other brands, and other issues (clumsy retention clips, too much leather, etc.) make this the most comfortable I've had. I considered gluing some moleskin to the back, but the stitching is less than 3 mm from the edge of the holster; I doubt I could glue it precisely enough to be worth doing.

The small size of the holster does mean that the gun butt is in contact with your skin. If you are in a really hot climate and want leather to prevent your sweat from getting on your gun, this might not be right for you.

I use this to keep my carry piece well hidden, while still accessible. Therefore I've adjusted it to sink as deep as possible. Another reviewer noted that single-handed rehostering is difficult and I agree (it's not impossible but I prefer to use my weak hand to make sure garments don't get into the trigger). But I'm much more likely to need to draw quickly than reholster quickly. I use this for IDPA competition and don't feel the holster is holding me back. Well, I'm sure a more purpose-built holster would be faster, but I really amtrying to build skills applicable to daily carry.

A good feature of the Galco is that the retention hooks are each secured with two fasteners. This leads to less shifting than I've found with other holsters, including the Crossbreed MiniTuck and the Comp-Tac Minotaur MTAC. And like the Crossbreed, the retention clips are low-profile, unlike the MTAC (the MTAC is not worse, it's just more adjustable, but that leads to greater bulk better suited to competition than all-day wear). So this Galco holster is great for subtle concealment.

The curve behind the gun butt is really only there to help you reholster and keep the barrel opening easy to find, and as noted above, does not keep your pistol's grip away from your skin. If you have grip tape or something on your Shield you may find too much grabbing or abrasion on your skin. In fact I have this same holster but built for a Glock, and my gen 4's aggressive checking really makes the Galco uncomfortable without an undershirt. Not a problem with the holster, just something to know.

Due to the carry-friendly texture of the Shield, this is NOT an issue with the Shield/Galco combination, thus the five stars. I would recommend this to anyone who needs a comfortable IWB for a S&W M&P Shield 9.

product_title: Kenwood KDC-252U In-Dash USB/CD Receiver
review_headline: Works exactly as advertised - Very pleased!
review_body:
Works well, functionally sound, sleek and attractive.

The USB port works perfectly for connecting to my iPhone 4S with iOS 7. On iOS 6, you had to go to Pandora mode to control the music from the iPhone. With iOS 7, I was pleasantly surprised to be able to control music via the iPhone music app while in iPod mode on the receiver.

I use this unit every single drive I make, long or short. It is the best purchase I have ever made. That being said, I have a few negative/neutral comments:

It lacks a Bluetooth connection for playing music, which is fine, it's just the difference between having a cord or no cord.
I have (RARELY) experienced these 3 bugs:
1. It seems to take forever to load the connected USB device, but this is fixed by either unplugging and plugging the USB back in, or by turning both units off and on again. I suspect the main problem to be in my iPhone.
2. if you fast forward a song in iPod mode, releasing the fast forward button fails to stop the fast forwarding. Fix this by unplugging and plugging the USB device back in again, and it usually goes back to where you started fast forwarding.
3. The displayed song title is incorrect.
These happen RARELY, and I use this receiver A LOT.

BOTTOM LINE:
The product works exactly as advertised. If you want more features, pay for them.

review_body:
I had looked at these in the blister packs while shopping. I thought they were like the NC Star Precision Grade Bipod that I also purchased on Amazon. They are not !
While only time will tell how durable they are not Quick or easy to adjust and though they appear to employ carbon fiber they are strictly old school and I mean really old low tech.
The legs are locking slip joint which means if you unscrew them they will fall off.
The side to side boom is a screw and nylon lock nut with a slide joint and need tools to make adjustments.
The action only makes it difficult to pull the pods into position. It try's to twist and usually succeeds when you pull down.
I don't know about you but while I might have a Leatherman with me in the field A wrench is probably a stretch.
I am sure to fix all this with some JB Weld but I wish I had checked my order history and just ordered the NC Star.
My only saving grace is I got this for a Smith & Wesson M&P 15-22 so it wont make much difference I hope but Id not trust this with a heavier caliber or firearm.

product_title: Harbinger Big Grip No-Slip Nylon Lifting Straps with DuraGrip (Pair)
review_headline: Attention Negative Reviewers: Not Made To Add Texture To Bar
review_body:
Sorry, I don't understand the bad reviews. "I lift 24/7, these suck--they don't help grip, they're too slippery!" Okay, first, these aren't made to add grip to a bar. The bar is usually knurled, or textured in the spots you would put your hands on for various lifts. How could a textile strap offer more grip than chalk + deep textured metal? The purpose of the strap is to lock the bar into your hand via leverage with your wrist. Once you wrap the strap, you can easily tighten it by twisting the strap around the bar with grip pressure. This strap will simply help you lift heavier weight by not relying on your handgrip to hold weight up. It won't make the bar any more "grippy" because that's not what its designed for. If you give bad reviews, understand the purpose of the product first. You would not review a boat by saying it drives on the interstate terribly--so apply that rhetoric to all items you review.

In summary: Have used these straps for about 10 years. I go back and forth between lifting raw and assisted, but for olympic lifts these will help you hold up more weight. It locks the weight into your arms by leveraging your wrists into the bar. It will not improve any sort of texture on the bar for gripping, because it's not made of sandpaper. These are durable, and IMO get better with some breaking in. They are more than long enough to tighten around a bar, but you can also overlap your wrapping for heavier dumbbells for shrugs, rows, or whatever you need them for. You don't need any assistance to get them wrapped and locked in, assuming you have everyday wrist dexterity.

product_title: TOUGH-GRID 750lb Paracord / Parachute Cord - Genuine Mil Spec Type IV 750lb Paracord Used by the US Military (MIl-C-5040-H) - 100% Nylon - Made In The USA.
review_headline: Worth the money...every cent of it!
review_body:
My kids and I do knots a lot and we already got the cheap ones from local shops to practice with. We made robe hammock using those cheap ones but never feel safe. We were debating whether to go with middle of grade Type III 550lb or the ultimate TOUGH-GRID 750lb Type lV Paracord. The price difference between type III and IV wasn’t that much so it was a no brainer for us to go with Tough-Grid. We ordered the 1000’ spool and it shipped super fast. Customer service was also top notch and very personal. Bill took good care of us (you will know how he is). The Tough-Grid cord is very easy to work with knots because it is just slightly bigger than the Type III 550lb. They are super strong. If you do cut it, “burn” the ends immediately because the outer sheath will fray much faster than the Type III sheath (7 strands) since there are 11 strands tightly packed inside the Type IV Tough-Grid outer sheath. Here are 2 tips on how to “burn” the ends, pick one:

1. Cut the cord a couple of inches longer than you need it to be. Holding the cord horizontaly move it (with a little tension) over a flame at the point you wish to cut it. The outer sheath (mantle) melts and narrows down to about 2/3 diameter. Let it cool and cut it at that point. Don't burn the cord. Only melt it. Then the mantle will hold the core (kern) in place.

2. use a wet paper towel. Get the end of the cord burning, wrap the paper towel around it and run it down to and off the burnt end. It tapers the end so can be easily threaded through something.

product_title: Arthritis Hand Exerciser Adjustable Resistance Gripper Exercises for Seniors, Weak and Hand Therapy Patients
review_body:
On a scale of 1 to 10 I give the Archer hand grip exerciser a 10. I really like it! This hand exerciser not only offers a good forearm workout I can exercise my fingers and hands as well. There are several hand exercisers listed on Amazon that look similar to the Archer hand gripper. The difference between the others and this one is the maximum resistance level of the springs. The other hand grips have double the resistance (around 88 lbs.).

I tried one of the heavier resistance hand grips and when adjusted to the heaviest tension it was pretty tough to squeeze. It would be on only rare occasions that I would use it set at the most difficult level to workout my forearms. When set on the lowest tension level the finger exercises were too difficult to do at all.

I am not a golfer or baseball player myself but I think the Archer hand gripper will help golfers and baseball players get a stronger grip and improve their swing. The only drawback I can see with the Archer hand exerciser, if you want to call it that, is if you want a hand grip with a super heavy resistance level (I consider the Archer hand grip to be at a moderate level) or, if you only want to build huge forearms, you may want to go with a heavy forearm builder instead.

The Archer hand tool shows several finger exercises you can do with it. I think using any of the heavier hand exercisers to do them would be tough, or impossible, for most people. In my opinion, the main feature that sets the Archer Hand Exerciser apart from the other hand exercise tools is that people can do various finger exercises with the Archer hand grip and then increase the tension to get a good forearm workout as well.

product_title: Cascade Creek Yakgrips
review_headline: Comfortable Grip but does slide a little
review_body:
These grips performed well in terms of reducing blisters on my hands. I went out one day with just one pad to see if there was a difference and there definitely was. Made for much more comfortable grips. I have a Caviness CavPro KPC which it fit nicely on. Even with my ergonomic grips, these made the paddle more comfortable. You WILL need to have a 2-piece paddle (comes apart in the middle) to install this variant. Although they sell the one with Velcro that comes apart in the middle (which I actually ordered but received this) that may work, you can't be sure that they will send that one unfortunately (maybe discontinued?).

HOWEVER, the grips did slide a little bit when wet, which is inevitable. And frankly it's impossible to say how much they will on your paddle because paddles vary greatly in material and shape. My paddle has a different material for the grips with a feel similar to graphite which these grips did hold on to well enough that it didn't bother me much. But with an aluminum paddle, or plastic, it may slip more. Can't really say. It IS rubberized on the inside of the grip so it's not neoprene all the way through, but when the rubber gets wet it's a little less grippy.

Overall I was satisfied with the product, it did what I'd hoped and it's not to expensive so if it doesn't stay in place on your paddle like you'd hoped, you can use tape/zip ties to tighten it or just let it go.

product_title: Saucony Women's Bullet Tight Shorts
review_body:
Before I get to a review of the shorts I need to share a bit about my figure because body shape might impact how these fit. Even though I am in my late 40's. I am pretty fit. I run 3-4 miles three times a week and do interval weight training twice a week. My body is not perfect and pretty much hasn't been since I had kids and my stomach decided no amount of planks could persuade it to be flat again. My thighs touch but no one would consider me fat or even pudgy.

When I first put these one I was impressed with the fit and look. They truly complimented my figure and are comfortable. I had no discernible camel toe and they were not at all sheer. I've tried on other shorts like this that allow my glowing white bottom to be visible through the fabric but these provided full coverage with no visibility of my bottom or even my panty lines. I double checked these concerns with my husband. They have a back zipper key pocket at the waist, which is nicely lined. They also have a pocket on each leg, although I can't imagine what I would want to put anything bulky in there.

My issue with them began as I wore them around the house. The legs began creeping up and one even kept rolling up just from normal walking and moving. I think they need to be 1-2 inches longer to prevent this. Since they wouldn't stay down in normal movement I figured there was no chance of them staying down on a run or while lifting weights (but keep reading). There is a continuous draw string cord but I found it to be useless.

After wearing them and getting ready to toss them in the wash I noticed that their care label suggest line drying them after a machine wash. Well I am not a big fan of line drying simply because I must do 10 loads of laundry a week and would prefer not to have to remember to pull an item out. For the purpose of this review I made the effort. They washed nicely, held their shape and color with no fading, shrinking, or loss of quality. I hung them to dry.

I decided to try them again after they finished drying and my experience with them changed completely. The legs stayed down while walking around the house. I went outside to lift weights on my lanai. The legs stayed down while I lifted, did squats, jumped rope, did steps, and crunches. Thinking maybe my initial opinion was too hasty, I decided to go for a run to further test them. I jogged, walked and did wind-sprints and the legs stayed down! I don't know if it was just washing them that solved the leg problem or if my sweat helped keep them in place (because here in the Southeast I assure you I need gills to work out) but the problem seems to be solved. As long as I am actually at least perspiring they stay in place nicely. If I completely cool down I still experience a bit of ride up (1/2 inch) but not the same roll-up I had before washing.

Overall, these shorts look great on. Their quality is fantastic. For my thigh shape I would be happier if they were 1-2 inches longer in the leg.hung them to dry.

product_title: Blackhawk Enhanced Tactical Rappel Rope Bag, Large (200Feet)
review_headline: Great rappel bag. Very versatile. experts only.
review_body:
The Blackhawk Enhanced Tactical rope bag is a excellent product with many capabilities. This bag is designed for experienced professionals. Rappelling with the rope already hanging is much different than rappelling with the rope in the bag. Normally when rappelling the rope is fully deployed the weight of the rope is hanging on the rappelling device creating friction even before you grab hold of the rope. I on one occasion was rappelling down the side of a 200 foot grain elevator with all the equipment I needed for the job the rope was hanging all the way to the ground. When I went over the side me and my equipment weighed about 450lbs. I actually had to reach down and pick up rope just to move down the line. At 75 feet I had to start holding tension and lock off the rope to work. The closer I got to the ground the more important it became to properly lock off the rope.
With the Blackhawk bag strapped on my harness and leg things get serious quickly if you are not properly trained with experience it could get dangerous quickly. With the rope in the bag and strapped to my harness and leg there is no hanging rope to cause friction. This is a tactical bag and requires skills above average to be safe. This is a tool that allows you to rappel at high speed in multiple positions. This bag is not for beginners, the faster you go the quicker things can go wrong. Also if you make a fast rappel to the ground you must quickly get your rope out of the rappel device or it will burn your rope. I would recommend this bag for police or fire use unless you're extremely proficient with rope management, and proper rigging . This is a great bag that works well if properly used.

It is dull and lacks luster.  It looks nothing like the picture.  Finally, it has an odd varnish applied to the handle than smells bad.  I have Marble's knives from when quality meant something.  This is NOT one of those knives.  I paid roughly $20 and it was far too much.  The final insult not shown in the picture is the big "CHINA" stamped on the other side.  These used to be made in Gladstone Michigan.  Not anymore.  Think about it - in order to get this to market for $20, it probably couldn't have cost more than a few dollars to manufacture.  A sad joke played on an America where quality and made in USA meant something.

product_title: Polar Loop Activity Tracker
review_body:
I had the Weight Watchers Activity tracker for 2 years prior to purchasing the Polar Loop. The ActiveLink tracker worked flawlessly. I can't say the same for this product. The bluetooth sync fails at least 1-2 times a month. In most of these cases, if I leave the product alone, it will correct itself within a day. I've had to re-install the phone software at least 4 times after the software fails to recognize the phone. The battery life is half of what is advertised. I have to recharge the device every 3-4 days.

I did purchase the heart rate monitor (the main reason I selected this product over the competition) as an add-on. When the connection with the phone works, the ability to have a monitor for indoor training is great. The inconsistent connection has made this less effective than planned however. I'll be looking for other compatible devices to pair with the monitor in the future.

Support for the product is horrible. I have written many times to the support line. I receive a canned response a month later asking me to reconnect if I continue to have the problem. Needless to say, by the time I received that response I've managed to reconfigure the product to work again. However, the company is aware of problems with the product as numerous firmware updates have been provided in the last few months. I hope the next few updates correct all the inconsistencies. For a company that excels in sports related monitors, I would expect more.

product_title: Withings Pulse O2 Activity, Sleep, and Heart Rate + SPO2 Tracker for iOS and Android
review_body:
After talking with friends it seemed like everyone had the Fitbit. but I wanted the most bang for my bucks and that was Withings Pulse 02. It was Cnets #1 pick for activity tracker and there were a bunch of side by side comparisions out there and Withings came out on top. I picked this for that reason only. I have used it for only 1 day but I really like the fact that I don't have to do anything but wear it. No real button pushing to start an activity, it just works. I also like the fact that it tracks when I am going up and down stairs. The heart rate monity and the O2 sat was not really a factor in buying this but it is neat. I did a sleep study and it tracked very well. I didn't sleep well and it's monitoring was on track. for $99 you can get the step down from this but I wanted the extra's ($30.00 worth) for $20.

Update!!! 10/31/2014

I wanted to say that there were alot of great reviews on the Withings Pulse O2. I have to say that it is neat, the interface is neat, I like the fact that I can wear it and forget. I don't have any crazy buttons to press when I want to be active. I love the fact that it has a monitor of not just your steps but also height you went. But....beware after only 4 months of wearing it I am on #2, my wife is on #2, my friend is on #2, why you ask. Well it is the fact that it can be finicky. I have had to reset the device more times that I can count because it doesn't either sync, it freezes and stops counting my steps. The fact that it is not waterproof, or even water resistant is also a big failure in the design. I have convinced about 6 people to buy it and 1 time or another someone has had a problem. The newest problem is that my friends/leaderboard will stop showing what every's steps are and you have to remove the android app and reinstall it for it to start working again. Lastly one of my friends had to send it back because it simply stopped working. I regret buying it and wish that I had bought something that was less flash in the pan and more reliant this is not. I say this all as my humble opinion

product_title: Ontario Knife OKC Rat Ii Sp-Black Folding Knife, 7Inches
review_body: Amazing Knife for the price.  I really like pocket knives and have a small collection folding knives.  I am not an expert but certainly an enthusiast.  This knife really surprised with its high quality, flawless operation, and versatility at such a low price.    I got a pink one originally for my girlfriend after she lost her blue Mini Grip. When it arrived, I put it through the paces and it performed very well.  Not one complaint.  I liked the knife so much I bought one for myself.    It came razor sharp.  The action opening and closing is super smooth, allowing easy one handed operation.  The blade is perfectly centered and has no play when opened.  The liner lock has solid lock up and easy operation.  The handle scales, while nothing exotic are tough and offer decent grip.    This knife compares favorably with other similarly sized knives such as Benchmade Mini Griptillian, Spyderco Delica, or Kershaw Leek at a fraction of the price.  The only place it falls short is in blade steel.  The AUS 8 is more of a value steel, theoretically, without the edge retention of the higher end steels in those other knives.  I have not noticed a difference in my use so far.  What I have noticed is that it returns to razor sharpness very quickly and easily when sharpened.    Overall this is a great knife at a great price.  Value wise it is very tough to beat.  In my search for the perfect pocket knife, I am pleasantly surprised such a good knife can be so affordable.  Is it as nice as my Sebenza?  Not quite, but at 1/15th the cost, it is such a better deal and I won't cry if I lose it.

review_body: I have had this device for 5 days. I would love it IF IT ACTUALLY WOULD SYNC OR STORE DATA WHICH IT FAILS TO DO MORE THAN IT SUCCEEDS. I am so frustrated. The final nail in the coffin? Customer service is only open weekdays East-coast time. In 2014? Insane. I am so very disappointed. After losing the first days data, and then waiting for the customer chat line to open the next day, I was informed there had been an outage of the software support. Um...no notifications or apologies? I researched for six months obsessively and extensively before finally settling on a Polar Loop over a Garmin Vivofit or a Basis watch. Big mistake. review_headline: Versatile and sturdy design. As previous reviews have pointed out
review_body: Versatile and sturdy design. As previous reviews have pointed out, lower body exercises are limited by weight and are somewhat more awkward. I have tried exercising one one leg/foot alone, or doing bodyweight squats or lunges to supplement. Upper body exercises have plenty of angles and movements. The main pros are the ease of setting up and the smooth action of each movement which really gives a good stretch and sense of muscle activation. The only major con I would envision aside from lower body exercises is the lack of designated weight as it is a function of your bodyweight. At this point in time I have grown accustomed to viewing exercises as a percentage of my weight, ie pullups max out at 68% on the machine, while standalone pullups are 100%. You can also have a chart handy of your weight +/- 5 lbs with the resistance converted from % to weight. I did compare user reviews here on Amazon and other sites versus similar machines and I can say confidently that I would purchase this again.

product_title: Daisy 415 Air Pistol
review_body:
Bought the Daisy 415 through Amazon, got it on day three. It's mostly plastic, therefore rather light.
Feel is good, there is good power coming out of this gun.Trigger is very smooth, loading is a learning experience ( I now load bbs in 8 seconds). Sights are fixed and here is where I have some problem. At 25 feet the shots were all grouping 2 to 3 inches 10 to 11 o'clock. I manage to get some accuracy by using some whiteout to place a dot in the middle of the rear sight to create a 8 sight. Place the green of the front sight almost on the white dot aliened with target got me the best result. The CO2 is also a concern. I keep getting less shots for every canister. I hope I can get additional seals. I have been looking at other Air Pistol and I have decided to stick with this for now.

Now Oct 23rd 23014. Back June 2014 I purchased this Daisy Powerline 415. I commented on my experience with this air gun, in which I stated that this gun was rather light. I just wanted to reiterate that the power of this gun is awesome. There are 2 improvements that could be done to this gun, that would easily make a overall best and that is; 1) Give this gun some weight( more metal parts). 2) add an adjustable rear sight. The price would go up but would be worth it. I have been using some left-over Lucas transmission non-slip oil to the tip of my Co2s and the seal have been working fine. Left a Co2 in the gun for 2 months (not remembering I had) took it out shooting and it was still blazing. Just bought me a Umarex Legend P.08, is has the weight and bit more accuracy but no where near the power.

product_title: Rothco Canvas M-51 Engineers Field Bag
review_headline: A Bag for the Zombie Apocalypse
review_body:
This is a fantastic bag for the nerdy commuter who needs to carry everything (really, everything). It has tons of pockets and flaps to organize and store things.

Unlike a typical messenger case, this bag is tall rather than wide. If you use mass transit and ever have to stand on a train or bus, you find that it doesn't stick out into the aisle when you wear it across your shoulder -- so it tends to carry more compactly than a wide bag.

While I usually adore fancy "girlie" bags, I am far too hard on a computer/book bag to use them every day. I have had this bag for nearly two years and have not managed to damage it. It has been on numerous road trips, hiking trails and daily commuter travel. I have thrown it into the washing machine and hung it outside to dry. It is still as solid as the day I bought it. All the hardware is intact and working well, the velcro still holds, and there are no holes or signs that it will fall apart anytime in the next ten years.

The only caution I have - if you want to use this as a computer bag, be sure to measure the computer and make sure it is not wider than the bag is tall when closed. Mine was slightly too big, but all that meant was that I could not secure the twist closure on the front flap. But since the flap goes all the way over, this was not really a problem for me and it still held everything safely.

product_title: SE KHK6320 Outdoor Tanto Knife with Fire Starter
review_headline: Great knife, fire starter falls out of handle
review_body:
This is a great little knife. Mine came razor sharp, in contrast to other reviews out there.
The idea is perfect: a small, one piece, fixed blade with excellent grip, finger groove, tanto blade design, and tough steel.

I haven't tested the steel so can't comment beyond that though. I needed a knife to add to my set of survival gear just to have a small, sturdy cutting tool, but may use it as a handy cutting tool when the need arises. It seems sturdy enough for regular use.

The extra cordage is a great option to have in a rough spot, so another great idea. I wasn't interested in anything fancy from the sheath, just something to hold it in so it won't cut anything it's not supposed to when not in use, and easier to get to.

The one obvious issue I have is the fire starter. I tested it out just to have a little experience with it before I would really need it. Right away it fell out of the plastic grip. Mine was clearly not used, still was black and in new condition. I'd put it back in, and it'd fall out again with a little use. It gets really frustrating quickly. I could still produce sparks, but with a lot of effort, and a lot of that effort was just trying not to pull the fire starter rod out of the handle.

For the price this is a really excellent tool. I might keep a knife sharpener handy because I'd like to get a lot of use out of this little blade. I'd still recommend it, but just be warned the fire starter has that issue.

product_title: Spyderco Lion Spy G-10/Titanium Plain Edge Knife
review_body:
So someone wanted my opinion on the Spyderco LionSpy. So whether you like it or not, here it is.

First impression was "wow, this thing is big". After getting it out of the box I gently opened the blade all the way. Amazingly, the frame lock bottomed out on the blade right away. I mean it locked all the way down. I could not push it even the tiniest bit. A Very impressive feat in my opinion. I can say that none of my Benchmade's or ZT's will do that unless I flip them out. If I gently open them they will lock, but I can always push the frame a little farther. So, anyways, I'm thinking to myself, " Self.. Its going to be a stiff one to unlock". Well, it was a little. Although it was stiff, the frame lock end did not "catch" or "grind" against the blade. Obviously this part of the knife was met with a lot of attention to detail. I would give it a definite thumbs up for quality control.
Being an owner of a DPx HEST/f, I was curious about how well the Rotolock worked. It was smooth and easy to operate. Maybe a little too easy though. I can see a slim chance of that locking on its own. But what harm could that be! "Oh no my blade is locked better!". Well at least it isn't skin tearing stiff like the HEST/f is.
Now the only real complaint I saw from other owners online (part of my pre-purchase anal retention) was that the belt clip was too small. I'm not sure how that is a complaint. It works very well and being a " deep" clip and being so small, one would think that there is a tiny knife in your pocket, not a "Croc Dundee" folder. So, I love the pocket clip. The only way it would be better, is if it randomly put cash in my pocket.
So....the blade....the BLADE! Absolutely love it. The shape is great for what I mostly use it for. Not much stabbing going on in these parts of Central Michigan! Well...not with knives at least.. The curve at the end is enough to do slicing and the rest is great for chopping and hacking. (Sorry for the technical lingo jingo ;) ). The details on the blade are very sharp. Really digging the the inlay painted Spyderco on it. The blade is thick and heavy, makes you feel sure of its quality and build. Makes you want to find something and hack it apart. Now the Elmax, that is something only time will tell. It is a pain in the donkey to sharpen, but once you do, you will not have to sharpen it for a long time. The frame of this knife is matched to the quality of the rest. I'm not to concerned about how it looks, even though it does look great. It is comfortable to hold for those of us with larger hands and has nice rounded edges to prevent any discomfort.

product_title: Sub Sports Mens Short Sleeve Compression Top T-Shirt Base Layer Vest
review_headline: It's like a glove for my body
review_body:
Thoughts:

The material used in this compression shirt is thick, cool to the touch, and feels great. Quality and stitching are top notch, also. I bought this compression shirt to wear under my gi while training jiu jitsu, mostly for the sweat-wicking and body-cooling properties. I can say that, not only is it great at wicking sweat away and keeping me cool, but it also fits very snugly to the point where I forget I'm wearing it! It's like a glove for my body. I like that they offer several colors, however I went with black just to contrast with my white gi. Might get more adventurous with the colors later on as I buy more of these (yes, I already want more).

Sizing:

I'm 5'7'' @ 130lbs, pretty slim, but fit guy, and I ordered a medium based on the other reviews here saying to order a size up (I normally wear size S t-shirts). It fits nicely, although the compression is tighter is certain areas. For example, the compression on my biceps is more noticeable than the compression on my oblique/rib area. The medium is not loose on me, by any sense of the word, however I *think* that I could go with a S if I wanted some serious compression.

My advice for those wondering about what size to go with would be this
- If you want *a lot* of compression, order your normal t-shirt size.
- If you want a moderate amount of compression, order one size up from your t-shirt size.
- If you want a loose fit (I don't know why you'd want this), order two sizes up from your t-shirt size.

I would probably adjust this scale one size up on all my recommendations if you're a particularly bulky/thick person, as I'm fairly slim.

Some notes and observations:

- Others here have noticed color bleeding onto their skin or other fabric when using this for the first/second time. I did not notice this with the black color, in fact I wore it without washing the first time, and it didn't transfer any color to my whitegi. I'm guessing this might be a problem with the other colors, but I'd be willing to bet that black and white are the safer colors to get if you're worried about color bleeding
- The washing instructions say never to put your shirt in the dryer. Well, stuff happens, and mine accidentally ended up in the dryer because it was hidden in another article of clothing. Good news is that it survived the ordeal in one piece, and doesn't feel any different. I'll be careful not to risk it again, but just so you know, this shirt can handle being sent through the dryer accidentally without being damaged or shrinking terribly.
- Keep it away from velcro. Velcro really tears up the material, so keep this shirt clear. I washed this with some board shorts, and the velcro on the shorts ended up attaching to the back of the shirt, and the material started pilling a bit. Thankfully it was a rather small area.

Needless to say, I'm very happy with this shirt, although at the time I purchased it, it was $5 cheaper. Here's hoping SUB lowers their price back so I can pickup an entire wardrobe worth of these things.

*Note, this review only pertains to the SUB DUAL Short Sleeve compression shirt. I have not ordered nor tried on any of the cold weather compression shirts, long sleeve compression shirts, or graduated compression shirts.

product_title: The Friendly Swede Silicone Long Hair Swim Caps (2 Pack)
review_body:
I decided to buy a swim cap on the suggestion of my doctor. After having constant problems with my ears clogging up and getting minor infections off and on, getting water in them is a no-no. I am not a competitive swimmer so I cannot say anything about their "speed in the water" but I can say they are very comfortable, fairly easy to put on with my hair damp and the cap wet and they do a great job at keeping water out of my ears. even after swimming and splashing around for several hours my ears were no more damp than when taking a shower. They do fit tight, (and they are supposed to) but being silicone they are quite comfortable and I can only imagine they would work just as well in swimming competition as any other latex or silicone cap. After a few minutes in the water I don't even notice them anymore aside from sounds being a bit muffled.
These are a great value, basically getting two for just a bit more than some single caps are is great and the service from The Friendly Swede is great. I WILL buy these again and would recommend them to anyone who needed a cap for any reason.

product_title: game face gfm4 cqb aeg airsoft rifle - 0.240 caliber(Airsoft Gun)
review_body:
A friend of mine upgraded to this Gameface GFM4 rifle from his TF4 M4 not long ago, primarily for the metal gearbox feature. I was able to heft and fire this airsoft gun on several occasions during our games.

To briefly go over the features of this gun, the body, stock, grip, sights and accessory rails are all plastic to keep the cost of the gun low. The stock has a rubber butt at the end of it which must be removed to access the battery compartment. Included is a stock 8.4V which works fine. The gun fires at anywhere from 15-17 rounds per second alone running the stock battery.

The front sight is rather unique. It's integrated into the rails, meaning when you fold it down (pop it in) it blends in perfectly with the rails (The sight itself has picatinny slots but I wouldn't adjust running anything over it). Also on the body, we have the body pins that keep the receivers together. Can't take those out without a hex-head screw driver or a really small allen wrench.

Finally, the barrel (Inner and outer) are metal. The magazine is a plastic 300 round Hi-cap. Very solid gun with a good heft (7-8 lbs of weight I wager) and has excellent mobility in CQB (Shorter barrel, plenty of room for accessories on the RIS system).

The FPS is advertised at 400 (with .12gs I imagine) so I clock the FPS with .20gs (the most \\"desirable\\" ammo) at 330-340 FPS -- perfect for CQB and still leaves an impact so your opponents will \\"feel\\" the hits.

Oh, also it should be noted that \\"Made in Taiwan\\" is emblazoned on one side of the mag well (opposite of the Gameface logo). Finally a change from your average Chinese-made airsoft guns (nothing against them though).

Personally I'd recommend a Red Dot Sight (Keep it as close to the rear sight as possible, but keep that rear sight on the gun in case the batteries of the RDS run dry!) and also some rubber rail covers since the dry rails can be rough on the hands.

You can buy this game in sports/hobbies stores for around $120-130 new (That's the price my friend paid anyways). Ask for the CQB model with the RIS system.his game in sports/hobbies stores for around $120-130 new (That's the price my friend paid anyways). Ask for the CQB model with the RIS system.

product_title: fBIKE Direct 6 Speed Folding Bike
review_body:
I've only had this bike for less than week and I'm already loving it. Hopefully I'll have the same feeling in the long term.

It came in good condition with no damage or even a scratch. Took a short time to unpack and put it in a ridable condition. It's a snap to unfold and refold, especially once you figure out what the steps are. Strongly recommend to go to the manufacturer's website (fbikedirect) and watch the video on youtube. You can also read what the other accessories are intended for on their website.

Bike feels already tuned up, but it might need another touch up after some time. Shifting is smooth and easy. I only needed to adjust the orientation of the brake handles to my taste. Pleasantly surprised that it had a rack, which wasn't shown in the pictures on the Amazon's page.

I'm impressed with the range of the handle bar's height. I use it at the highest level for an upright ride for my back. Handles could be a little softer though. Saddle is decent but could be better. I think I'll use it for a while before upgrading eventually. I'm 6 foot tall and have relatively long legs, I have no problem with the size of the bike.

Now the performance. I was really curious about the relative performance of this bike compared to my mountain bikes (I have no road bikes). So, I selected a paved area and rode my best mountain bike and this bike for about half hour each on consecutive days. To my surprise, I averaged 12 miles per hour with both bikes using a similar effort. When I tried to go as fast as I can (without killing myself), I achieved about 18 miles per hour with fBike versus 20 miles per hour with the mountain bike. That's something I can live with for all the other advantages this bike brings.

Can't wait to take it to trips in the trunk of my car.

product_title: JEF World Of Golf Automatic Putting Cup
review_body:
I have several other putting ball return gadgets that I have bought that are a big disappointment. This one isn't too bad.

PROS:
1. Battery - So far we have putted about 500 balls on this and the battery is still ok.
2. Portability - That is where this shines. You can take it anywhere and practice. I have actually taken this to the practice green in our course so that my daughter does not have to keep walking to the hole to pickup her balls from the hole. Not to mention usually there are so many other people practicing there, so we don't have to use the holes there. We can even try different pin placements.
3. Inexpensive - For the price, it is a good deal. Of course if you want the best, prepare to pay for it.

CONS:
1. It is a little noisy when it returns the ball, but not a big deal.
2. Too light. I wish this was a little heavier so that it wouldn't move when you putt a little strong.

SUMMARY:
This ball return works for me and I will update this review again in a month or so so that I can have time to test its durability.

product_title: Casio Protrek PRW2500B-3 Altimeter Watch
review_body:
Only My 2ND Casio & MAGIC. Had to say it twice. At my age I am an analog guy, always wondered why people ever even wanted anything digital. I mean, Analog gives such a better actual \\"picture\\" of time. But then I got old, got crippled, got so I was always around my iPad for reminders, alarms etc just to remember when to take meds etc. Yeah, don't get old.

The folks who use these on a regular basis can tell you ALL about how they work, but how important it is to first take the time to SET THEM UP CORRECTLY for YOUR specific region of the world. Well I never read direction in 65 years. But I do watch YouTube videos. Trouble is, nobody has one explaining how to set this particular module up that I could find. Luckily, there were tons of videos last week that taught me how to set up my somewhat similar GShock G7900A Rescue Concept Watch. Being a former surfer who surfed all over the world, oh how I WISH I had these watches before I got crippled. But life & War happen....

I wanted an Atomic watch since they were invented. Why? No reason, I am just a gadget junkie and HAVE to have everything. Well if you are like me, THIS is your watch! It did take me over an hour to figure it out. I went to bed depressed since I was unable to do any manual set using the Colorado Atomic Clock. I got the L1 signal (the weakest but at least showing me it was seeing SOMETHING. But then after a few minutes got the dreaded ERR error message. I have bought weather stations before that just never got their signal so NEW it would never work. Had all my alarms set, tides and barometer set, moon set etc. But to be honest, the part of my gadget junkie was just seriously let down when I went to bed. Yes, I read all the reviews on watch forums as well as at Amazon about put them in a window and at midnight that magic Atomic Clock Fairy would make everything all work. Yeah right....

Or so I thought. Got up at 5 AM this morning and ran for my watch. OK, crawled to my watch. Sure enough, the trick of placing my watch face down and aiming my big honkin sensor towards Denver worked. I was honestly like a teenage kid again. Dumb as it may be, I am just beside myself that I have every single feature on this watch working within 10% of anything my GPS and weather station confirms in ALL categories. I'll be honest, unlike anyone else I read who wrote any review, I really didn't care much if ANY of it was accurate except that stupid Atomic Clock. I just wanted another toy to constantly play with. I am beyond excited it to discover that mine at least is a surprisingly useful tool as well as being a new toy.

This watch arrived direct from Amazon with a charge showing at medium battery level. I played with it for a couple hours last night and all morning inside. I then took a 1 hour cruise in 82 degree bright sunshine on my electric mobility scooter. I got home and it now reads FULL. All my alarms for medications worked, all my features worked, and I could not be happier. I was shocked to find this cheaper and DIRECT form Amazon, and not from one of their third party sellers a the next to cheapest price. I bought it for about a dollar more than that third party seller since THAT gives me the full and REAL factory 1 year warranty. Plus I used my American Express Card to pay so if it dies in TWO years, THEY will pay me in full for a new watch. Been there done that twice now with home surround theater systems whose HDMI pass through's failed on me. Saved me a couple thousand bucks now on free extended warranties.

The green tinted face on this does make it somewhat harder for my eyes to see. I regret that and knew/expected that ahead of time over the cheaper black version.with a white face. But I wanted the military green with camo band more than anything. My years in the USMC and all the fun I had getting myself crippled for life and all, well, I just didn't want all that fun to stop:-) Honestly, the way they set this watch up is wonderful! (to ME). The band is very dark and the camo very mild & understated. In other words, you don't look like some kind of deranged GI Joe wanna be out waiting for a flashback...This watch is just a very dark, muted and VERY nice looking, expensive and professional looking watch. It looks like exactly what it is. A tool, a tool that you can use in a pinch to do a lot of various things to help you. And if it didn't do a DARN thing, I would still love it since it just looks so darn cool. Maybe I just got lucky? Mine shows Made In Japan, NOT China. Don't know, don't care. If you are worried this looks too military, it does NOT. It still pulls off looking like a piece of professional equipment (again, to ME). The trade off for the muted green over the black, or other color choices, will be the fact that the face sort of washes out the colors. Yet, it also ADDS some color in doing so. In other words, it is a trade off. I still have mixed feelings on that. I somehow think it would look strange if it had the white face of the standard watch? And it is a very light, almost shaded green that you see. However I end up feeling about it, I wouldn't trade it for the world. And now, I can even play with this thing and see what the time & tides are all over that world I used to go surfing in. I don't think you can go wrong with this watch. In ANY color you choose. The last point I would make is the size of the face. One reviewer here thinks it is too small. NO IDEA WHAT HE WAS COMPARING IT TOO? Maybe a girls watch? All I can say is mine is actually BIGGER than on my Casio GShock G7900A Rescue Concept Watch. And that is significant since this watch is actually physically smaller than it! I have a smaller wrist than most so that is another huge selling point about this watch. It is thinner and has a smaller diameter than my bright red GSHOCK model. And there is something else. Pick a screen, ANY screen. I have lived 65 years somehow, yet never found any watch that shows CLOSE to as much information on EVERY screen as this watch. It is simply stunning, just how much info they managed to cram into this double screen set up they created building this computer on your wrist. Also being former Law Enforcement, I will have my eye out for the Dick Tracy Model I expect any day now:-)

product_title: Voodoo Tactical The Edge Shooter's Gloves
review_headline: Good tactical gloves, with a couple of caveats
review_body:
These gloves are fairly well constructed. Very similar, in fact, to a pair of Hatch Shorty Operators (without the kevlar component) which I had to return due to bad stitching that affected the fit.
Here's what you need to know:
1)They fit a full size too small.
For me, that worked fine as I'm actually more of an XS, so the S fit, albeit tightly. The more you put them on and wear them, the more they stretch to fit your hand.
2)Cut off the velcro elastic wrist strap - don't even hesitate - just cut it off.
This strap serves no purpose other than to act as a wrist tourniquet, and will cut off all blood supply to your hand - get rid of it.
I recommend that you take a look at a popular online auction site to get these exact gloves a fraction of the cost - that's where I copped mine.
Finally, excellent dexterity with these. Is the stitching perfect? No. Do the knuckle guards line up perfectly on each glove? No - in fact, my right glove fits perfect while the left one has the knuckle guard sort of sewn about a millimeter off so that when I make a fist, it isn't super comfortable.
But for what I paid, I could care less. Plus, you're buying a made in China product, so just make the best of it.

review_headline: I got these for dead lifts.
review_body:
First let me speak of the product itself and its constructions.

The wrist straps are made from quality material. The velcro tightly and do not give me any impression that they will ever come apart. The hook itself is covered in a quality coating that will also last for years. The metal pull through strap is a bit of a pain to get to work and I found that I couldn't easily pull it through and secure the velco. I had to slow down and take my time. However, the product seems to be very well made.

Now to what I used them for, deadlifting. I was looking for something that would help me stop losing my grip on the bar. I chose this as "taking the easy way out" thinking that I'll just put these on and not worry about it anymore. Well, after the first lifting session I realized a couple things.

1) These completely change the feel of the deadlift. I never got that "hooked in" feeling to the bar just before the lift occurred.

2) The actual hook itself doesn't close around the barbell as close as it could. It feels like I have open hands the entire lift. This makes everything feel very unusual.

All in all, I would suggest simply using chalk and increasing your grip strength if you are looking at these for the same reasons I was. I will not use these ever again because I feel like I am completely cheating myself while using them.

product_title: Only You Can Fire Your Gun Instantly In The Dark. Real Gun Safety. Lifetime Warranty. SAFTLOK
review_body:
In theory and design is should/would do as advertised. I am however getting ready to return this as fast as I can print a return lable and bet it dropped off at the carrier to be sent back.

The design of this is such that it installs under the grip panels of your 1911. You have to use the rubber panels that come with this Saftlok no others will work. The rubber panels do feel nice and soft to the grip, however they are also make for a wider grip to hold which may not be a one size fits all ordeal. To install these you have to remove your old grips as well as the screw bushing on the left side of the pistol. You then install a new lower bushing on the bottom screw hole and the top hole receives a small flat head screw designed to hold this lock system in place. You then install the rubber wrap around grip with your old screws.

To use the lock you pull your slide back and chamber a round. You then apply the manual slide safety. Then you pull pack the locking bar piece of the SAFTLOK against the lower of your slide safety and push a button to lock the bar against your slide safety which then will not allow your manual slide safety to be lowered into a firing position until the combination has been entered in to the SAFTLOK.

Now you don't really enter a combination by numbers as you would think. What you actually do is push down one of three little button levers once for each number of the combination. Such as the lock I received the combination was 812. So the front button had to be pushed 8 times. Then the second button had to be pushed 1 time, and the third button then pushed 2 times and the lock would release the bar against the manual safety allowing you to lower the safety and fire your weapon.

Now here is what I didn't care for.
Screw bushings are not a hard metal so in removing the two on my 1911 one removed with out problems. The other the screw slots stripped out and I ended up spending a good whilethen removing that last bushing.

The lock is only held in place with the lower screw and bushing on the left side of the grip. The top bushing/screw hold on the left is filled with a flat head screw keeping the lock in place by slipping through a hole in the frame of the lock. The bushing that is provided with the SAFTLOK is so long that it extends into the magazine well and will not allow for the magazine to be inserted. This could be ground down with a small grinder with extreme care, but it's not for me to do.

Considering everything in a nut shell, not to mention in an emergency trying to remember how many times to push a small button the correct number of times I will pass.

Now I need to get back on Amazon and order a set of screws and bushings so that I put my 1911 back into service.

review_body: First, I admit it is pretty. If you can get over the trigger pull (I've read some very disparate scale readings) which is heavy enough to pull one off of any stationary target, in a clamp it is easy to see the projectile leaving the barrel at any and all angles, inconsistency defined. Forget trying to hit anything moving, on purpose, I mean (you know who you are). Ah, I have the 'real deal', so why bother with a BB gun? Well, this one, at least. It is easier to practice with (city-quiet) whenever one needs to and living near population precludes the 'real deal', so make do. The 6mm stuff is much better for keeping a sharp eye and there are tons of vids and forums to keep that unit working. This Umarex P-08 is a spendy paperweight. Right out of the box it could not be loaded until enough of the grip was trimmed away at the magazine release to stop pressing it in and keep the magazine from even making it 2/3 of the way into the unit, read; sloppy. If anyone reading this has an assembly drawing or tear-down instructions, you probably work for Umarex. Just know why it is that you are buying it; if for looks and to fill a holster for reenactments, go for it, if for accuracy and keeping a sharp eye, you will be lucky to hit a tin can at all from ten feet against the trigger pull alone.

review_headline: So far I'm quite pleased with my purchase and it has all but replaced ...
review_body:
I purchased the Stealth Align a little over two weeks ago to help with the copious amounts of soft tissue work that my back needs to function. So far I'm quite pleased with my purchase and it has all but replaced my previous foam rollers. It should probably be noted that this is from the perspective of someone who competes in powerlifting.

Pros: It cracks my back every single time
The crevice allows you to increase the amount of pressure on your back by holding weights on your chest without putting pressure on your spine
The number of angles you can attack a knot with on this thing greatly exceeds a traditional foam roller, or even some of the more specialized ones

Cons: The Stealth Align is a little less firm than other black foam rollers. Coupled with its 8 inch diameter this makes it a bit harder to really dig into tight sports.
The center disks seem to be slightly larger than the outer edges so they don't touch the ground when it's resting. Although when lying on the roller it compresses enough that this is no longer the case.
The center channel seems to be a teeny bit too wide for you to be able to hit the fascia right next to your spine.

All in all I'd say that if you are someone who has any back troubles or if your already foam roll and want to take it to the next level, the Stealth Align makes for a great addition. It'd be nice if the disks in the middle were a bit more firm though.

review_headline: Not Significantly Helpful Enough to Justify Cost
review_body:
I've worn inexpensive compression gloves and had hoped these would be excellent, considering the cost. Medium was too large so I got a Small, but I still haven't found them to offer enough compression to make my hands feel any better.

However, I missed the return window and don't want to waste the purchase. So, one thing I've done to make them more effective is to pull the fingers down until they cover my second knuckle and also to roll the top down so there is double compression around the lower part of my thumb. Underneath the gloves, when I do that, I put an analgesic cream on my trouble spots. I've never had a skin reaction, but I only use a small amount of the cream.

When I really need it, I put both gloves on one hand and roll both tops down to the thumb base level, which does give good compression. Then, I switch after a few hours, when the pain is calmed down a bit in the first hand. I type that way or sleep, which should indicate that it's not too cumbersome. I have also worn them under compression gloves from the drugstore and doing that has made them more effective as well.

Most of us will try anything to help deal with hand pain, so I suppose these are worth a try for many people. But, try them and immediately send them back if they don't work, to avoid paying for yet another item that never is used.

product_title: Frankford Arsenal Platinum Series Rotary Tumbler 7L
review_headline: Forget Thumblers Tumbler..Get this Frankford Arsenal !!
review_body:
I had dabbled with alternate cleaning methods for my brass but found them ineffective (ultrasonic) or messy (Thumblers Tumbler)....Then I tried this tumbler from Frankford Arsenal and fell in love. It's still a little messy but because FA specifically designed this for cartridges it works a lot better than the 'general purpose' tumblers that most people have used before.

This model features a molded in rubber liner...compared to the loose liner in the Thumbler. It features easy-on, see-through end caps (on both ends) instead of the multi-thumb nut lid found on others. It's also molded HDPE instead of metal (so no rusting or scaling). The base station has a built in timer AND is direct drive instead of using belts (that stretch, slip, or break).

I've used this with full (30 pounds) loads twice and half loads 4 or 5 times. This design easily cuts the messiness from the other tumblers in half. The use of plastic (the good way), direct drive, and other handy features make this an EXCELLENT buy for using as a cartridge prep device. For straight wall pistol cartridges it's a 'good' upgrade but your basic vibratory tumbers work just as good...but for bottleneck pistol or rifle rounds this thing is magic! Cleans inside and out and primer pocket so well that the rounds look brand new. It will probably replace my Lyman 1200 for my rifle rounds just because of that.....like I said...for straight wall, fairly clean pistol brass it's not needed but every so often to get the deep grime/corrosion off.

The .041 pins are fine...heard stories about them sticking in holes....but have had ONE that had lodged SIDEWAYS in the neck of the round (not the primer pocket)...and that's out of @3k rounds of .223 I've run through it.

No complaints...just works and cleans the brass AMAZINGLY!!
