product_title: Galco Tuck-N-Go Inside the Pant Holster (Natural)
review_headline: A good holster for the price - NOT meant for Solo models with Crimson Trace
review_body:
Galco makes good quality products. No doubt this model would have served me well - IF - the Kimber Solo with Crimson Trace had actually fit. The Crimson Trace device on this Kimber creates a rounded protrusion on the top right side of the grip, directly above where your index finger extends (if you are holding your Solo in the right hand). Thus, any holster needs to have a matching rounded shape or cutout for the Crimson Trace to be able to seat fully into the holster.

This Galco has a strong metal wire sewn into the top edge of the holster. With great difficulty I suppose a person could make modifications.

The waist and belt clip are made of plastic. There were not sharp edges to snag on clothing and the plastic appears to be strong but flexible enough to survive extended wearing.

Since this didn't work for me with Crimson Trace, I did find a solution at ConcealmentSolutions dot com. The owner of that business does have the Kimber Solo w/Crimson Trace blue gun to do customer work with at reasonable prices.

Bottom line - A good holster for the price as long as you are aware of the limitations.

BE ADVISED - the gun pictured in the listing is NOT the Kimber Solo. I believe it is the Kimber Ultra Carry which is a larger gun which means the holster pictured is a larger model of the TUC634. Nevertheless, the design is accurate, just a different scale.

What I didn't realize was the whole workout was much more than just the strap exercises. A healthy warm-up and warm-down with stretching, cardio and anaerobic mixed in. I felt the results in two weeks. In four weeks I had more power and endurance in the water. I highly recommend the system.

review_headline: Bear Defense Spray on two occasions
review_body:
I had the chance to use this Bear Defense Spray on two occasions, one was during a promotional radio comedy show. The Bear was tame and I got $50 for Spraying it on a Bear. Didn't seem to work at all, it sneezed a few times but it didn't do a thing. If it hadn't been tame (w/ a trainer), I would have been torn to pieces.

Occasion two was when I went hiking in the mountains. I came across a brown bear near a small creek and he came at me. I froze, reacted calmly, took the Bear Defense Spray and used it. The only thing it did was startle the Bear, it retreated but eventually came at me again, but I had time enough to run back to my truck where I hid for safety.

Bear adrenaline, either from male 'heat' or anger, is enough to override the effects of a little pepper spray burst, just like a man on drugs or alcohol can still attack if hit with pepper spray.

In all, I wouldn't recommend these Bear Defense Sprays at all unless you are dealing with a Bear cub.

review_headline: Great glove for light to moderate free weight exercise
review_body: I compared this glove (Harbinger 1250 Training Grip WristWrap Glove) and the Harbinger 140 Pro WristWrap Glove before deciding to purchase this one. I have small hands, and it has been difficult to find gloves that fit correctly for lifting. I went for a glove with a wrist strap because of a wrist injury (not related to lifting). Due to this injury, I have had to maintain rather than increase the amount of weight that I lift when doing any free weight exercise. I went to a local Sport Chalet to try on the gloves, and was lucky that they had both in stock in my size (small). I preferred the Harbinger 140 Pro WristWrap Glove's fit over my hand, as well as its ease of removal. However, I found that the Pro's wrist support strap was too shallow, and did more to strangle the end of my ulna than to actually support my wrist. I had the opposite problem with the Training Grip gloves-- the wrist strap fits comfortably over and above (up the arm) the end of the ulna and supports the wrist well. I find the fingers to be too loose for my preference, but because I tend to prefer lighter weights and higher reps, I haven't actually had any problems in my workout because of it (other than a slight decrease in overall comfort). The Training Grip is difficult to removing after my workout, and I'm a little worried I might break it over time from trying to yank it off, but so far the material has not torn. I would say all in all, this is a great glove for the price. I would give it 5 stars if it fit my fingers the way the Harbinger 140 Pro WristWrap Glove does.

product_title: Spyderco PINGO Slip It Plain Edge Knife, Black
review_headline: High quality, but a bit flimsy
review_body: The build quality on this knife is very good...the FRN handles are comfortable, well-textured, and rounded around the edges.  The sheepsfoot blade has a thick spine, is nicely contored and boasts jimping on the choil.  The blade comes  razor sharp.  It even has a groove on the back that holds the blade in position when half-open.  The backspring is strong and reliable.  The pocket clip comes almost to the edge of the handle for deep / low-profile carry.  There is a lot to love about this knife.  When I received mine, there was noticeable side-to-side play in the blade.  Tightening the lone pivot screw did help, but no matter how tight, the frameless handle simply does not provide enough rigidity where the blade attaches to the FRN.  When closed, the blade easily moves from center to either side and sticks slightly off center.  Yes it weighs less without a frame, but it loses some solidity / durability.  For me this makes the knife difficult to consider for any real EDC duty.  I expect play to develop quickly and worsen over time.  The choice to only have a screw head on one side of the pivot is the second flaw.  It is compounded by a pice of plastic inside which will break if you over-tighten. Love the shape, blade and quality, but not a fan of the frameless design.  Would recommend only for very light duty.

product_title: Shoreline Marine Bilge Pump (Manual 36-Inch)
review_headline: works great, just had to figure out to screw the hose end into the outlet
review_body:
Have had this pump for a couple weeks now and have used it several times, pumping out water from a small pool, helping fill/empty small pool for ducks, and cleaning out some areas that has gotten flooded (thanks to irresponsible electricians knocking a drainage pipe off under my home allowing sink water to collect under my house, which is a WHOLE other story...)

Does a great job! Even with the not so clean water the only difference I have found is a little bit harder to pump but NOT difficult to operate in the slightest.

It did take about three days of my struggling with the hose to figure something out thought... I have seen where others have complained about the hose coming off or leaking, well, I figured out that I had the hose turned around the WRONG way. The hose has a plastic cap typething on one end and I had thought that the plastic end was meant to fit into the outlet on the pump and while it does fit in there, one pump and it either blows right off or the water being pumped out seeps out majorly from the outlet.

Turns out the other end of the hose SCREWS INTO the outlet... I wouldn't have realized this has I not turned the thing sideways while trying to figure out how I was going to glue or tape it together. Yup, it screws into the outlet and since then... NO leaks from the outlet, and NO problems with the hose blowing off...

seems like such a simple thing but I don't think I am the only one who overlooked the small threading inside the outlet....

good luck, great pump :)

product_title: Magpul Stock Set For Mossberg 500 - Black
review_body: Great set. Everything came with what it was supposed to and arrived very quickly. Would do business with the seller again! Edit:    After having it on my Mossberg for some time now I figured I should update this review a little. Firstly I must say that the weapon feels better with the Magpul Forend and Stock than with the factory parts. The factory Forend was loose and did not have a very solid feel to it, the Magpul Forend made the Mossberg feel much better when just holding it and more importantly while firing it. This Forend will also make it very easy for me to attach a flashlight. Being that this shotgun is used as a home defense weapon, I found it important.    As far as the stock goes, I had no real issues with the factory stock other than I feel it looks outdated, which is why I wanted to replace it. The Magpul stock is adjustable by using inserts (that come with this set). With another small purchase, I think it is around $20, you can have all the hardware on your Shotgun to attach a sling. The Magpul Stock is very easy to remove in comparison with the factory stock as all you have to do is remove a small clip on cover and remove a small hex screw. For those who have not taken their factory stock off yet, you will find a screw deep in the stock, when trying to remove it, it will feel like it is never ending and will take an eternity to remove. I decided to keep the length of the stock short so it is easier to use in the house (should I ever have to).    Everything feels and is well made. I have not been able to damage any of the Magpul parts accidentally. They do feel lighter  than the factory parts as well, if that is something you might be looking for. As far as recoil goes, I have not really noticed a difference, maybe if you added more inserts and extended the stock, the recoil may lessen.    Hopethis helps, if you have any questions, just ask.    Edit #2:    Just a heads up for some of you 500 owners. You will need to purchase these as well unless your stock forend was different than mine.    [...]  and    [...]    Not saying those are the best or the ones you should buy, nor are they the cheapest, they are just for reference. Hope this helps.

Incredibly ergonomic handle with jimping everywhere you'd want it to be. You can choke up on the blade quite well due to the back curve, and actually do some pretty fine work with this. I don't know why people find recurve blades hard to sharpen. With a round ceramic rod, it's simple. Do not try to sharpen a recurve blade on a flat stone. That is agony. The recurve shape is great for outdoor work and carving things up. The blade is thick and strong and, oh- S30V!. I love this steel above any. That's just personal preference though. It holds an edge like it's life depends on it. The G10 is grippy without being sand-papery as on some scales. The fit and finish on mine could be a bit better- some places the steel liner will poke out under the G10 and the tip isn't perfectly aligned in the middle of the closed handle, but the grind is perfect and functional. Looks aren't everything. The stud is not a stud- it is a blade-stop. When flipping the blade open, the pin keeps the blade just that much more solid. There is 0 blade-play. The flipper design is fun, but when engaged, the slick of the liner lock is so dang LOUD. The flip action is slow, as the blade is so heavy, but I don't need a fast-engaging blade. I removed the tension spring and the knife works just well with a small flick of the wrist. I prefer completely manual- less things that can break. The liner lock engages 100% on the blade- rock-solid. It does not stick in the slightest when disengaging it. The clip is perfect and can be placed in any of four position, tip up left and right, or tip down left and right. This knife is carriable for everyone, but lefties will have trouble closing the lock- unless you've practiced.

review_headline: Close to Perfect and getting better ...
review_body: After about 3 months with the V800, it's time for me to update my review. I'm a frequent runner but do not follow a fixed training plan. For my purposes the V800 is very good and by far the best GPS/HRM that I own. Miles ahead of the Garmin 910XT, the various Garmins I owned or older Polar models. In short here are the V800's features I am most impressed with:    - Great usability as an everyday watch, great display, long battery life, features such as alarm for weekdays only, vibration, ...  - Easily readable display while running  - Fast pickup time for satellites, though it does tell you to stand still which I usually ignore  - Mobile App is great for a quick overview or motivational boost  - Flow is getting better with every release  - Polar promised to deliver connectivity to Strava in September and so they did. This gives me a lot of confidence that they will continue developing this product.  - Integration of the activity monitor    The only downside is the incompatibility of the V800 with Ant+ infrastructure, navigation, speed and cadence on the bike. So please Polar people create some way to use the V800 with Ant+ or other industry standards. Until then, I will continue to use my Garmin Edge with speed and cadence and have my heartrate on the V800.    P.S.: my watch took on some water recently. I got a replacement from Polar in a couple of days, so let's hope it was just a fluke and it's not a general problem with the proofing.early that I couldn't get the \\"tap\\" to work. It's more a SLAP as somebody commented. So I got it working now and it is quite interesting to see my \\"recovery status\\" whenever I like with a quick slap on my wrist.

product_title: BARSKA Tactical Red Laser Sight System with Flashlight and Mount
review_headline: Mediocre quality and definitely not TACTICAL
review_body:
Just mediocre quality laser sight and flashlight. I wouldn't definitely use it as 'tactical' and putting the word 'tactical' is just ridiculous.

Just out of the box, the pressure sensitive switch for the laser worked for a couple of times and the solder points in the laser tube cap and in the switch came loose. I took it apart the cap and the switch and re-soldered the connections to make it work but I am not sure how long it will stay in tact. I haven't try to fire my rife after installing the device which is attached the scope but I am pretty certain that it will all come loose again after a first shot considering the quality of the device.

The laser point is not really sharp and it's hard to zero-in the point with a small hex wrench that came with the package. Putting batteries in the laser is also a paint point for the last battery constantly pops out of the tube when you try to put the cap back on.

The flashlight is not that bright either. It is not well focused with a few shades.

Only thing that might be worthwhile to keep is the mounting bracket.

That said, tomorrow, I will attach it on the scope on my Gamo Whisper air rifle instead. I think it will work much better on a low impact device that is not 'tactical' or shots real bullets.

product_title: Winchester Model M 14 Semi-Automatic CO2 Air Rifle
review_headline: Excellent with two annoying inexcusable flaws--Now 3 Stars
review_body: Love the gun, like the design how the co2 is separate and uses well made brass seals.  Power and accuracy great.  This is a nice quality Japanese made air rifle and anyone criticizing the use of plastic is not being realistic for $80.  Now the dumb part.  Several other reviewers commented on the co2 arrangement and while a little of a pain what was stupid was both provided hex allen wrenches broke immediately upon use cracking at the tiny lanyard holes.  They should just put metal wrenches in for a few pennies more.  I used a 10mm allen wrench and it worked good but including a metal wrench should have been a no brainer.  One more small detail that would be a nice to have is a flip up butt plate which is a feature I love about the real M14 but would raise cost a bit.  Update - less than a week later I'm removing one more star because one of the screws that pushes the co2 into the seal is plastic like the broken wrenches I mentioned above. Given these parts have to have the strength to pierce the co2s. This part is typically metal and it was a poor choice to go with plastic! I will contact Daisy for a replacement and I still LOVE how it shoots (tried BBs and they were surprisingly accurate!)  Update 2 - still going strong but annoying to have to baby (be gentle) when torquing the plastic puncture screws on the magazine when changing co2.  Hopefully they fix this Achilles Head in an otherwise cool air gun. Big Props to Daisy for sending out a replacement magazine the day after I called them, so the customer service was SOLID

product_title: Hammerli 850 AirMagnum air rifle
review_body:
I have an Air Arms S510 in 22 and a Marauder pistol/Carbine in 22
All shooting of the 850 has been at 10 meters. I shoot my S510 at 10 meters on low power.
While the 850 with a 3-9 compact scope won't shoot as tight as the 510 with the best pellets out of both guns it does a good job.
To be honest I am splitting hairs It will hold .250 groups all day. it likes the JSB exact 15.89 gr
It also does well with H&N FLD TGT Trophy 14.66 gr.
My gut tells me that it is less pellet picky than the S510 But most S510 shooting is at 25 yards and full power so it's just a feeling.
Now for the down side German Engineering my back side. The bolt has to be doubled pushed forward
(The bolt hits the magazine and stops you pull it back and push forward again and it will chamber) this happens about 50% of the time with some of the Magazines.
also Air Arms and Crossman don't have an auto safety on their repeaters nor do they suffer bolt closure issues, though they do cost more.
But for the person who doesn't want to pump up a PCP air gun and wants to keep there pest control to 25 yards or less and small pests at that. This gun is a blast. Could you kill a crow at 25 yards certainly with a head shot my S510 shoots 925 FPS with an 18 gr pellet compared to 630 for the 16gr if that (not tested yet) So body shoots could be an issue for the 850 as range increases.
For the $$$ this is a fun gun to shoot. I would buy it again and recommend it.

product_title: Solio Mono-i Hybrid Solar Charger
review_headline: Don't buy this or any Solio products for that matter
review_body:
I haven't had this for long so I can't say much about how well this thing works/doesn't but mostly because you need to buy these separate iGO power tips to be able to charge Anything... (even though it is slightly my fault, should've read the description closer) because of this I do not recommend buying this, even at the low cost of $10 or less, I personally had reasonable expectations with this, to only charge up stuff a little bit/charging itself from sunlight very slowly, fine.. but I don't agree with having to buy the tips separately at all... if only there was a universally accepted connector that will work with almost everything, such as USB...

Now I wouldn't have as much of a problem with this, if those tips (at least one or two of em) were included or only cost about $1 but no, they usually cost over $5 for EACH tip, so that will add up real fast if you want more than one tip, so basically they seem to scam you out of money by selling you a cheap somewhat functional device so that you can either toss it when you get it or go ahead and buy the tips you need as well... Please don't buy, instead just get a decent portable power bank and a good solar panel to hang in your window (or wherever) and you'll have a much better experience.

update, I've tried this out a bit and have been charging it using a 7W foldable solar panel and it works alright although the supposedly 1,000mah battery in this thing is closer to about 500-600mah, I can only charge my phone with a 2100mah battery up to about 25% or so from a full charge, so its a bit handy if you're ever running low and need a boost but don't count on it doubling your usage or anything.

I keep this in my wallet all of the time and usually also carry a small Kershaw Chive as my primary pocket knife for every day use.

Don't buy this as an every day carry knife you expect to use consistently but do buy it if you find your self needing a sharp knife every once in a while. Very well built given it's applications. review_headline: GREAT SCOPE READ BELOW IMPORTANT INFO
review_body:
INITIAL REVIEW-6/14
I have many other Vortex products and just got this a month ago right when it came out (i was on a waiting list from B&H photo) and mounted it last weekend for my hunting trip and noticed that the zoom stops working in between 5-6 power. I put a Vortex Crossfire II 3-9 x 50 next to it just to make sure I wasn't crazy and sure enough the 3-9 scope had better zoom at 9x than the hog hunters claimed 12x, there must be a problem. I will return it to Vortex for them to check it out and replace. Maybe I got a first line dud but you never know, I would wait for this product to pass more quality control lines before purchasing. This sucks because I really wanted this scope to be better than my other crossfire scope as it should have more zoom power 12x? no.
NEWEST REVIEW- 8/14
I sent my scope back in to Vortex and just got it back a few days ago. Inside the box was an invoice (no charge) but it described that \\"inspected scope missing screw on erector tube lens, replaced screw/loctite.\\" A missing screw was not visible from the exterior of the scope and I am glad that Vortex found the problem and even more so - fixed it and sent it back to me promptly. Since the initial purchase I bought a second one from amazon and did not have any issues with the second scope and the initial returned one works flawlessly now. I know that I had received one of the \\"first off the line\\" scopes and probably had not been checked for quality. I am glad that Vortex stands by the products they produce and customer service is always top notch. Thank you!

product_title: Spyderco Delica4 Lightweight FRN Flat Ground PlainEdge Knife
review_body:
Do some quick googling and find reviews everywhere. This knife is verifiably awesome. The ZDP-189 is a little expensive, which is really the only con to this product. In my particular case, the edge was chipping a bit until maybe the 3rd or 4th touch-up with the Spyderco Sharpmaker, at which point the steel seemed to hold a good edge without problems. The knife is crazy light and very well built. Tolerances are excellent, though you might have to play with blade centering (if blade centering is something that bothers you).
This is all good - until I found the Caly 3.5. My main complaint with the Delica is the fact the handle is longer than the blade by quite a bit; for the same handle length a longer blade would have been easy to implement. This is exactly what the Caly 3.5 offers: roughly the same ergonomics (distinctly different but overall not drastically so) but with a much better handle - blade ratio.
Same steel, fancier looking and noticeably more blade makes the Caly 3.5 the winner for me.

All in all the Delica is really good, and the ZDP-189 only enhances the design. For my taste I prefer the Caly 3.5, but that's just me.

review_headline: Great for runners who are nervous about running tights

product_title: Coghlan39;s Trek III First Aid Kit
review_headline: An acceptable starter kit, but needs extra equipment
review_body:
This kit is generally good as a base kit to start out with. I chose this kit as an addition to other equipment I wanted to buy (including a shovel and sheath). It is a start to a decent first aid kit but certainly is not fully prepared.

I received the kit, which was not in a plastic wrapper, but had the black fabric handles stapled to the cardboard piece they use to hang the kit on a store shelf. The kit itself is about half the size of the Adventure Medical Kits Weekender bag, in terms of dimensions. It is barely large enough to hold a standard sized pair of trauma shears diagonally.

It contained almost all the equipment listed, but was missing the safety pins (well, I couldn't find them). Everything else was accounted for. I was expecting to fill the bag with extra equipment, and, as it shows in pictures, the bag is large enough to fit a lot more stuff into (and you should indeed do this). It contains two 6 dram pill vials, which will be good to put the medication in that you need.

The bag is very thin; you can actually read the first aid guide (which is insufficient) from inside the bag. I don't mind this. Most of the pockets and flaps are made of two layers of fabric, but it does feel like it might break apart.

I added the following stuff to the bag:

-1 trauma shears $4.00
-1 CPR mask $4.54
-1 QuickClot Sport $9.00
-1 tube of bite relief ointment (from around the house)
-Some antihistamine pills I wrapped in aluminum foil
-1 Red Cross Wilderness and Remote First aid guide (you can print this from the Internet for free; the pocket guide is the only one that will fit into the kit)
-Irrigation syringe, 10cc (I went to Walgreen's and asked the manager the cheapest syringe they had with no needle; he went to the pharmacy and I ended up with one for free. I am unsure of whether they now think I'm a heroin addict or something, but I did get a free syringe out of it)
-Antacids, aspirin, ibuprofen, Imodium pills wrapped in aluminum foil that I got from our medicine cabinet at home.
-Thermometer from the dollar store.
-Cotton swabs.
-Pencil.

Note that if you don't have this stuff you're going to be coming close to the price of the Weekender bag from Adventure Medical, which has a lot more stuff and is a bit better quality. However, I was able to afford a QuickClot bag with the money I saved, and I wanted this in case of serious hemorrhaging.

I picked this kit because most of the stuff it's missing can be bought at the dollar store, and the stuff that it does have is generally hard to come by. It's not the best but it saves room in my backpack and does the job. I would give it three-and-a-half stars if I could; it's not perfect but I think it will work when seen as a skeletal kit that you add stuff to as you go along. I may update the review if I find the equipment in the bag to be of poor quality.

product_title: Poison Cue - BOLT 1
review_body:
Short version: I've never handled a cue of this quality in this price range. I gave it five stars because there isn't an option for six.

Long version: I normally shoot with a Predator 314 shaft on a Lucasi butt. That set up is about 4 times the price of the Poison Bolt1, and the Bolt keeps up with it. The layered tip shaped nicely, plays like a soft tip, but holds its shape like a mid. While the low deflection venom shaft has noticeably more deflection than a 314, it well superior to a traditional cue if you prefer LD shafts. The unilock bullet joint has a metal pin that works smoothly, and a wood to wood joint that is a softer hit than metal to metal. The butt is plain but well crafted. The biohazard logo is a bit hacky in my opinion, but it's unobtrusive. If you are looking for a no frills cue that vastly outperforms its price tag this is a good choice.

product_title: Plano Protector Single Rifle/Shotgun Case
review_headline: 5 stars for value only, not safety; although a little shallow for bolt action
review_body:
When I received the case, I liked it. It looks decent and all I wanted it was to protect an old bolt action single shot Sears J.C. Higgins shotgun my father left me. I re-blued and refinished the stock and wanted to protect it. Yes, it does what what the item description said; protect. I knew from other reviewers the foam lining flops out since it isn't attached to the case. I fixed that nuisance with dabs of glue.

It has four latches. It has 3 places to put padlocks for airline travel, Of course 3 locks for all lock tabs is inconvenient,but that would be what you would need for home safety. The reason is because the middle tab to put a padlock may keep toddlers from opening it, but it is so flimsy that it appears all one has to do is twist the lock on the ring tab to easily break it. So I would not consider this a safe case around children. Please, if you have children, DON'T CUT CORNERS on safety to save a few bucks.

My single shot shotgun does fit with only a few inches to spare lengthwise, but when I went to close it the lid hits the bolt on the shotgun. I had to use some extra pressure to close it, but it does close just enough so there is no buckling or bulging of the case. It would have been nice if it was a little deeper, but it works.

I do like the appearance. It has a hunting scene molded into the lid. Nothing elaborate, but a nice touch for an inexpensive case.

It did a decent job. It is a time saver. However the tolerances felt a little loose. There are other tools out there costing twice as much but the B.O.N.E. and Gunzilla combo worked well for me so I will stick with it.

product_title: Wilson Sporting Goods Ultra Complete Package Golf Set
review_headline: Don't wait to get started just buy this set
review_body:
Before buying this set, I owned the similar Top Flite XL set for one round of golf. I am a beginning golfer who has been plaing 1-2 rounds per week over the last month.

Bag - This bag seems to be a slightly better quality bag than what came with the Top Flite XL set. There is a nice soft lined pocket that I use for keys, wallet, and cell phone. The stand works just fine and levers open with an automatic pedal at the bottom of the bag. I only wish a rain cover came with the set.

Putter - Works just fine. I however wish it was more of a mallet style putter but that is a personal preference. The paint job on the putter head is rather cheap looking.

Irons and PW - I find the irons and wedge easy to hit and appear to be well made. The finish of these clubs is the best in the bag and is better than those included in the Top Flite XL set.

Drivers and hybrids - It is easy to make contact with these drivers. The yellow alignment arrows on the tops of these clubs are easy to see. My biggest complaint with the entire set is the finish on these clubs. The paint is great but whoever did the masking job must have done it in their garage. The edges of the paint are uneven and a bit erratic. Out of fairness, I had this same gripe with the Top Flite XL set so it seems it may be an issue for clubs in this price range.

Overall, I like this set quite a bit and would have given it 5 stars had it not been for the finish issues on the putter, drivers, and hybrid.

product_title: Sportsman 2,000 Watt Portable Generator
review_body:
This *is* without a doubt the worst product I have ever purchased. Yes, I know you're thinking LP Propane, no gas to haul around. It will store well for occasional use. It should be less exhaust fumes. Gee, I've been on the fence about a generator but this one is really cheap. Who cares if the thing doesn't really deliver 2000 Watt peak, my uses are more limited. So here's why I say "run":
1) This thing produces the most obnoxious chemical smelling exhaust when it runs bar none.
2) It smells really bad out of the box before you run it. Ever bought some really cheap Chinese metal tool that is greasy to the touch. Imagine one 55 pounds big! It requires oil to run, so you are really not escaping petrol and cleanup if you thought you might be.
3) Power output is so poor as to only run the smallest electrical load you can imagine. It cannot run a box fan at full speed, and no I'm not kidding.

Mainly this thing produces about the same amount of chemical smelling exhaust as a large diesel truck. It has multiple warnings not to run it in even a covered area. Trust me, I know why. This this could not be any worse than it is in any way. I suspect those that gave it a positive review were paid to do so.

So quit your whining, pony up, and go buy that Honda generator you really want. (I will tomorrow).

product_title: 91/30 m44 Mosin Nagant Rubber Recoil Butt Pad with 10 Mosin Nagant Stripper clip by FSI
review_body:
The fit on the butt pad is decent, but not spectacular. Then again, the stocks on most Nagants can be described with the same adjectives, so I'm not really complaining. The problem is that it's pretty hard, and although it makes a difference, is not as profound as I was hoping for. After drilling the holes out of it, I still feel like it could be better. The worst part, however is the UNHOLY SMELL of the thing. Why on earth is the rubber so nasty to the nose? I had the thing in my basement family room for a day or two and befroe I realized it the whole place smelled like turpentine! It's started to subside at this point, but DANG.

As for the stripper clips, they appear to be consistently well made and function well with practice. Hey guys, they're not supposed to feel like closing the bolt on a fine rifle - they're stamped pieces of pot metal, for crying out loud, and semi-disposable at that. These do, however, seem to be completely reusable and of reasonable quality. Practice makes perfect, and they definitely let you reload faster than the alternative.

product_title: Bear Archery 1st Shot Bow Set
review_body:
My son received this bow just before his 4th birthday and immediately took to shooting. It is easy for him to pull and he is able to shoot it 20+ yards with ease. Accuracy is not high but that has little to do with the bow and has to do with the attention span of a 4-5 year old. I feel this bow will last him for quite some time and have actually experimented with the Goblin, which is much harder to shoot. We won't be upgrading for some time.

I saw a review mention the arrows flying oddly side to side. We had that happen a few times but it was squarely about form, and loading the arrow correctly. It is not the bow. Now that we have the arrow's loaded properly and have worked on all our forms (4 adults and 3 different 4/5/6 year old kids have shot this bow) the arrows are flying straight and true.

Very highly recommend this bow!

I'm not quite as sold on the arrows that come with it. They are flying well, but the vanes are showing wear, especially the one that must consistently run along the grip when the arrow is shot. I'm not sure how long they will hold up, though they continue to do well at this point, after hundreds of shots (with many running along the grass as we edge our low-to-the-ground target). We may switch him to fletched arrows when it is time for replacements.

product_title: Sightmark SM21031K 6-100x100 Spotting Scope
review_headline: From the range to the field
review_body:
There are several different tactical spotting scopes on the market but the price tags usually associated with those scopes are upwards of $1,200 to $2,000. The Sightmark 6-100x100 Tactical Spotting Scope offers exceptional quality and features for half the price of other scopes on the market that don't even offer the high end magnification. The features are exceptional on this spotting scope, especially the knob for cycling between 6-25 and 25-100, which is very user friendly. This is an extreme positive, especially when you have gloves on.

I used this scope for spotting my groups on target during a rainy 35° day and humid 90° day. At both extremes there was not any fogging or other issue at all, which was quite impressive. The only personal issue I had was I felt I could not get comfortable with the relief due to no rubber eye guard. The scope focused flawlessly through the magnification range. Once I got on the top end of the scope's magnification range, there was some slight distortion, but not enough to make me put it back in the truck. With the scope tipping the scales at 53oz, one would not find it too cumbersome to pack it for a day's trek.

All in all, this scope is the complete package. Sightmark hit the mark in my opinion with high quality glass, user friendly features, fairly lightweight and all for a price that will not break the bank. I would recommend this spotting scope to those that put a lot of time in on the bench or those that need that extra magnification for hunting situations such as a Midwest scenario.

product_title: Acog 3 X 30 Scope Dual Illuminated Horseshoe/Dot .223 Ballistic Reticle
review_body:
This is a magnified optic that you can take out of the box (case) mount on your rifle with no other mounting accessories required, sight in quickly and have all of the close range target acquisition speed of a red dot with the benefit of a magnified optic with built-in bullet drop compensator easily getting you on target out to 500+ yards. It sounds too good to be true but it is true.

These ACOGs are very ruggedly built, have surprisingly clear glass and require no batteries to operate day or night. I find it amusing that some competitors count this as a negative--that you would have to send the optic back to Trijicon in 15 YEARS! to have the tritium replaced. I would take that any day over having to carry spare batteries or worry about the integrity of electronics exposed to temperature and repeated shock--no thanks.

If you have older eyes and shoot past 100 yards this is a great solution. Don't get me wrong, I am a huge fan of the Aimpoint Red Dot sights and quality knock-offs for short distances but if you are like me and have older eyes, shooting past 200 yards with a red dot is just not fun. Sure you could add a magnifier but now you are using a lot of rail space, adding significant weight and introducing additional points of failure.

It is not my intention to say how great this ACOG is by bashing another product. This sight stands on its own perfectly with its rugged design, clear glass, excellent choice of reticles and any lighting operations w/o depending on a battery.

If there is a better optic out there that gives you very quick close-range target acquisition and longer range magnification with a combat accurate bullet drop compensator, I am not aware of it at ANY price.

If you buy this optic you will continue to be impressed with its performance with no disappointments. That's a guarantee!

They are a little heavier than others but the payback is longevity and usability. Will definately recommend them to my friends and add them to my other rifles when I can.

Have two of these now.... one on .22 WMR, which has fired over 500 rnds and is shooting 1.25 MOA groups at 100 yards, consistantly. The other is on an M700 which holds 1.5 MOA groups at 200 yards with over 300 rnds fired. Both remain impressivly clear and accurate. product_title: Everyday Holsters Smith & Wesson M&P Shield Hybrid Holster IWB Right Hand
review_body: This is a good holster for the M&P Shield. The leather, clips, and kydex are all of high quality. The kydex is molded to fit the M&P Shield very well and has very good retention even when the holster is not being worn. I drew and holstered the gun smoothly numerous times without any hangups.    The reasons I gave this 4 stars and not all five, is because:    1. The way the leather was cut left some \\"sharp\\" edges around the sides of the leather that contacts your body. This was an easy fix with some scissors to dull the edge.    2. I feel that the holster is a tad big for the Shield, or maybe I am too skinny (6'1\\" 185 lbs). The problem I found is that there is excess leather to the right of the sights. I wear the holster at the 4 o'clock position. As the holster contours to my body, the extra leather in the forward area folds out noticeably and also hinders the holster's ability to bend a little. As I said earlier, it could be because I'm rather skinny. If I had more meat on my bones, then the extra leather in this area might not be an issue. So, I grabbed some scissors and trimmed this area. The problem was solved and the holster fit and felt 100% for me. Now I do not condone trimming the leather on this holster, as it will probably void the lifetime warranty offered by Everyday Holsters. Modify if you choose at your own risk.    Since I was already trimming, I went ahead and removed excess leather from the bottom of the holster level with the top of the two bottom clip holes. It is a nice feature to be able to adjust the heights of the clips individually, but I was satisfied with where the clips were in the stock location. I had no desire to adjust the height or the cant of the holster any further, so I trimmed this bottom area out. It was not necessary, but I like the way it made the holster more compact.    I believe you can post pictures to amazon reviews, but I haven't done so before. I'll try to post pictures of how I trimmed the holster for you all to see.Overall, great quality holster for a great price compared to some of the other brand names out there. I also like to buy USA made whenever I can and it's great to support a small American business by buying holsters from Everyday Holsters. As I said above, the main qualm I had with this holster and why it receives 4 stars instead of 5, is because of the excess leather at the front top of the holster. However, this might not be the holster's fault but rather my body type. You can't really expect one holster design to fit everyone's body perfectly. Therefore, I took the liberty to tailor the holster myself to fit how I pleased.    EDIT, below are links to pictures showing how I trimmed the holster. product_title: OPTP Slant (Pair)
review_headline: Perfect for stretching your calfs and lower leg
review_body:
I first got into using a slant board for this stretch when I went to physical therapy after back surgery. I had always done this lower leg stretch after running with both my feet planted level on the ground. My PT therapist had a slant board, and so I understood just how effective it can be to use a slant board instead of what I had been doing. I've wanted to buy one of these, but the price of the wooden ones is just too much money for me.

I came across this item while browsing Amazon and decided that the price was right and that I'd give it a try. In short, this is a perfect slant board for a lower leg stretch. Yes, it's only a black foam slab cut on a bias, but it supports my body just fine and doesn't break or become misshapen. I think this product will be very durable and I can't imagine it not lasting for at least a few years, if not longer.

While you get two slant boards with this product, I'm only using one. The picture shows this product to be a bit narrower than it is in reality. I position the slant board about 2 feet away from the wall, put both feet on it, and then lean forward, using the wall as support. You can immediately feel the stretch in your lower leg. I do three sets of 30 seconds each.

The product stores easily and is as light as a feather. If you're a runner or need physical therapy that includes this stretch, consider this product. This is one of those times when less expensive is actually better! I'm not sure how this would hold up to day-in and day-out use in a commercial setting like a physical therapist's office, but for an individual or family, this is an excellent product that does the job at a very affordable price.

There are no instructions that come with it, and I'm not aware of any other use for it other than this stretch. If you live in a small apartment, storage might be an issue you need to think about. If, however, you have the room to put it away after each use, it is ideal for its purpose.

Highly recommended.urpose.

product_title: Denix Pirate Cutlass Sword (Nickel )
review_headline: This may be the only review you ever see on this.  lol
review_body: Nice looking display sword.  I bought it to augment a pirate costume and this looks more than real enough to fullfill that role.  My first act out of the box, however, was to remove the screw-on end piece and take the handle/hand guard off.  The tang is pretty narrow and it allows for a bit too much flexibility in assembling the grip and hand guard.  Mine arrived with the tang slightly bent and the handle/hand guard assembled sloppily and visibly off center.  It comes apart easily so it wasn't a difficult fix.  The process did reveal that the tang is narrow, thin and not very strong.  I'm not sure if this blade can handle a lot of rough handling without eventually fatiguing and snapping off the tang altogether.  I certainly would never let the blade hit anything when it's being swung.  The ease with which the end unscrewed also means that I'll be adding Locktite to it and checking its tightness regularly.  Don't want my sword falling apart unexpectedly.  Not a problem for a display sword but as a costume accessory, it's going to require gentle handling and frequent maintenance.  Blade is metal and unsharpened.  Handle/hand guard is cast metal as well.  Sword makes a nice sound as you pull it from its scabbard.  The scabbard fits the sword well, but the faux wood/leather finish (not sure what they were going for pattern wise) is nothing more than a large decal.  The edge of the decal shows noticeably with the light at the right angle, so my first improvement will be to cover the scabbard with faux leather or something more realistic.  Looked for a long time to find a review of this item and couldn't, so this may be the only review you'll find on it.  Hope it helps.

product_title: Surefire G2-LED G2 80 Lumens Runtime: 2 Hours Nitrolon® body LED flashlight
review_headline: My favorite light, but outdated now
review_body:
Most of what I mentioned in my review for the G2 Incandescent review applies here. To sum it up briefly: Average lighting and battery life, very durable, good size and ergonomics, lightweight, nice grip texturing. It's probably not worth the current list price ($76), and I got mine for about $55. Nicely customizable, but a casual user should just get a new one unless budget is a major constraint.

I do notice criticisms in other reviews about bulb durability but I can't actually say I have broken the light element, so I can't comment on that. However, the head dissipates heat well and the light itself is very robust. It's a 'just right' size that fits into pockets, pouches and handbags with ease.

The beam is a great improvement over the G2, offering a useable beam with an intense hot spot, capable of blinding someone at short ranges in daytime and revealing detail well at night. The battery life is just average - usually a bit over two hours for me. Newer and brighter lights are available, so again I'd only get the G2 LED if you really like the ergos (like me) or can't really afford anything else.

If you wanted to mix-and-match heads from the 6P line I'd probably just buy a G2 Incandescent, since they are otherwise the same light. The lockout tail cap is pretty standard Surefire. It's nice that it provides a single-output, on or off option plus a constant on and a lockout, but it does actuate accidentally easily in a pocket and isn't too tactile in my opinion. Plenty just change to a Surefire click cap.

With the G2X being available for $50 now, it's essentially replaced the humble G2 LED. It's not really even expensive compared to the G2 incandescent, so fair warning there.

product_title: Polar Loop Activity Tracker
review_body:
I spent hours researching this activity tracker and finally decided to make the purchase. I considered this activity tracker and the Garmin Vivofit because they are the only two that can be connected to a heart rate monitor. There are many comparisons online that you can read to see the differences between the two. Although many preferred the Garmin (mainly because of compatibility with Android, which Polar also has now), I went with the Polar because of the superior heart rate monitor. My interest in these devices started with research into a heart rate monitor watch to provide feedback on my workouts. I looked into the Polar FT7, which probably would have done everything I needed, but the activity tracker seemed to offer a lot more features. I also came across the Basis, but it clearly states it is not to replace a heart rate monitor for exercise. Anyway, the Polar H6 and H7 heart rate monitors are apparently two of the best you can buy. Not only do they sync with the Polar Loop, but they can be used without the Loop with a smartphone should I decide I don't want to wear the activity tracker anymore.
In my research, I viewed reviews from Jim's Review Room on YouTube, read huffpost, dc rainmaker, among other various bloggers, many of which received the product for free for their review. I highly recommend reading/viewing these before purchasing so you know exactly what you're getting into. There were some common complaints about the loop, but I think this is an excellent product. Specifically,
* Cutting the band: yes, you have to cut the band to fit your wrist. This means that the band will fit you perfectly, without the extra rubber hanging off. To me, this was a good thing. I'm wearing this thing all the time, I don't need extra bulk. If you cut too short, Polar will send you a new bracelet. It is very comfortable.
* The button: Oh, the button. In so many reviews, people complained about the button. There is NO PROBLEM with the button. The problem is with the instructions. People complained about pushing the button and getting no response. In fact, DC Rainmaker says he got no response 50% of the time when pushing the button. The online manual for the Loop tell you at various times to tap/press the button. The problem is that you cannot push this button because it is not a button, it is a sensor. Gently slide your finger across the sensor (like you would your smart phone) and it responds every time. I noticed this was the way the Loop was being operated in the Jim's Review Room Video and it is the way the Loop was designed to be used. It is unfortunate that the instructions are worded in such a way that people think the product is defective since pushing the button doesn't work.
* Step counting: Several bloggers mentioned that the "steps" were over-calculated using the Loop. The first time I put on the loop, I sat at my computer viewing the website, then walked around my house for a few minutes. It already calculated 90 steps, which I knew was impossible. So, checked out Polar's website to see how steps are calculated. It turns out all movements that are recorded are converted to "steps." This does not calculate steps in the literal sense, the point is to record movement.
These were concerns that I had before purchasing, based on reviews that I have read. I have been using the Loop for a couple of days now and I am very impressed. It has been very accurate so far and I have had no problems syncing with my phone or computer. review_body:

#2 I have added two new triglide sliders to both of the mainbody straps. I found when I had it heavily loaded (which is easy to do) it was more comfortable cinched up tight. It loosened easily though, so I modified it.

It is starting to show visible wear after a year and a half of daily use. 5 countries, and about 5 military schools and trainings. But it is not wearing out at all.

product_title: Oceanic Vortex V-6 Full Scuba Diving and Snorkeling Full Foot Fins - Size 9/10 - Ice Blue
review_body:
went on a trip and brought Oceanic Vortex V-6 Scuba Diving and Snorkeling Full Foot Fins for snorkeling. we are avid snorkelers and we snorkeled a lot. out of all the fins we bought and brought, these were universally considered the best of the group. recommend 2m socks to go with. i am a women's size 10.5 and got size 9/10 and they fit great. The foot on these does not expand up the ankle as far as others, making them more comfortable and flexible. I never got cramps and was the fastest in the water with great control. we did a lot of research and bought a few things, so perhaps our time can help you.

second best: Aeris Velocity full foot scuba diving & snorkeling fins. My husband wears a size 12 or 12.5 shoe and got them in size "12-13/2x large". They fit well. But the V-6 is well worth the extra $15.

Scuba pro jet sport fins: these are really dive fins, and require boots, not socks. Really big and heavy - not good for going into a suitcase or for travel.

also bought Promate Snorkeling scuba Dive DRY Snorkel PUrge Mask Gear Set. fogged a bit; one of them leaked a bit; but overall they were the best of the ones we tried. heard you were supposed to use SoftScrub on them before first use. didn't know that. will try.

Also got Cressi Palau Long Fins were pretty good for a set for our son whose feet are not yet fully grown and we didn't want to spend the extra $$ knowing they will not last. but wouldn't recommend the fins if you can get a full-foot fin.

not pleased with Promate Snorkeling Scuba Dive set with Pace fins (FN430). the mask was good, but the fins were awful.

product_title: Zensah Compression Leg Sleeves – Helps Shin Splints, Leg Sleeves for Running
review_headline: Feels great for about 10 uses. Good for another 10.  Then it's nothing special.
review_body:
I purchased these to use instead of compression socks. I wear them every single day under my slacks so that I can wear regular socks, but still get the benefit of compression.

Out of the package, they were very, very snug and felt fantastic. After a couple work weeks, I noticed that they still felt pretty good, but were much easier to get on and take off. They'd apparently stretched out a bit. Now after several weeks of use, they are little more than leg decorations, which may be neat when wearing shorts. But under slacks, what's the point?

I have not washed them once -- just worn them and taken them off at the end of the work day. I work in an office, so it's not like they're getting soaked in sweat. Anyway, with nothing more than normal wear, there has been a dramatic deterioration in performance. I even find now that I have to pull them up a few times a day.

Better than nothing.

product_title: ASICS Quick Lyte Low Cut Socks
review_body: I've been searching high and low for a good running sock... seamless toe, light, and thin enough to allow for ventilation, sweating, swelling, etc. I slipped one on and it felt like I was practically barefoot... the most comfy running sock I'd ever worn. Decent price for a 3-pack, too. I was so excited about this sock that I ordered three more packs. That's a dozen pair of these \\"perfect\\" socks. Well, after one washing I discovered they're not as perfect as I initially thought. I still like them, but a couple of things to be aware of... these socks are so thin they should be washed in a garment bag and air dried. Treat them like delicates. Being tossed in a washing machine could fray the stitching a bit and they will definitely shrink. Also, if you normally wear a large like me, size up and order an XL. The women's socks only go up to L so Amazon will send a men's XL which fits me perfectly. On a positive note, they do hold up well in the shoe and the heel tab prevents slippage (when wearing the correct size, of course). I don't expect these to last long so I ordered a thicker brand of Asics socks which I also like, along with a couple pair of Balega socks. I probably turned off a few potential buyers of this sock, but 3 stars is better than no stars. :)

product_title: Xiser Commercial Mini Stairmaster, Polished Alloy
review_body:
As an old and heavy guy, I was delighted to take this out of the box and find that it's massively made of thick aluminum. This makes me feel that I will be able to use it energetically without it suddenly breaking and/or pitching me off onto the floor. Very promising!

The assembly of the unit is as simple as can be. The resistance of the unit is adjustable, and I found that neither extreme of the adjustment is too great for a weak guy like me to operate the Xiser. I tried the heavy-resistance setting briefly and slowly, and it seemed to me to be difficult enough to provide a challenge for someone who is in good shape if he used it at substantial speed.

The lighter-resistance extreme seems better for me. I set up the unit for that and used it for a while. Because I have questionable balancing ability, I held onto the front of my big bureau and things went fine. The foot pedals are big enough that I feel secure standing on the unit while operating in---provided I have something to hold onto. Thinking back to when I was younger, I believe I could have quickly learned to operate this unit while just standing on it and holding onto nothing.

Summer is coming soon here in the southern USA. The Xiser looks at present like an ideal way of getting good exercise while staying inside in the air conditioning, without leaving home.

I'll update this review later, after I've had further experience of the unit.

product_title: Clicgear Model 3.5+ Golf Push Cart
review_headline: Why Buy Clicgear, is it worth the extra dough?
review_body:
Clicgear is not the cheapest golf cart you can buy, so why would you pay extra? Because it's higher quality? Probably, but since I have not been able to use others products I cannot specifically say. Better design? Yes. But is that worth nearly double the money from a very good Caddytek? Probably not. So why then? Because Clicgear products are well designed, and you get quality products, but you also get the most accessories that are well integrated bar none!! Who wants push a golf cart on a hot and humid summer day? No? Then attach a large umbrella and just walk down the fairway in the shade. Or how about it starts to rain? Pull the umbrella of the quality attachment on the side of your cart, screw in the handle on the push bar, and open your umbrella and stay dry. Hang a towel over the handle and keep your hands and grips dry. You don't want an umbrella that just points straight up in the air? Buy the Clicgear adjustable attachment that allows you to point it in nearly any direction your heart desires.

You'd like to be able to take the weight off your feet from time to time while waiting to tee off, or on the fairway? Just have a seat! The Clicgear chair accessory is, guess what? Quality. Open the cart, attach your bag, attach your umbrella, and then attach you chair. It's spring loaded so it's out of the way when using the cart for it's primary purpose. Want to sit down out of the sun? The chair is under the umbrella, so you can stay cool and sit down at the same time. Just well designed.

Cart folds-up to a very small footprint, and the bag stop magically turns into an extremely well placed grab handle. Standard cup holder comes with, but guess what? Clicgear has an accessory to hold much much more. By far and away the most number of accessories for the carts and demonstrate why they have taken this market,and now firmly own it. Nice brake, nice alignment feature. Overall, well constructed and beefy.

So when you buy Clicgear you get the best the market has to offer in design, quality and versatility.

Issues? Biggest issue is that you cannot collapse the cart while the bag is attached. Also the collapsing methodology is a bit complicated in that you have to spin it upside down, and the center arm for the front wheel does not \\"click\\" so your not sure at first exactly if it's in place or not. Once you know how it works, the quality is excellent, so that's what really matters right? Yes, but less mechanically inclined people will find this very confusing for a bit until they've opened it several times. But you don't get something for nothing. The cart collapses until a cute little ball that is really easy to carry and put away just about anywhere, but you loose on bag versatility and the ease of assembly.

Overall, Clicgear is clearly #1 in my mind with their total design, quality and accessories, but if keeping it on the bag is critical, then you won't like this unit, but your giving up a lot elsewhere.

Update (6/6/14):
I have to say I did not figure out how to open and close this device in the easiest manner. I consider myself very handy, and I watched the video on how they recommend:
http://youtu.be/SGpzbctuOxw
and I was embarrassed! Very easy to open this way :)

I've added cigar holder, very slick!

One pointer I'll give about using this cart (or any push cart I suppose) is to keep your arm relaxed; allow your hands to almost touch your belly while walking and this provides a really nice and comfortable walking arrangement. If you are like me, I tended to straighten my arm and lean over a bit and push, but the cart does not require this much effort, and this configuration is not comfortable on your body because it is not your normal walking position.

I aligned the front wheel this morning, very easy and there is a video for this as well:
http://youtu.be/eRNYugJ8GFM

I have now used the cart several times, and my wife has used hers even more than I, and we both are delighted. They are very handsome and garner a lot of attention, particularly my wife's with the umbrella and chair in place; she is the envy of all the other lady walkers.

As I mentioned earlier, the qty and quality of the accessories is top notch. Just well thought out, and constructed products.

Oh, one last thing; I considered 4 wheel carts when researching and now I am glad I went with three. Three is very stable, easier to turn, and probably easier to adjust tracking, although I have not seen the 4 wheel. Frankly, not sure why a four is required; easier rolling? Possibly, but the 3 rolls pretty easy. I guess a side by side would the only way to confirm, but your adding weight too.

product_title: MTM Pistol Rest
review_headline: Nice For A Revolver - But Rail-Mounted Gear Might Be An Issue
review_body:
I got one of the Case-Gard Pistol Rest hoping to make laser and iron-sight alignments a bit easier at the range. The Pistol Rest appears to be well made, with the V-Neck piece locking solidly in place. I read where one reviewer had the V-Neck piece keep coming off. Hopefully that won't be an issue but if it is I'll try a similar fix. The flat surface where your hand rests is a bit flexible, but not overly so. When you're done, the V-Neck snaps into a cradle under the hand rest making it easy to store or transport.

My problem is that I have a Viridian C5L Rail-Mounted Laser/Light on my Ruger P95. The laser is fairly large, and extends almost to the end of the frame under the barrel. There's just not enough \\"empty\\" frame at the end to safely rest in the \\"V\\". Also, with the \\"V\\" having a fairly sharp angle, it forces the laser to sit up quite a bit and be wedged against the two sides. I'm not sure if this is going to be an issue with recoil, but it is a bit concerning.

The only \\"fix\\" I can come up with is to have a thick V-shaped pad placed in the bottom of the \\"V\\" to provide a somewhat flat surface for the flat bottom of the laser to rest on. Hopefully I can adjust the pad height until the laser sides are just touching the inner walls of the \\"V\\". That way it'll be supported, but not wedged. If it proves successful, I'll then make a more permanent fix for my application.

Bottom Line: If you have any rail-mounted gear (laser and/or flashlight) you might reconsider buying this Pistol Rest for this very reason. However, if you have a revolver or a semi-auto pistol with at least a 1\\" section of empty frame exposed on the business end, you should be happy with this item. Hopefully I can get it to work for me.

One note: I found the edge around the thumb hole a bit sharp and spent a minute dulling it with a file. I didn't deduct points because it was easy enough to do. In addition, the overall quality of the components offset this minor issue. Again, considering the price, quality of the design, and good components, it's tough to quibble over minor stuff.

Finally, as indicated in the title, this is a knife that wants to be used. This may sound odd, given that it's a tool, but there are many "trophy" knives being purchased that never do more than cut paper (for show) or leave the house because the owners don't dare to scratch them. However, this Buck knife just feels like it is meant to go to work and can take it. Cutting boxes, whittling wood, shaving burs...whatever is needed. .

review_headline: Good sound. Great for the BMW Z3
review_body:
I purchased this sub-woofer to replace a Harmon Kardon dual voice coil subwoofer in my 2000 BMW Roadster which literally turned into dust. After doing my research I had the choice between the Audiopipe, a Pyramid and the kicker 6.5 inch. Since I have read that the pyramid couldnt handle much and the kicker not only exceeded the price I was willing to spent but also didnt drop in without cutting off the edges, I went with the Audiopipe. R. Atkins review on Amazon helped me to give it a try.

Just as R. Atkins, I had to snip off and replace the original spade connectors on the wire harness and use forked lugs instead because this speaker uses screw terminals but that was a minor issue. The RED and GREEN cable with the bigger terminals in the original enclosing are the positive wires while grey and black are negative.

Again as mentioned by Atkins, this speaker was also slightly deeper than the original HK subwoofer. However, I have to partially disagree with Atkins solution proposal. The plastic ring from the old sub isn't enough as a spacer. I needed to add some self gluing foam stripes i placed in between the ring and the sub. Without it the sub sounded completely distorted.
Another issue I encountered once the sub was dropped behind the seat was that it touched the metal of the car since it was sticking out more than the original sub. What I did was to place a few foam stripes under the sub enclosures so it tilts slightly forward. Then once dropped in, I placed some more of the foam underneath the back screw holes of the enclosure so the tilt is stable and sufficient. The two front screws are enough to hold the whole thing in place.

Was it hard to drop into the box and replace the old sub? Not at all if you know which cables are + - and you have the right materials for the alterations at hand.

What about the sound? It probably isnt as good as a kicker which costs over 2x as much and requires more work than the Audiopipe but its definitely enough to get the full range of sound and let every one around you know that you are listening to music.

Likes:

-Great fit and easy to take on and off...I don't feel like I'm "wearing it out" swapping it out.
-As everyone else has already said...it has a fantastic tactile feel that Magpul is famous for...good grip, but not too obtrusive
-I've had no problems with plugging head phones or chargers (Apple and aftermarket) into it and the camera cut out is fine
-Very good looking case...color options are pretty awesome as well.
-I haven't dropped my phone with this case on (yet) but I suspect it will protect the phone the same if not a bit better than other cases in the class

Cons:

-I don't care for the button covers. I get it...they keep out debris and dust real well. But I struggle with the volume buttons...especially when I'm trying to "snooze" my alarm in the morning. Maybe they will break in though...
-The "grid" design looks good and helps with grip...but I don't always enjoy holding the phone in the talking position with them. I almost wish I could get one that is just a solid case with their awesome coating.

product_title: NFL New Era OtT Hood
review_body:
I read the review concerning the sizing of this product and was concerned. I decided to buy two anyways, as I wear hats frequently and don't mind the "hat with hood" look.

I'm glad I did!

SIZING:
I am 6'3'' and weigh around 230. My neck size is a 17 1/2, and I experience no problems. I have no feelings of constraint. Both hoods fit exactly the same and are made of the same great material. I have a friend who has an 18'' neck size and he LOVES the one I got him.

MATERIAL:
The material listed is "DWR Tech Fleece" and that translates to 92% Polyester and 8% Spandex. The inside is soft and the outside is that slippery shiny material that feels expensive and sometimes actually is expensive.

What do I wear it with?
Honestly- Anything. Even things that already have hoods (which probably looks funky, but I don't care). It is good for a jacket that doesn't have a hood, or a jacket that can have a hood removed so you can look cooler with this one. I've honestly even worn it with a T-shirt before.
HAT- I wear several flat billed hats with mine. The magnet is nice- keeps the hood up, keeps it in place. My fiancé tells me I look stylish when I wear it, if that means anything.

I'd say go for it. It's a great way to support the team on game day, or when you're just out for a quick errand.

product_title: 2XU Compression Performance Run Sleeves
review_headline: Good quality, but is it a good product...maybe...but meh, not for me.
review_body:
I run either barefoot or with minimalist shoes, but had a bad toe injury (and no, not running...actually on an escalator of all places...ironic, should have taken the stairs:)...so I got a bit out of running shape. When I started back, I was having trouble getting my calves back into condition, so came across this product. After some research, I was pretty much completely sold on the promise that this was the solution. I used them for a almost 3 weeks on a regular basis (running 4-5 times a week), following all the advice from other users and the companies website. But, I still suffered from very sore calves, and my recovery time was no better than it had been without them. I also found that wearing them changed my gait quite a bit, and not for the better. So I started experimenting, and would go a day with/day without. I found when I wasn't using them my recovery time was actually reduced, and my run speed was increased, and I also felt like I expended less effort. So all of the benefits that these are supposed to provide, I only achieved when I WASN'T wearing them compared to when I was.
Of course, this is only my personal experience, but I would say that these may be great for diabetics, or those sitting in car/desk all day. But I see no benefit or reason to make these apart of a runner's routine...other than if they just like the "look", and/or it provides some sort of psychological boost.

product_title: WindJammer by ShedRain 2044A 58-Inch Arc Vented Auto Open Jumbo Umbrella
review_headline: Not what I expected from shedrain.
review_body:
Having used their windpro line in the past, I can attest that shedrain usually means quality (or maybe that has changed over the years?), I find it interesting seeing \\"made in china\\" as a bullet point in the features list, maybe I should have taken note of that before ordering this model.

Exact same issue as another reviewer here; had the umbrella for about 4 months and 2 of the internal supports broke, making the umbrella effectively useless... I only used the umbrella maybe half a dozen times during that time span... my friend's $5 umbrella from home depot has lasted longer and shown better durability. Maybe if they change the price of this model to $5 then I might consider buying again, but otherwise sorry this is pretty pathetic quality for a $20+ shedrain-branded umbrella.

Update: After having contacted ShedRain about a possible replacement (this was back when I had only had the umbrella for 4 months, well within their LIFETIME warranty time frame) I have to downgrade my review to a 1-star for a truly lousy experience, I was told that to get a WARRANTY REPLACEMENT for a DEFECTIVE umbrella, I had to pay them a return shipping fee which iirc was about $15, and they weren't going to pay for my defective one to be shipped back to them, either! Ultimately, a product which costs $23 with no shipping fee, ends up costing MORE to REPLACE than it does to BUY NEW!

These umbrellas used to actually be durable, about 8-10 years ago Shedrain made the toughest umbrella I had ever bought; it lasted a good 3 YEARS and SEVERAL DROPS and hurricane-wind-like days (50+mph) with NO problems.

Now, however, they are doing something HORRIBLY wrong in the construction process, and effectively refusing to provide any sort of customer service to make up for it, it's obvious they KNOW that they're churning out garbage because otherwise they would honor their WARRANTY and replace DEFECTS for FREE... if they were to do that with the quality they are putting out now though, they would surely go bankrupt.

The point in the umbrella where all of the supports connect at the very top is the worst quality I have ever seen, the last two umbrellas I bought from them had supports ALREADY BROKEN at that point which had to be replaced (ironically, THEN they would replace them for free, as long as it was broken DAY ONE), and for the ones that didn't, the slightest drop or bump resulted in them breaking off from there, or from the flimsy weak-plastic assembly completely breaking. And what is this about a \\"fiberglass frame\\"? This thing is the same likewise weak and furthermore rust-prone metal frame that I'd expect from a dollar store umbrella; it got rained on ONCE, I forgot to leave it open to dry, and I ended up with PERMANENT RUST STAINS on the umbrella, from ONE TIME that it got WET!

product_title: Freefisher Fishing Line Reel Spool Spooler System Tackle Black
review_body:
Loaded maybe 50 reels so far. It does work as claimed but it takes a little practice to get it to work right with spinning reels. Don't wind too fast or line dispenser will not keep up with rotation of bail on reel. It will still work but you loose some benefit of winding on reel with no twist. Also if you wind too fast and you are loading a larger spinning reel (3000 or 4000 series) you'll pull the line off spool sideways and the line will wrap up and snag.

Line spools with very small center holes can be tricky to load on winder and properly tension. Don't let a bad first impression fool you. After a couple tries you'll get the hang of it.

One last tip when winding spinning reels - hold winder straight up vertically so spool doesn't have to fight gravity when spinning.

product_title: TaylorMade Men's Rocketballz Stage 2 Rescue
review_headline: Perfect for a beginner/high handicap player, tested with launch monitor
review_body:
I have been playing a Ping G20 hybrid clone, as well as some other clone hybrids. With a laser range finder, I was trying to pinpoint the exact distances I was hitting using those hybrids and my long irons. It turns out they were all in the 140-145 yard range, even with the G20 3H clone - all with solid and clean hits. I took advantage of the sale on the RBZ 2 Rescue and went to Golfsmith to try the actual G20 against the RBZ 2. I'm really a beginner, so my swing speeds aren't all that great.

Looking at some of the LPGA players with driving distances longer than the average male, many of them are playing 5-PW irons with a variety of fairway woods and hybrids. After using my laser rangefinder and some driving range sessions, I can understand why since my long irons (3, 4, and 5) are basically doing the same thing except the 3 and 4 aren't consistent at all. The hybrids are just much easier to launch out of the fairway and rough.

The launch height is better on the G20, but it just isn't going far enough. With the RBZ 2 3H, I was getting 10-15 mph faster swing speeds (75 mph), and a distance of 182.2 yards. The sales rep provided some tips on ball position and stance, and we both agreed that it would be a useful tool for me while I develop swing mechanics and technique. Considering my long irons (3-5) and current hybrids (3H, 4H) are peaking around 140-150 yards, the RBZ 2 helps bump my yardage into the zone I was looking to fill.

One thing to note is that the RBZ Stage 2 is longer than competitors' hybrids. The RBZ Stage 2 3H is 19* loft, 41.25\\" standard playing length. The Ping G20 is 20* loft, with 40\\" standard playing length. While this may account for some of the increase in yardage, the Speedpocket greatly increases forgiveness and feel. The ball \\"tings\\" off the face with a proper hit. The standard 65 gram shaft isn't too bad, and seems to not hamper feel. The launch height isn't as high as the G20 though, but the launch monitor data showed the G20 wasn't going to meet my need to close the yardage gap. Based on my local course, the most heavily used club after my putter and driver would be one that can reach 170 yards or so and none of my current clubs would fit the bill.

Overall: 5/5 stars, great price right now which makes it competitive with inexpensive clone clubs. The Speed Pocket feels spectacular. The graphics are fine to me, as is the race yellow head cover. The Matrix \\"RocketFuel\\" shaft feels good as well, It is longer than competitors' hybrids but is still easy to hit. As a beginner/high handicap player, I felt this club is a great value and provides a lot of bang for the buck.

Specs: 3H, 19 degrees loft, 352 grams total weight, shaft length of 41.25\\" (standard, regular flex RocketFuel 65gram shaft).

product_title: Steiner 10X50 Rallye Binocular
review_headline: Limited Purpose 'Sports View' Binoculars Built to Mil-Spec
review_body:
If you peruse the German Steiner website, there is no mention of the Rallye series. It is evident that this is a re-badged Police P1050. In fact the manual enclosed is for a completely different model. And wholesaler states in the description \\"... I made a quantity buy.\\" The identical bino badged as 'Police' sells on Amazon for $400, so these are a relative bargain on a high quality Steiner Binocular. My guess is that there was a large cancelled order.

The mil-spec design means high quality components and highly ruggedized construction. However there are some things you should be aware of..,..they are HEAVY, weighing in at 36 ounces, and they fill your hands. I sure wouldn't call them compact. A tripod connection would be in order, but no dice. With no magnification adjustment, the bino's are not so good for birding or hunting. The Steiner web site shows them being used by a spotter next to a sharp-shooter.

The main features are a huge depth of field combined with a wide view, razor sharp optics and great light. They have no zoom, but you will not have to refocus them as an object moves. They are a good choice for Baseball, (you can see both the pitcher and batter + follow the ball into the field), fantastic for auto racing, but at the ballet, they will crush your tuxedo frills.

The weight means discarding the tiny cord and getting a real bino harness..and a bag.

UPDATE***: After having these for a while and comparing them to my other bino's, I am raising the rating to five stars. The depth of field and great prism's in these are so far superior to the sub=$250 consumer product offered in the marketplace.

review_body: Purchased this for my AR15 and am extremely happy with it.  I was originally thinking of purchasing a shorter one, but after reading reviews I went with the 30" length.  Ideally would be great to have a few inches shorter, yet it works great and I'm very happy with it. It's better to have it a little long rather than short (which allows it to be used in a longer rifle).  Good construction, but I would advise using a bore guide. Without it, it's possible for the rod to flex when initially pushing it in the barrel. If you don't use a guide, I'd make sure to initially push while holding down the rod a little and not at the handle. Once it's a few inches in the barrel you can push from the handle without over flexing the rod. Having this one piece (vs. multiple pieces) makes storing it a little less convenient, yet I don't think it would last if it did have break points. They would eventually become weak points and bend. product_title: Rukket 10x7ft Pop Up Golf Net | Orginal Rukknet | Practice Driving Indoor and Outdoor | Backyard Swing Training Aids
review_body:
