Taking it down is pretty simple as well once you get the hang of it. The first day I tried to put it away I struggled for quite a while to get it right. My wife finally figured out that you just need to let the net do the work of coiling itself into position - don't force it. If you have to force it you haven't done it right. When done right, it folds up and is back in the back in maybe 2 min tops.

The bad - when it's windy this thing folds over quite easily. Even when I have it spiked down, the spikes aren't strong enough to hold it in place against a semi stiff breeze, and it ends up pushing the top part over anyway. It's a bit frustrating to use on a windy day because you'll be constantly trying to set it back upright. If you can, use it indoors or a garage for best results.

review_body:

It's really well-balanced too, and it gives you a great sense of being \\"grounded\\" when you hold it. The angle of the shaft allows you to look straight down onto the club face without distraction of the shaft itself. It took a little practice to get this under control, as I usually use a Cleveland Blade putter, but I did begin to really like this putter. It's well-balanced, so you get a nice firm hit when you strike the ball. The clubface has a 3-degree angle to it (it's embossed on the underside of the club) which I've never seen before, so it gives your puts a little jump, which I actually like and need. I'm not sold on the overall design - I found those giant squares too distracting. That got to me sometimes. Also, since it's a mallet, and I'm a terrible golfer, occasionally the tail end of the clubhead would hit the ground during a swing, which drove me insane. That's why I use a blade to begin with. BUT I do like th weight of the club, and I like the way it strike the ball - you do get a good sense of confidence when using it. So for now, I'll stick with it. I'll also let you know how this performs over time!
** UPDATE **
I love my putter! It's been quite some time, but I now love this putter. The weight and size have taken getting used to, but now I hate blade putters! Very rarely, I'll swing incorrecly such that the back of this behemoth will hit the ground - drives me nuts! But - overall I've really learned how to dial this one in. My putts are usually really good distance-wise. Now, if couldn't hit STRAIGHT!!!!

product_title: TITLE Weighted Gloves
review_body:
I use weighted gloves in the aerobic classes in the gym. I have been doing so for years ever since I got a free pair with a Beach Body product a few years back. The simple little extra weight really gives my workouts that extra oomph.

For the most part there are two types of weighted gloves. The type that fit like a real glove in that you have to affix them to each finger. And then there are the other types that only fit around a finger or two. The advantage of the full gloves is that fit securely on you hand and will never fall off. OTOH, they are usually a bear to put on and take off. The advantage of the minimal fingers gloves are that they are easy to take off and put on. However, they can slip off if the Velcro unsnaps and your palms are open, so you just have to be mindful of that possibility.

I like the minimal finger gloves because sometimes during an intense class I have to take them off for a break. And then I can quickly put them back on.

The Title Weight gloves are great for that purpose they easily come off and come on and the Velcro has yet to unsnap so no slip off worries. But because the title gloves sorta warp around the wrist, it adds an additional layer of protection from slip off. The only bad thing is that unlike any weighted glove I have every had, this one very clearly list the total weight on the gloves. It says 3 pounds but really each glove is a 1.5 pounds. I don't want people thinking I'm working with 3 pounds - I'm not. I like keeping it real or I am never going to really improve.

Otherwise, great glove - I'm glad I took a chance on this one.

review_headline: FreeMotion 790 Interactive Treadmill - I Purchased Two, One Worked Perfectly, The Other... The Display Is INOPERABLE!  5*s
review_body:
I suppose if you get one that works, 5 stars are probable; I however, am experiencing both Joy and Pain, as I wait for my Husband's treadmill to be located. I actually purchased our two from Sports Authority, who is working really hard to find us one in our area, since that particular store is completely out. As Amanda stated in her review, the entire display is INOPERABLE on the broken one, which leads me to believe there's a serious defect in the product. FreeMotion/Icon Service wanted to send me another display, to which I replied... "I DON'T THINK SO!" I insisted on a NEW Treadmill, because that's exactly what I PAID CASH for! The customer care Rep said that to get a new one is a lengthy process, so he suggested I stick with Sports Authority's effort to find one.

Anyway, for the one that works, we absolutely LOVE IT and I hope we continue to feel that way. We both were able to get the 1-Year FREE subscription to iFit by calling Icon Service customer care line at 800-999-3756 and referencing the last paragraph, first column on page 22 of the User's Manual - where it states to Enter the activation code from the iFit Live flier that came with the treadmill. I assume their banking on no one reading that part, because there was NO iFit Live flier in the box, hence my call into Icon Service. I was thankful for a great customer care rep (different than the rep mentioned above) that took care of that issue.

All in All, I believe the 790 is a Great Treadmill, including the iFit feature, when it's working. I Love It, and I can't wait until we get the other one, so I can run side-by-side with my hubby.

Happy Trails Everyone! I wish you the best in your Health and Fitness Goals!

product_title: Benjamin 392 Bolt Action Variable Pump Air Rifle (.22)
review_headline: Quality Control Seems To Be A Lost Art
review_body:
You're going to get a mixed review here...

There are several things that I really like about this rifle. In fact....were it not for one thing, I probably would give it a five star rating.

But the one issue I have with this rifle is serious enough that I have to knock it down to "just ok".

The problem? really bad alignment of the barrel in relation to the sights.

First...let me say that when I purchased this rifle, I immediately purchased and mounted a Williams Peep Sight for it. This is where the problem comes in....

If you mount the Williams sight and center the sight aperture, the rifle shoots about 2-3" to the left at 20 feet. If you try to adjust the sight all the way to the right, it will only move the point of impact about 1". Now...I should mention that I'm a little annoyed with Williams as well, since I believe that they should have a better range of adjustability in this sight. I finally had to resort to putting a couple of small washers as shims between the sight body and where it mounts to the rifle. When I did that, one of the screws that holds the sight on the rifle was now too short to thread into the rifle. And of course.....the sight looks totally tweaked when it comes to where it is mounted on the rifle in relation to the bore axis. This is why I say that there is something amiss with the way Benjamin has put this rifle together. Either that, or the barrel is just extremely out of whack in some way. The front sight appears to be perfectly aligned and is not leaning to either the right or left. I don't know what else the could be causing this problem and I don't really see any really good solutions when it comes to correcting this on this rifle. I think the idea of having to use "Kentucky Windage" with a rifle at the price-point of this one, is really asking a bit much on the part of the manufacturer. Do they not at least test fire these rifles at the factoryto see if they hit at least close to point of aim with the sights centered on the rifle? This is why I question the quality control of this rifle. I will say this, the rifle groups extremely well. It's just grouping way out in left field. Not what I expected from a rifle with the reputation that this one has.

review_headline: Mat does exactly what I was hoping for
review_body:
I have been doing Beachbody exercise programs for over two years now (Insanity, P90X, Focus T25). There are hardwood floors throughout my house with area rugs, and I managed to TOTALLY destroy the living room rug with all the running, jumping and quick moves. I tossed the rug out and now just have the hardwood floors in the living room, and I wanted a mat that would both protect the floors and not slide around during my workouts. I discovered the Square36 Cardio Mat and it has done exactly what I needed it to do.

Yes, there was a very strong rubber smell with the mat...but if you are looking to order a new one, the smell is much less overpowering now with the latest generation and rubber blend they have recently come out with. I know because I had the original version of the mat but had an issue with some tears in it (my own fault...I had it folded for storage...don't do that!). The company was very gracious and offered a replacement. It says a lot to have a such a responsive company that truly care what customers think and are willing to work with them! I have been using the new mat for several weeks now, and I am extremely happy with it.

My living room is the only place that I can workout in the house, so I do have to move the mat out and store it after each session. The mat is quite heavy and requires some lugging, but I consider that an extra boost to my workout. Also, it really has to be this heavy to stay in place with these intense kinds of workouts. The surface grip is super, even with sweaty hands. I am 6'1", and there is plenty of room for various movements and exercises. I never wanted or expected the mat to be plush like a yoga mat...it's tough rubber, and that's still much better than pounding on the bare wood floors.

I live in the northeast and this has been the winter from hell, so I haven't been able to air the mat outside yet. product_title: Cold Steel 80PGTK GI Tanto 7" Carbon
review_body:
A little background about me: I am a heavy user of knives. I have many knives, and I prefer to carry a fixed-blade knife at work as well as a pocket knife.
There are a few things about this knife that I like, as well as a few things about it that I don't like.

First, I'll start off with the sheath. The sheath is amazing, I had never used a Secure-ex/Cordoba/Kydex (all very similar) sheath before, until I had this knife. I can't say I had my hopes high, but it works better than I thought- very easy to draw and to put away. It is strong enough, and holds the knife well enough that I can run with it on my hip and not worry about it flying out, and when drawing/sheathing it, I don't have to worry about loosening or buttoning anything. One thing I did not like about it: the belt loop it came with. That part is made out of nylon and attached to the plastic with screws. Durable enough I'm sure, but I prefer my knives to hang lower than most people (with the top of the handle being around the bottom of my waist). A simple fix with some paracord and it was fine. After all, it's just farm and ranch work, I don't need to impress anybody with looks.

I love the design. It is a strong design, to be sure, and I admit that I didn't expect to get much use out of a tanto, but it holds up well with everything that I have used it for. I have had this knife for almost a year, and I have used it to cut down cedar trees (some over six inches in diameter), carve wood, cut tall grass and thick weeds that the mower cannot get (and sometimes hitting some unseen machinery with little more than a dent or two in the blade), cutting into soup cans when I forgot my can opener, and prying open things that should not be done with a knife. In fact, when describing it to my friends, I just simply call it a pry-bar with a sharp edge on it. :-)

As for the edge itself, it did not come as sharp as I like my knives to be, but I am very picky in that regard. I re-beveled it from about a 25 degree to about an 18 degree bevel, and it was sharp (but not razor sharp), but even at that bevel it withstood a LOT of abuse, day to day, almost constantly. I literally dug out mus-thistles out of my gravel driveway with it, and did not see ANY new nicks. I never got the edge to be razor sharp, but hey, its a rough use knife, not a razor. That's what I carry a pocketknife for. The 'guard' on it provides a good grip with the hand on the one side, but the index finger on the other side, right next to the blade- if you wanted to use it for self defense, and grabbed it like that, there would be no way for it to slip from your grasp. (And with proper sharpening, it could be sharp enough to use as a combat knife as well.)

The handle is..ok.. In fact, if it had a better handle, I would have given it a five star review. It is a full tang, which is what I need, but after a sustaining lots of wood chopping (and a little throwing, which is hard on all knives), it started to fall apart. The scales did not break, but one of the screws fell out of it, and after some hitting, the scale moves on me in a way that I have to move it back to continue. I temporarily fixed this by rapping it with electrical tape until I find the time to get a screw and fix it properly. Also, the black finish came off where stuff would rub against the blade, which was mostly on the grind towards the tip, but that is to be expected with a guy who stabs it into the ground often and chops down trees with it. I can also conceal it upside down underneath of a large (and somewhat baggy) coat, if that is important to you. It could also be concealed in some other places, but It is illegal to carry it like that (because of its size) and I never did that in public, just messing around for fun.

All in all, I am impressed for this knife, which I remember getting for somewhere around 20-30 USD. I would probably spend up to around 45 dollars on this knife if I lost this oneor something happened to it.

I would highly recommend getting the one with the secure-ex sheath.. the other version comes with a nylon sheath, and anyone who uses a knife daily for work knows how bad they are- they do not protect you from the knife, nor do they withstand much abuse...

P.S. this knife is made in China. This is no issue to me, as it is still good quality, but for those of you who wish to support the American economy, here is your FYI.or something happened to it.

product_title: Cold Steel 1917 Cutlass Handle with Leather Scabbard
review_headline: A great addition to my collection.
review_body:
This makes a great addition to my collection. I own several cold steel swords, knives, tomahawks, and even a spear. But this is by far the most well built of all of them. And that's saying something.

Of all the cold steel products I own this is my first choice for a larger survival blade. It's good for defense in closed quarters and has enough reach to be effective in open areas as well. It also doubles as a machete.

The only down side is that it is a bit on the heavy side and the point of balance is almost 6 inches from the guard. Which makes it hard to wield for long periods of time. But that weight adds power too. Also if you intend on using this I recommend you watch cold steels saber training videos on youtube. The main reason being that most people swing a sword like a bat and use too much wrist movement. If you have the right technique the weight is much less of an issue. Personally the point of balance is much more of a concern when it comes to swords. Too close to the guard and you have no power. Too close to the tip and you are off balance. But I would rather have the POB closer to the tip rather than closer to the guard. After all you can always compensate for the in-balance with good technique.

The sword itself came well greased and packaged separately from the scabbard. It also had a nice edge to it with the exception of the last few inches by the tip. Which was easily fixed with a file and a stone. The blade and guard also have a nice even bluing. Also please keep in mind this is not a knife. If it is too sharp it will chip or fold when used. This sword in particular has a very hard temper and can have more of an edge to it than longer or thinner blades. But it should not be razor sharp, nor does it need to be. To be honest some cold steel swords I have bought came too sharp, requiring me to dull them with 0000 steel wool.

Additionally, one of the rivets in the grip was not as tight as the others and stuck out a bit. So I tightened it with a flat head and used a file to smooth out the male end of the rivet to match. I also covered the handle in masking tape to prevent scratching while I was filing down the rivet.

Now for those who don't buy or collect a lot of swords this may sound like a lot of work. But I assure you it is not. Swords are hand made unlike most cold steel knives so they will have some imperfections. But for the money cold steel makes great stuff. If I had to do this kind of thing with an Albion that I paid $1,500 for then I would be a bit disappointed. But for $150 I have no complaints. To be honest I have gotten swords from cold steel that were (relativity speaking) perfect. Which goes to show you just how good cold steel is.

Furthermore, the sword came with a dark brown scabbard rather than the tan one. Which may be historically inaccurate in terms of color but the quality is still there. To be honest I was actually quite impressed by the quality of the scabbard. It fits well and is made very nicely considering the overall cost. Also I personally find the dark brown scabbard to be much more attractive than the tan one. All in all with the proper care and respect this sword will be around for generations.

P.S. For those who are interested I will be uploading photos of my sword to amazon for all to see.

UPDATE: April 2015

So I've had this thing for about a year not and I've got to say my opinion has changed a bit. After all I have swords from windlass, hanwei, darksword, and I even just got an arms and armor rapier. Now I won't bother comparing this $150 sword to a $1,200 or even $600 sword. That would be dumb. I will however compare it ti every other sword I have. Don't get me wrong It's still durable and well made but there are a few issues I have with it.

First, it's too heavy. Yes, this cutlas was made to be on the heavy side but mine is a bitoverly so. Now that being said a few friends have bought this and none of them weigh the same. Mine, as luck would have it, is heavier than the other two by as much as 9oz. That's over half a pound. In the sword worlds that's a lot.

Second, the secondary beveled edge is too steep. What I mean by that is where they sharpened it is at to great an angle. As a result it doesn't cut well as is. I have re-profiled the edge twice using a belt grinder. However it took some doing to get it up to snuff with my other swords that cost about the same. Even the 1917 cutlas machete from cold steel cuts better out of the box. Even not the cutlas is so thick that it's almost as good as the machete was when I got it.

Long story short every cold steel sword I have, with the exception of the Italian long sword, required a lot of work to get it up to par. None of my other swords from other companies have required any work done to them. If you don't mind doing the work this is probably just as usable and durable as my darksword or arms and armor. Now that's assuming the Q.C. doesn't miss a tempering issues or what not.

In the end I still like cold steel. However, I won't be buying swords from them any more. I will buy their knives, machetes, training swords and axes. product_title: WaveToGo Azodin BLITZ 2011 Electronic Paintball Marker - Orange/Black Ultra 47ci Bag Combo
review_headline: Great Starter Marker But The Equipment Suffers
review_body:
Marker:
The azodin blitz is a great starter marker, it has four firing modes, it is a little heavy so if this is for a young kid he might end up using the remote line wich will solve the problem, if not the weight could help you to build strenght. The build quality is excellent, it feels very nice when holding and on top looks awesome. It comes with a manual, wich gives lots of details on the marker, it also comes with various orings and spare parts in case you need the wich on the long run will help. The barrel is a 12" autococker,wich is a little short to my liking, so it is compatible with most marker barrels. On azodin's website you can find a digital verison of the manual plus some others for leaks wich will help you a lot when you encounter a leak(for example i once put the valve in facing the wrong way and i would not have figured out what went wrong if it wasn't for one of those manuals). The trigger is ver nice and smooth, but also adjustable so you can very easily set it to your liking. Cleaning the bolt is the simples thing and overall full disasembly is fairly easy. The two buttons in the back ar a little tough to press but at least you won't be changing the modes by accident.

Mask:
I straight up changed the mask almost immediately, mainly because there is a small gap between under the lens and the mask, i got hit in the mask and some paint got through and got in my face, nothing to dangereous but it still is.
I don't know if it was only my mask that had the gap, but i also found that removing the lens was very tough.
The mask aplies some pressure on the forehead wich is uncomfortable but if you use a headwrap or anything on your head it will be no problem.

Squegee:
This works fine and i like it, the only thing i don't like about it is that in order to use it you have to remove the barrel so you might not be able to use it comfortably in game.

Oil:
This is some very good oil and does lasts you some time.

Case:
This case can be a little bit too long since you have to store the marker with the attached barrel in this case, i found myself using the box the marker came in to store it, but since the case comes with a velcro strap it is very helpful as a case for my tools and manuals.

Remote Line:
I don't use it a lot since i play speedball but the few times i've used it it didn't fail me.

Harness & Pods:
GxG pods are very nice and will last you a long time. As for the harnes it will not last you a lot but it is preetty decent, it has a spot for your tank if you use the remote line, it hold the pods in very well with a velcro strap, i have used this in some rough games for about 15 games and i still use it, though i am in my way to switching to a diferent one since i have seen two small tears in the fabric. I also find the sideway style of holding the pods will make them hang from your side wich can be in the way.

Hopper:
This is a decent electronic hopper and it works very well but it has a downside.
It uses two 9v bateries(the marker uses one)
Also watch out if you are going to fire cheap paint, since the hopper rotates sticks in order to move the paint and get it through so if you fire cheap paint you are probably going to get some broken balls with your movment plus the rotating sticks.

Tank:
This tank is very good and holds up a nice ammount of compressed air(DO NOT BUY A CO2 TANK WHATEVER YOU DO, THEY DO NOT COMPARE IN ANY WAY TO COMPRESSED AIR PLUS THEY ARE HARD TO FILL) the only bad thing is that since it is longer and not as round as many other tanks finding some tank cover for it will be difficult but if you put a layer oof socks on it it will do just fine.

Overall this kit is recomendable for someone who is just getting into paintball but doesn't want to spend a lot of money since they are not sure for how long will they play. If you are interested in playing and also commited to spend a little more i recommend you buy this marker alone and get better equipment separately(it will cost you half of what this kit costs) since you will spend more on replacing this equipment.

product_title: American 45 Degree Offset Rapid Transition BUIS Backup Iron Sights For Rifles Comes With Manual
review_body:
I purchased this American offset BUIS for a hundred bucks off, but minor irritants prevented this from being a four or five star product. It was intended for my S&W Optics Ready MP15, which did not ship with iron sights.

On initial inspection the American offset BUIS looked like a great product. The overall fit and finish seemed nice, and it felt like a quality product. The sights easily installed and confidently locked onto the Picatinny rail with no problems.

The first thing I noticed was that the rear sight windage adjustment was too soft. In comparison, the factory rear indentation stops on my Colt AR15 is far superior, providing a nice, clean, solid stop between adjustments. Each click on the Colt inspires confidence. The American offset feels soft and mushy in comparison.

Another problem was the rear aperture adjustment. It was difficult going from the small aperture to the large. It would rock to the halfway point and then come to a firm stop. It required considerable effort to push it over to the full stop. Going back to the small aperture was not as much of a problem, but required a bit of an initial push to get it going. It is possible that with time (wear and tear) these two problems would have smoothed over.

I might have forgiven the above problems and kept the sights, but the final show stopper was the semi-glossy finish. It looked great, but at times I would get massive glare that interfered with obtaining a clear sight picture. When I held up my AR with a light source from the upper right, all I could see was glare from the lower left side of the cupped, small aperture. As such, I returned the sights for a refund.

product_title: TOUGH-GRID 750lb Paracord / Parachute Cord - Genuine Mil Spec Type IV 750lb Paracord Used by the US Military (MIl-C-5040-H) - 100% Nylon - Made In The USA.
review_headline: This is the paracord to buy!
review_body:
This paracord is fabricated to the MIL-C-5040H Type IV standard. Type IV paracord is required to have 11 3-ply inner core strands (including the marker strand) and is rated for a minimum break strength of 750 lbs at a minimum elongation of 30%. This cord for is typically used to rig cargo parachutes. Nominal weight is 165 feet of cord per pound.

Compare this to MIL-C-5040H Type III paracord which has 8 3-ply inner core strands (including the marker strand) and is rated for a minimum break strength of 550 lbs at a minimum elongation of 30%. This cord for is typically used to rig personnel parachutes. Nominal weight is 225 feet of cord per pound.

Compare this to the stuff being sold as ‘550 paracord’, well there is no comparison – this stuff should only be used to make decorative items, not for uses where breakage would be an issue. This cord is typically a thin non-conforming construction and made overseas as cheaply as possible. I posted a picture showing the TOUGH-GRID paracord vs some decent commercial 550 paracord. For pennies a foot more – you can get the TOUGH-GRID cord you can trust.

TOUGH-GRID sells the real MIL-C-5040H Type IV paracord, cut to length from large reels, coiled into tidy hanks, labeled and bagged. The paracord I received was top quality, snag free and matched the camo patterns shown. The cord holds knots well, but can still be readily untied. The orders are ‘fulfilled by Amazon’ – so quick shipping and the A-Z guarantee, you can’t beat this.

review_headline: Is not snug, will deteriorate over time
review_body:
I got this holster because frankly, it was cheap and seemed neat.

At first it fit the gun great, the clip can be moved on either side depending on what hand you are, and it feels comfortable inside the pant.

After maybe a month, the material got loose, and the gun started to be way to easy to slip in and out of the holster. The threading around the clip material started to thread, and looks like it won't last much longer.

DO NOT use this as a pocket holster like some other's out there that are. The way this is designed and the angle, it looks like it may fit fine in a pocket, and at first it does, but after walking it'll angle out and the gun or the entire holster will fall out. Trust me, my dumb self did that because I just needed to get to my garage for something really quick, and it fell out on the garage floor, thankfully I kept in safety and the thing didn't shoot my ankles.

All in all, it's a ok spare holster, but I would invest in something more durable and well made than this if you wanted to spend more money. For what I want to do with it, it works for now.

product_title: LUCID Red Dot
review_headline: GREAT RED DOT and AMERICAN MADE
review_body:
This is a true value and quality. I have purchased several different dots; some good, some not so good. This one was at the top of my price range but after several reviews both here on Amazon and elsewhere, decided to buy. I use this for target shooting and prairie dogs. That is it, no combat type training or anything like that. Range most of the time.

This is a rock solid unit. Nothing cheap about it. The size is just right to sit on my AR platform. I have it mounted towards the back of the rail because I have not purchased the magnifier yet. It is a very easy to use unit but recommend you take a few minutes to read the manual

The adjustments are different that other dots (at least what I have used) and first time around I didn't read and was adjusting the wrong way. (long story) I had thrown out the instructions and the good people at Lucid sent me a digital copy real quick. Up and going.

Once I dialed in the correct directions, 7 shots is all it took for ZERO at 25yds. I use the dot but there are several other options to choose from if you like. I did find as I switched from one visual to another, the difference on ZERO was minimal, probably more the shooter than the scope.

I did put the QD unit on this and like that much better. It puts the latches on the left side of the rifle rather than the right which is how the screws come.

The photocell is a nice feature and very sensitive. Shot in bright sun and showed box and it picked this up and made adjustment.

I also bought the FLASH KILL but have not really used it yet.

I thought shooting this "scope" design red dot might be more difficult since used to the block style. After about 10 rounds, I had no issues with being able to focus all around and through the lens.

I have Troy gas block BUS's and they are lower 1/3 for line up for those interested. I figure if my battery fails, just pop in a new one and go again. Nice to have though.o again. Nice to have though.

product_title: Texsport 14100 5/16 Tent Pole Replacement Kit
review_headline: Does the job: Eureka Wind River dome tent
review_body:
My thirty-year-old Eureka Wind River dome tent finally split a pole and I went to the Eureka website for a replacement. They had replacements available in the right diameter but the length was three inches shorter than the ones that support my tent, even though Eureka list the part specifically as a replacement for the Wind River. Though I like to use OEM parts whenever possible, I ordered this product through Amazon because it was the right length.
The poles arrived and they checked out with a caliper right at 7.9 mm and fit into the female end of the existing poles fine. The set includes four poles with ferrules, a coil of shock cord, various end pieces for different tents and a long piece of wire to thread the shock cord through the poles. The steel ferrules looked a bit chintzy and one wasn't glued to the end of the pole properly so I replaced it with the aluminum one from the original broken pole by sawing the old one off the pole with a hacksaw and drilling out the ferrule with a 5/16 twist drill. A little two-part epoxy and twenty four hours provided me with an almost exact replica of the original.
I camfered the raw Fiberglas end of the replacement with sandpaper at a 45 degree like the ones from Eureka and strung the new shock cord which was probably the hardest part of the whole project. The "needle" provided with the kit is next to useless in stringing the cord. I just fed the cord through the pole by hand and tied off the ends with a stevedore's knot.
Since the shock cord was made to stretch through the four poles in the replacement kit, it was short for the six-pole assembly I needed. I would recommend to anyone in the same situation to try using the old shock cord.

product_title: Speed Rope, Adjustable Ultra Speed Cable Jump Rope for Conquering Double Unders, 10 or 11 ft, Carrying Bag and EXTRA Cable || For Crossfit WODs, MMA, Boxing, Cardio Exercise and Fitness
review_body:
First off, this jump rope is great and terraFIT has the best customer service evar! They actually take customer feedback into account when designing/re-designing products!

Anyway, everything about this thing is small/svelte. The handles are small in diamter and very light, and the rope is a thin cable that is coated in plastic. The handles are an outer black plastic piece, with an inner white plastic piece that rotates and is connected to the rope. There is an adjustment in the handle to change how much movement/"play" there is between the two parts of the handle, and you want to double check that it is set loose enough for the inner white plastic piece to rotate freely.

The rope simply slides through eyelets at the ends of the handles and has two small metal stops that let you adjust the length of the rope, which you WILL need to do (it comes pretty long). They advise that once you have the rope length adjusted that you cut it to suit, so you don't have a bunch of extra rope swinging around.

The carrying case is a really nice touch.

All in all this is a fantastic jump rope that can achieve some crazy speeds because of how thing / light it is, VERY easy to spin it quick enough for double-unders. On the other hand the rope is so light that you pretty much cannot feel it swinging around you. IT IS VERY DIFFERENT THAN A ROPE BASED JUMP ROPE that you may have used in elementary school. A normal thick rope is easy to feel swinging around your body so you can pretty much feel when you should jump. WIth this TerraFit rope you MUST develop a rythym because you cannot tell where the rope is at very well. This is a skill that will take some time to develop if you aren't used to jumping rope a lot.
I read the reviews that said "not for beginners" and didn't understand what they meant, but it's the heft/weight of the rope that makes all the difference in the technique that you have to use. Once you get used to itthough it's great!

End of the day this rope is worth buying for 3 reason 1) you can spin it super fast 2) it comes with a spare rope 3) terrafit is an awesome company.

review_body: This is an excellent lightweight slicer. I use it as a neck knife and I don't even know it's there most of the time. review_body: This is the third Possum Hollow guide that I have for different rifles. I looked on the Possum Hollow web site to make sure that this guide would work for my 98 Mauser chambered for 7x57, or 7mm Mauser, before ordering. It arrived promptly after ordering and fit my rifle perfectly! It is precision machined out of Deldrin, a high grade chemical and solvent resistant plastic, and it slides into the bolt bore quite tightly. Like all of the Possum Hollow bore guides it does not come with a solvent port but you can order one from the company and it will slide right into the socket provided in the end of the guide. Personally I prefer this lack of a solvent port because this way I can drill in my own solvent port that lines up with ejection port of the rifle that I am using it on. This also gives me a hole to put a drift in to help pull the guide out of the chamber. It should also be noted that the chamber portion of the guide, with its silicone O-ring, fits very tightly into the chamber and because most chambers are tapered it can be very difficult to remove if you use a lot of force to jam it in place. The guide comes in a plastic tube, that is very useful for storage, and several spare O-rings.

product_title: Condor Rip-Away EMT Pouch
review_headline: You get what you pay for. Pretty Good.
review_body: I was looking for a "pouch" to put all my essential medical gear in, for my GOOD bag, survival bag,camping bag, EDC, whatever the hell you wanna call it. It looks exactly like it is advertised.It has plenty of compartments which i believe is very important when it comes to medical. I went with condor because 5:11, and black-hawk, didn't have what i considered a good medical pouch.They had no compartments, totally empty. This pouch is now attached to my 5:11 rush 12, fits great on the side, not too bulky or cumbersome. You should be able to fit all the BLS equipment you need. I can and i am a EMT(EMT/Firefighter). I plan on getting BLACKHAWK speed clips so that ill will be able to detach this within seconds from my rush 12. I love black-hawk and i love 5:11 because i honestly think they sell quality products, Maxpedition sells great products too i just think they are a tad over priced. Just my opinion. Everyone should expect poorer quality with condor, i am sorry but its the truth, that's why their prices are very reasonable. IT DOES NOT mean their products are crap. The stitching on this pouch seems OK, i don't foresee any problems with it BUT right when i got it one of the straps just came off, it was weird i don't know how it even happened. Might of been bad stitching, maybe it was already cut, to be honest i can't figure it out. All i gotta do is sew it back no biggy. Inside seems a tad cheap but it gets the job done,  the outside durability is just as good as any other top notch brand. The only other company that may have a pouch that outdoes this one for the things i was seeking is Maxpedition. Do your research i hoped this helped.  P.s. Just like you practice with guns, practice with your medical equipment and do your research, doesn't help to have it if you don't know what to do with it. Seconds are important and their are no redoes in an emergency.

review_body: I bought this as a nightguard to wear while i'm sleeping. I know it's for sport, etc, but my orthodontist recommended it. Well, it definitely does not work for that. It molds to my teeth and orthodontics (like it's supposed to) but how are my orthodontics supposed to work if this thing counteracts them and tries to push my teeth back into the molded position every time I wear it? Am I supposed to re-mold it every week so that it doesn't mess up my orthodontics? And even then, i'd still be messing up my ortho if I used it everyday. I'm sure this product works fine for people without ortho, but I bought it specifically because it's supposed to fit over my braces. Because it produces an air tight fit over them, it counteracts the entire purpose of braces (to align teeth), and thus is useless for me. It addition, once I put it on, it's really difficult to get off. I almost have to pry it from the back, fearing that I'm going to break my wire. If Shock Doctor wants to make a product that is truly exclusive to people with orthodontics instead of making a product that both people with and without orthodontics can wear, they should make a guard that has a wider inner channel that doesn't mold so tightly. I feel like I was a bit deceived by the advertising b/c this product is not for someone with braces unless you want to risk messing up your orthodontics. If I could return a used mouth guard, I would.

product_title: Gerber 31-001693 GDC Tch SknPckt Fn
review_body:
It is weird when a company decides to build something that is exactly what you are looking for.

Since a youth I've carried a pocket knife, this is the norm here in Louisiana. The only issue is that when using clip carry you can scratch sensitive items. If you decide to pocket carry, then you nick up cell phones, key fobs, etc.

A few weeks ago I started searching for a new EDC knife. Something that was "soft" and friendly in pockets. Strangely enough someone at Gerber of all places figured there was a demand for this. I'm not really a fan of Gerber, as I've always felt they relied heavily on celebrities like Bear Grylls to sell products.

However, I like to put my money where my mouth is. If someone builds the product that is just for me, then I'm willing to support it. If this knife does well, then some other brands may go for a knife that is "soft" with no hard edges exposed. Competition will lead to better products and better prices. The price was low enough for me to give it a shot.

Blade; I've not put many miles on the blade, but let me say that it is razor sharp. It comes with one of the sharpest edges I've seen someone sell a knife with. I think another thing that helps it be so sharp is the thin profile of the steel.

Lockup; There is some play in all directions, but this is to be expected for a small affordable gerber. It met my expectations here. Pressing the release and closing isn't something I can do one handed easily and safely. More on that later.

Size; The size is a very good compromise between usable and tiny. There is enough handle to get and adequate grip. Any less and for me it would be very difficult to use.

Deployment; This is the only area that I think could be improved. Due to the deep pocket carry this was designed for, they use a closing spring that is VERY strong. There is a lot of resistance when trying to open the blade. This prevents you from having an open knife in your pants. It also makes deployment a bit difficult one handed.

I'll be honest here. This is the first time I've really "injured" myself on a folder. Trying to one hand open the little guy I ended up rolling my thumb up and into the blade as it slightly opened. Humbling moment there! Before I knew it, I was bleeding.

Currently I'm using two hands to deploy this knife. Which is perfectly fine for what I want this blade for, utility purposes. I didn't buy this as some quick deployment folding fighting knife.

Summary; I like this knife. It meets my expectations. Basically it is a knife for the sake of having a knife. Doesn't do anything exceptionally well, aside from pocket carry. There are plenty of better knives, but none that I have found as pocket friendly.

review_headline: Great training product that lasted about 2.5 years.
review_body:
Would definitely recommend this product to anyone who wants to improve trigger pull and tighten groups -- hitting the target. I used this in my Sig SP 2022 (9mm) and Glock 34 for two and a half years. Likely shot 100 to 200 shots per month. You can move through the house practicing and instantly see if where you thought your sights were was the actual point of impact by seeing where the laser dot lands. Easy way to improve accuracy with the actual guns you will be firing.

The only reason it did not get 4 stars was because it suddenly stopped working properly. It only now shots a dot when I unscrew the lid to change batteries. As I unscrew the lid the laser will momentarily flicker on. When the lid is screwed down tight, it will not activate with trigger pull or when the activator is pushed down with pen. The impact pad where the pin hits is a bit dented. What most likely happened was that over time the impact of the pin loosened or damage some small electrical components inside.

I plan on purchasing another. It is a great tool for sharpening accuracy in the convenience of the home and without spending a lot of money on ammo.

product_title: Spyderco Delica4 Lightweight FRN Flat Ground PlainEdge Knife
review_body:
This is the 3rd Delica I ordered - this one as a birthday present for our son who is in Cub Scouts and recently got his Whittling Chip.

The Delica - especially this version fulfills a couple of basic requirements I have for knives:

- the locking mechanism is solid - once the blade locks open, it stays open. If one accidentally hits the back of the blade, it will not fold back. On the other hand, a closed blade will stay closed - the lock puts enough spring force on the closed blade that it will not accidentally deploy - had that happen with an older Cold Steel AK-47 knife and it was not pretty.
- The blade holds a good edge and can easily be re-sharpened. Having the full flat grind helps with the cutting ability of the blade.
- The grip has an excellent texture pattern. Even with wet hands one has enough purchase to establish a firm and positive grip.
- the clip is highly reliable and can be adjusted four ways (tip up/down, left/right hand carry).

I've been using my own Delica four about five years and it is still my go-to knife. The one that I just purchased will last my son for a long time - hopefully well beyond his time in Scouting.

product_title: Maxpedition Fatboy G.T.G. Versipack
review_headline: Good concealed carry option for backpacking
review_body:
I've been trying to figure out a good concealed carry option for backpacking, and I think this is going to work. Wearing a large backpack with a weight-bearing belt takes away the most common options for concealed carry. I looked at chest pouches and leg pouches and decided to give this one a try. I'll carry a subcompact G27 so considered getting the smaller Versipack Thermite, but I'm glad that I got the Fatboy for the extra room. The G27 fits just about right in the Fatboy pouch with a little room to get your hand in and draw. I wouldn't want to try to retrieve the gun from anything smaller.

It looks and feels like good quality construction, and I like the overall look. The extra pouches make it look enough like a typical hiking pack that I don't think it screams out "gun." I also like the way that my large water bottles fit in the water bottle pouch. As others have said, the "phone" pouch seems to have dimensions more suited to carry extra magazines than a smartphone, but there are enough pouches to carry a phone and a decent amount of other gear. It looks like it was made primarily to throw over your shoulder, and I didn't find a leg strap in it, but the shoulder strap seems to do ok as a waist strap, and it generally feels comfortable there. I like the look, the construction, the good job of concealment, the ease of drawing, and the overall functionality of this pack.

product_title: Kershaw 3850 Swerve Folding Knife
review_headline: Exactly what I was looking for.
review_body:
I've owned a total of 6 Kershaw knives in the past. This is my 2nd favorite next to the Scallion model. I wanted a solid, mid-size, one touch pocket knife. This delivers wonderfully. I simply don't see another Kershaw quality knife comparing to this one with a price-point anywhere near it.

Pros:
-The blade is very durable and the hinge is tight and strong. I experienced zero issues with any 'wobble' or looseness as described in other reviews.

-The textured grip works well. The only improvement over the current grip would be if it were rubberized, and that is simply not my choice being the wear that occurs on rubber grips.

-The assisted opening works perfectly. I am not a fan of using the 'thumb nub' to operate my knives. It is such an odd angle to swing that it becomes difficult. The small lever on the back side of the blade works great here. I've read that some people were complaining that the speed was slower than other knives. Being the blade is so much heavier, this is understandable. However, saying a knife falls short for mere milliseconds in opening time from other models is hardly a valid complaint in my mind.

Cons:
-There is no blade lock on the knife. I found it to be a nice touch on the Scallion model since the knife opens with such ease. I can't see this posing the problem I would initially imagine, however, being that it has yet to open accidentally on me to this point.

The item that I placed an order for read: HCO Outdoor Products NightXplorer Programmable Resolution Trail Camera, Camo w/ Delay UWY-NX50, and Protective Metal Camera Cover.

product_title: Horizon Fitness EX-59-02 Elliptical Trainer
review_body:
I bought the Horizon Fitness Elliptical Trainer after reading mostly positive reviews on Amazon. However, the machine did not live up to expectations. Below I detail my 2 main complaints, and then provide some additional comments.

Con #1: The elliptical makes a knocking noise on each revolution. It is loud, and also I can feel a bump with each stride. I called tech support. They were fairly helpful. After going through some basic troubleshooting, they told me they would send some replacement parts and a technician would come out to make a repair. Despite promising the spare parts in 2 days, they sent the package UPS SurePost, which took 6 business days to arrive. The technician arrived on time, and quickly diagnosed that the wheel was the problem. He replaced the wheel, but now there was a knocking sound on the other side. He told me I would need a new wheel and even ordered it for me. A few days later, the knocking sound returned worse than ever, on BOTH sides.

Con #2: The heart rate monitor is awful. It consistently displays incorrect values, by up to 50 BPM. Often when I grasp the heart rate handlebars, it takes up to 2 minutes for the correct heart to "lock in". In the time before the correct rate locks in, it just seems to guess, by counting by 1 upwards or downwards. For example, I will grab the handlebar...and 85 comes up. Then 86, 87, 88, 89. Keeps thinking. A minute or two later...145. Finally. The issue is that it takes too long for the correct heart rate to display, and that it shows bogus heart rates in the meantime.

Other issues that users have commented on.
1) The elliptical does not have a fan (consistent with item description).
2) I like that there is an auxiliary cord to plug in an iPod. The speakers are not very good, but it is still a cool feature.
3) The water bottle holder is placed really low on the machine, making it unreachable for a lot of people. I am able to reach the water bottle by tucking in my shoulder, crouching down, and grabbing the bottle, all while continuing to pedal. Not the most comfortable thing, but once you do it, it's not that big of a deal.
4) There are 10 resistance levels. The difference between each level is significant. I find that I spend a lot of time on level 1, with shorter bursts of level 2 or 3. Maybe every machine is different in this respect. This isn't really a complaint as I would not expect a low- to mid-level home machine to have the same pinpoint control of resistance as a gym-quality machine would.
5) There are plenty of different workout options to choose from, providing a fun experience trying them all out.
6) Setup was pretty straightforward, taking me about 2 hours. I suspect someone who is more handy could assemble it in 30 minutes.
7) The box was extremely heavy, and I had to carry a couple pieces inside at a time. The main component at the base with the flywheel inside was particularly heavy...probably about 40 pounds.

If Horizon Fitness is ever able to get the knocking resolved, I will upgrade to 4 stars. The 5th star would come from fixing the poor heart rate monitor design, but that is unlikely to be fixed.

It has the hook and eye closures in the back so that I don't feel like I'm trying to squeeze a walrus into sweat sock.  It is thicker than a typical, but not quite padded bra.  I took one star off because the hooks have bent a little after 6 months of use.

review_headline: Four Seasons Store sent me the wrong knife (and then sent me the right one)
review_body:

Also, the knife itself appears to be pretty decent although I think the lockup is a little unsafe and could possibly become disengaged if handled the wrong way. However, they sent me the wrong knife so this purchase has been a major disappointment. Hopefully their return and replace procedure goes a little better.

UPDATE: Four Seasons shipped out the correct knife within a day after I notified them of the mistake and sent me the following message, \\"Thank you for contacting us. We apologize for the mistake. Here is the tracking number [...] by usps. As for the wrong knife. Please keep it.\\"

That's pretty good customer service so I'm increasing my rating from 1 star to 4 since the knife is actually pretty good, especially for the money.

review_body: I am really skeptical about things I see on TV like this.  But swimsuit season is coming up so I thought it couldn't hurt to try it.  Also, I had a baby about 4 months ago and really need to start working on my mid section.  Let me tell you that after using this thing only twice I can feel the burn all over my upper body (all sides of my arms, my chest, etc).  I struggle to find workouts that work those areas well and this did a great job in just a couple of minutes.  I will say that I'm not feeling a whole lot in my abs just yet.  I'm going to work on my technique (you will see in the instructions that it's about quality and not quantity) but I'm confident I'll feel more...especially as I work up my number of reps. review_headline: Can't beat it for the price
review_body:

Unfortunately, the design and safety features of typical pistol cases have not changed much in that time.

However, the SINGLE PISTOL CASE FROM PREMIUM TACTICAL SUPPLY is not a typical pistol case. This gun case has been specifically designed so that once it is shut and locked it cannot be opened without using tools. The inside of the case contains a foam interior and the case is TSA compliant. Also, in terms of design the SINGLE PISTOL CASE FROM PREMIUM TACTICAL SUPPLY is a huge improvement over other pistol cases I have seen because of its size. Other pistol cases I have seen are somewhat bulky and cumbersome for the weapon they carry. For example, the case I played with as a kid was about the size of briefcase and most single pistol cases today are about 11.5-12 inches long and about 7.5-8 inches wide. The SINGLE PISTOL CASE FROM PREMIUM TACTICAL SUPPLY is smaller being 10.2 inches long and 7 inches wide. The size difference might not seem like much, but it makes a huge difference.

Although I am not currently a gun owner if I ever purchased a small firearm, I would probably purchase the SINGLE PISTOL CASE FROM PREMIUM TACTICAL SUPPLY to keep my weapon in for transport. Also, if any of my friends or family members who are pistol owners ever need a gun case, I will suggest they buy the SINGLE PISTOL CASE FROM PREMIUM TACTICAL SUPPLY. product_title: THE NORTH FACE SURGE DAYPACK
review_headline: I tried so hard to love this backpack...
review_body:
I carried a messenger bag for work for about a year and just got tired of the setup. Missed having a backpack so I did a ton of research and then went to REI and tried on a bunch. I finally settled on either TNF Recon or Surge II, and bought the Surge II. It's a really nice pack, and here are my thoughts:

LIKES:
- Great construction
- Lots of thoughtfully designed compartments
- Comfortable shoulder straps
- Looks sharp (not a lot of mesh, so a professional could tote this thing around...maybe. read on)
- Good padding for laptop/tablet
- Easy-to-store waist belt
- Sternum strap with elastic
- Great padding on the back
- Love the small, bottom compartment for a power supply (fits the one for my MBP perfectly!)

MEH...
- BIG North Face Logo. For over $100 I'd rather not be forced to advertise for you. A small, subdued logo maybe?
- Laptop pocket doesn't open 180* like the other pockets. Huh?
- Adjustment straps are looooong, with no way to gather them up. So they just blow in the breeze. Not great.
- Big metal zipper pulls that kind of clank together
- \\"Water bottle pocket\\" is almost not big enough. It's almost better suited for storage of something else. How hard is it to do a proper bottle pocket?

NO BUENO:
- Top grab handle is about as thin as a shoelace. Seriously. I don't think it'll break but it sure isn't comfortable.
- Did I mention the long adjustment straps?
- Not enough top-level storage dividers. The bag is very tall and everything just goes to the bottom
- Non-removable sternum straps. :(

Most of my complaints about the bag are subjective, but two design points I think are abject failures. The first is the grab handle. That's just stupid on a bag like this. The second design failure is the sternum strap. It's functional and adjustable but not removable. UNLESS, like me, you take a pair of pliers and literally pry them off the nylon-covered plastic tube they slide up and down on. That's a HUGE pain in the rear, and what proved even more problematic was putting them back on. Took me almost 30 minutes and it proved almost impossible. For most people you will leave the strap on, or pry it off and leave it off, but on principal alone this shows a design failure. It would have been SOOOO easy to design this strap to come on and off simply. But this is from the company that makes you wear their giant white-on-black logo, so they must know better than you about this strap.

As you can see there are far more pros than cons. Don't get me wrong- this is a good pack. At the end of the day, though, for me it was just a little bit too big to be an everyday bag. The biggest con for me was the fact that everything gravitated (ha) to the bottom of the bag. Which wasn't horrible, but you're carrying a bag with a bunch of empty space at the top...why not just have a smaller bag? Example: My 13\\" MBP was absolutely swallowed up in the laptop compartment. I think you could have put a 19\\" TV in there.

I wish there was a TNF bag the size of the Recon with the looks and the features of the Surge II. Ultimately I returned this bag and went with a 5.11 Rush12. product_title: Kershaw 1770 OD-2 Knife
review_headline: Nice little knife, but maybe too small
review_body:
First, excellent craftsmanship, fit and finish perfect.
Second, I nearly draw blood ... mine ... every time I use this little fun blade.

I like the opening mechanism, my friends to whom I showed the knife when it arrived from Amazon all find it too hard to open. So out of 5 people, 4 did not like the design

When operating the unique flipper I find my hands (which are a large glove size) move into vulnerable blade reachable positions. The same can be said for closing. The diminutive size and novelty of the action just work together in a way that has me looking to see if I just scraped deep enough that I will start to stain the furniture if I don't dress my latest negligent episode.

The blade shape is rather strait without much of a belly, very similar to the Kershaw Leek, so with the blade shape combined with the diminutive size, the OD-2 is only really suited to light tasks.

It is fun, if not a little dangerous in bigger hands. It is sharp and well suited to more polite tasks, Removing a thread, paring one's nails, opening a letter are all suitable jobs.

I have no complaints about the blade steel, action, or workmanship. It is a novelty and does not fit a real functional niche. I never find myself carrying just this knife, it is more of a toy than a tool .. maybe it is this mindset that leads me to come so close to bleeding all the time. It has traveled with me every day since it arrived, I would not replace it if I lost it, but I do not regret making the purchase. If you are looking for a fun little blade this won't disappoint, if you are looking for a little workhorse it will.

Honestly, I am not loyal to any particular brands, but if you are looking at buying a hub style house, buy something other than Frabill. product_title: Vortex® StrikeFire Red Dot Rifle Scope(Suitable for AR-15)
review_body:
I got this optic to mount on my CMMG .22LR conversion upper. My primary goal was a low cost optic for the rimfire upper, since I already shelled out for an EOTech for my centerfire upper. What I didn't know was this was low cost, with almost high cost quality. Or in other words: one really gets the most bang for their buck with a Vortex Strikefire.

Pros
- Lifetime warranty. I have yet to avail myself to it, nor have I heard many instances of people needing it, but it's nice to have it there, and that the company stands by their products
- All mounting equipment included. It comes with the standard 1in riser for mounting on a flattop upper. Other heights are available. I got a cantilever mount additionally.
- Nightvision mode. I don't have any quality NVGs to use with this, but it's cool? What it does is it dims the dot down for use with NODs.
- Red/Green dot. I got this because my brother is red/green colorblind and I wanted to see what optics would work for him before he mounted one to his rifle, especially cheaper ones. This was one of the primary features I got this optic for. If it works for him, I'll let him use this one, and try out the SPARC.
- 2x Magnifier. It's nice to have it?
- Good brightness

Cons
- 2x Magnifier? It's not really enough to be useful, and one has to remove the cover for the eyepiece (or whatever the correct term is). It also narrows the field of view (as expected) and shortens the eye relief on the optic. I found that I would have to shift my optic back one or two notches on the upper rail to get good field of view with the magnifier. It might be better to simply not use it.
- As others have noted, it's easy to bump the NV button. Actually, all buttons are in a position for them to be easily bumped.

I like this optic. It's a good price, and good quality. There are plenty of reviews online that likewise tout the strengths and weaknesses of this optic. I've seen it be mounted to centerfire uppers that generate much more shock than a .22LR, so I know it'll hold up very well for my usage.

product_title: LifeSpan TR1200-DT3 Under Desk Treadmill
review_headline: Upgraded after 5yrs at a standing desk...
review_body:
I've been using standing desks for about 5 years and I finally decided to bite the bullet and get a new desk and treadmill. I picked up a an Edison table from VersaTables and a LifeSpan TR1200-DT3. The desk is fantastic with the treadmill after you remove the cable tray down at the foot of the desk. I was planning on purchasing a GeekDesk but the monitor stands, cable management, and under-the-desk CPU holder were decisive features for me and helped me conceal loose cables.

Here are a list of things learned or questions that I've now answered:

*) The reason I decided to get a treadmill was because my legs and back would ache after a full day of standing. I'm a fit individual, but the stiffness... ugh. I prefer the ache from a good run or some exertion, not standing. Anyway, I finally bit the bullet after pining over a standing desk/treadmill for a few years. When I finally ordered the treadmill I assumed I'd walk at 1.0mph or something reasonably slow so that I could program and/or type with a low error rate. Well, after about four days I settled on 2.0mph because at 1.0mph I find my head moves forward and backward in a rocking motion in order to keep my gaze steady on the monitors. At 2.0mph it's much more natural and I don't have this feeling like I just climbed out of a small boat in choppy water. With time I think I might creep a bit above 2.0mph for the bulk of the day. This surprised me in a very pleasant way.

*) I'm a work-from-home dad who does programming and administration with a toddler running around. I called LifeSpan to ask if there was a way to disable resuming at 0.4mph and it turns out there is. This is huge because last time I almost pulled the trigger on a treadmill was a year ago and back then it wouldn't have been possible. Here's what I learned: Enter "Engineering Mode" by pushing "Stop + Up Arrow" for three seconds and cycle through to option F019 and change the setting from "0" to "1" and you should be good to go. Note, if you're an old user of the model this option doesn't exist. In talking with the sales rep at LifeSpan they added this feature around mid-2013. With the toddler near, it was going to be a deal-breaker if I had to constantly mash the Up Arrow every time I had to step off and tend to ___fill in the blank crisis___.

*) This is important (and obvious) to parents: the treadmill belt is not much different than a belt sander. Put a locked gate up around your treadmill and keep the fingers out. There is a gap to the left of the belt that is about 1 pinky wide for infants (at least on my unit) and I did have a close encounter the day after I set mine up: nice little abrasion and scab. I don't fault the treadmill for this, it was clearly a dumbshit parent moment when I stepped on and didn't fully lock the gate behind me (and oddly enough, he hasn't shown much interest in the treadmill since). Anyway, a bit of caution - I'm pretty diligent as a parent and this spooked me how quick that happened. If applicable, consider yourself warned.

*) Barefoot. Definitely walk barefoot and not in shoes... or socks if it's cold and you know you're going to be standing for an extended period of time on the belt. I switch to socks because my feet will start to perspire on the belt (it doesn't breath terribly well). Under no circumstances do I recommend using shoes, however. If it's a work environment, use Luna Sandals or something, but if you're going to the trouble of walking while working, you probably care about your arches and the worst thing you could do for yourself is put arch supports under your feet while walking. Read "Born to Run: A Hidden Tribe, Superathletes, and the Greatest Race the World Has Never Seen" if you want an introduction. I have a 0.5" difference in my leg lengths due to an ancient skiing injury and haven't had any issues running barefoot (last 8 years) or walking barefoot. Anyway, barefoot.

*) I didn't see this one coming, but it completely makes sense: my abs were tight and sore for the first few weeks. It makes sense, but I didn't expect that transitioning from a standing desk to a treadmill would result in much, if any, physical discomfort or new aches, etc. Well, my abs. They ached for a while, and in a good way. The reason is pretty simple: my head needs to be stable in order to see what's on the screen, it's your core that stabilizes your upper torso. Anyway, this was something I didn't expect but I appreciated at the time.

*) And lastly, this is for the guys: don't do boxers. I'm not kidding. Briefs? Yes. Boxer briefs? Yes. Boxers? Only if you're a masochist. After a few days I finally changed things around and am happy I did so. I walk to the store frequently or frequently go on day hikes using boxers, but ended up falling back to any form of brief. It's not the same as running in boxers, the slower motion of walking... catches differently. This isn't a hard lesson to learn or figure out on your own, but it wasn't something I saw anyone comment on when I was getting ready to purchase so I figure why not be fully transparent.

*) And lastly,the unit arrived with a bum console that required me to flick the power on and off repeatedly to get the unit to initialize correctly. I called LifeSpan and they did send me a replacement that arrived within two days and I've had no troubles since.

... I think that just about does it. I'm averaging around 15mi per day right now and am very pleased. In hindsight I'm ticked I didn't do this earlier, but the F019 option wasn't available earlier, so earlier would've been maddening. First world problems of the world unite? Good luck in your stationary travels.

product_title: Firefield Laser Boresight
review_headline: Gets stuck in barrel if not used properly, no switch
review_body:
The sight is okay from a technical standpoint. It's accurate and bright. One problem is that it runs out of batteries after an hour and there is no on/off switch. In order to turn the laser off, you have to physically remove the batteries or turn the cap just enough that there is no solid contact. I was able to keep it off with the cap screwed in by turning it to a certain point, but any pressure on the cap or impact would turn it on.

The sizing of the actual case is also not the best, so it tends to get stuck in the barrel. I was sighting the rifle by keeping the bcg locked (I was testing with an AR15) and accidentally hit the bolt release, which the boresight did not like. It took me about 10 minutes of stepping on the charging handle to dislodge it, even with an abundance of lubricant. This permanently chipped the front of the sight in such a way that it will not fit in the barrel without getting stuck there, even without the bolt behind it. Consider removing the bolt when sighting this to avoid the same fate.

product_title: Daisy Outdoor Products Single Pump Target Pistol (Brown/Black, 13.5 Inch)
review_body:
I spent a lot of time researching .177 pellet pistols before I bought this one. My priority was "accuracy". I didn't care about fps, power, distance, 'cool factor' or any of that. I was not looking to kill anything (although I'm not opposed to reducing the rat population if the situation arises). I live on a lake and am just interested in plinking, target shooting, and hitting tiny pieces of floating debris as it flows downstream. I have handled "real" guns all of my life. I don't like to use scopes (unless shooting extremely long distances--1/4 to 1 mile). So with all that said, this Daisy 717 Powerline exceeded my expectations for a $150 production pellet pistol. Once I adjusted the sights and trigger to my liking I was able to hit very small targets within 25 yards. At Match competition distance (10 Meters) this pistol shoots extremely tight groups (with the occasional expected "flyer"). My pellets were mostly Crossman lead Competition Wadcutters ($7.99 for 500) or Daisy non-lead alloy flat heads ($11.99 for 500); neither one anything particularly fancy. I tried many other types including Meisterculgen Match pellets, but found no discernible difference for the higher cost. In addition, I wasn't happy with the bolt sticking a little about every 5 shots or so, causing me to eMail Daisy company. They immediately sent me a free FedEx return mailing sticker, did the bolt adjustment no-charge and returned the pistol in excellent working condition. The moral: buy American from a reputable American old-time arms manufacturer.
Also, this pistol is a pneumatic pump, i.e. there is no spring, it is not a "springer" like almost ALL the other non-CO2 pistols out there. This is important. I also purchased a Balkai IZH53M ($70+shipping) Russian made pistol that IS a springer; I heard they were also accurate. They are similar to the Benjamins and the other Chinese made pistols. The comparison=there is none! The Daisy, although a little more expensive is a much better, easier to cock, sight and shoot, and way more accurate.
Note--with either of the guns I use (and really like) the Gamo self-resetting metal targets, the Gamo paper target holder metal box and their cardboard targets, and the Stoeger spinning red metal target. At 10 meters (30 feet) they are challenging and fun. I have heard that the rifles with the higher fps will dent these targets, but the Daisy Powerline and Balkai pistols will not. Hope that helps.

product_title: 5.11 Tactical Covrt18 Backpack
review_body:
I've had this bag for about a month and I am loving it so far. There are a ton of pockets and I am surprised that I am finding uses for all of them. It offers quick access to a ton of stuff. It looks great, not tactical, but also doesn't look like a bag for a high school student. The zippers work fantastic. Like a lot of people, I wish it had a waist strap. It could be a bit lighter, there is probably twice as much padding as needed on the back, the straps, and laptop sleeve. But it is very comfortable when loaded heavy. The green color is best, looks better in person and is not too bright.

I use the bag while traveling and when biking to work every day. It is really too big and heavy for a hiking day pack, and its too small for a tent and sleeping bag for overnight backpacking. But its great for all other occasions. I think it will be perfect for doing touristy stuff during my upcoming trip to Europe. It has a concealed carry compartment thats made for quick access to a pistol, I use it for quick access to my binoculars or camera.

The only real criticism I have is about "QuickTact accessory straps." They are these big heavy duty velcro strips on the shoulder straps. They are completely useless to everyone. I guess they sell a cell phone case that you could velcro to your shoulder but I can't imagine why anyone would want to do that. I assume they will come out with more accessories for these straps, probably for holding ammo mags, but I won't be needing them.

review_headline: Nice supported and warm elbow, but miracles don't happen
review_body: I purchase Evoshield arm sleeve after some issues with great fatigue on my  right hand's elbow and bicep. I have a feeling of pain really strong, which means I couldn't throw a baseball two days in the row. Wearing sleeve makes everything better. My hand from forearm to bicep is warm and muscles stay tight, meaning supported to avoid hurting in great extensions, like passes. I can't say the pain is gone completely, this would be a miracle! But in my point of view, people, who have fatigue like me, have to follow a specific routine to avoid injuring. First of all, apply some counter-pain cream (pain reliever, heating, analgetic cream) in your hand and wear the sleeve. Secondly run 1-2 times around the field and then have a good stretching. You hand muscles would be warm and loose and also supported from sleeve tightness. Apply pressure but don't overdo anything if you start to feel fatigue. When you're done with practice do some stretching and after having bath apply some counter-pain again. Enjoy the game!

product_title: Guard Dog Diablo Tactical Stun Gun Flashlight, Maximum Voltage,160 Lumens w/ Three Settings
review_headline: The first one broke within a month
review_body:
My girlfriend and I go for walks at night so I bought this combo flashlight and stun gun to carry in case we need light (obviously) or to fend off any angry dogs or other rabid beasts. One night we actually did have a dog come running at us barking and growling, which was quite frightening, but all I had to do was press the stun button once and the sound alone scared the dog away. I'm glad too because I would hate to actually have to use the stun gun on anyone or anything.

The problem is that after about a month or so the unit started to malfunction, the flashlight would flicker, and then the stun gun stopped working altogether. I contacted Guard Dog for warranty support and they asked me send it to them for repair ($8 to ship). After over a month of not hearing anything or receiving a replacement I contacted support again and they told me they have been backlogged on returns going back to Nov (it was Jan). In my case maybe the squeaky wheel got the grease because I was also told that my return was being processed that day and the original unit was deemed defective and they would be sending me a new unit.

About a week later I received a box containing 2 batteries, but no flashlight? I think this was an error in the shipping dept. because on the invoice it had somebody else's name. (Some poor guy didn't get his batteries) Then several days after that I received the replacement flashlight. I have had the new unit for about a month now and so far it is working just fine. I will update my review if things change.

Maybe I was unlucky and got a rare defective unit, OK things happen, but after the return process was horribly slow and the shipping error occurred I now have some concerns about this company and it's product. Overall this flashlight has pretty good reviews on Amazon, which is why I bought it in the first place. However this was my experience, and frankly 3 stars is generous.

review_body: First off, I have plenty of experience in the area of mouthpieces; i've been wearing mouthpieces for contact sports for about 25 years. And after meticulously following the instructions, the first attempt to mold this Brain-Pad never even made it into my mouth before my fingers curled the gum guards. On the third attempt, I got it in my mouth and bit down... After pulling it out and examining it, one of the gel pads had shifted, it was only halfway between my teeth and both outer edges were too far away from my molars. Think of it as the difference between a "U" shape and a "V" shape. So on the fourth attempt I get it mostly right. (Though I never got that gel pad to recenter) Except that upon closer inspection, I bit through the front of the mouthpiece, top and bottom, and that off center gel pad, had a pocket inside the mouthpiece. A pocket filled with water or saliva that when the mouthpiece was squeezed or manipulated it would ooze out. I thought to myself, "now that isn't very hygienic." product_title: Ultra Paws Rugged Dog Boot
review_body:
My 100 lb. lab drags his back paws and wears his pads down. He got to the point that he would lay down in the street rather than walk. These shoes saved him.

He took to them immediately (back paws only) and has not hesitated to walk his daily 3 miles since, We only use them on his back paws & so rotate the pairs to get extra wear out of them. The set lasted about 45 days even using two tubes of shoe goo for repairs. I recommend that you coat the toe and first inch or two of the bottom with ShoeGoo before you take them out. This is really critical if your pup drags his or her toes. The material will wear through on asphalt rather quickly without it. We live in Tahoe and these are ok in snow and lack traction on ice.

When the bottoms finally developed holes that could no longer be plugged with goo, I cut the soles off some old minimalist running shoes. I cut them to size and glued them onto these shoes with the Goo. They haven't seemed to bother him and now he has a more durable sole with a tread.

review_headline: Use this with a Burris Fullfield 2 Model Scope 3-9x40mm Optic
review_body:

Make sure you coat the bottom with blue loctite and it is free from oil / grease before mounting on top of your rifle's receiver. Put a dab on your mounting bolts and it will set after you tighten it down to create a solid "zero" movement mount that is engineered right without any inconsistency in optic alignment. For your scope ring screws- coat the threads with clear nail polish so if you have to remove the optic- you can but at the same time- no bolt will "wiggle" loose under any recoil. It works wonderfully and keeps things simple.

Cons: none- Cons would be if you didn't buy it and went with a cheap two piece mount.

Bottom LIne: to achive optimal accuracy- you need a solid foundation for your optic. This with some blue loctite and clear nail polish is the best solution to achieve small groups from your hunting rifle- cost effective approach.

4. The door attachment is secure and when in place mimics the same movements of machines that you would find at a gym

The illustrated (photos) exercise chart is a very large poster. If you have a dedicated room in your home for working out, just post it and you are set. I workout in my living room so this would not be very attractive...so I cut it into sections and laminated them. This has worked well for me and it is easier to travel with chart.
