product_title: SKLZ Air Station - Sports Equipment Dryer System
review_headline: Does a nice job of drying clothing but for this price I'd want a heating element option
review_body:
[[VIDEOID:mo1S4QKO8697Z8V]]We have an active family that loves to hike, an activity that can often get our clothes wet, especially in these winter days of melting ice and snow. When you come home with wet boots and shoes, you don't want to put them in the dryer because that can ruin them (and the dryer) but you don't want to wait for them to air dry. The Sports Dryer System seemed like a great option, especially because it's also good for wet helmets, padding, skates, etc. Assembly was simple - four screws with the included wrench hold the bottom onto the tub, and the rest just snaps into place.

The dryer itself is rather large - it is essentially a large plastic tube with a fan at the bottom that blows out air. There are 8 pegs with air vents inside of them with a top peg for a helmet. Each peg/arm doesn't have a fan - there is just 1 fan for the whole unit. The fan is powered by an small AC adapter. A simple \\"on\\" button allows you to pick 1, 3, or 6 hour run time.

So how does it work? Well, first thing I noticed is that it is REALLY LOUD! I mean, so loud my wife made me turn it off because it was bothering the whole family. Second, there is no speed control to make it softer. Third, it does dry the shoes faster than leaving them out, but why not have some sort of heating element just to dry the air a bit? This is literally just a fan. Fourth, I noticed the AC adapter got really hot. I'm a bit concerned it is undersized for the load of the fan.

Do I recommend it? For $20 you can get a box fan and point it at your clothing until it dries. For $200, this is a solution looking for a problem. If it was a bit quieter or had some source of heat, I might consider it. But I really can't recommend it. See my video to hear how noisy it is.

product_title: Caldwell XLA Pivot Model Bipod
review_body: This is a rock solid bipod.  It gives you the stability you need to make the long shots with confidence. I have typically used Harris bipods in the past.  At less than half the price, I gave this one a chance.  So far it seems every bit as good with one bonus over the Harris models I have used.  The legs pivot which means no more picking the whole thing up to re-position if your intended target moves to the side.  I use it for coyote hunting which means it gets a lot of use on every outing.  I have taken it out seven or eight times  in the two weeks I have had it and have had no problems whatsoever. My rifle is a tad under 13 pounds.  This bipod has no problem with the weight.  I used it on a night hunt and had no problems setting it up in the dark.  I'm  6'4" and it is a little tall for me if it is fully extended. The segmented rings around the lower leg make it easy to get the length right every time by simply feeling how many rings are protruding past the upper segment of the leg.  This is a big plus at night when its dark. If you are looking for a quality bipod at an affordable price, this seems to be a great option.  If I encounter any problems, I will update this review.  UPDATE:  I have been using this bipod for about two years now.  I am still very happy with it.  Most of the use has been with a .223 Rem, but I have also used it with a .300 Win Mag.  I haven't fired a lot of .300 win mag rounds while using it, but it has held up to the recoil just fine so far.

review_headline: MIR 140 lbs PRO Adjustable Weighted VEST Review
review_body:
I love this vest. It has helped me to build muscles and to firm up. I use up to 50lbs so far but it is good to know that as I get stronger I can increase it at my own pace. Or if I am not up to using it at 50lbs I can decrease it.

The problem I have with the vest which is why I only gave it a 4 rating is that it digs into your shoulders which after a period of time can be painful. I have made my own pads to go under the vest to reduce the cutting in effect but it is still painful if you walk around or jog with if for 1-2 hours.

If you have wider shoulders it should be fine but I don't so it digs in right on the nerve. Also it is rather pricey. If you can find it cheaper go for it! If several people in the household do weight training then it is versatile for everyone to use at their own ideal weight level. Just not at the same time.

I recommend this vest but but it may cause pain in the shoulders and by the neck if used for long periods of time without padding to help reduce the effect![[ASIN:B002SLSUF6 MIR® - 140LBS PRO (LONG STYLE) ADJUSTABLE WEIGHTED VEST]]

review_body: I have 3 SKS rifles that have never been issued with wood stocks in pristine condition. I want to shoot them so I thought I would get some synthetic stocks to save wear and tear on the wooden ones. These came up on Amazon and had an excellent price point so I thought I'd buy 2. I don't know what kind of plastic they are made from. Looks like ABS so if it is then they should be fairly break proof. Quality looks good for Made in China. Typical out of the box Chinese deficiencies -  one of the metric nuts used to secure the butt to the fore-end didn't have a thread so I had to tap a thread. I had not much trouble installing them. Some tuck points needed a bit of filing. Instructions were clear and complete. I put them on a Russian and a Chinese SKS. Both went on the same. I had trouble installing the trigger group back in on both rifles. It seemed to be very hard to snap them back into place like something was in the way but I never could figure out what it was. They will snap in but with a lot more pressure needed than if the original wood stocks were used. Top and bottom Picatinny rails are nice on the fore-grip and handy for different sling configurations. I would have liked to see a groove in the bottom rail to accommodate the bayonet so it doesn't have to come off. I cut a groove allowance in the bottom rail on a router table to accommodate the bayonet when folded. The 3 position collapsible stock is excellent to adjust for different shooters. All in all great for the price.

product_title: BackBridge By Dr. Sinett
review_body:
Several years ago, I started experiencing sharp pains in my neck and lower back that got worse over time. Some days it was difficult to walk or even move my head. I saw a couple of doctors and they gave me a list of stretches to do and told me to take ibuprofen. I thought I was going to live with the pain forever.

I was given one of these to try and was very skeptical to say the least. However, I stuck with the regimen (2 times a day for 2 minutes at a time) and my back pain was greatly reduced within 6 weeks. After a few months, it was almost as if I never had a problem. It has even helped my sciatica.

I started on the first level and made it to the last level in about 7 months. I still use it, but only once a day, and sometimes I even skip days. But if I go a week or two without it, the pain starts to creep back. (I still have to be careful about what movements I make because I can still easily wrench my back, but I have no trouble running or turning my head anymore.)

There are very few things I fully endorse, but I believe in this product so much that I bought one each for my mom, brother, and sister this last Christmas. It's crazy that more people don't know about it. Even crazier is that some people I've told don't believe me. Or maybe they don't want to invest in it. If you have back pain but don't want to spend the money on this thing, put it on your Christmas or birthday list. Seriously.

review_body: Yes, this is a good quality ball, but the sizing if completely wrong.  Do not order a Gymnic Ball 22" and under unless you are buying for a small child. Obviously you can do this by releasing some of the air, but then the ball is even smaller.  There are many exercises to do on this ball, easy to hard.  Please don't make the same mistake and order the wrong size.  I liked Fitballs the best, but everyone is telling me they are not making them anymore.  I'm hoping to try out Wacces... Can anyone tell me about their sizing/quality?  On the cheaper end, I've purchased Tone Fitness, which seems to be good after blowing up, but have not tried it (yet, again on the small side).  Not sure how this ball will last overtime, but it was $17.00.  Can't beat that.  Oh, wait I've purchased Theraband too!  Go huge with them...they are way off.  I have yet to find the perfect ball that compares to Fitball.  I hope this review helps someone.  Thanks.

4) Leather case is brown, not black as pictured (no biggy, but still)

product_title: Schwinn 470 Elliptical Machine
review_body:
I bought this machine for late night workouts since I work third shift. I love ellipticals and use them often.

Pros
*runs smoothly
-this is one of the reasons I bought this machine. I need a quiet machine. I live in a condo and my last machine I had to use headphones or I would have to blast my TV just to hear it.

*easy to put together
-I put it together by myself. I used a short bar stool to help hold pieces. Instructions are great.

*you can adjust the position of fan vertically
-I like this because sometimes I want the fan to hit me in different areas.

*Speaker system is great
-the sound is better than using my speaker phone on my cell phone for music or you can even talk on the phone if you have enough wind in your lungs. Auxiliary the cord is included.

*you can keep your phone at its charge.
-it doesn't really charge your phone but you don't lose your percentage while using your phone. If I start off with 20% and I use my phone the whole hour, I may end up with 21%

Cons
*the manual for the actual machine has to be printed online.(Only assembly instructions included)
-not a big deal but I don't have a printer. I guess I could go print it elsewhere but I would prefer a small booklet I could keep in the cup holder for a quick reference.

*Calorie count is wrong.
I contacted Bowflex about this and they sent me out a new console. The new one is a little better. The machine says i'm only burning 4 calories a minute. One of the reasons I bought this machine was too link it with myfitnesspal and my calories are wrong so I have to just add it myself. Not a big deal but it is one of the main reasons I liked this machine. I know i'm burning more calories than that!

* when handle bars are in motion you can not reach your tablet or you will get hit
I like to play candy crush or maybe check a text message. Its hard to do anything on your cell phone cause those bars are coming inward. Its even hard to take a break from them and use the heart rate sensor bars without getting hit.

*the machine too heavy to move alone
needed help to get it into the space I needed it long term.

Shipping
Ceva delivered the package. They didn't call the day before to verify delivery like how they did with my TV. The time was scheduled between 8 to 11am. I called at 1015 to make sure they were coming. They came at 1030 am with one person. He told me they were slow and he came out just for me. Well why make me wait all this time and look out my window for a truck lol? One delivery man for or a 250lb box. Of course I live on the 2nd floor and had to leave it in the hallway in a corner. I wish I had to option to pay extra for a second delivery man so it could be brought upstairs. Or if somehow I knew I need assistance I could have had a male there to help the delivery man.

To sum things up I give it 4 stars because overall its a great machine. Some things that bother me may not bother the next person. I think its a quality machine and the customer service has been ok. I have not received a call to make sure the calories are better or anything. But I am sure if I call they will take care of it. I'm going to just keep this console and get over not using sync with myfitnesspal. I hope this review is helpful.

product_title: PRISM ZERO G
review_body:
I am a sailor and enjoy simple single-line kites when I can't get out on the water. Some days, however, there is no wind. The notion of a kite I could fly in zero wind was what sold me.

My first few outings were in about 5 to 8 knots of wind, and I had almost no luck because I was trying to launch it by myself and basically had no idea how to control it. Lots of nose-dives, no flying. Then I had a few evenings of almost zero wind and finally had the \\"a-ha\\" moment. A gentle toss downwind and a well-timed pull on the line and it soared up and arced back downwind. Awesome!

I have never done any fly fishing, but it seems very similar insofar as you need to carefully time when you let out slack and when you pull on tension. At times you get a significant pile of sting at your feet and it is a challenge to pay it in and out quickly enough, but even that is pretty fun. It is possible to turn the kite, but I can't verbalize how its done--- it just sort of happens---sometimes even when I want it to, haha.

Anyway, I'm no kid anymore (40+) but this is enough to put a silly grin on my face and it is an enchanting toy. Much better than sitting on a couch waiting for the wind to build...

Once I have zero wind flying figured out, then I hope to try again in light wind.

review_body:

I have had two shipped.

The first had something shoved through the top (single layer cardboard) of the box, and pierced the back support cushion leaving a hole.

The second had the end-cap of one of the support legs (nearest the pictured model's right foot) shattered, taking out the inbuilt storage wheel as well.

Looking at the packing, this box has been designed to be in one orientation during the entire shipping process. No provision made for it being rotated and the bench shifting toward the top of the box. There are warnings all over the box about how any damage is the carrier's fault, but not a single "This end up" arrow that I saw.

For now I have given up having an intact unit shipped to me, although the bench itself is very nice. Other foldable benches I have seen at brick and mortar retailers seem very chintzy by comparison. I will try again when the demoralization eases.

product_title: Amazon Jungle Survival Knife with Sheath
review_headline: $11 for a Rambo style survival knife? This is a GOOD DEAL for the money!
review_body:
The blade itself is about 9 to 10". The whole knife is about 13" the construction is very durable and sturdy.
The blade is really sturdy and has a saw built into the back.
The knife comes with a survival kit in the handle (matches, fishing kit, etc.)
I found the sheath much to my surprise to be a better quality than I expected.
The handle could be a little longer, but I have large hands but it's still good.
I bought mine from Budk for $12 (not including shipping) the Amazon Jungle Knife is a great alternative to the "officially" licensed Rambo knife. The official Rambo knife costs anywhere between $65-$120 depending on who you buy it from. I checked all the review on the officially licensed Rambo knifes and those were rated as "not good" for the money you spend and were ALSO made in China.
I thought I'd save a lot of money and buy this knife instead and am VERY HAPPY I DID. It combines both knife (Rambo I and II) in one.
I was a little skeptical because of the price but was surprised of the GOOD quality.
The blade is sharp and so is the saw back which looks awesome too!
It's a very menacing looking knife and not SO super large so that it will poke your side every time you sit down while strapped to your belt.
It looks like an expensive custom knife with OUT the high price tag.
The sheath appears to be actual leather but I could be wrong? I have seen others slam it as pleather but I disagree! It's not a bad quality sheath at all.
This is a great knife for the price, Bud K has a lot of neat stuff for decent prices, I've never been disappointed with anything I got from them. I Love Budk.
I see a lot of people putting this knife down in their reviews, but come on? People are throwing it at trees, at the ground and using it as a hammer? REALLY?
I guess depending on what your going to use it for, but myself, I use it as a box cutter at work. I have broken 3 box cutters on thick card board boxes so I bought this knife and it does the job.
I get compliments every time someone sees me using it. I am always asked "Can I see it" and they all Love it as do I. How can you beat $12 bucks for a knife?

product_title: Ultimate Arms Gear .22 22 Caliber Universal Rifle Pistol Hand Gun Field Complete Gunsmith Cleaning Kit with Military Style Carry Storage Case
review_headline: Great for beginners, but beware expanding
review_body:
I loved this kit when I bought my first rifle as it contained everything I needed for cleaning it. I especially like the inclusion of the chamber brush.

That said, I do have a few issues with the kit. The first, and largest issue for me, is that the threading on the pole does NOT match the standard threading used by companies like Hoppe's, and so any other brushes you buy, such as a larger caliber brush for your next rifle, runs the risk of not fitting properly in the threads. It held ok, but I had to push the brush through, then take it off and pull the pole back and put it back on, etc. My other issue is that the pole is in several pieces and needs to be assembled. This is not a problem in and of itself, but the ridges where the pole pieces meet are not completely flush, which can cause damage to the barrel.

As a bargain first kit though, I highly recommend this product. For anyone who is more experienced and knows what you will need, you may be better off getting either a higher end kit or buying the parts separately.

Just as a side note, I still use the little dropper bottle, it works great and doesn't leak so it is the best I have used so far, the attachment that allows larger brushes to be attached, and the patch holders. I have since replaced the brushes and the pole though.

product_title: RDX Adjustable Leather Gym Skipping Jump Speed Rope Weighted Fitness Training Workout Exercise
review_body:
Don't get me wrong, this is a decent looking speed rope... However, I could have made one just as nice in my workshop. There are no specialized parts here... the "swivel" is just a typical cable end, attached to the handles with a screw and a pair of washers. The handles themselves are well made. The "RDX" stickers on mine looked like they were applied by a legally blind chimpanzee with Parkinson's. Once I pulled the stickers off, the residue left behind was a serious pain to remove.

As to the performance of the rope, it works very well. It's heavier than other ropes I've used, and that helps to really get it moving for a great cardio workout. I'm not sure that the bearings and 90 degree swivel helps much other than curb appeal; I'm sure it would work just as well with normal handles.

Non-technical users will surely love this rope, however if you're a DIY type of person, you'll feel ripped off since you could easily make this yourself. In fact, I've been collecting components to make my next rope after purchasing this one.

review_headline: Don't buy without PROFESSIONAL club fitting
review_body:
Anybody buying golf clubs without a professional club fitting is simply grasping at straws. And going to a big box store for a fitting is NOT a professional fitting.

STRONG ADVISE -- get a professional fitting for a certified fitter who's primary goal isn't selling equipment.

He will tell you:
1. Shaft for your tempo and speed
2. Offset needed for the speed of your hands
3. Style of head based on YOUR swing characteristics.

Bottom line -- these clubs will be great for some; terrible for others. And the way to know is a fitting. Get fit and then order these IF they match up what the fitter suggests. I got fit then re-shafted set of 1998 irons.

One other thing, the main way these clubs get longer is by calling a 5-iron a 6-iron. Don't believe? Why do you think they needed to invent GAP wedges -- it's for the GAP they club makers made between and wedge and SW over the years.

product_title: FINIS Swimsense Performance Monitor
review_headline: Great idea... just does not work
review_body:
Got the Swimsense several weeks ago. I was super excited, and had read a couple of reviews that said it was great. Have tried it multiple times. The first time it was pretty good. I did about 1400 yards, it had me at 1275, not too bad. As I watched it during the work out it seemed to be way behind on the laps at all times. Yet at the end it popped up the right laps. The next day it was less then stellar 1400 it had me at 1725 and I had done 1900 yards. Since then its gone down hill. The first time I tried some different strokes I was pretty impressed with the results on the dashboard, since then its been getting worse. One day it had me at 50% of my laps done in backstroke. All I did that day was a 200 IM. I have tried changing the settings around a little on the intervals. It defaulted to manual so I tried automatic. That just seemed to make things worse. Yesterday After doing a 500 warm up, it had me at 1 lap 100 yards. I spent so much time playing around with the watch yesterday that my planned 1650 work out was really only 1000. However the watch had me at 250 yards at a total time of 4 minutes.

The clock does not work on my unit. I had the unit on the charger over the weekend at my office. It said it was fully charged. I started it up before my lunch time swim. The time was off (AGAIN) so I set the date and time. an hour later when I went to the pool it was still showing the time I had set an hour before (and yes I did hit save). I reset the time and started swimming. 20 minutes later time had not changed, reset it and still did not work. When I got out of the pool to shower I looked at the unit and i noticed the time was at least working (wrong time). I watched the seconds tick by.. 1..4...5...6.........8...9 It was a good 2-3 seconds between each change of time. From the time I left the pool, showered, got dressed and walked out the clock said a total of 4 minutes had elapsed. It was more like 15-18 minutes. For reference I left teh unit on teh charger turned on all night. The clock is now 12 hours and 22 minutes behind, and the date is now a full day behind too. Checked my workout yesterday and it says PM so it was set correct yesterday.

The charger is another issue. When you put it on the charging base, the bands act like a spring and push it off the connectors so it wont charge. So you either need to latch the band around the charger as if the charger was your arm, or you have to put the watch face down on the table so the charger is on top. If you latch the band it presses right where the USB cable comes out of the base, so I fear that the band forcing that cable to the side right at the connection will wear out the connection and it will fail. The other method to keep the unit connected to charging base is to put it upside down, but that rests it on the face and I worry that doing that is going to scratch it.

Also if you do any kicking sets, it does not work. Not sure why you they could not just add a manual lap counter so that when you are doing a kicking set, you could mark your laps on your own since your hands are free. Also I hooked it up to Myfitness Pal, and after all my workouts, yesterdays was the first to push across. (Though in their defense, that could be a myfitness pal deal)

After having such high hopes, I am very disappointed. I think there is some possibility, but frankly I would wait a version or two to see if they get the bugs worked out. I frankly never expected it to be perfect, but being off 75% means that it is worthless as a tracker for me. I have been counting my own laps for 32 years of competive swimming, I may have to go old school again :-)

I am going to try a hard reset on the unit, check for the updated firmware again, and if it does not start functioning better i am going to return it.

PS Just to not sound negative, the Dashboard is awesome, and the Bridge works really well. My computer seems to always have problems connecting to USB devices (takes a couple of plug and unplugs) but the unit gets picked up right away. The navigation was a little tricky at first, I reread the manual, and realized its actually pretty easy. You can get around inside fairly well. If I can get this working to any level of comfort I am excited to try it in open water. Right now I take my Garmin 310XT start it and put it in my cap so its mostly above water. Hoping it works in open water and the laps dont mess up the overall distance calculations.

Cheap, durable and highly effective, they are the benchmark that other silencers always try to beat. Having said that, the Bowjax silencers are an adequate second. This particular model uses zip ties, (or you can serve them in) to attach to the bowstring. I intended to use the zip ties only as a temporary measure to test these out with, but I must confess that they are a cheap but quick and effective way of installing these. I'll keep them as is, at least until I install a new string this spring.

After having String Leeches and Doubledowns continually break after limited shots, I gave these a try. They seem to be more pliable than the earlier design of years back. I installed them in minutes on both my Bear Anarchy and Empire. Both bows are whisper quiet without any string silencers, but with the Bowjax installed, the shot became nothing more than a slight dull thud. While I have had many experiences in the woods of a quiet bow paying off, this year of six deer shot, four of them had other deer with them that didn't run off, or soon returned after the shot, offering another shot opportunity should I have chosen it. They have been durable so far, but the heavy spring practicing coming soon will prove their merit. I have faith that they will prevail, so much so that I will give them their deserved five stars.

I recently had a partial knee replacement and an indoor bike was recommended for knee strengthening and general aerobic exercise. I researched various types and brands, and settled on this based on my needs, the moderate price and the reviews. I am 6' 2" tall, and part of my review is based on that.

This is a Semi-Recumbent bike. This means that you are not lying back as you would in a Recumbent bike but, rather, sitting up straight as though you were riding a road or mountain bike. Unlike those, your hands grip bars that are down by your hip area. Unlike a normal bike, though, the pedals are located well forward of your knees. It results in a very comfortable position for either short or long exercise sessions.

Assembly of the bike was quick and easy (about 15 minutes) with clear instructions. Let me say now that this bike is pretty heavy, so although it is foldable & movable, you'll want to keep it nearby where you will use it. The seat is large, comfortable and well padded. The backrest is tall enough to easily accommodate someone of my height and is also well padded. Everything about this machine is well designed & comfortable, even the pedals. The computer that tracks performance turns on automatically as sson as you start to pedal. You can delete all the info when you are done except for the odometer (cumulative miles) that tracks total distance up to 999.9 miles.

For pure aerobics, the settings from 1 to 4 are fine. Settings 5 thru 8 really provide enough resistance that you enter the realm of strength and/or endurance training. The resistance setting knob is easy to reach while you are riding, so it is easily adjusted mid-stream. The pulse-rate feature seems to be pretty accurate, but it does require you to keep both hands on the "handle bars": not a big issue.

With the seat set for the maximum height and wearing sneakers, I found that the bike forced my knees to a full 90-degree angle AND pushed them up high. The pedals are made of plastic and are smooth enough to be gentle on the feet. With socks only, I was able to get my foot further into the pedal straps (ball-of-the-foot with sneakers; foot arch with socks alone.) This set my legs a bit more forward and my knees didn't go up as high or bend as much.

Other than this single issue (unique to my height & knee condition), the bike is great. It's sturdily constructed and is rated to 300 lbs., though I suspect it would hold even more. My wife, who is 5' 4", has also used it (with sneakers) and the seat easily adjusted for her height. The magnetic flywheel is incredibly quiet, even at high speeds. It is very stable in use and doesn't shake side-to-side. If you don't want to leave it in place, it is easy to fold but, as I mentioned earlier, it is pretty heavy and not so easy to move, so if you plan to fold-and-store, keep it close to where you will use it.

For me the pros out way the cons, therefore I will continue to use it. Although if I was to purchase this band again, $25 is too high for the quality you get. Somewhere closer to $15 would be more acceptable.

Schedule third attempted delivery; again given an 8 hour window and promise to call. After waiting home and not going to work for a couple hours, I called their dispatcher to find out what number I was on the delivery list, and possible ETA. They said they don't know and could not provide that info, as it was up to the driver (again, unacceptable in 2014 - so much for efficient logistics). Driver did call with a notice of about an hour, and they did deliver, but it did not look good. The driver said I needed to sign that the unit was delivered, and if there was damage I needed to call Estes and inform them. I called Estes, and they said I could have refused deliver, and should have noted on the paperwork that the unit was damaged (again, not what the driver said). Over a 2-week period, I spent hours on the phone being passed along or sent to dead ends where the phone rings to infinity with Estes Express - apparently they don't know about the technology known as voice-mail.

On the PLUS side - Horizon Fitness has been great in trying to resolve the issues and have been very accessible and is trying to make things right. Will update once fully resolved. product_title: Marcy Diamond MD2109 100-Pound Stack Gym
review_headline: A nice gym for toning and moderate strength training
review_body:
This is a versatile home gym that does a pretty good job of working different muscle groups. The price is affordable, and the footprint does not take up an entire room. It does not give you the same workout that you might get with free weights or using professional grade equipment you might get with a gym membership. However, I am a busy professional balancing work and family, and taking time to go to a gym in the morning or after work is not an option. Having something at home makes it much easier to pop in and get a few sets. It also allows me to get in a workout after the kids go to bed without taking up the entire evening.

If you are looking to get insanely ripped, this is not the home gym you want. The weight stack is only 100 lbs, and if you are a serious weightlifter, you will max this pretty quickly for chest presses. But if you are looking to tone, build a little endurance, and moderately increase strength, this might be a nice affordable option if you have limited space.

The one design flaw is the orientation of the chest press handles. There are upper and lower handles, and they are both vertical. It seems like it would be more natural to have the handles horizontal, to closer simulate the configuration of a free weight bench press. Other than this, I am pretty happy with the unit.

product_title: EVERLAST HAND WRAPS
review_headline: Great overall, but could be improved
review_body:
I purchased these hand wraps as a gift for my brother to use with a punching bag (under small boxing gloves). They seem to be great quality: soft, brightly colored, well sewn.
The directions for wrapping them on your hands were fairly clear, except that the images did not seem to match the instructions exactly. At one point, the directions seem to say go under the hand while the image shows wrapping over the hand. If you do it the incorrect way, the side of the band where the velcro can attach will be face down instead of face up at the very end. So then you must undo the wrap and re-wrap everything so the velcro side will be face up. A similar issue occurs if you accidentally twist the band during the wrapping process. A simple fix that would make these hand wraps perfect would be to have the soft velcro on *both* sides of the wrap. You could probably add this yourself if you are crafty, but my brother just ended up labeling each of the wraps so he could remember which side to pull across his palm at the beginning of wrapping.

review_headline: It is not exactly as the company website portrays it
review_body: If you have used the simulator on the EOtech website before actually using the sight, you may be a bit surprised.  As advertised the sighting dot and the outer ring are based upon an optic projected onto the sight glass, much like a heads-up display on an aircraft works.  Yet, the projection of that image is not as precise as the simulator makes it seem.  It is a series of fine dots.  In fact, whilst signting a rifle with it on a sunny day with snow on the ground, the outer ring was not substantially noticeable even with the brightness adjustment setting at its highest.  I have used other manufacturer's "red dot" type sights (such as Tasco, Leopold, and others) and found the brightness and clarity of the illuminated sight picture better than this sight. I kept it, however, because I wanted the one inch single dot that no other manufacturer offers.  Other than my observation of the brightness, I haven't enough working time to comment about the durability and functionality of the sight.

product_title: MTM Arrow Plus Case
review_headline: Really light duty- Gret for storage.
review_body:
Probably wouldnt use this for hunting or long distance trips. But for home use it will work just fine

PROS- Holds 36 arrows stacked tip to tail and tip again -> + <- + ->
- Big with extra storage compartments
- Decent carry handle
- Lockable
- Compact enough to slide under bed or hide in a corner
- Will hold larger length arrows
- Has hinges although they are plastic they are however like a real door hinge so they wont fatigue everytime you open the case.

CONS- The foam insertts used to stack are low density rectangles glued together (2 PER SIDE) with 6 slits on top and 6 slits on the bottem- meaning 18 arrows on top and 18 on bottem when stacked three high; doing this makes it so you have to pull the foam inserts out if you need to get to those bottem 18...
- The case is only light duty at best with plastic latches
- Closing the case with the foam equiped isnt possible without replacing the foam, modifying the foam, or simply squeezing the foam before closing the case.
- The glue used to hold each of the fouur blocks together is cheap; will redo
- No notches/gaps in the foam other than the slits making the foam expand outward further and further the more arrows you load making the previously mentioned closing more difficult than nedded...

Overall great concept; would easily spend double if they made a real (LUGGAGE GRADE case as described) hard case with a decent foam that has somedensity- And with the individual compartments had closing tranparent lids with latches (possibly removable) in it.

And a much sturdier broadhead wrench (metal encased in plastic would be nice)
I would recommend this to a friend but not for hunting- you wouldnt need 36 arrows anyways.

product_title: Casio PAW5000-1 Atomic Tough Solar Analog Digital Watch
review_headline: nice Pathfinder with a few shortcomings
review_body:
I'll start by saying that I have a couple of Pathfinders and this is probably the one I prefer because I don't always wear a watch but when I do...

Pros:
Looks great - print on the face seems small at first but I got used to it
Reasonable to good accuracy on barometer and (less so) altimeter for a device of this price point
Analog compass reading a plus
Swapping between home city and world time setting never gets old, watching the hands move on their own, exchanging with the LCD. Great if you bounce back and forth between 2 locations on a regular basis.
Tough Solar means no need to change batteries every year or 2, automatically sets to atomic clock
Buttons feel solid so far

Cons:

LED light doesn't light up the LCD display. Since the hands aren't illuminated, this is more a daytime watch. LED can be set to 1 sec or 3 sec on as well as auto on.
Altimeter scale change goes from 400' to 4000', is printed in meters on the outer ring
Can't set timer in increments less than 1 minute
Alarm is weak high frequency, hard to hear, chime likewise

Would not hesitate to purchase again. Main uses for me are while snowboarding, hiking, having a compass for line-of-sight bearing calculations, other terrestrial activities, etc. Probably not the best for diving or aviation but there are plenty of other choices in those areas.

product_title: Cold Steel Rifleman's Hawk American Hickory Handle
review_body:
(Revised 1/28/14) - In an attempt to be accurate,honest and provide a useful review I have updated my comments below. My new comments are within ( ).

Well, you've come to know that what is advertised is not necessarily what you get. Received this today
1. This is not Cold Steel but American Tomahawk Company (American Tomahawk Company is owned by Cold Steel)
2. It's made in Taiwan
3. The head is loose. Affixed to the handle with(a \\"set screw\\" with a Hex head. The side of the screw screws into / or against the wood of the handle. This concerns me a bit that the screw could come loose through use). The handle flares out so the head will not fly off, but it does wobble and does not give you a sense of security. (I did unscrew the head, firmly seat the head so it did not wobble and set the screw again)
4. The handle is rough, splinters and needs a good sanding.
5. The edge seems fine.

It appears the quality of Cold Steel had gone down over the years. (and I'm still not impressed with the quality)

------------Update----------------
More on American Tomahawk (do not confuse American Tomahawk Company (Cold Steel) with American Tomahawk).

American Tomahawk owned by Andy Prisco
[[ASIN:B0017WJR9U AmericanThawk American Tomahawk VTAC Lagana]]

In researching this issue I found there is a company called American Tomahawk owned by Andy Prisco. Peter LaGana founded the American Tomahawk Company in 1966 with the original Vietnam Tomahawk design. The provide \\"high quality\\" equipment for the military and law enforcement. Their Tomahawks cost upwards of $100.

Cold Steel registered the mark \\"American Tomahawk Company\\", est 1992, NOT affiliated with the above \\"American Tomahawk.\\"

The comments below are from Andy Prisco Last edited by Andy Prisco; 07-27-2006 at 01:39 AM.

\\"I'd like to address some of the remarks regarding the \\"American Tomahawk Company\\" nameto clarify the confusion that exists in this thread, about this issue.

Cold Steel registered the mark \\"American Tomahawk Company, est 1992\\" nearly 10 years before I approached Peter LaGana to discuss the new American Tomahawk Company. Neither Peter nor I were aware that Cold Steel ever registered this mark. In fact, I am not aware of any industry professional, magazine editor, or advertising professional, that was aware of it either. It was never used in any Cold Steel product catalog.

In April of 2002, nearly one and a half years after our investment in developing the brand name, \\"American Tomahawk Company\\", Lynn Thompson contacted me to inform me that I was infringing on his intellectual property.

We sought counsel from Intellectual Property attorneys, who concluded that Cold Steel's failure to ever use the mark as well as its \\"supplemental\\" status on the trademark register, (i.e. not on the principal register) made it clear that Cold Steel was not entitled to exclusive use of the mark. Additionally, our American Tomahawk Company had right of first use as well as proof of investment in developing the brand name within the purchasing public. We communicated this position to Cold Steel. Nonetheless, Mr. Thompson demanded that my Company purchase the mark for an exorbitant amount of money to avoid legal action.

In an attempt to preclude the cost of litigation, I submitted a proposal and payment schedule to Cold Steel, which was ultimately refused. It was immediately after those discussions ended that Cold Steel began to print \\"American Tomahawk Company, est. 1992\\" labels and attach them to every Tomahawk they marketed and sold, which to my understanding, were all imported and remain imported.

This dispute never rose to any formal legal complaint. Cold Steel continues to use the mark.

We have received nothing but support from countless industry professionals regarding this issue. Cold Steel's productsare of excellent reputation and Lynn Thompson should be credited as a pioneer in this industry. However, we don't see eye-to-eye on this matter and probably never will. If anything, Cold Steel's recent use of the mark helps them sell their own imported Tomahawks, which has on several occasions resulted in the customer believing they bought something from us. Therefore, their use of the mark doesn't help me sell mine. However, many people don't want to spend over $100 for an axe. For those customers, there is Cold Steel.\\"

See other products from American Tomahawk here on Amazon.com http://www.amazon.com/s/ref=bl_sr_sporting-goods?ie=UTF8&field-brandtextbin=American+Tomahawk&node=3375251

product_title: OUTBAGS USA OB-17TAC Nylon Drop Leg Thigh Holster w/ Mag Pouch. Family owned & operated. Made in USA

review_body:
First, lets face it. At 4.5+lbs the Desert Eagle isn't the easiest thing to carry. This holster is well made, and holds my DE snug and protected. I wish there were ways to secure the extra strapping once adjusted (I don't care to cut off excess). The secondary strap isn't worth the aggravation unless you feel better with it (or plan on running/wrestling a lot with your DE). It come off without any problem. I did some jumping jacks, ran around and it stayed right were I put it (wearing jeans, leg straps not very tight).

The biggest problem with this holster, and it has nothing to do with Outbags, is you better have a sturdy belt! I tried it with a decent belt, but all that weight was too much for it. A tactical web belt, or high dollar leather (made for carry) is needed. Plenty of belt loops are a plus. For the price you can't go wrong. It'll make a good way to carry on hikes, or at the range. Not surprisingly, my 1911 was swallowed up by it... it's made for the Desert Eagle!

product_title: Condor Recon Chest Rig (Black)
review_body:
I have been using this rig for combat training at the range and it works well for what it is, however it does have some shortcomings. First, the rifle mag pouches: this will hold 6 AR mags easily in the front double stacked pouches and up to 6 pistol mags on the front of those. If you are running an AK you can SQUEEZE 6 mags in, but don't count on being able to withdraw them quickly or without a big fight as AK mags have a slightly larger outside circumference and the extra curvature seems to seat them in much tighter. This is a drawback for me since I usually train with my AK's. The other drawback is that once the rifle mags are all out, the pistol pouches flop around a lot since you now have two layers of mag pouches empty behind them. (Don't you dare put an empty mag back into your rig, put it in a dump pouch if you need to practice mag retention) this makes it extremely hard to speed reload your sidearm after your primary runs dry. Condor does make a very similar rig that has 6 rifle mag pouches in a single row IN the panel which eliminates both of these problems and keeps a lower profile for going prone as well.
Other than these issues the construction is good and sturdy and Molle webbing is everywhere. Straps are adjustable and I have no problems with fit at 6' 2\\" 215lbs, there is room to adjust up or down so I can wear it over a heavy winter jacket OR just a t shirt. Shoulder straps are padded and it is comfortable to wear for hours without annoyance. There are also a few pouches in the panel itself that will hold extra rifle mags as long as you don't plan to speed reload from them, and a nice admin pouch in the middle panel with a mesh pouch behind that against the body as well.
I plan to buy the single stack version of this rig and add pistol mag pouches to it because it just runs faster and more efficiently for what I need it for, but you may prefer the double stack if those issues don't bother you.

review_headline: Sturdy but there's one big design flaw ...
review_body: I love the material, the strength of the velcro closure, and the extra wide width of this belt, and it does get the sweat going, with or without a workout.  My only concern is that when you wrap it around you, it's almost impossible to get the two ends to lay exactly one over the other. Invariably, one side will come down just a little bit lower than the other, which exposes a small patch of skin underneath to the belt's wide swath of hard, scratchy, skin-chafing velcro. if the velcro end were tapered (like the McDavid trimmer belt), this would be the best belt I've ever used.  One of the reviewers here gave me the idea to taper the top and bottom of the velcro end myself, and that's just what I did. Took a pair of scissors and cut a  piece off the top and bottom, so that the belt is narrower on the velcro end, and now there's no possibility of "velcro chafe" when I wrap the belt around me. The belt is holding up fine (no fraying of the neoprene or unraveling of the  stitching holding down the velcro! The scope I mounted is a Brunton Echo with 40mm obj, 1 inch tube.

It all fits perfect on the rifle, perfect height, eye relief distance, cheek weld. Like it was all a custom order from some high priced gun shop. Nope, just from amazon with it's often great pricing!

I think a 50mm obj lens would still work with this setup with the take down rifle. Looks like there's still about 1/2 inch clearance (tad bit less, maybe about 10mm) from the 40mm obj bell to the rifle barrel.

Some reviews of this mount insist they needed height with their rings for the take down rifle version. With the 40mm obj, and the UTG rail and this UTG QD ring set, there' plenty of room, and I really think with a 50mm it would be OK too.

I'm not sure what these "rings" are considered, but my guess is mid height.

The mount "seems" to be able to hold up, time will tell. Mounting was easy. Un mounting with the QD lever and remounting was easy, kept my zero too.

On the top of the rings are mini rails which seem useless since most scopes elevation/windage adjustment knobs will take up most of the space in between each of the 2 rings. product_title: Spyderco Benchstone Ultra Fine 2" x 8" W/Box
review_headline: Keeps my straight razor in great condition
review_body:
I bought this for honing a straight razor, mainly because I didn't want to mess with conditioning/leveling the surface of an actual stone. And being a fan of Spyderco's Sharpmaker ceramic sharpening system, this seemed like a good way to go. It seems to work perfectly for the job. I hone my razor about once a month on this, and use Thiers-Issard sharpening paste on a leather strop in the interim. I've been doing so for about a year with no hitches. At one point I had to go coarser to get rid of a ding in the edge (from stupidly bumping the blade on the faucet), and worked back up to this stone. It left a perfect edge.
After using this stone, I take about 50 passes on the smooth leather strop and then enjoy an awesome shave.
As a bonus, this stone is quite flat and travels well, although it is dense enough that I wouldn't call it 'lightweight'.

product_title: Under Armour UA Fleece Glove
review_headline: Great glove... but only for 3 weeks!!
review_body:
I was actually really excited to receive these as a Christmas gift. The fleece material was comfortable, the touchscreen sensitive fingers were very accurate when typing with the gloves on, the fit was perfect, and the hidden key pocket was a nice touch. But most importantly to me, the grippy material on the palms of the gloves were great for driving and for making sure my phone didn't slip out of my hands. True, like other reviewers have said, the gloves are not meant for extreme cold, but I don't walk outside much and spend most of my time driving from place to place, so they were sufficient for my needs.

Fast forward three weeks of casual use. The "silicone grippy palm" is shedding at exponential rates. It is comprised of "Under Armour" and "UA" lettering and, at this moment, I have over dozens of these letter's threads dangling from my gloves. Not only does it look terrible, but clearly I will soon lose the grippiness that I valued most in this glove.

If you value being able to hold onto your phone or not have the steering wheel slip out of your hands, don't buy these gloves.

product_title: Magpul Polymer Trigger Guard, Black
review_headline: WOW -  I'm not sure where the positive reviews come from on this cheap junk
review_body:
The Magpul polymer trigger guard is a great idea. But it is executed poorly and will likely cause you to damage your AR.

My rifle: Colt AR6720 - an amazing firearm that never ceases to please me with it's quality and accuracy. Weighs 5.9 lbs. Love that gun.

The Magpul polymer trigger guard installs between the ears of the trigger guard attachment points with a surprising bit of slop, just enough to allow the topside ear to flex as you drive the tight fitting roll pin down. This flex can't be helped or avoided by supporting the bottom side ear with a block of wood (which I did).
The deal killer for me was the hex wrench installed screw that self taps into the forward attachment point - replacing the spring indent pin that allows the original mil spec trigger guard to swing down for winter glove use. I lubed the screw before attempting the install, and then gingerly applied just enough force to get the screw started on it's job. The magpul supplied screw stripped out where the hex key is supposed fit, and was rendered stuck halfway installed. Now I was faced with the stripped screw protruding out the side of the trigger guard, ready to snag skin and clothing. I had to tape up the receiver to avoid marring the finish, then use a metal file to remove the protruding cheap metal screw. A simple job became an unsatisfactory hour long hassle, and black magic marker had to be applied to the bright metal exposed by filing off the original black finish. Frankly, at that point, I would have liked to kick Mr Magpul right square in the nuts.
Sorry fellas, this is cheap plastic junk you are considering placing on your valuable weapon. Just say no.

product_title: Wartech "Blaze" AO Rescue Knife w/ LED Light - Blue
review_headline: A really good knife for a really good purpose
review_body:
I received this knife as a gift this Christmas. This is a knife that everyone ought to own, not just knife junkies. To date I have rescued anyone, including myself, however I am impressed with the construction, feel and utility of this knife. It just looks good. it
has some heft and feels like quality, regardless of the price. It opens easily with thumb or forefinger and has a bit of assist. It is a little tight and does not open to lock without a little flick of the wrist, but this is most likely due to its newness.
This is not a pocket carry knife. The little led light that rides on one side makes this knife a knife for the car, the tool bag, the back pack, but not the pocket, unless you have giant pockets or carry nothing in them. The light is bright and could be a lifesaver in an emergency, which is the purpose of this knife. The seat belt cutter, the light the multipurpose blade all speak to this. This knife will find a home in my truck. Oh, did I mention the little pointed tip? It is designed to break auto glass. The nature of the tempered glass in autos keeps them from breaking into great knives when broken, but shatter without making dangerous shards. This makes this glass difficult to break unless you know the trick of that little tip. Thieves use spark plugs to break glass. With this knife you can break your way out of (or into) a wreck without trying to find a handy spark plug.
I like this knife. The clip works well and is nice and long. Guys get your wife one of these for her purse of something. Explain that it is a rescue knife, not a battle knife, and you'll have an extra piece when you need it. And priced right. .

review_headline: For what you pay, it's not bad........

"The amazing thing about a dancing bear is not how well it dances, but that it dances at all."
This scale is kind of like that; as cheaply as it is made and as simply as it operates, it works surprisingly well. Two caveats, though: Keep it level and try for constant temperatures where you are using it. Buy a reference weight, also, for calibration.

The vernier scale on the .1 grain scale is fairly intuitive for machinists and anyone who has ever read a vernier height gage. I had to show my neighbor how to read his, but he got it very quickly. A video on YouTube would solve this problem for the desk jockies and paper pushers who lack real-world experience.

The pivot for the balance is, simply put, a razor blade. Leave it alone. I had to very carefully clean the surface of the matching seat for this with a piece of 120 grit wet-and-dry, as I suspect the cutter they used to mill the seat was dull and left a poor finish.

product_title: P90X DVD Workout - Base Kit
review_body:
I bought this last year as part of my New Years resolution. I only made it 30 days or so into the program but would recommend it.

The Kit
The kit is great! It comes with multiple DVDs, a fitness guide and a nutrition booklet. I still use the nutrition booklet to this day - it's a great guide for grocery shopping, recipes, etc.

The DVDs
The DVDs are fun! I really enjoyed the workouts. The first day I started I couldn't do any of the moves. I struggled but plugged along. I felt silly doing some of the things but it turned enjoyable and by a week into the program it got easier. You'll need to purchase hand weights and a pull up bar. I bought the resistance bands but a pull up bar is the way to go. You can get everything from target. Tony is a trip and I got a kick out of working out with him. I also enjoyed the extras they had - each DVD has new people who are just amazingly in fit but they always have one person doing a modified workout and they spend time showing you how to do it with them - which was so helpful. The DVDs are an hour long including warm up and cool down. a small clock is in the corner letting you know how much time you have left.

The results
Yes, you will see results regardless of your fitness level or duration into the program. I did it for 30 days and then went off and on it for a week here and there. I lost 40 lbs from March to May (190 to 150 lbs). On the days I didn't do the DVDs I still followed the nutrition plan and got in 30 min on elliptical. It was a good way to re-discipline myself. I stopped working out in Sept and am now back to my original weight which means I'm breaking this back out again... which is another reason I'd recommend it. It's a great tool to have and pull out when you needed it. You'll learn some good tips along the way.

It took a little time to assemble the vertical portion (the tread portion is already assembled). I used my own Phillips screwdriver and 1/2" ratchet. The tread slides over a solid sheet so its sturdy. I think running would be a problem due to a longer stride but fast walking works. My research showed me that most of the repairs on treadmills are from the motor or the electronics failing. So simplicity is not only cheaper, it lasts longer.

product_title: Galco Ankle Lite / Ankle Holster for KAHR MK40, MK9, PM40, PM9
review_body:
I bought this for a Kahr PM 9. I usually don't carry an ankle holster but wanted something for a backup piece or something to carry when I really needed concealment. An ankle holster is also nice when you are driving and have your primary piece on your hip.

My other ankle holster is a "famous brand" which is advertised as being used by the Secret Service. The Galco is very similar to the famous brand. I don't think either is superior but my other holster is for a Glock 26 which is just too heavy for ankle carry (IMO). The big advantage of the Galco is the add on calf strap that gives you additional support.

You can put this on in the morning and wear it all day with comfort and concealment. Of course like all ankle holsters, it is going to be a lot slower than carrying on a belt. One thing I like about it is that unlike a pocket holster, you don't have a muzzle pointed at the person sitting across from you at a table. I know that a pistol is not going to fire itself but I have a visceral reaction to having a firearm pointed towards someone even when it is in a holster (conditioning).

Like all systems for carrying a concealed firearm, this holster has advantages and disadvantages but overall I think this is an excellent product.

As a reference, my primary carry pistol is a Dan Wesson Concealed Carry Officer (a light weight 1911) which I carry on my right hip. The CCO is going to be way faster to present but sometimes it is not appropriate for social events.

I do carry only when it is legal to do so.

I bought this piece directly from Lifting Large. Long time powerlifter that has come to appreciate the benefits of adding a more upright squat exercise to my routine. Want to blast your quads? This will get it done.

With all due respect to the good doctor above who complained about the shortcomings of this piece of equipment, I would like to disagree about a couple of points he made.

The Zercher Squat/low hook placement is designed to do exactly that...Pull you forward. It's your job to counter the leverage by keeping your body upright. Trick is to gradually ease into it with the weight. Powerlifters love Zercher squats as a compliment to deadlifts, and work great for those of you that do not like pulling dead weight off the floor. Whether you're standing when you start, or are starting from the squatted position off pins on the rack, this is a great exercise for your legs, back and the rest of your core.

I've put as much as 400 pounds on both the highest and 2nd position, and it hasn't killed me or made front squatting unbearable. I'm not sure what the doctor's exact issue is with choking, and again, I'm not here to bash him at all. At 6'2" I have no problems whatsoever with being choked, and the padding on the harness is more than adequate. In fact, compared to trying to cross your arms, or doing front squats using the Olympic clean grip, this is a piece of cake. Oh, and I also have the Sting Ray, which is a decent product for not a lot of money that eases some of the pressure doing front squats, but is required you use the cross arm technique.

The harness adjusts to accommodate any shoulder width, so the only issue I can see potentially being a problem is torso length. That is something you should check with the manufacturer or seller if you are concerned, which I'm sure they will gladly help. Mike at Lifting Large has always been kind and very helpful with me.

Also, keep in mind this is nota "hands free" device. You don't have to keep your hands on the barbell, but you should keep your hands on the pegs where the bar is supported for two reasons. Doing so keeps the harness from moving outward, and it also keeps it in place during your squat movements. The general idea of keeping your hands and elbows up is to pin your shoulders back to keep you in a proper upright position. Don't slouch your upper back and lackadaisically go through the movements, or you'll likely have problems. However, the same can be said regarding virtually every exercise.

So, yes, I love this. I've been using it since I bought it and the price has been worth the investment. For me, the benefit of being able to do front squats without pain far outweighs any cost disadvantage.

Ultimately, it's up to you, though. All you can do is try it out and decide for yourself. Mike from LL has a very good return policy, so there really isn't any risk. Keep in mind, no exercise worth its weight is going to feel like an herbal massage, and part of a good exercise's effectiveness is forcing your body to have to work to complete the rep(s). Even better is something that employs other muscles in addition to the ones you're primarily wanting to work. Stabilizer muscles, posterior chain involvement, and a stronger core are great things. So, it's a win/win.

I'm no doctor. Just 25+ years of lifting experience learning from professionals, as well as injuries that have forced me to pay attention.

There are other ways to do a front squat, but for me, this is by far the easiest and most effective.

product_title: Border Guard 4 40Ser Tanto
review_body:
I know and love a good quality factory knife: nothing feels quite like a Benchmade, Spyderco clipits have that surprisingly satisfying edge, Kershaw blades offer a wide selection of affordable quality, and, of course, CRKT always delivers genuine utility in a long-lasting, durable, economic package.

However, sometimes, you need a knife that gets the job done, feels great, and can be treated as disposable even though it'll be with you for some time. For this reason, despite all the naysaying knife snobs, I love a good Chinese-made Smith and Wesson: they get the job done. In fact, even though I have experience with many factory knives and a particular fondness for Columbia River products, one of my favorite knives was the original Smith and Wesson Border Guard, sporting a partially serrated tanto blade at just over four inches in the best feeling knife grip I've ever used. It was a knife you knew you could count on in daily work, one which could get you out of a submerged car, and one you could use very effectively to defend yourself thanks to a fantastic grip. Did I mention that the grip on this knife--four deep finger grooves complimented by an aggressive sandpaper--was phenomenal?

Unfortunately, I am a law abiding citizen in a city which prohibits blades over four inches long, yes, verily, verily, even a few hairs over four inches.

It was my hope that the BorderGuard4, with its precisely four inch blade, would allow me to carry my favorite cutting tool on city streets. Sure, that wonderful grip would be marred significantly without the finger grooves, but it's still a great knife: thick aluminum scales and a thick blade make the thing almost indestructible, the blade has essentially the same long and narrow tanto profile, and it looks and feels like a tough piece of work. If it is anything like the original in this regard, it's still gravy, right?

Yes, sort of, and no. You have to feel the grip on the original border guard to understand how good the knife is, especially for those with larger hands: the finger groves give the best tool retention short of a Karambit-style fingerhole, and the notch at the back of the knife is perfectly situated for the thumb. You feel in complete control of the blade, and its going nowhere.

Not so with the BG4. Don't be deceived- it looks like the original, and is still as durable, but is nowhere near as practical. The indented thumb rest has been invaded by an uncut frame, such that your thumb now rests on two thin slats of metal. At least there is gimping/notches cut into these two slats... except for the fact that the frame is gimped unevenly (one side has 1-2 mm cuts, the other .5mm) and then paint fills in these insignificant cuts. The macho dual (oh, please...) "blood-groove" on the original has been replaced by a single groove; unfortunately, while the first was excessive, the groove on the BG4 is too short, making the thing look like a toy. Finally, the glass breaker has been re-angled; it is now more safely nested in... your palm.

There is a reason why I was able to order the original Border Guard from my local Streicher's police supply, and yet they didn't carry this one. Take their advice and mine: don't buy this knife. It's a fine knife, and would be a great knife to give your child before getting something nicer, like Kit Carson's M16 series by CRKT; while it will dull somewhat quickly, this is a plus: what a great tool to learn to sharpen on. Then again, you could also do this with the original Border Guard, which costs less while being a better knife.

This knife is different in kind, not degree, from its parents. Don't waste your time.

product_title: Spyderco Hungarian Folder G-10 Stainless Plain Edge Knife, Black, Right
review_body:
Style is not just about frills, it is about the user finding a way to identify with a tool. And if you can identify with a tool, you will find ways to make it work for you. This definitely rings true with the Spyderco Hungarian.

Not only is this knife drop-dead gorgeous, it is a fully functional cutting tool capable of outperforming whatever you have in your pocket right now. The slender handle indexes in your fingers, not your palm, and the combination between its curvature and double-guards creates maximum lock-in for comfort, control, and precision. The angle of the blade allows for drag cutting with minimal effort, making it great for slicing tasks that require accuracy over brute force.

The all-steel functional components, full access to the opening hole from left or right, open spine construction, and long yet light and slender design are also huge benefits for this model. The XHP steel takes and retains an aggressive edge despite all the abuse I heap on it, from kitchen to office chores. In all it is both elegant and highly useful, making it the best Spyderco folder for me personally. I tried finding another folder I like as much as this one, and ended up buying a second one of these. The search is finally over.

product_title: Magpul Industries Rail Light Left Mount, Black
review_body:
I bought this to mount a small (1-cell CR123a) LED, scout-type light to my M4 carbine. I had been attaching a light directly to my 9-o'clock rail and that wasn't doing anything for me. With some of the other mounts being more than the light in terms of $, I figured I would give this one a try. For $30, sure.

I have to say it's exceeded my expectations. It's very solid. The plastic is more reinforced (with fiberglass or something, I'm guessing) than the regular XTM panels so it's very robust. It's also very adaptable, as the description states. You can mount either a Surefire scout light to it, use it as a 1913 rail for a TLR-1 or something like that, or use the mounting rings to attach a light directly to it (that's what I did). Once it's all mounted up the mount is very solid. The thumb-ramp-thing is also very useful as an index point.

So why not 5 stars? There are two things I'm not crazy about. The first thing is the large diameter of the rings. It is true they do work for lights as small as 0.75" OD, but when you use a light that small the only part of the ring that actually contacts the light is the very top. So it's more like a clamp than a ring that hugs the body of the light. It's kind of hard to describe. I would just think that with the awesome engineers at Magpul they could design a ring that somehow collapses down on a smaller body light. That, or just send two sets of rings (small and large). Not a deal breaker, but it looks like my light has a 32" waist and is wearing a 40" belt.

The other thing I'm not crazy about is the way the bolt heads are exposed on the bottom edge of the panel. With the light at the 11 position, that frees up your 9 o'clock rail to get a full purchase with your hand. And, because this mount generally follows the contours of the XTM panels you can really utilize that rail section, right? Well, yes, but be prepared for those bolt heads to be right in the middle of everything ready to rub your little fingers raw depending on your grip. Again, not a deal breaker, but for anyone that's ever shot a LOT you know that even the smallest pressure point will turn into a big blister (or worse) at the end of the day. So, I really hate that the brilliant Magpul folks didn't spent a little more time and figure out a way to countersink those bolt heads to create a clean profile that isn't going to either tear up your hand or make you alter your grip.

I can still recommend this light mount, though. It's solid and will serve you well.b your little fingers raw depending on your grip. product_title: Gun Tote'n Mamas Pleated Slouch Bag
review_body:
My old concealed carry purse was finally beaten up enough that I had to replace it. Easier said than done because most CCW purses are designed for smaller handguns. I generally carry a 1911, and the height of most gun compartments isn't tall enough to allow for a fast, easy draw. The pistol gets hung up, if it fits at all. After a long search, I've found the perfect bag. The entire center compartment zippers open, allowing for concealed carry of virtually any handgun. As with most CCW purses, the compartment has a velcro pistol holster that can be adjusted for your gun of choice and the best angle to draw your weapon.

The bag itself is very good quality with sturdy construction. The handles are reinforced with steel cable, which is an absolute necessity. Both walls of the center compartment are padded, and there are compartments on either side to ensure that your weapon won't create any suspicious bulges. There are a couple of things that kept me from giving the bag five stars. The handles are a little shorter than I like. The non-weapon compartments are not wide enough to fit bulky items without looking odd. And the cell phone pocket is not wide enough to fit today's larger cell phones. If your cell phone can't be confused with a tablet, you should be okay, but it's too small for my phone.

Overall, I highly recommend this purse. It's worth every penny.

The glide of the foot pedals is soooo smooth - I hadn't realized I have been putting tension in my glutes instead of using my rotators lately.  Happy to say that my turnout is as good (if not better) than it was in collage when I was dancing! Yes, it is heavy for its size, but it is also brawny.

The spine of the blade is THICK (4.5mm), but it thins down very quickly; mine has what it seems to be a 15+15deg edge bevel, but as the blade is already thin (~0.55mm) where the bevel begins, the resulting bevel is short (as a comparison, my Manix 2 is ~0.80mm where the edge bevel begins).

Shaving hair sharp out of the box (not splitting hair yet), as every Spyderco I had.

If all you need is a pocket knife that cuts, there are many excellent cheaper options from Spyderco. This is a work of art, and as such, it costs more than its composing parts.

product_title: Tac Force Assisted Opening Folding Pistol Knife - Black
review_headline: An interesting pistol shaped knife for those who like to collect unusual blade products.
review_body:
I have been an avid collector of knives and other weapons (Japanese, Filipino and other Knives, swords, cane swords, guns, tactical pens, Yawara and other short sticks etc.) for most of my life. I purchased this Tac Force Assisted opening folding pistol knife because I thought it was a unique looking piece of equipment.

The blade is 3 1/2 inches long but the total length of this gun knife when opened is 7 1/2 inches. The tip and the blade is sharp stainless steel. This product was made in China where a lot of knives on the market seem to come from. The knife springs open when you pull back on the front sight. The entire unit is metal and feels great in your hand. It is very reasonably priced in my opinion.

I don't know how practical it is to carry this gun knife but I found it to be rugged, durable, and fun to play with opening and closing the blade portion. If you like collecting unusual blades and weapons you might want to check out this knife.

I only give five stars to products I review if they stand out in an extreme way, either by being fantastic for their price, exceptionally well-rounded, or performing in the top 1% of their class. In this case, all of the above apply.

As with the hundreds of knives before it, I put this S1 Forest Knife through a variety of tasks to evaluate it--batoning, rope cutting, chopping, slicing, food prep, thrusting, hammering, spine striking, digging, throwing--and it simply never faltered on a single one of them. The premium steel and robust edge geometry make the blade extremely rugged and resistant to damage and corrosion. The handle material is virtually indestructible, and creates a positive grip in dirty and slippery conditions. The tang protrudes through the pommel to form a hard hammering surface. I was able to take apart trees with this knife, dig a fire pit, break rocks, make tinder, make a fire starter, and make dinner, without sharpening once.

No exaggeration, this can do it all. It is the ideal survival knife, and well under $200! Any serious outdoors enthusiast or knife enthusiast should have one.

product_title: TacStar Side Saddle, fits 12 Gauge 6Rd Remington 870/1100/1187, Black
review_body:
I put this on a Rem 870 Express non-supermag. It fits great and holds shells very tightly. i dont believe any non-destructive jarring could pry the shells loose unless it was for an extended period and even then it would have to be for a very extended period. The plastic is very rigid and i havent tried, due to not wanting to break it, but i doubt you could pull the shell out 90deg from the saddle. i dont think the plastic would give enough but again, havent tried. Installation was easy just follow instructions. I had never installed one and didnt have too much issue. Make sure to use a brass punch if you need some force to remove the OEM pins. They are softer and should not damage the metal. I have a fully metallic upper on my Rem 870 and have to constantly run a oil rag over it to prevent rusting. I added a little extra lpx oil on the back and had it on for a good 3-4 months before removal. No rust at all, excess oil but no rust.

BEWARE: It may impede/ completely restrict your original stocks capability to fully cycle. It did on mine and i was forced to replace it with the Magpul forend. Wasnt an issue for me but if you want the original forend to stay on or cant afford to replace it... you might consider a smaller/different saddle.

product_title: TITLE Deluxe Leg Stretch
review_body:
I purchased the TITLE Deluxe Leg Stretcher by TITLE Boxing to improve flexibility and strength for myself (45) and my 4 boys (8 to 17 years of age) all taking TaeKwonDo. We have progressed into high rank where technique and execution are paramount to advancing further. I look for economical ways to improve ourselves; this item fulfills the economical and improvement requirements. It's not heavy and can be kept at arms reach for ongoing use. The price point is good but if you can get it below $25.00, it would be a good bargain, below $20.00, I wouldn't hesitate. If you can buy it used, it's almost impossible to damage to the point of not being able to use it.

The stretcher comes with two leg extensions, a pull bar, 3 nuts, bolts and washers, and a joining plate. All surfaces are painted black, the interfaces/contact points have a nice foam pad, the ends of the square tubular frame are capped with a black plastic cap. The joining plate allows the leg extensions to extend ≥180º.

The Leg Stretcher is productive in stretching the legs in the way it was intended. It's completely manual, so you control the amount of effort used and, therefore, based on the tolerance you have, the amount of stretch you can manage. I start a routine by stretching to my limit for a few seconds, backing off for a few seconds, shaking out my legs. I sit back down with the stretcher and am usually able to see immediate production by being able to pull the stretcher further back. I hold that for a few seconds and then do my TaeKwonDo workout.

It works. I'm happy.

If you feel pain anywhere except the intended stretch area, you can make adjustments where the Leg Stretcher contacts your leg. Make sure the foam padding is between your body and the bare metal.

High-end stretch machines pry your legs apart at the knees, this may be to prevent knee pain. I felt some knee pain with this device due to an MCL injury and side-loading myknee in an unnatural way (the knee is not a ball joint). This can be alleviated by bracing your knee, rotating your knee to prevent unnatural loading, or by moving the contact point of the leg stretcher from your ankles to an area above the knee, there's plenty of adjustment in the device to be able to use it in this way.

Don't overstretch, take your time, enjoy the results of greater flexibility.

product_title: Aim Sports M44/Mosin Nagant 91/30 Scope Mount (Short)
review_body:
I am glad that I read other reviews before purchasing this mount. Perhaps some people have a different situation because of variations in mosin nagants. My mosin nagant is a 1945 Izzy.

My basic scenario:
1) Sprayed rear sight's leaf pin with liquid wrench. Let sit a little.
2) Placed rifle in gun vise/clamp. Used steel punch (3/32) to knock pin out. Easily.
3) The top part of the sight came right out. I left the spring in for pressure on mount; as I planned to use the original pin and not the crappy screw that came with this mount.
4) I used a 1/8" drill bit and piloted the aluminum mount to be the same size as the original pin size.
5) I kept filing slowly from the base of the mount, putting it back to the sight, and reclamping with a C-Clamp to see if the holes lined up before I would punch the original pin through it. THIS TOOK FOREVER!!!!
6) After I punched the orginal pin; it holds it well in place. Then, I worried about adjusting/screwing in the set screws. They are very important in order to level the mount.
7) I did file the one allen screw; I didn't understand why they were all pointed when the one touches a flat base?

-- I mounted my LER scope and used a laser sight to get it close to where I need to be...hopefully for when I shoot later.
-- I hope that the mount holds (I hope that I didn't shave off too much from the bottom of it).

In all, this requires pretty many basic tools and patience...but for $5-8...It could be worth the modding.

My biggest complaint is lack of Customer Service. You can only send your questions through their web site then wait very patiently for them to answer. It took between 1-3 days for them to reply to my request, not always with a good answer to my question(s).

Best thing I like is that they partner with My Fitness Pal, which is my preferred weight and calorie tracker. Pulse, however, is not the only device to sync with MFP ... I suggest you look at others like Fitbit, etc before making a decision.
