I will admit, it became slightly easier after a few days. I even spent about an hour inserting/removing the firearm to shave down some of the pin that goes into the barrel. Finally, it became much easier to insert/remove the firearm while not wearing the holster. It is not possible to insert the firearm while wearing the holster, but I knew this prior to purchase. However, I was unable to remove the firearm from the holster while wearing it, I could eventually, but it took a lot of force and two hands. I would not trust my life on the ability to remove the firearm if I really needed it. Another thing I didn't like was it felt like the holster was going to pop out of my pants whenever I would sit down which made me a little nervous when going out to eat and other public places that required me to sit. I purchased this for an XD 40 and I ended up picking up another firearm that was slightly smaller to conceal carry with a completely different holster.

product_title: Barska Blackhawk Waterproof Monocular
review_body:
I received this as a gift from the wife for Christmas. We use the wish list feature on Amazon for our gift shopping and love it.

What I like:
The product is well built and fits in my hand perfectly.
I do were glasses but not when hunting. I did try using it with and without my glasses on and you will notice your field of view at 1000ft will be reduced with the glasses on but still usable. I will be using it without my glasses on so no worries there for me. The focus works great and stays adjusted when set.
As for how fog-proof and water-proof it is, time will tell. I don't go soaking my stuff in sinks of water for testing but I'm sure it will survive rain and snow.
I like the rubberized coating and soft rubber eye piece.
The lanyard is removable for mounting to a single rod or bi-pod and I like the lanyard.
So far it has met all expectations to include value.

Cons: non so far.

review_headline: Cheap Plastic, loose parts, jams easily, do not recommend
review_body:
Ok... so it feels and looks like a cheap plastic toy. My 25 round magazine kept sliding around in the loader and the bullets were not only getting pushed into the magazine but also below it to the sides of it and anywhere else possible. This caused jams.

So after about 16 or 18 bullets successfully loaded in my 25 round magazine using this loader, the force required to push another bullet in the magazine became stronger as the spring got more and more compressed (as it should). However the loader couldn't handle it and would not load another round into the magazine which lead Another Jam.

Applying additional force (anything greater than that of a child) to the loading gear only caused the plastic gear in the loader to start deform.

So it does work but for me it is cheap quality and jams often and does not allow a full load on a 25 round magazine. I dont think with continual use this product would last more than year before being destoyed either by accidently dropping it or wearing the gear out from repeated loadings. Would not recommend

review_headline: Small knife with loads of character
review_body:
Edit 3/5/2014
One of my negatives below was centering or alignment of the blade. It just required a little tightening of the pivot screw. so really no negatives as the thumstud and clip finish I mentioned obviously were just changed. Not significant at all. And this knife still truly deserves its 5 star rating.

You can see I did not order mine from Amazon. I had a gift card though a chain store so I purchased through them. I noticed there were only 3 reviews so I thought I would add my 5 star rating for this knife as well.

There is just suppose to be one version of this knife. I received one that did not have dual thumbstuds. It is easily reversible. The clip did not have the same finish as the titanium on the back. Also I have seen on youtube reviews that the spacing from blade to liner on either side when it is closed is dead even. Not so in my case. Not sure if that is a grinding issue or something completely unrelated? It has not been an issue so far.

Those are the only \\"negatives\\" (thumbstud, clip finish, alignment). The only one of concern for me would be the alignment but I highly double that is a real issue. The handle, fit and finish are what attractred me to this knife. If you can find it in a store I suggest handling it. I have not heard anyone say they didn't like holding this knife but it is a smaller knife with a bigger knife feel because of it's extra height/width.

Some do complain about the clip. I like the clip. Just takes a little pull to slide over my jeans watch pocket. With minimal effort I can get it on with one hand. Fits great. Just a little sticks out near the lanyard hole.

In my search for the smallest knife that did not feel like I was using a tiny knife the Boker Pipsqueak is what I came across. I really love the feel. Let's face it none of us are paying $200 for a knife because it strictly works. Most $50 knives are more than sufficient. This is a wellthought out design. The custom pimpsqueak knives from neil blackwood I've seen from $800 to $1200. Same steel and design just a different handle insert or clip finish Essentially you're getting a custom knife for just a little money.

product_title: Goson Leather Concealed Gun Carrying Handbag Purse Buckled Front Pocket with Silver Studs
review_headline: What Every Girl Who Carries Should Have
review_body:
This is a wonderful bag. I have been wanting a conceal carry purse for sometime and all the ones I have looked at in gun shops were like two hundred and up then I tried Amazon and was amazed at the price difference. Seventy three bucks? Surely they can not be nearly as good. I would have to say it's better. Not only for just conceal carry but also as a regular purse. I have five other purses and this is the one I am now almost always using.

First of all I should say I really hate the idea of carrying a gun in a purse. I preferred way is in waistband (IWB). No other way will give you faster access to your weapon and the chances of being away from it is lessened. However, when dancing on a club floor you really don't want some hot guy you finally got the attention of to put his hand on your lower back (or someplace else) and notice you have a gun. Real good chance it will end any future getting to know each other encounters. Plus, our clothes are just more form fitting and sheer than those of men making it more difficult to hide a gun. Yes, a purse can be a good option when you are trying to still carry.

For those club nights or another you decide to use the purse to carry this is a fine choice. The main area is split into two sections. I really like this idea compared to just one main compartment. You have the standard little zipper pouch in one then another zippered one in the other compartment along with a place for like 4 cards or whatever else you want there. They are both spacious area and you can carry a fair amount of stuff in them. I noticed one women said in her review here this purse is to big and would probably hold two guns. Not at all. I usually carry the Ruger LC9 which is a fairly small gun but I don't see fitting two inside holsters in it. Without, probably but would not recommend it. I have several bigger but with this kind of purse you do not want to stuff it full like any of you others. This will make it much harder for you to draw and replace your weapon should you need it. Of course, for days you carry IWB feel free to fill it up. Overall I would say this is a medium size bag. It won't hold your sink but you can put a fair amount of stuff inside. This purse does not have any side or back pockets. The reason for this is the gun is accessed by the two sides of the purse. These do zipper up of course and also lock which is a nice touch. They were kind enough to toss in not only two keys for it but four of them. Nice to have a few extras on hand. It does have a nice front pocket that is very convenient. The inner part is zippered while the outer pocket is held close by Velcro. I usually put my cell phone here and I can easily get to it when needed. The zipper part think 2 packs of smokes. Unlike most of my other purses this one is leather and the overall look and smell (I love the smell of leather) is very flattering. I also really like the strap. It is perfect. Stays well on my shoulder and not to long.

Overall I think this bag is fantastic and something every girl who has a carry permit should have for those times when keeping the gun on your body is not a good option, even if they are few. I do want to point out one thing before I close this. You need to practice your draw from this purse. This is true with any holster IWB or out but is especially true for purses. This brand or any other. There are some great videos online or even, better yet, see a qualified instructor for tips. It will take you longer to draw your weapon from this than another kind of holster. You also have a zipper and a Velcro strap that wraps around the gun inside to deal with in drawing. You also have the purse itself you will need to get out of your way. I know this only takes a second but is still much slower then drawing from a Kydex or leather holster on your body. Proper drawing techniques and practice is key to being able to quickly get to your weapon in a dangerous setting where every second counts.ts.

review_body: I had high hopes for this fitness tracker. I've had a long history with Polar HR monitors and thought this fitness tracker would be the one to get it right. I had a compatible HR monitor and I was anxious to get started. (I had a Fuelband, which I was generally happy with for 1yr. It died nearly a week after the congratulatory 1yr email and the 1yr warranty was up.) I picked this device because it would be one less step to incorporate my HR monitor data and it supposedly had sleep and inactivity monitors. After less than a month, I'm returning this as the software and the hardware are not ready for prime time. More than 50% of the time, synching with my iphone 5S results in a error message. More than 50% of the time, it takes 5-6 attempts to even get the display on the device to wake up. The sleep function is pretty useless. It tells you how long you slept (unlike the UP which tries to distinguish sleep quality- light and deep sleep). The inactivity monitor rarely went off for me  despite having a desk job where I KNOW I sit still for long stretches of time. Also, the battery is pretty poor. The 7-10 days advertised (real life was 3-4 days) only applies if you don't synch much- that straight from customer service. So if you don't ever care to track your progress, this is the fitness tracker for you! Customer service did offer to replace the device but looking at fitness boards, the issues I had are very common.

product_title: Concept2 Model D Indoor Rowing Machine with PM3
review_headline: A workout I look forward to. My "Me Time".
review_body:
I've been searching for a tolerable workout solution. This is not only tolerable, but actually quite enjoyable.

I'm 5'10" and finished high school in decent shape and size... probably about 165lb. I then went to college for a year and my life-style became so bad that I got fat so fast I had stretch marks on my sides at the end of the year. Then I got married and became a full-time computer programmer. Bad for the belly. I'm 23 now and 210lb.

I tried other things. I tried a treadmill, but it was just so boring and painful I could never muster the courage to get on it. I tried an elliptical, but it felt like I had to do it forever to really get anything out of it. Also it did nothing for the upper body. I tried running outdoors, but it was torture and I developed shin splints. I tried biking and I would have enjoyed it, but it hurt my butt too much to stay on it for more than 10 minutes. I tried kayaking, and loved it, but it's quite the hassle to load it up and drive to the water.

I was never aware of rowers till I watched the show House of Cards. I looked them up, and after a little research, I decided I had to have one. $900 is quite a commitment though so I decided to buy a $75 hydraulic one to try it out. Once I tried it I was hooked and immediately ordered this Concept2. Shouldn't have wasted the $75.

I started out doing 4000m in 25 minutes, and a month later I'm doing 6000m in 34 minutes almost every day. I'm very pleased with rowing. Total body workout, and it feels good. It's not torturous like running or p90x. I like that you just get on and go at whatever pace you want. I usually do the first 1000m at an easy pace to warm up.

If you're planning to get this, make sure you have a good way to track your weight. I can already tell that I've made progress with this machine in a month, but I didn't have a scale until the other day so I'm sad I don't know what the numbers are.

The machine itselfis quite a beast. Reviews of other rowers all complain of poor quality, but the Concept2 is built to last. I also love the log card that tracks your workout history automatically.

It is somewhat loud. I watch Netflix on my macbook while rowing at full volume (just the built-in laptop speakers). I have to turn subtitles on because I can't hear it well enough over the Concept2's fan.

I got blisters on my hands pretty fast, but they're turning into calluses now.

All that to say... rowing feels awesome, and $900 is a small price to pay for something you'll actually want to use to get in shape.

A polar sensor is missing and some screws missing. The machine has physical damage as well. It seems like due to poor packing it has gone through stress damage during shipping.
Issue 2: - I made the purchase enquiry few days before Black Friday(19th Nov). I clearly asked if there will be a deal or a promotion. I was told the company does not brings down the price, and even if there is , it will be matched as there is a 30 day money back and price match guarantee. The company offered a tablet on black Friday. I called back, couple of times and was told that they will check with the manager and get back to me. Haven't heard back yet and am going to return it today as I feel the matter is being dragged to 30 days return period expiry leaving me at a point where I will have no options.
Issue 3: - I talked to company representatives and every time I was told I will get a call back. Nobody has called back yet. Every time I get told they will check with the manager and get back to me with a resolution.
Issue 4: - The product was sold to me, credit card was charged but no receipt of purchase was sent to me, unless I called and complained about it.
Issue 5: - I was misinformed that there is no installation provided in Canada when the machine was sold, where as I received an email later on from the company that they offer installation from third party.
Issue 6: - On receiving the damaged package I called the company right away and informed them that I am not installing it so it can be sent back. I was informed to open the damaged package and start installing as they promised they can fix the issues later on if anything is missing. After all the hard work of assembling the machine, and not hearing back from them, I have to disassemble it and pak it to sip back. It's a waste of few days and efforts on top of the frustration that we just look at this un-assembled machine and I feel sad and stupid as it hasn't been used even once.
Issue 7: - You can make a purchase over the weekend but for any returns or issues you will always get the same response that they have to talk to their manager who is in on Monday and only available in afternoon. Only manager is allowed to authorize returns and he is hard to get in touch with.
I would assume that the manager wants to ensure good customer service, may be that's why he wants all the returns to go through him, but at the same time when you cant get in touch with him or he wont call you back then it would look as an excuse to not return. I called to return and I was told to call back on Monday. straight honest answer - there is nothing I can do about it.
Issue 8: - They can help with installation only on weekdays. If you think you would want to assemble the machine with someone over the phone to guide you. you have to do that during weekdays either after you return from work or may be take a day off. there is no installation support over the weekend.
I hope customers as well as company finds this review helpful.
Regards,
Shivam

review_headline: Better than the competition mixer unit
review_body:
I bought one of these to replace the unit I bought with Salt Terminator. While these superficially resemble one another, the Salt Away mixer has a third valve selection that allows you to run raw water through your muffs. I typically run fresh water through the muffs until the thermostat opens on the engine, then run the Salt Terminator through. This mixer unit allows me to do so without having to pull the muffs off between steps to insert the mixer unit. The competing Salt Terminator mixer only allows on or off operation; you can't choose fresh water/fresh water with chemical/off as you can with this one from Salt Away.

Remember, it doesn't matter what salt extraction chemical you use in this; any liquid will work. But this is a nicer way to get the job done.

Overall my biggest complaint would be how cheap the device feels and looks. I knew it'd be a bit odd selecting it but I didn't realized it'd look so odd. Kind of feels awkward being in public with it personally.

I'm not surprised or really dismayed by the idea of needing to sign up with a service to use the device as I had to do that with fitbit as well. I know that bothers people but with devices like this they tend to expect you to do that.

The device only tracks steps which isn't terrible if that's all your interested in but coming from the fitbit it felt like a definite step down (bad step humor) in terms of the functionality. There's some sleep tracking as others mentioned but I take off watches when I go to sleep so I have no clue how that works.

I'd say you should probably just get a normal pedometer instead -- it's nothing special but nothing to write home about.

product_title: Mountain Man Recurve Bow Stringer
review_body:
If you look at my reviews, I love to praise products. In this case, I can't say anything good. Last night I went to string up my bow with a brand-new, never used, highly recommended Mountain Man Recurve Bow String that I bought on Amazon. Having bought my first recurve bow decades ago, this was a no-brainer. Or so I thought. I was just about to finish stringing, sliding the second loop into place, when "whack!!!" (It was a *loud* "whack") The bow limb smacked me just above and alongside my right eye. Yes, Ouch! Confused at what just happened, I noticed the small end of the stringer was completely gone and flown who-knows-where, propelling the bow limb into my eyebrow. I won't go into the very bloody details, but I will say that just 1/4 inch more to the left and I'd have lost an eye!

Today I have the blackest of black eyes and a one inch long gash through my eyebrow. Please understand I am *not* complaining about Amazon. The Amazon service rep with whom I spoke was terrific! I'm only writing this review to caution prospective buyers to beware of this product. Oh: What actually happened with the bow stringer that caused the problem? The cord of the stringer is still intact, so what obviously happened is that the end piece was not fastened securely to the cord. It simply pulled loose the knot, let fly the bow, and nearly took me out in the process! Ultra-bad news! Such a defect in manufacturing could result in serious injury or death. Hopefully the stringer I bought was an exception, but I'll never chance another one from this company again!

product_title: Mil-Tec Military Army Patrol MOLLE Assault Pack Tactical Combat Rucksack Backpack 30L Dark Navy Blue
review_body:
This is a 30L bag, so obviously it's not a 3 day bag. It's not very wide either, but this you can obviously see on the measurements. It does expand outward a lot though. It is basically the same concept as the Maxpedition Falcon 2 (25L). Except this bag is made out of 600D polyester, which is way smother and much more flexible than 1060D Nylon Maxpedition uses, it feels like sand paper but is more durable and probably better water resistance wise. The polyester is much appreciated in terms of the feel, flexibility, and expansion for packing. I know because I have the Maxpedition Falcon 2. I think the Mil-Tec bag may have better stitching when it comes to the Molle webbing too, because it's less tight, so it gives a little and doesn't rip, it maybe double or triple stitched (not sure). Maxpedition is very regid, not flexible, so the molle can be ripped if pulled too hard, it happened to me. Unless my Maxpedition bag was defected.

Overall it compares very well to it's competitors as a tactical bag. The main difference is probably the material the bag is made out of and the compression Y strap that Maxpedition has. This is a great small bag.

review_body: I absolutely love love love this table!!! I have had it for almost a year now and I cannot find one single thing I complain about. I would recommend this product 100%! All my friends love the design and I wouldn't trade it for anything!!

product_title: Berkley Trilene Big Game Monofilament Custom Spool
review_body:
I've been using Berkley line for as long as I can remember. Its always held up well and the knots stay tied. Of course with large line like this Big Game version you'll need to use a wire leader. Don't blame the line if you don't. As with all fishing line you'll need to change it out once in a while, depending on how often you fish. It's also a good idea to give it a good rinse with fresh water after each use. The green tint on this version is great for the Gulf of Mexico, making it totally invisible.

Highly recommended.

review_body:
If you didn't buy it don't review it.
This is a authentically designed Smith and Wesson pistol with full metal construction.
SA and DA actions, smooth accurate trigger action , spare sights, spare magazine and barrel
change tool. The gun does 435 fps with a decent powercurve that lasts solidly for the
majority of the gas cylinder pressure. The barrel is rifled. The Grips are rubberized and
the balance is all there in this gun. Made in Germany. The pistol is a lot of fun, accurate enough
to 30 feet. Its the best made pellet revolver available with no real fault that I can comment on , only
praises. The price reflects on the fact that there is no other replica on this level of quality
available. Stainless matte finish..
Shoot it have fun, stay sharp.

It's basically disposable. Go buy a CRKT. Any CRKT would be nicer than this and not much more expensive. This is most definatley a "you get what you pay for" situation.

review_body:
This is a slick operating tool vice a reciprocating saw,but,the cutting blade bent so I can't rate it any higher.I am very content with Viking Solutions customer satisfaction. Without any provocation from me,they sent me a replacement for the Deer Splitter that I had a problem with. At 66 yrs.Old and disabled,this deer splitter is the best solution I have ever used. I have hunted for 50 years in many states including Vermont,N.Carolina,and Virginia and consider myself qualified to field dress and process any Deer. The Deer Splitter is the best thing I have used yet to Split a deer from one end to the other,without getting cut or messy.So much easier. This thing should have come around years ago !!! If you don't have one,or,have never tried one,then you need to get one and save yourself some time and aggravation { maybe some bandaids }.Many thanks for the product and for STANDING BEHIND IT.
Roger D.

review_body:

product_title: TAPOUT XT DVD FITNESS 12 WORKOUT TRAINING PROGRAM BASE KIT
review_body:
I bought this workout set from Dick's Sporting Goods almost exactly a year ago. I was on a bit of a health kick at the time, and had been doing various things to lose what ended up being about 25 lbs over the course of a year. At the time, I was looking for a toning and strength regiment that didn't involve a gym. I was also looking for something active and fast moving, something trackable (like with a calendar or timeline of some kind), and something with a "trainer".

I don't remember how I was introduced to Tapout XT specifically, but I was excited to try it.

I must say that I really enjoyed it. There was NO DOUBT that I was working out during these DVDs. There were some days I felt like passing out and would have sit down for 3 or 4 minutes to get my heart rate down and drink some water and level out. Other days I blasted through the workouts better than some of the participants in the DVD.

I noticed an obvious improvement in my abilities during the workouts, from the pushups, to the resistance bands, to my overall endurance, and of course my appearance. I think I lose like 4 lbs, and was upset about it bc I didn't understand why I wasn't losing weight, but I also was eating all things I thought were healthy but really were loaded with carbs or sugar. Right at the tail end of my Tapout XT 90 days, I switched to Atkins. I lost another 8 lbs. I had VISIBLE abs, I wasn't embarassed to be in a swimsuit, I was buying cuter clothes, people were noticing I had lost a lot of weight. I was buying pants in a size 6, when I was previously a 12. It was a good time for me.

I have a ridiculously small apartment, and I was still able to do all of the workouts without an issue. There were a couple moves that I felt like I maybe had to stifle them a bit, just for lack of space, but other than that I did not have any issue. You do not need 700,000 sq. ft to do this workout.

I snapped the band that came with the set, probably a month in. I got myself two different bands after that, with higher resistance. Man, does that make a difference. I also bought some weighted gloves, which also make a difference.

I did the Ultimate Abs DVD 5 days a week, instead of the 1 or 2 that the calendar suggests. Abs are an issue for me and I felt that once a week was not enough. I saw results much quicker that way, and the DVD is 15 long, there is no reason to not do it.

Once you get good at the moves and have done the DVD rotation a few times, you can start to just listen to headphones and mute the TV. After awhile, Mike gets annoying. I also do not like some of the participants in the back. A couple of them are wayyyy too fit for the average person to be seeing doing this work out. Its like, okay we know that these are professional fitness people (which Mike tells us), so of course they're going to be beasts. There are a decent number of average people as well , though, so that makes up for it. Sometimes the people have to take breaks like a regular person would have to, or struggle with the moves. It makes you feel like you're doing this with people who aren't perfect, and it also makes you feel kind of badass when you do something better than them.

Are there dozens of other workout sets like this? Yes. So really just choose one and try it. I did not do P90X bc it required some equipment that didn't come with the set, and I was sick of hearing about P90X. I have a few friends who are into MMA training, and I figured I'd try something in that family. I've always wanted to do something that would "tap" into my sometimes aggressive nature, and these workouts really require you to like get angry and really punch, kick, etc. It was a good release.

In conclusion: totally decent workout. You will notice that you get better, and you will probably want/require heavier equipment like the weighted gloves and the heavier resistance band. I saw a review early on when I purchased this that told the same thing and I was kind of like whatever, no. But he was right. And it was actually exciting getting into it and looking for heavier stuff. I felt like part of the fitness world.

The only bad thing... and this may just be my own issue, is that when it's over, it's over. You've gone so hard for three straight months, eating differently, working out 6 days a week. When this set is over, you're kind of like----- okay..... and now what? I didn't want to do the set all over again. I guess I could have and I probably should have. I moved on to a Nike workout thing on my phone, bought some weights. I did it for awhile, but eventually fell off. That was around July. Since July I have gained back 10 pounds and I see it. I don't eat well anymore, and I don't work out. That is my own issue. But the fact that this was just a 90 day thing, DID psychologically do something to my motivation once it was over. So my advice to new users is to have a plan for what to do AFTERwards. Figure out how you will maintain what you've accomplished. If you want to just go down to three workouts a week, then do that, if you want to pretend its not 90 days and do it all again, then do that. But don't just stop and try to figure it out at that time, bc you will fall out of your routine and it will be becomes REALLY easy to just not workout anymore.

I have all my DVDs right next to me and I am online right now getting a PDF of the calendar bc I am going to start it up again. I don't like being a yo-yo exerciser, but I figure it's better I begin it again, than just succumb to the comfort of laziness. Plus I can tell that other people notice that I've gained my weight back, and that just sucks.

I recommend this product, and good luck!! Have major water on hand, and a towel, and somewhere cool nearby for you to cool down. I had to step outside most days. You WILL feel pumped after the workouts, and you WILL be sore as all hell. I could barely walk, sit down, or reach over my head the first couple weeks.

product_title: BBB bike tools chain tool Nautilus 2 BTL-05
review_headline: Product description inaccurate, but the tool worked well.
review_body:
The spare pin was not included. The spare pin was not listed on the package. There was no place to store the spare pin inside the product or on the open card it was zip tied to. I bought this specific product because the description said it had a spare pin. I foolishly believed the description and must shop again instead of having this simple need fulfilled.

The chain tool itself looks and feels cheap. The metal part has scratches and surface irregularities in the form of small random bumps. The black rubber handle looks old and used, with scratches, scuffs, and a subtle white haze. I wouldn't mind these minor problems after I used the product a few times or stored it with other bike tools, but to see such low quality in something brand new sent the message that the factory did not care about what they were doing.

I just checked the company's website. Their photo of a Nautilus II BTL-05 chain tool showed a notch next to the handle with a place to store the spare pin. The product shipped to me was different, with no notch, just a flat, angled surface. Evidently this version, labeled on the package as a Nautilus II BTL-05, is different and inferior to the one described here on Amazon. Again, I bought this one because it was the only one that offered a spare pin, a spare pin that I needed to replace one lost from a mini chain tool. I thought having the included spare pin would be convenient and save money. Now I have wasted my money thanks to wrong information in Amazon's product description. When companies redesign products, they should change the model numbers so customers aren't severely disappointed and angered after buying things and finding they don't match the descriptions. It is also the responsibility of the seller to accurately describe products and check them to make sure they match before sending them out to customers. Wrong information wastes everyone's time, but I guess it is good from the seller's point of view to keep customers ignorant and in the dark.

I can't trust any product information now. It would have been easier to go to a physical store and see similar products first hand rather than be digitally lied to.

review_headline: Nice build, smooth ride, and a cool computer
review_body:
This elliptical is a nice upgrade from my [[ASIN:B001DEV3FI Horizon Fitness EX-57 Elliptical Trainer]] that I purchased a few years ago. The ride on this elliptical is smoother and it has some extra features and a much better computer.

=== Assembly ===
The box is very large and very heavy. The delivery person was nice enough to bring it into the house even though he didn't have to. I assembled the unit myself in a little over two hours. It was not easy to do alone. A few of the parts are pretty heavy and large, and some parts were difficult to hold up and screw in at the same time with just two hands.

One assembly tip: the manual has you connecting and pulling the wires for the computer through the unit and then assembling the rest of the unit before testing the computer. DO NOT DO THIS! Do yourself a big favor and test the computer first. Do it twice: once after the initial connection of the wires to the base (to make sure your wire connection is tight enough and to make sure the computer works); then do it again after installing the large part that the wires feed through (before assembling the rest of the unit). Trust me, you do not want to learn that your connection wasn't tight enough and then have to disassemble the entire thing.

=== Build and Features ===
Build quality is nice. The ride is smooth and the entire unit feels heavy duty and sturdy. There are plastic \\"wheels\\" in the front for wheeling the machine around, although the build quality of these things make me a little nervous if I have to wheel it around in the future, especially across a wood floor. There are also plastic levelers for leveling the unit on uneven floors.

The foot pedals are large and grab onto my sneakers just fine. The part of the unit that raises and lowers the incline seems sturdy and the adjustable incline adds an additional challenge and feel to your workout.

The computer has a lot of features for multiple users and for setting up different goals based on time, calories, and heart rate. There is a wireless heart rate monitor that operates with uncoded POLAR-compatible chest strap models that operate in the 4.5kHz - 5.5kHz range, or you can use the contact heart rate sensors located on the stationary handles.

There are two LCD screens. The larger one allows you to select users, goals, and track your progress using bars. The smaller one below is configurable and shows a variety of information like your calories burned, heart rate, time, distance, etc. Using the computer, you can also view a history of workouts and by uploading data to a USB drive, you can view a detailed history on Schwinn's website.

The built-in adjustable fan is a nice little touch but don't expect to be blown away... it is nice for gently cooling your face a bit. There is an AUX jack for plugging in an MP3 player or your smartphone and the speakers are adequate for listening to music in case you do not have any other speakers in the same room.

The water bottle holder is large enough for most water bottles, and there is a ledge to place a book or tablet on (although it will cover the larger LCD but not the smaller one below it).

=== Summary ===
So far, this appears to be a quality machine for this price range. I have been using it for a week and a half and am much happier with it than my old elliptical. product_title: Power Balance PRO ION Silicone Wristband - Genuine (Various Colors)
review_body:
I've always been skeptical of these low powered magnet and hologram thingies that people have touted for years. But as I'm older now and have some regular aches and pains, I got curious about the Power Balance Pro after asking several people who wear them about their experience.

I don't presume to know how it works - if it's psychosomatic or actually causing change that works - but it DOES work for me. I did not get it for athletic performance or balance (I don't have problems there...) but I do have bursitis in my right shoulder and live with inflammation in my elbow, wrist and fingers. Within minutes of putting this Power Balance wristband on, I could tell a noticeable difference in lowered discomfort. Especially on cold, rainy days. When I take it off, it only takes 30 minutes or usually less to notice an increase in said discomfort. Maybe it's all in my head but it is certainly working for me and I am happy to have the Power Balance Pro. Whether it's psychosomatic or something else, the end result is lowered discomfort, so I'm happy.

Another really nice surprise was opening the package and finding a second unit with the word/label \\"Gift\\" on it. That is nice, and it's classy, as well as very appreciated! I'm a believer now and give this thing (and the vendor who shipped it SUPER fast!) 5 stars because in my world it deserves it. I would buy again and from the same vendor.

product_title: 110 Percent Play Harder Men's Clutch Compression Tights + ICE for hips, glutes, lumbar, ITBand, quadriceps, hamstrings and knees
review_headline: Great Idea, Good Quality, Limited Application, Not as expected
review_body:
I really wanted these two work. Someone I know has a pair and said they were great. Its an excellent concept so I decided to get my own. I wear all kinds of compression almost every day when exercising and have several top brands.

I cycle 3 times a week, cross fit 3 times a week, and yoga 3 times a week. Each time I am wearing some variation of compression skin whether its a top, bottom, sleeve, warmer, recovery etc. Every single other compression item from every other brand works perfectly and fits perfectly. These 110 tights however have 1 major flaw in their design which make them absolutely useless for my purposes.

First off, they look great, fit great and the material is very nice looking and feeling. The compression is also substantial and seems to work well. Certainly a high quality product so there is no problem there. Where they dropped the ball is, there is a large continuous stitching that starts at one knee, comes up the thigh slightly inward, continues across the pelvic region, then back down the other side to the other knee. It also has an identical one on the backside. This appears to bring the inner thigh panels, and crotch panels, and bind them to the front and rear leg panels. Herein lies the problem.

The location of the stitch and the fact that it is continuous rather than stopping and starting again at the leg/pelvic crease, renders these useless for any type of fitness where you would require to squat or lunge in any fashion.

Every other pair of compression tights I have has the legs, and crotch, butt and inner thigh, all independent from each other to allow maximum movement and functionality, with no restriction point.

These 110 tights are basically for sitting and recovering only. If I were to squat down rapidly, they would explode and I would be naked. :)
I was under the impression that these were able to be used as fitness tights, then you can immediately insert the ice packs and begin recovering right away. That is how its pitched and presented. They even come with a thermal bag for the ice packs to be taken with you to use right after whatever you do. That is not entire true.

Bottom line. I am returning them due to their limited application. I can't see spending $200+ on them. If you are only looking to walk, light jog etc... and or just use them to sit around in then they are great. If you want to do anything vigorous in them, make sure you wear underwear in case you blow em out in public.

product_title: 3 in 1 Game Table - Octagon 48" Bumper Pool, Poker & Dining in Antique Walnut By Berner Billiards
review_headline: Nice looking table that plays well and is built to last
review_body:
Excellent table. This table looks like it should cost more. It has excellent quality wood, a good craftsmanship (hard to tell from the pictures, the feet have animal claw shapes carved into them), and best of all it pretty much comes assembled. Just bolt the table to the base, and the base to the feet. Done. The bumpers are attached, the leather pockets are attached, and the felt is glued on. Beauty. The bumpers, while plastic, are a nice composite plastic type that perfectly emulates the old fashioned rubber; this is a good thing because rubber bumpers wear out a lot faster so here you have the best of both worlds.

This table is also all inclusive; you get the bumpers, balls, two sticks (which are two piece and fit inside the table when taken apart), the tabletop and even pool chalk. The sticks are nice quality, too, and the correct size for the table. It does not come with chairs and I'm glad because the package was heavy enough. The guy who delivered it helped me drag it into my apartment, so that was nice of him. Someone always answers the phone at this company, too, and when I requested a day and a time for delivery they honored it.

I actually bought this for my father's surprise birthday present, and a friend and I dragged it into his house and assembled it in about ten minutes while he was upstairs. Made for a great surprise. Note, however we had our own tools; they include only a basic sheet metal stamped wrench. All you need is an 11/16 wrench or socket head and a level.

The stock pictures are a shame because it doesn't do it justice. Even the pool sticks have a really nice finish to them that shines.

I watched the videos on the humanxgear web pile, and there is no way I am going to use this gadget as in those videos. HumanX wants you to lie out flat on your back, so that you are stretching your back as it curves over the gadget. Then use those muscles to sit up, crunch, and so forth. If I did any of that, I would be in pain for a week.

I use this gadget to *limit* the stretch. I do sit-ups, but I use the gadget to limit the bottom half of each sit-up to about 45 degrees, measured against the ground. Works for me.

As one reviewer noted it does say the associated App is free then it appears you have to pay for it. However, I called Lifetrak and after a bit of a delay they sent me a promotional code and I downloaded the App for free. The Blue tooth connected perfectly. All seemed fine. Then it happened. I got a Low Battery warning after having the unit for a week. I kept the unit on over night and by morning the low battery warning had disappeared, the unit lost all its data and reset to 1-1-13.

I got a return label from E-signal which requires I pay postage for the return, so I have the prospect of being out of pocket for a device I do not have. I am going to call Lifetrak today to see what they will do before I return it to E-signal.

Sadly, this was a great product when it briefly worked. I will update this review once I hear from Lifetrak. They could also solve the dismay of purchasers who are told that the App is free only to discover that it costs $1.99 by including in their literature and on their website an explanation that a promotional code is available for a free download.

product_title: MetalTac Airsoft Speed Loader with Capacity of 100 Bbs
review_body:
This item, which is cheaply made, flimsy, and mass produced, can still benefit from some backyard tweaking. First up is the adapter, which is ill-fitting, prone to movement - and in my case complete detachment, which resulted in errant BBs' bouncing everywhere. Fix this by using modeling glue to permanently attach this adapter to the body of the speed loader. Once this adapter is secure and acting as one with the loader, your speed loading will increase in efficiency. Second, for the adapter to be able to slide over the the magazine port (mine is a mag for the HFC Mac 11), I sanded down the insides of the adapter, where they come in contact with the magazine. (You might do this first, if necessary, before gluing it to the speed loader, to minimize the intrusion of sanding dust.) This will lessen the chance of the adapter splitting because of excessive spreading of the flanges, when pushed over the magazine port. Finally, when loading, you will notice a \\"sweet spot\\", where BBs seem to suddenly load without resistance. Find this sweet spot right off the bat, by holding the speed loader gently rather than firmly, thus allowing you to find the natural angle and the least resistance to loading.

Again, this item is cheaply made and inexpensive. But work with it, doing your best to make it work - and it should work for you.

product_title: Under Armour Men's The Original UA Fitted Tank
review_headline: I don't see what the big deal is
review_body:
I'm a huge fitness person; martial arts, lifting, cardio, and even the occasional "P90X" tape, I do it all. With that being said, one thing I don't think about too much is my clothing. For general exercise, I have some cheap sleeveless workout shirts and shorts. That's about it. But I wanted to try "Under Armour" as these products are supposed to be so high and mighty in the fitness world. And for one reason in particular... the cheaper shirts I have stink! Even after washing them my workout clothes smell awful. They are not regular shirts but some off-brand workout shirts of similar material that help absorb sweat away from the body. With that being said, I was willing to spend a little more on exercise clothes if it could get rid of the odor.

I looked in to the Under Armour line. Supposedly this shirt has "Anti-Odor technology prevents the growth of odor-causing microbes". Well, after wearing this through about 10 workouts (and washing after each use), this shirt is starting to stink like all the others. So much for their anti-odor "technology". This material doesn't feel like anything special over the cheap workout shirts I got in Target. To pile on top of that, the under armour logo kind of started peeling off after the first wash.

Lastly, I don't like the size. I am a medium and bought a men's large (to have extra room for exercise plus I know this is a "fitted" tank top). I'm not crazy about the "fitted" feel, I think they make these shirts a bit too tight of a fit. I bought a size up, I can't imagine what the medium would feel like.

All in all, I don't think the price justifies the quality. The logo peeled off after one rinse, the odor technology sucks, and I think these shirts are a bit tight. With Under Armour, I think you are paying for the name. There is, in my opinion, no difference between these and a cheap workout shirt from wal mart or someone else. You are only wearing it while you exercise, who cares where it's from or what it looks like? I would consider some of their other exercise clothing but for regular shirts, or at least a simple tank top, I don't see what the big deal is to spend $25 on.

product_title: Weslo Cadence G 5.9 Treadmill
review_headline: After 2.5 years of use I'm reviewing this
review_body:
I've owned this treadmill for 2 and a half years now, so I feel I can give an informed review of this thing.

I actually purchased this from a store other than amazon which sounds like \\"fall-part\\" for $220, which included shipping. I think it is more expensive now at the other store too, my timing was lucky.

I bought this treadmill because it seemed relatively sturdy for a cheap price. Anything cheaper starts to look like a bicycle without wheels. Anything more expensive seemed to be adding a dubious amount of value for great additional cost. This was inexpensive enough that I wouldn't feel too bad if it broke after a couple years. The common story I heard when inquiring with people about treadmills at home was, \\"I have one, but its broken now\\".

It is still working for me. I just walk on it while playing on my laptop computer, at 2.4 mph. It shuts off automatically after 100 minutes, but you can just restart it if you want to keep walking.

The walking tread is plenty long enough that I can put my home-made treadmill desk over it and have no fear of falling off the end (I'm 5'10''). The walking tread is luckily just short enough that I can fit it into my buick lesabre, if I position it diagonally from passenger front seat to driver-side back seat. I didn't know this when I got it, I was just lucky. It is tricky to get in there though because I have to make it unfold after sticking it partway in to get it in my car. The console stand rests across the back seat. And I have to remove the base with the 2 wheels on it, but there are no wires or electronics in the base, so there is no risk of messing something up by taking off that piece. Save the allen wrench to do this.

I would be afraid to remove the console to move the treadmill. In the instructions it states in bold not to remove console because the wire connection can be broken. When I put it together, the wires do snap in, and there is no way to safely unsnap theconnection without breaking it. So I leave the console on, and it just barely fits in my car.

I do notice that the tread slows down ever so slightly when I put my foot down, but it is very slight. It is very consistent though and hasn't worsened over the years, so I don't want to fiddle with it when it is so reliable. The consistency of the slight slowdown makes me think it is the relatively light motor straining rather than an actual belt slip.

I didn't notice right away, but it does have a slight incline. You can remove the incline by lifting up the tread and flipping out the plastic feet on the bottom of the end. You can see the feet in the picture on this site, folded down to level it out. I leave them folded in all the time. You certainly cannot push a button to adjust the incline like an expensive treadmill. You get what you pay for.

It has a 250 pound weight limit according to documentation at the time of my purchase. Not an issue for me, but it could be for others. This website says 275 pounds it the limit. Maybe they decided to bump up the limit after some stress testing.

This treadmill has exceeded my expectations for its price. I'm glad I got it. It has minor drawbacks (minimal motor, not the best for running), but when you consider the price you could easily do much worse. And if you're just gonna use it to build a walking workstation, the disadvantages are irrelevant.

product_title: Airoh Aviator 2.1 Carbon Helmet Large
review_headline: Exceptional - Light, Comfortable, Runs small in size.
review_body:
I just received this helmet and am surprised how light it is. I've never had an issue with my helmet feeling too heavy. I've been using some of the less expensive Fox and main stream brands in the mid 100's range for pricing. My issue was ALWAYS in overheating. I was really looking for the helmet with the best venting.

I've not ridden with it yet so I can't speak for that but it certainly has internal venting that I've not seen anywhere else.

I read a lot about it's weight as that's kind of their main selling point. I kept thinking, "yeah, that's nice". I was pretty surprised from the moment I first tried it on what a difference it was over my other helmet. I suspect that after a ride with this, if I ever put my other helmet back on it would feel like I was riding with a brick on my head. This feels more like my kid's bicycle helmet and not a full faced motorcycle helmet.

This does run small. I've always wore a medium helmet. Everything I read talks about this being kind of a "narrow" helmet. My medium in the Fox helmets fit fine but was perhaps just a hair on the large size. This one in medium fits tight. I wish I'd could have gone to a store to try them on to see how large fits.

If your current helmet is a tight fit you should probably go a size larger. I'd been in trouble if my Fox was tight fitting and I'd ordered the same size.

Another note, there's not much room for your ears. I ride with a Scala Rider G4 headset. It was pretty iffy putting these in. So I did a little modifying of the foam to give just a little more space for the ears.

If you ride with a headset this might be a be too tight unless you are willing to remove a quarter inch of foam in the ear pocket. I hated doing that but I had to order this helmet out of Europe as they didn't have the 2014 model I wanted anywhere in the US at this time. Perhaps if I could have tried on a large I'd have gone withthat and the ear space would have had enough room for my helmet speaker. It really was close.

product_title: Ka-Bar Bowie Black Finish
review_headline: KBAR Large Heavy Bowie Survival Knife
review_body:
I have had this knife for 4 years. I"m trying to find something about it I do not like. (wish it had an exposed tang) instead of the modified full tang. I've beaten the heck out of this knife. I mean it's cut a few cords of wood. I use an axe to cut wood - (Big Northeast Oak) Fiskars X27 Axe is AWESOME. Than when I pile wood I baton it with a knife while hitting it with a nice piece of wood about 14"inches long and heavy enough to move the Knife into the wood. This is called Batoning. Youtube "How to Baton wood"

I Baton to make the wood I cut with my axe into smaller wood for the Wood Stove. This knife does it all. It can process large logs and also cut wood into very thin narrow pieces for kindling. It can cut branches it's a "fast" knife. Light enough but heavy at the same time. It is my go to knife. I love the Blade length and LOVE LOVE LOVE the handle. It's big and I have long fingers. It is a joy to hold this. It's razor sharp and also a VERY good looking knife. I consider this a Medium to Large Survival Blade. It really "Slices" through wood. You can hear how the wood "cracks" it does not "bust the wood open" it' literally slices it. That's because it has a flat grind. I have
Other knives. The Ontario SP8 Machete can handle bigger jobs being it's .26 inches the entire length of the blade where as this Knife the Kabar Heavy Bowie starts off as .23 thick than tapers down til the tip (after all it is a "Bowie" style Blade" The Ontario is "Heavy" I consider that a "Big" Survival Blade. The KABAR is more all around and it chops smaller branches better cause of the blade configuration. The SP8 will chop wood branches faster - the SP8 is more of a heavy chopper while the KABAR is more of a heavy slicer if that makes sense. I use the KABAR as my Medium Batoner. For BIG BIG wood I have other knives one custom 10.5 inch blade 5/16th's thick *Cost over $250 and the Ontario Sp8 cost $44.00. My other Medium chopper is the Ontario SP19 7 inch Blade. The Sp19 was discontinue from Ontario a few years ago. IF you've read this far you are very interested in the KABAR Heavy Bowie. If I had to have one blade it would be this one. Is was my every day favorite but now I like the Ontario SP19 better cause it's a little smaller and a little tougher and easier to wear on a belt - - but I've hit the KABAR with everything I have - even when it hits massive knots in wood and I would have to try to pry the knife out - this knife handled it all - it's a GREAT GREAT blade that I can not see them discontinuing unless they make it smaller like everything else due to the rising prices of metals. This Knife is a GREAT one to have on the Farm or truck or back pack. This is NOT a belt knife. I say anything larger than the Cold Steel SRK is not for a belt. PS - this one chops REALLY well also. No need to spend $90.00 on a knife get this one as your all around big knife you will not be sorry. Bigger some times is better.

product_title: Sandpiper of California Bugout Backpack
review_headline: Not what it used to be
review_body:
I bought two bags (black, tan) in Iraq and, to my regrets later, gave them to my friends. Since then I yearned to get another one for myself. The price of this backpack in the US is disheartening. It is perhaps about 2.5 times what I paid in a war (Green) zone. But what disappoints me the most is not the price, it's the quality.

The one bought from Amazon feels rather plasticky. The material used seems rather different. It's hard for me to describe it, but I feel like I am missing something. Unlike the ones I got in Iraq, it does not convey the feeling of toughness and reliability. I share concerns with other reviewers about the zipper. The metal clip to connect the harness is also of questionable durability: it's small and of low quality. The backpack is lighter but have rougher edges. Somehow I feel this is a different product, but sadly inferior to the ones that I once had.

I suspect the SOC switched the producing factory in China (perhaps for lower cost) and its quality goes along with it.

I returned this product

product_title: Wireless Security System Remote Control
review_headline: A great simple alarm for the money, easy to install if not to program
review_body:
This alarm is easy to install, but a bit of a pain to program! It's worth it though because this alarm does what it says. It is set it and forget it. The infrared sensor is easy to mount (in drywall you don't need a drill, just bear down on the screwdriver and the screws go right in). The slide-out mounting of the infrared sensor is good too, makes it easy to change the battery (when the battery's low the flashing light will change its pattern telling you to change it). You can buy extra remotes easily, they are widely available, but you will have to make the control box learn" the new remote before you can use it (the remotes come with instructions on how to do it but like i said, programming this thing is a pain!) It has a feature that will call you and tell you if the alarm has been activated and a phone cord jack for that too. I don't know how well that works because i don't have a land line. It's expandible, you can add lots of sensors wherever you need them, i think up to 6 (but it comes with one so you have to buy them seperately).

You can set a 5 second alarm delay or a 30 second delay. Like i said, programming is a true PITA, i could only get it set for 30 seconds so that's where it is staying at. But the programming part is really it's only flaw-that's why i give it 5 stars. It's easy to install, the remotes are available and cheap, you buy it once since there's no service contract to pay. Installation is easy, you can use push pins to hang up the control box. You don't have to splice any wiring all you need is a power outlet. And you can easily take it with you and reinstall it in your new place if you move.
After two years it is still working great.

In the mean time, the only thing I can say is that \\"when it's locked, you can't get into it\\". The positive is that I know from experience that, if you don't have the key and the safe is locked, \\"you can't get into it\\". Perfect if I'm a thief. Not good if I'm the owner. Will provide further updates on how long this locked steel box remains in my basement safely guarding the nothing that is in it.

Update: AMAZON to the rescue! I painlessly submitted a return request, repackaged the safe (thank goodness I hadn't destroyed the packaging), greeted the delivery company the next day when they came to pick up the safe, and my new safe (with keys and other accessories) arrived within two days. AMAZON even alerted me that the defective item was on its way back to them and that I wouldn't be charged. Now, that's what I call customer service. I've increased my rating to 4 stars because the safe is what I needed at a price I didn't mind paying. I am holding one star back because of the packaging.

product_title: HumanX Kettlebell Arm Guards
review_body:
I have been doing the Skogg System workouts for a few months. I live in a small, rural town with no kettlebell trainers in sight. It might be an issue with form since I don't have a trainer to correct me, but even after watching many YouTube videos and kettle DVDs, I can't seem to do cleans without getting a few bruises on my wrists after an intense Kbell workout. It doesn't help that I seem to bruise easily on my own! To help remedy my problem, I bought [[ASIN:B008VI716E CFF Kettlebell Wrist Guards; Great for Cross Training and Kettlebell Training (Kettlebell not included)]].

How the HumanX arm guards compare to the CFF (which I've been using for a few months)-

COLOR: I have black CFF guards, but it also looks like you can get pink. HumanX has 3 color choices.

SIZE: I'm an average-sized female, and for both being one-size-fits-all, the HumanX are definitely larger. The CFF are maybe 2/3 of the size (in terms of height). On me, the HumanX guards fit looser than the CFF (but not so loose that they are useless).

PROTECTION: this is the biggest difference. The CFF has a plastic rectangle sewn between the layers. As long as that rectangle is in the correct location, you are protected from cleans and things. The HumanX, as you can somewhat see from the product image, has long, skinny sections of protective layers that sort-of hinge, so your wrists are protected all the way around. It's not a plastic material, just extra padding.

If I'm doing a workout with lighter weights, a shorter duration, or less wrist-banging moves, I would definitely choose the HumanX guards. I like the 360 degree protection and not having to worry about aligning the plastic piece (as in the CFF) to the correct location for cleans, etc. However, if I'm doing a workout where I need a bit thicker of protection, I'd go with CFF for that tougher plastic protective layer.

So, 4 stars because they are great for general kettlebell use, but if you're workout is a little more intense, these might not be the best form of protection for you.if you're workout is a little more intense, these might not be the best form of protection for you.

review_body:
This is a follow-up review on this item.
After owning this rifle for a few months, I in fact would not purchase again. I've come across some design flaws... Firstly, being a break barrel rifle, the end of the barrel is not exactly in line with the back half of the barrel in which you place the scope. My particular unit is so out of line, that it is indeed impossible to zero my scope. Removing the scope and placing the windage adjustment on the built in sights as far off to one side as I can get's me close enough to hit a squirrel at roughly twenty yards. Which is good enough for me. Second issue I have is, the vibration caused by the spring. It is normal to have vibration on an air rifle, but mine was enough to cause the screw that holds in my windage adjustment on my sight, to fall out. I had to super glue in the piece of the sight after hunting for it in my yard for three months. Overall, the build quality is nice on this rifle... Just need to make improvements on the rear sight, and better QC at the plant for alignment of the two halves of the barrel.

product_title: MTM Snap Caps, Ga 20
review_headline: Poor quality.  Will chip and crack if cycled through shotgun.
review_body:
MTM makes many fine products, but they really should have stopped making these cheap poor-quality plastic snap caps years ago. But people still buy them because they are inexpensive. If you are just going to use them for long term storage to release the firing pin spring, they will obviously work just for that.

But if you've got a pump or bolt-action shotgun (yes, there are bolt shotguns), the rim on the snap cap will be chipped and worn away by the shotgun extractor whenever you cycle the snap caps from the chamber. After you do this a few times the extractor may not be able to grab the chipped rim and extract the snap cap.

The firing pin cushion is also quickly permanently indented after a few strikes. And the body of the snap cap may crack if cycled many times in a pump gun.

Metal snap caps are much more durable. Every brand of plastic snap cap that I've used in revolvers, rifles, and shotguns have fallen apart after a while.

product_title: Men's Tactical ColdGear® Compression Leggings
review_body:
Sadly only bought ONE of these and the matching tops for a hunting trip that had (according to the thermometers we had) temperatures of 16 F during the coldest times (not including windchill factor of the snowstorm, and rainstorm that hit us) and 35 F during the warmest clear and sunny days. The trip was 2 weeks long and thankfully I had additional UA ColdGear that I had purchased at a previous date because wearing the same thing multiple days in a row gets a little uncomfortable. Even though I only had 2 pairs of tops to rotate and one bottom that I wore every day, there was no bad odor that I had to deal with. I did however air them out in the tent at night when I slept. I wore these compression tops and bottoms as base layer, plus a cotton T-shirt, and a flannel long sleeve under my very thin but insulated waterproof jacket and bibs and stayed very warm. The only times it got chilly and uncomfortable was when the snowstorm and rainstorm hit us and the winds were upwards of 20-30mph, plus laying/sitting still at a stand with this happening doesn't help either.

Needless to say, if I had not purchased these for my trip, I would have not lasted the 2 weeks in that weather. My only regret is that I only purchased 1 pair before the trip. I would have preferred to have 3 pairs of each so that I would have been able to rotate Once I got back I ordered another pair (black though to have a different set).

I also purchased the camo UA liner gloves to fit under my Goretex gloves and Under Armour Men's ColdGear® Infrared Hood that also helped, especially when wind, rain, and snow roll down your neck. I love the UA coldgear because it is extremely light for the warmth it gives you, very tight to skin so you forget you have it on as it is very comfortable, and very fresh as well for when you sweat. I will use this gear for skiing, hunting, camping, and any other activity that requires warm clothing with light weight for high activity. Heck I might just wear it whenever it is cold out and I don't feel like wearing heavy jackets :)

The curved, hook-blade is what works. Also, from experience, cheaper rescue knives do not break glass very well, because the glass-breaker stud isn't hard enough. The Buck Redpoint Rescue Knife breaks glass very easily with just a light tap.

product_title: Browning BTC 1 Trail Ranger Camera, Brown
review_body:
Super Fast Shipping! 11-6-13
4 stars at this point based on the review I read on this camera from trailcampro.com -
I will put this thing in the field immediately, and write an updated review in a month or so.
With a 0.68sec trigger, and a 2.1sec recovery time, it should be a decent camera, especially for the price.

01-10-14 Update:
Camera functions flawlessly. Great pics, day and night, no white out, no over-exposure to speak off. 3 shot rapid fire mode is excellent, and with triggers spaced 5 sec apart, you'll never miss a shot. Trigger distance and flash out to about 60' - well beyond my expectations. Battery life is currently at 66% (been out for over 2 months on the mode I just specified, over 5k pics). The camera case couldn't be better, water-tight, blends well, and the size of this camera is perfect. This is the camera for me, I will be buying more!

The only con I've seen with this camera is there is some blur if there is heavy movement, however not enough blur to have problems identifying the subject. Overall 5 stars, well done, Browning, well done.

review_body: I purchased these fins especially for a trip, my 11th, to Mexico's Riviera Maya.  I have never liked the idea of renting fins from dive shops and the fins I already had were very long, difficult to pack and difficult to walk in to get to the water from shore.  I found the U.S. Divers TREK fins to be just right for my needs.  I snorkeled on three occasions on this trip and had not one problem with the fins.  The padded fin straps also protected the backs of my heels from painful irritation.  Others have noted this and I found it to be true: These fins are not for those with wide feet. I've been using BMP resistance bands instead and I am pleasantly surprised at how well of a workout they give. You can work out every major muscle group, and since they have the door and ankle attachment, you can do many different exercises to keep things fresh and reduce muscle memory.

I was a little worried that they would not provide enough resistance, but I was wrong. Since you can clip in different bands to the handles, you can get a lot of resistance. For example, I usually do curls with 70 lb. straight bar, and these bands easily accomplish that and more. I tried doing more but I couldn't.

These won't replace a gym membership completely, but if you are looking for a way to stay in shape without buying a bunch of dumbbells, this is your product. I thought this light would help brighten the entire area.  The light came on during the first use and I spotted a hog just outside the lighted area.  It was hesitant to come and turned around but came back a few minutes later.  The light came on again and helped me know that there was something out there as I am 100 yards from the feeder deep in the woods.  I did get the kill shot so I can't complain.  I am purchasing another light to help light up the area a bit better from another angle but mostly to get the signal that something is there.  Will see if the hogs are nervous with the extra light.  I would recommend that this product be used as a back up to a brighter light such as a kill light as I don't see how it could have provided enough light by itself to get good and lined up on anything through the scope.  Its best asset on this product is the motion sensor and that is why I am purchasing another one.

product_title: Maxpedition Operator Tactical Attache
review_body:
I have been using a Maxpedition Operator as a work bag for around 4 years. It is the perfect size for a small to midsize laptop, all of my EDC gear, including some small tools, all of my cords and chargers, an iPad, a full-size notebook, assorted electronics, and office supplies.

The Operator really excels for carrying lots of flat items, and that is what I would recommend it for. As a weekend or overnight bag, it is not ideal because it does not allow for enough expansion to pack a meaningful number of garments. That being said, for carrying around your work electronics and assorted small items, it works quite well. It sits nicely behind the seat of my truck, and is just the right size for carrying using the handles or the shoulder strap.

The build quality is typical for Maxpedition, which is pretty solid, but not going to last forever. The wrapping that Maxpedition uses on its shoulder pads and handles tends to deteriorate pretty quickly. I have owned a bunch of Maxpedition gear and this problem is pretty much universal across the line, in my experience. The zippers are not the super-heavy duty zippers that you might find on some of the tactical nylon gear made in the USA by smaller manufacturers. As much as I love my Operator, it is about to get retired because the zippers are all starting to, or already have split. I have definitely gotten more than enough use out of this bag for what I paid for it several years ago.

In short, I absolutely love the design features of this bag, and only wish that it was made to higher specs using better materials and components. If Spec-Ops Brand or London Bridge Trading made this exact bag to their specs, it would be worth around double what the Operator costs, and would last much longer.

I find VZ thin profile grips a little skimpy, Ahrends 1911 grips just right, and these on thick side. While this is certainly subjective and causes no material problems in achieving a proper grip, I still took a star off since the pistol doesn't feel as good in my hand as it used to. Other functions were perfect: the on/off switch works as advertised, battery installation is OK, and you can readily choose by squeezing with your middle finger when to engage the laser. In this regard it is better than the other two models I have.
I believe that laser sights are a very good idea for a self defense handgun. While these are expensive, they are, IMHO, worth the price and there is nothing better on the market for a 1911.

product_title: Bowflex SelectTech 1090 Adjustable Dumbbell (Single)
review_body:
I bought these on sale from Bowflex directly about a month ago. Here are some things you should consider before buying:

(1) The handles have very pronounced textured grips on them, and if you are going to be doing any serious weight, you will likely need to use gloves because the strain it puts on your hand is higher than with a typical round textured handle (like i n any gym).

(2) The most difficult thing about these, to me, is that the dials on either end are very narrow, which means that any time you are balancing them on yourself before starting a set, it will be very uncomfortable if there is significant weight on them. For example, if you are using all the weight on a bench press, and want to balance them vertically on your thighs before starting the set, the tiny circumference of the dial makes it press deep into your thigh and very uncomfortable. This is only an issue if you plan to do heavy lifts, but that is the main advantage of these over the 5-50s type.

(3) No matter how little or much weight you use, the dumbbells are going to be very wide. This is not a problem yet, but it is a little cumbersome.

The good is that it is very fast to switch between weights, they seem well-made and there is absolutely no installation (unlike the bench I got---phew). Overall, I am mostly satisfied except with (2); when you are trying to do a large lift the last thing you want is not to be able to stably start the exercise and it to be hurting you and wobbling. I am not sure I would buy them again.
