product_title: ProSource 125-Pound Heavy Duty Garage Utility Canoe and Kayak Storage Lift
review_headline: Have an open mind, be creative and the possibilities are endless!
review_body:
I have tried MANY of these lifts. There are basically two types of these on the market. They can be broken down into single or dual PULL rope systems. On a single rope system (usually the cheaper ones meant for bikes) the front and back can not be raised or lowered independently. The problem with this is that I have had a bike fall and almost hit me because the front of the bike was higher than the rear causing the hook which was on the seat to slip off. This mount has a dual rope pull meaning that as its coming down you can keep the item level.

I have 9 of these in my 3 car garage I store the following

1. [[ASIN:B00004RKB5 Werner D6224-2 300-Pound Duty Rating Fiberglass Flat D-Rung Extension Ladder, 24-Foot]]
2. [[ASIN:B0000VYDHU Werner MT-22 300-Pound Duty Rating Telescoping Multi-Ladder, 22-Foot]]
3. [[ASIN:B0017ZT2L0 Louisville Ladder FS1510 300-Pound Duty Rating Fiberglass Step Ladder, 10-Feet]]
4. [[ASIN:B000KL2YB2 Louisville Ladder FS1506 300-Pound Duty Rating Fiberglass Ladder, 6-Feet]]
5. [[ASIN:B002UQ1UHO Yeats 59-Inch Aluminum Dual Strap Appliance Hand Truck]]
6. [[ASIN:B00EEA5C1O Thule Atlantis Rooftop Cargo Box]]
7. [[ASIN:B005W1UV4C Gorilla Carts Heavy Duty Dump Cart]]
8. [[ASIN:B0000DD0YX Grizzly G9956 Heavy-Duty Double Air Filter with Remote Control]]
9. [[ASIN:B004M2BINA Power Wheels Dune Racer, Green]]

Lets look at the basics

Installation

Instructions stink, you WILL need to be handy, if your not then this item is NOT for you.

First off is deciding where you are going and what you are planning on mounting. For instance my 4 ladders are all grouped together about 12\\" apart from each other. I took 2 2x8's cut them to 54\\" and bolted them to 4 floor joists (use HEAVY lag bolts AND washers). What this does is distribute the weight of the 4 ladders over the 4 joists and ensures that nothing is going to sag or fall. I then used 6\\" lag bolts to attach the 2x8's to the ceiling. Once that was done I then needed to modify the brackets to accept larger lag bolts to attach them to the 2x8. This can be easily done with a drill bit and cordless drill. I then attached the black mounting assembly to the 2x8 once again using a high quality lag bolts AND 2 washers to distribute the weight (2 bolts PER bracket).

Direct mounting to your ceiling.

On items like the Thule cargo carrier I simply drilled out the hole on the bracket to allow it to accept a large lag bolt and washer and merely bolted it directly to the ceiling (ensuring you are going into a floor joist). to support the box itself I ran the straps through the mounting points of the box to ensure it wouldn't slip and fall.

What to do with the left over rope.

The units come with a small bracket that you mount to the wall. You simply wrap the excess rope around this to secure your load. On items that are rarely used I fore-go this step and merely wrap the excess rope around the item itself. This works out great on items you rarely use or where you don't want the rope in your way. For instance for me I only use my ladders a few times a year so I just wrap the rope around it to secure it. On items such as my yard cart which only gets used for a month in spring I just tie the rope to a wheel or to the handle.

Woodworking uses.

I have a ceiling mounted dust collector, It was always a pain to clean the filters because the unit was 8' off the ground. I removed the mounting hooks from the ProSource mount and replaced them with a bolt with a circle loop on it. I then attached that hoop to the mounting chains of the collector. Now when I need to clean the filter I just lower the bad boy down onto my table saw and can access it easily without needing to stand on a ladder or on top of the table saw itself.

Power wheels

The trick to mounting large bulky items is two fold. First its important tofind the items center of gravity. If you merely hang it, there is a chance it could shift sideways and fall. The second part is finding the right mounting point. In other words WHERE are you going to attach the hooks to. On some items you may need to use the straps or it may be necessary to \\"customize\\" a mounting solution. For instance On my older sons power wheels I removed the hooks added in a piece of slotted steel from Menards and then attached 4 hooks to it (2 extra hooks from another kit for a total of 4 hooks). So what I ended up with was the two lift ropes each going to a bar with a hook at each end, That way I just attached a hook to each of the 4 wheel wells and lifted it up from there.

I guess what it comes down to is how desperate you are to get stuff off the floor in the garage. In my case even though I have a huge 3 car garage we just end up with a ton of junk. It all adds up in the end 7 bikes a couple of powerwheels a couple of scooters, the lawnmower, all the other junk that goes with a yard and then my tools just eat up space and you gave to find a spot to get rid of some of it. I think the most important thing here is USE YOUR IMAGINATION and improvise when necessary. For instance on my yard car I mount it upside down because its easier to hook onto the metal wheel supports vs. trying to attach to the plastic bucket.

SAFETY

If you don't think something is going to stay in place, IT PROBABLY WONT!
If in doubt get a couple of carabiners and some extra rope and create a safety hook to catch the item if it falls.

And here is what it comes down to. These probably are not the \\"ideal\\" solution for everything you have but they are cheap, They are relatively easy to use and can be modified to suit almost any need. I'm pretty fortunate my garage has an 11' ceiling. and all my junk is off the floor and doesn't get in the way. When you take all that into consideration its a 5 star product. (these will work fine if you have 9' ceilings in the garage, don't recommend them if you have an older garage with 8' ceilings)

About my reviews.

I have a pretty basic rating system

3 stars = meets expectations, in order words it does what its supposed to do.
1 & 2 stars = fails to meet expectations, doesn't cut the mustard.
4 & 5 stars = exceeds expectations. Its gotta REALLY rock to get 5 stars.

I try to be as detailed as possible without getting technical. There are a lot of reviewers out there that just give too much info I try to keep it simple.

In the event that I am reviewing an item through a marketing campaign. IT WILL BE CLEARLY STATED within the review.find the items center of gravity. If you merely hang it, there is a chance it could shift sideways and fall. The second part is finding the right mounting point. In other words WHERE are you going to attach the hooks to. On some items you may need to use the straps or it may be necessary to \\"customize\\" a mounting solution. For instance On my older sons power wheels I removed the hooks added in a piece of slotted steel from Menards and then attached 4 hooks to it (2 extra hooks from another kit for a total of 4 hooks). So what I ended up with was the two lift ropes each going to a bar with a hook at each end, That way I just attached a hook to each of the 4 wheel wells and lifted it up from there.

I guess what it comes down to is how desperate you are to get stuff off the floor in the garage. In my case even though I have a huge 3 car garage we just end up with a ton of junk. It all adds up in the end 7 bikes a couple of powerwheels a couple of scooters, the lawnmower, all the other junk that goes with a yard and then my tools just eat up space and you gave to find a spot to get rid of some of it. I think the most important thing here is USE YOUR IMAGINATION and improvise when necessary. For instance on my yard car I mount it upside down because its easier to hook onto the metal wheel supports vs. trying to attach to the plastic bucket.

SAFETY

If you don't think something is going to stay in place, IT PROBABLY WONT!
If in doubt get a couple of carabiners and some extra rope and create a safety hook to catch the item if it falls.

And here is what it comes down to. These probably are not the \\"ideal\\" solution for everything you have but they are cheap, They are relatively easy to use and can be modified to suit almost any need. I'm pretty fortunate my garage has an 11' ceiling. and all my junk is off the floor and doesn't get in the way. When you take all that into consideration its a 5 star product. (these will work fineif you have 9' ceilings in the garage, don't recommend them if you have an older garage with 8' ceilings)

review_headline: Not bad but has some problems...
review_body:
This is the first electric treadmill my family has bought and it's okay aside from a couple of problems. For the most part, the treadmill is usable, but the thing requires way more adjustment than is needed. I just spent 2 hours fighting with it trying to keep it from slipping to the right when walking on it. If you walk on it without using the hand rails it slips to the right for no apparent reason.

I have adjusted this several times as per instructions. Furthermore, sometimes this treadmill knocks because you have to tighten it so much (just trying to keep it from knocking which doesn't work).

I have to say I am somewhat disappointed with this because it's way too much hassle in adjustment (compared to our old manual treadmill which was easier to do).

I took a chance with all the hit and miss reviews, but I came out a bit charred because it seems half the people with negatives were right and the positives were also right.

1. The belt keeps slipping no matter how I adjust it.
2. Even after looking for 3rd party help it still goes off to the right.
3. Random noises sometimes from operation (and my brother and I are below the weight limit).

There are some positives though.

1. The treadmill is quiet.
2. It's fine for what we need it for.
3. Installation was very easy. There was little work to be done in the initial setup.

If you want to take the risk and have a solid way to return it, I would go for it. Otherwise, don't bother and look elsewhere.

On a side-note, my box also came with a hole in the bottom side of the treadmill, but the plastic was not punctured at all.

review_body: I bought this base hoping to mount my True Glow red dot sight on my Pardner Protector H&R 12 ga. The holes line up fine, but the bottom of the base does not engage the milled slot because it's almost .120\\" too wide. I gave mine to a machinst friend to take off .060\\" per side and it should drop in nice and snug. This is a good steel piece, and will work if you do your part. It is not \\"plug and play\\", or at least it shouldn't be. Using only the screws to mount this base and letting sit over top the receiver groove without engaging it is a recipe for failure, IMHO. -use of firestarter significantly dull the blade and leaves char-like stains
-firestarter grip is somewhat uncomfortable
-sheath doesn't maintain a firm grip on either the knife or the firestarter. They fall out easily.
-after about a year the paracord handle became a tangled mess and fell off. I'm left with a hunk of metal that resembles a knife. This makes the knife uncomfortable to use for extended time. I sure if you needed to though, you could rehandle it.
-but remember, IT WAS TWO DOLLARS!

Now that we're through with the con's, let's get to the pros!

POSITIVES:

-it is capable of fire making
-IT WAS TWO DOLLARS
-the handle was comfortable while it was on
-IT WAS TWO DOLLARS
-the cord handle that fell off worked well to tighten the sheath
-IT WAS TWO DOLLARS
-the sheath is roomy and I fit tinder in it.
-IT WAS TWO DOLLARS
-it created many sparks
-IT WAS TWO DOLLARS

product_title: iHealth Wireless Activity and Sleep Tracker for iPhone and Android
review_body:
I've had my iHealth tracker for at least 3 weeks now and have found both positives and negatives about it. I'll just report my experience and let the reader decide.

First, mine only cost about 60 bucks, on sale at Walgreens. I purchased it using my FSA card since this tracker is FSA eligible. My first complaint about it was that the styling isn't very chic. The look of it on your arm will definitely not gain you \\"cool\\" points.

Set up was very easy though and you can do it without the aid of instructions. Just download the free app, enable bluetooth on the device that you used to load the app, go to the app Settings, and let the app \\"find\\" the tracker and you're all set. I recommend enabling the save to the Cloud function else your alarms will only go to the app and not the tracker.

It syncs to the device at the touch of a button. I like the app. I have it loaded on an iPad and it's easy to read and to update. I wish it had more functionality, like the ability to drill down to more detail in the Sleep data, but it does allow me to manually enter blood presser data which is a plus since I don't use the monitor that you can purchase as part of this line. I found entering Meal data as difficult as it is on most other Nutrietion apps so I won't take points away from this device on that one. You can \\"save\\" meals though so that you don't have to start from scratch recreating the details of a meal that you've had before.

The device itself was fine to wear, at first, but by day 7 I found that the weight of it began to annoy me, especially during sleep. It's thick and would cause me some discomfort during the night. I eventually began wearing it on my arm backwards at night, which helped some.

My greatest disappointment with the device is that it does not work reliably for me. A few times each week I sync it just after waking only to find that it stopped recording 2 hours in. It has shutdown twice, though it had plenty ofcharge left. Since the sleep data is my favorite thing about both the device and the app, I found this discouraging.

The iHealth tracker is one of the few wristband trackers that has an actual display so you can press the button anytime and see the time, number of steps, distance covered, calories burned and battery life. It's easy to set for sleep mode but I find it is sometimes reluctant to switch it back into steps mode. I have, at least once, reset the device by holding the button for too long in an attempt to get it to change modes. Also, I find that slipping it into the wrist band is difficult. It pushes out easy enough though.

It has good battery life; I usually go 3 days on a charge. And it only takes 2 hours to give it a full charge. It is \\"splash resistant.\\" It's at accurate at counting steps as any other accelerometer.

I plan to return mine for a refund. I would suffer through the styling of it if it more reliably collected sleep data, but waking to find that it stopped tracking at 11:30pm is too discouraging for me.

product_title: Camelbak Thermobak Omega Hydration Backpack
review_headline: If you need to hydrate for a whole day...
review_body:
Typically, an adult male needs about 2L of water a day, but this amount must be increased if you're active beyond normal walking and sitting at the desk all day long. I bought the CamelBak ThermoBack (3L) in Multicam for camping/hiking/training and it has worked out wonderfully.

If you're new to CamelBaks, I'd say get one. If you're a CamelBak alumni, the Multicam ThermoBak is of the same quality as the regular colorful variations. The inside bladder and tubing is black not blue, the mouth piece is Flat Dark Earth not blue, and comes with a FDE hose cover to match the webbing. The Multicam carrying pouch is durable, and has ambidextrous openings for the hose. I wish that the CamelBak logo patch wasn't so big and obvious. I also wish there wer two lines of velcro loop instead of one... maybe some PALS webbing on the lower part. But I digress. Now, 3 liters is a lot of water... that's six 16 oz bottles of water. A full one lasted me a whole day under the hot Wisconsin sun in June while I ran and crawled through a medical course at a sand stone quarry with white sand (the reflection was killing us).

Being 5'8\\" and wearing a Medium shirt, the 3L Thermobak was slightly too long. The bottom of the CamelBak would interfere with the pouches on my utility belt. Also, the backpack-like strap system is fine if this is the only thing you're carrying, but if you have an actual backpack or carrying a rig on your chest, then this system is no good. There are D-rings at six positions on the TermoBack, but I could not figure out an effective attachment method to any of the gear I had. Maybe somebody else might have better luck. If you really want a CamelBak attached to military gear, I recommend the newer ThermoBak AB with the Direct Attachment System (DAS) or the ArmorBak which is DAS-Only (no straps),

review_headline: Very good, but with small problems
review_body:

Upon removing the bokken from the packaging, the first thing I noticed was that it was darker than I had expected (almost black). The weight is quite nice, and the center of balance is about 8\\" from the end of the tsuka. All in all, it seems to be sturdily made, and I feel that it could take enough of a beating for light sparring, although I only intend to use it for practicing forms.

However, I have noticed two issues, neither of which matters to me, but which may matter to you. First of all, the packaging came apart somewhat, and the kisaki was a little scuffed. More importantly, however, the tsuba could not actually be fitted onto the sword, because the opening was simply too small.

As a result, I would not recommend this for sparring, but for practicing form, it seems to be a good practice sword.

Update:
Recently, not realizing how much space I had, I accidentally hit a thick post made of hardwood at full speed, about 10cm from the kisaki. There is a noticeable crack at the point of contact, about 1/4 cm deep. However, considering the shear amount of force I was using, I'm surprised that it didn't split. I have broken more durable seeming bokkens with less force. This thing is more durable than I thought.

However, I also eventually decided to go all or nothing to attach the tsuba. Naturally, as I began to increase the force, it shattered into 5 pieces, never even getting past the kisaki.

review_headline: Can't really tell any difference myself....pretty much a waste of time.
review_body: First of all, those folks complaining it won't fit don't know how to put it in! You need to put a little WD-40 or similar on it for lube and rotate it into the cover near the rear of the unit.  It's a tight fit....I used a small punch to rotate mine in position.  Once you finally get it to snap into the cover, you can push in into the rear of the cover for final positioning using a longer punch ( larger end against the buffer ). There is an inherent, and dangerous glitch in the design of this holster. The first time I noticed it was when practicing drawing and firing the pistol at the range. On the second attempt I couldn't withdraw the pistol from the holster. I am a very strong male and I have carried a variety of semi-autos in both inside and outside the waistband. Once the holster was clear of my clothing I looked it over carefully and found no obvious problem - no reason the little gun wouldn't clear the holster and it went in and out without a problem - until I put a little pressure on the sides of the holster with my thumb and forefinger. product_title: SwingTIP Golf Swing Analyzer
review_body:
My expectations were very high when I bought this. After using it, I find it useful but I am a little disappointed with it.

Pros:
1. Easy to pair with an iPod Touch 4th Gen.
2. Easy to attach to club. It comes with some fitting tape that will make it snug.
3. Draws out your swing path in a Blue and Yellow line for Backswing and downswing.
4. Analysis will tell you things about your swing. There is text beneath that enumerates the details of your swing.
5. Allows you to record a video of your swing.
6. It was accurate when I tested whether it could tell if I was making a short swing or full swing.

Cons:
1. The tips given are very generic, short and vague.
2. It does not really show your swing. It appears to be the same animation of a swing every single time. I would have preferred something that actually shows the animation of my swing. Drawing the swing path line drawings are useful but not enough.
3. Swing speed is not very accurate. My Swing Speed Radar said 87 mph. This one said 65.

Summary:
If you have the spare change, sure, get this as it does have some useful, albeit limited features. My advice is first use an iPod or Tablet to take many videos of your swing. That really helps out a lot in finding issues with your swing. I watch mine on my computer and play it side by side to a video of the swing of Tiger.

product_title: NcStar Compact Pistol and Rifle Green Laser with Quick Release Weaver Mount
review_headline: Not as Bright as I Expected
review_body: I own four different green lasers all different brands.  I read several reviews before purchasing this laser, and partially choose this specific one because so many people raved about it's brightness.  Of the four lasers that I own this is by far the dimmest (and yes I did check the battery and tested several different brand new CR123 batteries).  Being dimmer has both pros and cons.  If I were using this laser at night and did not want to give away my position then this would be my laser of choice.  There is almost no visible beam unless it is very foggy.  My other three lasers project a very bright beam that that is visible from anywhere at night.  If you don't care about being seen at night (Like if your using the laser for intimidation)or if you are using this as a day time laser then I strongly recommend that you NOT buy this laser.  It is not visible in day light at 100ft out and anything closer than that you probably won't need a laser to help you hit it.  My other green lasers are easily visible at 200-400 yards in broad day light! So this is basically worthless as a day time laser unless you are using it indoors.  Otherwise it is a good quality product.  I wish they advertised the laser power in the listing.  I think brightness is such a relative term, if you have only used a red laser then of course you will think this is bright because it is much brighter than a cheap red laser, but I have other green lasers that are easily 10X as bright as this one that purchased for approximately the same price. I am only giving this a 3 star rating because I was expecting to buy a day time green laser that was bright enough for use outdoors in day light.

Visually disorient the attacker with the flashlight, pull out the unit hidden in your pocket, which can even be accessed in a struggle, and then let em have it. I really don't like to carry water bottles, and anything strapped around my waist or hips drives me crazy. review_body:
I don't usually leave reviews but the reviews were what got me to buy this new workout. Before T25 I was dedicated to Insanity but those workouts were too long. I noticed after 1 week of Insanity that I would catch myself fast forwarding through the 30 second breaks (because i did not need them). When T25 claimed that it is only "25 minutes a day" I was skeptical at first because Insanity claimed to have a certain time limit, which was not the case. Also, I though to myself, 25 minutes a day? In my head that meant that there would be maybe 3 breaks and 2 stretch routines, making the real workout to be about 15 mins more or less. When I bought this new workout, I was very IMPRESSED that it was actually 25 mins of working out, NO BREAKS NO STRETCHES! It made me work harder than Insanity in my opinion and its only 25 mins. When I do the workouts in T25 I put a cover over my television where the time stamp is so that I would not know how much time I have left, that way I can give the workout all I've got. From time to time I would catch myself wanting to know how much time I have left, so I would remove the time cover and I would pleasantly surprised at how much time flew buy.

Think about it. The work out takes less time than watching children shows like "Spongebob Square Pants" Which is a 30 min segment. You can't beat 25 mins a day. Another great aspect of this workout if that Shaun T. is only asking you to workout for 5 days a week; therefore, Saturday and Sunday you do not have to workout. If you want faster results then you have a choice to do a random workout for Saturday and Sunday. I usually workout on Saturday's and Sunday's because I know that I can fit it into my schedule and the workouts only become easier and easier. Don't worry though because he has another cycle of workouts that challenge you even more than the first cycle. If you feel like the workouts are getting too easy, just go to his more advance workout cycles and see if you can keep up, if not, you know that you need to spend a little bit more time in the first cycle.

product_title: GSI Outdoors Dukjug - 1 Liter
review_body:
I ordered this water bottle (blue) along with one package of Aquamira Water Purifier Purification Tablets as a kit. I really wanted the Chlorine Dioxide Water Purifier Tablets and the only way I could buy them through Amazon was with the water bottle. I haven't tried the tablets yet, but I have used the water bottle and overall I'm pleased with it.

It has a nice solid feel to it, although only time will tell if a plastic bottle will hold up to outdoors use and abuse as well as a metal bottle. Having a rubber hand grip is a nice touch, and I'm rather intrigued with being able to hold up to six feet (2 meters) of duct tape under the rubber \\"dog bone\\" area. Seems a little gimmicky, but I can see the benefits of having some duct tape while in the great outdoors. I do like having the insert in the wide mouth, makes drinking just that much more comfortable. Having a measuring guide on the side is also nice, and could be useful for campfire cooking when you need an accurate measure of water for freeze-dried dinners. Of course, the one-liter bottle size is just perfect if using water purification tablets, as the tablets come sized to treat one liter of water.

The size of the bottle is a bit of a problem though. It has a wide diameter, and with my \\"normal\\" sized hands I'm barely able to get a comfortable grip on the bottle. My wife, with extra small hands, would probably need to use both hands to hold it, especially when it's full of water and heavy. While the diameter is no problem for my day pack, I also use water bottles when kayaking, power boating, or just driving long distances. The bottle is too large of a diameter to fit in any of the drink holders. It's a small thing, but having someplace to put a water bottle in a boat or car can be an issue. (I rate four stars because the bottle will not fit in my drink holders.) The wide diameter compared to it's height does seem to make the bottle more stable and less prone to tipping over when seated on it's base, so that's something.

Overall a good purchase.it's base, so that's something.

Overall a good purchase.

product_title: Spalding Portable Basketball System - 50" Polycarbonate Backboard
review_body:
I had looked at various models in the store before buying this, just to see what size backboard would work well. I settled for the 50\\" but really wish I had gotten a bigger one. I'm actually surprised how many shots can miss the entire backboard. Serious, I am shocked. One would think... jeez, you should be able to at least hit the darn backboard... but there are times lol.

Anyway, issues with this:

* The lift mechanism is VERY hard to use both up or down. I need to see if there is something I can loosen up a bit, but as of right now it is just a beast to try to lift or lower and then get the pin in at just the right spot. And I'm a big guy, 6'4\\" and strong. Particularly difficult are the extreme high and extreme low positions. And, really, these are the only two positions we use. We move it up to 10' to play and put it back down to the lowest setting when we're done (to keep the winds here from blowing it over).

* It is a beast to move around, especially when full of water (I don't have a hose that can stretch that FAR). Our driveway, like most, is slanted. It seems very dangerous when I'm trying to push it down the driveway to sidewalk to use. Thankfully, I only move it twice a year: Once in the spring to the sidewalk on our cul-de-sac, and once in the winter after I drain it.

* I don't like the water container. I have to stand on it when adjusting the arm up or down and when I stand on it, it gives. I imagine over time it will break. That sucks because this thing was expensive.

* The \\"ball return\\" is a joke. After playing weekly over the summer, maybe three balls were ever returned.

Things we like:

* The backboard and rim itself seems very sturdy. No silly shaking around when you hit it with the ball.

* The whole system doesn't move around at all on you. Once it's in place and full of water, it stays.

* Nice look.

* Installation was easy, and not too time-consuming.

I was pretty sure I was going to end up going with a competing brand... I had price watches and everything on various models of that other brand. Spalding ones were always very expensive. I saw this on lightning deal and went ahead and sprang for it.

I know this review seems critical... and it is... but really we are happy 4 stars out of 5 with it.

product_title: Trophy Ridge React 5 Pin Bow Sight
review_body:
You set the top pin and one other pin and all the other sights are set for the other distance. So you set the top for 20 yards by moving the entire housing around (that's the only way the top pin can move), then set the 40 yard pin (any other pin will do but if you set the 30 the margin of error is larger, ideally you would set the 60 but I'm not that good) by turning the up/down knob and the 30, 50, and 60 yard pins move the correct distances apart. It took me a while to set the 20 just right over and only about 20 minutes to get the 40 set but after that I went right to the 3D range and put 3 into a \\"deer\\" at 60 yards, 2 were even killing shots.

A better shooter could sight it in my quicker but I have a hard time determining if misses were because the sight is off or if it's just me.

For me, I still wouldn't take a poke at a deer past 15-20 yards but it's nice to know they are set. I hated having all the other pins just sitting in a pile at the bottom of the ring.

I like that it's tool less as well and has versatile mounts. The only thing i would change is; I would add a vibration dampener. Not because it vibrates but... why not?

product_title: Schrade SCHF10 Drop-Point Full Tang Fixed Blade Knife, Black
review_body:
I received my Schrade SCHF10 by the delivery date and in good condition. I figured for $40, how could you go wrong? I was not expecting this much knife for the price. The blade alloy is supposed to be similar to AUS8, which in my experience, has been durable and holds an edge well. The blade grinding is well defined and consistent from side to side. The blade is full tang, with an exposed pummel and lanyard hole at the end. I can only say for myself my knife was more than adequately sharp out of the box. I can touch it up, but it's a minor issue. The Micarta scales are the bomb, usually seen on more expensive knives. They're cut and profiled for the hand and lend an upscale look the Schrade. Jimping is generous and found on the topside of the blade, continued on the forward topside of the handle as well as the rear most underside of the handle.
As for the sheath, well, what were people expecting at this price point? That's not to say it isn't serviceable; it is. It just isn't the $200 sheath you see on YouTube. Buy one of those, they would be well deserving of this knife.
So, is this a good knife? Actually it's a great knife. My question is, how much more money would one have to spend to get more survivability than this blade would afford you? I own my fair share of K-Bars but I would be hard pressed to spend $30 more for the comparable knife in the BK series.
A cautionary note for back packers and others: this thing is heavy. As for side carry, I'd be hesitant to do that as well. I plan to carry mine in a Kydex sheath bandoleer style. Your results may vary.

review_body:
I have owned a number of BB guns that shot pellets as well as BBs but this is my first pellet only gun. The instruction sheet is well outlined and easy to understand. I followed the instructions step by step and all went well starting with the CO2 cylinder installation and test firing. Next came a slight bump in the road which was experienced with the loading of the pellets. The problem is not with the product but with my fingers. I do not have nice slim fingers so loading the pellets with my \\"substantial\\" sized fingers was a bit tricky but doable. However, all the instructions were completed and I was ready to fire.

My usage for this pellet gun is rather modest. I have some bird feeders at the front of my house. The seed droppings that result from the activity of the birds attract other small animals. When my Dobie looks out the front window and sees any of these animals he goes berserk with barking. I use the pellet gun to chase away the bark causers in order to restore quiet to my living room. I don't try to hit the animals but just scare them away. This gun does a fine job of doing just that. The pellet speed and the firing distance are just fine for my purposes therefore I rate this product five stars. The weight is nice, the appearance is nice, the price is reasonable and the performance is more than satisfactory. It's all good.

review_headline: Ok stand, ot for prolonged use.

You need to be mindful of the size tree you have it in, the "capture" teath in the climbing surface are spaced about 7 inches apart, so in a tree smaller than about 10 inches in diameter the teeth do not contact the tree, and can cause it to slip...not a good feeling when you are 20 feet off the ground.

I do like the fact that it has the quick collapse feature, this makes it very easy to transport, despite the fact it is very heavy.

review_body:
Bottom line: You're not beating these for the price. I got the 105lb set (2x 52.5lb sets). The plates were sort of loosely packaged but were individually plastic wrapped. Many had some oil residue on them, which cleaned off easily with some lighter fluid and paper towels (best solution for oil and sticky residues). Many had little dings or small flecks of missing paint, but seriously who cares. For about $100 shipped, they're such a deal and they aren't meant to be show pieces.

The collars have a rubber spacer which allows them to friction lock to the plates nicely. Doing bicep curls, peck flies, and even tricep exercises — where you're holding the dumbbell by the weight plates — the plates don't rattle and stay firmly in place. The weights fit great on a 1\\" barbell bar so if you're not doing 52.5lb bicep curls you can allocate a bunch of the plates to your barbell, saving money on weights for that. I got these, two 25lb plats, two 10lbs plates, and this barbell bar - [[ASIN:B004X166W8 B004X166W8]] - giving me a very complete set without breaking the bank.

THEY LOSE A STAR FOR: The bars have that crosshatched pattern cut into them for grip. On one it was perfect. On the other it was slightly lopsided, so on one side the cuts were deeper and on the other side they were shallower. If I lifted with bare hands this wouldn't mess with my lifting but it would tug at my 'OCD'. Thankfully I lift with gloves so it's totally irrelevant for me. They're made in China and make no apologies for being a cheap option, so set your expectations accordingly.

product_title: Kick-EEZ Dual-Action All Purpose Recoil Pad LARGE
review_body: This is the second one I've purchased, and will likely buy more.  I recommend you take your time when grinding, don't let the material overheat.  I noticed it gets very grippy and sticks/skips on the sanding belt when it gets a little too warm from the friction.  This can leave chatter marks, not very pretty.  I worked on removing small amounts of material at a time, letting it rest 5 minutes or so between passes to be sure it stayed cool.  Once I got the rough shape done using a medium grit, I finished it nicely with a finer grain belt (working slowly, a little at a time as I got close to final shape) and then with a polishing compound, so it looks good.  Big improvement in felt recoil compared to my old, slip on pad.  There are some popular named pads made from other material that may be easier to grind/shape, but this material is better where it counts with regards to felt recoil (in my experience).  Worth the extra effort.  If you can't do the grinding yourself, buy it and take it to your local shop to be fit, I think you'll like it.

If there were clamps to \\"permanently\\" attach the bottom portion to the barrel, you could remove the top portion and disassemble your rifle without concern for losing zero (assuming you are using the forend for some sort of optic use).  All in all, the product was clearly designed with the intent to save money on production rather than to be a product that will receive actual use.

review_body:
We are new users to the world of kinesiology tape. My 13 year old daughter is a gymnast and has been dealing with Sever's Disease (which by the way is not a disease at all) since she was 8 years old. I went on YouTube and found a way to tape her heel's for heel pain.

I read the reviews on both KT Tape and Rock Tape. Since I could go to my local Sportmart immediately and buy the KT Tape, I decided to do that just to see if it made a difference. I applied the tape just like the video instructed. My daughter walked on her feet and right away she felt no pain. She had been having pain in her heels just walking lately.

The next test was to try it at the gym. She tells me it is defiantly less painful and she is back training on all events at the moment.

Since it helped, I opted to order the Rock Tape as the KT Tape did not last more than one day. I also ordered the Mueller pre tape. The Rock tape holds better but still lifts on some of the edges. We use the pre tape to secure the edges each night and have gotten up to 3 days use out of one taping.

That said, neither tape has miracle hold but, the Rock Tape is definitely better. And since using it has helped reduce her pain, we will continue to use the Rock Tape and the pre tape.

product_title: Nathan Nutrition Flask with Race Cap-Pack of 3
review_headline: Better than the standard Nathan bottles
review_body: I bought this pack because while I was running with the Nathan 2 bottle belt, one bottle felt out and landed on the nozzle, which pushed the nozzle in and broke. I had to throw it away and I can't run with just one bottle (training for a marathon). I searched online for replacements and came across these flasks with the race cap. These base bottle is the same as the original Nathan flask that comes with their belts. The only difference is the cap. I prefer the race cap because all you have to do is squeeze and water shoots out at a decent pressure. Compared to the original, where you had to pull the nozzle up and then bite down, the race cap is much quicker and easier. I've run with it plenty of times and it never leaked! As opposed to the original cap where if I didn't push it down all the way it would splash out of the nozzle. I would recommend the race cap over the standard one because of the functionality and simplicity. Not sure why they don't put these as the stock ones with their belts. Cleaning also isn't an issue if you have a nozzle brush, like the OXO bottle brush set or the camelbak ones. Overall, great product, no problems so far!

product_title: Ar15 Combo! Aluminum Carbine Quad Rail 4-weaver/picatinny Rail Aluminum Handguard. + Foregrip with Pup Out Bipod
review_body:
This rail/foregrip/bipod combo has a little bit of everything for a pretty good price. Obviously the grip isn't ergonomic, but it's not overly large either, so most adults and even teenagers should be able to get a good grip on it. The bipod isn't going to give you the stability that a standalone bipod would, but it still gives you enough support that you can hit some good groups. A friend of mine hit around a one to two inch group very near the bullseye of a makeshift target with the bipod at 60 yards or so, using a red dot scope with no magnification. That might not sound impressive, but bear in mind my friend is not a trained shooter, and has only fired rifles two or three times before.

The parts themselves seem to be pretty high quality, and they're easy to install (though you'll want a buddy to get the rail on). The bipod release button is nice and solid, with enough give that it can be pressed easily but not so prominent or easy to push that you could accidentally set it off. When you do press it, the bipod comes out in a hurry, so don't put anything in its way! This of course is because it's spring loaded, which is what makes it stay in the triangle shape while out of the grip.

Overall, if you're looking for some added functionality and aren't too worried about perfection, this is definitely worth a buy. Considering the fact that it's foregrip/bipod combo, I have no complaints at all.

product_title: 5.11 Tactical Rush 6 Mobile Operation Attachment Bag
review_headline: Knew what I wanted to use it for...
review_body:
Sometimes you'll catch a review where someone complains about \\"limited uses\\" or small size. To that I say... did you not know what you wanted to use it for before buying it?

Well I did, and I wanted this bag for an expanded EDC. I say expanded because I include a small \\"survival/bug out\\" kit in this bag with my every day stuff. It's basically my \\"get home from work alive\\" kit, to get me to more supplies if needed. But primarily it is used for...

-Carrying my everyday supplies to work.
-Going to the gym.
-A concealed carry travel bag which I keep on the passenger seat when driving alone. This bag's unique ability to pull down onto your front waist like a fanny pack makes it an amazing choice for concealed carry. HOWEVER- I don't mean to suggest this is the best way to carry if you needed to get to your weapon fast. As long as you are always aware when out in public you should be able to recognize a threat in time to take cover and retrieve this weapon.

Unsolicited advice: If you do use this bag for a CC DON'T EVER PUT IT DOWN OR LEAVE IT ALONE. If you put a weapon in this thing it better be locked in your car or on your back at all times. That is common sense to most people who read this... but just in case you didn't think about that- keep it in mind. (I live in AZ, so carrying in this bag is 100% legal even without a permit.)

Just to give you an idea of how much stuff you can fit into this bag, when I go to work I fill this bag with:
-A Samsung Note 10.1 tablet computer (fits perfectly)
-A large water bottle
-Basic first aid / survival kit
-Multi tool
-Lock for gym locker
-Extra clothes to change into after gym (rolled)
-Wallet, phone, keys, sunglasses
-I could fit more in it, but I just don't have the need.

It fits a lot of stuff. One of the best things about it is... if I was in an emergency situation and needed to bug out, when I get home I can easily attachthis bag to my Rush 24 with 4 simple straps and be on my way to safety.

All in all I'm in love with this bag. It's great for an EDC, a CC (with a cautious and responsible mindset), and a great bug-out addition.

product_title: Tactical Military Foldable Foregrip Bipod Grip M16 AR-15 AK-47 AR-10 new style
review_body:
Received this bipod grip today, no problems with the seller or Amazon. No instructions with the unit. Figured out most of it, and with some insight, was able to get it to fit on the bottom picatinny rail of the USM4's AR-15 hand guard. So far, so good. Noted the two halves were slightly apart, leaving the possibility of a pinch, but it didn't pinch me. Found it rotated slightly in traverse, was very loose and unstable. Finally figured out the two things that looked like buttons were releases, but though they moved slightly, nothing happened. Twisted, pushed, wriggled, and finally, for no known reason the legs popped out. Ok. Used the buttons to adjust the length, and they worked a bit rudely, but did work. Pushed the legs back into the pod, and they wouldn't stay. Hurt my hand slightly pushing and hitting them in, finally they stuck. Took the unit off, and noted a screw head common to tactical add-ons, used a dime to loosen it, and the gap widened a tiny bit, the loose tilt and turn got looser, so it was even less stable. Loosened it another turn, and the legs popped out. Difficulty getting them back in, but finally did. Re-installed on the picatinny, and had exactly the same problems. It feels and is unstable. The design is interesting, and with closer tolerances, might actually work (with a better button setup to release the legs).
Dry firing found it too loose, too unstable, though otherwise ok. Closed the legs and it pinched my palm slightly, and the legs had difficulty being pushed back in. It wouldn't "lock" them inside the grip until about the 7th time, occasionally leaving one leg partially out, one in place. Tried it on the Core AR 15, and same results.
The concept is good, in my opinion, but this unit was poorly done. On the positive side, it has a slightly scalloped grip that I prefer to the Grip Pod's simple round grip, though the Grip Pod's piled rings grip isn't bad. I have a Grip Pod on the Core AR, and it works perfectly, easily, and is stable. Will give this Gun Tech unit to a fellow shooter who wants to try it, and have ordered a second Grip Pod for the USM4 setup.s perfectly, easily, and is stable. product_title: Polara Golf XDS Extra Distance & Spin 3-Piece Golf Balls
review_body:
I just want to say that I am about a 13 Handicap and have broken 80 once in my life. My goal has always been to have a shot at 79 everytime I go out to play.....However, my driving usually made the feat quite difficult. I was skeptical about playing a USGA non-conforming ball at first but considering the fact that I will never compete in a US Am or Mid-Am persuaded me to try these balls out. So I originally purchased a trial pack from the Polara website. Took them out to the local executive course to try out. OMG! These balls are absolutely amazing! I had a legitimate shot at a 33 on the back nine that day, and continually break 40 for 9 holes most days with this ball. I am now a Polara customer for life!

I began to only line the ball up with my target from the tee, and then played around with adjusting my lie only in the fairway to see how the ball flies when aligned vs. not aligned. Here is what I discovered:

1) The ball flies straight - Slices turn into baby "Nicklaus" fades. The dimple pattern causes the ball to self correct in flight. These XDS balls have a normal trajectory with every club, unlike the other Polara balls which have a lower trajectory.

2) Wonderful feel - i thought that these balls would be lacking here, but pure iron and wedge shots feel like "butta!" I'd compare these to a Titeleist NXT tour in feel.

3) LONG! - Since these balls fly STRAIGHT (no distance lost left/right) with little side spin, they release when they land. When i played regular golf balls, I put so much spin on the drive that when they landed, they stuck, robbing me of distance.

4) Fairway play - When I lined the arrow up with my target from the fairway, they flew straight.....when I didn't, they flew strainght! The only difference I noticed was when you lined the ball up, there was more lift and flew only slightly higher. I also noticed that if you placed the ball with the alignment arrow perpendicular to the target, wedge shots had a lot of spin. Definitely one-hop-and-stop.

5) Putting - Has a nice soft feel.....not balata soft, but deftinitely soft. Rolled true, regardless of the assymetrical dimple pattern.

6) Intangibles - This ball allowed soooo much more than the above review:
- FUN: Regularly having birdie and par putts is what it's all about! You can start trying to strategize more and enjoy the course your playing rather than getting frustrated with lost ball after lost ball!
- Time Saver: You are in the fairway or slightly in the rough. Not a pond, the woods, a neighbors dog house....
- Confidence: No more jitters on tee boxs! just try to put the best swing you can on it and let it fly. This confidence then translates to all other facets of your game
- Focus on other parts of game: Now you can really focus on improving the most important part of the game....getting the ball in the hole (wedge play and putting).

I highly recommend this ball to any player not attempting to get into a USGA event. And for you purists out there, give us a break! Golf is a hobby and a form of recreation. Its not meant to be frustrating! The game is inherently difficult and you still need to gauge the environment/course/lie, select the right club, play the right shot, read a green, and execute a swing. This ball simply gives you confidence to keep putting in the effort and concentration to do your best. I can honestly say that I now have a shot at 79 each time I go out!

Happy golfing!

product_title: Powerline BSGLPX Leg Press for BSG10X Home Gym
review_body:
First, let me say that I love my BSG10X home gym. I hoped that I would love it even more with the BSGLPX leg press attachment. That is not the case, however. My leg press attachment arrived two days after I ordered it and in perfect condition. I have no complaints about Fitness Factory.

Here are my observations:

The good: Yes, you can perform a leg press with it and It is very compact. It also was well-packaged.

The bad:
1.The accuracy of the manufacturing leaves a lot to be desired. My leg press attachment is offset to the left(from the vantage point of the seat of the BSG10X) so that the pulleys do not align (another commenter had the same issue). The right foot plate is also closer to the seat than is the left, although neither of these manufacturing defects renders the unit unusable. Body Solid, it's time to pay a visit to the manufacturer and check the alignment of the welding jigs.

2. The leg press attachment is uncomfortable to use with soft-soled shoes, such as sneakers. The single-arm design uses curved foot plates with a tight radius. The curved foot plate presses on the arch of your foot rather than distributing the load across the heel and ball of your foot. Higher end gyms avoid this effect by using parallelogram arrangements and a flat foot plate. I compensate by wearing bicycling shoes (without cleats) that have a rigid sole. The rigid sole spreads the load and prevents the discomfort. If you are considering buying a combination of the BSG10X plus the leg press attachment, I recommend opting for a different gym that has a parallelogram leg press.

3.There are no instructions on how to use the leg extension station or the low pulley when the leg press attachment is installed. Taking the leg press unit on and off during an exercise program is not really an option because the removable part of the leg press attachment is pretty heavy (I'd estimate 20 lbs.), and not easy to keep in position with one hand while you try to insert the clevis pin to hold it in place.

4. It is possible to access the leg extension station and the low pulley by detaching only the bottom end of the leg press cable and rotating the leg press attachment away from the BSG10X. The leg press attachment will rotate about 30 degrees until the end of the cable fouls the pulley on the leg press attachment, stopping its movement. This is fine for access to the leg extension station. It also gives pretty good access to the low pulley for biceps curls. I am concerned that fouling the pulley will cause failure of the pulley over time.

5. The leg press attachment blocks direct access to the low pulley for other low pulley exercises (glute kickback, abductor and adductor exercises). Moving to the side makes those exercises possible, but means that the pulley is not aligned and the chain rubs against the leg press attachment. This would have been an easy design fix.

6. I expected the leg press attachment to fold flat to the floor when both cables are released. It does not, due to interference at the hinge. The stress on the area around the hinge is very great when both cables are released and the leg press attachment moved as close to the floor as it will go. It also presents a tripping hazard. I don't place the attachment in that position. I intend to post photographs of these issues.position with one hand while you try to insert the clevis pin to hold it in place.

review_headline: Today is day 60 of my APY60 program and it's only the beginning...
review_body:
My yoga instructor recommended the APY60 program to me after I had been practicing yoga for about 6 months. She was trained at Kurt's yoga studio, believes in his methods, and felt very strongly that I could benefit from the program. She was right.

I feel that the small investment I made by purchasing and using APY60 will benefit me the rest of my life. I noticed increased body strength, mental focus, flexibility, and endurance after a few weeks and I am pleased with the results.

The daily blends (10-15 minutes) were a good start to my day, before going to work. The weekly practices (40-45 minutes) which I did in the evenings, seemed difficult at first, but got easier each day.

I do believe, as Kurt Johnsen (the founder of American Power Yoga and the APY60 program) says, that the system is something that you need to incorporate into your life. Yoga is a lifestyle, a lifetime journey. Use APY60 to help you on that journey, whether you use it just as a stepping stone to another form of yoga or other mental and fitness program. Personally, I am using it as a stepping stone to my next step which is \\"The Ultimate Yogi\\" program, but I will take those things that I learned from APY60 with me and I will continue to visit APY60 in the future as I rotate daily through my yoga DVDs.

For best results, I also believe that yoga is something that needs to be practiced daily, or at least every other day. I noticed this when taking days off during vacations. I missed three days once and I could tell a huge difference in my practices when I continued.

Namaste :-)

product_title: Timex Ironman Run Trainer GPS with Heart Rate
review_headline: Highly functional and easy to use
review_body:
This watch has many features to track the details of your training workouts (min/max/avg heart rate, min/max/avg speed and pace, time, distance, location, calories, elevation gains & losses, time in heart rate zones, time in speed/pace zones, etc.) which can then be analyzed easily with the associated software.

It also has the ease-of-use and sturdy build of other Timex watches such as the Ironman series, with just the added complexity of managing the GPS and HR sensors. But even that gets easy after a few times of using it.

The display is highly customizable, to show whichever metrics you want during your workout and in whichever line you want them, either in 3 lines with a big font in the middle line or in 4 lines with smaller fonts but more metrics displayed. Note, in order to customize the display options (I like to have different setups to use in different activities), it's easier to do it through the settings in the Timex "Device Agent" PC software that comes with the watch. There are up to 8 programmable display settings and you can switch from one to another during your workout without having to stop. You can segment your workout in laps and will get full data (i.e. all of the above metrics) for each lap.

You can store up to 15 workouts in the watch, which is more than enough as you can download the workouts to a PC before you hit that limit.

The watch build is solid, and the wrist band is fully replaceable if it ever breaks (which is unlikely as it is quite solid, unlike in other recent models Timex has put out lately that have thinner wrist bands).

The watch is bulky but quite light and nicely shaped so it doesn't look nor feel like a brick in your wrist.

The HR sensor is quite accurate (I have compared it against treadmill sensors with no detectable difference) and it never loses the signal unless you go in the water (i.e. HR sensor can't be used for swimming). The GPS sensor is very accurate and reliable as well except for sometimes the first few seconds after it says it's ready.

The online training software Timex is associated with (TraininPeaks), which is used for analyzing your workouts, is great, quite intuitive and highly functional even in the free version (I have not tried the full version). It is linked to Google maps so you can "play" your workout and watch where you went and what heart rate, speed and elevation you had at each moment of the workout. I recommend using this online software not just for the awesome analysis features but also because it tracks your fitness and alerts you of some things such as for example when you've improved your lactate threshold.

Overall, this is a wonderful GPS/HR watch. Nicely done Timex.

In any case, I have re-established my exercise habit (I find that early morning works best for me) and have improved my diet considerably.  The kit is really put together really well, with the DVDs, a journal/food diary, an instruction book and a cookbook, so it is a great buy.  I even canceled my gym membership because I feel that I get so much more out of exercising along with Jillian's DVDs than I do going to the gym, and I can always go to the track if I need to add some cardio.  As an example, I had attempted Jillian's 30-Day Shred program (a DVD separate from the 90 day Body Revolution set) a few months ago and found Level 1 to be hard, so I gave it up; now I can do Level 3 of that program without much difficulty, so I know that my fitness level has improved.  I highly recommend the 90 day program.  I'll update this review when I complete my 2nd go-round with the 90 day program.

review_headline: I'm embarrassed I waited for so long to get one of these
review_body:
I am instinctively (perhaps reflexively) skeptical about exercise and health products that get lots of breathless coverage in health magazines, are pushed by late night infomercials, and discussed by the obsessed people on the treadmills at the gym. I started to hear about foam rollers a year or so back and thought that the rank odor common to most gimmicks out there. There were the requisite flood of YouTube videos promising to 'change my life', hours of spot-specific exercise routines, commercials promising that I could look like the fitness models shown working out with this revolutionary new product, etc. I figured that this too would pass and went about my business.

Fast forward a year and I had the opportunity to pick up this product from Amazon as a trial. I was not expecting much but after a short time using it I am a convert.

Pros:
1 - In general foam rollers allow you to use gravity and your own weight as a means of massaging and stretching muscles. When used in specific ways you can also presumably get some strength training benefits, but I have not gone down that road yet. After a short time using this product I have been amazed at how effective it is at relieving tension and completely freeing my upper back of knots.

2 - This roller comes with a very simple to understand set of instructions with pictures illustrating its use for all the major muscle groups.

3 - There are additional videos online, but I have not yet watched most of them. I found the printed instructions more than adequate to get me started.

4 - This roller will support large folks - I'm over 220 pounds and it had no problem supporting me. At 15\\" wide it's larger than many other products on the market.

5 - It's compact, light weight and hollow. I am considering bringing it along on my next business trip as it, when stuffed with my workout clothes, socks and t-shirts, effectively takes up almost no space in my carry-on.

6 - I'm not an expert on the full range of foam roller products as this is my first one, but this product seems to be exceptionally well made.

Cons:
None yet

product_title: 250 Recumbent Exercise Bike
review_body:
My wife and I are totally satisfied with the Schwinn 250. Here is the data:

- We are in our mid-40's. Wife is 5'4". I am 6'0" 205lbs. Seat settings for my wife leave one more notch forward available to use. I'm about 5 notches back on the seat; with about 4 more available. The bike is very stable and has solid construction.

- Seat pad is thick rubbery material outside, good solid padding inside. Appears that it will last a long time. Comfortable; even after a long session. Easy to wipe down too.

- Pedal operation is quite and smooth. No whirring sounds like the older style ped bikes. The magnetic resistance technology works great. Being taller, I was concerned about my knees hitting the control panel; but that does not happen with the Schwinn.

- Using the electronic display is easy enough. There are hints at the bottom to get you going with the setup. The display is bright and clear; easy to understand. If you try to create more than one exercise profile, you must press-n-hold the Schwinn Advantage button for about 3 seconds. When it beeps, then use the up/down arrows to select which profile to create/edit. The 250 Schwinn can hold two user profiles if you want to track performance over time. There is a cup-holder on the display, and a place to set a Kindle book-reader, or similar device. The built-in fan is worth-less; I can cough more air than it. Haven't used the MP3 sound speakers, but they look very tiny inside. Probably good for listening to talk-radio or something like that.

- Assembly took my wife and I just over an hour. Instructions for setup were straight-forward. Wrenches were included. Be sure to be careful with hooking up the wires. They can get pinched.

- The pulse-rate monitor works every time for both of us. Just put the palms of your hands over the sensors located on each side of the seat.

Over-all, we are happy with our purchase. This recumbent bike is easy on the back and leg joints, but still lets us get a good heart-pounding sweat-filled workout.

===== Update 4/7/2015 =====
Thought I should give a quick update: My wife and I still are using this bike. It has held up great! Not a thing wrong with it. Typically, we bike about 30 minutes a day, and use it about 5 times a week. The seat cushion is in great sharp and hasn't deformed or broken down. This is a very solid exercise bike and has performed flawlessly. Still highly recommended.
========================

review_headline: Broke after using twice, Sole Customer Service unresponsive.
review_body: After setting up the elliptical and using it twice, the right wheel kept jumping the track after taking a few steps (we both weigh well under the max lbs. noted). A quick google search (and information in the manual) indicated that it might be a problem with 1)too much dirt or too much lubrication on the track, or 2) bolts not tightened enough. I cleaned off the track and wheel with rubbing alcohol and placed a small amount of lubrication back on the track. My husband and I tightened the bolts. The wheel still keeps jumping the track after a few steps. I tried calling Sole Customer Service and was placed on hold for 40 minutes (even though the recording stated that I was in position 1). After holding for 40 minutes of waiting at position 1, I somehow jumped to position 2. With no indication that my phone call would ever get through to a live person, I hung up and sent an email request through Sole's website. I received an email a day later asking me to fill out a form. No big deal, except that after I filled out this additional form, I received an email two days later stating that I needed to send my original receipt and then a representative would contact me. Why was I not notified of this during the first email? I could have sent all the relevant information if it was requested of me up front. I emailed a copy of my receipt within an hour of receiving the email. I still have not heard back from any Sole representative either via email or by phone. This equipment is basically useless. The wheel jumping off track during use is incredibly dangerous if your knee is in the wrong position when it goes off track. I would not recommend this model and I'd go a step further in not recommending any Sole products for lack of customer service.

product_title: Callaway ORG 14S Cart Bag
review_body:
I wanted to replace my carry bag because it doesn't hold enough beer in the side pockets ;) Actually I wanted to switch to a bag with 14 dividers as my old Callaway bag only had three and my new clubs were constantly banging each other. I golf regularly and just got new clubs. I needed to try and fool myself into thinking I would treat them like they were my children.

I decided on this bag and have been loving it every round so far. There are ample pockets and compartments and the putter tube is awesome. I always hated having my putter with the rest of my clubs because the irons would sometimes knock my putter cover off while driving around in the cart. Doesn't happen now since the putter is on the outside of the bag. The largest pocket on the right side is lined to keep drinks cold and has two drain holes on the bottom. The putter tube is on the left side and you can't see it in any pictures. It is really a great convenience to have it on the outside of the bag.

When the bag is strapped in to the cart there is a very firm and reinforced loop the cart belt goes through. THIS IS GREAT!! My carry bag always twisted in carts and made all the pockets tough to get into. This cart bag hasn't budged so far.

As for the front pockets.....there are three and an open compartment on top. I don't use the open compartment as I fear my reckless cart driving will result in whatever is in there flying out and getting lost. The top compartment is for things like wallets, cell phones, personal belongings, etc. It is lined on the inside with a felt that prevents any scratching. Below that is the pocket I use to store my tees and markers. You can easily fit a few hundred tees in it. Bottom pocket is for balls. I would estimate you can store four dozen balls in there.

On the right of the front compartments is a velcro circle for your glove. Nice, but not my thing. I put my glove with my tees. The open compartment I don't use has slots on the front to store more tees. There are also two slots on the inside of the open compartment for pencils or markers. I put a sharpie in one and the other is not used.

The bag is stable when standing at the drop off. I haven't had a problem with it falling over.

It comes with a plastic alignment marker. It's a fluff bonus. I pulled it off as I mark my balls before they go in the bag.

product_title: FINIS Neptune
review_body:
I have been an avid swimmer for the past couple years and have always wanted to be able to listen to music while getting a great workout in the pool. The FINIS Neptune MP3 player is exactly what I have been hoping for.

The device's rechargeable batteries were already fully charged when I opened the package. Downloading music onto the player is as easy as plugging it's included USB cord into your computer, then dragging the song files to the mounted folder. The MP3 player clips onto the back of your goggle strap and the sound conduction pads clip on the sides of your goggle straps right in front of your ears. The sound waves are conducted through the bone into your inner ear. It is amazing how well this technology works.

At first the sound was a little shallow, but after adjusting the built-in equalizer and repositioning the conduction pads I got a much better sound quality.

PROS
- Music while you swim!
- Easy configuration
- Comfortable
- Holds lots of music
- Built-in equalizer

CONS
- Poor playlist control

I definitely recommend this device for anyone who loves to swim and wants to be able to listen to their music while they workout in the pool.

product_title: 849540 Weaver, 40/44 Riflescope, 4-12X44 Adjustable Objective Matte Dual-x
review_body:
I picked this up at my local gun store to go on a 5.56 AR-15. Normally I have an EOTech on this rifle but I have a hunting trip coming up and wanted to bring this rifle to do some varmint shooting so I needed something with magnification. Since this is just for plinking and shooting the occasional raccoon or squirrel I didn't want to spend a ton of money. My criteria when selecting a scope was 1) magnification greater than 9X, 2) a brand name I've heard of, and 3) under $300.

This was one of two scopes the store had that met all three criteria. I mounted it to the rifle with a pair of $12 rings I ordered from Amazon. When I sighted it in I was a little nervous because I didn't have a bore sighter but the first shot was on paper at 50 yards. Shooting 2 shot groups it took 3 adjustments to get it zeroed.

Other scopes I've purchased have been Leupold or Nikon, so that is my point of comparison. It is not a fair point of comparison because those scopes cost 2-4x as much.

The scope serves its purpose. I think I paid about $225 and I feel like I got a $225 scope. I can shoot with it, but the eye relief leaves a bit to be desired, especially at higher magnification levels. I also get some fishbowl effect around the outside of the image. Since I was shooting in daylight, I can't comment on light transmission. The parallax adjustment is a nice feature, but to be honest I couldn't really tell a big difference when I cranked it from one extreme to the other so I'm not sure if it's just my eyesight betraying me or if it doesn't really do much.

All in all the scope will serve its purpose, but here are two thoughts I have...

1) The store also had a Thompson Center 12x scope with built-in rings for $100 which would probably have yielded similar results

2) From what I've read online, the Vortex Viper series of scopes are in the same general price range and get good reviews. This scope has some bad reviews elsewhere. If I didn't have time constraints, I would return this one and order a Vortex Viper.s elsewhere. If I didn't have time constraints, I would return this one and order a Vortex Viper.

The FREE belt is a bonus, but the buckle kind of bulked out a little if you wore a duty belt with them, so I went with the velcro duty belt liner instead, but by themselves as casual wear, the belt included is just fine.  They come in the usual 'law enforcement' colors, ie, black, dark navy and brown, but because of our jobs we went with the olive pants and the PROPPER tan shirts and it made for a great uniform combination.  For duty wear, these are very comfortable and they held together wash after wash.  I think as far as duty pants go, these were the best design for the dollar and they're very professional looking and I especially liked the straighter legs as opposed to the puffed out pockets of the BDU pants.  These pants were my favorite uniform duty pants and it was a shame the day I had to turn them in when I left my job, but I definitely had to get a pair (in olive) for casual wear for hiking and camping and fishing.  If you're a law enforcement official and looking to get a great pair of pants that offer a lot for your money, you can't go wrong with these.  If you're looking for a comfortable pair of travel pants or casual pants for outdoorsy activities, you can't go wrong with these.  They fit, feel and look great! product_title: Pittsburgh Penguins NHL Hockey LED Light Crank Key Chain
review_headline: It's a nifty little flashlight to have with you!
review_body:
I bought this flashlight about 5 months ago and I must say that it was on my keychain for about a month, but it is now sitting in a drawer for now. It's not there because I don't like it, it's only there because I needed to take some things off my keychain before it got way too big and bulky in my pocket all the time. I like the idea of a crank flashlight because the only time you need this type of thing is when you can't get to any batteries anywhere. It is easy to crank and the light is actually very powerful for such a small flashlight. I was impressed by how much light was given off by this.

The Penguins logo is printed onto this silicone-feeling area on the front of the flashlight and it looks very nice. I have bought many little Penguins-styled gizmos and gadgets, and this is one of the higher quality pieces. I do like the Penguins aspect of it!

One thing to keep in mind is that the crank for it sits in a little hole in the side of the flashlight, but it comes out of that hole and into the "ready to crank" position very easily. That is the main reason I will not be using it on my keychain because I found that every time I took it out of my pocket, it would be in the wrong position and I would have to fix it.

I found that the crank coming out of the indentation where it usually sits and the fact that the amount of times I would be using this was not worth it to keep it on my keychain. If I was in dire need of a flashlight, I could always use my phone. But if you find yourself needing a quick flashlight that you can get to easily, then I would recommend this to you!

product_title: Moultrie M-880 Low Glow Game Camera
review_body:
After buying, and quickly returning for repair, a StealthCam CORE trail camera I read the reviews and decided to go with the Moultrie M-880 trail cam. I've only had it out for a few days, but the 900 plus pics it has taken so far are outstanding, regardless of the time of day or night. The StealthCam had a narrow beam of light illuminating a tiny spot directly in front of the camera in the night shots. Not so with the M-880. It's night flash illuminates a wide field to both sides and pretty far out in front. The shots of the deer jumping and running are surprisingly clear, regardless of the time, day or night. Very little blur, if any at all. Color is good during the day, no white washout in night shots.
My only complaint would be the rather thin manual that comes with the camera. I didn't find it all that helpful in intitially setting it up and the software you can download from Moultrie, well,let's just say I couldn't get it to work. I could get it downloaded but then I had trouble unzipping the files so that it would work. I'm currently using the software provided by StealthCam as it is actually pretty user friendly. The only other complaint, again, is in the download area. I can't get it to download the latest software updates. I sent Moultrie an email requesting help, so far, after 2 working days, no response.
But I'm still giving the camera 5 stars as that is what the review is for, the software I can figure out eventually. As far as the StealthCam I sent off for repair, I'll be selling it when it comes back in.
