product_title: Vanguard Endeavor HD Angled Eyepiece Spotting Scope
review_body:
UPDATE April 11, 2015
This spotting scope has been great for use on the target range. We never go to the range without it. My son has two Russian sniper rifles and enjoys shooting at targets so far away he would have a lot of difficulty adjusting his sights or his scope without the aid of this scope.

Original Review...
For years I had an inexpensive pair of binoculars which seemed to be fine for me. Then as a gift from my company I received a much better pair of Nikon binoculars which blew me away with the image quality. As an amateur photographer I appreciate the advantages of a good lens, and I own two of them. The quality and sharpness of the images are well worth the extra cost. The same is true of this Vanguard Endeavor HD 82A Spotting Scope.

This is only the second spotting scope I've ever owned, and the last one was about 20 years ago so it simply can't be compared to the quality of the image or build of this Vanguard scope. The optics here are superior in color, sharpness, and brightness provided by the 82mm lens.

My son and I enjoy target shooting. He has a Mosin-Nagant Russian sniper rifle which is quite accurate at fairly long distances. We have been using my digital camera and Nikon binoculars for spotting his targeting. This spotting scope improves our capability dramatically. The much longer zoom and bright image allows us to see greater detail and help sight in his rifle optics.

The optical quality of this scope and the overall build of the unit are great. I was surprised how bright the image is. Materials are top notch, feel solid, and look well designed. I expect this scope to perform for many years due to the quality of the design and build.

For the size of the optics this scope isn't too heavy and is easy to handle. At 4 pounds it is lighter than my DSLR with a long lens attached. The way the eyepiece locks into place is comforting. The adjustable eye cup makes it much easier to sight once the scope is set up and fixed on a distant target.

We especially appreciate that the 82A is Waterproof and Fog Proof. We are somewhat restricted in our target shooting in the summer in California due to the very dry conditions and chance of fires. So we do a lot of shooting in the winter months when the fire danger is quite low. Winter rains, cool weather, and some fog in our area are common so we will be able to use the 82A in those wet conditions. Neither of my DSLR cameras are waterproof and I'm always nervous when I'm in a situation where is moisture.

The 82A has a quick focus course knob and fine focus knob making it much easier to adjust for those distant targets we shoot at. The side mounted Fast Aim Sights help a lot to quickly zero in on our targets too. Comparing this to our Nikon binoculars or my long zoom lens on my DSLR, well there is no comparison. I can never hold the binoculars steady enough to do the job, and the tripod mounted camera is fine but it has insufficient zoom.

I also appreciate the ability to mount the 82A on a tripod; something I was never able to do with the binoculars. However I'm going to need a better tripod due to the long zoom of the scope. The tripod I have now simply moves too much when I'm adjusting the focus and zoom.

The only place this scope falls a bit short for me is in the sharpness of the image. It is just great for target shooting, but as I considered purchasing the Vanguard PA-202 Digiscoping Adapter for my DSLR I decided against it. My standards for sharpness aren't met by this scope. No matter how hard I try I can't get the image to be as sharp as I'd like no matter what zoom level I adjust to. Again for target shooting this scope is really good. It also exhibits slight purple fringing when I view the moon. I would never be happy with moon shots with this scope, although for just viewing it is great. As a targeting scope it is excellent though and that is it's primary use at our house. I rate it 5 stars in spite of the image quality issues. If I were buying something for my digital camera I'd make another choice (likely another lens and not a spotting scope) so it is unfair to take a star off for that reason. I hope others don't automatically eliminate this scope for their DSLR use. I am particularly fussy about sharpness, and I have a 24MP camera with a couple of very expensive lenses that meet my standards. If you own a point-n-shoot or a megazoom camera I'm sure you will be quite happy with the images you achieve using this scope.

We keep the 82A in the box it was delivered in. The supplied pouch is inadequate to protect it against bumps. Vanguard should increase the padding of the pouch all over.

It's a small thing but I'm very fussy about lens caps. Those supplied by DSLR lens manufacturers are seldom good to me. Most of the time the supplied caps are hard to grip. The lens cap on the 82A is one of the best I've seen. You can grip it from the outer edges or from the center finger pinch points and get a good grip either way.

product_title: New Balance GPS Runner
review_body:
Okay, first off, people on here need to chill out with the angst against anyone who might want to do more with their watch. Excuse me for thinking it's cool to plug in your watch and have your data download so you can simply chart your long runs, pace, etc, without geeking out on a bunch of spreadsheets.

Having gotten that out of the way, this is a decent watch. It takes about two minutes to get the signal and then I'm off. You can customize your display settings, mark laps, and store workouts. I have had no problems with it so far after a month of use. Yes, you do need to read the manual to understand it, and the manual could be a bit more verbose, but all in all it's the low end solution and it still has some decent features. Also, I have been very pleasantly surprised by the battery life - as long as the GPS tracking is off when not in use, it can last a few weeks.

I don't think it's wrong to want to do the other stuff with your watch, but this one is just the plain, HR monitor, and GPS tracking. For more features you'll have to spend a bit more, which I wasn't willing to do, but am still very satisfied.

product_title: Upper Bounce Trampoline Anchor Kit (Set of 4)
review_body: I watched our neighbors trampoline float straight up into the air, then start rolling and crash into our fence at high speed during a storm, so I knew it would be important to have anchors for our trampoline we bought on craigslist.  I looked at all of the reviews for the different types of anchors before deciding on these.  We have really hard clay here in east Texas, and this was a concern - the anchors couldn't be wimpy. That being said I had absolutely no issue installing these anchors.  I hammered in a piece of rebar to make a hole that was slightly larger in diameter to the approximate depth of the anchor, then filled the hole with water to soften it up.  I used the biggest smooth rod I could fit through the eyelet of the anchor as a \\"T\\" handle to crank the anchors into the ground.  I made sure they were low enough that I would never be able to hit them with the mower blade.  I tested each one by attempting to pull them out, but I couldn't get them to budge - at all - and I tried.  The straps took a little time to figure out, but it was getting dark... (I checked them the next morning to be sure they were in correctly).  In my opinion this is an excellent anchor system.  The only possible improvement would be to replace the straps with cables, as only then would a person be absolutely sure the trampoline is not going anywhere.  One thing is sure the anchors aren't coming out!  It's common to have very high wind here, and we've had some since installing the anchors, nothing has shown any signs of movement.  It's nice to know that if you want to take the anchors back out you can - just unscrew them from the ground just like you put them in.  You might not be able to reuse the same hole though because it gets tore up on the way out - The first two I put in I had to move as my placement would require one of the remaining anchors to be really close to a huge crack in the ground.  The anchors I received are black powder coated, not plated like in the picture - I think that's a big improvement as powder coating is tough.

I don't know how I am going to use it. It would be great for chopping, prying things up, and a few other task because it is so heavy duty. It is good quality steel and good construction. The problem is it is too big and thick for fine work. I sharpened it and was happy with the edge, but this thing is built for chopping and brute force work, not fine work. If you use it for brute force task it quickly loses its edge. I am thinking of sharpening it with a metal file like I do my hatchets from now on. That way I can quickly touch up the edge without a lot of work. I don't know if I will carry this knife. It is big, heavy, and limited to brute force task. I would be better off with a hatchet or machete and a smaller knife. I am on Amazon shopping for another knife right now because this one will not do what I want.

I like the bottom part of the sheath. It is a very nice plastic sheath but it attaches to a floppy nylon loop at the top. This is so you can remove the loop and attach it to a pack or something. That is great but for belt carry it looks strange.

Update: I recently bought a Mora bushcraft knife [[ASIN:B009O01H0Y Morakniv Bushcraft Carbon Fixed Blade Knife with Sandvik Stainless Steel Blade, Black, 0.125/4.3-Inch]] and I like it a lot more. Far sharper, better steel, and a hard edge on back for striking a ferrocerym rod or scraping. It is light weight and I am a light weight hiker. In short I like it a lot more, but it is not going to take abuse like this knife. I also have the cold steel thrower that is an excellent survival knife. I am going to have to do a review on this knife soon. [[ASIN:B000BSY9AI Cold Steel True Flight Thrower Paracord Wrapped Handle (Sheath)]] The thrower has good steel, holds an edge, is a strong durable blade and it hasa thin light weight sheath that is real easy to carry. Consider this knife also.

I used a file and find sand paper to remove the coating and put a sharp corner on the back of the knife. I may remove it all eventually as I see no need for the black coating. The knife could not strike a spark from a ferrocerym rod without doing this.

product_title: Kimber PepperBlaster II - Gray
review_headline: Great ergonomics and overall feel, nice (albeit unnecessary) sights, tiny complaints.
review_body:
I'm giving four stars because I think it could be better, not because there is something necessarily wrong.

I'll start with my thoughts: Device fires lower tube first, then upper. Given the high probability that deployment may be necessary inside the danger zone of 2-3 feet having the bottom tube go off first means that the first shot if aimed mid face will hit the assailant in the mouth/ chin. Certainly less ideal than in the eyes/ forehead. Having said that I also could counter argue that perhaps the the idea is that the user would want their last shot to be the most precise. Either way I'd advise any user to \\"double tap\\" if the device is ever needed to be deployed.

Pros: Range! This device is all about being able to deploy non lethal force on an assailant from as far away as possible. If you need to put a shot of OC in someones left eye from ten feet away, this is the go to. Ergonomics! Feels like a pocket pistol and has similar accuracy to a Taurus Judge or other 410 shotgun pistol but less lethality. Stopping power! Based on video demos I've seen it seems to have an immediate and debilitating effect on vision if it hits in the upper face followed by a total shutdown within 30 seconds or so if it gets into the eyes and or nose.

Cons: Limited point blank functionality. From 3 feet or less you would really need to be calm and precise because you only get two squeezes and the spread will only be 4-6 inches in diameter. Capacity: While two perfectly placed shots are more than enough to stop one man of any size, if faced with a multiple attacker situation or if in panic both shots were deployed inaccurately one could be in \\"a heap of s***\\" fairly quickly.

Summary: If you are a good pistol shot and feel as though you manage high stress situations well and just want a non-lethal option for carry then this may be perfect. If you are more familiar operating hairspray than a firearm you should get something that is more aerosol based and better for the spray & pray approach to self defense.pray & pray approach to self defense.

Handle shows custom woodworking, a nice brass reinforced pommel, with plenty of grip space to use this weapon with one or two hands if desired....usually not desired! The blade has a crushing side along with an interior cutting surface...I have a biase for single edged weapons, being a Japanese stylist....and the weight of the blade is intense.

This superbly crafted knife is fantastic....for you muddle heads who care? the sheath is reinforced leather with real solid metal fittings...forget about the two toothpicks that come with this setup....They detract from the otherwise intensely beautiful, curvaceous, functional quality of this traditionally constructed Kukari. For the price? It would be hard to find a better Kukari at any price! my only thang would be the weight of this weapon which is substantial making quick movements involving fine motor coordination a little slow at times..... But it is a Kukari after all and a fantastic one at that!

product_title: Bushnell Laser Boresighter
review_body:
Bought this item at my local store here in Alaska, since it's already here and figured why waste energy shipping even though it would be cheaper if purchased through Amazon.com.

I previously tried one of the cheaper 45 ACP bore sighting cartridges and found they performed horrid as my barrel has a feed ramp. In other words because of the ramp on the barrel feed, the cartridge casing would not seat at a perfect 90 degree into the barrel and especially with the slide closed down on the laser bore sighting cartridge. Needless to say, I returned that gadget and purchased a more suitable bore sighting instrument such as this one.

The only problem, this instrument cannot sight barrels of short length, as both the tip and the 45 degree cone need to seat into the barrel perfectly. One of my handguns has a rear windage adjustment screw. If I ever disassembled the rear sight containing the windage adjustment screw, having a laser bore sight device would save a lot of time and hassle!

This instrument has a cheap cloth velcro case, which doesn't seem to remain closed and properly secure the plastic parts and screws. Dinged one star, albeit, the instrument seems to work perfectly fine. I also read a previous review which recommended stretching the main battery spring. I did so, prior to any initial testing, so cannot comment as to whether this issue still remains with the newer models.

product_title: Saunders No-Twist Conventional & Recurve Bow Stringer
review_body: I hurt my shoulder using this! The pad slides and is actually a stupid design. Placing the pad on the limb instead of at the tips makes you have to use more force and travel distance while pulling to bend the limb. So actually one limb is flexing from the tip and the other after the pad inevitably slips is at almost the middle of the limb where it is rigid. It's still a real challenge even after taking out the slack from the stringer rope. I bought one of those Webster nylon strap stringers that spans both tips and it was like magic! I would never recommend buying a stringer that uses a pad mid limb. It puts to much stress on the limb that is doing more of the flexing to compensate for the other that is at mid limb. This means equal flex on both limbs plus less travel distance that you need to pull upward. I highly recommend the Webster. Any other that is from tip to tip will probably be just as good.

product_title: SNIPER Scope 3-9x40 1" Tube Full-size AOL W/E QTA, Tactical Zero Locking/Resetting, R/G/B Mil-dot Reticle, 2.5" Sunshade
review_body:
When I take the mildot reticle out of the equation, optically it seems pretty good. I'm a serious photographer, so I'm really picky about the quality of my optics. Normally, I don't have a problem paying money for good optics, but unfortunately I'm on a bit of a budget at the moment.

The mounting hardware I found a little puzzling. The instructions don't seem to state how tightly they should be torqued, There's definitely a gap between the half's, but I'd be very reluctant to tighten them all the way down.

The turrets turn crisply and have a nice little ring for locking them... Major plus. I was impressed that the unit came with two batteries, another thumbs up. The caps and sunshades appear reasonably rugged and require a bit of effort to remove, which is a good thing in my opinion.

The only thing that I have to say is a bit of a disappointment is the clarity of the reticle. When simply leaving it powered off, it looks good. You can definitely separate the dots from the cross hair. However, once you turn it on, that's where things get a little meh.

All three brightness's of red, it's pretty difficult to separate the dots from the lines. The greens are difficult, too. I had better luck with the blues. My only real gripe about the illumination is that it's rather difficult to differentiate between the highest and lowest brightness settings on both red and green. Blue is a little better.

Just an observation here, but I'm thinking that of all the colors, blue might be easier on eyes readjusting to the darkness, if shooting in low light situations. Also, in looking through the objective lens, both the green and red show up like sore thumbs; blue does not.

Maybe, it's just the particular unit I received.

As soon as I get it mounted on the rifle I want to use it with and get some range time, I'll update the review.

product_title: Joist Mounted Pull Up Bar with Neutral Grip Handles by MS Sports
review_body:
So, you want a pull-up bar, but those dinky doorway doohickeys don't cut it. This is the solution. My old house (built in 1915) has wide molding around all the doors and not many straight angles. One of those pull-up bars that wedge into the door frame became a death trap in my home. The joist-mounted number is sturdy and secure, as well as out of the way in my basement instead of cluttering up the living spaces. So, the complaints I've seen in other reviews: 1) the bolts are too short, 2) no instructions, and 3) rough grips. Let's take them one at a time.

1) This problem seems to have been fixed by all your complaining. The bar comes with 8 carriage bolts. Four short bolts to mount the neutral grips and four longer bolts to mount into a floor joist. The longer bolts are long enough for a standard 2-inch joist. Any thicker, and you'll need to stop by your local hardware store.

2) True, there aren't instructions, but come on people! This is pretty straightforward. Aside from the bolts, you have three pieces: the main bar and two grips. If you can put the round peg into the round hole, you can master this. Match up the holes and screw in the bolts for the handles. Mounting the bar to your floor joist will take a little extra handiwork. You'll need a drill, a standard socket wrench set and a crescent wrench (two crescent wrenches will work too, if you don't have a socket set). Oh, and don't forget the level. I also needed a second pair of hands to hold the bar as I screwed in the first two bolts, but otherwise it was a one-person job. You can do it.

3) True, the grips are rough. Toughen up. After a week or so, you'll grow callouses.

Enjoy!

product_title: New Grip Force Gen 1 2 3 Glock BeaverTail Adapter 17, 19, 22, 23, 24, 31, 32, 34, 35, 37, 38
review_headline: Does what it says. But not the material you think it is!
review_body: First of all this is a great product. 5 stars for being everything that it says it should be. Me being a 1911 guy I have tried to drink the glock kook-aid and have tried to adapt to the grip of both a 19 and a 17 for over a year now. I have gone as far as to take off the front finger grooves, under cut the trigger guard, and take out the back bump for your palm swell. Everything I could do to change the bore axis and have my hand ride differently was getting me closer to the grip I loved but still not quite there. The Grip Force Adapters helped my hand ride up even higher and gave me even more of that 1911 feel. Was it like a glove no of corse not, and for the price point nor should it be. I was never concerned about slide bite in the first place so I can't comment on that aspect of that. But I will say this. I CCW my 17 because the 19's grip is still too small for me. I have big hands and in a pressure situation I could never get a good consistent grip on that pistol. On the 17 I can and the Grip Force Adapter helps facilitate that. The reason I gave it 4 stars is because of two reasons. 1 in all the pictures it always has a very hard polymer or almost rubber like appearance to the adapter. When they arrived they wear obviously much lighter and thinner.  Now granite once on the gun they use the receiver as reinforcement so you will be fine but I would have preferred one in the box instead of two but make that one thicker higher quality material. The second reason I give it 4 stars is because the finish on the edges is very rough. They have sharp jagged edges where they are punched out and are not de-bured. Now just about anybody who is putting one of these on there pistol may also consider themselves a kitchen gunsmith so I would hope they would be savvy enough to have some either small light files or high grit sand paper on hand to soften and taper the edges the way I did. I then took a Birchwood Casey blacking Pen and hit the edges because the material turned white on the edges from being roughed up. Also for gods sake don't use your Tactical Dremel on the edges. Your burn right through the stuff. Buy these, they are great, just don't expect they same polymer or finish as your Glock!

There are two retainers/springs under the sights that were moving around loosely, causing the small aperture to fall forward after each round. The retainers were bad from the start, right out of the package, but it was too late for a return (~40 days). At the range, I figured I would try to fix the springs at home. Unfortunately, one of the springs dropped out from additional shooting or transporting, and there's nothing left to fix. To get the other spring out, I flipped the handle upside-down and shook it a little.

The supplied rail does not fit into the carry handle due to some sort of tack weld over one end of the spring pin keeping the bolt in place. Nothing a little dremel wouldn't take care of, but you shouldn't need to do this.

product_title: Coleman Instant 6 Person Tent
review_headline: Fantastic, but let's manage our expectations here.
review_body:
I bought this tent a month ago, but just used it up at Big Bear this weekend.

The setup was a breeze, as has been well documented. A friend helped me, and we had the thing up in about 20 seconds, but I could have done it alone in less than a minute. Then staked it out, and I was good to go. I bought the rain fly, as I have camped many times before, and the idea of a single skin tent is absurd to me!

Size wise, we need to be realistic here. Everyone raves about this tent, and I will happily join the song and dance, but only a few people have been realistic in their reviews about the size. The box says it can fit 2 queen sized mattresses in the tent. No way. Just isn't going to happen. It will fit one, with a really good amount of room for your gear, and to get dressed etc. I'm 6ft tall, and can easily stand up, not just in the middle, but I can walk around in this tent.

Now on to the performance. On the second night, we were hit by the biggest thunder storm I've seen in seven years of living in CA. Buckets and buckets of rain, super loud thunder, and very bright lightening for at least an hour. It was awesome, but I was worried about the tent! This was its first test. I was unfortunately on a slope, and had a lot of rain runoff going straight under my tent (I had a tarp underneath the tent). At one point I reached down from by air mattress and felt the stream running under super thick tent floor. The rain was lashing down. Guess what? Everything was bone dry inside! The wind came, and I had not set up the guy lines, so I was worried about that. No problem - Instant tent just took whatever gusts of wind came at it, and carried on standing strong! I was so impressed. In the morning, there was a little water in one of the corners, so I will spray some sealant over that corner, and all will be good. I was pleased that I bought the rain fly, as I could open the vents at the top of the tent, and still be safe in the knowledge that I'll be about as wet as Palm Springs in the summer.

The zipper problem everyone mentions is legit. They didn't really think that one through - It does get caught, and it does require a two handed opening. I would have like to have been able to open the tent from the top of the door, but alas, that option isn't there. Oh well.

This isn't a hiking tent, as it's big and cumbersome, but for drive in tent camping, I really think it's ideal. This gets a 10/10 from me. I've never owned a better tent. The windows, and subsequent airflow is second to none, and the ease in which is goes up, makes this little beauty a hit. Just know what need out of it size wise, and you'll be good to go! So happy with this tent, and can't wait to use it again.

product_title: SKLZ Power Handle - Baseball Resistance Trainer
review_headline: This is an excellent, high quality training tool for resistance training ...
review_body:
This has got to be one of the better SKLZ inventions yet. I am a bit fan of all the SKLZ products and have tried out and reviewed several of them from ones used in golf, lacrosse, basketball, baseball, and soccer. They are well-thought out and very well-made. Some, owing to the nature of the product, tend to be much more durable than others. This Power Handle Bat Handle Resistance Trainer is one of them. Although this can be used inside by shutting it in a door, I much prefer the idea of attaching it to a chain link fence for safety reasons.

If you have anyone else in the house and they open a door, you or someone else could be injured. I used this one on a bathroom door because I knew no one would be opening it from the other side. If you do decide to door anchor it, the recommendation is to anchor it to the strong side of the door. The “strong side of the door is the side that closes toward you.” Although there is a small, rather insufficient cautionary sign warning people not to open the door, I’d suggest you make your own. Better yet, use the fence method so you’ll be visible and can exercise safely.

This is a really solid unit with an aluminum bat handle, heavy fence/door anchors (carbineers), and a 1/2 inch in diameter latex cord. The SKLZ Power Handle Bat Handle Resistance Trainer would be an awesome addition to those who have a PT regimen to follow as well. I tried out a few of the exercises and could really feel the resistance. There are recommendations for repetitions and sets to strengthen your arms and improve your swing. This is an excellent training tool for resistance training.

product_title: Saxon Equileather Ladies Zip Up Paddock Boot - Size 8.5 Brown [Misc.]
review_body:
Pros: These wash off extremely well, just hit them with the hose. They are reasonably comfortable, the zipper works, and the keep the water out if you're walking in wet grass.

However...

If you're looking for boots that will last, these are probably not the boots for you. I'm on my second pair, and this one has ended the same way as the first, with the synth-leather on the toe completely detaching from the sole after a few months. The synth-leather has also disintegrated around the original split, at the toe-seam- around the hole, there is nothing but fabric.

If you only need boots for a thirty minute to an hour ride a couple of times a week, they might last you a while, but if you plan on working in your riding boots, or riding every day, plan on replacing these within six months. My old Ariats withstood a lot more usage (about a year) before the (genuine, non-synth) leather finally split (although, unlike these, they did not separate from the sole and are therefore still usable, as long as the ground isn't wet).

All in all, these are just okay. For everyday usage, they just aren't very sturdy. I tried these originally because they are significantly cheaper than real leather, but if you have to keep replacing them, it comes out about the same.

product_title: Stamina 5325 Magnetic Upright Exercise Bike
review_headline: I Love My Stamina 5325 Exercise Bike
review_body:
I am a 62 yo woman with two hip replacements. I used to exercise a lot but lost my moxie in the last several years.
This bike came fast, well packed and with included instructions and assembly tools.
Because I have some limited mobility, the most difficult assembly act was putting on the cross feet, down at floor level, but I managed it. The only other difficult part is finessing the inner cable, but it can be done with patience and holding your mouth right.
Everything else was logical and well instructed.
When I started out, five months ago I could only manage five minutes at the lowest setting. I am now riding an hour, with 3-4 sprint periods. I weigh over 200 pounds, but as long as I am careful, mounting and dismounting, not to tip the bike forward, it holds me securely. The wide padded seat is excellent.
I live far away from any gym, now, and looked quite a while before I decided on this Stamina 5325 magnetic upright exercise bike.
I definitely got my money's worth.

review_body:

Started off, the torsion bar broke Not the biggest deal, but it was a major reason for my purchase of the knife. I've had the knife since June, so it lasted a while, but... eh. And don't actually tighten them or the clamp will rip completely.

Conversely, I had originally bought a pack from a local Radio Shack. Problem was, they only sold a variety pack so out of 16 clamps, only 4 of them were the size I needed. product_title: Diadora Team Bag
review_headline: Design flaw! you cant lock this with a standard travel lock!!
review_body:
I got two of these bags in Forest and Maroon colors. I loved them since I got them till I started to stuff them up and realized that none of my Travel TSA or non TSA small locks would fit through the holes in the zippers. I was very disappointed as I have never had such a problem with any of the duffels I own. Then I just looked over all my bags and found that every other one had a fairly large hole in the zipper clip for the lock. Not these!!

Well I didn't want to return them as the quality is pretty decent so I took out my drip and enlarged the holes!! Now yea my locks do fit them but the new bags have worn looks on the zippers. Btw when I say zippers I mean the clasps/pullers (hehe) or whatever you call them. (The ones you pull to close a zip!! Gosh cant remember the word for them). Enlarging the hole with my simple drill wasn't much of a issue except for the little loss of paint on the clasps.

The other reason I took off 2 stars is that there is no front pocket which is usually standard for all duffels this size. I wonder why they didn't put it there but that pocket is very handy if its there for your cards, cell phone and other small items.

Pros:
Size as expected
Colors as shown
Decent quality
Great looks
Nice strong zips
Shoulder strap
Shoe pocket

Cons:
Zipper clasps holes not big enough for a standard travel lock.
No front large pocket
No inside pocket's

product_title: Vortex SPARC Red Dot Scope
review_headline: Vortex Sparc the perfect HK Lower 1/3 co-witness Red Dot
review_body: I bought this Vortex Red Dot because it appeared to be a low profile optic that I could use with my HKs and possibly a Vector MP5 clone. With a Low profile Kley-Zion rail mounted on an MP5-.40 it's a perfect lower 1/3 co-witness with the original HK sights. Great if you are ever in a situation where the batteries have gone dead. The 2x magnifier is a real bonus as other optics manufactures charge $200-$300 just for a 2 or 3x add-on. I have an Eotech on my AR which I believe is a better choice for that weapon, but for an HK (or AR), hard to beat this red dot for the price,form and function. Note: For other HK clones the Kley-Zion rail might not work. On a Vector MP5 the distance between the claw pads is over 1.0\\" and the rail will not slide over the tabs without modification. The Kley-Zion rail will also work with a HK 93,53 but unless you remove the rear sight you will not be able to put the 2x magnifier on as it is too close of a fit. To my knowledge I have never seen another rail/Red Dot combo that will give you a co-witness on an HK. There is probably a Red Dot somewhere that also might work with this or another rail, let me know if you find one!

product_title: Timex Men's Ironman Road Trainer Heart Rate Monitor
review_body:
This is a fairly good exercise watch. For my purposes, I just set it to display time and heart rate. That's all I really need it for. All the split time stuff is pretty much lost on me.

Before you get your hopes up - this watch has no GPS capability. Most people doing outdoor training like running, biking, etc. require GPS. So, this watch isn't for them. Maybe it's OK for walkers but I think its real use is in the gym or workout room. You can check both the time and your heart rate before starting the next set. GPS watches aren't good indoors because most won't display anything until they acquire satellites.

What I most like about this watch isn't the watch at all. It is the heart rate sensor. It takes a replaceable battery, that's a big plus. Also, the strap has a fastener. I can put it on without pulling it over my shoulders or butt. Ever try to replace a stretched out heart rate monitor band? It's miserable. This one shouldn't stretch out nearly as quickly as others. Also, it's wide enough to be a bit grippy.

The display numbers are large enough that it's easy to tell time, but I wish the other display element were a bit bigger. I can't read the heart rate with just a glance. It's the curse of getting older.

If I were into all the split time stuff, I'd hate the button layout. I have to take care to avoid the mode button when I want to press the stop/reset/set button because I tend to put index finger on one button and thumb on the other. But.... I'm not into that so not a problem.

product_title: Thule Vertex 4-Bike Bike Rack
review_body:
Unlike some other reviewers, my hitch came complete. The instructions were fine, except for the section on mounting the anti-sway cages that did not make it clear which one of two possible mounting directions. Once you put a bike on the rack it is clear, however, which way the anti-sway cages mount. One additional drawing would have cleared that up though.

For everyone with a 1 1/4\\" hitch, here's the deal: this product is drilled with two holes to mount to a 2 or 1 1/4\\" hitch. One hole is for a tiny 6mm screw. The other is for a beefy 12mm screw, but it was drilled too far out in my opinion, so that it does not allow the hitch to slide far enough into the car's hitch receiver to provide good stability. I suspect this was the cause of some of the other reviews that complained about wobble. To solve this, re-tap the 6mm hole to make it 12mm, and then you can slide the hitch all the way into the hitch receiver and have almost no wobble when tightened with the 12mm screw. You'll need a good-quality 27/64\\" bit to drill the hole (200rpm worked well for me) and a 12mm tap; the steel is soft and not difficult to tap. Now it rests very solidly and with no play in my hitch; probably with less play than it would in a 2\\" hitch because I don't have to use the adapter.

So, I'd give it 3 stars if I had to live with the wobble because I wasn't able to tap a better hole, 5 stars if they tapped the suckers in the right place to begin with, and I've dropped one for the two hours it took me to put everything up, think about how to fix the wobble, re-tap the hole, and then try it all on again to make sure it works.

No problems with the straps on my January 2013-made model, by the way; the system as a whole works very nicely and is very rugged.

product_title: ProMag Archangel Sparta Pistol Grip Conversion Stock, Black Polymer
review_body:
I had been wanting this stock for almost 6 months and actually had a pre order from Archangel on their website. After checking and seeing that amazon had it in stock and at $100 cheaper, I decided to order here and cancel my order from manufacture.

Assembly was a pain in the butt, and yes i followed directions. Specifically the hardest part for me was getting the trigger assembly into the stock and have it fit flush. The fit was so tight that i feared i would bent parts of my mini. After Much time I was able to get everything to fit, after about 2 hours. I noticed that when a mag was inserted the fit was extremely tight, i mean way too tight.

The next day I took my mini with Sparta stock to do a live fire test. I had 3 factory 10 round ruger mags. Went through the first mag and still noticed the same tight fit. When i went to drop (eject) the mag it was stuck and would not release. The only way I was able to get the mag to release way by pulling the trigger group.

I contacted Archangel and sent in my stock, they said that it could be warped. I am still waiting for the replacement stock.

review_headline: Strong enough for a man, but made for a woman?

First off, as not so tall as I am, they're almost too short for dips and definitely for pull-ups/rows. I cannot straighten my arms without my back resting on the floor.

product_title: ChicoBag Vita Contemporary Collection Reusable Shopping Tote/Grocery Bag
review_body:
I've spent years hitting and missing this whole idea of carrying my shopping bags into the store with me when I go shopping -- so i don't have to carry paper or plastic out with me when I leave... The Chico-Bags finally fixed the problem of leaving them at home -- leaving them in the car -- having too many or not enough....

since each bag wads up into a little light-weight ball of nothing -- and has a clip -- I just clip one to my bag and leave it there all the time. I keep half a dozen of them in the back floorboard of the car -- when I stop at the store, I just grab them and clip them onto the one already dangling there as a reminder... I end up with a multi-colored daisy chain of bags.

When I get home and carry my bags of groceries up -- I just toss the empty bags on the table, and when I sit down with a cup of coffee -- I start stuffing them back into their little pouches, and clipping them back onto my purse.

As long as I never leave without my purse -- I never leave without my Chicos.

Haven't been without them since.

And now everybody I know will be getting them for their birthday.... :D

I keep both the regular shopping bag size for produce and heavy things -- and the Vita size which are much bigger and really good for carrying paper good and chips and such.

product_title: Ontario 499 Air Force Survival Knife, Black
review_headline: Not the knife in the picture
review_body: If you'll notice, the first picture (posted by Amazon) shows a knife with a black blade and butt and a sheath that is tan in color. Some of the customer pictures are of a knife with a dull gray blade and butt and sheath that is leather/brown colored. I received the one with the dull gray blade, and the initial plastic wrap says that it's a "Rothco Survival Knife - New" but when you open it, the back of the sheath has a sticker that says "Ontario Survival Knife" or whatever. The Ontario knife (on Amazon, look for "Ontario Survival U.S. Military Issue") looks much closer to what I received after ordering the Rothco knife, and seeing as how the back of the sheath says "Ontario," I can only assume that they are selling the wrong item, wrapped up and labelled as the correct item. The Ontario one is very solid though, and extremely sharp out of the box. I think I will keep it and save some headache, though I would have preferred the Rothco. If anyone on the Amazon staff sees this, please try to fix the problem.

product_title: Bushnell Bear Grylls Edition BackTrack Original G2 GPS Personal Locator and Digital Compass, Orange/Black
review_body:
We were so hopeful about getting two personal GPS's for use in our up coming Colorado hunting trip. We set up the GPS's per instructions which were minimal. Then set the way point at our driveway. Then we drove a short distance around a curve and down a hill to see how the GPS's would function. One pointed one direction, and not towards the house. The other pointed in a different direction (and not just a slight difference from the 1st unit), and it was not towards the house. We walked a ways with the units thinking that might activate them. No. They did turn, but still not towards the house. Next we drove to a shopping area. Setting the way point in one parking lot, we walked down the sidewalk then across the street into another parking lot. We could see the spot of our way point, but the GPS's were pointing in the wrong directions, and the two units were not pointing in the say direction.
We don't know what happened, or why it was giving us such bad readings. We sent them back to Amazon for a refund, which was promptly give to us. The prompt refund was the only good thing that happened out of this exercise.
We were very disappointed in Bushnell and this product.

product_title: Concealed Carry Fire Arm Fobus Paddle Hand Gun Holster Model SG-09. Fits to: CZ CZ99 Zastava, Sig/Sauer Sig Pro SP2009, 2022. Conceal Carry
review_body:
Bought this for my Sig SP2022. It does not come close to fitting. The picatinny rail on the SP2022 hits inside the holster. Right where you see the \\"SG-09\\" imprinted on the outside of the holster. Look directly under the \\"9\\" and you will see where the holster narrows. The rail hits there, hard. It is not a close tolerance/tight fit sort of thing. The pistol will not enter the holster any further, period.
Sometimes I think that FOBUS does not actually take the time to grab a pistol and see if it fits. I think they just go off of drawings, and say, \\"yep, she fits\\". This makes two FOBUS holsters out of the five that I have purchased that do not actually fit the pistol listed.

product_title: FINIS Neptune
review_headline: extremely annoyed by this inferior quality product as it turned outright dead after 12 uses

The Neptune did not respond regardless how long the power button is pressed or any other button is pressed. This is performed when the USB cable is detached.

As an electronic engineer myself, I came to pronounce it totally dead after these careful diagnosis.
The huge problems ensue:

.I will loss at least 20-30 days for the replacement. The summer suitable for swimming is short and is quickly running out. This is extremely annoying.

product_title: Nathan Trail Mix Hydration Running Belt
review_headline: Holds iPhone in a LifeProof case!!!
review_body: I bought this because I recently changed from a smaller Android phone to iPhone 5.  The iPhone along with the LifeProof case I keep it in would not fit in my current Nathans fuel belt.  I chose this one, as it looked like it had the roomiest pouch.  I can get my iPhone plus case into the pouch, tucked snugly against the back of the zipper pouch leaving a lot of room for other things, as well as there is a nice little Velcro pouch on the outside for chap stick or other small things you may want to access quickly. My only gripe is that I really wanted a 4 bottle belt.  The new 4 bottle Nathans belt colors are just garish and I couldn't do it! (Sorry Nathans!).  I like to run with my two full bottles on my front, and the phone and stuff in the back.  Kind of balances me out.  Now everything is in the back. I tried to run with it all in front, and the weight just seemed to pull my lower back forward, so I guess I just need to get used to the new set up.  For me the most important thing was getting my iPhone to fit, and Nathans it the brand I love.  I am a longtime runner who has had every kind of fuel belt.  Once I found Nathans that was it.

product_title: Hornady Electronic Scale (1500 Grains)
review_headline: There is an identical item for a fraction of the cost
review_body:
I am not 100% positive, but I believe this scale is the \\"American Weigh Signature Series Black AWS-100 Digital Pocket Scale, 100 by 0.01 G\\" with \\"Hornady\\" labeling. I own the AWS and it is a good little scale for checking powder in larger caliber rounds. I have successfully used the scale to weigh my .40 rounds. But when I used it to check my .32 S&W Long it was not accurate enough because I was trying to weigh around 3.5 grains.

This Hornady scale gets the one star because, as stated above, I firmly believe this is the exact same scale as the AWS for 3 times the price.

review_headline: An excellent Expandable baton, which I had carried for several years.
review_body:
I have probably carried and taught just about every type of police baton in the past, including this model (Monadnock Detective 26 inch Expandable Baton). I have been a lifetime student of numerous Law Enforcement Defensive Tactics, martial and many weapon arts. As both a student and instructor I have taught and carried numerous types of batons (PR-24 Baton, My favorite baton, Standard Solid Straight baton, my second favorite baton, Persuader/Yawara stick batons and the metal expandable models) and used them in training as well as on the street.

This model was one I had carried for years when it first came out from Monadnock. I found this baton to be rugged and durable. You should be aware that this is a friction lock type of baton, which is not as good as a Monadnock Auto lock model baton or just a standard solid one piece straight baton. The friction lock baton must be opened by swinging it out strongly to lock in place with the three parts of the baton. This baton may also loosen while in the expandable position when used to strike a training bag. The auto lock models can lock out using either a pulling motion or a swinging motion. Nevertheless, this Friction Lock model baton does have good points and if this is the type of police baton your department approves, you may want to purchase this model.

In conclusion, if you are seeking a traditional Friction Lock type of expandable baton, you may want to check this Monadnock Model.

Rating: 4 Stars. Joseph J. Truncale (Author: Use of the Monadnock Straight Baton (MEB))

product_title: ncstar aprlsrg Red/Green Laser + Weaver Style Mount+remote switch+one bat...
review_body:
This laser is as advertised and works effectively. The green laser is very bright for a civilian unit. I tested daytime visibility in direct sunlight on a hot and very bright day. Against white horizontal concrete (my drive) I could make out the green dot to about 12 yards. Pointed at a brown vertical surface under the same lighting conditions the dot was clearly visible at 40 yards. The red is a different story, as expected I couldn't see it at all in daylight. Surprisingly it wasn't visible very far at night either, but inside a house was perfectly usable at 40 ft. Outside I could not see it at 40 yards in the dark. I'm not sure if that was due to its range or due to the fact that the beam is very tight and the dot at about 30 yards looked to be about an eighth of an inch (like a BB) in diameter. My eyesight might not be good enough to see it at a longer distance. That said, this laser is for home defense and probably would never be used at a distance of more than 20 yards and it certainly would not point your position out to an intruder. The green at night produced a tight beam and was bright to at least 600 yards. It did produce a visible beam right back to the source so wouldn't be good for use at night unless you don't mind being pointed out. I believe the dot would have been visible at a much greater distance but I have no objects of known distance beyond 600 yards to target to verify that.

The vendor sent the wrong item initially and their policy of waiting to receive that item back before sending the correct one was irritating and potentially could have ruined the transaction due to a time constraint that I had and because they only had one more in stock. Their policy is appropriate for returns due to defects or because of customer mind changes, but not in cases where they sent the wrong product. To their credit they shipped the original item so quickly that I was able to return it, wait for them to receive and check it and then ship back the correct item and I still received it before the original estimate.

The reason for the 4 stars is that for many people the limited usable range of the red laser at night might make this unit unacceptable. The fit and finish were very good and the pressure switch was simple but effective. Sighting adjustment was tight, controllable, and easily completed in less than a minute matching laser to iron sights at 40 yards. The end cap, if used rather than the pressure switch is of no value since the only way to turn it on or off is to tighten or loosen the cap. Cant imagine why anyone would use it.

I haven't fired the weapon with this laser attached, but will be doing significant shooting over the next two weeks. If the laser fails, the sight doesn't hold zero or the mounts have any issues staying tight I will update this review.

review_headline: You probably ordered this b/c you messed up your b/c rollpin that came in a lpk
review_body:
This roll pin works, and they send the right roll pin.

Easiest way to install a bolt catch roll pin is.....take a pair of channel locks or regular pliers, wrap the teeth of it with electrical tape, get your pin in position and slowly clamp down with the channel locks or pliers, it'll push right in place......no more cussing about a no good roll pin punch or trying to beat it in........just use a roll pin punch to countersink it after you use the pliers and you're good to go.

Keep in mind that a bubble level will suffer slightly compared to something like a cermaic ball level. While the cermanic ball will show cants starting around 1 degree most bubble levels will not show a can't until around 3-5 degrees.

However, on an AR, that protrusion is slanted. As the bag fills, even though the metal is stiff, it will slide down and off. I just got back from the range and am super upset. In 2 30 round clips, I had *8* hung up shells. Worse, the jam caused the casings on the shells next in line to become dented, and so I didn't want to risk reloading them in the clip. I walked this thing to the garbage after only 2 clips.

I would say maybe great if you are shooting a couple groups at a target and taking some time to bs and hang out, empty the bag... If you are working on putting triple taps in a target from a high capacity clip, don't bother. The frustration isn't worth it.

product_title: Springefield XDS Sneaky Pete Holster (Belt Clip)
review_headline: XDS 45 Belt Loop Sneaky Pete Holster
review_body: I purchased the Sneaky Pete belt loop holster for a XDS 45 pistol 5 round clip. I am a 70 - 6' 3\\" 230 LB. man with a spare tire so that rules out mounting it in less then the 3 o'clock position and the straight up and down cant of the pistol tends to eliminate anything much greater then carrying it greater then a 3 o'clock position. I think it would be uncomfortable to sit with carrying it in anything less then a 3 o'clock position. Its size is about a 1 ¼ thick, 4 inches wide and about 6\\" tall. A holster for the 7 round clip (which they do not make) would make it extra wide and bulky, putting it into a full size 1911 configuration. The glove leather looks smart and attractive contains something valuable. This could attract like minded bump and snatch teams.  The size is large for a standard cell phone case, too small and thick for some tablets. I choose to tell and think of the holster as a small newly designed fanny pack or a belted man purse carried on my side. The magnets hold the flap well enough, but could be a little stronger. It is easy to open. My narrow wide oak dinning room arm chairs make for an interference fit when I sit down. The trigger guard is 90% covered which leaves a snug space just wide enough to get two fingers between the handle and the lip of the holster for drawing. Hope you do not have very large, thick, fingers. Could use and be a little more space there. It is not configured for a speed draw. The gun is held in the holster pretty well and doesn't flop around with the Kydex insert. One handed re-holster could be smooth with practice, but the flap lends itself to be held open with the weak hand. The space between the belt loops just barely permits it to fit the belt loop of my 501 and 517 Levis between the twin holster belt loops in the 3 o'clock position. The holster belt loops are rather tight against the case and do not lend the holster to be used with a thick (almost) 1/4\\" thick belt. I normally wear a 1 ½: wide western design leather belt made with thread putting it a little larger then a ¼\\" thick. It is very difficult to fit the belt through the holsters belt loops and therefore taking off and on is arduous. I wished I had ordered it with the clips. Wearing it n the car it is comfortable. The seat belt comes across the holster and may interfere with opening the flap. The holster solved two major concerns I had about Concealed Carry and the first one being; carrying it in an IWB holster and printing through the shirt. The second is using an IWB holster sitting on the john in a public rest room with more than one stall and the pants drop to the floor. The guy in the next stall sees the gun and panics. What he sees now is an innocuous fanny pack. No cops get called to the store.

Let me start off by saying that I'm not the type of golfer that changes clubs every other week, especially with putters. I previously had a Walter Hagen forged blade putter, which I used for 11 years. While at a scramble, I saw the Versa 9, and instantly loved the weight, the feel, and the optics. I've never been a fan of the 'lines parallel to target' aiming systems, hence why I stuck with a blade for so long. With the Versa's 'perpendicular to target' aiming system, I had to give it a try. After putting with it at a local Edwin Watts, I fell in love with it. The price tag was higher than I like to spend on a club, but finding it on Amazon for considerably cheaper pushed me over the edge. I am now putting AS GOOD with it after 2 rounds as I was with my blade with 11 years experience. I can't wait to see how my game improves.
Because golf clubs are so subjective, I can't blindly recommend this to everyone, but what I can say is that I couldn't be happier with mine, and you should definitely try this one the next time you're in a store that sells it... then come get a better deal on Amazon! Happy putting!

product_title: PUX Women's Shoeless Support Socks
review_body:
So excited! Finally found something I've been looking for forever--something that will support my very flat feet when I need to walk barefoot! I just put them on and walked around and love them. I had extensive foot surgery 6 weeks ago. A fix for a botched bunion repair that was done 11 years ago--involved breaking my metatarsal high on my foot, and that meant a plate and four screws up on the bone. The joint at the toe itself was also cut and moved so another screw. Then they sliced off part of the bunionette on the other side. They also fixed the botched hammertoe from the botched surgery so one more scar and one more screw. Finally, she dug out a mass of nerves and adhesions from two previous surgeries (unsuccessful) for a painful Morton's neuroma. (That part is still feeling like a bad bruise on the bottom of my foot.)

At this point post-op when I'm at home, I often don't put my special shoe on to walk around the house, but that makes walking hard because I need to keep my weight on my heel and the outside. I put this thing on and wow--no pain and no strain! No pain on top, no pain on the bottom where the neuroma was. NO PAIN!

So I'm a VERY happy camper and just wish I had bought these sooner. I will experiment with them awhile and will make any necessary adjustment as needed. Also, I have skin allergies to latex and other things, so if I'm allergic to these I will post (pretty quickly) a follow-up to this review..

This doesn't bother me whatsoever as I never use the "1" position except for travel and I can just use the "2" spot - no biggie. product_title: uxcell Plastic Fresh Water Retractable 7 Sections Telescopic Fishing Rod 2.1M Length Blue
review_headline: No surprises, just what I expected, great if you want to put in a little extra work.
review_body:
First of all I want to say that I had very low expectations for these rods. While they won't win any awards for finish, craftsmanship, or build quality, they will do the job. I bought two of these rods to introduce my young children to Tenkara, and they will do nicely for that. When they are broken I won't lose any sleep. I think they honestly deserve three stars, but I would certainly buy this rod again, and recommend it for people with a similar need. I might look for a little longer version next time since they are a bit shorter than advertised.

Some specifics that may interest some potential buyers:
Material: Fibreglass, and it looks like it may have a bit of carbon thrown in to make it black
Action: it looks to be about 7:3, but a soft rod like you would expect from glass.
Segments: 7, Bottom three are blue, and the top four are black.
Lillian: it is on the stiff side, but my test line had no problem staying on. I suspect that it will soften up over time. It appears to be attached firmly, although a little rough at the edges. I will put a little gel super glue on the bottom to keep it from fraying.

It is an unsanded blank with a rough clear coat. There were a couple of segments on one rod that wouldn't extend, so I took the segments out and sanded them until they moved freely. So, one of the rods now has a sanded blank. The plug is a piece of EVA foam, and the end cap is a cheap plastic deal that screws in to threads that have either been cut out of the glass, or were molded in when the blank was wrapped.

To test it out I cut an 8' section of 15lb. Amnesia and attached it to the lillian with a loop/girth hitch. While Amnesia isn't well regarded as a Tenkara line I found that this rod handled it well. It is easy to load the rod, and casting is effortless. It is really hard to under power a cast, but not difficult to over do it.

All things being equal I think this rod is perfect for my kids, and I know they will catch fish with sakasa kebari I tied last night.

EDIT: As I noted above the rod was shorter than advertised. In reality, it is just so poorly finished that it won't extend to its full length. I spent about 10 minutes sanding off just about all of the finish from the black sections, and after reassembling it is exactly 210cm as advertised. Most of the extra length came from the tip section which almost doubled. While the action was slow in my test, it ended up faster on the stream with a shorter (8') #3.5 Tenkarausa level line, and 4' of 5x tippet. My 8yo son caught his first trout on a fly in Rocky Mountain Natl. Park over the weekend, and he is now a fly fishing convert. The rod performed beautifully.

I am adjusting my rating to 4 stars on account of how well the rod performs. In reality if you buy it as a \\"blank\\", and know that you will have to put some elbow grease into it you will have a nice short tenkara rod. I made a pine grip for my son's rod, and it turned out very nice.

product_title: Polar FT60 Heart Rate Monitor
review_body:
After reading many reviews and looking at many styles I ultimately decided on the FT60 and I could not be happier. I am data driven and the information the training computer has provided me has been very motivating.

The HRM strap is very comfortable and as long as you clean it according to the instructions provided you should have no troubles with it working. I wash mine once a week and get the sensors wet prior to each wearing, both of which are recommended/instructed practices.

I did not find the buttons hard to push or the display difficult to see. There is a button for a back light if running in evening. I have only used the back light at movie theaters ;)

The embedded Stars Program has also been fun to play around with. With stars you can create a training program tailored to your current fitness level with goals that change as you become more fit. Each week you can earn stars or a trophy based on how you did following your plan. Whatever you earned the week prior (stars or trophy) stays visible with the current time until the next week. So seeing the reward you earned every day can be rather motivating to keep it or do better.

I bought the flowlink so I could download my training sessions to the polar website. The information is well organized and very easy to read on the site. It is very easy to use as far as syncing the FT60 goes.

I would recommend this to anyone whether you are just starting out or already have a good routine down and want to see your progress.

product_title: Gerber Bear Grylls Ultimate Serrated Knife
review_body: I love Bear, very humble man unlike Les who bashes Bear every chance he gets. This truly is an amazing knife for $31 Only a few things to address! First. Be aware that the picture is of the first version however they send you the new and very improved model with a tougher pommel and a much better looking, feeling and better cut blade. as stated in another review, there are small metal retainers right at the top on the inside of the sheath to prevent the knife from cutting the sheath. They will dull the knife if not taken out carefully (i actually damaged my serrations before even using the knife). I strongly suggest you remove these, very easy to do. I took a small flathead screwdriver and pushed the metal fittings from the outside toward the inside of the knife cavity. They will then come out on their own or with the aid of the tweezers. Ive heard few but some complaints about the starter rod being mounted upside down but theres a reason. If it is raining, rain will bead off of the rod and fall, however if it was mounted upright it would sit and risk seeping in and wetting the cavity (not to mention if filled with water the sheath would have to be turned upside down to be emptied which requires removal) by mounting it upside down, water naturally leaves the cavity and rain doesn't flood it. There is a nice rubber washer to keep moisture out anyway that i know for a fact can keep the starter dry even when submerged. The machined section on the top for using the starter is absolutely an absolutely genius design and so darn useful allowing you to strike the starter without dulling your blade or taking that beautiful dark coating off the blade. The diamond sharpener is the real deal: definitely a high quality tool, the sharpener is intended to keep an edge on the blade (not a honing stone) with this sharpener you could essentially keep your knife sharp enough to use until you run out of blade. One thing i wish is that the serrations took up less of the blade. The fineedge is now available (which i also have) but Bear uses the serrated because if you need to cut your rope fast in a life threatening situation, a fine edge is just not gonna \\"make the cut\\" Pun definitely intended. Grab yourself one of these bad boys, pull those metal pieces out and you've got yourself one seriously awesome knife.

product_title: SKLZ Refiner Driver Graphite Pro-Hinged Training Club
review_headline: Comparison with the Medicus dual hinged driver
review_body:
I am not new to a hinged training club. I have been using a dual hinged iron from Medicus and it was really a hit when it first came out. The Medicus iron really helped me to correct my swing and I carry this club always. Now I have a similar one but a driver this time from SKLZ. First of all, the SKLZ Refiner driver has a great build quality and finish. And it is a hittable club. Unlike the one from Medicus which has a dual hinge, the SKLZ Refiner driver is a single hinge club. I have used the Refiner for about a month, but I have not had much difference between the Medicus and the Refiner. Both of them bent whenver my swing rhythm was wrong and I did not feel that the dual hinge was more or less sensitive than the single hinge or not. The Medicus iron felt little more solid but this difference might come out from the fact that the Medius is a steel shaft iron and the SKLZ Refiner is a graphite driver.

SKLZ claims that the Refiner is the only graphite training club and I felt good that the SKLZ Refiner gave me the exact same feeling like the driver that I actually use. The adjustment tool came with it allows you to loose or to tight the hinge, but I did not need to use it. In fact, my son just started to learn golf and the SKLZ Refiner helped him to get the proper swing rhythm. I wished that I had a training club like this from the beginning of my golf. This training club might not work best for sub-90 golfers, however, the long-time beginners like me or my son who just started to golf got lot of help from it. The one thing that the SKLZ Refiner is better than the Medicus is a price. I paid pretty high when the Medicus first came out. For some people, the price might feel stiff, but I can quarantee that you will get your money's worth. Now I am carrying the SKLZ Refiner driver and the Medicus iron at the same time and love both. I can assure you that these hinged clubs help for your swing and heartly recommend this.

product_title: KEM Arrow Standard Index Playing Cards (Pack of 2)
review_headline: Not the best choice in high quality plastic cards.
review_body:
Let me start by saying these KEM Playing Cards are a great product. However, if you weigh some of the other factors besides the cards themselves, you'll find that KEM is definitely not the best choice.

The first and most obvious is price. You can purchase a similarly high quality two deck pack of plastic playing cards for around $10 cheaper. The next factor, and to me even more important, is the fact that KEM no longer provides replacement cards for ANY of their products. You can double check this yourself (It states it clearly on their website). Trust me, I know, because I lost the deuce of diamonds for one of my decks and now I'm stuck with a useless 51 card deck. It is for this reason that KEM would be my last choice of all the plastic cards.

Other options that my experience can speak to are Copag and Da Vinci. I've purchased both and I'll tell you right now, Da Vinci is my favorite. The cards are beautiful, cheaper (than KEM), come in the same kind of hard case, AND they come with two nice, red Da Vinci cut cards (Make sure the description on Amazon explicitly includes cut cards because if it doesn't, you won't get them). KEM cards do not include cut cards, nor do Copag. Also, in the Da Vinci cards, there will be a nice little extra card which you can mail in for replacements in case you lose a card. I haven't looked into replacement cards for Copag, but I'm assuming they do offer them.

The Copag cards are very nice as well. However, I personally favor the feel and look of the Da Vinci cards. One of the things I prefer on the Copag cards is the font of the card rankings, ie K, Q, J, 10, 9, etc. It is a very clean and crisp font. Also, the Copag has pretty awesome Jokers if you're into that kind of thing. The price of the Copag and Da Vinci is roughly the same. However, it seems to me that there are more design options on Amazon for Da Vinci than Copag, but I'm not entirely sure.

Anyway, I hope this helps in your decision making process. Enjoy and good luck!on making process. Enjoy and good luck!

product_title: Eurotard Women's Jf010 Body Shaper
review_body:
I picked this up after a back injury as the other medical back supports were lacking in size for my hips and non-metal support. I have to clear a metal detector at work, so typical back supports were out of the question, while the WalGreen's lower back support brace did well and didn't go off, it did ride up off my hips while sitting and didn't offer support low enough for my pulled muscles in my lower back. I was looking at other traditional back supports when one reviewer mentioned an old fashioned girdle was more supportive than the medical one she was given. That got me to thinking. I also needed something to go down low enough on my hips for the support but not so much support that the rest of my torso was squished. I opted for the 3X size since if I was purchasing this product for slimming, the 1X would have been right, but the measurements for my lower hips were on the upper end of 1X and I wanted comfort as well as support. This shaper comes with little straps to attach to your bra to keep it from rolling down. Here is the but, I have a long torso and this one, in this size, is a bit longer than I had thought, but that works well for covering my hips for support. Shorter torsoed people may need to consider this length difference when ordering a size up, as the next size up also expects to take up more space in the around/circumference part making it fit the torso better. This is like going up a size in pants only to find you don't have enough tummy pooch to fill out the stride from the waist to the crotch of the pants resulting in a bunching/gathering of fabric at the crotch. I wanted something to support my lower back and not set off the metal detector at work, and that is what I got. If you want slimming, this will do it as well to smooth out those bumps, but do not order a size up because you will not get the smoothing you will get if you order by measurements. The size chart is:

Small 4-6 Bust:33.5\\"-35.5\\" Waist: 26.5\\"-28\\" Hip: 36\\"-37.5\\"

Medium 8-10 Bust: 36-38 Waist: 28.5-30.5 Hip: 38-40.5

Large 12-14 Bust: 38.5-40.5 Waist: 31-33 Hip: 41-43

XL 16-18 Bust: 41-43 Waist 33.5-35.5 Hip 43.5-45.5

1X 18-20W Bust: 44-47.5 Waist: 36-39 Hip: 46-49.5

2X 22W-24W Bust 48-51.5 Waist 39.5-43 Hip: 50-53.5

3X 26W-28W Bust:52-54 Waist: 43.5-45.5 Hip: 54-56

You need to size based on measurement and not your store size. Also take the measurement of your largest area to determine the best size for you as that area will be squeezed the most if you order based on the smaller measurements. I measured a Hip of 53\\" around the fullest part of my bum, so I could get the lower back support I needed, so to make sure I could flex and be comfortable for 12 hours, I sized up one. Take your measurements carefully and do not be stunned by your size in this and similar garments or you will be unhappy and get your fit wrong.

Edited 06/29/2013: I received the size 1X and have been wearing it to work. This one does support my lower back as it does go down over the hips. I haven't had an issue with rolling as long as I use the straps that attach it to the bra, which are awesome. It is not difficult to get on by stepping into it and pulling over my hips and bum. The fabric is soft and smooth on my skin and doesn't itch even when I running around work and get sweaty. My back doesn't seem as sore at the end of the day from the extra compression support on my muscles which increases blood flow like my compression stockings do. When you work long hours on concrete you need all the support you can get!

product_title: Traditions Performance Firearms Plastic Handgun Snap Cap (.45 ACP)
review_body:
Doh! They don't eject, jamming on extraction. So what did I expect? The cause would probably be lost on Homer Simpson, as it was lost on me when I bought them.

Of course the first one loaded from the magazine will not eject when the slide is manually pulled back. The bullet simulator is still in the case and the ejection slot is not wide enough to clear that easily. How often do you unload a misfire?

Don't forget that when loading from a magazine, the first round must be removed before the second can load. And that can't happen while the extractor still has a grab on the rim, and the tip of the bullet end can't clear the ejection window. Doh!

Since I wasn't thinking when I bought, it's hard to diss the product. The problem not mine is that fumbling around with more than one in the mag causes dings in the rim that should be smoothed out. I think the brass is softer than that of an average case. I knock off a star for that.

So beware, don't expect these to eject. I have learned to NEVER, NEVER, NEVER drop the slide without something to load from the mag, so that's what I'll do with these, one only in the mag, then use the ol' thumb to cock and fire again for training.

You may have upwards of $5000 invested in that thing, why would you want to drop the slide on an empty chamber?

One of the previous reviewers mentioned that he us using a hard rubber cylindrical insert into the primer slot. I think I'll find the hard rubber motor mounts I stashed some where, hope to find a gasket cutter the right size as the .45ACP primer diameter then block off the case end with something short and curved so as to enter the breech and eject easily. Maybe only one will work.

product_title: Spyderco Tern Slipit G-10 Plain Edge Knife, Black
review_body:
This is the Byrd Tern, Byrd's first slipjoint. For the low cost, this is a nice non-scary folding knife. To keep the cost low, the Tern (as with all of the other Byrd knives) is made in China.

The Tern is 3-5/8\\" long when closed. It's made of two black G-10 scales and a non-locking backspring. The G-10 is nicely textured for the price, and there are no liners. The G-10 is good. I'd compare it to the Kershaw Chill as far as quality and texture. It's not as aggressive as a Spyderco Tenacious, but is grippy enough for the knife to not move in your hand. Also the screws are Torx. Size 8 for the handle screws and pivot pins (there's one on each side of the blade), while the screws for the pocket clip are T-10. The clip is wire, which I prefer. It doesn't snag on your pocket and it can be switched to the left or right side, tip up only. There's no lanyard hole, which I normally prefer, but it's no problem here. When the knife is closed, the blade is centered perfectly. Overall, I like the handle size and shape. It's just a tad smaller than the Meadowlark, which is good for a slipjoint.

The blade is 8Cr13MoV, typical of Chinese-made knives from good manufacturers. It's been compared to AUS-8, but I think it's closer to 440C. The knife came shaving sharp; I didn't even have to strop it. It's fully flat ground, which seems to be the standard for the new Byrds. I like it a lot. The blade surface is a bit wavy, much like the Tenacious line. This is a first for me on Byrds, as all of mine have been perfect. Maybe this model is being made in the same factory as the Tenacious? The blade is Spyderco's typical leaf shape and is 2-3/4\\" long with a 2-1/8\\" cutting edge. I rather like the blade shape, typical Spyderco. The spine and choil are also jimped, but not as aggressively as I like. But for a slipjoint, they're more than adequate. A word I'd use to describe the jimping is, well, dirty. It looks a bit uneven and there appears to be small dings in the sharp points of the jimping. I'm splitting hairs here with a $20 slipjoint, but it's something I noticed. Opening is accomplished with the normal Byrd hole (comet? talon?). It's the same size as on the Cara Cara 2, Meadowlark 2, etc. and works just fine for me. There's a halfway stop in the blade. You can feel the blade \\"snick\\" in the halfway position when opening, but it doesn't slow normal deployment.

I normally don't like slipjoints, but this one caught my eye. It took the expensive UKPK and kept the G-10, while keeping the low cost of the FRN slipjoints that Spyderco produces. In fact, the Tern is cheaper than those. For a twenty dollar bill, this is one hell of a knife. Kabar Dozier, Kershaw Chill, Byrd Meadowlark, CRKT Drifter; those have all been the epitomy of the \\"best\\" $20 folder. product_title: Benchmade - 943 Knife, Clip-Point
review_body:
I ordered the benchmade 943 Osborne design in black finish because it was all the was offered at the price point of $162. After opening the package up and discovering the satin finish I was quite pleased. I originally wanted the silvery finish because the black finish on blades will wear with time. This knife is smaller than I expected, but is very light and capable. I forget I have it on me at times. The axis lock can be actuated so fast you may think it has an assisted opening. The big question...is this knife worth the $162? I say yes. Now is it 7 times better than a kershaw skyline for everyday carry? Absolutely not. This knife is very cool but on a value scale it has high competition. It is a very well designed knife for people with too much money and an appreciation for an everyday carry knife that will satisfy on many different levels to include easy of use, fit and finish, and somewhat of an exclusivity given it's price point.

Pro's

-Excellent lock up
-Fast blade deployment
-S30 Steel holds sharp edge
-Fit and finish solid and is conversation worthy
-functional clip which is left side reversible
-Axis lock is ambidextrous
-gorgeous silhouette
-great ergonomics

Con's

- MSRP $220/ high barrier to entry
- Some have complained of a dull factory edge
