product_title: Umarex RWS Hyper Velocity 2137509 200 Rounds Air Gun Pellets, 0.177 Caliber, Orange
review_body: Love these. Keep in mind that they are more or less a novelty item, and they would be terrible for hunting, or long range target shooting. They certainly would penetrate some pretty thick skulls though... Anyway, I did some testing on these, and I was honestly impressed. They are made of a very hard alloy which seldom deforms,  even out of very powerful air rifles. The only thing so far I have found harder than the pellets (worth shooting at) was a VERY high quality steel saw blade. They pancaked like a normal lead pellet on that. At first I tried to do a coffee can pen test by lining up coffee cans and shooting through. It penned 2 and left a deep dent on the third. Now this alone is respectable, but as it turns out, the pellet had key holed and was penetrating these cans SIDEWAYS. It would have gone through more had it not keyholed. Next I shot a 1\\" thick aluminum plate. The pellets did not ding off as I expected, but instead stuck in the metal, sabots and all, like an arrow in a wood target. This alloy is HARD! I shot some pine next. A normal 7.4g lead pointed pellet punches about 1\\" on pine for me, but these pellets went through the first board and then embedded themselves too deep to see in the next board. Probably about 1 1/2 inches pine wood penetration. Lastly I shot a brass tool holding tray about 1/16 inch thick. A normal pellet just deeply dented it out of my 1200 fps rifle. I tried the hv pellets in my avanti 853 (600 fps) and it PENETRATED THE PLATE THE 1200 FPS RIFLE FAILED TO WITH LEAD. Needless to say I was impressed. I folded the plate over a few times and the 1200 fps rifle punched through all three plates. The accuracy on these is questionable, I was getting about 2\\" groups (excluding strays, which are common) from 15 yards, which is about the limit for hyper velocity pellet range. Like I said, these are really only for novelty. Fun pellets, certainly worth the price. These are some thing you should try for sure. Happy trails~Ben

product_title: Ontario 9414BM RAK Ranger Assault Knife (Black)
review_body:
Great little primitive knife. Total opposite of fancy, flashy, showy, collectable, and yet the look and design is still beautiful in a twisted way only a Marine can love. This knife is a great utility knife. You can butter your toast with it, slice up your steak for the BBQ, maybe even fillet fish, haven't tried yet. You can cut your fire wood and do all your camp choirs. I find it the perfect size, after getting used to it. I can't believe I actually had doubt at first. Yes, it would make an excellent weapon also, if you need to get it all dirty and gross with yucky blood and guts.
The sheath is a decent universal sheath, but not a big \\"woo-ha\\" as a professional will get a sweet after market sheath to fit their style anyway. Same thing with holsters. Raise your hands if you have more than five holsters for the same side arm.
So, yeah, I like it. I think it will be my go-to primary knife for a long time. Five star, recommended.

Update: Just used it a few days ago to dress game. Now, I did take a wet stone and finishing file to the edge awhile back so I may have made it sharper than out of the box, but skinned perfectly, it went through bone very well, and it boned the meat, also with no problem. Funny thing is, I actually tryed doing the work with another knife first and was having problems, then I grabbed this one. Yup I will never make that mistake again. BTW, it worked so well that I didn't even nick myself once. Ontario Knives definitely earned five stars.

product_title: Delta Kill Zone Portable Midsection
review_body:
I'm shooting this target with a 397 grain arrow at 305 fps, which is generating about 82 ft-lbs of kinetic energy. The problem is that the arrows are going completely through the target with about 4-6 inches sticking out of the back side. This in itself wouldn't be a problem except that when the arrows come through the back side, they are pushing out chunks of material and leaving dime size holes in the opposite side.

When the arrows are pulled, the "front" heals nicely, but the backside is getting destroyed. I've only shot 30 arrows and the opposite side looks like it's been through the ringer already. I'm concerned that VERY SOON the loss of backside material will start allowing pass throughs. My only alternative is to shoot the bullseye on the ends, as the depth is greater than the width and the arrows shouldn't make it all the way through that end. Which pretty much defeats the purpose of buying a "deer" target to practice for that moment of truth.

Needless to say, I'm highly disappointed. Sigh

If you are shooting an arrow/speed combination that yields less than about 65-70 ft-lbs of kinetic energy, (maybe less) this target would be ideal, because, as I said, the front of the target heals nicely and looks like it would take alot of punishment if the arrows around going through the back. If you are shooting a speed bow with light arrows, or a moderately fast bow with heavy arrows, BEWARE!! You're not going to get very much target usage.

product_title: SKLZ Quickster Pitch Return (7-Feet x 7-Feet)
review_headline: Huge! Rolls (doesn't bounce) balls back to the pitcher....
review_body:
This is different from the pitch-back I used as a child, which was much smaller and actually launched the balls back to the pitcher.

This one is basically for target practice; it always slowly rolls the balls back to you. Most of the speed of the ball is absorbed by the net. It is huge: 7 feet wide by 7 feet tall. It is easy to set up and comes with a nice fabric carrying case. No tools are needed; there are several bars that lock together and the net is easy to connect. Total setup time is under two minutes if you've done it before. The net can go on backwards if you want an image of a left-handed pitcher (the picture is basically painted onto the netting).

The large net is great because even if you miss the strike zone, the ball will likely still hit the net and roll back. We start with several balls and it's quite a while before we have to go fetch any. The four included U-stakes effectively hold the frame in place. We needed a mallet to pound them into our hard soil. One mangled a bit but I got it to work. Otherwise, it is very heavy duty and sturdy and hardly moves at all when a ball hits the net.

While this lacks the fun of the old style that could \\"hit\\" the ball back to you; it works great as designed strictly for pitching practice.

product_title: Gould & Goodrich B802-26RLH Gold Line Two Slot Pancake Holster - Left Hand (Black) Fits SIG P220, P226, P226 w/equipment rail
review_body: I have a Sig P226, no tac rail. When I first placed the pistol in the holster, it was more than a snug fit. The hammer strap would not snap in because the leather was too tight to reach. I wore the holster around the house with the pistol equipped with a full mag to add weight to assist  the pistol to properly sit in the holster. It took three days of leaving the pistol in the holster for the hammer strap to finally reach the snap to be able to snap it in, but still too tight to be able to snap it in while wearing it on my waist. After leaving the pistol in the holster for about a week, I started to see wear lines on the upper slide from constant holstering and removal. Application of a little CLP on the slide removed the wear lines, but the holster is still an extremely tight fit. I have to hold the holster with my right hand while removing the pistol with my left hand when wearing it, otherwise if I try using one hand I will pull my pants up to my chest with the pistol still in the holster. The leather is nice and I enjoy the forward cant that allows for a positive grip on the weapon, but I feel like its more for show than practical use. With all the Blackhawk Serpa holsters out there with different models, levels and designs for a similar price, I somewhat regret not just getting one of those, and will most likely invest in the Serpa Level 3. I want to actually be able to holster and remove my pistol without using two hands, and the time it would take to allow the leather to break in to allow that is a bit much. If you have a newer model with the tac rail, it might be different for you, but even then I would recommend a holster that would allow you to apply an attachment.

product_title: Barnett Lil' Sioux Archery Set Yellow 1071
review_headline: Purchased for my 10 year old beginner, and I ended up loving it too!
review_body:
NOTE: This is NOT a toy. This is a serious set, I would recommend for ANY beginner age 10 & up. The arrows shoot right through my metal shed!

In attempts to get my 10 year old son involved with a good hobby, I purchased this set. It's bigger than expected - big enough that I can use it too (I'm a 5'7\\" female, btw.). Right after using it the first time, my son fell in love with archery. It's easy to use, we both learned to shoot the arrow after only the 2nd try. The bow has a 3 finger grip on the string so it won't hurt your fingers, and it also has a guide where the arrow sits so it's easier to shoot. We've also purchased a hip quiver (to hold the arrows) and an arm guard to go with this set. As an art project, I picked up some big white poster board and let the kids paint their own targets.

It's become a great way to spend time as a family. I even got my 4 year old a cheap $2 arrow from Dollar General so she can \\"practice\\" with us. :)I love this set so much I'm purchasing another for a birthday gift for an 11 year old. If you need it sooner, they have them at Dick's Sporting Goods (in green & hot pink) for $21.99.

TIP: For practice setup in a backyard, go to Lowe's and get 2-3 bails of wheat hay. We did this and I can't imagine not having it to set up practice. They're less than $5 a piece, gives the kids something to aim at and holds the arrows nicely.

product_title: Ice Bandana
review_headline: about as good as you can expect
review_body:
one thing i've learned about the reviews is you have to take the good with the bad.. some people are just not happy with anything, some seem to give reviews that are too good, or they're trying to increase their 'vine' rating etc..

But having tried this out for myself in tropically humid 85* Florida, I have to say it works about as well as you can expect it to work. For other climates that are more dry, the evaporating bandanas seem to work well.. but in areas with higher humidity, you can't rely on evaporation to keep cool.. here where I am, the solid freezing ice packs are the way to go.. and that's what this is. I tried it out last night on a 2 mile brisk walk and upon finishing about 45 minutes later, the pack was still cold and only melted about 3/4 of the way through. The only odd thing to get used to is you have the feeling of wearing a scarf and your mind can't get around that it's not something that is raising your temperature, but is actually keeping it lower. It gets colder as the fabric starts to get moist, which may be a problem for people who have skin problems and can't be in contact with something wet for too long. Imagine a wet washcloth with an ice pack in it.. this is what it feels like.

So it is what it is.. for the price, this is what you get if you need actual ice and not evaporation to keep cool.. and it works. Considering the timeline above, if you order the cheap backup ice packs to keep in the freezer, you can be on a constant rotation of having a totally frozen pack if you have the 2 backups.. they freeze fairly quickly, faster than the 2 hours they claim.. and if you really want to you can get two bandanas and let one totally dry when you go to change the ice out.. I'm not sure how they would work in direct sunlight yet.. probably wouldn't stay moist, and may melt a little faster, but it still lasts long enough for what I need it for.. when I need it at all. The only better option may be the Black Ice productthat keeps at a constant 50 degree or so temp for a few hours, and doesn't get wet at all.. but it's 50 bucks. I don't need something that much but i'd like to try it sometime. I'm interested in the long cooling time and the 'no fabric' material used that doesn't hold moisture.. this would be top line thing to have..

The only other thing I can mention is you have to consider the negative reviews and the size of the people writing them. People with small necks will write negative reviews saying it doesn't fit. Being a guy with a 16 to 17 inch neck, it fits perfectly.. the last two ice packs sit right up against my neck arteries.. and it's not tight on me even when tightened fully. If you have a smaller neck obviously it won't close fully around your neck.. but you really don't want this anyhow as you don't want to cut off blood flow in the least, especially during exercise..

So for 10 bucks it's good enough for me. The only problem I had is they sent the wrong color.. but Amazon is good about these things and just gave me a refund, they didn't even want it back.. o yeah, another good use is to just forget anyone can actually see you looking like a karate kid throwback and tie the thing around your forehead.. this works amazingly well to keep you cool.. in fact now that i've done it this way, it's my favorite way to wear it to keep cool.

product_title: Standard Horizon HX300 Floating Handheld VHF
review_body:
Being kind of a newbie in marine communications I was a bit confused as to which model to purchase. After seeing a promotional discount offer in a local brick and mortar marine store, I ventured online to read some reviews and do some comparison shopping. I found a great deal on Amazon and picked up this unit.

The radio uses a USB charger, which is great, unfortunately, it is not a micro-USB so your cellphone connector won't be compatible. At least you can just carry the cable if the radio needs charging.

The unit, per the manufacturer, not my own tests (yet), say it floats, and when the radio is submerged in water, a flashing beacon illuminates.

From my own tests and use, the reception is great. Both weather and emergency bands. The radio will stay charged for an entire day on the water and still have power left for another half day. Provided you have it turned on, while out on the water.

Charging is quick. I have seen it charge completely in less than 2 hours from one bar left of battery. When it is done charging, whether turned on or off, it displays "FL" (meaning FULL).

I needed a handheld radio, thought the floating feature with the blinking light, while in water was handy.

Since this radio does everything I needed, and was reasonably priced in the very low hundred dollar range, I found it a good fit.

Hopefully this review has helped you. Good luck. :-)

product_title: Smith & Wesson Search & Rescue CKSUR1 Clip Point Fixed Blade Knife Rubberized Aluminum Handle
review_body:
Alright, so i purchased this knife roughly 14 months ago. I backcountry camp at least once a month (often twice) and have always brought this knife with me as well as a smaller folding one to complete smaller tasks. I used this knife regularly while camping for a variety of standard camping tasks, including some light wood splitting. The CKSUR1 arrived reasonably sharp, seemed well made, looked sexy, and worked nicely... to begin with. The black coating used on the blade does wear a bit, but seems to hold up well. At the 6 month point, the pin that holds the grip/guard/stop on the tang sheared and came loose/fell off. Luckily, with a full length tang, i fashioned myself a temporary paracord handle to finish my trip. I have no idea what it was made of, but based on the ease of drilling it out after, it seemed like aluminum. I replaced the pin with one i custom made from high carbon steel. That eliminated any problems I had, the knife remained relatively sharp with semi regular honing. Fast-Forward to 14 months after purchase, and the tip of the knife (1.5\\" from the point) snapped off while splitting a 2\\" diameter piece of wood. This knife should have been able to easily handle such a task. I think I'll be going back to my Ka-Bar, despite the CKSUR1 feeling better in my hand.

PS. Does anybody know if there is a warranty on this knife?

product_title: Benjamin 392 Bolt Action Variable Pump Air Rifle (.22)
review_headline: Good but needs a rifle scope mount
review_body: I have had this rifle for 2 weeks now and have put well over 100 shots thru it.  I had no trigger issues at all like some have noted.  I was using a springer GAMO express that had a kick like a mule.  This gun, by comparison, has no kick at all which makes it easy to be deadly accurate (I have taken out squirells at 30 yards up in trees with 6 pumps).  But I have mixed emotions about this gun because there is no place to mount a rifle scope, and it is accurate enough that a rifle scope is a big asset for long shots.  The B272 mount is useless to me, as it puts my rifle scope on the barrel so far from my eye I can't use it without putting the stock over my shoulder. I know you can mount a pistol scope, but that's not what I already have from my GAMO rifle.  Unfortunately, a rifle scope can only be mounted on the large diameter receiver end where you load the pellet.  There are mounts sold here that allow you to do that but they cost 1/4 the price of the gun ( Air Venturi Intermount, Fits Benjamin Sheridan Multi-Pump Rifles) and don't include the scope or weaver ring mounts.  Eventually I made my own clamping mount for the scope out of hard wood.  Really, though, can't crossman find a way to add an inexpensive rifle scope mount to the design?

product_title: Tasco Essentials 10x 25mm Compact Binoculars
review_body:
I really like these binocs. Theres only 2 problems with them and its probably not what you're thinking. First they use a primary focus knob and a single eye focus for differing eye weaknesses. The problem is with the fact that its only one eye that can do the fine adjusting. My right eye is stronger than my left and its the right that focuses. So I can get my right eye really sharp but my left is a little out of focus. Youre supposed to use the large focus knob to get your weak eye into focus but there are times when you cant (like looking juuust close enough to need the binocs but not far enough away to be able to focus... a drawback of a fixed power magnification). But its just a problem at those close ranges... anything over 25yd its fine. It would just be nice to be able to tweak both eyes.

The other issue isnt with the binocs themselves its with the case. The soft neoprene case is nice but the belt loop that they put on the back will just rip off the first time you snag it on a branch and then youre sweet little collapsible binocs are gone. Some reinforcement straps that go all the way around the case would eliminate this and not cost a whole lot more.

As for the positives of it they are a good magnification so that I can read peoples license plates across the parking lot in my apartment complex (50-75yds). The image is good, not too dark, which was a concern with 25mm objective lenses on a 10x magnification but its not a problem. They fold all the way up and the rubberized exterior feels good and sturdy in the hands. These will be perfect for the range, hunting, or just left in the car.

product_title: MARINER 4 PERSON BOAT SET
review_headline: Exactly What I Hoped It Would Be
review_body: For the last 2 years I had been using the main competition boat in this size and price range but I finally tired of how unreliable it was (poor valve design). I am very pleased with this product. Almost all reviews are of the 2008 model (yellow trim) but the 2013 model (red trim) is now shipping. Concerned over possibly quality differences, I called Intex and was assured the change is cosmetic, essentially trim color and design. I have had this boat on lakes ~ 100 acres in size, alone or with another adult maybe 6 times in the month+ that I have owned it and have felt secure in it, even when the wind has kicked up significantly. For the money, everything seems to be very good quality, with the minor exception of the battery bag, which can be seen in the back of the boat in the photo. Marine batteries are simply too heavy for this bag. A concern in previous reviews has had to do with the oars. To me, these appear to be very solid. Possibly the oar locks have been the issue, I am not certain as I have not used them, but the oars are good. The floor space is surprisingly large and the slatted floor does allow standing, for limited movement in the boat, but is not intended to constant standing. I have made and substituted a 1/2" plywood floor, and installed raised, backed, swivel seats for fishing. This makes room for 2 adults and plenty of gear. Online, there is much description of this process, by myself and others. The seat cushions that are provided are comfortable on the  bottom, but sit low and have no back support. There is an inflatable keel inside the boat but under the floor, which creates a v-shaped bottom when inflated, permiting better tracking in the water, particularly in a breeze, compared to similar models. This boat runs well when loaded, with a 30lb thrust electric motor, on lakes the size mentioned, but some have used 55 lb thrust motors and even small gas motors, with success. Adequate speed is a personal matter, often dependant on the distanceneeded to travel, but this boat can take a range of motors. This is not equivalent to a $3000 inflatable boat in quality, but neither is it in price. For this price, the boat meets all my needs and you will likely be impressed.

review_headline: Great mug, well insulated and water tight
review_body:
I had considered this mug previously, but the cost had deterred me. Recently my Starbucks travel mug finally wore out and so this was my choice for a replacement.
My requirements were it had to insulate well and be very secure and water tight. I often commute on a motorcycle and grab my latte/mocha etc on the way into work. And so it sits in my side cases while I am riding. I certainly do not want coffee and milk spilling all over everything. This Stanley mug is not just sturdy but also secure. I tested it for several days before trusting it in my side cases. That meant laying it on its side often. Tipping it over and being less then careful. After that test I felt comfortable throwing it on my cases while it was full. It has held up well in this short period of time, well enough for me to give it an excellent rating.
I also appreciate the fact that the lid can quickly be disassembles and cleaned.
As for insulation, the other day I was driving around eastern Washington in 95 degree heat. There was an iced latte in my Stanley, inside the car. The car was sitting in the hot sun for several hours and when I came back, I still had ice in the mug. I am not sure how they do it, as the walls are pretty thin. But it definitely insulates. And with a lifetime guarantee, I feel it was a good purchase.

product_title: Cathe Friedrich - Circuit Blast
review_headline: fantastic workout!  In my top 5 out of 300
review_body: I have over three hundred workouts, mostly advanced, and I have many Cathe workouts.  This workout ranks in my top five workouts that I've ever done.  No, it's not as difficult as some of Cathe's others, but I don't know if any other workout provides such a complete full-body workout--all in 42 minutes (using the "scambled eggs" premix which seems more difficult than the regular workout).  You do all sorts of push-ups, all sorts of plyometrics, and all sorts of dumbbell moves.  Most of the moves are fairly traditional, but the way all of the moves are put together makes for a workout that is fresh and interesting.  The absolute best thing about the workout is that you never ever ever repeat a move.  Every move is done one time and one time only.  (A very few moves are done on both the right and left sides.)  Additionally, you don't do the move until you're sick of it. You do various numbers of reps, and right when you think you've done enough, you have:  Cathe ends that move and you're quickly on to the next one. I have a love-hate relationship with bootcamp-style workouts.  I love the great workout I get, but I hate the boring, repetetive moves. There is no element of hate with this workout.  It has no dread factor.  None.  When I haven't worked out in a couple of days, when I don't have an hour, when I want to do a lot of push-ups, when I am flat not in the mood to work out, I do Circuit Blast.  If you're a serious exerciser and you want one of the best interaval workouts out there, get this one.  If you're looking for endless minutes of hard but boring moves, get this one.  You'll see what you've been missing.

product_title: Tapco Intrafuse AK Fixed Stock
review_body: My wife ordered this for me because I'm a charming man. (and she dented my car) First off, the only thing keeping this from a 5 star rating is the absence of the trap door in the buttplate for your cleaning kit. That said, this is a great option for those of you looking to get ditch your fugly, beat-up, wood stock and still keep the traditional look of your AK. It is exactly the same size as most original style wooden stocks commonly found on a variety of AKs. (Warsaw length) I laid it right beside a Romanian laminated stock for comparison, if you're wondering. I have to say I rather like the length of this stock, because I'm not an NBA All Star or a Sasquatch..I'm a normal sized guy.  If you are the aforementioned ball player or monkey-man, you probably will not care for the length of pull. I installed this, (and a Tapco original style grip), on a Hungarian SA2000M conversion that I was working on. For this rifle, I only had to file a small amount of the stock to allow proper fit to the tang area of the trunnion. Some will complain about having to \\"fit\\" these products, but I think Tapco has done well creating a stock that can fit as many variants as the AK-47 has. Plus, half the fun is working on one of your babies, right?  Now this rifle looks SO much cooler than when it had that Choate thumbhole/Dragonov looking stock on it. It feels rock solid when shouldered and transitions well to hip firing and back.  You're right on top of the sights when you get down on her too.  As always, take your time, get your fit right, and you'll be a happy camper when it's done.

I have Prime shipping. I ordered it on a Friday and received two boxes on the following Wednesday and the third box on Thursday. All boxes were in excellent condition as well as all the pieces inside. So when the UPS person brings you the first two boxes just let the driver know that a third box must arrive the following day (they are labled 1 of 3, 2 of 3, 3 of 3).

:::ASSEMBLY:::
-Manual for assembly: to download it just google \\"Powerline Cable Crossover Machine PCCO90X manual\\" and you'll get the PDF. It comes with the equipment but I recommend that while you wait that you read the entire manual so that when your product arrives you are already familiar with the pieces and steps. The way the instructions are written takes a bit of time to get used to but once you get used to it the instructions will be very clear to you.
-Don't worry that the manual is long and that there are lots of instructions. Once you read them once or twice and see the parts for yourself you'll see that assembly is very easy.
-If you're buying this also for triceps and biceps, then I recommend: [[ASIN:B00120P9HQ Champion Cable Attachment Package Pack]]. I got them and they are of excellent quality and love them!
-No tool is provided. But I assembled the entire thing with just my hands. After all is assembled you need a Socket Wrench to tighten up the 14 lock nuts that hold the whole thing together and six more (one for each pully).
-After I assembled the whole thing and saw the complete product with my own eyes I am not impressed with the quality of the product, especially with the cables - they are made of plastic and look cheap. The whole thing looks cheap. This product sells on Amazon for $409 (+$36 tax) now on 5/4/2013, so it must have cost the manufacturing company about $120 at most to make. That's right. This product cost them ~$120 to make, and they sell it for $409. This applies to every product ever made by any company (cars, computers, etc.). This is how business works. So now you know that you are in fact getting a cheap piece of equipment. I took a couple business and economics classes in college so take my word for it. Low manufacturing cost and big profit is what drives business. But the equipment looks nice and I love it!
-Assembly was very easy and even if the instructions are only ~90% clear, the other 10% can be figured out by common sense.
-Whenever you install a pully holder or mid pully holder during assembly, do not tighten up the lock nuts because at the very end of assembly (Steps 5A-C) you'll be inserting and routing the cables so the pullies will have to be taken out real quick to do that (very easy).
-Step 2B: you'll need a wrench extension for those two lock nuts. If you don't have it then they won't fall of until maybe an hour of exercise.
-The leg attachment (thing that wraps around leg) is actually pretty good. The thing looks very cheap and it looks like it won't work but when I tried it, it actually worked really well! I tried it for the hamstrings and quads and it worked!
-Step 2D: IMPORTANT - here the instructions forgot to mention to first apply silicon spray on the Vertical Frames BEFORE attempting to slide down the assembled Weight Frame. So do not forget to do this! Otherwise you'll have to literally hammer it down to slide! That's what I did until I realized I needed to apply silicon spray... It was so frustrating and I even thought I must have gotten defective parts (wrong size)! So I have warned you of step 2D.
-IMPORTANT: After you finish assembly and you test the product you'll notice that it is not smooth at all and that the Weight Frames simply stick to the vertical frames and don't go down. This just means that you have to apply silicon spray but only on your personal \\"range\\" of the vertical frames that the weight frames will use. After the silicon spray, they'll be extremely smooth! This step is also NOT on the instructions but it's common sense.
-99% of the assembly can be done by one person. The only exception is step 3A-3B - here's where you attach the long cross beam to the two tall vertical frames.
-Took me a couple hours to do the entire assembly since the instructions were not worded well and it was my first time with this product. Now that I've done it once, if I had to do it again it would take me maybe ~30 minutes.
-I also own [[ASIN:B000VLRVSC PowerLine PPR200X Power Rack]] (for squats and safe bench pressing) from this company and I tell you from experience that if you are not careful when you put the weight plates on the holding bars that the paint will come off. With the power rack I just put strong tape on the bars to prevent this so you can either always be extremely careful or just wrap strong tape around the bars to prevent paint from falling off when you take out the weight plates over time. This product does come with a tiny bottle of paint in case you need to re-paint it a bit.
-This piece of equipment is fully stable and sturdy after all bolts have been tightened up AND the two bases are properly wide apart. If they are not enough apart then the equipment won't be sturdy so distance is important here!
-My non-olympic weight plates fit perfectly.
-It came with two crossover handles (they feel very comfortable).
-If you do decide to get the Champion Cable Attachment Package Pack, then I highly recommend getting two extra links (at any local store near where you live) or on Amazon: [[ASIN:B00B84NS4M 100mm x 10mm Zinc-Galvanized Steel Carabiner Snap Link Hook - 3-3/4\\" x 3/8\\"]] (weight limit of each 100mm link = 500lbs, total = $7.38 including shipping for two) because this way you can leave four of the five attachments connected to the equipment at all times and the other can just be left hanging on it too. Or else with just the two links that come with this equipment you'll have the three attachments left unattached which can be VERY annoying.
-Lat exercises should also technically be possible with this if the attachment is bought and you use your own chair, and even rowing is also technically doable with this equipment.

:::WORKOUT:::
Very smooth! It is a pleasure to finally own my own! I tried cable crossovers, triceps pull-downs, bicep curls, and leg extensions (for hamstrings and quads).

product_title: Concept2 Model D Indoor Rowing Machine with PM3
review_body:
I have a lot of weight to lose and little space for indoor equipment as I live in a tiny Manhattan apartment. So, I was looking for a product that would allow me to do a cardio workout without being noisy or taking up too much space. I went back and forth between a spin bike and a rowing machine and I am so glad that I chose this Concept2 rowing machine. I had read the online reviews and I was impressed by the high ratings and that people stated that this is THE rower to buy in terms of quality.

First off, it it at arrived undamaged and was delivered quickly. I am an out of shape woman and I easily followed the instructions and put it together in about 20 minutes, by myself. I hadn't rowed in years, so I watched some youtube videos on rowing form to remind me about proper form. Unfortunately, I did this only after I rowed on the machine for the first time and got sore hips from improper form. So, unless you are a skilled rower please remember to review your form with online tutorials before rowing, or risk injury!

Once I got my form right, I really began enjoying my rowing workouts. I love that rowing works my entire body and that it is not hard on my joints, as I have bad knees. The more I use it the more I can increase my intensity on the machine and row for longer spurts. I was at 10 minutes per workout when I started rowing and I am now up to 25 minutes per workout. I row to music and this rower is not very loud, at all, so I can listen to my music at a comfortable level as I row. Additionally, I have not had any problems with the functioning of this machine, despite months of rowing. I have also toned up and have seen weight come off since starting my rowing exercise routine.

In terms of setup, this machine hooks together in the middle for quick setup and then unhooks and comes apart in two pieces to save space with storage. It also has wheels to help you move the front heavier piece around, as needed. Setup and storing it both only take me two minutes. I store it in its two upright pieces in the corner of my living room and it does not take up much space at all. I pull a piece of furniture in front of it when it is stored upright in the corner and people don't even realize it is there.

Overall, I agree with the other reviewers, that this is definitely a five star machine. It is gym quality, solidly built, makes little noise and it will work your entire body. product_title: Unisex Tactical 5.11 TPT L2 Tactical Durable Flashlight
review_body: I like it. I gave it 4 stars and not five because there is no place to put a lanyard on and also because of some other considerations. I suppose you could place a clip on it, but then you would lose that special feel of touching ( very comfortable feel) and using this flashlight. You could also get a belt holster. This is really a polymer version of the 5.11 Atac L2, but with some notable differences. They are both bright, around 200 + lumens with two CR 123A batteries. They both have a nice beam but with enough spill to illuminate the areas adjacent to where you are aiming. Although they both have a crenelated head, the Atac could inflict some real damage to an attacker because the head crenalations are sharp. With this polymer version, the sharpness is gone. But, you could still hurt someone with a poweful blow. So, in that sense, the polymer version is not what a law enforcement agent may want. Still, I like it. It is so very light and comfortable. you can easily carry it in your pocket or purse. As with the Atac L2, it has momentary activation by simply pushing the tail switch halfway, before it clicks for constant light. The default is high intensity. A double tap gives you low intensity. A quick triple tap gives you a poweful strobe. Simple, thus tactical.  It does not have the rather unique "lock" of the Atac L2, which comes from rotating the tail switch to prevent inadvertent activation. I am not sure you really need that feature. Of course, the polymer version is about 40% or so less expensive than the Atac, a nice feature. So, in conclusion, a very nice and very light flashlight, with some key  tactical features. You will love the feel of this flashlight and will want it in your pocket or purse.

review_body: Honestly, I didn't expect much to begin with when the cost of this set is still cheaper than either a front or rear genuine Magpul MBUS (authentic MBUS sights NEVER come as a set). With that being said, I didn't expect them to be complete garbage either. I was wrong. They don't lay down well, the rear sight aperture wiggles when flipping the sight up (forcing you to push it back in place) and I actually broke the rear sight when putting it on my .22 upper. I have the real MBUS sights on my 5.56 upper and the comparison is like water and wine. Not only is the construction of the PTS sights horrible, they look horrible too. There are a lot of burrs and excess flashing on the edges from the molding process. Despite the dolled up "made by the PTS division of Magpul" claims, these are just some Chinese knockoffs. I wouldn't depend on these for even my .22 upper, and I don't do air soft but I wouldn't even recommend them for that. DO NOT BUY...YOU WILL BE SENDING THEM BACK. Don't be a cheapskate to try and save a few bucks...save the headache, spend the extra money and buy real, American made Magpul MBUS sights.

product_title: Birchwood Casey Universal Touch-Up Pen, Black
review_headline: This isn't "just a sharpie" that's been relabeled....
review_body:
I assure you this isn't just another black sharpie that's been relabeled. This ink adheres FAR BETTER than a that found in a standard sharpie. Especially to materials like matte-black aluminum or steel. I use it exclusively on AR rifles and hand-guns that get banged up, mishandled, and/or marred and dinged during assembly. It's not going to make a lower receiver with a huge chip in the finish look un-touched, but it will make that shiny exposed area of aluminum that you gifted to said piece MUCH harder to see.

Fill in the damaged area with this 'sharpie' and immediately (maybe 2-3 seconds after applying) rub what you can back off with your finger (aggressively). Repeat this process several times if needed and you'll notice how it blends with the surrounding area around the damage much better than just one application and letting it dry. This method also seems to force the ink deeper into the affected area. Be warned that this \\"INK\\" is no-where near as durable as the baked-on finish that you damaged. It will easily wipe off with alcohol, and most cleaning agents. Essentially it's the cheapest fix I've found for those eye-sores that seem to jump out at ya.

product_title: Cold Steel Kopis Machete
review_body: This was an impulse buy for me. I ordered it as a companion to the cold steel spartan, which I love and have also written a review about, but I absolutely love this machete. for under $30 you can't go wrong. I previously purchased cold steel's gladius machete, which is good for what it is, but more of just a fun little toy than a serious chopper. The kopis is both of these. When I first got it out of the box, I was blown away. It was a little bigger than I had expected, but that was good. Out of the package, the edge was quite rough. I had the same problem with the gladius machete, which I easily fixed with an arkasas stone, but its still a little annoying finding the same repeated discrepancies in cold steel's machetes. The blade is a lot thinner than I had expected. I was nervous on how durable it might be, but it is very flexible and I can bend it quite a ways and still have it return to its normal shape. This also makes it much lighter than would be expected from its size. I have taken it out many times to clear low hanging branches and brambles on my property and it has proven to be a very efficient chopper. If you are in the market for a good solid machete for yard work, and running around in the woods I would highly encourage you to buy this machete. My only complaint is the sheath. There really isn't much that can be done about it because of the shape of the blade. But three fasteners may be a bit excessive. I wouldn't advocate this as a zombie prepper weapon for any of you dumb kids considering that. It takes quite a bit of time for me to get this thing in and out of the sheath and into action. By that time I'm sure the zombies are already picking my brains out of their teeth.

product_title: Stainless Steel Guide Rod Assembly Glock 17,17l,22,24,31,34,35,37 GEN 1,2,3
review_body: I installed this on my competition Glock 34 gen 3 with a KKM stainless threaded barrel, muzzle brake, and weighted magwell after reading many reviews here and on other sites. The guide rod looks great and I could see it lasting much longer than the plastic guide rods. It also adds a little bit of weight to the end of your gun. I did not have the same problems as other reviewers as far as installation or fitment. The problem I had was ejection direction and muzzle rise. As indicated by testing at multiple distances including 7.5 yards, 10 yards, and 5 yards during rapid fire mag dumps, this guide rod and spring combination increased muzzle rise, moving my groups about two to three inches high. The other problem is brass getting thrown everywhere. with the factory spring and guide rod, the brass is ejected in the same place almost every time. With this guide rod/spring combination, brass is thrown everywhere, including in my face and at people behind me. I thought high groups could be my grip or trigger finger and the brass getting thrown everywhere was either my ejector or ammo until I changed back to the factory guide rod assembly and never looked back. I could understand if there was some kind of indication that this spring was much harder than the factory spring, but I have seen no such indication anywhere. Even if I could change the spring, I would think the whole purpose of having this is to have a guide rod/spring that is ready to go.

It fits flush with my castlenut and lower reciever. Two raised flanges fit into the recessed area of the reciever cap to lock it in position and the adapter is held firmly in place with a single allen screw. Its a very well made product and installation is non-destructive to the threads on the reciever extension. So, unless you want to spend hours destaking and restaking, adding a traditional adapter while risk damaging your lower, castlenut or reciever extension in the process or spending a big chunk of change having a gunsmith install a traditional adapter for you. Then this is one product you should definitely consider.

product_title: Sunny Health & Fitness Upright Magnetic Exercise Bike
review_headline: Quiet, sturdy, easy to put together, decent workout
review_body:
*Great qualities*

Assembly:
A few of the reviews had me worried about how difficult it would be to put together, but honestly it was a breeze. All the pieces were labeled and packaged together according to which step in the assembly directions they belonged to. Directions were very easy to follow: simple, written clearly, and illustrated. Package also included all tools needed. I'm a woman in my twenties and had it all put together by myself in under an hour. I did hear some reviews about bolts coming loose after awhile, so I put loctite on them all just to be safe. So far, no trouble.

Size:
Takes up very little room, and is light enough to move around easily.

*Good qualities*

Noise:
The bike operates quietly. There's a slight whirring noise which can be expected when pedaling something, but it's barely audible. It does clink a little now and then (probably just from the resistance cable), but overall it is not loud at all, and you would be able to watch T.V. easily without having to worry about cranking the volume.

*Okay qualities*

Resistance:
As far as the resistance goes, it's somewhat low. I haven't exercised in about 10 years, and although I'm about 130 lbs., I'm pretty out of shape, but I started out using this machine at level 4 without any real strain. I've been using it about a week and have increased the resistance to 6 now, which is still a pretty comfortable resistance while causing mild-moderate strain. Therefore, I'm worried about hitting a plateau in what the resistance can offer me once I've built up my muscle over the next few months. There are only two more levels to go, and I think they may not be challenging enough. However, if your focus is not on building up muscle, this bike would certainly provide a nice cardio/toning workout on a long-term basis. If you're looking to build super strong legs, this would just be a starter bike.

Bicycle Seat:
-Location - The seat, as mentioned in other reviews, doesn't have a lot of height to it, so this bike wouldn't be ideal for taller people. I'm 5'5\\" and can't really fully extend my legs on the highest setting. The seat is also pretty darn close to the handlebars, which is great for most people just looking to get some easy exercise. However, I like to be stretched out in a bit more of a spinning-style form, and the proximity of the seat to the handlebars isn't really ideal for that. However, if you aren't worried about having a spinning-style stance, the location of the seat in relation to the handlebars and pedals would be perfectly adequate.
- Comfort - The padding on the seat isn't awful. It's about the same as most bicycle seats, so if you find bicycling seats generally uncomfortable, you'd probably want a gel cover.

Handlebars:
No trouble reaching them, and with the padded design, there are multiple places you can place your hands. Not adjustable.

*Summary*

Overall, this bike is a wonderful value, and would suit the needs for the average buyer. If you're looking for something simple and easy to do for cardio or rehabilitation, this bicycle fits the bill. If you're looking for something to get you started on the path to strength and toning, this is a great bike to get you started. If you're already sporting pretty strong legs, or are looking to extend your spinning classes to your own home, this bike doesn't really have what you're looking for.

product_title: Maxpedition Falcon-II Backpack
review_body:
Okay, alot of A+++ positive reviews on this pack and for good reason. I wouldn't ignore the bad reviews but some things to take into consideration as follows:

It has a capacity of 25 liters. MAX capacity, so if you jam if full it lacks in let's say physique. Therefore, if you need more capacity, go with a bigger bag.

On the other note, its very very durable, very organized, and my favorite backpack. If your are experienced and have fined tuned or your gear, it can certainly function as an overnight bag. If your looking to get another night out of it, I would consider outfitting it with accessory pouches or stepping up to a bigger bag.

I do not typically use water bladders, I have just never been fond of them. Note, if you do incorporate a water bladder to this bag, which it does have a compartment just for that, you will lose a good majority of the main compartment.

I will try to keep it short. Top quality. Very durable bag. Very appealing to the eyes.

The only complaints I see are that it is too small. Well, it IS a smaller bag. 25 liters is not huge. It is PRIMARILY a day pack. The right person can make it an overnight pack in the woods.

I love my bag, and it has been through hell and back the past 6 months. If you try to cram 35 lbs of gear into it, it will be uncomfortable. I use it as a scout/day hike/warm weather overnight bag and have zero complaints.

product_title: Hip Hop Abs DVD Workout
review_headline: Great program once I got past the 2 defective DVDs
review_body:
I did the program for the allotted 30 days that it requires. Everything seemed okay until I inserted the 3rd DVD, which you don't use until week 3. The DVD loaded the menu, but it would not play the video portion. I ordered a replacement from Amazon and shipped back the original package that contained the defective DVD. The 2nd shipment had the same issue! I called Beach Body technical support, which was somewhat of a headache, given that their support is outsourced (I'll leave you to stipulate why it was a headache). It took about 10 days to receive the replacement DVD for the 3rd disc. The new one plays just fine.

I am very satisfied with the program as a whole. It is very low impact on knees in comparison to other programs that Beach Body offers. I won't go off on some random tangent on how great I think it is, I'll let you be the judge yourself of it based on the results I got from the 30 days.

I'm sure the comparison to a scalpel is over used, but I would venture that's not far off.  For a guy like me, that doesn't sharpen his knives often, this zdp sounds like just the ticket. I wish I could attach a pic to this review.  It fits easily in the change pocket of my levis 501s, if that gives you any ideas.  The Ambitious I have to cram in there uncomfortably, but the dragonfly 2 fits right in.  This is a dinky little knife that is good for opening packages and not scaring the heck out of your co workers.  Judging by their reactions, even the Ambitious was too big for the knife phobic LOL.  This knife doesn't weigh a thing, either.  I really like it.  It's just not exactly what I thought it would be.  I don't think I could chop vegetables with it or anything, which is kinda a bummer, but it's so small I can't imagine a cop or anybody would get concerned about it, even if I had to go into a court room or something.  It's perfect for 90% of what I need a blade for, which is opening packages and the like.  My Ambitious is good for general tomfoolery and abuse, and my Endura for 'tactical', which means it hardly ever comes with me, but I'm glad to have it when it does!  I took the endura out at the laundromat once to open a box, and realized I was freaking people out LOL. You could use this tactically in a pinch, and probably better than the Ambitious, truth be told.  I'll update this later, but for an EDC that I know will always be sharp, this fits the bill!  EDIT:  2 year update!  Time has come to sharpen this.  Luckily, it's only $5 to send it back to Spyderco to have it done.  I got probably 18 months out of the edge before it needed sharpening, and I have used this daily.  In fact, I miss it all the time while it's been mailed off.  Due to knife laws in CA(buy a knife in the mall, get arrested for posession in the parking lot, no joke!) I really only carry this one anymore.  I can't think of any task that it hasn't been suitable for  in the last couple years, including slicing vegetables!  heh.  The clip became loose and I never tightened it up, so it got lost along the way, but again I don't miss it due to CA laws.  I can't even look at my Ambitious anymore.  It's relegated to hiking backpack duty.  I wear 501 Levis usually and this knife has been completely unnoticeable in my pockets.  The only time I've ever wanted it to be larger is when I've walked through a dark alleyway.  Other than that, this is the perfect size.  My best knife purchase ever, I would recommend it to anybody.  ::::3 year update::::::  Time flies!  I used it a couple years until it needed to be sharpened,and then I shipped it back to spyderco to get a new pocket clip while I was at it.  Money well spent!   This thing just holds an edge like nobody's business.  I don't think I could go back to a softer steel after this.  I've never had it stained or rust, no chipping, and it has sufficed for my every day use.  I don't know how I can get my whole hand comfortably on a knife this small, but somehow I am.   I would buy another one as a gift without hesitation.  For me, it's the perfect EDC.  It's non obtrusive, legal in my area, and does everything I've asked of it.

product_title: Rawlings Heart of the Hide Dual Core 12.75-inch Outfield Baseball Glove (PRO601DCC)
review_headline: This glove made me a better player/coach
review_body:
First off, I'm not a professional and didn't even play play high school baseball. I'm an avid baseball fan and recreational player, mainly tossing balls around with my kids and coaching little league and such. I did play on my work softball team for a few years though.

Anyhow, here's the point. I go through baseball gloves because I'm rough on everything. But since I don't play every day, my gloves don't get a lot of break in too. I do like Rawlings gloves in general though because I find their higher-end gloves are generally softer out-of-the-door than competitors, I like the deep pocket wells, and I use the index finger hole when I'm playing catch or pitching a bunch - so it's nice to know the hole is there as an option of many of the Rawlings gloves. It doesn't get in the way if you're not using it, like if you're catching lots of flies or standing behind the batter.

Back to the point. Of all the gloves I've ever owned, this one, probably because of the way they stitched up the pocket, lays out flatter when open and rounds up quicker and tighter when grabbing than any other glove I've ever owned. It's almost like the glove does more work and I physically do less. Crazy, right? Before this one, I owned another Rawlings and it operated like any other normal glove. But when I put this one on, since among other things, the pocket has no seam and is all part of the same piece of leather that makes up the face of the glove, it's like another extension of my hand.

As they say, you get what you pay for. In this case, it's clear what the extra cost is paying for. I had a leather jacket repaired once and they leather guy told me that it's ridiculously hard to find single large pieces of scar-less, uniformly smooth pieces of leather, so that's why cheaper leather jackets and bags and such use more \\"scraps\\" of leather stitched together, while higher end leather products have fewer pieces, less stitching, and a uniform look throughout. This glove, among all the other gloves I've had to date and evaluated, meets that same criteria. Needless to say, I'm hoping this one stays with me for a long time. As I'm getting older and find the only times I use this now are for coaching little league and playing toss, it should be.

Other note: All gloves IMO should be broken in. I used Rawlings own oil and strap break-in kit ([[ASIN:B0034WKNH6 Rawlings Glove Break-In Kit]]). I felt it was just ok. Not terrible like some of the reviews. It made the glove smoother, but the break-in kit I got came with an oversized plastic ball that I felt didn't really do the pocket justice and the oil didn't exactly meet my expectations regarding softness. So I might recommend another product with high reviews like the Hot Glove Heat Treatment ([[ASIN:B0000ATDIC Hot Glove Heat Treatment]] and strap ([[ASIN:B004I5L9EY Unique Sports Deluxe Hot Glove Wrap]]).

Anyhow, I definitely recommend this glove for the amateur baseball dad, and I suspect it would do better than fine for most of the better players out there too.ut. product_title: Condor Tornado Tactical Leg Holster
review_headline: Other than the problems noted, this is a fairly good drop leg holster.
review_body:
The Condor Tornado Tact Leg Holster (Multicam, Fully adjustable). If you have TTD you should not get this holster (TTD=Thick Thigh Disease). I did a lot of packing, bike riding, weights, stair climbs and the straps max out on persons with TTD. The elastic on these straps aren’t what they should be either. They are thin, weak and do not appear to be aging well after 3 months use. After wearing the holster a while it settles in and loosens which required tightening or adjusting. Because the holster attaches to one location on your belt, it has the tendency to pull down your belt lowering it’s position on your thigh, thus loosens the leg straps and moves or flops around. I am observing this inevitability where ever and with whomever I seer using this holster. The gate guard had to adjust his the other day as I was driving up, rather than keeping his attention on the approaching concern. The holster also should only be deployed in urban or city environments. On a hunt, I have crossed obstacles only to find my hand gun gurgling bubbles in the river I am forging, hung in the brush and cat claw, making my progress more obvious and noisy.
I recommend that this holster be fitted with a method to attach to your belt in two locations, probably straddling a belt loop of your pants.

Other than the above problems, this is a fairly good drop leg holster.

product_title: Prism Stowaway Delta Single-Line Kite
review_headline: Very easy to use the first time and stow away is nifty
review_body:
Initially intended to get a trainer kite after seeing amazing kite boarders during a trip to Boracay beach last month.
After more research decided that mayhap I need to learn just the simple single string kite first before making a big investment.
This is a really good kite for what I needed, my 11 year old got the hang of it the first time too. It is easier to have two people for launching, but even she was able to launch it from the ground or by holding it herself unassisted - I guess it just depends on the wind conditions.
At this point we cant do anything too fancy with it yet, we are just happy to keep it up in the air for as long as we have. And when it crashes, and it did a lot because we were newbies, it's designed well enough to handle the multiple nose dives.
The tip is kept taut by the middle pole only. the side poles actually do not connect to the tip, I think it makes it more forgiving when it crashes this way.
The poles are like mini tent poles that bend and only the poles that traverse the kite horizontally detach and fold in half, every else stays in one piece. The storage case is really slick, easy to stow kite away not too tight fitting, and the way you can stow the spool on it is also nifty - it looks so nice you can't wait to fiddle with what's inside it, it beckons you :P
Kite looks beautiful up in the air - very vibrant. I did learn early to keep my fingers away from the string when its pulling up really fast, not just rope burn but it can cut a little - but that is just inexperience on my part. It was the first thing I warned my daughter about and she managed beautifully, even better than me. Maybe some kind of glove will be good to have in the future and some auto winder thingy (and maybe a folding chair to tie it on as I am resting and ...maybe beer too.) Seriously though it was too fun that I didn't realize time passing by...I got sunburn on my legs - so yeah toss sunscreen in with that.

product_title: SureFire E2D LED Defender Flashlight
review_headline: Great, now my wife wants one...
review_body: I bought this a few weeks ago after my concealed weapon carry permit teacher recommended carrying a flashlight for personal protection in addition to a firearm. I now carry it everywhere I go, day and night and I'm surprised how useful it has been. I ask myself now how I ever got by not carrying one! This thing is stupid bright. I take my dog for a walk at night in the dark each night and it has been awesome just to shine ahead at a parked car to make sure there's nothing fishy going on or to locate my dog if she doesn't come when called right away, or even scoping out a dark corner to make sure no one is lurking. Now my wife wants one to carry as she exits stores to walk to her car at night through parking lots. I can't say enough how great this flashlight is. review_body:
This is a great Airsoft.

ONE FAULT:
Like other reviewers say, sometimes when taking out the clip with BBs still remaining in it, a couple BBs may just fall out.

ACCURACY:
The accuracy is amazingly good. We've tested it up to about 25 feet so far and it is surprisingly accurate, the grouping good.

DURABILITY:
Very durable. Yes it's plastic but it feels solid and tight.

SAFETY:
It has a manual safety identical to a real 1911 style pistol. We shoot it almost exclusively INDOORS at a cardboard box target. To test this potential damage, I shot it point blank at my hand (using the 6mm plastic BBs it's designed for). It did sting and left a small blood blister but it did not break the skin.

A great introduction for kids to get practice with gun handling, safety, accuracy, etc.

Definition of STICTION. : the force required to cause one body in contact with another to begin to move. Origin of STICTION. static + friction

product_title: Buck BuckLite Max Folding Knife
review_body:
I don't know if this will post different and say this is the large version or not,which I did buy but on amazon it was a gift for someone.The medium model I bought at a K-Mart about four years ago on sale,two dollars cheaper and I'd have it right then?why the hell not.So let's review the knife...

Why Did I buy this knife?
In full blown honesty the Buck Ranger was my pocket knife before modern knives came about,unfortunately it was somewhat hefty and blocky for pocket carry.Belt sheath was a better option for it.The medium-sized Max seemed to be a good alternative to what I liked about the Ranger in modern form.It's not 100% like the Ranger but same steel,same blade length,lockback,similarity in blade shape...you get the idea.

Nylon Scales:
The handles have some texturing and it's a comfortable grip,I've drop it plenty of times and it's holding up well.The scales you can flex a little but not as much because the full length lockback makes it more solid,the Bantam it's much more evident.Can't really down the construction of a seventeen dollar knife it could be more solid with steel liners but it would add some weight...this is nice and light.

Lockback Function:
The opening of the blade isn't isn't slick like liner lock but it opens comfortably one-handed and locks up tight and just like a normal lockback closes two-handed.The blade does have some throw to it like a Buck Ranger so be ready for that.The thumb-studs for some reason I really like them...theyr'e nothing fancy they just are flat headed with nice tapering rather than pointy.

Clip-Point Blade:
The blade came very sharp out of the blister pack and not surprising had a sweet hollow grind with swedgework.According to Buck it's a drop-point but it's too sleek and contoured,extremely close to being the clip-point style not so widely used on modern knives...great balance of curve and straight edge.The finish is okay it is a satin finish but Buck does a stone tumble method so the steel turns out flawed/scratched looking.The blade is very comfortable and great for yard work or utility use.

UPDATE 3/5/2017:
Concerning the blade shape is where this knife loses a star.My first model is still going strong but I have purchased 4 or 5 of the 482 model as back-ups...so obviously I love this knife.The problem you'll find flat out is blade craftsmanship.Not the Edge 2X geometry or the swedge grind but just the look of the blade.Some have a nasty rounding of the blade spine looking like a odd crafted spear-point(which makes the Bantam look good).There's just not a 100% accurate look of the Max's blade.I have one in the box that looks nicer than the one I carry but the swedging looks a little shorter.This is a blade stamping and machining accuracy issue.I'd advise highly if you look to buy this discontinued model to get a good look at the blade craftsmanship first.

420HC Stainless Steel:
I'm not going to glamour this steel with hype as others do.For one 57-59rc in hardness on stainless and carbon steel was a common labor standard among the American knife brands like Schrade,Camillus,and Imperial.I don't know the names of those factory employees from those companies as they weren't marketing tools so forgive me...not sold on the BOS Heat Treatment labeling some secret recipe in hardening 420HC to 58rc(laughing).But pair this steel with Buck's Edge 2X?yes I do like the 420HC a lot as my personal use blade steel.Very quick to sharpen and brings back a razor edge,anyone that can't get good results from 420HC has no business owning a knife.Very durable too as this steel doesn't chip...holds up really well(thumbs up).

Does 420HC Stainless hold a good edge?
A very good question as I consider this steel to be 'selective' in edge retention...depends on the user.It's for someone who uses their blade for common cutting tasks like hunting,fishing,crafts,yard work/gardening,cutting a blisterpack or occasional rope.It won't hold it's edge as good as plain 1095 tool steel.But for being rust resistant,and how good of an edge it takes and so quickly as a stainless(competitive to 1095)?it does yield positive results in edge retention for the average user.With heavy amount of coarse materials cutting it does lose it's razor edge much quicker.That Edge 2X will work harder to cut more but yes 420HC will not fulfill every knife user's expectations...this is a general user's blade steel.

Pocket Clip:
The MAX is actually designed to be only for right handed carry for it's friendly price tag. but.All your hand contacts is the lockback spine so your key ring can't snag on the blade or your fingers contact the thumb-studs.It is a consolidated design by going this route but it hasn't been a crutch on my enjoyment of the knife.The steel clip is screwed on it's riveted but it's still tight,rides flush in your pocket,and it's not a chunky knife so it's pretty cozy.

Final Thoughts:
For seventeen to twenty dollars?yeah it's a pretty good knife by Buck.Of the Bucklite Series I think the MAX is more sturdy than the Bantam,zytel plastic construction and only half-length lockback design isn't quite as promising in durability.But the MAX does have a pretty good value behind it with no fluff to gimmick around...just function.4-stars!stant,and how good of an edge it takes and so quickly as a stainless(competitive to 1095)?it does yield positive results in edge retention for the average user.With heavy amount of coarse materials cutting it does lose it's razor edge much quicker.That Edge 2X will work harder to cut more but yes 420HC will not fulfill every knife user's expectations...this is a general user's blade steel. product_title: Bazoongi Bouncer Trampoline
review_headline: Good quality, great fun!  Now a permanent fixture in the living room.
review_body:
My 2-year had a favorite game of jumping on moms exercise ball (with dad's help). The plan for this trampoline was to replace the big ball with something a bit safer that she could do without her dad's help.

I looked at a half-dozen types of small trampolines and finally decided on the Bazoongi because of it's size and mostly positive reviews. My thought was a larger surface would be easier to jump on without landing on the springs (which seems to be the case). She's pretty accurate but likes to drop to her butt with her legs straight out now and then; the couple extra inches keep her heels from hitting the springs.

I noticed most of the negative reviews were concerning broken springs; I guess I am of the mindset that this is a mechanical device and things will break. No big deal to me, I don't see any way a broken spring could fly off and put an eye out since they are completely covered by the padding. Besides, a broken spring should be the least of your worries if you are buying your child a "dangerous" trampoline!

I can see how some people might have difficulty assembling it, there are a number of tight fittings (which is a very good thing). Instructions call for a screwdriver (for attaching the handle), I also used a hammer to pound the pieces together. In all, it took less than 30 minutes from the time the UPS guy left to when my daughter started jumping (and she "helped" me every step of the way). Two adults could make assembly a bit easier but it's definitely not required, just make sure all pieces are fully seated.

Quality-wise it's great for the money. Fit and finish is good, no sharp edges. 6 legs keep it stable when my 30-pound daughter is jumping (like a good girl) although she likes to hang off the handle which causes the thing to tip very slightly. Absolutely no problems when jumping normally.

Would recommend to anyone, just make sure you have the space in the house because this will quickly become a permanent piece of furniture. I'd guess she has used it on average 90 minutes a day for the past week since we put it together.e this will quickly become a permanent piece of furniture. review_headline: Great extra knife - Neck or otherwise
review_body:
I got this knife to be the other half of a fire-starting kit. It's sturdy*, sharp and the handle is real 550 cord. Comes with a Kydex Sheath and friction-locks into place. The neck chain is black metal ball (dog tag style) but seems also thicker than a regular dog tag chain. The picture makes it look like the edge grind has a lot of non-coated metal showing. In fact it is only about 1/8\\". The knife and sheath are small. Smaller than my hand. But it does make a good neck knife if that's your intent.

*About the sturdiness: It's a thin knife. Probably about 1/8\\" thick overall. It's not meant to be used as a pry bar or for any other job that requires pressure or lateral movement of the knife. It is pretty thin and I could see it bending or breaking. To cut though, it's sharp out of the packaging.

My use: I got this knife to be the \\"scraper\\" for a fire steel. I attached the fire steel ( [[ASIN:B0033HF4A8 ARMY Fire Flint Steel & Striker hangpack]] ) to the 550 cord on the butt of the knife then I wrapped the sheath in jute to be used as tender. It's perfect. I believe I could skin an animal with this knife but I wouldn't use this little guy as my workhorse knife. I could also see it being used as a spear tip. I don't think the tip would last too long in that capacity, but I believe I could get a few throws out of it if I don't miss.

I don't regret buying this and I'm giving 5 stars based on quality of intended use. I do think $15-$20 is more of a correct price though.

product_title: Condor H2O Pouch (Bladder Not Included)
review_body:
I'd read several reviews for this product on Amazon and other seller's sites and was wary ordering this. I wanted the Maxpedition version but they're a bit more pricey and I wasn't sure I was gonna like the concept. I've personally had more good luck than bad with Condor stuff in the last couple years.

Time will tell about durability, but compared to what I'd read elsewhere it looks like it should hold up just fine for what I do. I'm using it to mount a quart Pathfinder School water bottle, nesting cup and stove ring to my EDC bag (and if I like it there, a second one my bugout bag). It would work equally well with any 32 to 38 oz bottle/cup combo. In the front, pouch, there's room for a folding "esbit" style stove (12 fuel tabs inside), a vial of storm-proof matches, titanium LMF spork, Even with the lofty insulating padding there's still room for the cup/bottle fire hanger that came with the Pathfinder bottle/cup/stove ring combo and a cotton bandana that makes a handy pot holder/cup 'n' spork cleaner/char cloth base. There is even room to put in a 1/2 of a scouring pad or tuft of steel wool for cleaning!

One of the bad things I'd heard about the MOLLE mounting straps is that they had too much play in them. This worked to my advantage mounting it to an ALICE-width webbing strap on the outside of my pack. Afterall, that was the point: free up space in the bucket-style main pack. So a reported weakness turned out to work in my advantage.

All things considered, I really like it. If it holds up for a year of EDC and occasional hiking, I won't look back. I'd recommend it to anyone in the same boat as me: 1) want to free up pack space and grant faster access, 2) keep water/cooking needs in one place and 3) not wanting to penny up to more "nameworthy" makers yet.

product_title: Mcr Strength Muscle Clamp
review_body: At the time of writing this review, I have owned these clamps for a little over a year. I use these clamps for bench, press, squat, and deadlift!  Please note that I own a power rack, so if you're benching without a rack or spotter arms, then you probably don't want to use clamps as I do. For me, if I can't lift something I just lay it down on my spotters. The benefit of the clamp on my lifts is simply to keep the weights from sliding or shifting. On squat, sometimes one side can dip lower than the other walking out the weight, and that's where these come in handy. These are the quickest and easiest clamps I have ever used. Nice features include rubber on the inside to make contact smooth with the bar. I've read that these perform poorly on Olympic lifts where weight is being dropped, but I don't do any of those kinds of lifts. I do good old fashioned powerlifts. I've tried springs and Rogue HG clamps. The HG clamps are also good, but aren't as fast and easy. I'd say the HG would be more suitable for Olympic lifting.

review_body: Snap caps for Tokarev handguns are a MUST for dryfiring! The Tokarev is an incredibly powerful gun, but remember it is a handgun of older design, and the firing pins in them were NOT designed for prolonged dryfiring. The older design of the firing pin simply precludes that, and if you dryfire repeatedly, you WILL compromise the pin. So for dryfire practice, these are a must to preserve your firing pins. Replacement parts for this gun are NOT easy to find. Nor are they cheap once located. Further, quality of replacement parts can be inconsistent at best. Do the smart thing,and invest a few bucks into preservation.

product_title: Reinforced Looper Series Gun Belt
review_body:
This is the first gun belt I have purchased and I am really impressed with it. The difference between this belt and the regular leather belts I was using is night and day. My regular leather belts would not support the weight of my G19 very well. Also, my holster would slide around during the course of the day of sitting and standing and eventually creep towards the middle of my back. It stays put now with this holster. I generally wear this belt with jeans, with an undershirt tucked in over the gun and a polo or button down un-tucked over that. My holster is a Comp-Tac Minotaur which I wear at the 4 o'clock position, and I use C-clips rather than the standard clips.

My experience with the sizing: I followed their instructions for sizing and although the belt fits, I am used to having a few extra holes in my belts. I used their measuring method and got a 34 inch belt, which when I wear it puts the buckle on the second hole when I am wearing the holster. This leaves 5 holes that are too tight and only 1 extra hole in case I get a bigger gun or gain some weight. Not a big deal but I would have ordered a 36\\" if I had known this - although now I am starting to prefer not having all the extra belt material I normally have. Also, this belt is supposed to be 1.5\\" width, but my Comp-Tac C-clips that are supposed to be 1.5\\" are too loose. Luckily I also have some 1.25\\" clips and they fit PERFECTLY(snug when you thread the belt through). Unfortunately they are discontinuing those clips.

I would definitely recommend this belt to those who are budget conscious and to anyone who carries concealed (or open, for that matter). There may be better belts out there but I have nothing to compare this to. All I can say is that for the price I don't think you can find another belt like this. I'll update this review once I've worn it longer and when I can comment on its durability.

It was very satisfying that this ronin gear balisong was different than the others. They pinch like hell it you're not careful. Ergo, my butchered right index finger. It's my own fault though. I'd say a good 15 to 20 percent of my finger is filled with many tiny cuts, all of which burn like hell when doing chaplins.
