product_title: CAP Barbell Black Flat/Incline/Decline Bench
review_headline: Decent Bench at a Reasonable Price
review_body:
Update: April 20, 2013

The two leg cross bars have rubber plugs that are inserted into each end of the bar. Unfortunately, the plugs are made, not with pliable rubber, but with hard rubber and very thin \\"wings\\" that are supposed to hold the plug in place by pressing against the inside of the bar. It didn't take long for the plastic wings to break, so now the plugs will not remain in place and fall out with the slightest bump. I finally just removed them altogether, although if I wanted to I could use rubber bands or some other workaround solution to keep them in place. Not a deal breaker for this economically-priced bench, but a bit of a nuisance and disappointing that they didn't use a better material for the plugs.

-----

I've been using this bench for about two months now. I'm very tempted to give it 4 stars, but decided to go with 3, due to a couple of the cons below. Nevertheless, for the price, it is a decent beginner's bench and it has been a good purchase for me.

Pros:
- Price -- tough to beat.
- Adjustable back angle, which for any serious workout routine is a must.
- Simple, but decent, leg padding.
- Adjustable lower leg bar.
- Small enough to fit comfortably in a bedroom or home office.

Cons:
- Too small for someone big. I'm average height so it is not a big issue for me, but if you are 6' or taller, this bench likely isn't going to work for you.
- Not quite as sturdy as I would like. In fairness, it is plenty sturdy for all the normal lifts you would do on the bench, but I'd like my bench to be sturdy enough to be able to do step-ups (i.e., holding weights and stepping up from the floor to the bench and back down). I've done it a couple of times, but it just doesn't feel like it will be able to take very much of that kind of punishment, so I've stopped. I realize this is using the product in an unintended fashion, but some of the heavier duty benches can handle step-ups without a problem.
- The legs scratched my hardwood floor. They are supposed to be smooth and in fact are mostly smooth, but they are hard and once you put a person with weights on the bench and shift it around a bit during normal use, it can scratch. I ended up having to purchase pads for my floor. If you are using the bench on carpet or concrete it won't be an issue. If you have linoleum? Probably would also want to get pads.
- A related issue is the bench's tendency to move around. I would have preferred durable rubber padding on the bottom leg, rather than straight metal, as the bench can slip. The slippage isn't enough to cause problems while you are lifting, so I don't have a safety concern; just that the inevitable bumping and adjusting and lifting during normal use can shift the bench around a bit. Again, the pads I purchased help keep the bench in place.

Other:
- I haven't really noticed too much smell with the particular unit I purchased, and I am typically quite sensitive to odors. For a few days out of the box it was noticeable, but the new factory smell quickly faded.
- Took a little while to put together, but not any worse than most 'assemble-it-yourself' products.

product_title: Buck Knives 135 Paklite Caper Knife with Heavy-Duty Nylon Sheath
review_body:
The Paklite series has to be one of the most overlooked series in the knife world. All of the knives in the series are around $20 a piece and made in the United States. They carry a liftetime warranty and their quality is superior to anything else in this price range.

The Paklite Caper is made for, of course, caping. It also does a fine job at every day tasks. The knife is one solid piece of Buck's 420HC stainless steel, hardened to 57-59 on the Rockwell scale, often running toward the higher end of that spectrum. The entire knife is 6-3/4\\" long and just a hair over 1/8\\" thick. There is simple jimping on some of the key areas of the knife, but for me, the jimping is too smooth. The handle is skeletonized to reduce weight, and if you want to use some wood or plastic for a handle material, this is one of the easier knives to customize. You could also use 550 cord or something similar, but that's not recommended if you'll be using this to cape animals. This version of the Caper has a baked-on black coating, which helps with grip. It almost feels like a light coating of Kydex was painted to the handle. Even without a wrap or handle scales, the knife didn't slip when wet or bloody.

The Caper's blade is 2-1/2\\" long with a nice hollow grind, and mine came razor sharp right out of the box. All of Buck's steel get Paul Bos' heat treat, even this cheap $20 one, and that, coupled with the blade hardness, puts this steel in the range of 440C or AUS-8. It's extremely easy to get shaving sharp, and holds that sharp edge for a decent amount of time. The 420HC is pretty corrosion-resistant. Aside from being a great caping blade, this shape and size make an excellent choice for every day cutting tasks. I think the grind looks cool on the black version as well.

The Paklite comes with a simple belt sheath. It's black nylon with a light pack-cloth fill, and it keeps the knife retained with a simple snap. A plastic insert is attached inside for safety. A simple run nylon webbing is sewn on the back for belt use. A few people were concerned about slicing the snap's strap off when removing and inserting the knife since it's on the blade side; I haven't found this to be an issue at all. In the sheath, the knife doesn't rattle. If you choose to cord wrap the handle or replace the factory handles, you'll have to snip off some of the plastic liner. In the sheath, the Paklite Caper weighs just 2.2 ounces, which is lighter than a lot of folding knives.

If you choose to use the knife as it comes, clean-up is easy. Just wipe the knife down and let it dry. Throw the sheath in the laundry. All things considered, this is one of the best $20 fixed blades available. The sheath is my only real complaint, and it's not even that big of a complaint. I wish Buck would offer the Paklite series with Kydex sheaths, and I'd gladly pay $35 for a knife + Kydex sheath combo. As it is now, the Caper is a winner.simple run nylon webbing is sewn on the back for belt use. product_title: Stamina In-Motion Elliptical Trainer
review_headline: The second one works great so far
review_body: This machine was easy to set up and takes up very little space. At first, balance is an issue since there is nothing to hold onto; however, after a week or so it wasn't a problem. Until you are comfortable, definitely use it near something you can hold onto for support. As they warn, the wheels and moving parts could be a danger to small children and pets. My small puppy was curious during setup alone, so I keep a safety gate between us any time I use this. It only takes one mistake; it's not worth it.  For two months this machine worked awesome; it's a wonderful low-impact workout. Just days before the warranty expired, it seized up in the middle of a workout as if something inside broke. I tried WD-40, although the manual doesn't mention a need for this, but nothing worked.  Amazon was amazing about the replacement, and I had a brand new machine within two days, even before they received the broken one back from me (they paid full return shipping also). The replacement machine is past the warranty now and past the mileage where the first one broke, so hopefully it was just a bum machine.  The workout is great for those of us who prefer staying home vs. the gym; the size is perfect vs. big equipment in the house; the price is low. The only reason I gave 4 stars instead of 5 is that the first one did break, but they made it right with little impact to me.  *****UPDATE: The second one broke a little over two years after the first one. I did use it a lot and really enjoyed the workout, but eventually it locked up just like the first machine. I went a different route after that, not because I didn't love it, but because I don't want to fill a landfill with broken equipment.

product_title: Teeter Hang Ups EP-950 Inversion Table With Healthy Back DVD
review_headline: A miracle cure for lower back pain.
review_body:
In my opinion, there is no better remedy for lower back pain. You don't even have to hang upside down. I just go to 60-degrees for two minutes several times a day and my chronic lower back pain is no longer. (I have no financial or other interest in this company, but I wish I did.)

As for assembly, the instruction are very good, but it helps to view the video beforehand. All necessary wrenches are provided, but they are cheap cutouts and assembly will be easier with your own set. In spite of the apparent large number of parts, the assembly is easy. Left and right parts are stamped as such. It takes a little muscle power to lift the parts and tighten all the bolts properly, so I don't recommend that very elderly people try it themselves. It took me about an hour to do the assembly, but now that I have done it once, I could do it again in 15 minutes.

This morning, I woke up with a stiff back, so I hung at 60 degrees for two minutes, and my back has been loose and pain-free for hours. It's hard for me to stop talking about how great this product is.

By the way, Tweeter is advertising these units on TV, but it appears that the TV version does not have the advanced ankle restraints that the EP-950 has. Contrary to safety instructions, the new ankle restraints seem so secure (when clamped down tightly) that I don't bother to put shoes on before using the unit at 60-degrees. I think if and when I go to 90-degrees, I will wear shoes. But shoes are safer if you're not lazy like me.

product_title: STIGA Titan Table Tennis Racket
review_body:
If you're looking for a paddle that can instantly add excellent spin and control to your game, this is a great choice that won't break the bank.

The tradeoff for spin is that the Titan won't naturally deliver a lot of power to your shots (it's a very light paddle) but the ability to send a ball curving away from your opponent can be just as satisfying.

Having used a number of other paddles at this point, I'd also note that sometimes having too much stickiness in the paddle (like the Titan here) can make it hard to face better opponents. You'll be forced to respond to their spin with this paddle, whereas slicker, heavier paddles will often just ignore spin outright and allow you to just smash the ball back. Just a matter of skill level and preference, but overall I love this thing.

EDIT: I've been using this paddle consistently for a couple months now, and still recommend it as a great purchase for early players who want to step up their game. The first review of this product (by nofearforme, January 23, 2011) is a spot on breakdown of the strengths and weaknesses of the Titan.

product_title: TYR Swimple Youth Metallized Goggle
review_body:
I purchased these goggles about a year ago for my 5 year old son. Initially, they were great and we really liked them (actually, my son LOVED them!). Despite being kind of dark in indoor settings, they worked perfectly outdoors. My son never complained about water getting inside of the goggles. . .and the fit for his head was perfect and comfortable. He was also able to put them on and adjust the dual-straps on his head most days with zero assistance.

Well, in less than 6 months of use, the goggles looked pretty rough. The "metallized" lenses had a few scratches and the plastic adjusting piece would continually fall off. Despite these problems, my son was still able--and wanted--to use them. We would just snap the piece back on and continue like nothing happened. That is, until the piece went missing somewhere at swim lessons this year. After this occurred, we were forced to purchase a new, but different, set.

Overall, the goggles were okay. We did have some issues with fogging but not so much that we wanted to dispose of them immediately. For a young child, I wish that the metallized tint was a little more durable. Despite the scratches, the usability was still there and my son did not complain about them obstructing his sight. The only thing that I was most concerned about is the plastic-side clip giving out so soon. I cannot say that it was due to user error since it was rare that my son needed to adjust the tightness of the goggles. . .and if he did, more often than not, his father or I (or swim instructor) would help him with them. So, if it was not for that, I would say that these are 4 stars but since I am not sure about the plastic-piece being defective, I have decided to rate them as a "3".

product_title: Tai Cheng DVD Workout - Base Kit
review_body:
Please see Frieda's review for a GREAT comprehensive review of this product. I wanted to share my own story.

All good Tai Chi stories begin with P90X.
While attempting P90X in late 2011, my right elbow started to have severe pain especially during chin ups. I also had other medical concerns around general fatigue. I had to stop P90X. I needed to recover instead.

In July 2012, I ordered Tai Cheng. By going through the exercises, I discovered major muscle acid build up in my triceps and upper back muscles (teres major and minor). I also had high stress in the sides of my thighs that I never realized was there. It put unnecessary tension on my knees and hips. Tai Cheng breaks down and releases a LOT of acid from the muscles! I had to stop at 4 weeks and REALLY focus on drinking more water and getting my diet correct. After a month, I restarted.

As of today, I have completed 2 rounds of Tai Cheng! (1 round = 90 days)
All the stress is gone in my triceps and teres muscles. I believe that's what was causing me to be unable to do chin ups and causing elbow pain.
My legs also have no more tension. I feel taller! When I do yoga, I can get into positions I previously couldn't, especially where crossing my legs was concerned!
I'm currently 32 but started when I was 31. In the back of my mind, I was concerned about getting stiff when I got older. Tai Cheng has alleviated that fear! It's a secret weapon against the immobility of aging.

RECOMMENDATIONS:
If you attempt Tai Cheng, follow the diet and drink plenty of water. This workout releases MASSIVE amounts of acid from your muscles! The healthy diet keeps your body alkaline which neutralizes acid. The water flushes the material away.

Buy both the Foam Roller AND the Rumble Roller. The gentle Foam roller will help ease you through the painful spots. The intense Rumble Roller will help you with deep or specific spots. You feel very accomplished when a spot that was super painful even with the Foam roller is something you can attack with the Rumble Roller! :)

Because it helps you eliminate lactic acid build up in the muscles, Tai Cheng is great for:
- The elderly who can get onto and off the floor
- Someone who has always had that tight problem area
- Athletes who may not realize how much acid their muscles are storing.
- Someone who wants to properly prepare themselves before attempting a more intense workout routine
- Someone who has trouble getting on the diet of a more intense program like P90X because changing your diet AND exercise at the same time is just too much. (Like me!)
- Someone who's done some intense workout routines and needs downtime. If you've done 1-2 years of intense training, you NEED to recover with 90 days of Tai Cheng.
- If you're a klutz and want better balance and bodily control! It could be acid build up that's throwing you off!

CONS:
- Tai Cheng does NOT focus on getting you to feel your Chi. In other Tai Chi classes, the entire purposes is to feel your chi moving through your feet, body and hands. This seems Americanized so that those subtle things are left out. It's definitely West, not East.
- Beachbody over-sells their supplements throughout the videos. It feels intrusive. In the P90X videos, it felt more instructive.
- The menu navigation could have been better. It offered too many screens before you get started.

I do NOT consider any of these cons to be major flaws. I just want to be honest about it's mild imperfections. The program isn't perfect so I give in a 4 out 5.

product_title: US PeaceKeeper Rapid Deployment Pack
review_headline: Good choice when a tactical vest isn't practical.
review_body:
Although numerous YouTube videos and message forum posts would suggest that anyone and everyone should have a tactical vest for any shooting-related activities, I personally can't come up with many scenarios where such a setup is practical for me. If a person anticipates needing easy access to several magazines, backup weapons and tools over many hours or days without resupply, I can appreciate a greater need for this, but I am thinking more of a home-defense or bug-out situation where I need to move fast and with as little \\"getting dressed\\" time as possible. For those purposes, the Rapid Deployment Pack fits the bill perfectly.

As others have noted, this is made in China, but the quality is reasonably good. I suspect that opinions on durability will vary based on usage, but (hopefully) I'll be using this for storage 99.9% of the time, and the stitching, zippers and elastic all seem to be up to the task of securing the contents under at least moderate wear and tear. The rifle mag pouches may seem too small to make good on the stated capacity of two mags per pouch, but persistence and/or patience will get results, at least with the metal GI-type 30-round mags I use. I was not able to fit two double-stack 9mm mags (Beretta PX4) in the pistol mag pouch, but I honestly didn't expect to. This might be possible with other mags, however. I didn't find much use for the drawstring closure on the remaining exterior pouch, but this pouch can also be used for pistol mags, a knife or flashlight among other things. The inclusion of drainage holes at the bottoms of the pouches is a plus, although I also carry my mags upside-down since the velcro flaps don't provide enough coverage to keep out rain or snow. Interior capacity is generous if you are realistic about what you're trying to carry in a pack of this size. I use the three interior elastic carry points for a Smith & Wesson folding knife and multi-tool (in its own pouch) and a small LED flashlight. The remainder of the main pocket is occupied by a SWAT-T Tourniquet, an Adventure Medical \\"Wound Closure Kit\\" and Surefire EarPro earplugs in their own container. I have confirmed that the other zipper pocket has ample space for a compact handgun and then some. With nothing stored inside, both zipper pockets make fine mag dump pouches.

A major selling point for me is the carry position, specifically the single shoulder strap as opposed to strictly belt carry or a traditional dual-strap backpack. I don't anticipate ever attempting belt carry with this pack due to the velcro placement, but there is nothing preventing the use of the pack in conjunction with another backpack. Fully loaded (with loaded mags) the shoulder strap allows for very comfortable, secure carry. It could potentially hinder access to a shoulder holster, but there is room for adjustment. The Rapid Deployment Pack isn't big enough for a full-featured \\"Bug Out Bag\\" by most definitions, but there are plenty of larger alternatives available. It can function reasonably well as a range bag or as an EDC pack suitable for those using public transportating or riding a bike.

The only reason I didn't give a full five-star rating is that, as snug as the external pouches are, I feel that I came extremely close to ripping the stitching while inserting a second rifle mag in each pouch, although other reviewers have had success with PMags, which surpasses my expectations. Also, as others have commented, it is disappointing to buy a product with \\"U.S.\\" in the name and \\"Made in China\\" on the label, although frankly this has come to be the norm. Regardless, a good product is a good product.

product_title: Model .308 Short 4 OZ Heavy Buffer for use with standard Model 15 Buttstock
review_body:
It's basically a solid steel carbine buffer with what appears to be a Teflon finish. I cannot compare it's effect on recoil to other buffers as this is the only I ever used. I WILL describe the recoil though.

In addition to this buffer, my gun has a 20 inch barrel (Red-X), shark muzzle break, Addax Tactical Guardian lower receiver, Magpul ACS-L butt and Armalite recoil spring.

The recoil is a little heavy but soft. Comparing it to an M-14 is like comparing sitting on a hard stool to sitting on a sofa. The best example for comparison I can think of is a 6 year old child softly but firmly shoving your shoulder with one hand. Mind you, the main culprits to that are undoubtedly the weight of the barrel and the effects of the muzzle break. But this heavy buffer undoubtedly had to play a role. As far as reliability goes, well, the rumor about .308 ARs not being able to feed JSPs is true. But as long as \\"smushy tipped\\" ammo is avoided, the gun has AK like reliability. The gun also doesn't make a sound when you shake it, a luxury you don't get with standard buffers.

It's a good buffer overall. I'm glad I spent $20 on this in stead of $5 more on a standard one. Better for less.

product_title: Horizon Fitness EX-59 Elliptical Trainer
review_headline: Feels and looks great - a little light
review_body:
I would actually give this a 4.5 likely. One thing that bothers me is that it's light enough that when I stand with my feet at the back of the treads and don't step too lightly, the front end lifts up a little bit. I just adjust my stride.
It's QUITE quiet. The only real noise is the friction of the runners at the base, unavoidable. Watching TV or listening to music easily drowns it out. The beeps mentioned by others IS also annoying. It's loud for no good reason. After the warranty is up, I might look into opening it up and putting something to adjust the level. I ran for a little over an hour today with my wife sitting only ~6 feet away watching TV and it didn't bother her at all.

I'm 5'9\\" and the height is fine. My setup isn't - best place to use is under a build (down) ceiling covering heating ducts, so it's pretty low. If I'm not careful, I bump my forehead. The fan blows more on my chest than neck or face.

I'm currently not in the greatest shape, but I generally use it at the 4th or 5th intensity level and move at the 6.8 (mph?) pace. I've used it 4 times for a total of about 4:30 hrs. My shoes were tight, so once I took them off. Bad idea. The treads were not good on my feet; the soles are still sore.

It fits in a small space much better than I expected. It can easily set almost right up next to a wall, unless you need access from either side.

I don't imagine I'll test out the speakers much, as if I'm running inside, I'll likely watch TV shows or movies, or do as I do when I run outdoors, listen to music with earbuds.

After a couple uses I noticed that I could hear a jingling sound. I remembered to check it after today's session and the bolt/nut on the front right tread was loosening. Glad I caught it. I tightened it up and will keep an eye on it.

So far I'm quite happy with choosing this elliptical. If I had the extra $200, I might have gone with the next model up, but I have no regretson this purchase.

product_title: Drymax Run Hyper Thin Mini Crew Socks
review_headline: Plain and simple, they work - and this is a sock hater saying this
review_body:
I have been running in minimalist footwear for almost 4 years now, usually with no socks at all. I most often run in Vibram five-fingers, but also do huaraches in summer. In bad weather or whatever, I would force myself to wear my old Asics with socks. I have always had sweaty feet, especially when running, so I really fell in love with the whole sockless/minimal thing.

It took me a few years to build up enough callous/toughness to run 3 to 5 miles, and even then in wet weather (or when I stepped in a puddle0 I always got some small blister or another. Body Glide helped a lot, but lately I was pushing into the 5-10 mile range and I came to the realization that I would need different shoes, and some socks. Dang, there goes my free-wheeling hippie weirdness...

I did a lot of research before buying one pair of these socks, and they are just phenomenal. I can run 5+ miles in them with sweaty feet, no problem. They feel absolutely frictionless, and I honestly can't even feel them when they're on. It's like I'm still barefoot. This is gross, but since I have only one pair (so far) I sometimes forget them at work in my gym bag, and they're still uh .. "damp" when I put them on to run the next day ... and I still don't get blisters. To top it off, I ran this weekend and the snow was still melting on the trail ... I sank ankle-deep in slush puddles a couple of times. This used to be the kiss of death in my Vibrams -- it would have been an instant blister. Not with these socks! I just kept running, and within half a mile my foot felt dry. I got home and took off my soggy shoes, but I forgot to take the socks off because they didn't even feel wet. Weird!

If there is any gripe at all, it is that even though I bought the size that was supposed to be for Men, size 10, they seem to run big. And by big I mean huge. The material is super-extremely-light-and-stretchy, but the extra fabric that goes into the heel actually bunches behind my heel by my achilles. Still, they smooth out fine and I can't feel anything back there. I might try a slightly smaller size when I buy the next pair, but maybe not. I know these work.

You get great visibility with this thing - at its highest setting its usually TOO bright for my needs. I dial it down to the lowest output and it works great for the trails around NOVA/DC. I know come winter there will be mornings when I'll need it's highest output, so its nice to have that in reserve - but right now 700 lumens is overkill. Also, I'm concerned about blinding oncoming bikers/runners with the output this light has, so I always keep it pointing in a low attitude.

I voted 4/5 stars because I would like to have the option of using the "blinking" mode at various output levels for those moments when you can see fine, but just need a better "visibility" setting. This only allows one brightness level while blinking. Also, the mounting mechanism (tab) causes me concern, because it feels like I'm going to break it every time I try to slide it off. The entire mount also seems a bit loose on the handlebars, and I find myself tightening it on occasion.

But overall, this is a tremendously powerful light with a convenient USB charging capability - I'm happy to have it.

product_title: Condor Tool & Knife, Hudson Bay Camp Knife, 8in Blade, Walnut Handle with Sheath
review_body:
So this is a pretty well-made knife. On my example the handle scales had shrunk a very tiny amount, likely because I live in an arid climate and where the knives are made is probably humid. Considering the knife is less than $40 it doesn't bother me. I do have some issues with the design of the knife that weren't apparent until I had it in hand and was able to use it. First of all, the handle is a little slick. When I tried chopping with it the knife was slipping in my hand. It could also really use a lanyard hole. For what the knife costs neither of these is a huge deal since almost anyone could fix these easily if they desired, and in doing so customize the knife. And who doesn't like to buy inexpensive knives and mod them? The biggest issue is the grind on the blade. This beast is about 1/4" thick and the primary grind is so shallow that it might as well not be there. This means the knife has a very thick edge that impedes it's performance. I would really like to see this knife with a proper full flat grind and maybe even reduced on thickness, this would improve it's cutting performance.

If you have a belt sander to thin out the edge and like to tinker and customize your knives than this might make a good project knife.

product_title: UTG Deluxe Tactical Green Laser Sight
review_body:
I got this laser for my birthday to put on my \\"tactical\\" 22. My red dot sight just doesn't cut it in broad daylight so I thought this green would be better. It is only slightly better. If you are aiming at something in the shade it shows up just fine but other than that, my red dot is just as bright. That is not the lasers fought however. It is really bright, just cant be seen in sunlight. I didn't take off any points for me not being able to see it.

I don't know how true it keeps zero because before I could get it zeroed half of the adjusting screw broke off making the entire thing useless. For the price I would have expected some better adjusting screws. These are bright brass and protrude from the sight over 1/8\\". Enough to where I could grasp it with my fingers. For something that says \\"tactical\\", they should be flush with the housing or even recessed, and black. Hex head or torx would have been a good idea. The enclosed tool is useless for zeroing. There is too much slack for it in the slots of the adjustment screws and it gouged the screws quite a bit before one finally broke.

The thing does not have a click-on/click-off button. Instead you have to screw the the cap down tight to get it to come on. Back it off a bit and press it to give it the temporary on that they advertise. That in itself was enough to turn me off. The corded pressure switch worked fine for what little bit I tested it.

Did I mention it was heavy. That's not necessarily a bad thing I suppose. Like I say, seems well built.

It comes in a nice metal tin that makes it look all high tech and I was truly impressed until I tried zeroing it and the screw broke.

For the price it should have had better adjustment screws and an on/off switch of some sort. Its a cheap laser wrapped up in a heavy, pricey package. Look elsewhere

product_title: INSANITY Base Kit - DVD Workout
review_headline: It certainly works, but there is a high risk of injury.
review_body:
If you are just beginning to get into shape, there's a chance that this program will be too much for you. You could theoretically modify the movements to be easier on joints and ligaments, but there are no modifications given on the DVD.

I got into this and quickly lost about 7 lbs. in only 17 days. I looked and felt better. However, I eventually developed tendinitis in my ankles and was unable to complete the program. I had appropriate shoes and good padding on the floor. After my tendinitis healed (several weeks), I tried it again, and my tendinitis came back.

There are likely many people out there with strong enough tendons and joints to handle the program. I was not one of them. I have also talked to many others who have had injuries and issues when attempting to tackle this program.

Shaun T. is excellent and motivating, but make no mistake, this program is intense and not intended for everyone. There are other ways to get fit that are much safer for your body. I personally think P90X is a much more well balanced, safe, modifiable, and effective program.

again be warned about mounting! It's a large objective!

product_title: BLACKHAWK! 3-Slot Ambidextrous Black Pancake Holster
review_body:
I've used this holster every day for the past 5 years. Here are some reasons why:
- Reason number one is it's great for conceal carry since it keeps the gun very close to the body.
- It's also very light weight but extremely sturdy at the same time.
- The gun fits snuggly into the holster and there are no issues of it falling out... for extra security you can use the adjustable and ambidextrous thumb break (I don't use it, because I fell it is snug enough without it).
- When the gun's not in the holster (let's say you get home and instead of carrying the gun around the house, you decide to put it away), you can "flatten out" the holster on your belt and it becomes non-existent. You feel like you're not even wearing it. Then you can just open it up again and it's back in duty quickly.
- Because it's designed for a 'size' of gun (I use #5), instead of a specific gun, I can keep using the same holster when I decide to switch from a G17 to an M&P.
- It's versatile enough that I can put a G26 in it without affecting the sturdiness of the holster, even if there's empty space where a longer barrel would fit.
- You can say an advantage is having different cants (90degree or FBI), but I only use the FBI cant which I feel is more comfortable.

I'm sure I will keep using this holster for years to come, even if it has 1 flaw... Since it is nylon, after about a year or two (depends on the use), it will start stretching out a bit. The snug fit and the closeness of the gun to the body might be slightly affected. That is why I replace the holster every year or two. But I do so with the exact same model because of everything mentioned above.

A final note... I used this holster for competition last year. It worked fine and I had no issues with it, even if I did finally decide to buy a kydex holster which is more suitable for competition for different reason (that I will not cover here). However, by the end ofthe year, the inner seems ripped and the inner lining came undone. So I bought a new one to replace the old one.

In conclusion, it's one of the best holster I've ever had and I don't think I'll use another for everyday concealed carry, even if I do need to replace the holster for a brand new one every couple of years.

product_title: Spyderco Persistence G-10 Plain Edge Knife
review_body:
I purchased this knife a few months ago to fill in for a Kershaw knife that was more than twice the cost, but has a serrated blade that required sharpening and did not seem to hold an edge well at all. I just wanted an inexpensive EDC knife since I was kind of disappointed in my expensive Kershaw knife. Maybe I set my expectations a little low, but I was still really excited to get this knife based on other reviews. I have to tell you that first impression I was EXTREMELY impressed, but still skeptical about how it would hold up long term. So, now I am writing a review after using it for tons of stuff over the last few months. I have opened boxes, cut a lot of rope and paracord, whittled wood, shaved fletchings off aluminum arrows and lots of other everyday tasks. I was curious how the 8Cr13MoV steel would hold an edge, and WOW, it is still really sharp, and I haven't even sharpened it yet.

Let me tell you just how sharp it is...the other day I was working and practicing opening and closing it with one hand sitting at my desk. I wasn't looking at it and just trying to repeat the process over and over. As I was closing the knife I saw something white fall on my desk and when I looked down there was a fingerprint the size of a pea laying on my desk. I looked at my hand and realized that when closing the blade it had shaved off the skin of my index finger so thin that my finger did not even bleed! Now that is SHARP!

One last example to point out. I was working on a Cub Scout outing and we were making survival bracelets out of paracord with about 80 people. We had a lot of paracord to cut to length and we were doing it on demand as kids chose their preferred color. A few other people were trying to help and had their pocket knifes out and just making a mess of the paracord because they could not cut through all the layers cleanly. Now, this may not be the ultimate test of a knife, but I let someone borrow my knife to cut it when they were having trouble and they absolutely fell in love with it. They were amazed at how sharp it was and how fast and smooth it cut the paracord. Again, not trying to say that paracord is so resilient that no other knife can cut it effectively, just that in a real world scenario it stood out well above every other knife that others were trying to use that day.

For a knife that I was hesitant to buy because it kinda looked weird compared to knives I have owned in the past, I think I am now hooked on Spyderco and will probably end up with a collection. I was online shopping for a Spyderco for my wife and decided to write this review in the process. I hope my experience helps you make a decision.

UPDATE 11/11/13: If you haven't bought this knife yet or are still on the fence, get off the fence, this knife rocks! I have been using it for 8 months and I absolutely love carrying it. I have never had a knife that I enjoyed the opportunity to use as much as this knife. I also bought a Spyderco Byrd for my wife and it is a great smaller option for her smaller hands and pockets, but with the same high quality steel. product_title: Adjustable Shackle Paracord Survival Bracelet
review_headline: This is your paracord bracelet for small wrists.
review_body:
I agree with the other reviewer that mentioned how difficult this is to get on by yourself. It does help to lay the back of your wrist against your leg or a hard surface to prevent slipping, but be warned that this bracelet will take some practice in putting on, but is much, much sturdier than the typical plastic buckles. This thing is not coming off until you choose to take it off.

The paracord used to make this bracelet, for whatever reason, feels a great deal less abrasive than some of the other bracelets I've had in the past.

Now for the biggest reason I'm here writing this review: This thing fits great. I've had horrible luck getting a snug, exact fitting bracelet in the past. You just can't find many bracelets to fit wrists my size, and since they aren't available from the more popular listings, the quality tends to be lacking when you deviate from the most trusted sellers. Not the case here. My wrist measures almost exactly six inches. Yes, I'm a man with extremely tiny wrists. I ordered the six inch bracelet worried I was going to end up with something either a little loose or a little too tight since I ordered an exact measurement, but wound up with a perfect fit. I'm extremely picky about exact fit, which is why I've gone through so many of these things.

Feel confident purchasing to your exact measurement knowing you're going to get something to fit that exact measurement. Shipping was also very reasonable.

If only this seller made the beefier bracelets I'd be purchasing yet another one this exact second. Until then, my quest for a beefy type to fit my tiny wrist will have to continue.

product_title: Remington Hunting Cleaning and Maintenance Kit
review_body:
I just got this kit, and have not yet used it. I have read the instructions, and the instructions clearly state that you need an additional product. The additional product is REMtm Action Cleaner. Now I wonder if the REMtm Action Cleaner is going to require the purchase of yet more additional products.

I would also recommend the purchase of additional REMtm All In Bore Cleaner, and Rem Oil if you plan on using this kit frequently, as the supplied .5 oz, and 1 oz containers seem very small. I would also not recommend applying the supplied Rem Oil (with Teflon) to a rifle bore, as I have heard that Teflon will impact the ballistics of a rifle, and requires multiple shots to work it's way out of the bore.

Also, I think the marketing on the angle that you reduce the need for environmentally unfriendly trash is lame. As stated in the instructions, you will need a rag, or paper towels, to wipe the residue off the apparatus, and a couple of tiny cloth patches compared to a wiping rag or two doesn't seem like a reduction. In addition, this says nothing about the chemicals themselves. The kit is supplied with a \\"yellow gun cloth\\", but I would not advise throwing it in your laundry when it becomes soiled.

..

The more I study this kit, the less impressed I become. I found a site as noted on the box, at[...] This site claims \\"Cleans in just one pass\\". Well, I don't know what they mean by \\"just one pass\\", but the instructions on the box clearly state that you need to run the brush through the bore 5 times, and then run the squeeg-e through.

The video also states that the system will clean the bore and the chamber. I'd like them to explain to me how a brush can clean a chamber that is %50 to %100 larger than the brush diameter!

I also tried to order additional cleaning compound. The only place I can find to order the compound is at [...] This site has a similar product, but I have no idea if the formulation of the compound is the same.

I called Remington, but had to leave a voice mail for them to call back.

..

No return call from Remington, but I did send them an email, and got a response. I don't know how many drops are in a half ounce, but if you use the recommended 30 to 40 drops of the cleaning solution, I can't imagine that you would get more that 5 or 6 cleaning out of the supplied solution. Then you are completely SOL, since Remington does not yet have additional cleaning solution available. I ordered some from Rogers, which I can only assume is the same stuff.

My recommendation is that you purchase the Rogers kit, and stick with Rogers supplies and instructions.ation of the compound is the same.

review_headline: Doesn't get much better (for the price)!!! TL-BP88
review_body: This review is for the UTG Tactical OP-2 Bipod (TL-BP88).  Plan and simple, I could not be any happier with this bipod!  I bought this for my S&W M&P 15-22 and it is a perfect fit with a 25-round magazine (or any full size magazine) inserted when lying in the prone.  Note, however, that when the legs are not fully extended and a full-size magazine (25-round or bigger) is inserted, the magazine will touch the ground, but once you get behind the rifle and place the stock in your shoulder everything fits fine and the mag is off the ground.  I purchased this bipod to replace a UTG Low-Profile Deluxe Universal Picatinny & Swivel-Stud Bipod (comparable size to this bipod) because I did not like the way in which the legs had to be extended and when extended, the legs were not very secure and I also didn't care for the metal feet.  This bipod cures all of the problems I faced with the previous bipod!  I cannot believe how easily the legs extend and retract - I can simply pick up my rifle with one hand, extend with the legs with my other hand and they're locked and secure.  When I want to retract the legs, I simply lift the rifle with one hand, tap the release button with my pinky and the the legs quickly retract.  The rubberized feet are also a nice addition and wont scuff up as would metal ones.  For the price, I am 100% completely satisfied with this bipod.  My only [minor] gripe is that the bipod is made in China, but I suppose I could have made the choice to buy a \\"Made in USA\\" product had I been willing to spend more money - so I will not fault the company for providing a quality product at an affordable price.  All-in-all, this is a terrific bipod and if you have a S&W M&P 15 or 15-22, this is a great addition to your rifle.

product_title: Weider Total Body Works 5000 Gym
review_headline: Weider Total Body Works 5000 Review with Resistance Ranges / Values
review_body:
The Weider Total Body Works 5000 is a great value and perfect for those with limited space. I'm used to having a full squat rack, bench, and free weights, but that setup wasn't going to fit into a small apartment. For $129, I figured I couldn't go wrong with the Total Body Works 5000. I'd used the more expensive, better known Total Gym before so I was familiar with this type of machine. The biggest limitation is the resistance system makes it very difficult to great an intense lower body workout. The machine is great for upper body, especially for shoulders, biceps, triceps, and even chest (flyes). However, for lower body exercises like squats and calf raises, it's simply not enough resistance as it uses only a percentage of body weight. For these exercises, the machine is actually limiting your workout as you can just do squats and calf raises using your full body weight. However, it's great for exercises where you might not be able to lift your full body weight for several sets/reps. For example, the attachment might enable you to perform core exercises like chin-ups and pull-ups that you might not otherwise be able to perform properly at full body weight.

I actually like the design on the Weider Total Body Works 5000 better than the Total Gym. It's easier to adjust the incline and has 4 bands for extra resistance. However, the documentation is quite limited compared to the Total Gym. I imagine it would be hard for a beginner to understand how to do the exercises given the only workout instructions is a simple poster with sample exercises. The Total Body Works is also more limited than the Total Gym-especially for exercises like leg curls and leg extensions. The attachments are not nearly as good. Finally, unlike the Total Gym, no guidelines regarding weight / percentage of body weight lifted per resistance level are provided.

The only calculation of resistance levels I've been able to find were actually on Amazon in the post by Cyclist dated March 1, 2011. Using his method, I've attempted to calculate resistance ranges by level for the machine. My body weight is higher at 220lbs, but the levels were fairly consistent as shown below. The range is set by my calculated results and those of Cyclist. The machine only has 7 levels of resistance. Although there are 8 holes for setting the incline pin, the first setting simply locks the pin / board when not in use.

Resistance Ranges by Level (% of body weight)
Level 7 _____ 55 - 56%
Level 6 _____ 50 - 51%
Level 5 _____ 45 - 47%
Level 4 _____ 37 - 40%
Level 3 _____ 33 - 35%
Level 2 _____ 26 - 27%
Level 1 _____ 15 - 18%

For under $130 though, there is nothing that's delivers as much value as the Total Body Works 5000. Highly recommended!March 1, 2011. product_title: Tri-Angle Sharpmaker
review_body:
My favorite kitchen knife is my Shun (Japanese) 7" Santoku knife that is made from a super hard, forged steel and has a 16 degree bevel on each side of the blade. It is like no other knife that I have ever used - well balanced and super sharp.

American and European made knives typically have a 20 degree bevel per side. I take pride in having sharp knives to work with and in the past have used two other sharpening systems. The Spyderco system is now my favorite and can be set up and used in the 16 and 20 degree mode. Therefore, I can use it on all of my good kitchen knives.

If you love working with a sharp edge on your knives, then I believe you will appreciate my remarks. However, I need to find a good method for cleaning the ceramic stones. Over time the recommended processes leaves a lot to be desired. I'm going to try an ultra-sonic cleaner (at work) for a 1 to 2 hour period.

I watched the provided DVD and received an education. Later, I used the system stones to sharpen scissors and a potato peeler. What a difference in the performance of the 20 year old “spud” peeler after sharpening! I hadn't realized how dull it had become. product_title: Pachmayr Slip on Grips for Auto Pistols Large-Plain Slip-On Grip
review_headline: Fits Glock 20 SF and feels great
review_body:
I picked up a Glock 20 SF (3rd Gen) as the 4th Gen Glock 20 is no where to be found and the standard size 3rd Gen Glock 20 is almost as hard to come by. No biggie, but the 3rd Gen Gen Glocks aren't that grippy, and my large hands wouldn't mind a larger grip. Alas a rubber slip on grip addresses both challenges (or rather solving the former with a happy side effect of the solving the latter).

Anyway, enough of my back story. What you get is a soft, durable (extrapolating at this point, but will update in time), grippy, solution. It is big enough for full sized (even over sized like a double stack .45acp Glock 21 or double stack 10mm Glock 20), and it's flexible enough to fit "slim" framed versions of these uber Glocks and the more typical Glock 17 et al. It's a snug fit, and there is no magic lubricant or trick--you simply have to stretch and pull. It will take 5-10 minutes, but you quickly know that it will never come off without a lot of intent (and perhaps an xacto knife for the impatient). Once on the grip will be thicker, but only by a trivial amount. If you're grip is borderline too big, it may be too much. The transition from the Pachmayr grip to your gun's standard grip is almost imperceptible to the hand, and the grips size makes it very much on the periphery. The lines also help make it fit nicely. Lastly, do note that the plain grip goes right over my Glock's finger groves, and they remain (other grips add their own fingers, which may be good or may be bad).

I definitely recommend it to 3rd Gen Glock owners, as they are a but lacking in the grip. 4th Gen Glocks also benefit, especially if you're looking for rubber vs raised plastic, although you may want to go without a back strap to make installation easier (I imagine all straps would fit with enough effort). 1911 and Springfield XD owners probably want to pass due to this likely negating any grip safety.

product_title: Hobie Call's How to Train for Obstacle Course Racing
review_headline: Insight into the strategy of the master
review_body:
First off, I received my DVD in a personally addressed mailer from Hobie which meant a lot to me. Here's a guy who is at the top of his sport and he is taking the time to address an envelope to me. I was very appreciative of this and it shows you just what kind of guy Hobie is and how sincere he is about promoting our sport.

Overview: This DVD provides you not only with specific workout guidance, but it truly gives you insight into the level of intensity, commitment, effort, and the mindset that is required to be an elite obstacle racer. Hobie addresses all aspects of obstacle racing fitness and lays out exactly how he does it regarding nutrition, warmup, running, and upper body work. He delivers his advice in his straight-forward, no-frills, Hobie Call way - and then he puts on the weight vest and shows you how it's done. When you watch the video for the first time, you'll be incredulous at his level of endurance - a Navy Seal has nothing on this guy. From the warm-up through the absolutely insane upper body workout it becomes clear why Hobie is the best in the business. This DVD is geared for the advanced athlete, but Hobie addresses the beginner athlete and refers them to his website whereby they can modify certain moves and work toward improvement. I've been training seriously for obstacle racing for a year now by doing P90X, Insanity, obstacle related workouts, and marathon training but this DVD takes things to another level. It brought clarity to me in that I now realize I'm nowhere near elite status, but I'm encouraged by the fact that I now have an additional set of tools and guidance to help me get there.

Many thanks to Hobie for sharing the secrets of his success with the rest of us! Aroo!

product_title: 1210503 Out 28-pc Uni Gun Wd Clean Box
review_headline: I had some issues, but it does what it's supposed to.
review_body:
Right from the start, I opened the box to find that the handle for the cleaning rod was already broken off. That aside, the rod seems a little flimsy, but I was able to clean my guns with it without too many issues, it was a lot sturdier than I thought it would be. However, when attaching the adapter for using the shotgun brushes, the whole assembly feels a little wobbly. Again though, I was able to use it to clean my shotgun without any issues. The pick feels flimsy, I didn't use it in fear that I would break it.

Everything else performed just about as well as you would expect any other tool of its type to perform. I already had patches that I use for cleaning my guns, so I didn't use the cleaning patches that are included with the kit, so I can't say whether those are any good or not. The brush, is a brush, and it performs as you would expect from a brush. The jags work as you would expect, as do the patch loops.

Overall, the kit is pretty good, and aside from the broken handle (which I plan to fix with some epoxy), I would say it's worth a look. Again, it's not perfect, and the reason I didn't give it a higher rating is that the broken handle severely hinders the ability to use the kit effectively. With all the padding inside the box for all the tools, I would find it hard to believe that this could have occurred during shipping, so I am going to proceed under the assumption that this piece was broken from the factory. I feel that if Outers put a little more effort into the construction, and overall quality of these kits, it could easily gain a 5 star rating from me.

UPDATE: 3/15/2013
I contacted Outers about the handle, and they sent me a new one. Good customer service.

review_body:
This knife rocks! I owned the old Endura 98, with the molded plastic clip. In a couple of years it broke off, and soon after I lost it. I went through a series of blades of various manufacturers, all nice, but none ever measured up.
Enter the Endura 4 with the Wave! Totally redesigned with better steel, upgraded handle, and the wave.
* Pick it up, it feels like a tool. Edges are rounded and smooth, but the scales have a just rough enough texture for a fine grip.
* Open it, it opens nice and smoothly. No side play.
* Cut with it, ohhh so very sharp!
* Put it in your pocket, it sits nicely, and with the wave it opens itself on your pocket as you remove it.

I couldn't be happier. One caviat...Don't take it apart to clean it! It has some internal tension that won't allow you to reassemble it, and you'll have to send it back to Spyderco with a $20.00 check. (Ask me how I know.)
Several friends of mind have bought one after using mine for a task of some sort, and it's my default gift for man presents. I have many other knives, Benchmade, Kershaw, Gerber, Cold Steel, CRKT...all nice knives, but this one is by far my favorite for daily carry. I feel naked without it.

I researched knee braces online and initially tried the medium Shock Doctor Knee Support with Dual Hinges. When it arrived I could not get it past my ankle. I am 5'9\\" and weigh 180. I then ordered the large after calling Shock Doctor (the company) for help with sizing. When this arrived I could only get it onto my knee with a lot of force and then it was so tight around the calf that it was painful after 5 minutes. My 5'4\\" 120 lb wife could not get the medium past her calf and the large fit her. Both times Amazon let me return it with no problem. (kudos to Amazon)

I then showed the Shock Doctor Ultra Knee Supporter with Bilateral Hinges to my brother who is a hand surgeon and he thought this looked like it would have more support. I ordered the large and it fit perfectly. It is also much easier to adjust the straps than the less expensive one. My only gripe is if I use it for biking or Pilates the extra x strap on the back digs into the back of my knee a little. When I use it for tennis or golf I find it gives excellent support and is very comfortable. This one is only about $14 more than the other one and is more comfortable, has more support, is easier to adjust the straps and has a more realistic size.

product_title: Pulse R76 Airsoft Rifle
review_body:
Okay so I usually buy my airsoft guns from Airsoft GI or other professional stores. But this being my first AEG I bought it at walmart... Judge me if you will. BUT this gun has surpassed all of my expectations! Usually Crosman does not come out with high quality Airsoft weapons but this has been a keeper through and through. It has a full metal V1 gearbox and most of the gun is metal or a VERY high quality synthetic. it's sleek, dependable, and very easy to fix if it has issues of any kind. I bought two so I could give one to my brother and his had a sparking issue but ALL you had to do was unscrew the handle and use an allen wrench to tighten the gears which took no time at all. The gun fires about 370-400 fps and is accurate up to about 120 ft in my case, which is fantastic for such a low price gun. It is decently accurate despite the shorter barrel. The magazine is extremely hi-cap at about 490+ rounds and I rarely if ever have to wind it. the hop up is easy to adjust. And this gun has a good front rubbery RIS system. It has a front and rear sling attachment points which is yet another plus! SO.

Pros:
Metal body & gearbox
Good ROF
Great FPS 375+ w/ .20
Hi-Cap Magazine
Durable and easy to fix
Front RIS system
front and rear sling points.

Now for the CONs. The full stock is a cheap plastic which differs from the body. So I'm not sure why they did that but the plate on the back falls off often. The rail system for the optics is very wobbly and i would not put a scope of any kind on simply because it would do no good. The front sights are good but the rear sights are difficult to use with the optic RIS in the way. So if you find a way to remove it I would personally do so. Other than that I can find no real CONs to this gun. SO.

Cons:
Cheap plastic full stock that falls apart
Wobbly optic rail system
Difficult to use front and rear sights
In rare occasions gears come loose

I hope this was helpful!

product_title: Radians Custom Molded Earplugs - Tan
review_body: Despite the various reviews that say they couldn't get the materials to form properly I've been through five different batches of these and every time they form perfectly, as long as you follow the simple instructions. I've split the material in half to create two sets of ear plugs and also used exactly as directed and formed one set of ear plugs. The problem is why would you want these custom molded plugs. There are several very nice soft - reusable plugs that provide greater NRR (Noise Reduction Rating) than these, and they are very inexpensive, and fit every ear canal. I've purchased seven different brands of reusable plugs [NOT the disposable kind that come in large numbers to a box or tube] that run between $1.50 and $2.00. They all worked very well, blocked out all the noise, some were a bit softer on my ears than others. These Radians however, don't have nearly the NRR rating. You'll pay $15 to $20 for these, shipping included. Go to any major shoot and you can get custom made on-site, by a professional, for $50. Save your money, go with the reusable ones, and then get to a shoot and splurge a little. You'll be much happier.

product_title: Smooth Fitness CE-3.6 Elliptical Trainer
review_body:
I have waited for a review, to be able to use the eliptical at least 20 times to form an opinion. My first smooth I received had the whole plastic shell on the rear of the unit broken in multiple places. The shell covers the flywheel and has weak ponts where the screws secure the plastic to the frame of the unit. Amazon handled the shipping mishap and sent a second unit. Upon arrival of the second unit I went thru all the packaging before the delivery man left. I found one screw attachment broken, and decided to just accept it, and fix it with epoxy.
Now we will get into use of the item. After the second use two of the main bolts that hold the frame together began to loosen. I replaced the nuts with ones with nylon washers so they can't back out. After about the 10th use one of the footrests became completely loose, another bolt had worked itself out during use. After this I got a tube of locktite and applied it to all the screws. 10 more uses of 45 min + and everything is finally solid! The frame is heavy and is in turn stable. The flywheel and pivoting footrests create an excellent motion that is at least as good as the precors at the gym. So after tightening all the loose parts the overall unit is good, I just can't give better than 3 stars because there is room for improvement. Apply the locktite as you assemble and you'll have a 5 star unit, as long as the cheap plastic screw conections aren't broken on arrival

product_title: Kwik Goal Premier Referee Jersey
review_headline: Exactly as I expected, professional looking.
review_body:
This review is for the green, adult medium option.

I'm definitely happy with the shirt - it looks professional, fits well (true to size, generally), seems to be high quality, and fairly comfortable. Most importantly, it works just as well as the "designated" referee shirts you can buy through the USSF for around $50.

This is my third shirt bought from Amazon - black, blue, and now green. I bought my "official" yellow ref shirt through the USSF, costing my over $40 and not being any better than the ones I bought from Amazon. I've read about some complaints about the yellow jerseys here being more "school-bus yellow" and I honestly can't say either way. If you're looking for a yellow jersey, I'd be careful - it seems like quite a few people complain about the color of the yellow model. But the three colors I've bought (black, blue, green; various sizes) have all been true to size and color.

I've used the other two for a few years now, and the green I'll start to use this spring. So far, I've had no problems with wearing down, etc. - they seem to be very high quality, from what I can tell. I especially love the velcro pocket over the front pockets on either side - they keep pens, paper, etc. from falling out as you run and look very professional.

Very satisfied with my purchases. I'll probably be back when I need a red jersey next! I'd still be a little cautious with the yellow model from reading other reviews, but all the colors I've purchased have been great. Especially for the price, these are great - I find no difference in professional look from my black, blue and green jerseys bought on Amazon for ~$20 vs. the yellow USSF jersey for over $40.

product_title: Slendertone 7 Program Abdominal Muscle Toning Belt (Unisex)
review_headline: Opinion of a senior, overweight, citizen
review_body:
Don't let all these trim young people write us older, even overweight, people off when it comes to using this tool.

I have been using it for only a week. Nevertheless I may still have something to offer to others like myself who are curious and hopeful.

Principle One:
I understand that the belt will not remove layers of fat from the belly, which are covering the muscles underneath. I fully know that only exercise which causes the body to burn more calories, along with dietary practices, will get rid of the ugly and jiggly belly fat. Diet and exercise are necessary parts of getting in good shape, healthy, and MUST be done, totally apart from toning. This appliance will only wake up and strengthen muscles underneath the fat. Fat cannot be toned, or forced to change into muscle. Fat and muscle cells are as different from each other as toenails are from eyeballs. Muscles will never become fat, but they do atrophy. And fat will never become muscle. If you're going to buy this appliance, you absolutely HAVE to understand this principle.

My story:
In my case, I need to lose fifty pounds on my 5' 5\\" frame. I'm active, but in poor shape. A month ago our son gave us an Aria computerized scale for Christmas, knowing Hubby and I were trying to get in better shape. Our son has one, in addition to the FitBit and has lost 60 lbs with these aids, in a year. So, since we now own the fancy scale, I bought my own FitBit to go with it. I have been using the two together for a couple of weeks, faithfully. I know this is not a review of either the FitBit, or the Aria, but since they are part of my journey,I cannot legitimately review one without the other and still give an honest review.

Since Christmas, I have been losing 1.4 lbs a week with these tools. For my personality the FitBit and Aria are wonderful motivators. I can see exactly what I still need to do every day. I'll post reviews about those tools, separately, under their descriptions if you are curious about them.

As I lose the weight and fat, the flabby muscles under my top layers of fat will need attention, too. The trouble is, I quickly realized my muscles are weak from lack of use, almost as if they've gone to sleep and I have trouble getting them to work again.

I figure that as the fat goes away and my core is exposed I will look better, sooner, if I begin now to strengthen my abdominal muscles. Besides, strengthening muscles might help increase metabolism a little. This is why I decided to include the Slendertone, to give some help.

A week into using the Slendertone, even though I have much work left to do, I fully believe the Slendertone belt is going to be worth the investment.

After decades that included four pregnancies, the business of raising a family to the exclusion of exercise, working outside the home, a careless diet, and almost 30 years years of artificial hormone replacement after hysterectomy and removal of ovaries ... I finally looked at myself in the mirror was dismayed to discover I had gotten older. AND fat.

This is where the Slendertone comes in. Without the Slendertone I seem unable to isolate muscles to exercise abdominal muscles. The Slendertone seems to \\"wake up\\" the sleeping muscles. Without it, my body did not seem able to figure out how to make the muscles respond. With it I can \\"find\\" them to force them to work out. I also have a back problem. Use of the Slendertone protects my back.

I do not not just wear the Slendertone:
I don't wear it, then go about other activities, expecting the unit to do all the work. I don't seem to get the same result if I do that. When using it, I am fully engaged in the process and fully focused. I watch my belly while I use it. I pay attention to how it feels and assist the appliance so I can teach my muscles to respond. By paying attention to what it's trying to do for me I believe I'm getting a much better workout. By focusing on the 'exercise' while I'm exercising, I can make the muscles move \\"me\\" under my fatty top layer in a way that I can see. When I only wear the unit, expecting it to do all the work for me, I don't see, or feel, deep movement -- only strong tingling.

When I started a week ago, I could not tell anything was happening apart from what the Slendertone felt like when it pulsed. Today I can feel muscles working, and can see movement caused by muscle contraction.

It's been a week. I can report a subtle difference in the appearance of my belly. Of course it's too early to appear trim or toned. But I see slight change. Perhaps it's partly due to posture. I am feeling a tightening in my abdomen that has been long-forgotten, but I recognize the sensation again. I notice the deep tightening stays with me during the day, reminding me to contract and stand straighter, so my clothes drape in a different way.

I still have a very long way to go. But as the weight comes off -- and I know it will -- and my then-strengthened-core is exposed with the help of the Slendertone I am confident that this granny is going to get some years back. :-)

Would I recommend it? Well, yes ... and no.

If you buy it, thinking it will make you slim and take away your flabby and fat middle -- no, I absolutely would not recommend you waste your money.

However, if you get it with realistic expectations of what it is designed to do and what it isn't, then, yes I do. If you're willing to diet and exercise, too, and are willing to work at your goal -- not expecting a magic machine to do it for you, yes. Incorporate this tool, along with the other weapons and determination and I do believe it will help restore fitness. No matter your age.

It's early for me on this Slendertone journey to provide final results, as I said, but even now along with my FitBit and Aria tools, and careful diet practices, I'm surprised to say I'm noticing results in a couple of weeks -- seen only to me so far, but they are tangible, nonetheless.

When my top layers of fat disappear, I plan to have a strong under layer of muscle that will be ready for the 'reveal'.

Contrary to another opinion, I don't believe you have to already be \\"one of the beautiful people\\" for this to be a helpful tool.

* great price
* doesn't take up much space - i've never bothered to fold it up.
* doesn't require power - it can be used even if you don't put batteries in the computer monitor thing.
* offers plenty of resistance. i've used it for faster rowing (for cardio) at lower settings, and i've cranked it up to level 9 for a harder workout. there's a definite difference, and you'll feel it.

cons:
* the pedals are worthless. i removed them, and just stick my toes under the bar.
* the rower arms are a bit creaky during use. is a bit annoying, but performance is not affected.
* the computer monitor thing is kind of useless, other than when using it as a timer.

all in all, i'm REALLY glad i took a gamble & made this purchase. provides a great workout, without any impact.

product_title: Scuba Yoke Adaptor For Benjamin/Crosman PCP Airguns
review_body:
This is a very simple accessory to use on any Crosman PCP rifle or pistol... virtually all of them work with this setup and your favorite SCUBA tank, preferably made of aluminum alloy with a K-type Valve assembly. I thought that the K-Valve hose fitting off the yoke assembly matched up with the tank's \\"K-type\\" valve perfectly, and I had an instant fill up in my Marauder 25-Caliber Rifle. Actual time it took was about 20 seconds, ie to see the gauge on the bottom of my rifle, and the one on the fill-up valve, to read \\"3 Atmospheres\\" and promptly STOP there, all by itself.

Turns out that when the atmospheres of the source and the object that's being filled up are the same, that parity is reached quickly, and safely: the fill up stops at just less than 3 Atmospheres, and will not budge from there, without fail. I filled up my Marauder rifle and the Marauder 22-Caliber pistol at will, a dozen or more times per weapon, when I went shooting recently, and it worked exactly the same each and every time!

The PCP fill-up valve is handsomely either stainless steel or heavily chrome plated (I couldn't tell which it is), giving most of the assembly but for the black, krinkle-finished top (head of the valve) portion--it's 100% black and contrasts 100% with the fill valve and the rest of the assembly, which is either black metal or unpolished metal, your pick. Just the top of the valve assembly in the Crosman \\"kit\\" for K-style valves and tank assemblies is bare, or unfinished metal composition. The rest is chromed, polished stainless steel, or a combination of those surfaces and finishes//it looks GREAT! I haven't seen a lot of other tanks and valve kits at the shooting club yet, but I'm sure they all are NOT as nicely done as the Crosman \\"kit\\". If they are, then I'm dumb and need a refresher course in humility until proven otherwise I guess, Hah!

All in all I rated this K-type valve compatible yoke and filling assembly 5 stars, both for shipping ease from Amazon.com (my PRIME account), and the quality of the product and its great looks, out of the box. If you have a Crosman PCP rifle or pistol and it's qualified to use a system like this, your effort at the shoot, be it a club, outdoor recreational facility for shooting, an indoor facility (like mine is), I think your shooting is bound to take up a high-line for ease of effort compared to the hand pump alternative. A setup like this, for me, is the answer for my PCP weapons, and I won't be going back to the high pressure Crosman pump unless it's an emergency, my PCP system for fill ups fails for some reason, and/or any similar circumstance.

As-is, it's the cat's meow for shooting a PCP pistol or rifle, this Crosman \\"kit\\"--the yoke and fill valve system for any PCP rifle qualified by Crosman to use it. Cost is a trifle thing to consider when you think of all the hours of pumping it will take with a qualified hand pump to achieve essentially the same results...it's just simply back breaking work if you were to ask my opinion!

Even with the cons, I give it a 5 for longevity and accuracy. It does what I need it to do.

product_title: Magpul CTR Mil-Spec Carb Stock, Black
review_body:
I'm really not sure how people don't give this stock a 5 star rating. After reading some of the other reviews, its apparent that some people just don't read the product description carefully. This stock is amazing....plain and simple. After researching more than several stocks in catalogs and online, this is the one that everyone has great praise and reviews on, and this is why....

First, its specifications, are spot on.... I have a "mil-spec" AR, and there were no fitment issues at all, as some of the other reviews may speculate. There was a super tight fit even without using the extra locking mechanism. And after the secondary locking mechanism is used, there is no movement of the stock, at all, and is extremely secure in its position. I even gave it a few hard tugs in all directions, and no movement, where my original stock had some "movement/play/rattle" as most of you probably have also. Someone posted a review on how he didn't know what the measurements were... well, that speaks for itself, meaning that he probably doesn't know much about AR type weapon systems, because you should at least know the basics of whether or not you have a mil-spec or commercial type set up. So please check what type of buffer tube/stock you will need, so you don't order the wrong one.

In addition, the finish.... or small details of this stock are great as well. No rough edges, blemishes, or anything else that may hinder operation or comestic look. Another thing to consider, is please read the description... you don't get a buffer tube with this purchase. I read a review on someone complaining about not getting a buffer tube with his purchase. No where in the product description or even picture shows a buffer tube. And as far as price goes.... well people, sometimes you get what you pay for, and sometimes you don't. Flat ground profile makes the colt steel better at food prepping and similar low intensity tasks around camp better than my ax-ground falkniven, however it comes in second at chopping and batoning firewood.

Do keep in mind that it having high carbon steel as the blade material requires more upkeep in the form of moisture management and proper oiling in order to keep rust off than more corrosion-resistant steels. I can't comment on the edge retention as it hasn't been used that much yet. The one I bought on Amazon came with a plastic (kydex? zytel?) sheath which I prefer to any leather sheath. product_title: Advanced Technology Sks Pro Stk & Alum Upgrade Pkg - A.2.10.1110
review_headline: Serious shooters may need to modify pistol grip to make it more solid
review_body:
First of all I would like to say the aluminum upgrade is a must on this product if you are a serious shooter.
The product overall is ok considering the reasonable price. I did however have to make some modifications to it to suit my needs. The screw that holds the pistol grip seems to be very undersized. My grip loosened up and the screw eventually stripped out being that it is only a self tapping screw in plastic. It don't help the grip has to be taken off to take down the rifle. I fixed this by drilling a slightly larger hole and adding a larger screw. Grip is now secure I just hope it stayes that way or I will have to find a more permanent solution. I would have gave it a 5 star rating if ATI wasn't lacking in this critical area.

I am impressed with the folding stock. When extended it is very solid. It does however have a small amount of play when in the folded position which is not a huge deal.

Installation does require some basic skills such as filing and sanding to fit the stock to your rifle. I used a dremel which sped up the process. Just be careful not to take off too much at a time. Remove a small amount of material and test fit. The hardest part was removing the old fore end from the gas tube but is possible with the right tools.

If you are just looking for something to look good and shoot on occasion this is for you. Put it together and your good to go.

If you are a serious shooter and want 100% reliability from your rifle I would not recoment this unless you are willing to address the issue with the pistol grip. My next stelp is to make a tool to fit up in the bottom of the pistol grip that will allow me to reach the take down button without removing the pistol grip. This will require some drilling and grinding to the inside of the grip which is hollow. I will then permently mount the grip using JB Weld and the larger screw that I already installed. I believe this will give me the 5 star product I was looking for. If you are good with your hands don't be afraid to buy this and make a few modifications. ATI would have an excellent product here if it were a little more sturdy out of the box.

Yes, I said Trijicon, even though they aren't advertised as being from the same company that's responsible for ACOGs, these are made to accomodate their Accupoint line of zoom optics. product_title: Hoppe's Elite Bore Gel
review_body: I've use Hoppe's #9 all my life, but I thought I'd try this. I put it in the barrel of a Ruger P89 that I've shot frequently for a number of years, and let it sit overnight. Got big green streaks on about six patches. I ran dry patches through, and put it back together. Thought about it for a while, and put it in the barrel again, and again got those green streaks. That, of course, is copper fouling. I had to do that three or four more times before the copper was gone. Repeated that through my other firearms with the same result. I'll probably change to CLP for the general cleaning (based on a recommendation in a Patrick Sweeney book), but this stuff is the real deal. Buy it and use it. There are probably other copper solvents that do as well, but my old habits cause me to trust Hoppe's. Don't depend on regular cleaners. You really need a copper solvent for your bore cleaning. This works.

product_title: Pro-Tec Athletics The Y Roller Contoured Foam Roller
review_headline: Ridges let you pinpoint where the pressure goes
review_body: I received this through the Amazon Vine program.  I have a tight lower back -- very slight scoliosis and I probably contribute to my own lower back pain  by doing too much ab work at the gym.  My back pain is not severe but consistently annoying.  I have used plain styrofoam rollers and I feel that by comparison the Y roller is advantaged because as you roll it you change the place where the raised ridge meets your back.  So you can customize it to get the pressure exactly where you want it.  I am a small person so this really works well.  I do find that I am most comfortable using it right through a down sweater.  It can be too painful when not somewhat insulated -- but you can control this with your clothing.  I would think it would be more painful for a larger person who puts more weight down on to it.  I found that it really did release some of the tightness even the very first time I used it for a couple of minutes.  You can feel the tightness having dissipated right away.  It is definitely more effective (because more precise) than the plain foam roller and a lot easier to control the pressure points than using a tennis ball.
