review_headline: Not Quite Ready Out of the Box
review_body: I have several Zero Tolerance knives and this knife well made just as the others. The reason I say is that is not ready out of the box is that tension on the lock bar or I guess it's the liner is so tight that it is very hard to deploy the blade. Once you've managed to get the blade out, mine was impossible to release the blade. I read that there is a break-in period, so I kept working it put after hours of opening and closing, it was no better. I also read that if you put some pencil lead on the two contact surfaces that it would help the problem. No such luck. I took the knife completely apart, cleaned an lubed it and no improvement. It was so hard to release the blade that with the knife on my bench using both hands I could not get it to release. The only way to free it up was to put a screwdriver with tape on it in the knife and gently pry it open and even that took a lot of pressure. I slowly tweaked the locking mechanism to lessen the force so the the lock did not go almost 100% under the blade. It now goes about 50% under the blade and it works fine. Other than this problem I really like the knife and carry it every day. It seems to me that for this caliber and price of knife it should work right out of the box with out having to make adjustments to it in order to make it function properly. I know I could have sent it to Kershaw and they would have fixed it but who wants to do that?

product_title: Winchester 22-41206 Large Bowie Knife (8.57-Inch)
review_headline: A review after being used heavily for 7 months
review_body:
While this review may seem negative, i'm going to preface it by saying that i LOVE this knife. And i heavily used it for 7 months. Since the day it came in the mail it has been my favorite knife. It may be because i love larger knives, and this is the first one i have owned. But just the feel and weight(And the durability of it) has been great. It has survived countless chopped branches, saplings, and even a couple logs. I actually chose this over my axe and machete on multiple occasions while back in the woods. It doesn't hold an edge to an amazing degree, but that is to be expected with any 20 dollar knife. But it HAS survived countless re-sharpenings. And if you know what you're doing, you can put a beastly edge on this baby.
As far as the sheath goes, it's the highest-quality sheath I've seen for a low-cost knife. The part that houses the actual blade is solid plastic. Then that is wrapped by flexible plastic, and lastly it is wrapped in nylon. The duel straps are amazing, and make it feel very sturdy when it's strapped in the sheath. My only complaint with the sheath is that the belt loop is so huge. The actual sheath hangs at least 3 inches bellow your belt. I wish it was a smaller loop so the knife was up more, but it's a minor complaint.
Additionally, this knife is branded Winchester but from what I've heard, it's actually manufactured by Gerber Gear. So, if you have any opinion on Gerber, take that for what you will. The blade has no markings as to where it was made, but i would imagine Pakistan or China, as that's where the bulk of cheap knives are made.
However, it is NOT FULL TANG CONSTRUCTION like it says in the description!!(See the customer images i uploaded to fully understand why it isn't full tang) That is my biggest disappointment, mainly because it's false advertising. You run into this problem with a lot of knives, more in particular the larger ones because that's when tang becomes an issue; Between all the hacking, cutting and slashing. So be sure to check reviews on any knife!!
I found this out by(admittedly) being stupid with it, and practicing knife throwing with it. This is why i still give the knife 4 stars, because i doubt this knife will give out on you unless you're doing something equally as stupid. The butt end of the knife hit the board i was using as a target and it shatter into 3 pieces. One of them still being attached to the knife(see the customer images i uploaded and their notes).
However, this was easily fixed with a bottle of gorilla glue and wrapping the handle with electrical tape(Some may think this looks ugly, but personally i like the worn and used look it gives it). And i'd say overall the knife is more durable now since the gaps between the handle and the tang are filled with gorilla glue foam to absorb vibration. I'll still be using it ALL the time, and it'll still be my favorite knife. I may pick up the limited edition Winchester Bowie for light use and for a sort-of display piece(Simply because i like Winchester knives. Even if they're not made by Winchester themselves. The style is great).

product_title: Buff Denim (Wool Buff) - AW15
review_body:
Got this for some recently skiing. At first I thought it was a little itchy but lately I don't even notice it anymore. Smells great, doesn't stink even after I am using it as a balaclava and breathing through it.

Buff likes to advertise the dozens of ways to wear this thing- really, all I've seen useful to me is : scarf, balaclava, beanie, headband - that's plenty for me though. Could also double as a weak towel or tied into a bag - cut and used as rope possibly for nothing serious.

I noticed some other reviews stated that the wool version isn't as \\"tight\\" as the regular version so they couldn't get the balaclava to work - worked for me personally. I do have a larger size head though but having said that, I found the trick is to pull the Buff completely up over your crown and pull the fabric so that the rear side drapes completely over the top of your forehead. Then grab the fabric on a horizontal line around where your adam's apple is or would be if you are a lady - pull this fabric away from your neck while stuffing the front fabric down towards your chin. Using your fingers, work the remaining fabric between your face and the fold you are creating - pretty impossible to describe I guess, but it worked for me.

Personally I wish it was a tad thicker for more warm but I take it this is meant to go from cold to hot so they are keeping it thin for if you want to use it just as a Sun blocker.

Used as a scarf, it's not as toasty as a plain acrylic scarf, but it's versatility and ease of use [much easier to pull this thing over your neck than to tie a scarf, though not by much admittedly] makes up for it.

Overall, if it's really cold, less than 50 degrees, I would still go with a scarf [or the beefier Buff versions!!!] unless you are being active - but again the core feature here is it's versatility across different temps and environments.

OK, here we go -- the most common complaint is the on/off switch mechanism or the light coming on or going off when 'it' wants to versus the user doing the on/off switching! Here's the thing, while the on/off switch is simple in design, 'generally', I say 'generally', unless the switch is totally free floating and doesn't seem to do anything in terms of clicking into the on or off position but with such a 'click' that you can only discern with your fingers, you should additionally look elsewhere for the \\"culprit\\" if the light refuses to do anything. Enter what I termed the \\"quirks\\" of this light. NOTE firstly that you can easily check whether the battery is good with a simple meter test and then if you see an 'impression' of the light cap mini-coiled cap spring on the 'negative' side of the battery [positive side of the battery going into the light first], this 'tells' you that the mini-coiled spring device in the battery cap is in fact making good contact and working! Yes, it's always possible that the switch is defective or, indeed, even the light element itself may be defective but the probability is small on that because these lights are checked beforehand but in shipping the lights, things can happen. Now, and that said, here's the place to check -- the == FRONT part of the light == which also screws in and comes screwed in ==but== in now 3 cases [one of my own lights and 2 of an airgun hobbyist friend's lights of the same brand and model], the \\"culprit\\" was the FRONT part of the light! The price is right and with Prime free shipping, it's an excellent deal. product_title: SPRI Step 360 Pro
review_headline: A great blend of a step platform and a bosu!
review_body:
Since I already have multiple step platforms and a bosu, I didn't think I really needed yet another piece of bulky equipment. However after getting this for a Christmas present I realized this is the best of both worlds! Unlike the bosu you have a larger/wider area in which to step upon. It was always hard for me to use my bosu with my tennis shoes bc I felt I needed more grip from my toes and feet to make it work. I certainlt would wobble, but a little too much so I stopped using it. Since I purchased the bosu to de weight and strength work, it didn't get much use since it was too hard to concentrate on proper lifting form and balance. The step benches are perfect for strength work but they don't give you the balance challenge for functional fitness. The Step360 does!

I have started to use this with Cathe Friedrich's weight workouts (an advanced level so preview clips before purchase- these are much more advanced than the DVDs that come with the 360). Because of knee issues and prior surgeries I am unable to do tall step climbs/Leg presses anymore. Yet I still need and want to work the \\"thutt\\" area- that place where the butt and thigh meet. I also want to work my stabilizers and strengthen them as I am an avid walker and I want to now get involved with 5 and 10ks. This piece of equipment is allowing me to train the lower body in the way I want. I also lose how I connect a band to the platform for added resistance if I don't want to use dumbbells. If you want less wobble inflate it to the max safety point. If you want more challenge, let some of the air out. It's as simple as that. The platform as had a foam pad on top which helps keep you from slipping. I don't sit on the platform for upper body work, I still prefer my bosu and stability balls for that; it's more comfortable and I can get the angles I need a lot easier.

The cons IMO are:
1. The DVDs. I have the Deluxe upgrade DVDs from it was first released via informercial in 2010. I donot like Jesse, the male instructor; he gets on my last nerve so much so that I've only used 2 of the workouts. The workouts are short (a pro in my book) but there are an't many workouts included in the set without the upgrade which is no longer available.

2. The air chambers leak. Not badly, but every couple of weeks (I use this 1-2x per week) I need to add a little air as it gets too low for my liking. Letting some air out adds to the challenge but if too much air escapes then the challenge goes away completely.

Is it worth the money? That depends on what you will use it for and how often. I didn't use this for about 18 months and would have said it's a waste of $$$. But now that I use it, my bosu rarely gets touched. I also like it a lot more than a high step for 1 legged work and step ups. If you are looking to purchase it for that New Year's Resolution then I would pass. It's quite bulky and heavy and takes up a lot of space both inflated and deflated. The DVDs IMO are not worth the money and I wouldn't recommend them to anyone but beginners. Major boredom factor with them.

review_headline: Be careful who you buy this from. Read below.

Be careful who you but this hat from. I bought one black hat and one tan hat. I did not realize that they were being shipped and sold from two different companies.

The first one that arrived was the tan one sold and shipped from Tapp Collections. This one looked like a cheap Chinese knock off of a Chinese knockoff. The material was thinner than the old summer rip-stop cammies I used to wear. The Velcro stitching looks like it will come loose soon. The Velcro also looked like it was the last bit on the roll. There is a 1/4 inch strip that runs around two sides of it that has no loop fastener. This was a really bad hat. I didn't mind because it was going to be a back up hat that I kept in my SUV and it was cheap.

The black hat arrived two day later and was sold and shipped from BIGFLYSPORTS. To my surprise this one was in way better condition. It almost looked like a completely different company made it. It was made of material that was as thick as a normal baseball hat. The Velcro was sewn on a lot better. I believe that this will last a lot longer that the tan one.

Also, the tan hat arrived without any identifying tags on it. The black one had two tags on it identifying it as a Rothco product. Maybe the tan one was a counterfeit. I don't know. I would recommend using BIGFLYSPORTS instead of Tapp Collections.

product_title: Presto Pen Gun Blue Touch Up Birchwood Casey 13201
review_headline: Great For Some Purposes, Have Realistic Expectations
review_body:
First off it's meant for carbon steel. A lot of gun metal these days is stainless so keep that in mind.

Beyond that it can be great. On dark blue/black finishes it does a great job at taking care of scratches. FOLLOW THE DIRECTIONS on the pen. If you just apply it and let it sit it will look noticeably different than the surrounding area. Make sure to rinse and then rub to help blend. Be as precise as possible to only treat the affected area as spreading it all over will just make other areas noticeably darker. After you're done I like to treat the area with an oiled cloth. This helps to blend in the color with the surroundings by adding a sheen.

While great on scratches, if you're talking a splotch or a small area it won't be nearly as effective and blending can be a serious pain. Be realistic about what it can do, it's just a pen. Also, if you're talking about an aluminum lower or similar piece it would be best to use one of the Black pens.

I had to wipe the outside of the lens but there was virtually no fogging on the inside of the scope. My 3-9 power Leupold scope did the same. I have only had the scope a little more than a month so only rounds fired while mounted on a semi auto and bouncing around in my UTV tell how rugged it is. product_title: XMark Adjustable Speed Bag Platform XM-2811
review_headline: Solid construction, high quality, easily changes height
review_body:
It's always a bit of a coin toss to see reviews and a product description, and then order a product without seeing it. And I wasn't thrilled at the prospect of paying $57 just to ship this back if it was a bust ... But this choice was a winner.
Heavy steel, continuous welds (not spot welding) across the connecting pieces. Well designed to mount on wall studs, with brackets already placed 16" on center. Plastic and steel washers with easy to turn screws hold the platform at the height you choose. Locks in place easily and securely. When you loosen the screws to adjust the height, the platform doesn't fall on your head ... you have to maneuver it so it's completely parallel to the floor to let it slide down.
I'm not a boxer, and I use this for cross training, so I can't compare this to a "professional" platform, but in the past I had used lower quality platforms -- with great disappointment -- and this is clearly superior. I can still say that the platform does not shake when the speed bag is bouncing, so the return is consistent. No adding bags of sand on top of the platform to stabilize it, as others had written in their evaluation of competing platforms. Being happy with how it performs makes it more likely you'll actually keep using it to train with a speed bag, rather than to hang your clothes ...
Note: there are no instructions with this unit. Just the parts. And it's heavy -- 40+ pounds -- and unwieldy. I had a carpenter install it ... well worth the cost of one hour of labor to have him put it in. (By the way, he's 180 pounds and did a pull up off the end of the platform after installing it to show how solidly it was fixed to the wall...)

product_title: RS800CX Multi Sport Heart Rate Monitor w/ G3 GPS Sensor - Unisex
review_body:
Wow...I'm disappointed in the RS800CX. First of all...a word or two about me.. I'm in my 50s...and pretty active.. I bike 2000 miles a year, I rock climb, hike, snowboard and am a bit of a gym rat with spin classes, body pump..what have you. I own a Polar 720i which I liked because it did a nice job tracking my heartrate, had an IR link and also kept track of altitude and vertical distance which was great for bike riding, hiking and climbing. I also loved the fact that my heart transmitter would sync to all kinds of gym equipment such as treadmills, stair climbers etc...anything that was wired for Polar. What I hoped for was a watch that incorporated new technology and was a better version of the 720i....There are some benefits to this new watch..

The Menu structure is pretty well organized.
The Transmitter strap is even softer and more comfortable than my last one
There are certain modalities such as altitude, Heart rate etc which automatically bring multiple data items related to this mode into the screen view
You can view your HR as an absolute and also as a %Max which is nice for spin classes and other forms of HR training

Sounds good right?...here is where the rubs come in.

1) Polar chose a completely sub standard display technology which is readable in perfect lighting...but the low contrast ratio and highly reflective plastic housing make it almost impossible to read the new smaller print indoors, while in a dimly lit spin class or on a quick glance...My 720i, now 5 years old has a much, much better display in terms of readability...this is my biggest gripe

2)The watch strap is kind of short...if you are slight, it may not be a problem but it is much shorter than my 720I and I can barely engage a single hole in the watch strap. I was middle of the strap on my last watch

3) The nice new transmitter is NOT recognized by all the gym equipment that is supposed to recognize polar....Whatwere they thinking? Also...if you have other transmitters...including some of the very latest ones...they won't work with the RS800CX either.

4) They have all of this fancy software but not a lick of it works with a MAC computer...maybe not a big deal to some people but a real bummer if you own a MAC..no ability to get the nice analysis software to work on your computer.

So...POLAR knows HR monitoring but they made a number of cheapskate moves on the design of the watch/monitor and a number of careless choices on the design which leave me as a consumer feeling like I should have gone with Garmin. They also basically say that the minute you open the box, you own the watch...not very consumer friendly.

So...if you are petite, have the eyes of a 20 year old, are a PC user, only run outside and live in Phoenix and this is your first POLAR product you might be happy. If you don't meet this description...do yourself a favor and get a good look at this product in a store before you buy it....

product_title: Magpul iPhone 4/4S Field Case, Black, MAG451BLK
review_headline: Lightweight, Durable Material, Low Cost, Looks Good, Made in the USA!
review_body:
I bought this case for my iPhone 4S because the rubber edges on my white Speck case was wearing out. The white Speck case has rubber grey edges which protect the phone's screen, but it was wearing out and leaving my screen very vulnerable. So I bought this as a replacement after a couple days of research.

The main requirement for my phone case is the ease of getting into my jeans pockets. This case lets my phone glide into my pocket without and resistance. The Speck case gave me moderate resistance but not so much as an Otterbox Defender which has the silicone. On this requirement I give it an A+.

The second requirement is phone and screen protection. I haven't dropped my phone yet, but I am sure this case will hold up well; obviously though, not as well as an Otterbox or a Lifeproof case. The ridged borders of this case do in fact protect my screen very well. I give it an A+ on screen protection. Overall protection is TBD.

The third requirement is cost. I do not like spending over $30 on a phone case. I want a reasonable cost for the products I buy and the cost of this case was unreasonably low. I would have bought this for $25, but luckily it was for way less than that. So on cost, I give this an A++.

The fourth requirement is grip. This case may not provide the grip of a silicone Otterbox, but the ridges of this material do a fairly good job. For that I give it an A+ as well.

The fifth requirement is the look and feel of the case. I am not into bulky, rubbery cases whatsoever since they are a monstrosity on such beautiful, high-tech phones. With that said, this case gives my phone a nice, sleek appearance even though my 4S is white. The feel of the case is also great and smooth. I give it an A+ on both.

A nice little thing about this case is MADE IN THE USA. Support our companies who make products here at home!

Overview: A+. If you do not drop your phone a lot, and like it to slide intopockets without resistance, than this is for you. If you want your phone and screen to be protected for a low cost, this is for you.

If you drop your phone a lot, go for an Otterbox Defender. If you like using your phone around the sink, shower and toilet, go for the waterproof Lifeproof. If you like the more stylish options, get a Speck.

product_title: Pure Fun 12-Foot Trampoline with Enclosure Set
review_body:
We've owned this trampoline a little more than a year now and we are very happy with it. The trampoline itself has a solid construction. Raging wind storms have picked it up and blown it away three different times (once 50 ft. and another 100 ft.) and after returning it to its location, bending the net poles back into place, and sewing some tears in the protective netting with fishing line, the trampoline, which itself has not sustained any damage at all, is still going strong. It is large enough and more than strong enough for my 4- and 6-year old to both use at the same time. It has also withstood friends and neighbors, uncles and aunts, play dates and parties. My kids are not gentle and the surrounding netting has taken a lot of beatings, but it is still holding up fabulously. We live in an area that doesn't get snow, so I can't speak to its durability in sub-freezing temperatures, but it has been through several 100+ degree days in the scorching sun and several rain and wind storms, and the trampoline pad itself seems as good as the day we got it.

I'm not sure why people had issues putting this trampoline together. It seemed very straightforward and my husband and I assembled the whole thing in about an hour. The reason I've given it only 4 stars instead of five is twofold. First, the padding that goes around the outer edge to cover the springs is rather flimsy. I expect it to take some beatings from weathering, but there is really no way to secure it tightly enough to stay in place, and I am constantly having to adjust and readjust it after the kids have had a few rounds of jumping. After a year of use, it is worn and has torn in a few places. I think if it had been more tightly secured it would be in better shape now than it is. Second, the clips that secure the netting to the bottom of the trampoline fall off frequently. With all the jumping that happens, I expect some shifting and movement to the structure, but the stretchy elastic connectors areless stretchy than they once were and it's near impossible to get them to stay on long-term. Having said that, there are a few dozen of these connectors, so if a few fall off at a time, the netting is still secure. You just have to check it periodically, as you really should with any trampoline.

review_body:

I attached it, using a Weaver-style rail, to an old 8mm Mauser. Given the fact that most reviewers seem to use this sight on lighter guns like paintball or .22 or .223, I half expected the thing to break the first time I fired the gun. It didn't.

Not only has it not broken, it's steady as a rock. Part of that is the rail, which is well attached to the Mauser, but I'm impressed that the recoil hasn't shaken something loose. So far I've put a little under 40 rounds through the rifle with the sight attached. It has not wandered off its zero, nor has anything broken loose. I've also had it out hunting on some fairly cold mornings and chilly afternoons. I'm still on the first battery (it comes with two).

So for the money, I've found this little sight to be rugged and dependable. With a 5 MOA dot, it's not going to let you shoot the left eye of a gnat or anything like that, but within its stated parameters, it's a good sight for the money. product_title: Umarex 2252600 Morph3X Rifle /Pistol
review_headline: The best inexpensive bb gun for actually shooting at targets etc
review_body: The picture shows only the pistol mode but it converts to a rifle as well (with a stock, foregrip,  and longer barrel all included). The earler Umarex Ebos fully automatic assault rifle used an electric motor to make it work, but I found the best use was single shot for power and accuracy (the Ebos' auto mode sprayed the bbs with reduced power), and the electric feature interfered as the batteries kept dying and eventually it failed totally. This Morph in rifle mode is a great improvement as they have done away with the batteries and motor, making it semi automatic, which should make it last a lot longer. The trigger pull is longer as a result but I found after a few shots I no longer even noticed it. It is deadly accurate, I put a scope on it and it shoots just where you point it with good power over fairly long distances. I like the fact you can see how many bbs you have left at all times and I like the fact it holds 30 bbs. I wish they had included the bb hopper used on the Ebos as you could load hundreds of bbs at once, but it raised the height of the gun (requiring a weaver rail attachment to raise a scope to see over it) and cost more to make I guess. This Morph is the best inexpensive bb gun I have tried for combined power and accuracy, even with the supplied sights it is very accurate. It could be improved with a weaver rail on the botton as well (but you can use an offset weaver rail attachment to mount more accessories)and by adding the bb hopper from the Ebos, but otherwise it is as good as they get and at an amazingly low price. I have also owned the Drozd which failed, the Steel Storm  and the Ebos which went bad after about a year. This one is the best so far, unless you just want to spray bbs.

review_headline: So-So Ruger Mark II 6 7/8" Barrel Holster
review_body:
This is the second Bulldog holster I have purchased to fit my Ruger Mark II with a 6 7/8\\" barrel. There seems to be some confushion on exactly how to measure the barrel length on this firearm to fit a holster. Instead of measuring from the tip of the barrel to the front end of the receiver that it screws into, the measurement must be taken from the tip of the barrel to the face of the breach. If this isn't news to anyone else, it certainly was to me. Therefore, the first holster I ordered was too short, and this model which states that it will accomodate a 6 7/8\\" long barrel is a bit of a disappointment as well. The firearm sits deep in the holster and the front blade (sight) protrudes about a 1/4\\" to 1/2\\" beyond the holster opening at the bottom. This presents two problems: 1) the muzzle is not protected from being scratched and or from debris entering into the muzzle of the firearm, and 2) when drawing the firearm from the holster, the front blade snags on the opening of the holster and then rakes along the inside of the holster during the extraction (no wear marks to date since it is nylon).
I purchased this holster for range use only and did read other comments similar to mine before buying it and am therefore confirming those previous comments. I have several other Bulldog holsters and they fit their specified firearms very well. For some reason, the Ruger Mark II 6 7/8\\" barrel is just difficult to fit. In summary, if you are looking for a low-cost holster for range carry and slow, careful extraction, then this holster will do. If you are looking for it to accommodate anything more dynamic, keep looking and be prepared to fork over a lot more money.

product_title: Endurance T3i Treadmill
review_body: I've had this treadmill (Endurance XT3i) since 2005 and it worked just fine until this year. Mind you though, that until this year (2012) it was being used primarily by an elderly woman going no faster than 1.0 mph with no incline. This year however, I have been logging about 5 hours a week on it, usually at an incline of 3 and speed between 4.4 and 6.0mph. A few month ago the lifter went out when I stopped the machine and it read \\"Err7\\", which means that the computer no longer recognizes that the lifter is in place. The lifetime warranty is great and the replacement part was shipped out (at no cost) and the old part was then returned in the same box. The part was installed however the display then read \\"Err6\\". Tech support was called and all we had to do was unscrew the shaft a bit so that a few threads were visible and it worked just fine. However a few months later that same part went out again. Perhaps the machine can't handle all the bouncing weight that comes with jogging or running. I still like the machine and its great for the price, and since the parts are covered the only downside is waiting for the replacement (a few days to a week). The machine does come with a few pre-set modes, but they don't have multiple intensity levels so you still have to adjust them manually if they are too easy. (I find they are suited for a beginner). The distance and time displays are accurate and you can also set it to count down the time till then end of your workout. There is no heart rate monitor, though most are fairly inaccurate on machines anyway and if this is important to you I recommend buying a chest strap monitor. I also find that the calorie counter is very inaccurate since it uses a generic algorithm without taking into account weight, height, gender, age, and heart rate. (again a good heart rate monitor would be helpful since you can usually enter in those stats and get a more accurate assessment on caloric burn). The incline goes as high as 12 and max speed is10.0mph. To stop the machine there is a large button that stops the belt at a more gradual and natural pace but for an immediate stop there is a magnetic key on a string that can be clipped to you so that if you fall or trip it detaches and the belt comes to a halt instead of throwing you.

product_title: Saunders Double Eagle Pro Wrist Rocket Slingshot w/ Twin Flat Bands
review_body:
This slingshot has exceeded my expectations.
The quick snap band replacement system has worked exactly how it was supposed to, making changing/adjusting bands even easier than the tube bands for my other slingshot. It's not complicated but I did accidentally feed the bands through incorrectly (yes guys, read the instructions)and the clips wouldn't fit properly so make sure you do it right or you might have them pop out like some other reviewers experienced.

The slingshot folds down into a more compact shape which is convenient for putting it in a backpack or large pocket. The grip is the perfect size for my average sized hands and the contours make it comfortable. The bands that I got were the black bands and I have found them to be very powerful. The bands have not broken or gotten weak after hundreds and hundreds of shots.

NOTE: the pouch on these bands is designed specifically for shooting 50 Cal ammo (1/2 inch), but I did find that I could use a slightly bigger ball bearing as well. From experience, DO NOT use this pouch for ammunition smaller than 50 Cal or you may have a wild shot, which can be dangerous.

HOWEVER if you are like me and want to be able to shoot any size of ball bearing I did find a simple modification. I prefer to use a 3/8 sized ball bearing for target shooting so I took off the 50 Cal pouch and repurposed a leather pouch from a broken set of Trumark bands and fed the flatbands through the holes in the leather pouch. I then tied some typical rubber bands near the pouch to limit migration. I have posted pictures of the modification. This has worked very well for me and I hope someone finds this info helpful.

Even though I decided to modify the pouch that doesn't mean that there was anything wrong with the product. I would recommend this product, just make sure you know what you are buying and use it correctly.

product_title: Lee Precision 45 Colt Loader
review_headline: Saves a lot of money...very accurate
review_body:
Lee loaders are great for loading calibers like .45 colt. Big, rimmed, black powder cartridges like this one are very forgiving to reload. All you need to buy is bullets, powder, primers and lube. The Lee Loader is pretty much the only tool you need to reload accurate safe ammunition.

It reloads about a bullet a minute when you get used to it, which is much slower than a good reloading press, but you can't carry a press with you to the range or on a hunting trip. I reload while I watch TV sometimes and by the end of a show, I have a bucket of finished bullets.

These loaders are pretty easy to use. Just follow the instructions and you will be reloading like a pro in minutes. The resulting rounds are as accurate as any factory load and cost a fraction as much.

Add a bullet mold and you can get your ammunition costs down to maybe 5 cents a shot. I use a Lee double cavity flat point 255 grain mold number 90358. [[ASIN:B001TQ3PTW Lee Precision 452-255-Rf Double Cavity Mold]] The type of alloy you use for lead is almost irrelevant if you keep your velocity down under 900 fps, so you can shoot tire weights if you want. The .45 colt is very forgiving and eats whatever you feed it.

You can use any powder, but this setup comes with a .7cc dipper and a card listing which powders work with that specific dipper. The best powder to buy if you plan to use this dipper seems to be Hodgdon UNIVERSAL. It has the best ballistics using .7cc of powder with a larger variety of bullets. The Lee load card lists this powder for 160, 180, 200, 215, 230, 250 grain cast lead bullets. It also lists 260 or 300 grain jacketed bullets for this powder. I don't personally use Hodgdon powders, but I know people who do and they swear by it.

All the loads on the card are mild loads, safe in old guns, but this caliber is capable of much higher velocity if you buy a scale and use published loading tables. Lee also offers a set of dippers with a charge listing telling you how much of each specific powder the dippers hold. [[ASIN:B000N8OIE8 Lee Precision Powder Measure Kit]] It's cheaper than a scale, but not quite as versatile.

I recommend this product highly for anyone just starting out or who doesn't reload very many rounds per year If you reload hundreds of rounds at a time, get a RCBS Rockchucker. If you only need to reload a couple of hundred a month or just want to try out reloading, get this one. It works fine and costs less than a set of dies for a press.

review_body: I bought the Ameristep doghouse blind about 2 years ago for the sole purpose of being able to bring my 3 year old hunting with me. Over the past 2 years I only set it up and broke it down in the basement just to keep practice of the set up and break down. This blind can be very tricky to break down. There is a video on youtube which is basically a must watch, you will not figure it out yourself. Anyways, I bought 2 hunting stools to use in it as a regular folding chair will have you sitting too high to properly use the windows. This past week I finally took it out on a duck hunt here in Colorado. The blind had enough room for myself, my 3 year old, gear and a small portable heater (temps were in the 20s). The blind worked great until the afternoon winds started kicking up. Even with the blind staked out I had to grab the walls several times as I could swear it was going to blow away with me inside of it. I finally called it quitting time and started to pack it up. Since the winds were so bad once I took the stakes out I had to hold on for dear life so the blind would fly away like a kite. In my haste to break it down quickly as it was now acting like a sail in the wind I forgot to remove the tent poles and when I went to break it down one of the poles snapped. So now after my first use I have a broken pole (I guess that was my fault). Anyways, I would suggest this blind to someone who plans on hunting in calm weather. Any wind and you will be miserable. I would guess you could fit 2 grown adults in the blind, however it is much better used as a father-son, father-daughter or so on kind of thing.

product_title: Valeo Medicine Ball With Sturdy Rubber Construction And Textured Finish, Weight Ball Includes Exercise Wall Chart For Strength Training, Plyometric Training, Balance Training And Muscle Build
review_body:
Product: Valeo Medicine Ball (various sizes)
Rating: 4/5 (very good)

QUICK COMMENT ON WEIGHT SELECTION: Before getting into the meat of my review, here's a quick tip for my fellow newbies regarding shopping for medicine balls: one of the biggest difficulties in shopping for a medicine ball is that you NEED to know in advance exactly what type of exercises you intend to use it for, because that will determine the type of ball you need (i.e., soft or hard, large or small, rebounding or non-rebounding, etc), and its optimum mass for your needs ... and there's a scarcity of helpful information out there, especially on choosing the latter (mass). The Valeo is of the hard variety, and is intended primarily for things like plyometrics (ex: P90x) and rebounding. That narrows things down quite a bit, but it still doesn't give online shoppers a feel for how much mass they need. Here's my key point: the equation for Kinetic Energy is 1/2(Mass x Velocity squared). In other words, the KE of an object of known mass increases with half the square of its relative velocity. So, what does that mean to the average lay person ? Essentially, if you're doing low speed plyo movements, the KE isn't that dissimilar from it's motion while at rest, but once you start doing higher velocity movements (ex: rebounding), the kinetic energy involved in starting/stopping those movements goes up DRAMATICALLY, which is why you need a lighter ball for rebounding than for plyo. So, if you're using say 10 or 12 for moves like 'chops', I recommend starting 2+ lbs lighter for rebounding until you are well acclimated ... especially for WALL rebounding (where you replace gravity's role). In fact, you might even want another (even lighter ball) specifically for wall use - like (example) 12 for low speed plyo, 10 for vertical rebounding, 8 for wall rebounding. Hope that helps.

Ok, on to the review.

STRONG LIKES:

* DURABILITY: The rubber material used in construction seems extremely tough, and well suited for long term heavy use, which is important for use in rebounding.

* REBOUNDING: I haven't had a chance to experiment with inflation levels yet, but rebounding seemed pretty decent straight out of the box - a moderately firm overhead slam of a 10# ball onto concrete rebounded to around waist high, which seemed ok.

* GRIP: The grip is very securely non-slip.

MINOR DISLIKES:

* SMELL/MATERIAL: The smell and tactile feel of the exterior is very similar to that of a car tire, which most will either dislike, or at best tolerate. Because the material is uniform, it's probably permanent and unlikely to fade ... which could be an issue for people with sensitive noses who use/store these in smallish indoor rooms (ex: physical therapy). The smell also tends to linger a bit on your hands. The material can also leave minor scuff marks on hard abrasive surfaces, and tends to attract dirt, necessitating periodic rinsing. In my case, I've avoided the problem by moving from my patio (slate) to my garage, which has a poured concrete floor sealed with heavy duty epoxy-paint.

* OVERHARD: These balls are quite hard, which can be either an advantage or a slight disadvantage, depending on how you use it. A harder non-slip ball is great for things like ball-pushups, but an over-hard ball that's close to your weight tolerance can be quite jarring to use for say wall-rebounding, and leave you wishing for something a bit more forgiving. Also, for rebounding, don't even think about trying to use these against indoor dry-wall (not strong enough), wood floors (too noisy, bouncy, loud and scuff-prone), or carpeting (wont rebound enough) ... smooth concrete (preferrably epoxy-sealed), or a rebounder rig, is best.

* INFLATION: Most web-based descriptions of this product appear to go out of their way in avoiding mention that this ball must be inflated for use. The manufacturer provides a standard needle, but is unhelpfully vague in how much pressure is optimal.

Bottom line: despite the annoying car-tire smell and texture, this is a very solid and durable ball that's well suited for both outdoor rebounding, and indoor plyometrics ... although first time shoppers (like me) are recommended to be mindful of the different weights needed for both types of use (i.e., less weight is needed for rebounding than for plyo). Recommended.ides a standard needle, but is unhelpfully vague in how much pressure is optimal.

product_title: MetalTac Airsoft Speed Loader with Capacity of 100 Bbs
review_headline: Incredibly useful loader, good quality, saves so much time
review_body:
This speed loader is great. I use it all the time with my airsoft spring pistol to fully load a 20+ BB magazine in about 5 seconds.

Its just crafted of simple plastic but seems durable enough. It's really easy to use; just open the hatch to feed in BBs into the loader, close the hatch, place the loader mouth on the magazine, and press the spring injector down to load 3 - 4 BBs at a time. Once the spring injector goes back up, it places another set of BBs ready to be shot out.

Only small issue is that the very last BB you want to load does not come out of the mouth far enough to reach into the magazine, so once you pull the loader away from the magazine, it just falls out, which you can then just load by hand. This does not create any problems and is easily negligible for this time saving product. Easily recommended! And for a price like this and for the hassle it saves, getting this should be a no brainer.

product_title: Aurorae Synergy 2 in 1 Yoga Mat; with integrated Non Slip Microfiber Towel. Best for Hot, Ashtanga, Bikram and Active Yoga where you sweat and Slip
review_headline: Fantastic mat, no more slipping!  (But need to wash regularly)
review_body:
Most mats turn into a slip-and-slide for me within a few minutes of warm up of the Vinyasa I practice -- either I work hard, or I sweat a lot (or both), but a regular mat alone doesn't work for me.

Then I found this mat, and it's brilliant -- it's only a slippery when dry, so as the tip suggests, simply sprinkle some water for hands and feet. After that, it's great -- grippy, and also just the right balance of thickness (I can find my handprints for downward dog) but not so much to make balance poses even harder. product_title: Livestrong  LS5.0U  Upright Bike
review_headline: Good value, smooth but half baked electronics/console- No RPM display!!!
review_body:
The way I envision this frankenbike being created was a team putting a bike together from spare parts, Lance coming in and yelling \\"This thing isn't smooth enough, and where the hell is my watts display??? Oh yeah, more yellow!, What's for lunch???\\" And it was built.

This is really a high quality bike, it's only a software update away from being perfect (for the price) but the biggest issue is the display unit that was borrowed from a generic elliptical trainer or treadmill. What really sold me on this bike was the quick resistance level changer function (hit 2-20 and change resistance without hitting up 20 times. The smooth pedalling and overall nice heavy feel were bonuses. As good as the quick resistance change functions are, the metrics provided by the display stink and it changes resistance so slowly, you might as well be hitting the button 20 times. The knife in the back of any cyclist looking to do real training on this thing is the lack of pedal RPM and no polar heart rate meter integration. I knew it didn't list polar integration, but many of the lower priced bikes do work with a chest strap even if they say they don't, I'm guessing its due to licensing.

Pros:
-Good build quality, almost gym level
-Very smooth and near silent
-Flexible seating position
-Flexible hand positions
-XML based workout files, though only 4 are available on Livestrong, but you can edit these and create your own workouts!!!
-Easy to read display, nice green color.
-Watt meter!
-Easy to build, all tools needed are included and the parts are individually vacu-sealed meaning chances for missing parts are minimal.

Cons:
-Display is borrowed from a Treadmill or Elliptical trainer
----Loaded with info irrelevant to regular cyclists - Pace per mile, Distance (a contrived number) and Heart Rate if you glue your hands to the pads.
----Missing RPM display!!! It shows \\"speed\\" on a secondary display,but that's another contrived measurement.
----Heart Rate meter does not work with industry standard (Polar) chest straps!
----Built in HRM is very slow to respond, taking 15 or more seconds to give a reading
-Uncomfy seat, and replacement options require fabrication, does not use industry standard rails.
-Slow resistance level changes, if you are using a workout that does intervals, the until will take 20-30 seconds to go from minimum to maximum resistance.
-Livestrong dot com support is a complete afterthought and has nearly no support. They provide 4 workouts, and that is it.
-Data record to usb feature is nearly useless, you can only record five workouts and you might as well scribble them down on paper, the recorded stats are avg pace, distance, duration and calories burned, per workout.
-Needs to be plugged in, why not throw in a small generator so it doesn't need batteries or a cord.

Overall this is a great exercise bike severely marred by the electronics package, which is a shame. They do allow firmware updates, so there is some hope but since Lance's career is spinning down the toilet, who knows if that'll even happen.

Get this if you want a nice quality, smooth bike. Skip it if you are a metrics obsessed cyclist.

***UPDATE***
Looks like Johnson Fitness is alive and kicking, even if Lance isn't. I got in touch with them through their face book page (Livestrong Fitness by Johnson). I asked them about their firmware updates and if they addressed the display/RPM issue. Sadly they said there have only been bug fixes in the firmware update BUT, they seemed genuinely interested. I encourage others to reach out to them and tell them how much you love the bike and what features/metrics you'd love to see on the unit. There is hope for getting this issues resolved!

product_title: Speedo Vanquisher 2.0 Mirrored Swim Goggle
review_body:
Very comfortable and attractive-looking goggles. I bought them for the dual purpose of keeping chlorinated water out of my eyes, and the ability to see underwater clearly.

The goggles succeed at the first (usually), but fail at the second.

The \\"anti-fog\\" capability seemed to last one day--my first swim session with them. After that, it was Fogville.

I thought maybe I screwed up the anti-fog coating, when I tried keeping them de-fogged, using the spit technique, so I bought a second pair.

The second pair yielded the exact same performance characteristics. No fog on Day One. Fog City on Day Two.

The first pair, I (unwittingly) touched the insides of the lenses a bit. The second pair, I tried religiously not to.

Either way, I am unimpressed by the supposed anti-fog coating. I've tried keeping a tiny bit of water in them, I've tried \\"Jaws Anti Fogger\\" and spit. Sometimes, it seems that either the spit or the Jaws solution work. I may get several laps, an hour or a whole session, with minimal (or even no) fog. But mostly it seems, that no matter what, I always have to rinse the fog out.

It is like, they are five star goggles for the first lap, then they begin to tinge, becoming four star goggles. By the third lap, they are fogging up good, becoming a three star pair of goggles. By the fourth lap, there is only a little un-fogged area left, making the goggles two star. By the fifth lap, they are fogged up, and the anti-fog coating has clearly (or not so clearly!) failed.

On the plus side, I like how the goggles mellow the bright florescent lights over the pool. The Pacific Blue model makes the pool water even \\"blue-er\\".

To conclude my review, I am not sure it is possible to make a true anti-fog coating. If you go to youtube, and look up mask fittings at LeisurePro's channel, one of their experienced scuba diver/presenters explains to a commenter, that it is not possible to make a no-fog or anti-fog diving mask, because of the physical properties of the phenomena of condensation.ake a no-fog or anti-fog diving mask, because of the physical properties of the phenomena of condensation.

review_headline: My long distance locator band - it's durable
review_body: I have been successful in hunting bull elk for over 20 years and always take along my [[ASIN:B001681YBY Elk Inc. Power Bugle]] to locate bulls due to its tremendous volume. Also, replacement bands are a must when in the field since they don't take up any space, store well and are cheap insurance for knowing you can use your bugle when you need to. While elk hunting, there aren't many things much worse for me than to reach for my Power Bugle and find its [[ASIN:B001685I48 Protective Cap]] was jarred off and the band is missing or damaged. Before I bought the protective cap I used to coil the bugle and stick the mouthpiece in the end of the tube making it look like a big donut, but found I was ripping bands when I took it back out. The [[ASIN:B001689LVO White Bands]] are made of the thickest latex making them the most durable and are easy to use, but they do take a little more air pressure to sound than the others. I use the white band for locating bulls just before sun-up or late at night. The [[ASIN:B001681Y3W Gray Bands]] are in the middle for thickness and ease of blowing which provides for more versatility. It can produce the higher pitched sound sometimes equated with smaller throated bulls or for early season calling when a bull's throat hasn't expanded and become deep/hoarse from calling. The black band is the thinnest and best used for more intricate close-in calling and even making cow sounds. Since the black band is thin it can wear quickly under hard blowing and is more damage prone. Remember, in locating elk, you don't want to be threatening so just bugle without adding aggressive grunts. All you need is an answer to start your hunt. At the end of the season I store my replacement bands in a cool, dry and out of sunlight place. My bands last a long time and even after several seasons my stored replacement bands remain in like-new condition.

product_title: HemingWeigh Acupressure Mat
review_body:
It's good. You should absolutely try it if you're thinking about it.

1. The mat is shorter than I thought. It's about the length of my back.
2. Getting on the mat and getting off the mat are unpleasant. You're putting lots of pressure on a single part of your body that's touching points... The best way I've found to maneuver this is to go down like you're doing a chaturanga, but onto your back instead of your stomach.
3. There's a brief sensation of being jabbed by a thousand jabbers.
4. Then you feel warmth coming from where you formerly felt jabbed.
5. Stay with it for a few minutes, and you start to feel relaxed... the pain/warmth mixture becomes normal, and somehow it ceases to hurt. There's still pressure, but it's not painful.
6. You're going to have red marks all over your back at the end of this. They go away.

7. The mat is pretty cheaply made. This is understandable since it's pretty cheaply bought. The mat itself is thick, but the material covering it is very thin, and the points are plastic. It's rather unimpressive, but it still works. I'm unsure about the theory behind this mat, since the points will stick you wherever you lie down -- I don't know whether you're supposed to be aiming to lie down so that you get jabbed in specific places or whether it even matters.

It's relaxing. I'm buying another one for a friend because I liked it.

product_title: Maxpedition Barnacle Compact Utility Pouch
review_headline: The perfect belt pouch for me
review_body:
I usually carry a Maxpedition Sitka gearslinger with most of my EDC gear, but I wanted something smaller to carry the bare essentials on my belt. I tried a lot of other Maxpedition pouches before settling on this one.

The [[ASIN:B004H0VVDE Maxpedition M-1 Waistpack]] and [[ASIN:B004H0Z71Q Maxpedition M-2 Waistpack]] hold a lot of gear, but I felt they were too big. Also, they only zip a third of the way down, making it tough to reach small objects hiding on the bottom of the pouch. I liked the size of the [[ASIN:B004H49ZY2 Maxpedition Anemone Compact Utility Pouch]] better, but the front flap pocket made it stick out from by belt too much (and I didn't really use it, anyway). The [[ASIN:B004H0Z7IY Maxpedition Triad Admin Pouch]] is a cool idea (and cheaper than buying the three pouches individually), but it's massive. After wearing it for a few days I ended up finding a home for it on the outside of my [[ASIN:B004CK90FK Kelty Tactical Falcon 4000 Backpack]].

The Barnacle is just right for me. It's big enough to hold everything I need, but not so big it gets in the way. It's currently holding two pens, a small Sharpie, a [[ASIN:B00915I3RW 4Sevens/Foursevens Quark Tactical 123/ QTL Black Finish / Cool White LED G2; 2XCR123A; 246 Lumens]], an [[ASIN:B004M7U1ME Adventure Medical Kits Sol Rescue Howler Whistles (2) , 2 - Ounce]], a spare CR123 battery, a Bic lighter, a small hank of paracord, some Band-Aids, and a .380 magazine. There's still plenty of room to spare. It looks like a small digital camera case so it's easily ignored.

It attaches to your belt (or any other MOLLE compatible pack) with two [[ASIN:B004H4DPTS Maxpedition 3-Inch TacTie - Pack Of 4]].

product_title: Schwinn Airdyne AD4 Upright Exercise Bike
review_headline: There is a reason this product hasn't gone away
review_body:
To put it simply, it's a solid piece of equipment that works. I admit I miss the extra features that my $3000 machine did like mimic hills, created hill intervals, and so on, however, with this piece of equipment you get out of it what you put into it. The harder you pedal/work, the more resistance you will get back and believe me by using the arm handles it works the entire body. And if an area of your body is getting worn out, lets say your arms, let go and continue to pedal, and the same in reverse.

Also, this product is still seen in gyms, used by well respected personal trainers, you see them used by UFC fighters, and so on.

I wouldn't make this your only conditioning tool, but other things you can do does not require equipment like Burpees. So on one day do this, the other burpees, and so on.

In short, if you have the room and will use it past it being a drying rack but use it for what it's built for, then it's worth every penny.

FYI,

I've been wearing these for seven months now. This has really been a bad purchase for me. This is the most I've ever paid for toe socks and this is the worst experience I've ever had with them. I really don't mind paying the price for premium products. The brand may be, but this is not a premium product. product_title: Mizerak Donovan II 8’ Billiard Table
review_headline: Pain in the Yahoo to put together but turned out nice!
review_body:
We purchased this billiards table for our office so employees can use it on their down-time/breaks as a stress-reliever.

The billiards table itself is getting a lot of use and the reason why I picked it was because of the good reviews (beit only a few) and it was within our budget. Shipping was free with my Amazon Prime and it was also shipped and sold by Amazon so I could trust that I could contact them directly if I encountered any issues with the product.

DELIVERY:

The delivery process was good. It arrived earlier than expected. The delivery company CEVA called me ahead of time to confirm the delivery date and actual location for the delivery. However, when the delivery personnel arrived, they had stacked boxes on top of the longest-part of the billiards table which is clearly marked in large letters on both ends of the box: \\"Do not stack freight on top of this carton during shipping\\" which they overlooked. This lead to one of the top-rails broken in half (see photos).

PRE-ASSEMBLY:

It took three of us (2 females, one male) to assemble this item over a month. This was partly due to the fact that we could assemble it only a few hours at a time during work hours, AND (the biggie) because we had to wait for the replacement part that was damaged in shipping.

I called Amazon upon immediately discovering the damaged part but they were no help at all since you would need to box everything back up in its original packaging and try to ship it back to them. (Really??) But to their credit, they did offer to discount the price which I accepted since the part that was broken might be salvagable. I called the manufacturer as well and they were AWESOME! Escalade Sports is the manufacturing company and they were so easy to work with! I told them what happened. They asked for the part number and my info, and said a replacement part was on the way! Happy ending, right? Not yet. It took ES three tries shipping thesame part to me before I finally received one that wasn't damaged. The damaged rail is over 8-feet long and the skinniest part was the area that kept breaking in two. ES tried to ship the replacement part: first as-is with standard packaging; second, via FedEx with more beefed-up packaging, and finally, via freight truck so that it would lay flat on a truck bed. Before this, each time we received the damaged part, I would call them and they were happy to ship out a new one, no questions asked! So if you find that you've received any part of your table damaged, be sure to notify Amazon and then contact the manufacturer. There is a 90-day warranty on the product.

ASSEMBLY:

Directions were understandable and everything was in its own plastic bag and labeled clearly. You'll definitely need a power-drill and a smaller power-drill to get things assembled quickly.

The slatron was quite heavy but we managed to get it on. We also didn't need to use the shims that came with the table as our floor and the table were all level.

Be sure to be in a ventilated area when you start to put the felt on using the spray adhesive. We are in a work environment so the smell of the fumes went everywhere and we got a little loopy.

USE:

Once we got everything set up we tested it out and it worked great! We purchased red chalk for the cue sticks since the felt on the table was red. The table also came with a brush which doesn't work as well as a lint brush since the felt tends to ball up everywhere on the table within the first few weeks of use.

It's a hefty piece and so far has held up with lots of daily use--we've had it for three months now. If you plan to use this as a \\"showcase\\" piece you might be better off spending more money but for your average everyday run-of-the-mill billiards table this is a great buy!

I gave it 4 stars for quality, speedy initial delivery, and great customer service from Escalade Sports. -1 Star for what a pain it was to assemble and wait for a replacement part.

product_title: Pearce Grips PG-39 GLOCK Model 26/27/33/39 Plus Extension
review_body:
3 stars BECAUSE:

Pearce grips can be a pain to install on a generation 4 Glock 26 magazine. Look up some video's on how to replace it. I have shot about 800 rounds since I put the Pearce extensions on my Glock 26 here's what I find:

Pro's:

1. Gives your pinkie a natural place to rest so definitely more comfortable when shooting.

2. Allegedly gives you room for 3 extra rounds on the 9mm Glock 26*.

Cons:

1. They Are a pain in the butt to install on a Glock 26 Gen 4 mag. Why? Because this particular pistol mag has a notch on each side of the factory base plate. The factory base plate must be removed in order to install these. To do this: You have to get a pair of pliers to squeeze the sides while simultaneously removing the base plate and pushing down on the \\"button\\" located on the bottom of the base plate - all done at the same time! Other Glocks/ older Glocks don't have the side notches so is not quite so difficult to remove. Check youtube for some video's folks made to show how to do it. I will say it was worth putting these on for the comfort alone though it was a pain in the butt.

*2. I can't seem to get my 9 mm to hold the stated 3 extra rounds, as advertised by Pearce, after putting on the grips. The most I can add is just two extra round. Maybe it's a gen 4 mag thing, I don't know.

Overall, a great addition to your magazine and shooting comfort . If you are not good with tools, take it to your local gun range / store and ask someone to give you a hand. It's a quick procedure but you kinda have to be able to chew gum and walk / talk at the same time...if you know what I mean.

product_title: Nautilus R514 Recumbent Exercise Bike
review_headline: Solid as a rock, smooth as silk
review_body:
I read almost every review on this recumbent bike, and those on the Schwinn Model 250. The Schwinn is about 60 bucks cheaper, so I wondered whether the Nautilus was worth the extra money. Both bikes had about a dozen reviews with a Rating of \\"1\\", and that was a concern, more about that shortly. I settled on the Nautilus after reading a reviewer who stated that she saw the Schwinn in a Sporting Goods store, and thought it appeared cheaply made. She then ordered the Nautilus, and said, after getting it, that it was much higher quality than the Schwinn. I never saw the Schwinn, so I don't know if that is true or just her opinion.

I do know that the Nautilus is built like a tank. I bought it to help recuperation for myself and my wife, who both had recent knee replacement surgery. This thing would take many heavy use by a weight trainer, so I have no doubt it will last as long as we need it. It looks great, as well as looking and feeling solid. It's quiet as a mouse. A reviewer had said you could use it while another person was sleeping in the same room. I agree, no sound whatsoever.

NOTE: I followed some reviewers recommendation, and printed the manual for a downloaded PDF file. DON\\"T DO THIS! The manual shipped with the machine has been updated, and is easier than the one online.

The box arrived in one day (thanks, Amazon Prime), and had minimal breaks in the big box, mostly from the nylon straps used to secure it. I had UPS put it in my garage. I opened it, and immediately took all the parts out to get to the main frame and motor. I lifted this out of the box (it's heavy), and made sure the pedals turned easily in both directions. Almost all of the \\"1\\" ratings people had completely assembled the machine, then tried the pedals; only to find they didn't turn. I'm not sure why they would assemble it first, as several had read the reviews and should have known there might be a problem with the pedals frozen. My plan was that if the pedalsdidn't work, back in the box it would go, and Amazon returns here I come. Why try to fix a machine yourself that cost almost $500?

I carried the parts into the house to assemble. The frame and motor assembly was by far the heaviest. With my bad knees, I couldn't carry it in, so I carried it to the bottom of the 3 short stairs into the house, and pushed it onto a small rug I had laid in the house and over the top steps. Then I dragged the rug into the living room and carried the remaining parts in which were not heavy.

Assembly was not a problem, for the most part. I did what several reviewers had suggested - download the assembly instructions, and print them out instead of using the small print instructions supplied. The hardware is laid onto cardboard, the cardboard has labels for each set of bolts, washers etc. and then a shrink-wrap applied to the top. You need a box cutter or single edge blade to cut the shrink-wrap to get to the pieces.

Make sure you install the leg with the tiny wheels in the front, as it is used to move the machine around. Step one says to make sure the heart monitor cable doesn't fall into the frame tube. It came with the cable attached to the top of the tube with a tiny rubber band. Don't do as I did, and take the rubber band off, until you install the seat in Step 10. I tightened up almost all the bolts as I went along, against others advice to wait until completely assembled then tighten them. It made no sense in most cases, Step 10 was the only step where I got everything installed and lined up and only then did I tighten the bolts for that step.

Bottom Line: I'm impressed so far. I'll come back in a few months and update this review to share how the machine holds up with use.

product_title: Beeman Sportsman Series Deluxe Air Pistol - Model 2004
review_headline: A real bargain for a powerful airgun pellet pistol!
review_body:
Say what you want about this gun [and various have done just that, both pro and con!] but for the price, you get a very powerful .177 pellet firing airgun pistol that is very accurate. While it carries the famous Beeman [Germany] name, this is, more or less, a much cheaper knock-off of the 'much' more expensive German manufactured Beeman pistols.

Couple of things to keep in mind: Loading this single shot gun is, at least at first, let us use the word \\"different\\" and I had to chuckle when I visited various airgun forums and read some of the users comments who bought this gun either \\"pre-owned\\" or simply snatched it up in the bargain bin but in various cases the gun had no manual and the comment was by one such buyer, \\"OK, I'll bite! How the hell do you load this thing? There is no clip and the slide doesn't move! What's the secret? Anyone?\\" [sic]. Another user chimed in and made with the old chestnut, \\"You ask how to load it? Here's the answer: Carefully!\\" The other user then explained the process. Seriously, it 'is' \\"different\\" and here is the process in capsule form: pull back the silver metal HAMMER and then with your fingers of your left hand, simply lift up the top slide of the gun and 'keep' extending it all the way to the left [while holding the gun in your 'right' hand] until the slide is almost perpendicular to the gun itself ['almost' perpendicular but not quite], then in the piece you just lifted up, the slide, you'll see what is actually the 'back' of the BLACK barrel itself only it's now facing forward after you extended the slide to almost 180 degrees. Take a .177 pellet and place it in the hole of the barrel, the point of the pellet going in first, [yes, it 'is' rather awkward getting your fingers in there since there is not much space but you'll get used to it quickly within a few single shot reloads]. That done, NOW comes the cocking of the gun. Make no mistake, this is NOT an easy gun to cock! But then too, take a gander at that silver pneumatic cylinder and its rather hefty size and the cocking rod, this is no \\"toy\\" and while the cylinder requires a good degree of 'heft' to cock the gun, the resulting FPS of the pellet pays off handsomely! It delivers! My .177 \\"ammo\\" of choice is 'always' [and in all my pellet firing collection, .177 through .25 caliber] lead free PBA [** Performance Ballistic Alloy] pellets including those .177 hyper velocity pellets [RWS/Umarex] with the plastic holder. I even used some so-termed \\"armor piercing\\" .177 pellets in this gun [the ones with the mini BB in the tip] and again, this gun delivers quite a punch!

CAUTION: Watch the so-called \\"pinch-points\\" of this gun. When it reaches the point where it's in the process of getting cocked and you add that last 'uummmphhhhh' to close the slide [and make sure it 'locks' in place with the gun's hammer when you get that slide 'home'], the gun will 'grab' anything in sight like your shirt or, worse, 'pinch' your finger or your palm [left hand doing the cocking] so be careful and make sure your hand [or shirt] is clear when the cocking process completes itself. So too, one reviewer 'wisely' [I mean that only in the most 'complimentary' terms] mentioned or should I say cautioned against giving this gun to younger kids. This is NOT a young kid's gun or some hopped up \\"toy\\" -- it's 'very' powerful and the cocking process can easily cause physical harm to a youngster who may not have the requisite strength to cock this gun. I don't exaggerate this aspect of this gun. The gun cocking may indeed be \\"duck soup\\" to various adults or teens but when and if you 'get' the gun, you'll see for yourself that 'cocking and locking' it is not for those whose strength is not yet fully developed or those simply not used to such cocking effort as this particular gun requires! Hey, I've got some .25 caliber airgun break-barrrel rifles that cock MUCH easier than this pistol! For accuracy in either target shooting, plinking or small rodent pest control, this gun will do it 'especially' with .177 PBA pellets. And you simply can't beat the price of [at this review writing] $39.95.

One 'odd' thing, the write-up says \\"Beeman P17 Deluxe Pellet No Sight Pistol\\" -- what is meant by \\"no sight\\" escapes me! Ditto the word \\"deluxe.\\" The gun has both front and rear sights and the rear sight is adjustable for both elevation and windage. PS -- for safety on this particular gun, I use a glove on my left hand for the cocking process. Yeah, I know, that doesn't sound very 'macho' and particularly coming from an ex-GI and all that ==but== when I in fact did accidentally get a small area of my left hand palm 'pinched' in cocking the gun [\\"OUCH!\\" --with assorted expletives therein ... ], hey, that cued the protective glove forthwith and in fact did make the cocking of the gun easier! Scoff at the glove thing as you wish ... until YOU get some part of your finger or palm of the hand 'pinched' and believe me, the protective cocking hand glove gambit won't seem so odd! ;-)

The gun has an excellent 'feel' to it, decent weight and is very accurate at 'reasonable' ranges. If you can get free shipping, hey, go for it. Getting used to the gun's \\"quirks\\" doesn't take long and its performance, for its price, is well worth it! Pure muscle power to be sure but then too, you save mightily on CO2 and if you're looking for something that can't hurt keeping your upper body strength well exercised, this gun will do it! Are you ready for this? I have a friend who simply loves pneumatic multi-pump airguns claiming that he can indulge in his favorite long-term hobby, airguns, 'and' get his 'exercise' in one or should I say 'multiple' swoops/pumps! With this gun, true, just a single 'pump' is all it takes and, in fact, is all there is but it's a single 'pump' to cock the gun that will decidedly 'pump up' your arms! Alternate hands [one hand holds the gun while the other cocks it] for the full \\"exercise.\\" ;-)

product_title: Tenergy 9.6V 1600mAh Crane Stock Mini NiMH Battery Pack w/ Mini Tamiya Connector
review_body:
Got these for a custom ICS CXP build - Barely fits in the hand guard with enough room for a 24a polyfuse, deans connectors, and an Unconventional Airsoft Mosfet. Wires used on these are on par with Turnigy 16AWG High Strand silicone wires so the wires are much nicer than stock China Cells that come with most AEGs.

On a stock setup(JG, Dboys, AGM, etc) you should expect 1200-2000 rounds depending on how little you use Semi Auto versus bursts but on average will give around 1500 rounds on your typical China made AEG, on Taiwan made guns(ICS, SRC, etc) you may get higher due to the lower FPS strain on the motor. Expect over 2000 rounds out of a stock Tokyo Marui AEG on an average full charge.

Guns I've tested this in:

Fits:
Dboys Scar L
JG/KS/TM P90(with butt plate mod)
JG/E1 G36 Series Hand Guards
ICS CXP.08 Hand Guard
JG/TM/ICS M4 Hand Guards(likely all brands too)
M4 Crane Stocks
AK Fixed Stocks(untested)
JG Sig552 - Remove battery tray

Cannot fit:
ICS Sig552(untested on 551 series)
JG/E1/TM MP5J hand gaurds
JG/TM AUG Series(untested)

These may also fit in stock sized or extended PEQ-15 boxes, but I haven't had one to test with yet. I suspect it would work though since a stock 8.4v cell fits in the extended one.

All in all a good battery if you're in the market for a cell with an unusual shape or configuration. Similar output to Intellect cells but a little cheaper.

product_title: Caldwell Plink N' Swing Action Swinging Handgun Target
review_headline: Great target for 9mm to .45ACP as well as surprisingly fun for .22LR
review_body:
This is a great little reactive target for Center Fire handguns. I have shot it with 9mm, 38 special & .45 ACP at reasonably short distances and it has held up very well. Lots of bullet splatter marks after two range trips, but little or no pitting and absolutely no deforming of the plates, and I was shooting it with jacketed target rounds at much closer then recommended distances. Obviously the paint will only hold up to a certain amount of bullet abuse, but that's what spray paint is for.

It spins very actively when hit with center-fire rounds. The top target is small enough to be a challenge to hit at ranges appropriate to the firearm your using. It is not designed for rim fire rounds, and it will NOT flip when shot with a .22LR. However, it will still react, rocking visibly if hit with .22 ammo.

I actually prefer shooting this spinner with my .22 over the actual .22 spinner I have, mostly because it is sturdier (the one designed for .22 has a cheesy stand which means it falls over quite often and has to be re-set up). Even though it does not spin violently, that means it stabilizes more quickly which makes quick followup shots possible. It's good for drills doing double taps, or triple taps (Mozambique drills) with cheap .22 ammo. Although not as "effective" for training as regulation sized paper targets, it is more fun to drill with then paper.

I found on my last range trip that an additional fun exercise with .22LR is to hit either paddle so it starts to swing, then time your successive shots while the paddle is swinging away to increase its momentum, (either on the same paddle, or for more challenge, alternating paddles). This requires fast reacquisition of the moving target as it will not swing for very long when hit with a .22LR. Good shooting will cause the paddle to flip over completely (once) with a few well timed shots. The faster you get off a well aimed shot, the fewer shots it will take.

Please note (as can be seen in the picture) that this has no real stand, only two legs, so it MUST be pushed into firm (but not rock hard) dirt. I have found it drives into my local range's dirt fairly easily (especially as it is built strong enough for me to stand on the cross bar to push it down, and it has stood straight without falling over when shot every time (which is more then I can say for most of my other reactive steel targets). However, your mileage will obviously vary depending on the consistency of the ground in your range area. Very hard dirt may prevent it's being seated deeply enough to take the punch from center-fire rounds, and very soft dirt may give enough that the target will fall over.

This target is definitely NOT designed for center fire rifle rounds, and I would not shoot it with a rifle. It would probably hold up to rifles shooting pistol rounds such as .22LR or 38 special and even then I would set it further away then I do for pistol. That said, I have not done this so I have no actual experience as to how it holds up in this case. If you want to shoot steel with regular center-fire rifle rounds, you are probably better off with AR500 or AR550 steel gongs, and you really need to be working at long ranges (75+ yards) with properly angled steel plates to minimize bounce back. In other words, do your homework.

While the plates do "give" as the unit starts to spin, generally enough to direct any bounce back down into the dirt, I did catch a .38 special jacket "return to sender" full in the chest, which is one reason they say to use soft point (lead) rounds on steel. (I WAS aware of this danger and was wearing full protective gear including heavy clothing, so no harm, no foul). As in shooting all steel, you should be extra careful when shooting this target. Make sure you and all spectators are wearing safety glasses and full cover clothing, most especially if you're shooting closer then the recommended 75 feet.

As other reviewers have noted, packaging was horrible. My product came with the box open and mutilated and the product half hanging out of the box on delivery, mostly because it is shipped in it's product (store shelf) single layer cardboard box with no mailing "over box". This means the posts you drive into the dirt punch easily through the cardboard and out the box. Any paperwork (instructions, etc.) and the advertised stick on bulls eyes were missing from my package. However, Despite the horrible packaging I have not removed a star because:

1. It's a piece of steel, which is meant to be shot, there isn't that much you can do to it during shipping (or otherwise) that would hurt it, and despite the mutilated box, the product made it to me in totally undamaged condition.

2. The stupid stick on bulls eyes always pop off with one or two shots, so I wouldn't have bothered to put them on anyway. They would have gone in my range bag with the rest of my paper targets, no great loss.

3. It's a target... If you can't figure out how to use it, you shouldn't be playing with guns in the first place. Most of the "instructions" that come with these targets are dire warnings included (for good reason) by the firm's lawyers to reduce lawsuits. Shooting steel is a whole lot of fun, but if you have never done it before, do your homework and learn how to do it safely and not get hurt, which means more then just reading the warning pamphlet which would be included in the box.

Bottom line, a fun target for center-fire handguns (at least up up to .45ACP) as well as being a very satisfactory .22LR target (with properly adjusted expectations), at a reasonable price, slightly marred by poor shipping practices. Not for center fire rifles.

I have bought other tactical pens for twice the price of this one and I do not think they were any better than the Crusher Black Tactical Pen. My only complaint is that the metal pen looks like a weapon, which could be a problem if you are going to fly or you are entering a court area where they check for metal objects. Nevertheless, if you are seeking a good tactical pen for a reasonable price, this may be the pen for you.
