product_title: Browning Hi Power Lasergrip
review_headline: Product did not fit my Hi-Power.
review_body:
When the standard grips were replaced with this product, the laser cylinder portion stood 1/8" away from the frame. Every time the grip was squeezed to activate the laser and discharge the weapon, the dot drifted about a foot to the right(at 25'). I was able to stabilize the dot by gluing a small wooden shim between the frame and the laser cylinder. I suspect the problem may be the age of my handgun - it is about 40 years old and Browning may have altered the frame width over the years. Nevertheless, I feel that the manufacturer should have been aware of this problem and warn-off customers with the older model handgun. I also found that the grip pressure required for activation was a serious distraction for forming a sight picture and lowered my accuracy with the weapon.

At the same time, I purchased a small, frame-mount, bolt-on laser for my wife's Sig Mosquito which has worked flawlessly.

product_title: Shakespeare Synergy Reel, 10 Spincasting
review_headline: Great for young kids, but not that durable for me.
review_body:
With two sons, seven and eight, I've gone through four of these in the past two years with their 6ft ugly sticks. I tried 10lb braid on one of them but it didn't fair too well, so they settled on 6-8lb mono. While the outside seems fine, some rust was inside (I took them inshore saltwater fishing the odd time and rinsed them off, or so I thought). One of the reels just plain quit and kept spooling line. Another's anti reverse stopped working.

One is still in service with my oldest (now ten) and my other son moving onto an open spinning reel. I think I bought them for $15+tax each, so for a starter reel they are just great but don't expect them to last for more than a year or two. Would I recommend them? Yeah, for the price they did exactly what they had to do for younger kids and cast just fine while they lasted (hell, I bought four of them after all!).

A dead one sits on my desk and now acts like a kinda of stress ball for me.

product_title: Maxpedition M14/M1A Magazine Pouch
review_body:
I bought this to hold SCAR 17s (Heavy) mags, the full 20 round mags. I was having trouble as you could imagine finding anything that would fit them because they are a good bit larger than standard AR type mags. SO I started researching m14 pouches and found this.

Cons
It MAY not fit more than one mag, I am unsure for now because I only own one mag. But I could see where there would be an issue.
It DOES NOT come with any MOLLE strips at all, so get yourself some BLACKHAWK! Speed clips #5 or like item to strap these to your vest, backpack etc.

Pros
Fits one 20 round mag easily closing all the way and completely like it is meant to.
It is a Maxpedition product so like all their other stuff it is really well made and will stand up to good use.

Wrap up
In all it is a good product, I am still unsure if it will fit more than one 20 round SCAR 17 mag, or even what the logistics are if it will fit more than one 10 round mag. I just don't know. But I will say with one in the pouch it does `seem' to fit a little loose. But as far as I can tell this is the best option out there. I will come back and modify my review when I get another magazine and will even take pictures. But for now it fits my one mag perfectly.

EDIT: It does fit more than one mag in it, so the product is as advertised. However beware when you shove more than one mag in, it is really tight as one would expect.

review_body:

I decided to think about that for a bit, but wanted to go ahead and put a set of iron sights (BUIS) on it. After quite a bit of looking, evaluating, and pricing . . . I decided to go with both front and rear UGTs. I have not shot the gun with the sights on it yet - but, so far I am very pleased. They fit my Stag M3 easily and tighten down securely. A bit of blue Lock-Tite makes them very secure (I don't know that it is needed - but, figured it couldn't hurt).

The sight snaps up into place and down again very securely. No wiggle or slop. The sight mounts straight up on my rifle - no cant or whatever. The locking knob is somewhat large - but, I don't find it a problem - and makes it easy to tighten down.

The Amazon price was very very good - just about half of what I could find them for on other sites.

Again, I got both a front and matching rear sight. The rear is a dual apeture type (short range and long range). I like it very well also.

I did buy the UTG front sight tool as well. It sems to work just fine - but, again - I have not sighted the rifle in yet.

One note - this sight is a bit taller than the compact sights. It is designed to fit on a gas block or other front rail which is lower than the regular top and/or rear rail.

review_body: Picked up a set of these elsewhere, and they are very nice for the money. Note that these are not the X24 Hot though, so be aware. There are folks who say that this set is fake, counterfeit, seconds or low quality...not true. In accordance with their agreements with golf retailers, Callaway can't sell their premium lines through discount warehouses. This particular set is made by Callaway and is only marketed to discount warehouse retailers like Costco, Sam's club, etc. who purchase items in bulk and whose members pay an annual fee to take advantage of the savings offered.  The fit and finish is the same high quality expected of Callaway products. All of the club heads were sealed in plastic and individually bagged.  The woods came with head covers, and the whole set came in a Callaway Box. I needed a set and wanted a name brand but I didn't want to pay a whole lot of money. If you are a member of any of the various discount warehouses like Costco, check them out for yourself. This fit the bill perfectly, at least for me anyway.

product_title: Proform 6.0 ZE Elliptical
review_body:
I got this to replace a ~6 year old ProForm treadmill that had served me very well, but it was time to renew the annual maintenance agreement (worth every dime!) and my doc had told me to change up my exercise, so I decided to move to an elliptical. The reviews and good price convinced me that this was the one.

Assembly: not too bad, considering I hate assembling things. I did it alone, moving the parts from the packing case to the machine's location one by one. Several steps really do call for a helper, but you don't need help for most of the assembly steps. I had problems with a couple of cosmetic plastic pieces (which I just tossed after hitting my frustration threshold) and one major fitting that I still think doesn't fit just right, but the machine works fine. I had three big bolts left over which made me think I must have left out something important, but I backtracked carefully and found nothing wrong. Kept the bolts anyway. It's not a particularly lengthy or tedious build; you can see progress pretty quickly and consistently. Plan on 4 hours and congratulate yourself if you get it done in 3.

One reviewer said to tighten, tighten, tighten those bolts and use plenty of grease where indicated so I took his advice and my machine is absolutely silent except for the occasional beeping of the display panel. Do what the man says!

Others have pointed out that the fan is wimpy (true) and that the non-backlit display is hard to read in normal room light (also true). I keep a table fan and a small TV on a stand in front of the machine and so far I haven't paid much attention to the display. The bottle holder is perfect for my TV remote and a small flashlight if I eventually get interested in the display.

I have to agree with others who are miffed that an AC adapter for the display panel isn't included. I'm using alkaline D cell batteries for now and may or may not look for a suitable AC adapter later. It does seema little cheesy to leave out such a trivial component and then to charge an absurd sum for it as an add-on. Chinese power bricks are pretty inexpensive commodities these days so from one perspective, it's no huge deal if I have to buy one. From another perspective, it makes ProForm look silly and cheap. This would be a five star review if this pettiness hadn't been so in-my-face.

I'm finding that it's taking some time to acclimate myself to the machine so my workouts so far are pretty dainty vs. what this machine can do. I recall it taking me a while to acclimate myself to the treadmill, though. As with everything, if you do a little each day you'll be kicking it before you know it. Overall, I'm happy with this purchase.

I bought them for a less lethal option defense course and a citizen police academy ride-along (not at all related to my work vocation) and since I work in an office with a business casual dress code, being that these aren't jeans, they are still passable, so I love wearing them to work now.  I'm a network engineer, so I often need to carry tools around to data closets etc. so having pants with pockets that can hold everything and also not let my phone take dives out of them if I crouch down is fantastic.  Oh, and speaking of crouching down, the knees on these are great.  They allow for a full crouch position with 0 constriction.  THey have pockets built into the knee which would allow you to put knee pad cushions in them too.  I'm buying another pair of these for sure!

product_title: Century BOB Body Opponent Training Bag
review_headline: Best investment I've made since backpacking equiptment
review_body:
I bought backpacking equiptment a few weeks ago. But still.

This bob has taken multiple rigorous beatings from multiple people of varying sizes. A friend of mine that used it is 265bls. It is very sturdy. Here's what you do:

1.) Buy the bob online or at Sports Store
2.) Go to home depot. Get locktite for permenantly fixing the screws
3.) While at home depot, pick up 4 X 50lbs bags of sand. (just a few dollars each)
4.) Put together. Get yourself a nice sized funnel. Saw off the small end with a hacksaw until the opening is the same size as the bob's
5.) Use duct tape to secure the funnel to the bob. (you imagine the sand will easily pour into the bob, but it won't, because when you buy the sand it will more than likely be a little damp, and it will clump)
6.) Make sure the bob is in a spot you want to keep it. Shovel sand into funnel with a hand shovel, have the hand shovel or stick ready to jab down the sand into the whole when it clumps. Have patience. Because of the clumping sand, this takes awhile.
7.) Light a dubey. (washington and colorado residents only)
8.) Fill the bob completely with water - this will give the bob about a 250+lbs base if you didn't dump the sand everywhere

Hope this helps. Enjoy your bob.

product_title: Hatson Model 85 C Combo .177 Rifle, Camo
review_body:
Initial impressions. Five star based on price range.
Gun delivered from Airgun Depot is black, not camo. Expedited delivery was expensive and slow. Decided to keep gun because of time constraints.
I have not seen a air gun near this price range that can compare with the build and features Hatsan provides. Of course time will tell but this Turkish made gun is solidly constructed with good welds and solid metal parts including the trigger. The open sights were nice and bright in low outside light.
Some assembly is required for the scope. The rings were loose but a 2.5mm wrench was included and also needed for two of the three trigger adjustment screws. The other allen provided covers the third. There is a scope stop with two mounting locations and by flipping the stop four positions are possible for tuning eye relief. IMO, Loc-tite the four ring screws and scope stop when satisfied with the position. The scope itself is made in China but has a relatively clear and sharp view with fair light gathering. When focused at low power/ short range it stayed in focus when zoomed out for longer range views. This gun has some recoil so there again, time will tell if the scope stays put.

11/11 Finally did some shooting with this gun with good results. The open sights are very good in low outside light with my poor eye sight but not so much in bright inside lights. Still happy with the scope, clear and sharp. Both have really fine adjustments and take a lot of clicks to move the shot. This gun shoots small groups with the pallet used, Crosman 10.? gram heavy domes.

product_title: UTG Airsoft UHC 1911 Pistol
review_headline: Satisfactory except for the Slide Lock and Hop-Up
review_body: The [[ASIN:B002TUSJIY UTG Airsoft UHC 1911 Pistol]] is a fairy accurate representation of the real M1911 as it has most of the functional mechanisms and/or design. As for the actual performance of the gun itself, I find the gun tends to shoot very slightly to the left (tested multiple ways) and about 3-4 in. upwards probably due to the manufacturing error when attempting to make the fixed hop-up. This was very annoying at first trying to hit targets, but after awhile, I adjusted and once you know where to aim, it works like a charm.  Another problem I would have about this product would be the slide lock. It is very stiff when attempting to remove the lock to field strip the gun, and lining it back properly can take some work. I'm also slightly disappointing that it doesn't serve its main purpose of \\"locking the slide\\". Through experimenting, I've found it is possible to make it functional (You have to loosen the slide lock so that it fits into the smaller groove), but it still contains many flaws in that prospect. I don't understand why the manufacturers couldn't just make it so that you could 1) Move the slide lock and 2) Make it able to fit into the larger groove for ease. Other than that, out of all of my airsoft pistols that I own, this is definitely my favorite!

product_title: Sunny Health & Fitness Twister Stepper
review_body:
When I received this several weeks ago I was surprised. This stepper is sturdier than I thought it would be from the picture. Also it really feels like a small elliptical. It's approximately 10-15 pounds but it's light enough to place almost anywhere which makes it truly portable.

I have bad knees from old injuries so I was worried about how this would effect my knees. It only bothered me after the first 5 minute workout because the setting was too high. If you turn the knob at the bottom clockwise it loosens the tension while stepping. Also I was stepping too far down which was putting more pressure on my knees. By taking smaller steps (about half way down and up) it doesn't bother my knees and I can get more aerobic exercise.

Now I use my bike for 10 minutes, my treadmill for 5 minutes and this stepper for 5 minutes with only slight knee discomfort. Before my knee injuries I used to do at least twice this amount but now I have to be careful. This little machine is perfect for adding light to moderate aerobic exercise. It feels like riding a bike while standing up.

It does hold weight nicely because I am in the 200-202 pound range. After using this machine more than 10 times so far it appears to be quite durable. The attached bands to exercise the arms feel awkward to me so I don't use them. I use other bands to do that separately.

Overall after 5 minutes on this it feels like I jogged up a few flights of stairs. Perhaps in the future I can gradually increase my workout but for now this is perfect to add more aerobic exercise to my workouts. Also this was a fair price for a decent and strong portable stepper which is a welcome addition to my aerobic home gym.

The Fox Labs can at least has a warning about not getting over 120F. I wouldn't trust either over 100F. The people who make paint cans know how to use a metal top. product_title: Yukon Gear Men's Reversible Insulated Jacket
review_headline: Great Value - Quite - Warm - Water Proof!
review_body:
This jacket is really well made.

Pros:
- Quite: It does not shuffle and make noise when walking brush or when moving to shoulder a firearm ect...
- Warm: Kept me very warm at night (in about 28 deg temp). No chills or discomfort with the outside temperature.
- Reversible: I'll have to say, both inside and outside of this jacket are great. The print on the mossy oak side is very well done and clean. When Reversed, the blaze orange is nice and bright. (my hunting partner even said it was hurting his eyes. I turned to look at him and it was actually reflecting an orange hue on his face) - [this is a good thing]. When in 'Camo Mode' very little blaze orange is visible, however some is. (I don't mind this).
- Hood: Although not mentioned in the product description. This hood is not only reversible, but removable as well. Additionally, there is a zipper on both sides of the collar to attach the hood too when reversing from Blaze Orange to Mossy Oak, or the other way around. This way Your hood is not on the inside of your collar at any point... Simply re-zip it to the outside.
- Pockets: The pockets on both Mossy Oak, and Blaze Orange sides of Jacket are very nice. It is the exact same pocket layout in both 'Modes' of the jacket. Within the cargo pockets there are shot shell holders. This came in handy and kept my shells from jiggling around in my pockets, making noise.
- Water Proof: This is true. The material, although at first glance does not appear water proof However, This was put to the test. I accidentally had a pool of water (on top of my easy up) dumped dumped on my when I accidentally hit one of its legs. The water just (literally) bounced and beaded to the ground, leaving the jacket dry. I was actually mad that I just got soaked, but when I looked and realized that I was completely dry, I was rather impressed.
Price: Needless to say, Great Value!!!

Cons:
- Thick: Because this is a reversible jacket, it is really thick due to the fact that there are double the pockets and double the layers of outer material. Which simply requires more space when packing for your hunting trip, (not by much though. This is a con to me but will not effect how I rate the item, after all, it does state reversible in the description... Just something to be noted)
- Warm: I know, this is a Pro as well... but when scouting I found myself in the dreaded sun. I quickly became very warm. And because this jacket is quite thick, It was troublesome to fit in my bag or around my waist, or anything. (also will not effect my rating because this was my own fault for wearing it during a sunny, scouting hike)

All in all I'll have to say that this jacket is well worth it. I am pleased with the purchase and with the price. It does the job I wanted it to do. I'd recommend this jacket to anybody. product_title: Tenzing TZ 2220 Day Pack Hunting Backpack
review_body:
I purchased this backpack right before my deer hunt this year in norther Arizona. I was able to fully load it with a days worth of food, my 3 liter CamelBak pouch, rope, bullets in the waste strap pouch, skinning knife, extra socks, first aid kit, 2-way radios, extra batteries, hunting license and tag in the small pocket organizer, a flash light, and there was still room for my Sony Nex7 with a 300mm and a 50mm Nikon AIS lens. The pack weighed around 40lbs but the rigid frame and the waste strap made it seem quite light.

10+ miles later I had added my heavy 2 layer Cabelas jacket (1 layer strapped to either side of the backpack) and my back and shoulders were still doing fine. The next day my shoulders hurt a little but that may have been more from having my gun sling hanging off of them.

I did find that while wearing a large coat the side pouches on the waste strap are difficult to get to even when you pull them out away from the waste strap. It was much easier to get to them when my coat was off. The straps on this backpack are very easy to loosen and tighten making quick adjustments a breeze when putting on or taking off layers. Waring do not cinch the straps too tightly because the buckles will not hold.

The only real downside to this backpack and most day packs is the fact that there are only 2 pocket on the main pack and in the smaller pack there are not many organizers to put stuff in so everything may end up jumbled in the bottom of the pocket.

Overall I would recommend this day pack for hunting and general hiking as it is comfortable with a fairly large capacity.

product_title: Coitac CQB Single Point Rifle Bungee Sling Color Black
review_headline: Great Sling....Worth more than the price
review_body:
I know alot of people are hesistant to buy things due to price, but let me assure you, that this sling exceeds expectations. The 5 star rating comes from fast shipping, but more importantly, due to the fact that this sling is comparable to "other" 50 dollar (and more) slings.

This sling is rock solid...stitching is excellent, and I believe I read a review that stated that there were no "company" markings on it. That is false...Coitac is stitched on the sling itself on a small 1 X 1 inch rubber format. The "bungee" section of the sling works extremely well, as you need to put a little force to expand it, which is exactly the way its supposed to be. The plastic buckles work great, and there is no doubt in my mind that it will keep my 2000 dollars plus rifle on hand.

I've used several slings before, which was the point of my "other" slings comment, and this is not only comparable, it may actually succeed others, yet...its a quarter/half the price of others. I'm also 6 feet tall, and with the sling extended, there were absolutely no issues utilizing this sling.

I would recommend this sling for anyone, and if they have any knowledge on slings whatsoever, then they will see that this sling is indeed worth more than the price.

review_body:

The sight is very good, quick to use, and the ability to use or not use the illumination for the reticle is very desirable. But. the one issue that i am not it love with is eye position relative to the sight. You need to have a very good and repeatable stock weld and be able to position the sight so that stock weld works or you will experience shadowing on top below or to the side based on how your eye is lined up. I found that the further away from my eye I mounted the scope ( as far forward as possible) made the stock weld less critical. The sheer size of the reticle make acquiring a close up target very fast and easy and the cross hair and dot a more distant target more precise but a good red dot will be faster up close and an ACOG better at range, but I still like this unit.

I usually aim for knee level (you really have to be fast to do a round kick to the head) and I can now do repeated kicks without having to return to a two legged stance.

I found the BoarDRock to be the right level of difficulty for me. Someone with good balance or who is an experienced skate boarder might want one of the other boards (the Bongo Board) but for the average person, I think this is an excellent choice.

review_body:
Sitka Gearslinger by Maxpedition..

I will give a quick review of this bag..I am not going to go into specifics because they can be found on the numerous posts both here and on YouTube and on Maxpeditions website.
That said let me explain a little about my needs when it comes to an EDC bag. I live in a suburb bordering an urban center. I basically travel from my house to my car and from there into a building, for work and other business. On rare occasions I will travel by mass transport. On a whim I might stop at a park or go shopping. This being my daily schedule I was searching for a durable bag that was not to big which can carry my basic needs and have a little flexibility for specific items. Now I have viewed a lot of reviews that break down their EDC load out. Because of my situation I do not need half of the stuff I see people carrying. I have a basic bag in the car that I carry my \\"get home\\" equipment since I am usually no more than 3 blocks from it on any given day. This allows me to pack my EDC light.
So far the sitka has fit my needs very well. It is a sling bag so I decided to go for the sitka as opposed to the kodiak. I wanted the biggest bag possible that would still be comfortable as a sling. The Sitka is very comfortable even though I haven't stuffed it yet. I am a good sized guy about 6 feet 230 pounds..pretty solid:) At this size I find the Sitka to be a good size. It does not look like a child's bag as someone wrote, but it is also small enough that it doesn't look out of place anywhere.
As for the concealed carry compartment. I live in NJ so if your not LEO it is almost impossible to get a permit. So I use that pocket for flat items like a towel a cap and 550 cord. It is nice to know that it can be used for a quick transport if necessary :) It also works well for me when I am walking and want to listen to my IPad2, I can put it back there and feed the headphones through the bladder straw hole then feed them through the molle webbing on the strap to a point where they can fit in my ears comfortably. I just thought I would mention this since I haven't seen anybody do this in a review. I don't have a smart phone so I'm sure this won't be used this way once I upgrade to a multimedia phone. Then I can just use a phone holster and use the molle webbing for cable managment.
In conclusion I find this to be a comfortable versatile bag..It will not replace a back pack for long hikes and the such but that's not what I bought it for. If you like sling bags this is a perfect EDC in my humble opinion.lle webbing on the strap to a point where they can fit in my ears comfortably. product_title: Camelbak Adult Tri-Zip Hydration Backpack
review_headline: Decent pack but with a small capacity and low end waistbelt
review_body:
This pack is OK. It's a decent day pack, but I think it is overpriced for what it is.

The good:
Pretty tough construction, tri-zip design with the Mystery Ranch Futura adjustable yolk. Having an adjustable torso length shoulder harness is very important.

Good organization pockets.

Comes with a Camelbak bladder.

The bad:
The waist belt is very low end. To pair such a base waist belt with the Futura harness seems imbalanced between shoulder harness and waist belt.

The capacity is on the small size.

I called Camelbak and they do not have higher end replacement hip belts, but the REI Mars waistbelt can be swapped out (I have done this, but not tested under load yet).

Seems expensive for what it is.

Summary:
But by the time you buy a replacement waist belt, I think you would be better to just put a little extra money out and get a genuine mystery ranch pack with a Live Wing belt.

product_title: Pyramex Avante Safety Eyewear
review_body: These are the first sun or safety glasses I've ever purchased, and I chose wisely. They fit close enough to my face that they provide good protection, but they don't scrub my eyelashes like other glasses I've worn. The rubber nose pieces are very comfortable, and you can wear these glasses all day and forget they're there. I chose gray tinted lenses on a gun metal frame, so they look good enough that I wear them anytime I'm outdoors. The gray lenses really cut down on the glare outdoors, but they are a bit too much after the sun starts going down. I've taken them shooting one time already, and was able to see through my scope just fine while wearing them. It was the middle of the afternoon and fairly bright outside in the shade. The gray lenses might be a touch too dark if you were shooting in a dimly lit indoor range or near dusk. They don't interfere with shooting muffs. In fact, I like the way they go together, with my ear muffs holding these glasses comfortably in place while still blocking the sound of a rifle. The anti-fog vents will quickly clear up fogged lenses as soon as you get some air flowing over your face. They don't work if you're standing still unless there's at least a slight breeze. Overall, I highly recommend these to anyone looking for stylish and comfortable safety glasses at a decent price.

product_title: Adidas Youth AdiZero Football Receiver Glove
review_headline: Works well for my 7 yr old
review_body:
I couldn't find a glove that fit my son's hand at Sports Authority as they were out of stock on the cheaper gloves for the last couple of weeks. Didn't want to spend the $30+ for the gloves that were in stock. Decided to try these gloves since they were only $21.01 on Amazon. Ordered it on 10/16/12 and it was shipped the next day. Received it on 10/22/12. Not bad for delivery out to Hawaii. I have Amazon Prime, which is worth it since I order from Amazon quite often.

My son is 7 yrs old so I decided to purchase the small size. There was no information on sizing so I took a chance with the small since this is what fit well when he tried on the expensive gloves at Sports Authority. Turns out that sizing on these is fine. The gloves are snug and there is a bit of room at his finger tips, which will allow him to grow into them as long as he doesn't lose them(reason why I don't want to buy expensive gloves). The back is some type of stretch fabric that will expand. The whole front side of the glove is made of some type of soft vinyl, which is quite sticky. It feels pretty durable and my first impression is that it should work well for him. I guess we'll find out. By the way, my son's hand is 6 1/8 inches around his knuckles (excluding his thumb).

4/12/13 update: my son is still using the glove but has noticed the velcro is not sticking well on one of the gloves. He's been using the glove twice a week since we bought it so I feel we've got our money's worth. It might be time for a new pair since he's constantly trying to secure the velcro on the field, which is too much of a distraction.

The dvd and booklet both do a good job describing the exercises. There are also a lot of support services available through the web site. Maybe that's why it costs as much as it does.

The basic workout, which is all that I've tried so far, is challenging. I do most of my exercising on a Concept 2 rowing ergometer. The equipment appears to be made from quality materials. I suspend mine from a roof truss, which puts it a bit higher off the floor than it's supposed to be. product_title: Custom Craftworks Omni Cervical Relief Pillow
review_headline: Not enough neck support for degenerative cervical spine, compared to Soothe-a-Ciser.
review_body:
I have what my chiropractor tells me is degenerative spinal disorder...or a \\"reverse curve\\" of the cervical spine as shown in the X-rays. I used to work all day in front of a computer for several years which probably created/exacerbated the problem. I also have TMJ issues (not severe).

To try to coax the cervical spine to curve the right way again and relieve some neck pain, 2 chiropractors have suggested that I roll a towel and put it underneath my neck while lying down on my back on the floor for several minutes. Although this worked OK, I wanted something that might work even better.

I looked at various options on Amazon, read through many reviews and ordered two products that looked promising - the Soothe-a-Ciser Cervical Neck & Shoulder Reliever ([[ASIN:B000Y4YO54 SOOTHE-A-CISER CERVICAL NECK & SHOULDER PAIN RELIEVER]]) and this Omni Cervical Relief Pillow.

I've been using both for over a month now, and I definitely prefer the Soothe-a-Ciser over Omni. With Soothe-a-Ciser, I feel a strong \\"push\\" against the back of my neck. As you can see in the product picture, your head hangs over the top of the pillow, acting as a weight against the back of the neck and allowing your cervical spine to stretch. In fact, you may want to try it for a very short time for the first few sessions. In my eagerness, I rested 15 minutes on it for the first 2 days and my muscles were absolutely sore! After a week of rest, I shortened the length of time on it and worked my way up to using it for longer periods.

With the Omni Pillow, the contour of the neck is too soft and not high enough to have much support...a rolled-up towel behind my neck feels much better. As other reviewers have noted, the depression for the head is not nearly deep enough. The back of my head is on the flat side if anything and the pillow is *still* not deep enough. I can barely feel the hump of the pillow behind my neck. Although it is a comfortable pillow, it does not do much for my neck or shoulders.

I definitely do feel a difference after using the Soothe-a-Ciser, so I will continue using it. Hopefully it will correct my cervical spine back into its natural curve. I have stopped using the Omni pillow as it really doesn't seem to do anything much other than being a pleasant pillow to lie on.do much for my neck or shoulders.

I definitely do feel a difference after using the Soothe-a-Ciser, so I will continue using it. Hopefully it will correct my cervical spine back into its natural curve. I have stopped using the Omni pillow as it really doesn't seem to do anything much other than being a pleasant pillow to lie on.

product_title: 2" Torreya Wood Reversible Go & Chinese Chess Game Board
review_body:
I must not have received the same product as the other two reviewers, because what I received was complete junk.

The first tip-off was that the ends of the board were painted. Why would they paint over the end grain of torreya wood? Perhaps because the board was not made of torreya wood?

Then I tried to take off an ugly manufacturer's sticker that they had thoughtlessly placed on the chinese chess side of the board. The sticker ripped off part of the \\"wood\\" next to where the sticker was! The \\"wood\\", of course, was really a cheap paper laminate with a wood grain appearance and the board's lines printed on it. Underneath was... something white... still not sure what it is, but it is not wood.

To add more insult to injury, they can't even make the fake wood 2\\" thick, as advertised, nor even 1.75\\" inches thick, as another customer reported. Mine was 1.375\\" thick. I measured it with a metal carpenter's rule, so this is a fairly accurate measurement.

Last but not least, I contacted Asian Home through Amazon, and asked for either a refund or a real torreya wood board as replacement. I received a response 6 days ago, with no apology for shipping a product so unlike what was advertised, which stated that I would be emailed a return shipping label. Nothing about the money being credited back to me. And since then I've heard nothing. The customer service is as terrible as one would expect from an outfit that, either through incompetence or dishonesty, ships products that deviate so dramatically from what was advertised. So I'll keep the junk board, eat the $30+s/h, and write a review that warns others.

Long story short... complete junk, complete ripoff, stay away from Asian Home.

product_title: SureFire HS3-A-BK Maximus Rechargeable Variable-Output LED Headlamp
review_headline: Nice, but a bit over kill.  Broke After 2 Years.  Getting Warranty Repair Difficult.
review_body: A very well built headlamp, perhaps even overly so.  It is a bit on the heavy and bulky side, almost enough to be uncomfortable.  The light beam is a bit wider than I would like, but good for closeup work.  However,  closeup work probably doesn't need 500 lumens.    After two years of ownership, it will no longer hold a charge.  I charge and put it on the shelf while turned off, and it is totally dead within a few days.  It was sent to SureFire for \\"lifetime\\" warranty repair.  They kept it for two months and sent it back saying nothing is wrong.    Immediately upon receiving it back from \\"repair\\", I charged it fully to a green indicator light; and put it on the shelf.  Two days later it was completely dead and would not accept a charge from either the 110 volts wall charger or the 12 volt car charger.  It's now back at SureFire for another repair.    I downgrading the star rating because of this.  I'm really disappointed in the way that SureFire is handling this supposed lifetime warranty.    Edited November 2014.  They replaced the unit this second time it went back for repair.    Bottom line is that, when it works, it's the best head lamp I've ever used.  When it breaks, getting a proper fix under warranty is an arduous task.

product_title: Dye i4 Paintball Mask / Goggle Systems
review_body:
I have been playing paintball for about 8 years now. Love the game. I purchased my own equipment almost 3 years ago. Recently I decided to upgrade my hopper to a DYE rotor which caused me to think about upgrading my mask as well. I've been looking for a mask with a yellow lense to brighten everything up as the days are getting shorter and the woods are getting darker. Since the Dye i4 Tactical was the same color as the rest of my gear and rotor I naturally leaned towards it. Plus the lure of a superior HD lense had me going towards it not to mention the reviews on here and other sites.

side note: I have two other masks that I got for free basically- V-Force and JT Spectra Proflex. Both masks did well protecting against fogging, were comfortbable and covered my face well. Due to my JT being camo I wore that mask more often. It's served me well, but I was looking for a change.

After much hesitation over some people complaining that the size was an issue and others saying it's not, I went to a local store and tried one on. I am 6'3\\" 215lbs. The coverage of the mask was noticeably different than my JT, but it was hard to fully compare since I did not have a mirror to really look at the mask on my face. The forehead is about 1 inch lower and yes I am wearing the mask at the lowest point on my face to try and cover my jaw line as well. I have a dye headband so, I was thinking that should cover my forehead.

My Jaw line was still slightly exposed and talking... forget it. Then I'm really exposed, but who really talks in the middle of a gun fight?

So, I had a chance to try it out this past Sat. The place I went to had a ridiculous number of people that day more than 3x there normal crowd. Normally I never get shot in the head as I am a decent player, but on this occasion after trying to fix my gun from a ball break in the barrel I took two to the forehead just slightly above the top of the mask (where my JT would have covered). Granted normally I'm not distracted with gun issues, but the wrap did nothing. Nice welts. Later in the game I also took a graze on the jaw line which is a first getting hit there. I don't mind taking hits in fact I almost encourage them since I don't like hanging back, but the minimalist coverage of the mask is going to make me think twice about it. It's one thing if you are still in school and facial bruising doesn't matter, but when you have to go to work the next week and see customers... that doesn't work out too well.

Besides that, the clarity of the lense was great. I noticed a light surface scratch at the end of the day to the lense. Probably happened running in the woods. Vision was also great.

The mask never fogged, which isn't hard to beleive since it doesn't cover your mouth when it's open and you are breathing.

The ears were comfortable, but the mask wasn't as comfortable as I thought it would be. Could be because of the shots to the forehead, but it seemed too snugg. The headwrap could have something to do with that or it could be that I have a big head (which I wouldn't say is normally the case), but it wasn't a mask I would want to leave on all day where my JT never bothered me even using the same head wrap... could need more time to break in.

One of the ball breaks on my forhead dripped in the air vents on top to the inside of the mask. That's difficult to clean without taking off the lense because if you get water inbetween the lense layers (thermal) it's ruined.

So, inconclusion. I'm not giving up on the mask yet. After all I did just drop $130 on it, but it is not the end all best mask out there in my opinion after my experience. Maybe for kids and smaller people. It's dissapointing that Dye didn't make a mask with better facial coverage and it's not the ultimate mask some peopoe make it out to be.... unless they have small heads :-)

product_title: CNC Swashplate: Blade MCPX
review_headline: Metal swashplate holds up better, links don't bust off
review_body:
The plastic swashplates that come with the mCPX Helis tend to get broken due to the very small plastic ball links getting broken off. When the first one breaks off you can continue to fly by switching to the other pair (they have 4 balls). Eventually one of those will bust too and then your swash plate no longer functions and you need to replace it. The plastic stock ones are ok but don't hold up compared to this metal version. I've bought a couple of these now and never had either break, it's completely fixed the problem of broken swash plate ball links for me.

I've been really happy with the MicroHeli brand. Each of the many upgrade components I've purchased from them have been reliable and worked well. This swashplate comes in 2 versions. One has the anti-rotation bar on the side and fits the stock frame. There's another with the anti-rotation bar in the back and it fits the special MicroHeli frame. The reason they moved it to the back was so they could place it level with the balls and achieve a slightly better geometry in flight. I use the stock version and it works very well.

A brief mention of why you should consider try this mCPX heli: I really wanted to find a way to get my skills up to the level of inverted flight and some fun flying. The problem is that the cost of learning on a larger Heli is really high. To avoid the damage that a single crash costing $50 or more does to my pocketbook, I tried this micro collective pitch heli. I have been VERY pleased and have been able to conquer inverted flight and some tricks.

The pros of this Heli are simple. It's low cost (relatively speaking for a Heli) and very crash resistant. When you do break something the pieces are low cost and easily available. There are a few cons with this Heli. #1, it's very small, and easy to lose orientation with distance, it takes good focus to learn how it looks at anything past 25'. #2, the tail is a bit weak relative to the main motor and you can get tail washout with full energy rotor actions. There are mods for this and the Heli is still very flyable in spite of this. Depending on your eyesight and budget it could be easier for you to move to a larger CP Heli, I have friends who love the130 for this very reason.

The typical method of learning heli flying is to start with a coaxial heli which has 2 sets of counter rotating blades (Blade mCX2 ). That will help you learn orientation and the basic stick movement. Next, I went to a fixed pitch Heli to learn more control and stick management (Blade mSR). I stayed on fixed pitch too long and should have moved to this Collective Pitch Heli sooner since it wasn't that hard of a jump for me to make the change. I'll be sticking with this Heli until I have inverted flight and additional tricks down without damage. Next. I\\"ll move up in size since by avoiding crashes I'll be able to afford to fly the larger Helis. The great part about flying with this collective Pitch Heli is that I have it all programmed up on a DX7 with the very same controls and switches I'll be using on larger Helis, which helps me as I step up. Everything I'm learning and doing now carries forward.

After using my PT's simple white foam roller, I searched around for one of my own for home use. A well known sports store wanted $39.99 + tax, no thanks, so I went shopping on Amazon. This J Fit one is very high quality and is actually better quality and firmer density than what my PT had! It feels even more stable and solid than hers! Since I sit on it and I am not a super lightweight, I am glad to have something quality to do my exercises on. There's no use buying a cheap one to have it break and have to rebuy (as I saw with other reviews on Amazon).

I'm using this for female pelvic floor therapy but I am glad to know it can be used for other exercises including readjusting and helping your back and legs. Plus, my 6 year old *REALLY* wants to play with it. So after all this is said and done, if I no longer use it, he will definitely find a bridge or something to construct out of it. :)

product_title: Mil-Comm Three-Step Gun Care Kit - NRA Licensed Gun Care System
review_headline: Overrated.....does NOT clean all residue on a gun.
review_body: The MC25 cleaner came in a small 2 oz bottle that really isn't worth the price.  I wouldn't be surprised if this stuff is nothing but Simple Green cleaning solution.  It cleans ok but does not get off the carbon rings or whatever that black stuff is at the back of the cylinder and back of the barrel (the area right where the barrel and the cylinder meet) of my revolver.  It does not work on that residue at all, but seems to clean the bore of my barrels and everything else alright.  But from what I read and understood about this product, it's suppose to be all that, but it isn't.  If it doesn't clean your revolver the way you would expect it to be cleaned, then the product isn't all that great.  Further, Mil-Comm's web site says it doesn't affect the bluing on your gun.  Guess what?  After I cleaned, of all guns, a Sig Sauer, it appears the bluing came off, because it's not the same dark color as before I cleaned it.  It looks more gray now so if that doesn't mean the bluing came off as a result of using this product, then I don't know what it means.  As for the TW25B grease, when I first opened the bottle and used it, it was like oil (like the MC2500 oil) but then later it became all gooey like a grease.  I ended up not using that because I felt I didn't need this extra step.  It's unnecessary because the MC2500 oil essentially does something similar so I ended up using that instead after I used the MC25 cleaner.  It's much easier and cleaner to use than the grease.  All you really need is a cleaner or solvent and an oil.  You don't really need grease, unless you plan on storing your gun long-term.  So this \\"3-in-1\\" product is mostly hype and is overpriced.  2 oz bottle gets used up quick.  Next time I'll try the M-pro 7 cleaner/solvent and oil.  You really only need two products, not three.  I have a feeling that will work much better than this.

product_title: Magpul MIAD MIssion ADaptable Grip
review_body:
Very nice grip for folks with large hands, long fingers or folks with small hands/short fingers, as this thing can be changed configuration for both. Now for tips for the install:
First it is difficult to remove the stock grips to get this puppy installed.
TIPS: 1. To remove the stock grip on your AR15 (i have both S&W M&P15 and a Bushmaster) the factory grip is secured with a hex nut and lock washer. To remove the factory nut you will need an \\"allen wrench\\" that is around 4 inch long. I bought one set of cheapo long American size allen wrenchs (5/16\\" 1/4\\" etc) on Amazon and they did not work. Next I went to Lowes and bought a set of METRIC long allen wrenches for about $11.50 \\"ball end\\" style is what you want. The size you want is 4.5mm size. Do not try to use the plastic wrench handle that comes with this as it will reduce the length you need to reach the screw deep inside the grip. Then follow the U tube videos that warn you not to lose the detent spring that holds the safety selector in place when you remove the plastic factory grip.

TIP 2: once the old grip is removed, keep the gun upside down so the brass pin below the spring does not fall out. To install the new Magpul grip...first do NOT insert the metal \\"semi permanent\\" lock pin until all is completely done and then it is not needed! Next you will want to remove the front and back Magpul grip fillers, so that you can align the slotted screw into the hole in the bottom of the new Magpul grip, and once it is in the hole you carefully then reinsert the front and back faces of the grip.....and only then lower it into place and insert the detent spring into the hole of the Magpul grip and seat it on the brass pin in the reciever. Once you have it all in place you may start to tighten the screw. Make sure your safety selector switch is still working and will lock into the safe position. Then all you need is to put the base into the Magpul grip.

A bit more difficult thatthe U tube videos would suggest. Be careful, go slow, make sure you use the correct Metric size ball head allen wrench and have a flashlight handy to look down inside the factory grip.

This Magpul is really a great grip for your AR15! there is storage inside the grip for 2 extra 5.56 NATCO rounds in a specially designed rubber insert on the base which comes out when you press the release lever on the grip.

product_title: Kershaw Compund - Serrated
review_headline: For the price, you can't get a better knife
review_body: Let's get real for a moment folks.  For 20 bucks, you are not going to find a knife much better than this.  Yes, there is a difference between a knife made in China and one made in the US.  In this case, the biggest difference is the price.  A similar Kershaw knife made in the US to this would be a Turbulence, and that will cost you between 60 and 70 bucks.  So for about 1/3 the price, you are getting a knife that is at least 80% the quality of a similar US made knife.  I would be a lot more hesitant to use a $60 knife for hard use work than a $20 knife.  These Kershaw Chinese made knives are a low cost alternative for those who need a lower price point but also want a quality knife.  This knife is sharp as heck out of the box and pops right open and locks securely in place.  I continue to be impressed with Kershaw knives, whether they are US or Chinese made, you are getting a quality product.  I own over 70 Kershaws and routinely use the Chinese made knives because of the quality and mainly because of the price.  I am not afraid to use them because I would rather damage or lose a $20 knife than a $60, or above, knife.  However, if buying US made is important to you, then know that the lower price point Kershaws with 8cr13mov steel are made in China, and look to the Sandvik 14c28n or S30V or 154cm US made steel knives.  I own both the lower end and the higher end ZT knives and have to say I don't think I have ever been disappointed with a Kershaw knife no matter what price they were.

product_title: Galco Concealable Belt Holster for 1911 5-Inch Colt, Kimber, Para, Springfield
review_headline: To get any better you will have to spend a lot more.
review_body:
I purchased this holster for my 1911 Kimber Gold Match. Obviously the 1911 is a full size handgun and you are aware of it's presence. The holster rides high on the belt with a cant that places the grip close to my body just under my ribs. The holster fits on the belt, tight to the hip and stays in place. Drawing from the holster is natural and without effort. Re-holstering is also equally effortless with one hand.

As the other reviews have stated when you first get this holster you will think you made a mistake as it is a very tight fit. However, after the break-in my Kimber glides out of the holster, but the holster still retains the handgun firmly so it stays in place. To shorten the break in time I sprayed the inside of the holster with Lexol, a fine leather cleaner & conditioner I have used for years on leather upholstery. I then put a plastic bag over my gun and followed the break in procedure. I sprayed the interior of the holster once again, then placed thin plastic wrapped over my gun and left it in the holster overnight to dry. The next day the fit was still snug, but the handgun drew without unusual effort. Draw-EZ by Galco will make the draw even smoother. I have used holsters costing over $200 and they are quality holster, but for far less than half the money and a little time spent on break-in this holster is ever bit fit for purpose. review_body:
I am very happy with this scope. The quality is good, the optics are sharp, and the zero-reset turrets are a nice add-on. I put this on a bolt-action Marlin .22LR with medium rings, and it clears the bolt handle with about a pinky to spare.

I have a friend with a semi-auto .22LR with a cheaper BSA 4x32 scope on it. So I was interested to see what $100 buys you vs $50ish. Both do the job fine. They put a crosshair over what you want to hit, and you can knock the wings off a fly at 25 yards with a .22 rifle. That said, the brightness of the Nikon is superior, but the most obvious difference was how clear the image from edge to edge through the Nikon. On the cheaper scope, there is a bit of rainbowing/distortion at the edges of the glass.

In addition to better glass than a Wal-Mart bubble-pack scope (which I am not knocking, they get the job done), it has a lifetime transferable warranty. So on the whole, I am glad I went the $100 route with this scope.

product_title: XMark Fitness XMat Ultra Thick Equipment Mat
review_body:
I agree with the other reviewers that these are sturdy mats very suitable for the purpose of protecting the floor of a home gym. I have ordered 7 of these and 4 of the 7 seem virtually perfect. The other three have issues from minor to troublesome.

Two of the seven have slight waves when lying upright. The mats seemed to have been stored rolled up in the cartons and perhaps that resulted in these curls. Even after being flat on the floor of my gym for almost a month, the waves persist causing the edges to buldge up on one of the long sides by about 1/2 to 3/4 inch. They seem to behave better when placed upside down but then the embossed 'tread' is less sharp.

One of the seven was broken right out of the box (this one also has a wave to it as described above). There is no way to know if this occurred during shipping but the box was reasonably intact. (Imagine yourself as an extremely heavy 4 x 1 x 1 foot box and you will expect to be tugged around and dropped a few times when shipped by UPS.) The break was through and through, about half-way across the mat, parallel to and centered between the short sides of the mat. Fortunately for me, this last mat was destined to be cut into smaller pieces to fill odd spaces, so I expect that in the end this will not matter a great deal. However if this were the only one that I had planned on purchasing, I can only imagine the difficulties and expense in repacking and shipping back to Amazon.

Despite their weight, the pieces do seem to migrate a bit over the carpet. I've bought heavy duty velcro hook take to help with this and time will tell if this is a good solution.

The pieces seem ever so slightly off square. Enough that lining them up like tiles without the carpet showing between has not yet proved successful.

Despite these mostly minor flaws they do perform as expected and even the one with the two foot break will be almost fully functional.

*****

Update: several months later, I am happy to report that the mats are lying flat and the super Velcro tape keeps them fully aligned.

review_headline: Works great, with a little fitting

I put this on my Tantal. It's a great lower hand guard. I've got nothing negative to say about it. If you are familiar with working on AK's at all, you already know that almost everything has to be fitted, to some degree. This is no exception. I could not get it to fit into my Tantal receiver as-is. I had to sand down the sides of the receiver insertion area a little bit, no big deal.

After market Tantal upper hand guards are basically impossible to find, so if you get one of these, you will probably want to dye the upper hand guard to match. Get yourself a small pot that you don't care about. I suggest Salvation Army or something. Get a bottle of black Rit dye. Mix the bottle of dye with about a quart of water in the pot and simmer the upper Tantal hand guard for 30 minutes. It should be completely submerged the whole time. Rinse it off and you will have a perfect jet black Tantal upper hand guard.

review_body:

Remember! (I learned this the hard way since it isn't clear on their site.) Please correct me if I'm wrong

The 'Nike+ HRM' is for certain Ipod Nano's with the Nike+ Running app
The 'H7 HRM' is for Iphones (The latest model I think)
The 'Bluetooth Smart HRM' is for Bluetooth 4.0 w Smart Tech phones
The 'Bluetooth HRM' is for the older phones with Bluetooth (2.1+) like my Evo 4G Shift with Android 2.3 (Using Runkeeper).
The 'Wearlink HRM' is for Polar equipment.

You will have to wait a couple of days to get a response back from Polar if you have a problem.

I hear The 'Bluetooth Smart HRM' battery lasts forever but the 'Bluetooth HRM' eats it up pretty bad, but is the most compatible.

Update: (8/27/2012)
Everything works and syncs up just fine. Make sure when you are syncing the monitor to your phone the strap is properly moistened. Please remember to disconnect the monitor completely from the chest strap when done or you will be buying another battery.

product_title: Full Size Link Hylian Zelda Shield with Grip & Handle
review_body:
*TOP SHIELDS HAS THE HYLIAN SHIELD IN THE 1ST PHOTO* Just wanted to clear that up to everyone.

So I bought this for a new YouTube video I was in. I was Link, so of course I had to buy the shield! So I bought the shield and it came here really fast actually, it took about 3 business days to get to my house. Anyway, so I took out the shield and put on the grip and strap. And right as I picked it up, the grip and straps literally ripped out from the nails and ripped out a huge chunk of the back off in four places! So now the back of my shield was really torn apart already and I had to resort to my last measures...Duct tape. The duct tape was like the instant fixer for the shield, but the only downfall is, the back was covered in silver duck tape (so i suggest that you use clear packing tape to fix it if you had this problem). And after about a day of using the shield for a video, the duct tape wasn't doing it anymore, so I had to take off the duct take and redo it. Finally, we got so fed up with using the shield as a prop that we just decided not to use it. So what I'm trying to say here is that:

Pros:
-Great Decoration!! (Looks exactly like the Hylian Shield, I was comparing it for preciseness when I was playing the Skyward Sword and it was pretty spot on)
-Its not Plastic, but its not metal (I'm sure what exactly it is, but it is very sturdy)
-Looks freaking amazing on my wall with the master sword! When all of my friends come over, they are like THATS SOO COOL!!

Cons:
-Grip hardy works, Like I said, it literally ripped off of the back and I've heard from a lot of other people that their grip comes out of the slot really easily too

So overall, its a really great wall mount and a cool replica of the Hylian shield and any Legend of Zelda fan should totally get one. But if you are actually going to use it, just be REALLY careful with the back! And if it breaks, use duct tape to solve the problem!

product_title: Douk-Douk Knives Folder With Douk-Douk artwork Made in France
review_headline: Love and hate all in one package
review_body:
First of all in my opinion this is about the coolest looking pocket knife there is. Its ugly, odd and sexy all at the same time.
It's an old design that has history, and that coupled with its price means any knife nut should give these things a look.

This is a robust knife, far thicker in the blade than you would think. It is very thin over all as you know, and the spring is very heavy so opening is a bit of an issue.

Its the opening that kills this knife...you really need a good grip on the blade to open it, that means your hands need to be dry. Forget about grabing some fruit and washing it and than opening the blade, not going to happen. You will need nice dry hands to open it, and this alone really cuts down the usefullness of the knife.

You must take care in opening and closing this blade. There is far less room for error with this thing. Its a beauty, has great steel, can handle a lot more than you think just by looking at the pictures, but it is not a knife you will remove from you pocket, open, cut something, and close without really slowing down. I honestly think I could open and shut any knife I own 2-3 times in the time it takes to open the Douk Douk once. As a result this is more of a knife I carry when I think the likelyhood of needing a knife is very low. It would never do for work, and when food is involved my hands usually get wet from something...if not from washing items its from the cold drink in my hand...so it is not really a great picnic knife.

In the end I still really like this knife, but its far more of a looker than a user, based on the heavy spring and lack of a nailnick. (some Douk Douk models have the nailnick) Its a weekend knife for me. The only thing it does better than any other knife is look awesome, everything else it comes up short.

product_title: Rushfit Georges St-Pierre 8 Week Ultimate Home Training Program
review_body: OK, so about four months ago I finally came to terms with the fact that I had to lose weight. I'm a 37 year old male, 6 ft and weighed 262 lbs. I wore a 42 waist pant and had a beer gut and a \\"turkey neck\\". My doctor had just put me on blood press medicine because it was elevated. It was very depressing. I have never seriously dieted or worked out before and I'm not into sports (car guy). After seeing some pictures of myself in a pool with my kids I was just disgusted with the way I looked and felt and decided to do something about it. I wanted something that was not time consuming or too strenuous since I hadn't worked out much. I had seen the Bowflex treadclimber commercials showing great results with only 30min, 3 days a week worth of exercise so I bought it. It was difficult at first but got easier every day (I did 30mins every morning) and with a change in my eating habbits and my 30 min workout I lost 30 lbs in 3 months! People noticed a change, my cloths got lose and it was all very motivating! However, shortly after, I hit a wall. I couldn't get and stay below the 230 lb mark. I was getting a little discouraged. Then I saw the Tapout XT commercial and started to do some research. That led me to Rushfit. 60 days instead of 90 and all I had to buy was some dumbells (I got 2 10's and 2 15's) and a workout mat. When I started a week ago I was 229.6. I completed my first week, intermideit, with my 30 mins of cardio on the tradclimber everyday and weighed in this morning at 26.6! My body ached but it was a good feeling. My goal weight is 195 and I want to have a six pack. Something I havent had since high school. The vidoes are easy to follow, they give you alternitives to the moves if they are too hard and GSP is very motivating (especially when he has to rest mid-way cause he's also exhausted). The cool down is nice and relaxing and although the workout is tortuous, I really feel good afterwards. I have to admit, I was a little upset that today was a rest day. Iended up repeating day one just for the hell of it! Most of the reviews here are from folks who seem to already be in pretty good shape or have some if not a lot of past experience with dieting and working out. So this is coming from a regular out of shape guy. Try it, do cardio and alter your diet and you will see results. Trust me, if I can do it, anyone can! I will try to update this in the following weeks wtih more results.

product_title: Predator Blowguns - 48in. Two Piece .40 Caliber Blowgun
review_body:
If you have decided to go with a .40 blowgun this one works well. I have not noticed any issue with it being a 2 part gun instead of a 1 part gun. If there is a difference I would need special instruments to measure it. The natural variation in your blowing technique will make a bigger difference than that.

When ordering darts for this get some that come with a quiver (actually plastic disks with cutouts for holding the darts) as you will want to add some extra quivers so you can carry a variety of ammo on your blowgun. Don't be afraid to mover the various quivers, parts and pads around to suit the way you hold your gun and what you want to reach. Don't put dart points right behind where your hand will go or you will stab yourself on you own darts.

The \\"more\\" that I mention is that you can also use half of this as a 24\\" blowgun for short range shots where there is not room for a 48\\" blowgun. If you plan to do this, think about which quivers you want on the half you will use independently.

One thing worth mentioning is that bigger caliber blowguns have greater speed, range and power than the .40s. I know that seems backwards but a little research will prove this is true. The .40 is a nice toy but I would not take it hunting for anything larger than a big bug.

It could be great fun at a party, like a game of darts. It is also not a bad starter is you are just learning about blowguns. Blowing in a consistent way, not pulling to one side when you blow, learning how to assemble the dart and how to load them into the gun, how to compensate for greater range to the target, and which ammo does what are all skills you need to learn and this is an inexpensive platform for learning those basics. OTOH, if you do switch to a bigger blowgun in the future you will need all new ammo.

review_body:

They are compact, easy to use and allow me to move through the P90x program quickly and seamlessly. I live in a small apartment and the SelectTech 552 take up minimal space. You just turn the dials and lift. Its really that easy.

I read a number of the reviews complaining about the dumbbells moving and making noise. Do the move around a little when you lift? Yes. Do they make a little noise? Yes. However its minimal and if you are following the P90X on DVD you don't even notice. People who complain this bothers them must be OCD or have serious emotional problems. Its a very small price to pay for the ease and efficiency you receive from the SelectTech 552. Plus, the money saved when you compare to a room full of dumbbells is significant. My purchase price was $299.00 and with free 2 day delivery its really hard to beat.

Take it from a guy who worked out at the gym for years and has used traditional dumbbells and exercise bands to do strength exercises. If you are looking for a set of weights for home use, you wont be sorry.

product_title: Bridgestone E6 Recycled Golf Balls (36 Pack)
review_body:
I was a little weary about buying recycled balls but considering you essentially get three times as many balls for the same price as new I decided to check out this bargain. I figured worst case scenario I could use them in situations where I have a high probability of losing a ball (like over water).

Anyway, let me just say I was pleasantly surprised. The balls came neatly packed in a box and they were mostly e6 balls with a few e6+ mixed in. Of the 36 balls I received, 20 were the latest model e6 (with the dual-dimples), 9 were last year's model e6 (with the single dimples), 5 were e6+, and 2 were an even older e6 model. I would rate at \\"like new\\" condition (aside from one, which was pretty well worn but still playable). Only two of the balls had any kind of logo on them (apart from the Bridgestone logo) and none of the balls appeared to have any kind of identifying marks from previous players.

So yeah, even including the one \\"bad\\" ball, that's still 35 balls for less than $1 a ball: a great deal! I am definitely looking forward to playing these balls and will probably purchase another set after I finish with these :)

PRO:
-Good price for like-new balls

CON:
-Not all balls are the latest model or like-new, so if you care about that, best to buy new.

product_title: Prism Stowaway Diamond Kite
review_headline: Interesting idea but maybe not so much for an experienced flier
review_body:
DISCLOSURE: I bought a couple of Stowaways 50% off when [G.I.] Joe's Sporting Goods went out of business, not by way of Amazon.

I have a number of kites made by Prism, including some 2-line stunters and a speed parafoil. The company makes great, durable kites for serious fliers.

But I'm not so sure I can say the same for their entry levels, including the Stowaway.

The concept is a brilliant one-- until it comes time for repairs. I broke a spreader (top right side) in rough winds and I ordered a replacement part on their website. I forgot that tuning is important-- in other words, the bungee cord has got to be the very same tension on both cross-spars. I had to pull the cord for the replacement spar tighter and of course that messed up how the kite flew.

I think we broke the other one, too. My wife, who is not so into the hobby, decided to junk both of them. I shrugged my shoulders as I hadn't paid full retail price.

Prism kites are reasonably easy to repair for those who know how to do it; I had to replace a part on my Nexus and it's doing just fine. But my Nexus is a stunter that doesn't have bungee cord winding through it. That bungee cord just makes repair harder.

For casual fliers-- especially those buying kites for their kids-- really, I do recommend a cheaper-made kite, and one that has a triangular \\"delta\\" pattern. Gayla and X-Kites do make a few fabric kites and for a lot less money and that's usually what I see kids flying anyways.

product_title: Magpul PMAG 10 Round Limiter (Pack of 3), Black
review_body:
These work perfectly, blocking 20 round pmags down to a tight 10 rounds. Unlike other home-made DIY solutions, these are easy, look clean and OEM from the outside, fit perfectly, and even have \\"10 round\\" stamped into the release button (the part that's visible through the baseplate) so you and everyone know it's a 10-round mag.

My only criticism is that the limiter needed to be down shaved EVER SO SLIGHTLY to allow the dust cover/cap to be installed when 10 rounds are inserted. Magpul is obviously erring on the side of caution, making sure you will ONLY be able to fit 10 rounds in. In doing so, there's just a TINY bit more clearance needed to get the dust cap to clip on easily. By carefully sanding a VERY small amount from the top of the lock (effectively shortening it) I was able to custom tune the tolerance to allow the cap while still only allowing 10 rounds. If you try this, beware - do not remove too much material or you'll render it useless.

Also, just a clarification for us Californians, even Magpul says that these don't (by themselves) turn a 20 round mag into a *CA legal* 10 round mag. The law says it must be \\"permanent\\" and this is far from permanent; you will still need to pin, rivet, or epoxy this to the baseplate (otherwise, you could easily open the mag, snap the block, and have an 11+ mag). Building a non-permanently-blocked mag is just as illegal as constructing an 11+ mag. I know a lot of you want to hang on to the dream of converting it back someday, but save yourself the felony and just glue the damn thing in. ;)

product_title: Fenix E21 Flashlight
review_headline: A Compact Light With a Full-Sized Punch
review_body:
Dear Amazon Shopper,

This light is a superb option if you are looking for a compact flashlight that doesn't sacrifice illuminating power.

First, this flashlight is extremely durable. I have dropped this thing more times than I can count and it still looks as good as the day I bought it without the slightest hiccup in functionality. The on/off button is also conveniently placed and has thus far proven similarly durable.

Second, this flashlight is very light and compact. It's a great handheld flashlight that is easily dropped into a pocket (unless you're worried about ruining the lines on your slim-fit McQueen chinos) or set on your nightstand. Given that it is so small and light it's also highly maneuverable and would take up very little space in a hurricane or bug-out bag.

Third, this light offers tremendous illumination for its size. On its highest setting, it will literally light up a dark room. Even on its default setting the light is extremely potent and will not disappoint; a standard flashlight simply does not compare. Battery life is also excellent, as I have used mine intermittently mine for maybe a year now and have not had to replace the battery once.

That being said, there are a couple of minor nits for me to pick:

1 - The flashlight is not capable of remaining on its highest setting for protracted periods of time without risking damage to the flashlight. This seems a little skimpy to me, but in fairness, the highest setting puts out an awful lot of light for such a tiny flashlight and can't see where you would require that much sustained illumation of a flashlight this size.

2 - Turning the battery cap to increase the illumination was an odd choice. It would have been much better if there were a separate button to press to enable maximum brightness, but while odd, it's not necessarily inconvenient.

3 - Being purely cylindrical, this flashlight has a tendency to roll when lain on its side. This may result in the flashlight falling frequently depending upon where you place it and how careful you are (though it's built like tank).

4 - This light is a little pricey. At full retail, I'd say hold off on buying it. Wait for it to come down a little if it's at full price before you snatch it up. Anywhere in the 20's and it's a steal.

Bottom line: This is an excellent flashlight for what it is and none of its minor foibles warrant anything less than a five-star rating. product_title: Intex Explorer 200, 2-Person Inflatable Boat Set with French Oars and Mini Air Pump
review_headline: HOLY FREAKING CRAP THESE ARE AWESOME.
review_body:
With some new-found wealth I'd earned, I figured it was time to buy a boat -- nay, not one boat, but two! That said, my new-found wealth wasn't exactly massive, so I decided to buy two of these.

I'm a 23 year-old guy living in Washington, DC. The girlfriend and I have been meaning to go boating on the Potomac for a while, so I figured we'd give it a whirl with these boats this past Saturday. Mind you, we're both average height and build and weight.

These boats performed amazingly. We paddled back and forth from Rosslyn to Roosevelt Island and back and splashed around the river a good bit. They were durable enough for us to launch them from rocks along the bank, grind our way through really thick weeds, and drag them around on shore. They were light enough for us to portage by holding a boat with just one hand over our heads with no problem. They were sturdy enough for us to get in and out of the boats without tipping them once and turn around and change positions inside them. The paddles can be used as rowboat paddles or unscrewed and rescrewed into kayak paddles. We tried both without ever getting out of the water. They never leaked once and the only moisture in the bottom of the boats when we were done was what we'd dripped in there ourselves. I easily fit both of them after a little deflating into the back of my tiny '96 Corolla.

For $21, these seriously cannot be beat. Anytime I saw someone ogling our classy boats while we were in them, I shouted, \\"Only $21 on Amazon!\\"

review_headline: A 5-star watch with iPhone-like design breakthroughs marred by glitches
review_body:
SUMMARY: A 5-star watch with iPhone-like design breakthroughs marred by design flaws. Fix the flaws and I will love it.

USER NOTE: Veteran user of many HRMs over the years (Polar, Garmin, Timex)

PROS:
1)Big display with glorious easy-to-read digits for older eyes. Blows away all the silly little round watches out there. Memo to mfgs: round is for analog, it's makes no sense for digital
2)Innovative design philosophy of putting all the settings on the computer instead of pecking through impossible-to-understand settings on the watch. Bravo.
3)Innovative USB connector built into watch, I like
4)Quick phone access to technical support
5)$149 price point is outstanding for a GPS-enabled watch
6)Nice accurate mapping of route instantly available when syncing workout. Sync is easy

CONS:
1)Overly cryptic instruction manual, was stumped on several things which is why I know all about their technical support
2)Not one word in the manual about using an HRM!!! Have to go into a hard-to-find place on the watch, not the computer with all the other settings, to enable the new \\"device\\". Inexcusably bad
3)$70(!) for the HRM strap
4)Admittedly not advertised for use while riding a bike but that doesn't excuse the stupid tap feature for starting laps. Every time I go over a rough patch on the road the shock starts another lap, LOL
5)The watch correctly clocked my 32 minute bike ride but the online record stopped at 21 minutes when the GPS signal got lost. My Garmin, like all GPS watches, would also lose the signal here and there but it just registered the glitches, it didn't completely stop!
6)I run in elapsed-time mode but when I manually set a lap I want to see a 2-second flash of the current lap time, this is typical on other watches, but the Nike just flashes the lap number. Arggh!
7) Lap times are only tallied in tiny letters that scroll by on the bottom of the \\"history\\" setting. They are not uploaded to the software!
8)Loved the easy access to tech support but I had to twice ask if they were even familiar with the watch because they seemed largely unaware of how the watch and software worked
9) Agree with others: strap is too short for larger wrists or when wearing a jacket

product_title: Phantom Aquatics Velocity Scuba Snorkeling Dive Mask
review_body:
I swim about 1.5km-2km a week in a 25-meter swimming pool for self-paced cardiovascular fitness. I tried this product because regular swim goggles weren't working for me. Regular-sized swim goggles would press against the sides of my eye sockets and give me a splitting headache. Does the Aqua Sphere Vista Swim Mask work? Well, yes and no.

The mask is comfortable. The rims of the mask fit around your forehead and below your eye sockets. The size of the rim distributes the pressure evenly around your face, so there is little discomfort even if you have the mask cinched really tight. You also don't get \\"raccoon eyes\\" from this mask. The mask isn't perfect, however. It slowly leaks. At least, I think it does. The mask is somewhat hot because of its size, so the water slowly collecting around my eyes may be sweat, not pool water. I'm not sure. Anyway, I have to empty the water out of the mask every 10 minutes or so. In addition, the mask can really fog up sometimes.

So, in summary, it's a comfortable mask to wear, but it has some flaws. In the long run, it has helped me enjoy fitness swimming more. I'm still, however, looking for the optimum solution for protecting my eyes.
