product_title: GolfBuddy Voice GPS
review_body:
I have resisted buying a gps or laser rangefinder for many years. I had no use for a clumsy device that I would surely lose. Not to mention the time and effort to use it. Then I read about a gps device called \\"I am Caddie.\\" It sounded great. It was small, light and clipped to the visor of my golf hat. All I had to do was push a button and it would tell me the distance to the center of the green. On the way to buy \\"I am Caddie\\" I ran across the Golf Buddy and bought it instead. I am glad that I did.

The main reason I chose Golf Buddy was the display. I didn't have to push a button. The distance was always on display. I had the choice to remove my hat and read the distance, or push the button and hear the distance. The same button would toggle between center, front and back of green. The distance is accurate and quickly displayed. You can walk toward the green and see the distance change. The battery lasts more than 36 holes per charge and it seems like every course is already in Golf Buddy. There is nothing to download.

There is one flaw. The Golf Buddy automatically recognizes the tee that you are on and automatically gives you the distance to that hole. If you hook or slice your shot onto or near another tee, the Golf Buddy will change holes. This can be an inconvience. But, as long as you do not stray onto another tee, you could play an entire round without ever touching the Golf Buddy. One final note, I can't tell that I am wearing the Golf Buddy on my hat.

product_title: Winchester Big Daddy 7-M Gun Safe; 54 Gun Capacity (Black) (Mechanical Lock)
review_body:
After shopping for months I ordered this safe from Amazon. As pictured above, the interior is configured with two \\"easy access\\" gun racks and a narrow shelf system. This is the only image of the safe used by Amazon and by Winchester Safes. The same photo was even glued to the front of the safe when it arrived. Imagine my surprise when I opened the safe and discovered that the interior contains only a horizontal shelf with \\"layered\\" notches for stacking long arms, one in front of the other. No easy access racks, no narrow shelf. I understand that Amazon only commits itself to the written description of a product, not the image, but I'm disappointed that they use an inaccurate image, with no contradictory/clarifying written description. Amazon did offer a small partial refund.

I'm very disappointed with Winchester Safes service, and I would not recommend their products to others. After telephone calls and emails in which I asked for the parts to configure the safe as advertised, and then offered to buy the parts to configure the safe as advertised, Winchester ultimately informed me that the interior pictured in all the advertising photos for this product is a one-off custom design used only to stage advertising photos, and is not even available for purchase at additional cost. Their advertising is misleading, and they made no effort to stand by their product. I do not plan to buy their products again.

product_title: Trail-Gator Child Bike Tow Bar
review_headline: More difficult to ride with than attachment bikes
review_body: This is installed on my husband's bike and my (45 lb) son's bike.  I had previously been using an attachment bike at my family's house (I won't mention which bike as I think the difference would be standard with any of them).  My son's bike with the Trailgator leans back and forth to a greater degree than the other attachment bike, and this is due to play in the Trailgator arm rather than how firmly it is attached.  I also find that it is much more difficult to go around corners with this bike.  The child bike goes out to the side much more than an attachment bike, and my husband actually jackknifed the bikes going too tight around a corner (at a slow speed - he hurt himself, my son not so much as he was behind.  I think he turned left, and the child bike was to the left and swayed slightly to the right, and my husband lost his balance and fell forward/sideways).  We will still use it to ferry son/bike to the bike park, but we may go ahead and buy an attachment bike for longer trips that would involve bike lanes in a small city.  I don't mean to be overly dramatic, just to point out the cornering issue.

review_body: Got this laser and installed it. Used a bore sight to zero it in. product_title: Black Diamond Icon Camping Headlamp
review_body:
I own the black diamond storm, that uses 4 AAA batteries and gives 100 lumens. I mainly use the light for cycling at night in addition to gearing up for night dives.

The Icon 200 lumens is brighter in every mode, including the red night vision mode. However, as noted in other reviews, the center spot is not as focused and gives a wider area of cover. For cycling this works actually great as more of the road is covered. In heavy mist and rain it can cause a bit of light to be reflected back and the light not to be able to penetrate far, however, for normal every day use it is perfect. With the wider beam it makes it also easier to find gear when looking around as i find my vision tends to get focused when using a narrow beam light.

At first i thought the unit would be uncomfortable with the larger batteries, but it is actually more comfortable than the smaller unit that carries the lighting unit and the batteries in one housing. The only thing about the light that worries me is the simple catch that closes and holds the lid on the battery compartment, i have my doubts as to how long it will hold, as it does not seem robust, but i may be wrong there.

All in all a very good light and very powerful, but does take up some space to carry. The black diamond storm is a very powerful light that can easily slip into a pants pocket or clove box for when needed.

Review update.
I normally cycle at night alone, but did a ride with a friend the other night that had forgotten her light at home. The Icon had a large enough beam to light up the road easily for both of us cycling next to each other, without me needing to turn my head in her direction. Highly recommended for cycling and walking.

product_title: Sport-Brella Umbrella - Portable Sun and Weather Shelter
review_headline: Too Honest Review But I Like It
review_body:
I went to San Diego this September didn't bring a shade source for the beach so I went to every store I could think of and everyone had replaced their summer seasonal products with yep X mas paraphanalia so I tried a pool store and found this cute \\"shadebrella\\" as I call it for $39.99 on end of season clearance marked down from $79.99 (not worth that IMHO). I purchased two one for me and another for a gift.

Unless you are really really good theres no way you can get it set up in three seconds as the video denotes. I agree however it is easy enough...you open it like a normal umbrella, remove the clips that keep the two flaps anchored down from the top, lower the pole by unscrewing the knob, secure it with the stakes and string provided and bingo your good to go.

Some issues:

Pole doesn't always come automatically down I had to get assistance from my husband.
The clips are a cheap plastic and not easy to open so I will be replacing with light weight aluminum or galvanized steel ones.
The string provided is very thin and stringlike I had to untangle many times so I will also replace with a light weight rope and make my own.
The carrying pouch for the stakes and the umbrella itself aren't as heavy duty as I would like. The stakes are metal and pointy and can do lots of damage without coarser fabric for protection.
The stakes are too short and cannot possibly keep this brella from blowing away on a good wind especially in sand so I made bags that I can fill with sand or rocks and tie to the the flaps or place in the pockets of the brella to anchor. I luckily have all this stuff hanging around the house to make these changes so it's not big deal or expense.

One day at the beach there were 4 adults and two large dogs utilizing it as an umbrella with the flaps secured with the string. Another day we pitched it as a dome and there were two of us adults laying down comfortably. Note short beach chairs are great I don't recommend tall ones it's just to cramped overhead.

In closing should the company incorporate the above mentioned changes for their next version I think they can get the $80 but until this time I think I paid a fair price and wouldn't recommend taking the chance spending any more than I did. Enjoy

review_body: I decided to write this review after noticing some of the poor reviews here. I have never had a problem with the FT7 detecting my heart rate, or tracking my heart rate accurately. It never loses the heart rate (at least that I'm aware of), and it never jumps to some crazy number like 250. I have NEVER washed it in the washer. I rinse it in the sink in warm water after each use. All I've done is replace the batteries. The one problem is in the pool. I have a salt water pool and for whatever reason, the transmitter loses it's link to the computer. The FT7 is supposed to be suitable for swimming, but mine cannot be used in my pool. The website states that chlorine or salt may interfere. Most pools have chlorine. Chlorine creates salt in your pool. Therefore the only suitable place would be lakes, rivers, and ponds. The chlorine/salt issue should be clearly stated on the polar product webpage and in the polar user guide. Not in the FAQ's on the polar website. Other than that, the watch has worked flawlessly for just over 2 years now. I'm satisfied.

I adjusted the qd lever pretty tight, resulting in only a 1/2\\" down shift after removal and re-install. I would suggest if you buy one go ahead and get the other, you will not be disappointed.

**UPDATE** I am still truly loving this scope. I have used it for hunting and target shooting on my .308. It holds zero and I have the removal an replace shift down to .25\\" @ 100 yards straight down, if I am in a hurry. If I properly take my time, there is no shift at all. review_body:
Let me be frank. I started collecting knives this yea and in that time I learned about all the steel, etc. This was my first serious folder as it's well priced and there are glowing reviews. Well during a routine cut to break down some frozen pork ribs to eat later that day, I went to stab the the rib meat and what would you know the knife liner failed and I almost lost a finger. My only saving grace were my gloves; if it wasn't for my gloves giving people the bird would be a lot easier :P

Also 440a stainless steel is feels like garbage if you don't sharpen it right. As of today all of my folding knives are vg-10 or better and those knives I own with a liner lock which now I always inspect better be a \\"Bank Vault\\" because I'm seriously not going through the thought of losing a finger again due to poor craftsmanship.

P.S.
I will post a video of the liner lock failing by using just force of hands. THIS IS WORST KNIFE I HAVE! If you're having thoughts of buying your first knife, get a Benchmade Mini Griptilian or a Spyderco Endura FFG or Delica as the metal and lock up make a huge difference, also who cares about deployment as most of the time other deployment systems only take .5 secs longer. Save yourself a finger.

P.S.S.
I do have another Kershaw Knife, the [[ASIN:B0080IYV3Q Zero Tolerance ZT0350TS G10 Handle with Speed Safe and Tiger Stripe Blade (Non-serrated)]] a great knife despite what Nutnfancy has to say about it imo. his worst review. product_title: Benchmade - Rift 950-1 Knife, Reverse Tanto
review_body:
This is a really awesome knife, if you can get it for under $150 it is worth every dollar.

The Axis Lock easily makes this knife completely worth it. So far my favorite lock design on the market. It is a really great feature that allows you to open and close the knife very fast with some practice and timing the lock. Locks up securely with NO wobble.

The 154CM blade is pure success. Excellent, sturdy shape. Razor sharp I popped a bunch of hairs easily with next to no pressure applied. Very easy to sharpen as well because it is premium steel and does not fold or chip unless you are abusing it.

The G10 handle looks awesome and provides great grip. It has some very cool texturing to enhance grip and looks.

The pocket clip can be mounted on either side, but only for point up carrying, as the clip would interfere with the Axis Lock were other sets of mounting holes to be present.

Fantastic knife that is available in several versions with different grip colors and lock features.

product_title: NcStar Deluxe Folding Rifle Bipod
review_headline: Good enough but not for hunting
review_body: If you're looking for an inexpensive bipod for the range, this will work.  If you're trying to score a high quality bipod for varmint hunting, save your money. It rattles and the legs extend when you don't want them to.  It DOES NOT FEEL AT ALL SOLID UNTIL YOU SET UP with the weight of the rifle on it.  If you're moving through brush you will wish you didn't have this on your gun.  If you're planning on showing it off to your friends, they will laugh at you.  It feels cheap and it definately cheapens down your rifle.  But if hunting is not in your future and you're not trying to impress anybody, you will get a steady platform to shoot from once you're set up.  DO NOT consider this as a swivel bipod.  And remember, it's around $20!  For the price, you get what you pay for.

Lyne C. & her pups

product_title: Butler Creek Cobra Sling 36" x 1" Padded Tan
review_body: First off, I write my reviews and rate my purchases based on a quality to cost ratio and a comparison to competing products.  Most very good quality leather slings are pretty expensive.  That being said, for under $25, this sling gets a 5 star rating.  Now, if it was $50 and up, we would be looking at less stars.  For the money, however, this is a great sling.  It is comfortable and functional and it looks great on my Ruger 10/22 with a walnut stock (any rifle or shotgun with a wood stock has to have a leather sling to compliment it, in my humble opinion).  I like the design on the wide shoulder section and I also like the brass colored screws (not sure if they are real brass).  Keep in mind, though, that this is not a target shooting sling.  It is a carry sling.  It is designed for supporting the rifle's weight over your shoulder.  It is not designed for quick adjustment (requires tools) or for stabalizing your support arm.  In a pinch, you can wrap the sling around your support arm to help stabalize the rifle.  However, in my experience, the length the sling needs to be for shoulder carry does not lend itself well to stabilizing (not the right length).  Something else you should know; it does not come with sling swivels.  This is no big deal to me because my rifle already has them permanently attached.  All around, for a nice looking, affordable leather sling for carrying your rifle for casual varmint hunting, this does the job nicely.  I would highly recommend it for those purposes.

While being more than I wanted to spend for a knife, I now consider this a very good investment. Out of the box, the Native5 feels great when held, well-balanced, and very strong.  It is solidly built and the blade is very sharp out of the box, cutting effortlessly through paper and a few boxes here at work. I'm no expert on the blade steel, I just sought out the current best now, S35VN, and I can notice that the blade is far different from even steel on high end kitchen knives I have - this feels denser and heavier for its relative size. This also carries very well in the pocket, whether it's clipped on or not. I can think of nothing I would want more out of this knife. Like the other reviewers said, it's perfect. product_title: TYR Women's Durafast Elite Solid Crosscutfit Workout Bikini
review_headline: By far my favorite workout suit but you have to know how it fits when you order.
review_body:
This suit is not designed for cross training, so I don't know what the 1 star review lady was thinking running around in it. I could probably do it, but I'm not very large across the bust.
I'm a swimmer by trade and the suit is everything I expected it to be. It's not a recreational suit, so the top will fit like a compression top (aka= like sports bras) like typical swimmers suits.
I'm smaller busted, small B, with a larger back. The top is a great fit, although it's not designed for a larger busted woman- If you're a C or larger, I would go for a different size cut- TYR has a few more modest cuts, this is not a modest suit, it cuts down pretty low. If you're fit, it's a really nice cut. It doesn't shift when I dive or fly, I could probably play polo in it (although it's not that snug that another player couldn't yank it off if I did decide to).
The bottoms are okay, they ride low (I prefer them that way) on the hips but have moderate coverage across the back so flip turning is not an issue. There is a draw string as well if you need it. The bottoms are snug as well, so if you have a little across the middle, it might not be too flattering, but it rides low enough that typically I don't expect it would be a problem.
I typically wear 28's in my competition suits and 30's for my workout and polo suits. In this suit I fit an xsmall, so it does run on the snug side. If you're not a swimmer translated to standard dress sizes, I wear 6 and typically wear small to medium shirts (closer to medium because of my shoulders).

product_title: Sugoi Turbo Tri Short
review_body:
I got a pair of these as my first tri shorts for a sprint I have coming up. So far I have done all three sports in them and they work very well for the shorter distances that I've done. I was a little worried about the chamois in this model after seeing other Sugoi models that had very think pads. Luckily the Turbo's pad is very thin and easy to forget about while swimming and running. If anything, it makes the shorts a little more comfortable. The rubbery band around the leg does a great job of keeping the shorts where you want them to be.

I've used them for one pool swim so far and didn't notice any ill effects. Nothing on the care tag says to stay out of the pool, but it's probably safer to not expose to a ton of chlorine.

The only thing I wish they did a little more of was compression. I ended up ordering the small size and it fits nice and snug. But you don't get the feeling of a good pair of compression shorts. I'd also like if the inseam was a little longer, but I would say that the product picture on Amazon is pretty accurate. The panels on the side (just behind your hip bone) get a little see-through when you stretch them, as others have commented. But it makes the panel look almost silver. I'd doubt most people would look twice.

I'd definitely buy these again.

product_title: Stamina In-Motion Elliptical Trainer
review_headline: Excellent for under-desk use, potential for more
review_body:
Like a few other people who bought this unit recently, I received the older model - without resistance bands. In the end, it does not matter. Now that I've used the unit daily for a week (roughly 12-13 hours of use because I spend a LOT of time at the computer), I like it so well, I have been doodling upgrades and those new resistance bands are not where I'd put them at all. Small hand weights would be better than bands where they are now.

I got the Stamina even though I don't really like little exercise gear (I just bought a Hoist Multi-Gym) because I had a mystery lower back pain I blamed on sitting at the computer too much. Trouble is, I won't be quitting the computer any time soon and I'm bad at remembering to take breaks. So... that Hoist Gym will sit and sit most days. And I will sit and sit at a computer most days. I figured, \\"While I'm sitting, I might as well get in a little movement.\\" After looking at various alternatives, I decided to try the Stamina.

In two days, my lower back/hip pain disappeared. Now that I've done a few diagnostic stretches, I think my hip adductors on one side were protesting being plopped into a chair for too many hours daily. Adding just a little bit of quiet activity has already helped.

Do buy the Stamina and keep it wherever you're sitting for long. USE IT! Once you start, you'll keep going. It feels easy and yet it gives you enough movement to prime your motivation pump.

I only discovered the tightening knob this morning! It offers enough adjustment to feel resistance. Without any adjustment, it already felt like a quality unit. The feel is like turning a pedal in thick honey, sort of quiet and heavy and slow. Like opening a bank vault door. Very fluid. Tiny whoosh sound. You can carry on an active computer Chat or Voice conversation without interference.

I position my feet at various spots. (By the way, you'll need at least slippers, bare feet will hurt from sharp ridges onthe unit's pedals.) I also pedal backwards rather often. I lean forward and back, I move my knees in for a while, out for a while, etc. I vary my position. I haven't done any standing exercises and I don't even care what the gizmo says about how long I've been on it. When I'm at the computer, I just put my feet on the Stamina and go until I feel like stopping. I'd say I go 5-15 minutes an hour. If all I get out of it is maintenance in flexibility, that more than justifies the price. I suspect there will be updates to this review as I get more time to doodle accessories. This one's a keeper if it stays functional through daily use.

product_title: All Aluminum 6061 T6 M Enhanced Trigger Guard
review_body:
The trigger guard in the picture looks nothing like what was shipped. The one in the pictures looks identical to my Magpul guard. Given the price and the reviews that said they're identical, I ordered two.

What I got looks almost like the letter 'U' - far different from the Magpul-style guards. Not the sleekest look, but still better than the stock guard. It looks like the Blackhawk! trigger guard that sells for about $5 less than what I paid for each of these. I wouldn't be surprised if it is. I thought maybe they shipped the wrong parts, but both were labeled \\"T6 M Operator Enhanced Drop In Trigger Guard.\\" So, we're not talking about a shipping mix-up, but a deliberate attempt to sell something different than what's shown and described.

OK, so it wasn't what I ordered, but I figured I'd install them anyways to see how they hold up. Anyone that has put together a lower knows how anxious you get when you're one part away from finishing a build. When I went to put the roll pins in, though, they fell about 90% of the way through the guard. One quick tap and a pin was all the way in, but quickly fell out the other side when I shook the receiver. I could literally push a roll pin in by hand. So, the pins that shipped with mine weren't in spec, either. I ended up using the roll pins from my stock guards just to get them installed.

As another reviewer mentioned, the front of the guard has a push button like the stock guard. However, you can't actually drop the guard - the end of the guard that acts like a \\"Gapper\\" is too thick to pivot around the roll pin. You can drop the guard maybe a 1/2 inch.

Ultimately, I blame myself for trying to save a few bucks over just buying the real deal Magpuls.

product_title: Tetra Gun 004B1I Gun Grease 1-Ounce Blister
review_body:
Grease or Oil? Grease has some advantages over oils. Probably of biggest concern is long term weapon storage. Grease has a complete advantage over oil in that situation, as oils will harden, drain, and evaporate rather quickly (in a matter of weeks or even less) while grease will maintain itself over even periods of years. Conversely, grease also maintains its lubrication better during periods of extreme heat through heavy use and in many cases is more resistant to being used in a wetter climate or environment.

That is not to say that oil is bad. Oil does have an advantage when it comes to colder temperatures. Oil is easier to use and apply \\"in the field\\" without stripping a weapon down and can be applied with a dropper, syringe, or a small spray bottle. As the oils slowly run out of the weapon during use, they can take carbon and other fouling with them and deposit it somewhere else besides just holding it in suspension in the action parts. Oil for use in firearms is also frequently enhanced with additives such as a cleaning solution, a carbon solvent, and/or a longer-term, more robust protectorant (ala CLP or Break Free). You can also combine the uses of oil and grease in the same firearm without any major effects as the use of one definitely does not preclude the use of the other. Some folks like the thought of \\"grease for moving parts that carry a load, oil for rotating and small parts\\".

No weapon has EVER been designed around a lubricant. You should always properly lubricate your firearms. Just don't feel you must always use oil or your firearm will disintegrate. Just know what you are going to use, know its advantages, disadvantages, and limits, and use it as it is intended, and either oil or grease will work fine.

This grease works great, is easy to apply, and will last a long time.

product_title: PSE Wave Right Hand Bowfishing Package, 40-Pound, Reaper H2O
review_body:
I love my PSE Chaos Pink Bow (standard Compound) and keep in mind that I have only been shooting since Oct. 11 and less than a year - so this is coming from someone \\"newer\\" to the sport. First, I will admit I am having to re-learn a lot of basics with this bow. I am still only using it for target practice before I try the complications of the actual \\"fishing\\" so I am just focusing on the basics of the bow.

The Good:

- The price is great for the bundling and I couldn't be more pleased! If you bought the PSE Wave and the AMS package seperately it could easily go over $450 plus. Just at my local stores, the AMS package is $179.00 and in addition the $250+ for the bow. Buying them together is the biggest bang for the buck. In addition, it comes ready to mount reel and all my local hunting shops recommned AMS kit highly.
- Since I feel comfortable with the traditional compound and my PSE, this really has helped me alot to feel like I'm \\"transitioning\\" into this new aspect of the sport instead of \\"jumping\\" head first so to speak. Besides junior fingerdraw bows, I have never used a Long Bow or a Recurve (even after watching Hunger Games). So it made me feel it wasn't too far from my comfort zone.
- I love that it is not in green camo or pink. What they don't tell you, it is little fish bones on a blue surface camo like pattern. It is awesome looking in person!
- All PSE bows are rugged! They stand up to the weather and more importantly - children dropping them!
-*** PSE has some of the best customer service I've ever experienced. They wrote me a hand-written post card for registering my previous bow I <3 PSE!!! ***

The Bad (or what I call Jen re-learning the basics and things I wished people told me before I became obsessed with this bow package):

- I jumped from a generic Junior Learning Bows (~17-20lbs) to my PSE Chaos (~37lbs). I was good at sighting by eye in *short* ranges with the Junior butnot the longer distances < 20 yards. With my PSE Chaos I have fairly tight groupings at ~30-40 yards on a bad day. With this bow I am still trying to break my reliance of having a sight and re-learning to correctly finding my sight points manually on the curve of the bow and looking down the string while in hold.
- By default, the bow comes at 40 lbs pull so if people shoot below that, you or a shop will have to adjust it (I have no shame admitting that I don't pull above 40). Sometimes you can get it to your previous weight if is less than 40 lb but right now my pull is definately higher than my standard compound at 37lb - I am guessing 39lb since I have only got one rotation down on the bow from factory.
- I got \\"coddled\\", \\"use to\\" or \\"lazy\\" by using a wrist release. I now have to relearn how to correctly finger-pull manually without the aid of a release. The great thing is - they have finger guards ON THE STRING for a three finger pull!
- I don't know if it the new bow syndrome, the extra lb pull, or just having only one CAM but I find this bow much more difficult for me to pull, hold form and then sight. This is the reason that I am starting slow with cotton targets before moving to actually aiming for fish.

In summary, this package, PSE and the vendor is awesome. It came in right away and perfect condition.

product_title: Finis SwiMP3.2G Waterproof MP3 Player
review_headline: Innovative product. Worked for 2 years as advertised.
review_body:
I really like the SwiMP3. It really does work as advertised and is the only such product I'm aware of that doesn't require you to wear a swim cap to keep the earbuds in. I have now had it for almost 2 months, and have used it probably 10-12 times, probably a total of around 300 minutes. I have not needed to recharge it yet. After tightening my goggle straps sufficiently, I had no problems with goggles leaking. Sound quality is good and I have not needed earplugs to drown out other noises - even splashing. Stays on fine with flip turns. Shuffle feature works properly. The only downsides are 1) it does not allow you to sync protected music files 2) the controls are (necessarily) limited. There is supposedly a way to switch playlists. It doesn't seem too hard, but I haven't attempted it. After reading some of the negative reviews, I was somewhat apprehensive about buying it, but with the awesome Amazon return policy, I felt reasonably comfortable at least trying it. I considered getting both this product and the other waterproof MP3s and seeing which one works best, then returning the other one (I've done this a few times with other products), but I really didn't want to use a product that required a swim cap, as all the competing products seem to require.

So far, only have used it in swimming pools. I'm taking it into the ocean next week. I'll follow up on this review if the device stops working then, or in the next year or so. But, so far, so good.

Update as of March 2013- I've used this for nine months now, swimming in pools and a little bit in the ocean and it continues to work well. It seems to have a good battery life (at least 10 hours, I'd say, maybe more).

Update as of February 2013 - After owning it about a year and 10 months, it finally died. Well, I can't get it to turn on and play music, but it still connects to and is recognized by my computer so I guess I could use it a weird flash drive or something... I'm downgrading my review to 3 stars from 4 stars since it should have lasted longer. It worked pretty well for a while.

product_title: Maxpedition Sitka Gearslinger
review_headline: Daddy Diaper bag feels like a beta test bag.
review_body:
I have had the maxpedition sitka gearslinger for just over a month now and the design idea and function shows great theory and promise. In practice this bag falls a little short.

Pros.
The side sling design allows for easy diaper changes, especially on the fold out diaper tables often of inferior quality in mens rooms.
Holds a ton of stuff.
This is one sturdy bag.

Cons.
Weight distribution is awful! There is no way to pack this bag to make up for it. Most shoulder sling bags have a tear drop shape allowing the majority of the weigh to fall across your hips. The tight rectangle of this design makes that difficult. The water bottle pocket is on the wrong side! It really needs to be on the hip strap side, it is very difficult to access while the bag is on, but more importantly with a full water bottle it throws off the weight distribution. I have taken to carrying a 6oz sippy cup in this pocket and attaching a water bottle with a carabiner to the opposite side for counter balance.

Desperately needs a waist belt. The running strap helps the weight distribution some but it still pulls awkwardly if you are carrying a water bottle. I have tried rigging one up. After all that is one of the benefits of a MOLLE system, but it is awkward and hangs at a weird angle when not in use.

Extremely uncomfortable when used with a water reservoir.

This bag is heavy. Sturdy design but way to heavy for a full day of carry.

All in all I think this is a great beta test bag, but with the issues I have listed it is not ready for release. For those considering this bag for concealed carry, I can't imagine it would be comfortable with a water bottle.

product_title: Thule Stacker Carrier
review_headline: 2 Kayaks on an SUV? No Problem!
review_body:
After much research we decided to take the leap and purchase the Thule Stacker Carrier along with the rockers that are sold separately. End result? Very happy kayakers. We have 9 and 10 foot Dagger Approach kayaks and this system works beautifully. We bought extra Thule straps for a total of four straps. I highly recommend four straps for 2 or more kayaks, and make sure you get the ones that have the rubbery cover over the hardware (we just got two more exactly like the included ones), that one simple feature has already prevented what I am sure what would have been a window glass repair.

I have this system on a 2007 Infiniti FX35 with a factory roof rack. When we first put it on I couldn't even begin to believe that it would be stable enough to hold kayaks on at high speeds but they do not budge, not even a little. In fact, I think I said \\"that's it????\\" and was a little concerned about it until we hit the highway, when I realized how stable the carrier really is.

It says you can use this for four kayaks, and I believe it is strong enough to do so, but you'd have to have a pretty big SUV to have the width to do that. I think three would be no problem for most vehicles, just slide the system further to the opposite side of where you are putting the two kayaks.

Added bonus: this was installed and ready to go in less than 20 minutes.

If you aren't convinced: I was driving with kayaks on the roof when a major storm that blew down trees and knocked down power lines started. Winds were reportedly 40-80 mph. It felt like I had a sail or two on top of the car but the boats didn't budge.

They're decent, and pretty sturdy. And worthy for airsofting. But at high precautions of eye protection,I would say wearing safety goggles under the mask. I tried it, and it still fits comfortably. Decent, cheap, and neat mask here people. Still, there are better masks for a little more expensive.

review_body: I am of the opinion that the best cleaning kit is the one that use.  To that end, I like to have a cleaning kit that is easily transportable, and that means something that breaks down to carrying-size.  Enter the need for a multi-piece cleaning rod.  I know there is debate on what material to use, aluminum, steel, carbon fiber, or brass.  I am in the brass camp because there is less likelihood of a brass rod damaging my steel firearms.  The rod itself is a keeper--well made and durable.  I have used this brand for several years in rifles, pistols, and shotguns, both in and outside the military with no problems (well, one rod broke but that was due to another Soldier attempting to use a size-too-large cleaning patch in an M4 rifle, which was predictably a bad idea and I can't blame the rod for that at all).  The accessories included are all plastic and should be considered throw aways in my opinion.  Buy the rod, make it part of your kit and then buy quality brushes and brass cleaning jags and you will have everything you need to make your firearm run cleanly and reliably.  Edit 9-18-15-I am now on my third rod from this manufacturer, having placed them in each of my cleaning kits for all categories of work and my fun kit.  I like them that much and cannot recommend them enough.

product_title: Go-Ped Know-Ped Kick Scooter (Multiple Colors)
review_headline: You get what you pay for
review_body:
First off, this is not a cheap scooter, either by price or construction. I recently bought one for myself and ended up buying two more for family members who once they had given it a spin wouldn't go back to their BMX style scooters. Some impressions of the Knowped after having it for about a month...

PROS: The rubber tires and front and rear brakes are what make this scooter feel so much safer and smoother than the typical Razor-style design. I scoot on uneven surfaces a lot and never worry about tumbling, even going up driveway curbs. This is not a small issue for me as I've been pitched head first by pea size gravel while traveling by Razor before and no thanks to that happening again. I've no fears about the Knowped's ability to handle rougher surfaces without the drama I'd get from a scooter with polyurethane wheels.

Made in the USA! You kind of pay a premium for this privilege nowadays, but I'm proud of my homegrown scooter and its solid production values. It neither looks like nor feels like a toy.

Replacement parts can all be bought from GoPed or their dealers, if, on the off chance, you need them.

The KnowPeds I've purchased from Amazon all come with a black nylon strap attached to the steering bar. When the bar is folded, the strap loops easily around the stomp break for carrying. Other reviews mention a metal clip or connector for this purpose, but it's clear that they've changed over to the strap since then.

Fun! I look for excuses to go places on it. Walking just doesn't seem to cut it for me anymore!

CONS: The wood deck is very nice looking and feeling, but I wouldn't mind if it were around 7\\" wide vs. 9\\" wide. I have slim size 8.5 feet and they both fit easily on the deck with a little room to spare. I'd trade that roominess, however, for a slightly more streamlined deck shape. If you have larger feet, you'll probably appreciate the generous width.

The trade-off in having safer rubber wheels is a slight loss of speed. But I only noticed this when kicking up hill. Hills that would only take 10 kicks or so with the razor take maybe an extra 2-3 with the Knowped. And I'm talking \\"real world\\" surfaces here, so uneven sidewalks and bumpy roads. On downhill and flat surfaces, speed differences are noticed hardly if at all.

It really ought to come with a bell and handlebar streamers (I'm just typing stuff now to see if you are still paying attention).

Overall, I'm a big fan already of the Knowped. I can't say I'd recommend it to a person much taller than 6' or 300lbs. Our heaviest rider clocks in just under that and has no problems. Our lightest rider at 80lbs and 4'8\\" has no problems riding either.

product_title: KR25-BRK Mithrodin Sword
review_headline: A great prop/display item, well built and great design.
review_body:
Hello,
For those into fantasy swords, this is a nice one. Though prop only, don't swing it around for obvious reasons and some reasons bellow.
I'd give it a 4.5.

Pros:
- Quality seems to be very good, very sold construction, no odd gaps, blade doesn't wiggle or the like. Construction way better then those $30 prop Katanas ... but don't hit anyone with it, doubt the steel is made for hitting things (though it feels like it can do some major damage).
- Leather work is nice, braided, comfortable.
- Sword design is great, best I've seen yet to my eyes, but it's a very personal preference.
- Details on the blade and metal work are great, not sure if they spell anything out, but looks cool.

Cons:
- The balance of the sword is wwaaaaay off, it feels like the handle is empty, feels like an axe really, but you are not going to be swinging it around, so it's not a big deal, your display case won't care.

Minor Cons:
- It's a touch heavy to be a real sword, balance non-withstanding, it's heaver then you could comfortably lift with one hand and run around for an hour (not that anyone would do that).
- There was a tiny drop or two of what looks like hot glue on some of the metal, but cleans off easy enough.
- It took a bit longer to ship then I expected, not sure why, possibly because it's a sword and customs may need time or the like, don't know.

Notes:
- Because it's a prop it's not sharpened along the edge, but the very tip of it is incredibly sharp, so watch out what you're poking with it, I'll go through your dry-wall wall no problem.
- There are various limited editions of this thing available, for considerably more money, but I think those are only worth it if you're into the mythology of the thing.

If you like how it looks, this is a great quality prop sword.
Is it worth $100 (cost at time of writing)? ... I think you get what you pay for, so yes, it'sworth it.

I'm happy with it.

review_headline: Nice hat for someone with a small head
review_body:
I ordered two of these hats with expedited shipping. Being a unisex hat and me being a women with a slightly above average head, I figured it would be big enough right? I was wrong! I can barely squeeze it on my head with it at its largest adjustment. Also, the sweat band is rough and scratchy. Then there was the fact that the wire rim was bent in shipping and I have not been able to get it bent back into a useable shape even if I wanted to use them for someone with a smaller head. Also, I told my son I had a great hat for him for when it got rainy. When I tried it on him though, he said that the hat hurt his head because it was too small and uncomfortable. So there you go!

When I contacted the seller for a return (which is hardly worth it at this point anyhow) they wanted me to take pictures of the product and packaging so that they could file a claim with the shipper. Well, I have better things to do with my time, so in the kids costume drawer the $25 + $12.99 shipping hats went.

product_title: 3 Exercise Bands (Light, Medium, Heavy) and Door Anchor
review_body: First off let me say this equipment is great, my life style revolves around physical activity and overall health. I love to be healthy and to go to the gym, these 3 stretching bands are better than any other stretchers I have used better than Gold Gym, Valor Fitness, etc. I have tried many stretch bands but this is the only one I don't snap in half like a rubber band. Best part of it is that you don't get one level stretcher that might be too hard for some people, you get three! Bump up your resistance through just switching the bands, and the quality on these bands are great 3 years of daily use thank you Rockhard Fitness I will definitely look for more products!!!

product_title: Marksman 1073 Grizzly X2 DC Air
review_body: UPDATE: Got this at Wally's for $114 on a whim. It took about 200 or so rounds to break in. You WILL need blue Loctite to keep the 3 barrel screws in place. I put about 1500 rds through her now and I can do 0.5 inch groups or better in my basement 10 meter competition range - offhand, and the same hole cloverleafs from a benchrest!. I was also surprised at how well this gun performs outside. Consistent X-ring at 40 yards! I found that my gun does not like the pointed or domed pellets, so I shoot wadcutters and "hollow points" exclusively. Good looking, and has a  nice heft to it. No problem with the trigger for me, but I did replace the scope with a Barska 2-7x32 airgun scope and Simmons air gun rings. Like another review said - its hard to put it down once you find that sweet spot and I'm stocking up on my pellets too! Would definitely buy again!

product_title: Shiny Black ® Fiberglass Target Practice Arrows 22" for Children (1 Dozen)
review_body: These arrows were fantastic! Good Quality, and even though they're for practice, they pack a punch on my bulls eye target. Please bring them back on the website, I would love to buy more of these!!! Please? Thanks. :D

product_title: 5.11 Tactical Women's Taclite Pro Pants
review_body: My daughter wears these for work at the police department.  She likes the fit better than the brand the PD currently buys, and is lobbying for a change.  They are not as high waisted as other brands, making them more comfortable around the middle. They never wear out, they fade very little over time, and can be died back to original color easily.

review_body:

product_title: The North Face Recon
review_headline: Great, although, it hardly fits a 15in Computer..
review_body: It is by far the best backpack I've ever owned. It's also great to get a little discount off of what the retail price is on NorthFace website. I do have one hitch though. The backpack doesn't fit a 15 inch MBP Retina computer even though it is advertised as fitting 15 inch computers. I was a little disappointed by that since i bought it mainly for school use. review_body:
The unit is well packaged. It has reasonable and clear instruction for assembling.

Do not take a chance to assemble it alone. When you have it completed you will find out you have paid right amount of money in comparing with cheaper versions.
Thanks Amazon for free shipping .

product_title: Thera-Band Exercise Balls - Pro Series SCP-85cm-Silver
review_headline: Compares very well to other exercise balls including other Thera-Band balls
review_body:
This big silver ball is from Thera-Band's Professional series versus their Standard series. The Professional series is supposed to be twice as thick and is certainly a heavier and thicker material. Most Thera-Band balls are Standard and I have two of those, the green and blue Standard balls. I use these balls every day.

One of the ways I use this silver ball is actually as a chair, or seat right at my desk. I believe this is the most common use of this heavy weight-bearing ball with the interesting potential side benefit that as furniture it \\"might\\" qualify as a business expense.

The manual that comes with the ball has illustrations of many potential exercises. My favorite exercises involve using ankle and hand weights at the same time with my chest on the ball and also with my back on it.

Compared to other exercise balls, I found this one to be a good deal and also excellent for sitting on.

product_title: Harbinger Padded Leather Head Harness
review_body: Packaging was easy to unwrap. Item is very durable and strong. Would recommend this to anyone looking to strengthen their neck, you won't find a better product for it.

review_body: It was simple to put together.  My only complaint is that it's very difficult to lower or raise the goal with only one person.  Otherwise, great buy.

product_title: Mil-Tec Military Army Patrol Molle Assault Pack Tactical Combat Rucksack Backpack Bag 20L Black
review_body:
I wear this every day at work to carry about 20 pounds of tools with me as I move throughout the workplace, because I have to move from place to place on treks of a 1/4 mile or more. I've recieved a lot of compliments about it from other technicians.

The materials are thick and it looks like it will last a long time. Its definitely a cut or two above the typical bag someone carries their books around in at school. The straps, material, zippers, and stitching are much more robust.

It looks new after several months of use. Its a great bag. For the price of 20 something US dollars I paid, what I got is just astounding. I would expect this to cost $60 at least.

It is somewhat smaller than the typical backpack, so make sure its the right size for you.

EDIT 11-22-2015: Still using this bag 5 days a week to carry 20 lbs of tools around and except for a couple very small punctures caused by falling a few feet to the ground with the tools in it, its still like new.

product_title: Attwood 8MOO28330 Safari 2 2-Blade Weedless Propeller with 3.5-Inch Diameter, Black Finish
review_body: It has done a better job than the three blade prop but still will get boged down in the thick stuff. I gave it 4 stars because it eliminates most of the headaches. review_body: I recently purchased a Yakima Double-Down 4 for my 2009 Honda Element EX. Build quality is readily apparent and the simple fittings are a welcome change to my old bike rack. The rubber straps are well made and I really like how, at the press of a single lever, the rack swings down for me to access the tailgate. Well done, Yakima. Wishlist item: Yakima could improve on their powder coat finish to extend the life of the rack. it is, after all, mounted to a hitch and at the rear of a vehicle, therefore exposed to metal to metal contact with frequent on/offs and the elements.

product_title: UTG Adjustable Leg Holster for Pistol/Flashlight/Laser
review_body: Ok first of its not a $150 tacticool ultrabrand name gizmo BUT for what it is and what I needed it is great. My teen daughter is using it for her Ruger SR9 with taclight. I am considering getting one for my secondary pistol and old G17 that has to have an aftermarket rail to hold a light. product_title: Sher-Wood T30 Composite Stick [SENIOR]
review_headline: Lasted 10 days on an our door Inline Rink
review_body: I bought this stick because I needed a good budget stick to play on an outdoor rink.  I did not tape the blade up and played it raw against the painted smooth concrete surface.  The stick lasted til day 10.  My other composite stick (not going to mention) only lasted 5 days.  So this stick really held up well. (or at least better than the last one)  There are some videos on u tube on this stick if you u tube my name they should come up.  For a budget stick this is a great stick.  I just can't see paying 200 bucks or more to use a stick on an outdoor surface.  The blade seperated after day 10.  I contacted Sher-wood and they are sending me out a replacement asap.  I didn't even have to send the old stick back (like i had to do with the last stick and it cost me over 17 bucks to ship it to them)  With that 30 day warrenty it definately makes me a future customer of sher-wood products.  The stick is longer than most but i didn't cut it.  Still worked well good flex and has like a normal mid kick point to the shaft.

product_title: Diamondback 2012 Women's Serene Citi Classic  Sport Comfort Bike (White/Teal)
review_body: Love this bike. First delivery was flawed with bent parts but amazon reshipped and picked up the faulty one. My bike enthusiast son put it together with ease.I love riding it. Easy and like the suspension. No owners manual however which is an error. overall a worthwhile buy. But check it before you assemble as I nearly gave up when the first one came. But due to excellent and fast amazon service I got the bike I wanted.

product_title: Body Vision PT600 Power Tower
review_body: This is an excellent and well built product for the price.  I bought it when it was $99 and it was well worth it.  If you have no other work out equipment in your home you should have one of these.  Pull-ups and push-ups as well as some ab crunches are just a few feet away for whenever you feel like doing them.  You need do only a few at a time.  After a while you'll find yourself needing to do it.  The tower is also great for stretching.  It was perfectly packaged with quality nuts and bolts clearly labeled on a blister pack.  Once together it is super sturdy.

product_title: UTG 126 Lumen Combat Xenon Light, Handheld and Ring Mount
review_body: An incredibly bright flashlight that works as intended. I put this on my M4 and I've had absolutely no problems with it. I highly recommend this for any military personnel or for home defense. The toggle switch is very easy to use although it does look a little flimsy.

product_title: Ultimate Body Press Dip Bar Fitness Station
review_body:
In order to keep young (spiritually, physically, mentally), I really believe in the idea of our bodies, therefore, needing to continue experiencing the physical \\"dynamics\\" of our youth, as well as the spiritual and mental \\"dynamics\\" we experienced in our youth.

...Such as laughing, smiling, joking, playing. Physically - running, JUMPING and CLIMBING (when was the last time you jumped or climbed?), and tumbling/hitting/taking a fall, for instance.

Similarly, I believe they are synergistic - both the physical AND spritual/mental are like ying and yang... one begets the other. If you are physically, \\"young,\\" you are more likely to be spirtually/mentally \\"young\\" and vice-versa.

I realized this lately after purchasing the product below, thank G-d. Among MANY uses (check out the promo video for ways to use, beyond dips), one I am finding particularly \\"youthful\\" is placing this device in front of an entranceway (say, from kitchen to living room).

As I walk into either room, the device is there. I grab on to the side \\"rails\\" and lift my self/my body weight up and over - in essence, elevating myself from one room to the other. It's simple, yet quite evocative of a youthful feeling.

The \\"dip rows\\" (see the video in the link) remind me of the feeling of climbing monkey bars, for instance.

I'm very satisfied, it's easily detachable, sturdy once you put your weight on it, storeable and portable - great tool contributing to my health... and spirit!

To life! :)

***UPDATE Feb 2013***
Orignially, I gave this device 5-stars: it does what it's supposed to and is convenient. Unfortunately, on the other hand, the device's lack of adequate and ergodynamic padding/hand grips put a beating on my wrists and hands through use over time, so I don't use the device anymore. I couldn't focus on my workout (what the device is for) without needing to stop to attend to the wrist and hand pain.

product_title: Body-Solid Pro-Style Commercial AB Board
review_body: I am 5'6\\" 140 lb female who was looking for a way to keep exercising while dealing with various leg/running injuries.  I wanted to intensify my ab workouts but wanted to keep the cost down.  I initially purchased a slanted bench for appx $40, which turned out to be very poorly made even despite the supposedly above-average reviews.  After significant reseach, I settled on the Body-Solid and really could not be happier.  Yes, the set-up directions leave something to be desired, but that has nothing to do with the bench's functionality and sturdiness once you do put the thing together.  Overall, very solid piece of equipment.

product_title: McDavid Neoprene 431 Ankle Sleeve
review_body:
I sprained my ankle two weeks ago and continually resprain it. I bought this to wear to feel more stable and prevent rolling. It WORKS! It's supposedly minimal support, but that's good enough and it easily fits when wearing shoes (thin). I'm a skinny adult male with big feet, but I guess this ankles - I got a medium and it was perfect.

product_title: Bionic Men's Driving Gloves
review_body:
I used to drive a lot as a consultant, and went through a lot of driving gloves to help cut down on hand fatigue. Never used Bionic, mainly deerskin and Italian leather traditional gloves. Last spring I wanted to get out of my winter gloves early but needed a little bit of padding for the white-knuckle mountain conditions I drive through and picked these up. Very impressed by the location of reinforcements, they really did figure out where traditional gloves wear and stress, and put a lot of effort into fixing those.

I won't claim these are the best gloves out there, but for the cost, they are very nice. I never had a pair \\"last\\" more that a year, and I think these will last 2.5-3.

product_title: Kershaw Ken Onion Blur Folding Knife with Speed Safe
review_headline: Best Spring Assisted Knife I've found
review_body: This is my EDC.  Period.  Haven't found one that can beat it.  Sorta don't want to.  For years I carried the Vapor 2.  My first foray into spring assit was the Leek.  The Blur is a whole different animal.  This knife means business.  From the weight to the reassuring snap when its deployed, this knife was built for combat situations.  The ability to carry point down is a big plus as well.  Highly Recommended.

review_body: Showed up on time (and quick!) was able to start right when I recieved it. Great product in great shape!

product_title: prAna Women's Kira Top
review_body:
Another great looking Prana top.
This fabric is comfy, cozy and soft; much more forgiving than the Quinn tops that Lycra binds you more like a straight jacket.
On the flip-side, the fabric is thinner in the mid-section, so may show a few more speed bumps than the Quinn would.

I ordered the white/large and I am a 5'4\\", 38C about a 32\\" waist and 142 lbs today.

My only complaint would be that there is some stitching that is prominent in the lower breast area...appears on both sides of my top, but can be seen on 1 side of the Model wearing the white top. A little distracting (1 less star for that).

product_title: Exerpeutic 400XL Folding Recumbent Bike
review_body: I really love this machine, have gone from doing 2 miles in about 14 minutes to doing 2.5 miles in under 11 minutes. Just needed something to get me going and I can do quick 10 minutes here and there. Being a full time caregiver for an elderly man leaves little time to exercise...This was a perfect choice for getting me back into moving my butt or rather legs and getting my heart rate up. The bonus is I can get him on it for 10 minutes of light biking just to get his legs going after sitting all day... I was a little nervous when I first got it and saw the instructions, thought I would have to call someone to help set it up, but after reading the directions, it only took me just under an hour. I leave it in the corner so I have easy access or can get my guy to get on it for his 10 minutes and he has Parkinson's...Definately would recommend it for starting an exercise program, beginners or home caregivers...

product_title: Bridgestone B330RX B Grade Recycled Golf Balls (Value Pack of 36)
review_headline: Not what was expected! More of a B330 mix
review_body:
When looking for a new ball to play, I heard so much about the B330RX. At over $40 a box, I figured I would give this set of B-grade B330RX balls a try. When delivered, I was disappointed to find that half of them were the B330 or the B330S (Which are geared for faster swing speeds). Of the rest, 2 were the 2012 B330RX balls with the new double dimple design, and about 3 or 4 were the older B330RXS (Spin) balls. The rest were the older model B330RX balls.
....For having expected a box of 36 B330RX balls, I feel that I was cheated out of what I had purchased.
The only bright side; I do get to try all the different B330 models. However the reality of it is I don't have a tour rated swing speed, so half of this box of 36 balls are really not geared for my game.

The quality of the \\"B-Grade\\" balls are fine. The equivalent of finding a keeper when hunting in the woods or tall grass for wayward tee shots.

product_title: Injinji 2012 Performance Lightweight No Show Toe Socks
review_headline: Work great in Vibram Five Fingers
review_body:
I use these in my Vibram Five Fingers mostly to keep them from smelling as fast. They work well for that, especially when it is hot out.

I don't like how I can't feel the ground nearly as well with them on, although I am getting more used to it. I have three pairs that I rotate between, I have worn them each about 5 times, and one pair is already developing a hole in between the toes. They will end up being very expensive socks if they don't last very long.

Pros:
-Keeps Five Fingers from smelling as fast
-Keep feet cooler in hot weather
-Help prevent blisters

Cons:
-Can't feel the ground as well
-One of three pairs has begun to develop a hole after a few uses
-Injinji logo is clearly visible above top of shoes

product_title: Ultimate Arms Gear Tactical Made In USA Machined Steel Phantom Flash Hider Choke Suppressor Muzzle Brake Compensator For AR15 AR-15 M4 M16 .223 5.56 Rifle ( 1/2"x 28 tpi)
review_body: This flash hider (I use the term loosely) will do the job for the amount i paid for it. I installed it on a Kel-Tec PLR-16. The flash is still a huge fireball that blinds me but thats honestly no big deal for me personally. Just know that you shouldnt buy it for that purpose or it will be a loss. Build quailty seems to be rock solid. Its very similar to some higher branded versions (YHM)but the finish is honestly aweful. The blueing on it is truley horrible. If it wasnt spotless with no dings, I would swear that it was used. I plan to redo it to solve the problem but i was immediately dissapointed when i pulled it from the box. Its just easier to redo with a pen rather than ship it back & wait for another. Its purpose was to give the PLR barrel an aggressive look & it does that. It also didnt include a crush washer. The description didnt list one but i assumed it would. No foul on that just a note to future buyers to expect to purchase one (They're only about $3). Overall, it will do for me because i hate returning items & already had my new gun in hand. I get the look i want (minus the finish)so im happy. Fixing it wont cost much. I would have to recommend that someone else look elsewhere however. Similar name brand brakes can be had for about $10-$15 more with the crush washer included & possibly a better overall finish. My Prime Account with 1 day shipping makes it hard for me turn down good deals on here vs. ordering elsewhere & waiting a week or longer to get some items so i suppose thats my excuse. Ive done it before & this wont be the last.

Upon opening my package today, there were scratches in the leather where the muzzle enters the holder, and there was an imprint of a previous pistol inside the holder. I'm disappointed, but the functionality of the holster is what I'm more interested in. Not the cosmetics. The two belt clips swivel. A little difficult to slide in/out of my pants, but secure. I know that I have to break in the holster, of which I suspected before buying. Back to the belt clips, there are five holes total to adjust the holder up or down in the waistband. Very useful. I added the Pearce extension to the magazine, and its not that obvious through my button-up t-shirt. Unless I sit down or crouch low to the ground. Overall, this is a great holster for the Taurus PT709 Slim. I gave the holster 3 stars because of the seller sending me a used holster.

product_title: Smith & Wesson SWMP1BS Military and Police Knife with MAGIC Assisted Open and Scooped Back Serrated Blade, Black
review_headline: Good knife; but save your Money
review_body:
This is a decent knife. But it has some serious flaws.

First is the blade shape. The scimitar design looks beautiful, but is an absolute horror to sharpen. I had to work it on a whetstone to get it sharp evenly. Also if you're not careful it can deploy in your pocket, cutting it to shreds. Lastly more than once it the tip of the blade nicked my wrist.

Second the safety. Its garbage. Literally dont bother. It has a mind of its own and can't seem to decide if it wants to work or not. The safety also has a sticking point where the blade won't open or close unless you wiggle the safety. This would just be annoying on a normal knife but its dangerous, because of the tip, on this knife.

Lastly the spring. The assist works....some of the time. About 70% of the time actually. The spring is very stiff out of the box. It took approx. 200 deployments and sheathings for the spring to loosen to a point where the knife was usable. Within the next 200 deployments the knifes spring became too loose and began not opening the knife at all. I wouldn't rely on rapid deployment in a 'situation.'

This is a knife that looks good, has good weight, but just can't stand up to the abuse that someone who puts it through its paces. Not recommended.

product_title: Weaver Gunsmith Modular Level System
review_body:
I bought these to level a scope, which is what they are intended to be used for, yes? These are extremely low quality. The level tubes fell out of the plastic holders multiple times. Fortunately, they snap back in. The magnets are on the little clip-on feet which makes them way too high to stick to the receiver if the scope is already on the gun. There are magnets on the plastic holders as well, but still, they're too high to fit under a scope when it's on the gun.

For basic scope-leveling, this might be okay, but I wouldn't expect great results out of it. Mine was never quite right as I don't think the tubes sit level in the bases which will give you an off-reading.

Stick with something else or go to a gunsmith and have them level your scope for you. My local guy will do it for like $5 or something and it's perfect every time. Save your money for ammo.

NOW THIS IS THE BIG ONE: the whole reason I needed to write this review is because a couple nights ago I threw a pretty bad pass that ended up curving down and left short of my target. The place it happened to slide down so perfectly was down a sewer drain on my road. It dove right in the back and straight into the water below. We got the grate up and climbed down(pretty gross) all the while the light was still on as it floated at the surface. We got it out turned it off just in case and it has been working great ever since!!

If only the fiber optics were made of a more rigid plastic, this frisbee would be absolutely perfect in every way!! Buy this if you're serious about having a legitimate light-up frisbee!

product_title: Ultimate Arms Gear Saiga Rifle & Shotgun Tactical 6 Position Collapsible Stock +Rear Pistol Grip
review_body:
I don't typically fill these out but I researched these types of stocks for my Saiga 223 a very long time before deciding to purchase the UAG. I'm hoping this review will help someone else make the same choice with less worry.
This stock physically fit the rifle better then the factory one. It is rock solid and very well made. I read a couple of reviews on this stock complaining about play in the stock. These are probably the same people that won't be satisfied until they've spent a good $300+ to pay for a name and they will no doubt still have issues. The positioning of the stock is straight off the rear of the receiver. I noticed some stocks \\"Tapco T6\\" slant downward off the receiver. This does not. The stock's shaft is metal and adjusts to 5 positions in approx. 1/2\\" increments. No play amongst the different length adjustments. You can hear and feel it lock securely in place at each position. It has the same 1/2mm of play as any other tactical stock I've experienced if not less. The pistol grip \\"SAW style\\" feels natural and the recoil pad seems high quality. Not that you really need a recoil pad with this rifle but it did aid in keeping locked in on target. It came with instructions that are easy to understand if needed. Installation is very straight forward and the stock came with a hex key. It is made here in the USA by a family owned business which is all the more reason to buy it. Although I didn't see a made in USA stamp anywhere on it. I would buy this stock again but I don't think I will need to for this same rifle. I hope this helps someone. Jason 33yo Missouri

product_title: Lindy Fishermans Series Drift Sock
review_headline: a necessity for all kayak fisherman
review_body: I have been using this drift sock for three months and am very satisfied with its performance. It is a standard part of my fishing kit and is deployed to reduce my drift speed whenever the wind is pushing me along (which happens quite often). Materials are all heavy duty reinforced plastic sheeting and nylon strapping; I expect them to last for quite a while. I use a carabiner to attach the sock to my anchor trolley. The lines on the sock are long enough that a kayaker won't need an additional harness though most boaters certainly will. You will also need to attach a dump line to the small end of the sock to facilitate easy retrieval, otherwise you will be pulling in a sock loaded with water. All in all, money well spent.

product_title: Hoopnotica Fitness Hoopdance Hula Hoop DVD Level 2 (Beginner)
review_body:
Let's get this out of the way first: I took off one star because of the quality. It's not very good. Everything is clear and I actually appreciate the minimalist approach (no distractnig backgrounds and only one hooper to watch), but the picture is pretty grainy at times and could use some serious touch up. So it isn't a perfect product, but I'm not getting an instructional DVD for the pretty picture quality.

Personally, I have a handful of years of experience hoooping. I actually make my own hoops for that purpose, so I went ahead and skipped to the second DVD, which features three things I've been having issues learning: Shoulder hooping, leg/knee hooping, and the vortex (it's not referred to as the vortex on the video, but it's basically a continuous corkscrew they go over towards the end of that section).

What I really loved about this DVD was the no frills instruction. They don't make up cutesy fun names. The names make sense and most of the terminology you'll see is the same or very similar as you'll hear in hoop communities and on youtube. This is helpful if you want to reference other videos online in addition to this one, and I suggest you should. Hooping is an art and it can be very different from person to person. You may find another explanation for a move that just clicks with you and helps you finally get something you've been struggling with.

In addition, while this is all available for free on youtube, there is the benefit of having the moves neatly organized so you don't have to spend forever trying to figure out what moves you want to learn, in what order, and what they are actually called so that you can find them.

I know they tell you not to hoop with the video at first, but I did, for about an hour. I found myself able to pull off and sustain most of the moves I'd been struggling with. There's also a troubleshooting bit after each section that aptly covers the most common problems with eachmove.

The narrator's voice is fairly pleasant and not overly cheerful. There is a small bit after each section that shows one of the women free-styling the moves you just learned, and her expression is a little forced cocky and can be a bit irritating, but that's it.

All in all, I was really impressed and felt like a great deal of information was aptly covered. For the price I paid, I think it was extremely worth it and will definitely be purchasing the next DVD.

product_title: Combat Sports Submission Man Dummy
review_body:
After being injured and in the beginning stages of starting a family, I realized that I can't make it to the gym as many times as I would like so I was in the market for a grappling dummy to at least do drills when I can't make it to the gym. The gold standard is a dummy that costs $500 to $600 but I wasn't willing to pay that much with no previous experience with a dummy. I mean, \\"a dummy is a dummy\\" right? Wrong! What made me purchase this dummy was the price and the cheap shipping. It was a lock! But not all dummies are created equal, and you get what you pay for.

Since it's one piece, there really isn't an armpit and the head and neck just don't feel right. The arms don't bend right either. The shoulders are big too. It was very difficult to perform armbars (from in the guard and in mount), and triangles too (since the shoulders are big, you can't even come close to closing your legs). After one failed attempt to workout with this thing, I sold it. Returning it would just be too expensive.

With all that being said, the seller was great. I had some shipping requests, and they replied promptly. The price of shipping was inexpensive for the weight of this thing (80 lbs). If you really want a grappling dummy, bite the bullet and spend the extra cash. I bought the gold standard, and it's great; awesome workout!

product_title: Nike+ SportWatch GPS powered by TomTom
review_body:
I felt the need to write a review on this product as I am shocked on its overall ratings.

Prior to this watch, I was using the sportsband watch, after 400ish miles I decided that seems about right for dedication and I wanted to up my game.

Fast-forward- I bought the watch the day before my April Fools race this year, it went swimmingly, and ever since then it has gone perfectly.

Stats currently: 3/1/12-7/13/12 400+ miles added

Battery life: Great, it has died once on me, and it was because it hadn't been charged in days other then plug in upload, unplug. I had a 13 miles run midday-95% humidity, I had to stop several times and hide under bushes for 30 minute slots! So, a 2 hour bit turned into a 4 hour horrific memory. I had .25 left to get to the destination and it turned off, I was fuming! I thought, fantastic, suffering and now it meant nothing towards my challenges on the Nike site. GOOD news: it sync'd! I thought it drifted into the unknown. :)

Design: I'm fond of the term sleek, fashionable-- What you really want to know? LIGHT! It's fantastic, I was apphrensive at first as I was using the sportsband and that is like two feathers entangled on a rubberband. However, one run and it felt comfortable.. Now my tan line seems largely legit ;) It fits perfectly, 11 optional rungs, if you will to find your nitch, I'm the 5th one in, relatively small wrist for a guy, but it is snug on there, no sliding.

Durability: Hm, I decided against running with this baby on the Tough Mudder in May as the support team said water resistant, not mud, electric, fear!! haha However, I've had my share of rainy days, nights, and good old fashion- jumping in puddles fun with this watch and it has had no effect.

Other goodies: Website has boosted my game, the \\"friendly\\" challenges offer inspiration to run further and include others. It recently had a makeover; making it even more accessible and easy to share via Twitter/Facebook. Setting up personal goals, recieving trophies; for a mostly solitary sport, it feels nice to feel apart of such a community.

Overall: Cake walk to use, 2 seconds to set up, to link up no more than 30 seconds, clear, tap on the screen to light, has never dropped signal (Have done my share of woods-running (Jersey, Wharton parks) Fantastic coach, really pushes you to the next level.

I hope this helps, folks! Take care.

product_title: Nathan Intensity Race Vest
review_headline: Wear it like a vest, not like backpack straps! The sternum strap works!
review_body:
To any of you worried about the fit, especially the sternum strap: Try adjusting it again! After seeing several reviews complaining that the sternum strap was nowhere near the user's sternum (even used as an under-boob strap), I was anxious to see how it would fit me. After fitting it to myself, I think all these women are all making the same mistake.

To avoid the problem, loosen all of the straps all the way, then put it on. That's right, move the little elastic holders and loosen every strap all the way. Now put it on. Line up the front of the harness as you wish to wear it, which will probably look more like a vest than backpack straps. There shouldn't be very much wrinkling or bulging of the material. Then, move the sternum strap sliders to the height you would like them (i.e. across your sternum), buckle the buckle, and tighten most of the slack out of that strap without tugging the sides closer together. Now tighten the other straps evenly (remember, there are two straps per side). Again, this is more like a vest than a backpack. It's okay that the pouches are in front of you - if they are to the sides, you'll interfere with your armswing.

When this pack is adjusted properly, it fits like a dream. It doesn't feel like I'm carrying all the water and supplies I need. Also, don't forget that the tube can be cut if there's too much length for you - just remove the bite valve and use sharp scissors.

product_title: JOOLA 40mm Table Tennis Training Ball 12 Count Set (1-Star) - Orange
review_body:
Table tennis isn't what it used to be, and it won't be this way for long either. Some time ago, the classic 38mm table tennis ball was altered to 40mm. The 2mm size differential changes the game, slowing it down to some extent and certainly making for ping-pong being a different sport than it was years ago. And immediately after the London Olympics, table tennis will change again. Celluloid will no longer be permissible for table tennis balls AND there will be yet another size change upward, though this one markedly less apparent than before. We're waiting to see what material will be used instead of celluloid, but now may be time to stock up on whatever 38's are still available as well as the current celluloid 40's just in case you end up preferring them to what is to come.

So all that said, here we have seamless orange 40mm celluloid balls which have given us no difficulty in terms of balance and longevity. With consistent daily use, we've noticed, if anything, a lower frequency of cracking than with other balls. Though marked as training balls, we've seen no difficulties that would prevent these balls from being used within game play.

product_title: Marinco On-Board Charging Inlets
review_body:

My solution was to install this plug through the fiberglass wall of the camper and hook it to an auxiliary (GFI only) plug installed inside. All I have to do is plug the male end of a 12-14 gauge extension cord into the 120 receptacle on the shore power post then plug the female end into the camper at this plug. This energizes the auxiliary plug I installed inside.

This plug is well constructed. Since it is made for a similar purpose on a boat, this plug easily installs with a hole saw and the supplied gaskets and stainless screws to seal out any weather.

I had to modify each one by bending up the retaining clip and slightly pinching the clip to make the track more narrow. Once loaded, it does take some force to push the rounds down into the firearm, but they all fed in and it was ready to go. An ideal way to store a large quantity of ammo for rapid deployment at a later date. Probably a waste of time if you are just shooting at the range. It's easier to just load the rifle directly (SKS anyway, cant speak for the AK).

Overall, typical Chinese product. Cheap. Does the job. Don't expect perfection.

product_title: HDE® Equalizer Sound Activated LED T-Shirt
review_headline: My Grandson Thinks I'm the Coolest Grandmother Ever
review_body:
I didn't buy this exact design - mine has headphones on a disco ball - but I figure the review will be the same for all of the HDE designs.

You put two AAA batteries in a small case, plug the connected cable into the image square, and jack up the music. I put on AC/DC's Hells Bells and found I had to put the image right in front of the speaker and really turn it up for it to work well. Fortunately, it lights up just as easily with human speech and I have a family full of really loud talkers so that baby should stay lit all night. Later I discovered the volume was turned down and it worked spectacularly when increased.

The design calls for you to place the image square on the shirt where you want it and to cut a hole where the cable will run from under the shirt to connect to the square. Should work fine although I'll reinforce the hole with a some iron-on tape.

The shirt is very soft, adequately sized and well made.

Had to lower the rating a couple of stars after my grandson tried wearing it for a party. Although it functioned well, the battery would fall out of it's little pocket and the stiff design was uncomfortable and wouldn't stay in place.
