product_title: Century BOB XL with Base Unit
review_headline: Fantastic - like it much more than a bag
review_body:
I hesitated purchasing this for quite a while due to the price but left it in my cart. A couple of weeks ago, the price dropped over thirty bucks and I couldn't resist any longer, especially with the free prime shipping. I had debated about getting the regular sized BOB (no lower torso portion) but I am glad I chose the bigger one. I received a call from the delivery people asking what day I could be home for delivery, although they did advise they could not provide an exact time. They arrived before 10a on the scheduled day; the delivery guy was super nice and there was no damage to the boxes. The base comes in a tall, hexagonal shaped box and BOB himself comes in a large rectangular box. Other than putting water or sand in the base, setup is easy as you just slip BOB over the base and adjust to the height you want.

You will definitely want a large funnel to help with putting sand in the base; I chose sand over water because although the base seems very thick and strong, I did not want to risk it springing a leak in my house. The larger BOB version is easy to punch and knee with ease. However, be forewarned for the first few days, you will jump or be startled every time you walk in the room where he is located. It took me about 3 days to get used to him, but visitors always freak out. LOL

I have punched BOB with my bare hands as well as with fingerless gel gloves and boxing gloves, too. I do not recommend using your bare hands as the texture of BOB can rub or irritate your skin after a few hits. All of my friends have had a go at BOB when they come over and everyone really likes him. There is just something about punching a life-sized and realistic object which far exceeds a bag for me. He is very well made and feels like he will last forever. Gloves do rub off or \\"scar\\" his skin, but that should be expected. I have a t-shirt on him for now, although I really like the feel of punching without it. I look forward to getting some great cardio workouts with BOB for a long time.kouts with BOB for a long time.

product_title: Altus Athletic 4-Inch Natural Lifting Belt (Large)
review_body:
I'm using this belt as a back support after surgery. A friend loaned me his Altus belt thinking that it might offer my lower back some relief, and I was impressed with how well it alleviated much of my pain. I decided to buy one for myself.

The leather is softer than you might imagine, and the holes offer plenty of sizing options depending on how snugly you need the belt to fit. I wear a 34\\" pant size, and I needed to order this item in Large. I don't think the Small or Medium would have worked for me. If you're really hefty, you might consider the X-Large size.

It's clear that this belt will outlast me. It is so well made that you could almost make the argument that it is overbuilt! I read one review where the the writer claimed the holes were ripping. I don't see how that could be physically possible, so I can only assume he received a defective item. For me, this belt is highly supportive and extremely well manufactured.

I originally ordered the Altus belt that comes with padding, and returned it. (You'll see a separate review under that item.) That belt was uncomfortable because the padding bunched up vertically as I cinched the belt. It was not at all comfortable to wear, and actually caused me more discomfort than relief. If you're purchasing this belt for back relief, it would be my recommendation to go with the unpadded one that I'm reviewing.

Just a quick note on leather vs. a synthetic material, like you'd find at Home Depot. The leather belt offers a more rigid form of support than the others, and for me, it seems to do the trick. I subscribe to the bromide, \\"If it works, don't fix it\\", hence I'll stay with my Altus leather belt. If you're a weight lifter or if you're using the belt for other purposes, it may well be that another form factor would be more effective. I can only say that for helping me recover from a microdiscectomy, this belt has been the only thing that offered me lasting relief.

product_title: AK47 STOCK BUTT PAD RECOIL PAD by COI
review_headline: Doesn't necessarily work on synthetic stocks.
review_body:
I managed to get this recoil pad to just barely fit on my \\"Romy G\\" Romanian parts-kit rifle, which came with an original laminated wood stock. The mounting holes did not line up at all in my Arsenal SGL, with the AK-74M style polymer furniture. I doubt it would fit consistently on other aftermarket stocks, like from Tapco and the like.

A word of warning, check the condition of the existing buttstock by removing the stock plate. Avoid messing with your current set up if the laminate looks like it might separate or if it just doesn't look all that solid inside. The directional tension of screws from an imperfect fit will damage the buttstock's screw threads.

I think I'll stick with the slip-on pads.

product_title: Striiv Device Basic Bundle
review_body:
I have had weight problems on and off all my life. It is hard to get motivated to work out when you work overtime each week and take care of the house etc. This really helps me get motivated.

I love the fact that it gives me small challenges to complete throughout the day (200 steps in 5 mins, 400 steps in 15 mins etc) because they really add up in the end. If they didn't challenge me, I wouldn't bother. I got one for my mom and I and it's fun comparing our activity levels at the end of each day.

The achievements/trophies are fun. I'm a gamer and love achievements on Xbox so this is a sure way to get me to move. They have some that only happen once I believe-not sure since I haven't gotten them more than once yet- (like burn 50K calories all time, walk 100,000 steps all time) and ones that you can get every day (walk 1500 steps, walk the golden gate bridge etc). So it's fun always getting achievements for the work you put in.

The \\"game\\" really isn't much of a game but it is cute and a fun way to get people to want to walk. It's more of a garden sim where you can plant/build and collect money. I REALLY hope they add more. It would also be amazing if they went into different work out equipment as well. My boyfriend would love to have one of these when he goes swimming for example (so a waterproof future option would be cool).

I almost didn't buy it since I was also skeptical of all the good reviews here. Some think the reviews are fake but really it's just a great product and worth a try if you need some motivation.

Edit to add: I started using this less than a month ago (around May 15) and I've lost about 9 lbs so far. It might not seem like much but it's a great start! I figured I'd add that to the review to let people know again that it could work for you.

product_title: Aim Sports Red Dot Sight with 4 Different Reticles
review_headline: An inexpensive but decent Reflex sight
review_body: As far as reflex sights go, this isn't an expensive zero-parallax, red-green, solar/nuclear powered reflex sight.  I knew I wasn't getting any of those features when I spent less than $40 dollars on this item.  For the price, the value offered is exceptional.  It took a bit of finessing to zero-in.  I turned the vertical adjustment screw at least 5 full turns.  It seems that it didn't want to catch or something.  Once I got it zeroed in, it's been able to hold zero reasonably well.  I took the gun to the range and it worked fine.  Then I took it out on a trail (going through some pretty dense woods while it was suspended on a one-point sling) and even though it was bumped around quite a bit, when I brought the gun up to ready, the reticle pointed exactly where my bullets went.  It comes with a little rubber sleeve that slides over the lens. That's nice, though it's a bit awkward to take off and put back on.  On the brightest setting, this sight works great in daylight, though it's best if you have a bit of shade.  On it's dimmest setting, it's still a little bright/blurry for night use.  If you have a tactical light on your rifle to use in conjunction, though, it works well.  I've only had it for two weeks, but if it lasts 6 months, it'll be more than worth the price for me and I'd buy it again.

product_title: Pflueger 2-Piece Echelon Light Spinning Rod and Reel Combo (5-Feet, 6-Inch)
review_body:
I purchased this Combo 1 year ago as a quick impulse and have used it regularly since then.

Rod:
Pros: The handle is comfortable and transfers bites easily. The added hook loop at the top of the handle on the rod is a great and I don't understand why more rods don't have it. It assembles easily and unlike many other 2 piece rods stays together during your cast.

Cons: Very whippy, even for a light action rod. The guides are solid and have lasted a year without issue, but I would prefer it to have metal guides.

Reel:
Pros: Smooth retrieve and quick lock, ambidextrous handle for you left handers. The drag is easy to adjust and works well. Bail opens with the right amount of resistance and when you close it it's just as smooth.

Cons: No documentation available from Pflueger on a breakdown of this to oil it, or how much line gets pulled with each revolution of the handle.

Durability:
I've had some decent catches come in on this, Crappie, Jumbo Perch, Large Mouth, and even a Walleye. Through all of them this combo just kept asking for more. I've dropped it a few times on rocks, and concrete docks, with no problems still

Looks:
It's a fishing pole I didn't buy it because it will pick me up women, the entire pole being a matching red was nice.

Overall
If it was lost or broken, I'd buy another. It's so far served me well, and hasn't given me a birds nest or a crack in the rod.

product_title: Needak Soft Bounce Black Trampoline Folding Rebounder with Stabalizing Bar-R01-R05
review_headline: Bought this for my active little boy, now I use it!
review_body:
I purchased foremost for my very active 5 year old last winter to burn off some of his crazy energy. I didn't think the children's trampolines looked all that safe being very lightweight, and I'm not crazy about purchasing so many items manufactured in China. The Needak, being made in the US, was a huge selling point for me. I also figured I could use it as well to add some variety to my workouts.

The trampoline was very easy to assemble. The stabilizer bar was a bit more difficult only because you need to pry off the soft feet to take it on and off. We had the bar on the trampoline for about a month before it became apparent it was more of a danger to a daredevil 5 year old than a safety feature. By then, I had figured out how to jump on it as well, and was comfortable not using it :-) If your sense of balance is good and you are otherwise in decent shape, with no health conditions that would require the bar, I would probably just skip it and save $85. I almost kicked it multiple times trying to work out to some Urban Rebounder videos.

The bounce is great (we have the \\"soft\\" for people under 300lbs), and since I couldn't justify the expense of a Bellicon, I'm fine with the springs. They are not that noisy, can be oiled, and in fact, the package comes with a little container of oil and instructions on how and when to oil the springs. It appears using the springs the way we do, they should last between 3-5 years, and the cost to replace them currently is only about $3.50 each. I don't expect them all to fail at once. Bungee trampolines need their cords replaced more frequently than that based on my readings. This is a very sturdy unit, surprisingly so since it is also portable and easily folded.

Bottom line: My son loves it, I love it, and it's a great workout. This is a high quality product.

review_body: My company insurance is now giving out points if we exercise using a polar device and I purchased this last month. I'm finding that this is making me work out for over an hour each day and cause I love seeing a more accurate calorie burn count then I used to on the gym cardio machines.  There are also weekly assessments that the watch gives you based on your workouts.  One week I received, \\"Work out more in Zone 1\\"...last week I got \\"You're doing great\\"; I met my goal calories burned 4078/4050. product_title: Rothco Men's The Medium Transport Pack
review_headline: Perfect Size for Travel, a GHB / BOB and More
review_body:
I purchased this bag based on its size and the fact that it is water-resistant. Having a cheap backpack in the bed of my truck as my Get-Home-Bag, I learned the hard way to make sure that your bag is at least water-resistant, if not waterproof. Everything in my bag was soaked because of rain water getting in and I had to throw away at least half of the contents and let the other half dry out for a week.

There were other reviewers that had said that this bag is barely bigger than a shower kit and just a very small bag in general. I have to disagree. Yes, this bag can be used as a 'small' bag but it also expands into a very utilitarian backpack. When I first opened the bag it appear to be 'flat' but finding a video on Youtube that Rothco made demoing the bag shows that it expands outward immensely. This bag was designed to expand straight back, not sideways, which can get in the way of your arms when walking. It's more narrow than most backpacks, which I really appreciate.

I got this backpack for multiple reasons: My range bag, a simple 24 hour GHB / BOB and for our honeymoom in Hawaii. Being water-resistant and not too bulky, it is perfect for travel. I also wanted to make sure my 15\\" laptop would fit and it does almost perfectly.

It's extremely well made, also. The material just feels of quality compared to my cheaper bags and there are multiple additional points that add extra security, including a strap across the chest and a belt. Overall, this thing is perfect for my intended use. I would highly recommend this pack to anyone looking for quality, compactness and ample room.

product_title: Lezyne Steel Floor Drive Bicycle Floor Pump
review_body:
Pros:

- Screw-on mechanism works for both presta and schrader valves, very well thought out design.
- No air leaks when properly attached and removed (plus no more painful fingers common with clip-on hoses!).
- No effort pumping air into tire (see cons below though for note).
- Pressure dial accurate.
- Sturdy.

Cons:

- Not a huge con, but in case of presta valves it is advisable to briefly push in the valve after unscrewing it and before attaching the hose, as the pressure generated by the pump may not be sufficient to \\"open\\" the valve if it hasn't been used for a while, causing pressurized air to remain in the pump system.
- Bit expensive but feels it will last forever.

review_body:
I am 52 years old and have been lifting weights pretty consistently for 30 years. I have also done aerobics, sking, backpacking, windsurfing, etc., so I have always been in pretty good shape. This P90X program is an awesome conditioning program. It is VERY difficult, so if you are not in good shape, forget it. This program focuses on core strength, felexibility, balance, and upper body strength, pretty much in that order. I really love the Yoga X routine - I thought it would be easy - it is NOT!! You will nor believe how hard you can work doing these movements. Also, the Plyometrics program is fantastic, but REALLY hard. I had to back off on that one a bit because of knee issues.

Anyway, you can learn conditioning from P90X that you can use the rest of your life, even if you don't do the P90X routine more than once. I highly recommend it to anyone who is pretty fit, looking for a change, and looking to improve their overall fitness.

product_title: Bushnell Tactical Elite 1x32 Red/Green T-Dot Riflescope
review_headline: Good Red dot scope for the price
review_body: I purchased this Bushnell scope for a Smith & Wesson M&P 15-22 and while I wanted a similar red dot to those on my centerfire AR-15's I was not planning on paying twice the cost of the rifle for one. When doing my research there seemed to be a lot of high end and low end red dots but only a couple in the mid range. I went and looked at several of them in person and the Bushnell was the highest quality and closest in appearance and function to the \\"high dollar\\" ones I have on the center Fire AR-15's. The scope arrived in good condition and functioned as expected out of the box. It was very easy to mount and sight in and it probably could have been done without tools if you had a couple of coins. After using it for a few months and multiple trips to the range I will say it holds it zero perfectly. The rubber scope covers while nice for storage in the safe are essentially useless if you are moving about with the rifle as they fall off pretty easily. The built in \\"back up\\" iron sights on the Bushnell shoot about 1.25 inches high with the M&P 15-22 @ 50 yards but for anything larger than a rabbit I do not see this as an issue. I really like the T dot reticle. It aligns perfectly with the Magpul fold down front and rear iron sights. On the down side the sight adjustment screws and the knob to turn the red dot on and select the color and brightness of the reticle do not have what I would call positive stops. You can certainly feel them if you pay full attention but you can also leave any of them between stop points. Once sighted in only the on/off/brightness/color knob is regularly used and it would be nice had Bushnell spent a bit more on this piece. It does work as expected but as noted above you can leave it between clicks and while it does work on that position the reticle seems to flicker a bit which does not happen at all if it is set to one of the stops. I will not try and say it is comparible to the high dollar red dots but it is solidly built and has functioned asexpected since I mounted it on the rifle.

product_title: Qstarz BT-Q1000XT Bluetooth Data Logger GPS Receiver (66 ch, AGPS, Vibration sensor, 400K waypoints)
review_body:
This is my second self-contained bluetooth GPS receiver.

I previously bought a Dual Electronics XGPS150A, which is a non-logging receiver and works very well other than refusing to pair with a device that I really needed it to work with. I bought the BT-Q1000XT since that does work. I wondered about getting the cheaper (non-logging) version, but decided that for the incremental price I mas as well get the logging and may one day make real use of it.

This locks very quickly (<5seconds) even indoors. It successfully pairs and works with everything that I need it to (and a few things I don't).

I tried the logging, and it worked well, showing the track that I took, speed and altitude.

I am giving four stars rather than 5 because the software is, well, pathetic. It only works on Windows (I would have much preferred OS/X) and is not intuitive to use. There is a (free) utility written in Java (and hence works on the Macbook too) which has almost the same functionality.

The \\"free\\" cover that came with it is very cheap and nasty, but better than nothing.

product_title: Sevylor Colossus 4 Person Inflatable Boat 2012
review_body:
Had this boat shipped to me in Japan. Took it out on 1 foot waves on the ocean in southern Japan, didn't get more than 50ft out before the tide brought me back in, impossible to row in rough water.

But, took it out in an island inlet with a few hundred islands, where the water is stable and smooth as glass, and she performed brilliantly. The oars worked from the front facing backwards.

Only took her out two times. Second time, a small boat came by quickly and the wake pushed the boat into a big rock (of course it was teaming with marine life - including clam shells, and other really sharp items) which quickly ripped a 6\\" gash in the main chamber in the front of the boat.

Thank goodness for 3 chambers! Was able to limp back (almost 4km) to the closest main land mass, with girlfriend in tow (by the way she was scared to death we were going to sink). The two inner chambers kept the vessel afloat, with over 300 lbs of personnel onboard, but was easily unstable. The provided oars were replaced with the aluminum oars immediately on purchase... which helped get the vessel in quite nicely.

Never took on more than a few gallons of water, nonetheless, the patching is a pain, as Japan isn't in the industry of having repair parts for vinyl boats. They all seem to only have rigid hull vessels everywhere, and nobody can lead me to a local vinyl watercraft repair place... all I needed was a patch, glue, acitone...etc!

So, back on amazon to order my parts! Will be back on the water as soon as she's repaired! I love it!

The natural horsehide is of course quite a bit darker now from daily use but that is it. I have a drawer full of other holsters that I tried before getting the Royal Guard. product_title: LifeSpan TR1200i Folding Treadmill
review_headline: Great treadmill for the price - but USB drive not included
review_body:
This is a great treadmill. To get anything noticably better, you will need to spend two or three times as much. This is perfect for 99% of people using a treadmill at home.

Delivery through CEVA was great. Be aware of that if you are ordering through Prime. The delivery date you see is the date it gets to the shipper. You then get a call to schedule delivery. You will not get it on the date shown by Amazon. The CEVA delivery is \\"doorstep\\" delivery. They leave it outside your house. The guy said he is \\"not allowed\\" to go inside. However, a $20 tip and he helped me get this inside, down a flight of stairs, and into my basement home gym.

The box is large and VERY heavy. Do not underestimate that. Check the dimensions against doorways, etc. It is big. Removing it from the box only buys you a couple of inches. It is also VERY heavy. You will need two strong people to lift this. It can be dragged by one. Menuvering the box is very difficult.

Assembly is very easy. Many of the screws and bolts are already in place, so they need to be unscrewed first. The instructions are clear and all necessary tools are included. Just follow the instructions and a fourth grader could put this together. It took me about 15 minutes.

The motor is very quiet when running. Your footsteps make more noise.

The duplicate buttons on the side rails are great.

The heart rate is a gimmic, but works with a Polar heart rate strap. It should also switch the display to HR automatically when you grab the grips. It doesn't.

Two things should have been included but weren't.

1) The USB drive is NOT included. The photos make it look like it is included, but it isn't. They cost less than five bucks and 1gb is more than enough [[ASIN:B005P3JRAQ 1GB Red USB2.0 Flash Drive Swivel Design]]. It is stupid it isn't included. I searched through the packaging for 20 minutes until after calling customer service to confirm it wasn't in there. The USB is needed to tell it your height and weight - which otherwise will always be incorrectly displayed on the screen.

2) There is no lube included. Belt lube is like fifteen bucks. The manual says to apply before first use. Come on. At least a sample should be included. [[ASIN:B000FH10F2 LifeSpan Fitness 100% Silicone Treadmill Belt Lubricant]]

So, I really like the treadmill for the most part. The display is nice enough, but I wish it cycled or showed more data on each screen. Keeping your height and weight at the bottom is useless since it isn't weighing me or checking my height. Presumably it is using this for the calorie display, which is not that useful.

The fitness tracking software is nice, I guess, but requires an annual fee once the free trial runs out. Garmin doesn't do that. I'll have to figure out a way to hack the data file to import into my Garmin tracking software.

Not including lube or the USB stick leave a sour taste in my mouth after spending a fair amount on this machine. product_title: Streamlight ProTac 1L Professional Tactical
review_body: Great light at an excellent price. I've had it for several weeks and love it. This is my second Streamlight, and I own two Surefire lights.  My other lights were just too big to comfortably throw in a pocket or clip on a belt, so too often I had no light. Not a good situation when carrying a concealed firearm. Uses a single CR123 battery and is super bright. Small enough to throw in my pocket and never notice it. The metal clip is sturdy but good only for temporary placement, not for clipping on a thick gun belt as it will pop off.  Controls are pretty simple, which appealed to me.  There is a high, strobe, and low setting, in that order.  Press slightly to momentarily activate the high beam, and press harder to click through for constant on.  If wanting the strobe, double press slightly to momentarily activate strobe, and press through to click for constant on.  For low beam, triple press slightly to activate, and press through to click for constant on. If this sounds confusing... it's simple once you try it. I especially like the low beam capability, which is not available on my other lights.  Great light!

product_title: AIR802 Marine WiFi 2.4 GHz Omni Directional Antenna, 12 dBi ANMA2412
review_body: This has been one of the worst buying experiences I have ever had.  This company provided extremely poor service, the staff has limited knowledge, and the product is defective and not close to what was represented. They represented that this antenna has the highest gain of any on the market.  I tried it the first day and the reception was less than the 5\\" antenna that came with my wi-fi long-raing USB adapter.  I called the company immediately and they gave me the run around saying that I needed to try it at a different location and it would work better.  I tried this antenna at four different locations ranging from 1 block to 3 miles away from the center of town, all in a direct level line of sight, with no obstructions.  In no case did this antenna ever perform better than the 5\\" antenna.  I also bought a 12\\" antenna for $5 for a discounter and it performed as well as this large expensive antenna.  I called AIR802 over 7 times asking for support.  Each time they gave me the run-around, told me that I was too far from the signals, then too close, then I must be at the wrong angle.  They had no clue what they were talking about. They would not allow a return or refund.  I have never written a review before, so I do not normally complain, even with bad customer service. I assume that poor customer service is part of buying over the internet.  However, this was the poorest service I have every received.  I gave AIR802 many opportunities to help me, help me find a better antenna, return this antenna, or do anything to provide a solution that gave better reception than the little 5\\" antenna. They promised the engineers would call back. They never did.  When I did get to talk to one, he came up with the same non-sense suggestions like \\"You are too close,if you further away, this antenna will get better reception\\".  Of course it didn't.  I have dozens of photographs of screen shots showing the reception between the AIR802 antenna and the cheap small antennas to document the poor reception. I tried 4 different locations, reconnected the antennas several times at each location, rebooted the computer several times between antennas.  Nothing helped this antenna every achieve a signal that was any better than an antenna that is 1/10th its size and about 1/100th, the cost.  These guys are masters of providing a run around and no service.  They sell say they sell a lot of product, but it is readily apparent that they know little about it.  The product I received was defective and completely misrepresented.  The 12 dbi antenna gets less reception than the 2.5 dbi antenna I already have.  Don't waste your money or time.  Find another legitimate vendor that is willing to provide a quality product, stand behind it, and help you get achieve your goals.  This company is not one that will help.

product_title: Exerpeutic Inversion Table with Comfort Foam Backrest
review_body: A great buy for the money! Solidly constructed, reasonably priced and quickly delivered, this inversion table effectively helps with a variety of back problems. Compared to other products a couple hundred dollars more expensive the Exerpeutic gives the best value.

product_title: 91/30 m44 Mosin Nagant Rubber Recoil Butt Pad with 10 Mosin Nagant Stripper clip by FSI
review_body:
What a great kit! The buttstock is a hard rubber. I would say its a 35-40% imporvement over the metal butt plate. If the rubber were a little softer it would be the \\"perfect kit\\". Still a far cry from the metal one. You will still go home with a shoulder bruise after a day at the range. The best part of this is the 1.2\\" added length to the rifle. Honestly it does not sound like much, but it will allow for a more natural hold then before.

The stripper clips were a free added bonus. Plus they work. When stacked and loaded right, they do just like they should. Not too weak. I have used each a dozen times and only ended up with one clip slightly bent (but still works fine). Great combo kit!

product_title: Bushnell PowerView Super High-Powered Surveillance Binoculars
review_body: Very nice binoculars and they won't break the bank. The Powerview method of focussing is a tremendous improvement over the wheel. I would recommend getting a tripod adaptor because you're going to want to use these for extended periods of time and 10x is difficult to hold steady.

product_title: College Ladies Genuine Leather Clutch Wallet - Oklahoma Sooners
review_body: I LOVE MY WALLET.  It is quality leather with a securly fit ou soonmers emblem on the front. There is plenty of pockets for credit cards and space for pictures, change, and bills.

product_title: Meprolight Ruger Tru-Dot Night Sight for P345. fixed set
review_body: I really like my sights. They seen just as good as Novaks to me, at a better price. Highly recommended!

product_title: Ultega NavRun 2K11 GPS Heart Rate Computer
review_body:
This is one great little gadget! It is very easy to use, and the software is simple to install. I thought it would be much more complicated to set up, but it was a piece of cake!

Great GPS function and four different pulse zones. Don't let the cheap price full you, this is one hard working little gadget. Great for any walker, runner, hiker or biker in your life. My husband is a mountain bike fanatic and this watch has proved to me perfect for him. No more getting lost in the woods! Our one and only complaint is that the battery life could be a little longer. But other than that, perfect!

product_title: The Belly Putt- Putter Extension Kit
review_body:
At only $25, this is a great alternative to spending a couple hundred to try a belly putter. Installation was very easy and directions were straight forward. The website also featured a video that guides you through installation step by step.

The finished product was sturdy enough to use, but the extension wasn't solid. I'm fairly tall and had the extension installed near the end of the shaft. It did wiggle slightly and after repeated in and out of the golf bag, the end extension was pulling itself out and ultimately pulled out completely. Included in the kit is a sleeve that would allow the extension to be attached to the putter and a belly putter grip could be fixed over it. I did not use this piece and I'm not sure how much more sturdy this would make it.

Overall, it is great for those hoping to try a belly putter, but I wouldn't recommend using it as a permanent extension. Either spend the money on a true belly putter or have your putter re-shafted.

product_title: Opportunity: Soccer Art Print Art Poster Print by Bill Hall, 28x22
review_body: I bought this for my son. He loves soccer and wanted a poster we could not find one anywhere. This is a really cool graphic with bright colors and a good message. Really nice on his wall.

review_body:
The reason I only gave it 2 stars is the fact that you must where the belt very tight around your waist. The resistance bands are more towards your back and not at the sides of your body like most images show. When performing the excercises it will pull the belt down hard and it very very uncomfortable. If you can get the belt to stay put properly you can definetely get a decent workout.If I would have known about the PRO version, I would have paid the extra money as it has a vest instead of loose belt.

I would not recommend the product. Get the PRO version or Jumpsoles.

product_title: Deltech Fitness Flat Exercise Bench
review_body: When I purchase anything, I'm looking for value for my dollar, and I'm willing to pay a little more for the product if I find it. The Deltech Fitness Flat Bench fit the criteria I was looking for in an exercise bench. Solidly built and comfortable to use, there is no doubt in my mind it will last for years to come.

product_title: Body Rider Exercise Upright Fan Bike (with UPDATED Softer Seat)
review_headline: Great, but could use a better seat!
review_body: The bike was super easy to make! I'm a small girl and it wasn't too much work at all. The bike is really great and does exactly what I want it to do, but the seat is horrendous. It hurts your butt so bad if you're on it for a while. Even when I'm riding for 10 minutes, it hurts my butt pretty bad. I would recommend buying another seat!! The bike can make a lot of noise, but I also have a treadmill and it makes just about the same amount of noise. It's not a nuisance at all.

product_title: Bongo Board
review_body: I'm very happy with this purchase. I bought it for my mother for her birthday, because she had really been wanting one, and she thinks it's just the greatest thing ever! review_body: The hat came just as we expected it to.  There were no problems with ordering or receiving the item. I would order again.

review_body: This is a well-made novelty item.  Looks great outside on game-day, or in the game room year-round.  Will be purchasing more as little gifts in the future.

review_body:

product_title: Black Tom Anderson Kult Folder 6.25 inch
review_body: I bought this knife because I collect pocket knives, and I wanted to have on that was a little more distinct than otherones Ive owned. I LOVE this knife. You pull it out to open up a box and I will always get at least 3 comments on it. Its a mean and Narly looking thing, and the back hook works well for an improvised bottle opener. =P Although, Its not very practical, its very flat when folded, so it fits in your pocket, but the hook catches on EVERYTHING. The paint on the handle is also quite thin, And chips easily, And it looks horrible on a black knife. All in all, It takes some servicing (Tightening, touch up painting, Re- aligning the blade, Sharpening, Ect.) But its definatly a very cool show knife to brag about.

product_title: Stamina 15-0120 InStride Cycle XL
review_body: First of all, the cycle is so light that you have to have it against the wall otherwise it will slide around.  This would be no big deal if the stoppers on the end of each pole didn't come off constantly regardless of whether it was against a wall (I have half a mind to hot glue them).  Also, the bike doesn't really have any way to increase or decrease the intensity of the pedaling.  I think the T-bolt at the top is meant to do that, but it doesn't.  Lastly, when you use the cycle for about ten minutes, the metal rods that hold the pedals get scorching hot.  There is a warning on it that says (CAUTION - HOT SURFACE) but it seems to me like a major design flaw.  Overall, not what I expected, and not worth the money I paid for it.

product_title: MTM All-Weather Target Backer (Blue)
review_body:
We've only used it once thus far, but it worked perfectly and we can see that it will be useful for some time to come. It's easy to tape targets to the backer and then remove the tape from the plastic material afterwards. We're using it with the MTM Jammit Target Stand. The backer stands up well in a decent breeze, and the blue background provides a good field on which to place a target. My wife and I put two 8.5x11 targets on it, side by side, so that we can share a single target stand.

Update Aug 2013 ... the board now has a LOT of holes in it, but it's still going strong ... we always put our targets in the same place, so the areas inside those targets are almost completely gone, but the structure of the board is still very much intact ... I'm not sure how many rounds it has taken, many hundreds, at least ... I'm thinking it'll definitely get us into next summer anyway, which is better than I had expected originally.

review_body:

review_body: I tried a lot before I found these. The Gamma (spelling?) gel ones are the only others I've found that work this well, but they can't take a ball hit anywhere. These can take a ball hit and still dampen very well.

product_title: Whetstone Cutlery Last Samurai Battle Sword
review_headline: I guess I kinda knew when I bought it it would suck
review_body:
I got this sword at a gun and knife show a little while ago, then I read up on it and found out it's completely useless. Being the optimistic person I am, I decided to see if it was indeed absolutely useless.
It is.
I took it out and chopped down a tree that was an inch thick. The blade was bent before I had even finished chopping. I was able to bend it back. I decided then to just take it apart. The tang (the part of the sword inside the handle) was glued into the handle. They had not even bothered to score the tang for a better grip on the glue and the glue was hard and brittle. If you want to display this sword somewhere, it looks pretty cool. I think it's a little overpriced for that, but then, I've been spoiled by better cheap swords and knives. Essentially, to me, this is expensive scrap metal. Blech.

product_title: BBB Synthetic Black Cork Road Bicycle Handle Bar Tape
review_body:
The tape itself is excellent. It is more like a dense foam material (hence \\"synthetic cork\\" I guess).

At first it felt a bit tough, but as I rode it and as it was exposed to the elements, it quickly broke in and now feels soft, yet supportive. Not the most plush grip ever, but hey, they never said it was. They also have an excellent amount of grip. As for the small adhesive backing, it seems pretty minimal in terms of actually sticking, but it serves more as a means of gripping the bar and keeping it from unraveling. But, the bar plugs are on the opposite end of the scale.

The bar plugs are made of plastic that looks and feels very cheap. I was able to get both plugs in the ends, but one cracked in the middle, right through the 'BBB.' I was a little sad after this happened, but the plugs do their job, even if they don't look pretty or high quality.

Sum: Excellent bar grip, not-so-excellent bar plugs. Good for those on a budget, but I personally wouldn't buy it again.

NOTE: In the picture for black cork, the actual product you get does NOT have white dots visible. It is just solid black.

product_title: Do-All Outdoors White Wing Automatic Trap
review_body: My brother and I purchased this thrower to use at his bachelor party.  Overall the reviews were good so we thought we'd take a chance on it.  We're very glad we did.  There is some minor assembly, but it only took me about 20 mins to have the thrower put together (by myself).  The first time we tried it out, we went through about 40 clays, but we had a huge issue with clays breaking in the stack (about 25+% were breaking), but after reading some other reviews with the same issue, we added a bottle of water to the top of the stack.  This has almost completely fixed the problem.  We rarely have a clay break now.  We used the thrower 2 weeks ago and went through 250+ clays, with very minimal breakage.  We absolutely love this thrower.  I just purchased the 40 clay extension last night and hope to purchase the wobbler kit soon.  Overall, this is a great product for the money and Amazon.com has the best price I found anywhere.

product_title: Warrior Pro Hand Wraps, Black
review_body: First of all, I want to say how impressed i was with the super fast delivery. i received it before the estimated time and I love the product. They were a great deal and are very sturdy, great product! Would recommend to anyone.

review_body: I have been eyeballing these sunglasses for a while, so after my SMITH Aviators broke, I decided to buy these.  I'm glad that I bought them. They fit my face perfectly. review_body: The rangefinder is a great value for the price. Works great and easy to operate.I would highly recommend this item. The instructions said that it comes with a battery, mine did not.

product_title: Ultimate Arms Gear New Generation Mossberg 500 / 590 / 835 12 Gauge Tactical Shotgun Conversion Kit: Six 6 Position Adjustable & Collapsible Stock + Rear Pistol Grip + Shell Holders + Recoil Butt Pad + Sling Swivel Stud + Tri Rail Forend + Light + Laser + Grip
review_body: First off, I would like to let everyone know that this fit PERFECT on my 7+1 Mossberg 500 Persuader purchased at Big 5 Sporting Goods.  It was very easy to remove the stock forend, much easier than shown on youtube with the screwdrivers, slamming, etc.  I just used a wood dowell with a sock over it and tapped gently till the stock forend slid off.  All of the products were as advertised. The rail-mount for the laser is hard plastic and just SLIGHTLY bigger than the diameter of the laser, causing it to slide around in the mount. You could get a smaller metal mount, or just fix this issue by taking rubberized black electricians tape and going around the laser once or twice before cinching the mount down on it.  It doesn't move at all now.  Also, the laser IS FULLY ADJUSTABLE, regardless of what the other reviewers said.  One of the adjustment screws is spring-loaded.  Tighten this all the way down and you have no movement at all.  I got my laser dead-on and it does not move AT ALL, even after a day of shooting.  Thanks for offering this complete kit at a VERY good price!  Thanks be to YouTube as well!

product_title: Leatherman Style PS Multi-Tool
review_headline: Not TSA compliant overseas, be forewarned
review_body:
Mine got taken in Singapore on a recent visit after being through Houston and Moscow with it along with several US airports, so if you travel international, pack it. Since I already pack my juice, I don't really have a need for this anymore. Didn't have enough time to evaluate the tool, seemed ok, but nothing like the Juice or my Wave I purchased back in 1998.

Below are the emails to/from the Leatherman folks.

the TSA agents really liked it when they inspected it.

Any chance you'd send me another? I'm a Wave owner since 1998 and an
owner of 2 Juices, my wife carries a Micra when not traveling.

Thanks,
BW

-------------------------------------------------------------------------

From: Leatherman Consumer Information coninfo@leatherman.com
Date:

Hello,

Thank you for contacting us. While the Leatherman Style PS complies with TSA regulations (March 2009) and has been tested in airports around the world for travel-approved tools (visit [...] for full details), please remember that ultimately discretion is up to each individual TSA agent. I'm sorry this would not fall under the warranty of our tools.

I hope you understand.

review_body: Got my Timber Rattler Jungle Fury Bowie on Wed. 4-11-2012, a full 2 days b4 what the anticipated arrival date was to b. A full 10 1/2\\"s of blade and the rest is the handle. Fit and finish are superb...no rough edges and the wood handle transitions into the metal, that with your eyes closed, you can't tell one from the other. For me, the only knives I've had, or ever would have, are Bowie or Bowie style fixed blade knives. Yes granted, it's not a full tang, rather a rat tail, so you're not going to use it to chop down trees or lumber. It is a knife that should b used more for killing and self defense.  The blade comes razor sharp. It just has an overall beautiful feel and balance and appearance. For a knife that is $11.01 plus shipping, for a total of $18.50, one could afford to buy several. It is definitely worth owning. I'm getting another Timber Rattler called....Timber Rattler Large Safari Jungle Bowie w/sheath 440 Stainless. The only place I found it for now, is on eBay. It's $15.99 and shipping brings it to around $28.00. It too is beautiful.

product_title: Lunettes de soleil Rudy Project NOYZ SP048469RC
review_body:
My Rudy Project noyz glasses are comfortable and fit well which you would expect for the nearly $300 that I paid for them. However, less than a month after purchase, I noticed scratches on one of the lenses at the end of a trail run and contacted customer service as the glasses were said to come with a one-year guarantee against scratches and a three-year warranty against defects. Initially, I was asked where I lived and where the scratches occurred - the answer to both was in Taiwan. I was then told that the warranty information on the Project Rudy homepage was only for Americans. When informing them that I was indeed an American and could mail the lenses to the US, I was asked what I was doing when the scratches occurred. I was then told that I could have the lenses replaced at the cost that was nearly identical to a new pair of glasses as they did not occur in normal use and were \\"human factor scratches\\".

Seriously? Wearing Project Rudy glasses for running is not considered \\"normal use\\"? I suppose that the lawyer that crafted their guarantee assured them that the wording of it allows them to void any and all claims but this is a bit ridiculous. If I had purchased a pair of $20 glasses from the local shopping mall and returned them three weeks later with the same story, they would have been replaced, no questions asked.

So, if you have cash to burn and want a pair of glasses for walking around the mall and driving in the slow lane, you probably should check out the Rudy noyz. If you want to wear them outside for any kind of physical activity, best give them a pass.

product_title: 9.6V 2000mAh Nunchuck NiMH Battery Pack w/ Mini Tamiya Connector
review_body:
This is an ideal battery for an airsoft gun that is wired to the front. This battery will easily fit into any foregrip or peq box designated to hold a battery. I use this in my G&G Combat Machine, and the battery is enough for the motor to slightly pull back on the tappet plate during semi automatic fire due to the motor over spinning( The battery, is not enough to pull the piston during overspinning, so there is no damage to the gun while firing.) For the noobs out there, the battery can spin the motor faster than an 8.4V battery resulting in the gun to begin the firing cycle even after the trigger is released. This happens with all batteries, but it is more noticeable with a 9.6V battery. Overall there is no cons to the battery and the pros are...
-increased rate of fire compared to a cheaper battery or a 8.4V battery
-increased trigger response
-the battery comes wired to mini tamiya connectors which is what most front wired aegs use

Stop reading this review and get yourself a new battery!

review_body: [[VIDEOID:mo30Q27ZD74F2BU]]I just recieved it in the mail, it came a day earlier than what was projected. I found it to be heavy, and well made. product_title: Marmot Men's Precip Full Zip Pant
review_body:
I have owned this less than a year, but so far am impressed. The first time I tested them was at a park near my house during a massive thunderstorm. It was pouring heavy rain, had I been driving I probably would've had to pull over. I stayed out in this storm for a few hours and my legs stayed perfectly dry. I was a bit concerned about the zippers being non water proof, but thus far this has proven to be a non issue (waterproof fabric covers the zippers). I wore them hiking on the Superior Hiking Trail in Northern Minnesota last weekend and it rained on and off for about 5 days, the temps ranged from 35 to 65 degrees. I always wear a base layer on my legs, during this 5 day span I wore the base layer, and another breathable hiking pants, and then these pants for about half the time, and at times my legs got warm but never unbearably so. In other words I think they breathed fairly well. The other half of the time I just wore a base layer and these pants and that was perfect.

I like the draw strings at the bottom of the legs. I once stepped on a plank that sank underwater causing my boot to submerge, but because I had the draw strings tight around the tops of boots no water got into my boot.

Because I was tramping threw the rain and mud for five days in these pants they got dirty, and I was pleased to learn they were easily machine washable.

I hope that they continue to serve me well for years to come. At this time I have no complaints.

Danny T, Massachusetts

product_title: Stamina Pilates Box and Pole
review_headline: A Decent little box for pilates
review_body:
Yes, the vinyl fabric is rather slick...depending on the exercise, you can slip. So, I use my pad to help limit slipping. I cut a piece of Neoprene rubber...rubber on one side and cloth on the other...and use that as a pad to prevent slipping when doing the stomach massage on my reformer and something you might call a swan push with this box on the reformer. I push on the foot bar with my hands while lying stomach down on this box. Put the rubber side down and cloth side up on the pad and it creates improved friction with my clothes. Still...if you are wearing slick clothes...you're going to slip some. It's asking for a lot to have the surface so sticky that you won't slip regardless of what exercise you're doing.

I don't mind the metal handles, but they could be more curved...and easier on the hands. That said, why not use nylon strap handles? That's what balanced body uses.

One issue I have with this box and a fancier box I just got as part of a used deal on a balanced body Allegro Reformer...the boxes are hollow and have relatively thin sides. They dig into the mats on top of the carriage. So, I modified this box. Used 2x2 lumber and created a frame that fits inside the box. I used wood screws to hold the frame together and then drilled and bolted the frame to the bottom of the box...it fits all around the bottom edge on the inside Adds some weight, but not a big deal. Rather than have the bare wood sit on the vinyl covered surface of the carriage pad, I glued some thin pieces of scrap foam on the wood frame...the part that would sit against the vinyl pad of the carriage. That's it. Adds a little weight, but not much. Now it doesn't leave much of an indent on the carriage pad after I've been sitting on it. It probably makes the whole box stronger also.

product_title: Griffin Technology 9410-TUNBMBLB TuneBuds Mobile for iPhone
review_headline: They're okay : Damages at the jack.
review_body:
I had the non mobile ones way back in 2006 , at the time they were great with my iPod 30GB but I lost them ( and my iPod) in Jamaica ( some lucky kid has them now ). However, I brought the iPhone 3GS in 2008 and I was excited to know that they had a mobile phone version.

I suppose I became an audiophile between losing my iPod ( getting a new one ) and getting an iPhone ( both I used with the apple ear buds ) because I noticed something about these that i didn't before.

These are basically regular ear buds with a rubber attached around it. It took me maybe a month to get annoyed with how they sound because even though the rubber created a barrier to improve the bass, the treble was too high to make a real difference. The sound quality is subpar but thats not even the beginning of it...

Also , after normal use, the jack will in fact damage, theres no way around it. Griffin is pretty good with replacing them but you have to go through a some what abnormal procedure to prove that it is damaged. You have to purposely cut the wire and take a picture and then send it to them. I suppose that how they make sure you really can't use these anymore.

The control is also not ergonomically friendly because it's round. You'll need a bit more dexterity than you would on the regular apple ear buds.

Another thing, the material they use for the cover tends to fray, which is not good.

Over all, If i could give them no stars, I would. The only good points is the return policy but who wants to keep returning these every month. Save your money , buy another pair of apple ear buds at 30 bucks if you have to so to avoid these.

review_body:

As others mentioned, locktite probably wouldn't be a bad idea to help secure the inner \\"cone\\" along with the supplied clip. (I hit the threads and clip channel with it, nothing's budging here). I also disassembled mine and cleaned the packing grease n such out of them, then followed up with some CLP to make future cleaning easier.

Bottom line, these are basically the same design as the (way) more expensive noveske...sans being knurled and these don't have a pig stamped on the side. For $75 less, I can do without the pig. Functionally, these seem to be the same, they supress flash more than I could have expected, and are definitely much easier on the ears than any other I've tried.

product_title: Amber Sporting Goods Handwrap Roller
review_body:
Taking the time to put boxing handwraps into a tight roll after washing them is important. Why? Two reasons: 1) having the loose end in a roll makes them easier to put on, 2) having them in a roll keeps the material flat, which is what you need to get proper hand support during boxing/MMA work.

Anyone who has manually rolled their boxing handwraps after washing and drying can attest to it being a tedious and time intensive process. This is a very simple device that makes the process much faster, and produces a nice clean roll.

Pros:
- Simple: I doubt this little roller device will break. Ever.
- Effective: each roll takes just a few seconds using this device (instead of 60-90 per roll doing it by hand).

Cons:
- You have to keep the material taught and flat as it is added to the roll. Still MUCH easier than doing it by hand, but it would be nice if the design could incorporate the suggestion below to address this.

Product Suggestions:
- It would be ideal to have some way to ensure the wraps are flat (untwisted) and taught before material is added to the roll.
- To accomplish this, the manufacturer could put a slot feeder a couple inches below the rolling pin that would keep the wraps taught, and ensure that they are untwisted as new material is added to the roll.

Tip:

product_title: Guard Dog Diablo Tactical Stun Gun Flashlight, Maximum Voltage,160 Lumens w/ Three Settings
review_body:
Oh yeah! This is just what I needed. I walk my dog late at night, between 11:30 and 1am when it's pretty dark out, so I don't look out of place carrying a flashlight around. It just looks natural, and no one thinks anything of it. But let some weird-O make the mistake of thinking I might be an easy mark, and he's in for one hell-of-a-surprise. You really can not tell just by looking at this flashlight that it has a little something extra. When holding it and looking right at the business end of this thing, I can't see the prongs, they're that well concealed, even with the device armed. No common street thug will know it until he finds himself on the ground.

Which brings me to another point I'd like to make. Some have commented that this stun gun may sting someone, but it won't put them on the ground. Those people just don't know how to use a stun gun. Put it to someone for less than a second, and the result is as they describe; put it to someone for 2 seconds, and that person will experience muscle spasms; put it to someone for 3-5 seconds and it will cause loss of balance and muscle control, along with mental confusion and disorientation.

Unfortunately, most people don't understand that a stun gun must be held to the target for more than a fraction of a second, even if that means holding onto the target to prevent your attracker from pulling away from you too soon. You must resist the impluse to run away too quickly. That will leave the job half done, and your attacker, while initially startled, may come after you again. Think about it. Even police tazers leave barbs in their target until an officer removes them. While attached to the target, a constant voltage is being sent down a wire from the gun to the barbs. That's the way stun guns are designed to work. So if you want to use one, you have to be prepared to use it properly, or don't bother to carry it.

Having a stun gun that also produces a bright, 160 lumen light is a plus. That much light will cast a beam not just 25 feet or so, but 250 feet. Pointed into the eyes of an attacker, this light would definately stop them well before they got within stun range. While I don't believe it would result in any permanent damage, I do suggest you don't try it on someone just for fun.

And when all else fails, this flashlight used as a billyclub will really hurt someone. The business end will also break-out auto-glass with no problem, if you need to get out or get in to rescue someone.

This device comes with a completely worthless carry holster. Throw it away and get something that works and will hold up. Like some others, I bought the [[ASIN:B000BP8J7U Bianchi Accumold Elite 7908 Open Top Oc And Light Pouch (Basketweave Black)]]. An excellent buy.

product_title: Tri-Angle Sharpmaker
review_headline: Purchasing advice after 6 months of use - Design and Limitations
review_body:
I love knives and have been stuck for years not knowing what to do with my dull knives. I am a bit of a perfectionist and find sharping knives freehand inconsistent and very difficult to master and learn until the sharpmaker came along. With so many positive reviews in Amazon, and Youtube videos showing how 'fast' it is to sharpen knives on a sharpmaker, I initially thought that this was the solution to all of my dull knife concerns. The answer is yes and no.

I have been using the sharpmaker for six months now since the time of purchase and have already sharpened about 8 knives with good results. And would want to share my experience with newbies who are planning to purchase a sharpmaker.

1. Is this the one stop solution to dull knives? NO.
The sharpmaker can 'QUICKLY' sharpen ANY knife from dull to razor sharp if and only IF the blade has a 30 and/or 40 degree edge/bevel (15/15 degree and 20/20 degree on both sides of the blade). Any other blade angle/bevel from the above. It will literally take you forever to sharpen your blade with the basic set.

With blades that do not match the 30/40 degree bevel set on the sharpmaker, a re-beveling/re-profiling must be done. This is a process of removing huge amounts of steel from the knife to correct the angle to 30/40 degrees. This task simply cannot be done by the medium stones (roughest stone in the basic sharpmaker set). Some users recommended purchasing the spyderco diamond triangle rods for re-profiling and will make life much easier. I did not go through this avenue as I personally find an additional USD 40.00+ is beyond my budget. Plus reviews indicating that the diamond stones will still take time doing re-profiling tasks I opted for other solutions.

2. Whet Stones as a supplement
I strongly recommend that whetstones are a must to supplement the sharpmaker. I use both the coarse and fine side of the whetstone to re-profile a knife, once this is achieved. The sharpmaker is used to finalize the edge to a utility edge, or to a razor sharp edge. Both utility and razor edge can easily cut through paper.

So what about my concern with freehand consistency and how to deal with the mess of oil/water whetstones?
With the whetstones, I still do not do free hand. My solution was to build a contraption/jig that will hold the whetstone at a 20 degree angle, similar to how the sharpmaker hold its medium and fine stones. This way I use my contraption to re-profile/re-bevel any knife. This saves me a lot of time.

For comparison purposes, I have a kitchen knife that does not comply to the 40 degree bevel (about 56 degree bevel maybe). It took me 3 hours without any results on the sharpmaker. With whetstones, the job is done in 15 to 30 minutes. Then another 15 minutes on the sharpmaker to make a razor edge. I have also done the same technique on my cleaver and my cleaver is also razor sharp and takes about 30 mins to sharpen.

How about the mess? I use the whetstones dry. There have been a lot of research of using water/oil whetstones dry with promising results. And from my experience this is true. I use the stones dry as how I sharpen with a sharpmaker. My theory is adding oil or water on whetstones is to give the knife edge a semi-mirror like finish. Using it dry will give the blade a dull finish showing the scratch/wear marks done by the whetstones. This is where the sharpmaker comes in. After the 40 degree edge has been established by the whetstones. The sharpmaker will easily sharpen and polish the knife to razor sharp and give it a mirror like finish.

I made the jig by using wood, hinges, slotted flat bars, and screws and the whole thing cost me no more than USD 10.00
For people who does not want the hassle of building jigs. Some users suggest the sand paper method by wrapping a coarse paper over the spyderco stones. Well this does work, but the sand paper wears down too fast and at times gets sliced by the knife during sharpening. So be prepared to re-wrap sand paper on the stone in each sharpening. I initially did this method but the hassle made me go for a customized solution. For people who do not want to go for a customized solution, you can try the diamond stones but I have not personally used them to comment.

3. Is the Sharpmaker recommended?
Yes indeed! You just have to understand the design limitations. As long as you have a 30 or 40 degree bevel. The sharpmaker can do the job FAST. But if you don't have the correct bevel, it will take forever to sharpen a knife. With whetstone and sharpmaker combination I have already fixed kitchen knives with a ruler edge (literally flat edge as how you see the edge of a ruler) to razor sharp and pretty happy with it.

4. Other tips
The more I sharpen, the more I learn about knives and sharpening concept and technique.
6 months ago. My thinking was this: I need the spyderco diamond stones and spyderco basic set to resharpen knives.
Now. My thinking is: I need the spyderco basic set and spyderco ultrafine stones to make knives hair whittling sharp!

From my research, most newbies will always prefer diamond stones. While enthusiasts and pro sharpener will recommend the ultrafine stones.
Diamond stones and other coarse stones can easily be bought from any supplier. All these can repair damaged knives whether it be free hand or via contraptions/jigs. But what you pay for in a Spyderco system are the stones, stones that make knife edges beyond sharp. The spyderco medium, fine, and ultrafine stones are what you pay for.

My next purchase will most probably be the spyderco ultrafine stones. My dilema is if the premium is worth it or not. As the fine stones already gives me a razor sharp edge and already pretty darn happy with it (i can already shave with my knives). And making hair whittling sharp knives are more of an obsession for me to hone my sharpening skills. As for my daily activities I don't see an application where I need a hair whittling sharp knife.

product_title: P90X DVD Workout - Base Kit
review_body:
Let me preface this review by describing my job - every other week, 3-5 days in a hotel in a different city, perhaps a different country.

I had for years been an avid runner, but between the crazy flight schedules, the inconsistent weather, and the need to plan out routes in new places, I fell off the running wagon. 20 pounds and 3 belt holes later, I needed something that worked better with my lifestyle.

Trying to use gyms at or near the places I was staying was really hit or miss. Let's be honest, unless a hotel is designed around a sports theme (golf, spa, etc), the workout equipment will be less than first class. In most places, the norm you can expect is a ratty old Nautilus, a single elliptical machine being used by another guest for an hour, a 20 foot pool with 20% chlorine. No thanks!

A professional friend suggested the P90X program and my first reaction was 'not for me!'. Working out in front of a TV touched on an ancient prejudice that I had to get past - let's call it the 'Jack Lalane/Richard Simmons' phenomenon.

But desperate times call for desperate measures. I borrowed, and eventually bought the DVD's for one simple reason - they worked the way I worked. I could roll into a new city, drop my bag on the bed, and in 15 minutes, have weight bands in hand, doing Chest and Back or Pliometrics without any hassles.

The workouts required a minimum of equipment, space, and time - all things which one finds in short supply on the road. I was able to stick with it through 2 rounds and after a year off I am starting my 3rd round.

If you are someone who craves novelty, wants to socialize and work out, needs complex equipment or outdoors activity ... you should probably pass on this program. But for the time constrained traveling professional, I cannot recommend it enough.

product_title: MetalTac MT-014-SVDB AK Dragunov Airsoft Sniper Rifle Bolt Action Spring Gun, Tactical Black
review_body: I've only had this gun for about a week or so but long enough to understand it and get used to it. I've seen a lot of lower-end airsoft sniper rifles for a similar price and watched them fail airsoft players after not too long. I have confidence in this rifle - everything is either metal or very solid polymer plastic. And the only place I see plastic is the stock and the foreend. So as far as what needs to be metal construction, A&K covers everything.  PROS  -DURABLE(full metal construction)  -Hot FPS (~400 w/.25s, supposed to be ~500 w/.2s)  -EASY to strip down  -ACCURATE with quality BBs and hopup/sights adjusted properly. If nothing else, it can hit a human target beyond 100 feet, for a fact.  -Has a slick look to it, in my opinion. If you're an AK lover, you'd like this.  CONS  -Metal magazine wobbles in the mag well. Don't grip by the mag when shooting.  -I had to put Rem Oil in the internals to make the action smooth (cocking back the bolt).  -The UAG Scope Mount I bought prior to this won't slide on the reciever with the upper reciever cover on. So mounting a scope is going to be tough to do.  SOME PEOPLE think the M150 spring is hard to pull back. I would lube it somewhat if it needs it, but you get used to it.  Don't pull it the wrong way. If you pull the bolt at a weird angle you're obviously going to damage it. Have THE STOCK AGAINST YOUR SHOULDER AND USE YOUR  INDEX AND MIDDLE FINGERS AND PULL STRAIGHT BACK. Then push straight forward to load a round.  As far as customization, you could probably buy a wood kit for the stock and foreend. There's also a CO2 conversion kit available, which makes cocking the gun effortless but increases the velocity by a lot. And, of course, you can scope this gun.  Overall, I DEFINITELY recommend this to any sniper. Easy to use, simple internals, and performs great. And the price has gone down on this monster gun, it's a steal compared to it's original $180 price.  UPDATE - used it yesterday in a skirmish. It held up prettywell. The shooting was fairly consistent if you adjest sights correctly. The one thing is, I can't wait to scope this thing because iron sights are so iffy. I found out a little too late that only the Leapers 5th Gen mount supposedly works on this gun. So, gonna have to buy that, then get a scope.

review_body:
This is a preliminary \\"just opened the box\\" review. This magnifier is not particularly suited for reading. It'd be great for crafts or sewing.

Uses 2 AA batteries (a plus). (Button batteries are a minus, such as SR1130/LR1130.)

Getting batteries into the battery compartment is something a senior would find hard to do (a minus). It's not super hard, just awkward. You must have nimble fingers. I'd rather have AA or AAA batteries and have it somewhat hard to get the batteries. I don't like teeny button batteries where if you don't get the battery/ies in just right, the batteries flip out the casing, fly all over the room, and are hard to find. Button batteries for elders with dogs or cats are dangerous, since a dog or cat could eat one fairly easily and then you have a gigantic veterinary bill.

The light is very bright (a plus).

A round lens for reading is a minus; for sewing or crafts, a round lens is a plus.

During reading, this magnifier only shows a few words, not a whole line of text (a minus). \\"Not showing a whole line of text\\" leads me to believe that this magnifier is not good for reading.

The little stand is nice (a plus).

It has a spot lens too (depends on what you're using the magnifier for). A spot lens is suitable for sewing or crafts (a plus). I loathe spot lenses for reading--they get in the way (a minus).

I keep my magnifiers in a terry cloth pocket pot-holders so they don't get scratched.

The directions on how to open the battery compartment are in the battery compartment (a minus). That means if you can't figure out how to open the battery compartment by yourself, there are no directions to tell you--doesn't make a whole lot of sense, does it? You could go on the Carson Optical website and see the directions there.

review_body:

Luckily the other three are sufficient as to hold everything together and not vibrate or make sounds when running at about 7 mph.

In fact, the you cannot hear the motor at all, all that you do hear is the belt going across the deck. The speakers are sufficient, especially for this range of treadmill....they're not high quality but they will push some music to you w/o having to wear headphones.

I'll write more about the quality of the treadmill as I train for a marathon for this fall....(outside in South Mississippi gets a bit humid and scorching hot in the summer).

Update*
The front screw of the motor was loose, I had to tighten it up....didn't present much of a problem, just something I noticed while I was adjusting the belt.

By default the belt rides to the left a bit, you'll see a bit of a gap between the belt and the edge of the deck on the right side. I've tried to adjust this but it seems that the belt pulley coming off of the motor is just off to the left a bit. It's adjusted now and I have about 25 miles on it and is going strong.

product_title: VISM by NcStar  Molle Pals Vest
review_body:
The quality of this vest is quite good, for the price. The MOLLE webbing is consistently spaced and strongly stitched (two things that I have found can be lacking on other cheap MOLLE items). The front of the vest, from the chest down, is mesh; this definitely helps keep one a bit cooler. The back of the vest has a hydration pouch pocket, including two straps to keep the pouch from sliding down the pocket. The Velcro shoulder closures are very secure; the front of the vest uses two flaps on each shoulder to sandwich the back flaps, creating a very strong hold.

A few things to note: I am rather short (5'5\\"), and the vest ends up coming down a little further then I like, even with the shoulder flaps adjusted to the shortest height. Thus, the included belt rides low on my hips; it therefore cannot be comfortably tightened. However, this is not too much of an issue because the straps that hold the belt to the vest are very secure. The weight of the belt (I have 8 single-stack 9mm 15-round Hi-Point 995 magazines in Tuff Products pouch) is therefore held by the vest, and you don't even notice it.

Furthermore, if your stomach is more round than flat, the three buckles might seem a bit inadequate. They will stay firmly fastened, however your stomach might start to peak out between them. I am planning on replacing them with a zipper that I will sew on; this will not affect the adjustability of the vest because the girth is taken in/out on the sides.

I do wish that the sides of the vest extended further back, allowing for accessories (holsters, pouches, etc.) to be worn closer to the 3/9-o'clock positions. The smaller you are in the waist, the more the front panels will reach to the back; I am of the rounder variety, so this is not the case for me.

I gave this vest 4 stars for the quality vs. price; if it were more expensive, it would quickly drop to a 3-star product; if it had a zipper front closure and more adjustability in length, it would pop up to a 5-star.in length, it would pop up to a 5-star.

product_title: Muzzelite Bullpup - Ruger 10/22 Rifle Stock
review_body:
I called Muzzlelite before ordering the Bullpup. I told them I had a muzzle-weighted, 16.5\\" barrel. Muzzle diameter was measured as 0.999 inches. I was assured by a technician that it would fit. I might need to do minor trimming.

The truth is a little different! If I had a tool that could bore that accurately, I would be left with 0.04\\" of plastic holding the sling and the front site to the remainder of the firearm! That reaming would go about 3\\" into the Bullpup, so don't expect to use your trusty Dremel for that!

I still kept it - just paid another $60 for a new sporter barrel (18\\", so Bullpup meets federal regs) - and waited another week for that! I think that hurt the most. I settled for one with a front sight on it so as not to wait much longer than a week.

Other than that, it is pretty well designed, and has lent itself to other fun modifications. That included putting a Weaver-mount scope on it. Although from the picture it looks like it could take an AR-15 mount, it won't. I expected that, though, and don't see that as a real drawback.

I'm still having fun with it, and it does look wicked!

product_title: Crosman Phantom .177 Caliber Break Barrel Air Rifle up-to 1000 FPS
review_body:
I just received this rifle this morning and couldn't wait to try it out. (I love Amazon Prime...today is Saturday and I ordered it Thursday evening!) I had already read some reviews etc and was prepared for difficulty cocking the break barrel, but I found it smoother than any I had previously tried. It does take a good effort, but I am nearly 66 and maybe not as stout as I used to me, but stouter than most old dudes, I guess. My wife had a little difficulty, at first, but after getting the \\"leverage\\" she did just fine.

I set up a target to prepare for the time the very annoying squirrel attacks my wife's bird feeder again. My faithful watchdog is patiently sitting on the lawn, now to let me know when the varmint appears. He is 8 pounds of pure venom, that one. Anyway, the first shot was a little to the right, so I had my wife try it and she put one nearly in the same spot. So, I adjusted windage a few times and the last one was nearly dead center, so I think I am ready for that bad squirrel to show.

I had seen some reviews stating the sights were cheap etc., but although I am not expert by any means, I thought they were just fine and I love the way they line up easily. I thought I would get a scope for this, but now, I am not so sure...I may leave it this way and see how it goes.

For the money, I really like the way this rifle looks, feels, and shoots. I know we are going to have a lot of fun together. When we are enjoying our summer property, it will be nice to have this around to get rid of some of the creatures getting in the way of the creatures we love. Or just plunking for fun. Great buy, I think! I will follow up after I have used it for a while.

product_title: Thule Atlantis 1800 XT Cargo Box
review_body:
Purchased this Cargo box a couple months ago. Actually purchased it on a different site (found it cheaper). Purchased it for use on our 2007 Volvo XC90 for our trip from Chicago to Orlando.

I read a bunch of reviews on gas mileage and also noise. I did not see any noticable difference in the gas mileage. This was a 19 hour trip each way, and I got about 19.5 mpg on the trip. The posted mpg for highway with the Volvo XC90 is 20 mpg. So overal I think this was pretty darn close.

As far as road noise, there was some at first. But then I closed the sunshade on the sunroof and it got A LOT better. So, there was some, but I did not think it was very much. When we got to Orlando, I took the cargo box off. I was worried about parking garages and stuff (wasn't an issue really anyway). So, I took it off while driving around WDW for the week. The noise from the cross bars was substantially more than the cargo box. There was a noticable humming and tone that was clearly audible.

Note I did have a make shift horizontal bar on it. When I purchased the cargo box, I thought I had the factory horizontal bars, but I was wrong. So I made some bars from some 3/4\\" galvanized pipe and some hose clamps. Actually worked really well. Anyway, the profile of the bar is round. And it made A LOT of noise. A LOT more than when the cargo box was installed. So that tells me that the box installed moves the air very well.

Overall the box worked great. It looked good on the car, and held a lot. I had some trouble closing it before the trip, so I took some stuff out. On the way back, I realize the 3 points to put extra pressure on the top to get it to close. Then it worked fine.

I would think they could make the pins with a more pointed front so if they did not line up perfectly, it would self-align?

But otherwise it was great and I would suggest anyone get this cargo box.

product_title: Ben's Insect Repellent Pump, 4-Ounce
review_body:
This is some strong stuff. I transferred some over into one of those plastic 3 oz. sprayers you can buy at the grocery store to get liquids through TSA, and a few days into my journey the hard plastic container had turned soft and jellish. The degrading plastic didn't improve the chemical smell of the bug spray, either. Next time I travel I'm just going to pack the entire bottle in my checked bags, although I'm not totally confident that the original bottle won't leak if it's not assiduously stored upright. And the design isn't super space efficient.

On the plus side: I used Ben's daily in a high-malaria zone for a month and I didn't get a single identifiable mosquito bite! Maybe it was just luck, but other people were definitely getting bites. Four ounces will last a long time, probably even a few months of daily application. Also, I didn't really notice the smell much except when I was putting it on. So even though it may slowly turn my skin to a soft jelly, I'm sticking with it.

review_body: I tried 4 other cheaper watches prior to settling on this watch and they were \\"OK\\" but not great.  The watch is the one. Its also got the stop watch, timer, heart beat range and etc. if you need those.  The batteries can be replaced on the band and on the watch itself. I'm finding I prefer this watch over the display on my tread mill and at times strap it to the treadmill. This watch/band combo transmits using a digital connection so works right next or on my treadmill and I not see any interference.
