Containers are everything. And this container made by Guyot will handle everything you can throw at it and more.

1. Tight sealing lid - check!
2. Wide mouth for easy filling - check!
3. Reusable and durable - check!
4. Can withstand direct flame for boiling water - check!

As others have said, this is the canteen chosen by serious survivalists. The company itself is based in Maine and comes highly recommended by Swiss outdoor adventurists.

You won't be disappointed with the purchase. Well worth the money, since it will last a lifetime.

product_title: Jaguar CR-013 Series Crossbow Kit, 175-Pound
review_body:
This is a great croosbow for beginners. It shoots very well, easy to cock. The bolts that come with it are kinda cheap, I would invest in some carbon bolts before you start tring to sight in your bow. The bolts that come with it bend very easy. I found that a 18\\" carbon bolt worked best from about 20yards. The weight on this crossbow is awesome, you will have NO PROBLEM carrying this to your tree stand. The strap broke the first day, but you really don't need one with the light weight. I did remove the front sight to make loading bolts easier with the 18\\" bolts.

No cons on the crossbow.

Only cons are with the strap braking ( which I feel is unneeded anyways) and the bolts are cheap.

review_body: This was a major let down after doing the original P90x version. The workouts are not challenging at all compared to the original workouts, and the format is not as good either. Instruction is not as good, and timing between exercises is to close. I plan on using them to add into my original P90X workout routine as add ons.

product_title: 7" Handguard Ladder Rail Cover (18 Ladder Bar), Black (pack of 4)
review_headline: These fit like a glove and stay in place, look very cool too.
review_body: My rail came with covers, but they were very large and fat. They made the rails look cheap and bulky, I actually hated the provided rails. I found these rails and for this price I bought 3 packs just to have extra in case I change things around on my rifle. The grip and feel is perfect, the fore end doesn't feel like I am holding a 4 inch tube with little control. These rails have a rubber feel that is just enough to give a good grip but not sticky. They also add very little girth to the fore end. I think by removing the old covers and using these that it dropped some weight on the front end of my rifle also. review_headline: LOVE the machine. No online community
review_body:
The machine itself is fantastic... but, shouldn't be considered for competitive or online racing via Row Pro 3 software (which only supports Concept2). Row Pro is the only rowing software that actually has users racing online daily, with 6-12 races per day. Water Rower has \\"We-Row\\" which in theory is competent software... but no one uses it, which makes it useless. WaterRower over-sells this software and there \\"community\\" on their website, but it is non-existent. They have no forums, and no way of connecting with other members. Their driver support for PC's is spotty, and for Mac's - non-existent. The software is a complete mess.

The rower machine is great though. I wish I didn't have to sell it, but due to the limited ability to use it online and in competition environments, it doesn't matter how good it is, it's worthless to me.

product_title: 510IC Indoor Cycle by Diamondback Fitness
review_body:
First you should understand that this is a spinning bike. I would not recommend any spinning bike unless you have taken spinning classes and know what you are getting into. This is not a pedal-along-while-watching t.v. exercise bike. If done correctly, you will be out of breath and sweating profusely by the end of your thirty to forty-five minute workout. This is as it should be.
I have been an instructor of spinning in a local gym for the last eight years. Recently, due to time constraints, my wife expressed an interest in getting a spin bike for our home, and we begin looking for one. We first started shopping for a used Spinner Pro or Spinner NXT, because these are what are used in the gym,but none ever showed up in our area. I didn't want to buy a used \\"cleaned\\" or \\"reconditioned\\" unit sight unseen over the net. Buying blind just isn't for me, so we started looking at the local sporting goods and bike stores. The bike stores carried little or no indoor exercise bikes and the sporting goods stores had flimsy, wobbly things that were, to put it frankly, junk. In fact I would consider them dangerous. Then we found the Diamondback.
I was immediately impressed with the solidity of the unit. No loose seating, no loose handlebars, no slack anywhere. And my gosh, was it quiet! Taking it home, I had to modify the fore and aft positioning of the handlebars, but that was it.
Resistance is by computer, and is something that I will have to get used to, but it is very effective. The computer has a learning curve also, but won't be too bad for anyone who can read. It is smaller than a gym spinner, and it is lighter too, but in a home this is not necessarily a negative. After all it is not going to be used four times a day like the gym bikes.

PROS: Solid unit. Quiet operation. Price. Easily moved around. Easy, solid and positive adjustments. Computer controlled exercise programs. Can work you hard.
CONS: Computer controlled exercise programs. Can work you hard. Can work you too hard.

This is the first home spinning bike I have found that was worth buying. I would recommend it.ou hard. Can work you too hard. This is the first home spinning bike I have found that was worth buying. I would recommend it.

product_title: KA-BAR Full Size US Marine Corps  Fighting Knife, Straight
review_headline: My Review of the Ka-Bar USMC Fighting Knife
review_body: I bought the knife because I've wanted one for some time, and because of the good reviews. I'm sure you know that some things end up being made in a junk fashion to save costs, and the company hopes that people will accept their good name, and foeget about the change in quality. I didn't know if Ka-Bar had gone this route.  They didn't.  I was surprised at how strong its construction feels. Balance is great, and the fit in my hand just FEELS RIGHT. No looseness... very tight. Solid. The edge didn't look fine honed, but it did shave hairs from my arm. (Yes, I tried it....) I took it to a cardboard box and hacked away at double and triple thickness, just for fun. The box came apart easily. I've found that it meets my expectations handily.  The sheath got a few bad or \\"eh\\" reviews. I found the USMC logo to be respectfully impressed. Very nice. The leather is a bit weak, though, and as I insert the knife, the hilt scrapes away at it. No damage to the knife's finish, yet. The sheath would have been better if it was built to allow for a space at the hilt.. as it is, the thing needs to bend to allow re-sheathing. I'll probably go for a hard cased unit once I decide on one. For now, though, I'm happy as is.  If you've wanted a full-sized Ka-Bar, this little girl will make you happy. It's the real deal.

product_title: Smooth Fitness 5.65 Treadmill (2014 Model)
review_body:
My husband and I live in an area with cold wet winters and we wanted a treadmill for basic exercise purposes so we could stay in shape when we didn't want to run outside. He is a runner and I am a walker (very fast speed walker). After lots of research on different review/critic sites, I landed upon Smooth Fitness. This 5.65 model fit the specs we needed and was in our price range so we made the purchase. We bought and had it delivered at the end of 2011 but didn't set it up and start using it until January 2012. So far we have been very happy with this treadmill. The functions seem to work, it's comfortable to use and it doesn't seem to be too loud (for a treadmill). It is probably used 3-4 times a week by each of us. So far so good. I wouldn't say we have any complaints. To be fair this is also our first treadmill we've owned, so we also don't have anything to contrast it against. If I had to do over, I would make the purchase again.
One note- we have the treadmill in our bedroom and wanted to put a mat on top of the carpet/underneath the treadmill to protect the floor. We found the treadmill did not roll well on top of the mat. In fact we could barely get it to roll. Instead we just had to get three people to lift the treadmill up on to the mat. If you are also trying to get a mat under yours, save yourself the time of trying to figure out how to roll it on and just get more people to come help you lift it.

product_title: KEP Italia Mica Riding Helmet with Black Grid
review_body: Once you try this helmet, you will never want to use another helmet again.  This is the ultimate Bugatti of helmets!  The first time I tried it, I never again had \\"helmet hair\\", nor did my hair or bangs get wet or squashed. The technology on the air flow circulation is incredible. The lightness and comfort of this helmet is unbeatable. It does not move or slide. Once I misplaced my helmet and had to use my old Charles Owen helmet, and it felt like putting a concrete torture device on my head, that weighed a ton. Afterwards my hair was wet and all squished, leaving a mark on my forehead.  With the KEP, you can control how much air flow you want depending on the weather. Also, unlike the top GPA which allows rain to come through it's vents, and your head still sweats, the KEP has no openings for any rain to enter. With the \\"Mica\\", you can just wipe off the water and it's as good as new. With the detachable inner linings, the fit is custom and you can wash or inexpensively replace the inner lining.  The outer shell lasts forever.  The KEP design is very flattering as well, compared to other helmets. If you read about the technology, it outperforms most other helmets. In the crash tests, it is one of the safest helmets on the market.  I am glad this helmet is available in the US. I am noticing that more and more FEI riders are switching to the KEP helmets.

product_title: Cold Steel 97KMS Kukri Machete
review_body: Out of the box the Cold Steel Kukri Machete with PVC Handle (13 inch blade and 18 inch total length)  is utility sharp (dull-ish) with smudgy black finish coating that's also on the blade edge.  Produced in South Africa, from first look it's not very pretty or impressive at all.  The Cordera sheath is from China and good for storage.  It's dirt cheap and looks it too.  I won't go too much into the sheath as it does the job and you would have to pay good money  to get a better one.  For those experienced with knives this might be disappointing for $20,  but considering that I got this for just under $16 I think it was a great deal.  Surprisingly the knife is good enough to open up a coconut that I was holding in my hand  (disclaimer: don't try this at home and get a vice to hold the coconut)  Using several short precise swings, I easily popped opened a coconut (pre-barked).  One handed long swings this thing won't go through more than an inch of wood, so it's decent for clearing brush.  The weight of the top of the blade provides enough momentum to really get the job done.  If you sharpen this knife, you'll be able to clear objects with much less force than other brush cutters out there.  Overall the knife is very durable and can take a serious beating.  If you check out some youtube videos, you'll see some people have used the same knife to chop through 2x4's (using a 2 lb engineering hammer to force it through) and concrete blocks (by hand).  So in conclusion, it's a rough diamond, but a diamond nonetheless.  The factory edge is dull, but if you want it to be easier to use, get a file and get to work on that edge! ;)  The alternative is to blow $180 on the Cold Steel Gurkha Kukri. :D  You'll get a thicker and sharper blade but you won't want to use it on anything for fear of staining the polish. ;)

product_title: Black Mountain Products New Strong Man Set of 6 Resistance Bands
review_body:
Bought these for P90x and love them. Even though the max weight is 30-40 lbs, that's plenty for a P90x workout.

These are indeed, the highest quality workout bands I've ever used, hands down. First off, the bands are not too long, which is a common problem. They are just the right length so you don't have to loop them and step on them to shorten them. The bands are not going to come out of the handles; they are securely in the handle. The handles are hard plastic and look and feel as though they can take plenty of abuse.

On the instruction sheet there is a chart that shows what band color corresponds to what weight. There are also exercises listed on the instructions. I wish that they included a small, high quality laminated sheet that I could put on my wall that shows the band color/weight chart; that'd be nice. Right now I have the instructions taped to the wall that show the band color/weight chart and it's pretty ghetto looking.

There is one issue though that may be a concern for some, but I didn't mark the product down because I knew it going into it. The strongest cable tops out around 30-40 lbs, so if you need more weight, you can't add weight/other bands. Some other band sets allow you to add multiple bands to one handle, but that's impossible to do with these. The bands are fixed to the handles, so if you want to use two bands together, you're essentially going to have to hold 4 handles, and that's really hard to do because they are big handles. But the other side of the coin is that this is one reason why these bands are so good, is because those parts that can break off with being able to add bands are eliminated. Like I said, I knew this going into it so it's not a flaw, but might be something that you don't like.

If you have any questions, just ask in the comments and I'll try and respond promptly.

product_title: FLIRTY GIRL FITNESS PROGRAM
review_body:

However, it was a different approach to my workouts (always went to the gym and it got a little boring)and I heard that it could help with weight loss as well I purchased the Chair Dance, Chair Fit,Booty Beat, Abs & Booty, Pole Dance, Pole Fit plus the pole to give it a try. The Chair Fit workout is very inventive and utilizes what you have at home so you're not buying a ton of other things to work out with. It was a very great workout that left me sore the next day. Even though I workout almost every single day, I subsitute that for two workout days and I've noticed that I'm getting stronger from the last time I use that particular workout. Chair Dance and Pole Dance is just a nice little bonus so you can learn something sexy for your partner. I wouldn't use Booty Beat nor Chair Dance as a form of exercise though.

I do agree with the other reviewers that the packaging is less than ideal. When it was shipped to me, the Pole Dance DVD's container broke and the DVD has a scratch on it and I can't see the second part of that workout because I haven't had the time to get a DVD doctor to fix the scratch. If you're a bigger woman, you won't be able to use the stripper pole because of a weight restriction. Abs & Booty seems really disorganized. You will feel and see some results but not as dramatic as the commercial states. I was also given a menu of food I can eat and since I have Celiac Disease, most of the things on the menu I can't have. The food that I can have, it's not bad. I really wish that one day they'll have a fitness center in my area but for now, I'll use the videos!

product_title: Helios 4-weight 7' Fly Rod—mid Flex
review_body:
This is probably my favorite rod for small streams, though I have to admit that paraphernalia intense a sport as fly fishing is, I've got more than one favorite...

This one combines short length and light weight with surprising power and the ability to handle large fish.

Many people associate nothing more than six inch brookies with small stream fishing. What you're probably not prepared for when wading small streams is the wily brown trout that may be parked under an undercut bank or in a pool just a bit deeper that you'd expect in such small water. When one of these lunkers grabs your fly, watch out.

If you're armed with this Helios 4 weight you'll have a fighting chance. The seven foot length is perfect for managing overhanging branches and negotiating the tight spaces of your favorite brook. Orvis' mid flex taper allows controlled roll casting at short range, but still has the punch to deliver a # 12 Wulff into a stiff breeze. And you can drop small files with unexpected delicacy and pinpoint precision when needed.

This one is a classic...

product_title: Overboard 25 Liters Premium Waterproof Backpack Gear Bag
review_body:
This bag really works! I used it on a mountain bike, hike and repel trip. Lots of mud from the bike's tires, light rain, and lots of water from repelling in two small waterfalls were all kept out.

It sat securely and comfortably on my back for all the activities, even while repelling down the waterfalls and while unhooking at the bottom with water pouring on me and swimming from the base of the falls.

It has a lot of space. With extra space left I was able to hold dry clothes and towel, a camera and its bag (not the small hand size ones), sandwiches, bananas, extra water, roll of toilet paper. In the inside pocket and also with extra space left, my keys (car and bike lock), pocket flash light, pocket knife, glasses in case. The outside mesh pocket is perfect for bottled water / energy drink size beverage (20 OZ). There are lots of options to hock other items to the outside of the bag, I was able to hock my helmet.

A few useful points:
- do not over pack it. You want to get a few rolls of the top to ensure water is kept out
- when locking the top, make your wraps tight, use the top locking system instead of the locks on each side and use the velcro strap the runs from back to front to go over the top lock. Make the lock facing forward or backward instead of upward. I find the top lock system makes the seal tighter. Directing it forward or backward and placing the velcro strap over it secures it away from branches or other things that can hock your bag.
- carry a plastic bag or two inside it so you can put your wet items into the plastic bags so they will not wet all your other dry stuff!
- your friends will love you more when you can make a dry towel appear when everyone is wet and cold, you may want to use it first .... !

This Style CS is a tiny little tool that provides scissors, tweezers, and a file (of sorts, not the same level of usability you'd find on a \\"real\\" multitool) and it's packaged to look (as others have said) like the Skeletool's baby brother, carabiner and all, and which I find endearingly cool.  The bottle-opener and knife are nice as well for when I don't have the bigger tool handy.  This Style has joined my keychain making it EDC Jr. and both together are a nice useful and wickedly cool looking pair.  I considered other keychain friendly tools (Micro, Squirt, and a couple Victorinox) and I have a set of Swisstool keychain tools, but the Style wins a place on my main keychain because of the mini-caribiner; it allows me to quickly and easily attach/detach it to/from my keys for convenient independent use.  It also lets me hand it out as a bottle opener without handing out my keys with it.  That it pairs well with my Skeletool certainly cements my preference.  In fact, I think that the two should be sold as a set to begin with, or this one as a bonus/accessory to the other.

product_title: Copper John DN3 Sight Light Bracket
review_body: I bought the copper john (dead nuts 3 mark iii) sight (6 months ago), only to find out that it does not work right in the first place. The sight and the 3rd axis are somewhat flush but not perfectly. Apparently, this has been an issue with all of the dead nuts sights (I found this out when I took it to a shop yesterday to find out what was wrong with the wind adjustments). When I bought the sight, I took it to a different shop because it seemed like it had to be really tight or it would move around while on the bow (3rd axis and sight do not line up perfectly). This has been determined to be a flaw in the design of the dead nuts 3 sights and a common issue. Now, when you install the windage adjustments, it does not do much justice. The sight bracket and the 3rd axis bracket has to be so tight that, the windage adjustment cannot turn without EXTREME pressure and even then, it does not adjust up and down without loosening the main screw for the 3rd axis with an Allen key (isn't it funny that we buy the wind adjustments to avoid using the Allen keys and to make last second adjustments, and yet, we still need the Allen keys?). It will adjust left to right with extreme pressure and you hear the \\" Pop, Creak, Crank\\", noise. I messed with the Allen adjustments on the knobs and it does not matter because the problem is the sight bracket to the 3rd axis and the 3rd axis to the sight. I took it to another shop that I confide in for everything now. He sells the dead nuts 3 (therefore, not as bias as a shop that would not sell it). He said that 3 of his pro shooters (that shoot for his shop) tried it with the SAME ISSUES! They have a dead nuts 3 mark i that they tested and have been trying to sell for a year now. He said they had the same problem. He looked at my sight to check the windage adjustments and said everything was right. It was his conclusion (as well as other people) that it was a design flaw. $103 bucks for the sight (plus shipping, don't remember what I paid for shipping), $10 for the light (15 after shipping), $16 for the light bracket (after shipping), $22 for the adjustment kit (after shipping), and 10 for the 2nd axis (after shipping). So,  $166 Dollars plus the shipping of the sight. What an expensive mistake! The sight is durable but, what good is it if it has to be cranked down and ineffective?

review_body: I'll start off by saying this is a nice little knife for the money, even though amazon sent me one of these in white instead of black :-). The description is a bit thin though, so I'll fill in some of the gaps. First, the knife is 7.5\\" in the OPEN position. The blade measures at 3.5\\" and the handle make up th rest of the length. The blade is almost as thin as a straight razor, and has a wicked sharp point. The edge was not great, in fact it was rolled a bit. This cleaned up quickly on a fine stone, but it needs a little work to be shaving sharp (which I believe it should have no problem obtaining). Folded, the knife is just over 1/2\\" at it's widest, roughly 1/4\\" thick, and 4\\" long. product_title: Confidence Power Plus Motorized Electric Treadmill
review_headline: I wish I could have used this treadmill!
review_body:
I was so excited to get this treamill a week ago. It came out of the box pretty much put together already. I couldn't find the user manual at first (it was stuck in the bottom of the box under styrofoam) but I'm a smart girl and the device was easy enough to unfold, screw in a couple of knobs, and plug in. Presto! Then it turns out that I receive a treadmill with a busted power button. It turned on, let me select my speed and how long I wanted to walk for, but pressing the power button on the display did nothing.
So this happens, and I'm very understanding of it. I emailed the seller, they gave me a couple of troubleshooting ideas- with a very prompt response- and those did not work, so they said they would ship me a replacement as well as a prepaid sticker to get the broken one out of my house.
Today the replacement arrives... and the UPS deliveryman has no knowledge of needing to pick up the broken unit. So he drops off the new one, and now I have two treadmills in my apartment. Moments later, I find that the sticker was attached to the side of my replacement. That would have been good to know. Before UPS left. So I got to go online and ask UPS to come back to my apartment... for a charge of $9.23 to pick it up. All they needed to do was TELL me it was there, I could have been saved that money that I did not need to pay.
But I was still ready to write that off, until I took out my new treadmill, got it set up, turned it on, set my speed and time and hit power. It counted down the way the manual says it should and then.... nothing.
One defective unit is one thing. Two is a totally different story. And now I'm so disappointed because I really did want this treadmill! It looks great, it's exactly the right size for me... but I don't think that third time is going to be a charm for this. I'm currently waiting for a reply from the seller to see if there's any troubleshooting to be done on this one, but I think I'm going to have to try and get a refund, because this is just too much.

UPDATE 2/8/2012
The company is going to refund the treadmill and pay for UPS shipping, so that's something, at least. Still would not recommend this treadmill for obvious reasons, but I do appreciate them trying to replace it for me and eating the shipping costs.is just too much. UPDATE 2/8/2012 The company is going to refund the treadmill and pay for UPS shipping, so that's something, at least. product_title: Petzl GriGri Belay Device 2.01 With FREE Climbing DVD
review_headline: Lighter than the original, just as useful
review_body:
This and the original Grigri are the two most common assisted-locking belay devices. I've had some experience with the original, a few weeks with this, and none with the Trango Cinch or the like, so take my impressions for what they're worth.

The major reason you'd buy an assisted-locking device is for the extra safety margin. The Grigri has a locking cam that halts the rope when it pulls out at a certain speed. That's a tremendous boon where the belayer is inattentive or inexperienced, or where the belayer can't see the climber. It's also next to impossible to get the webbing of your brake hand stuck in it, as I've seen twice occur with sudden falls to ATCs in the last three months. And when your climber wants to hang, it's a lot easier to sit and chill when you don't need to keep constant heavy braking tension.

Relative to the old Grigri, this one is significantly smaller and lighter. The old one could feel like an anchor if left on the harness for difficult climbs. This one, not so much. The friction lip is also a bit wider and easier to slot your fingers under, a helpful fulcrum if you're holding the cam down to feed rope. Inside, the rope grooves are sharper and tighter, which allows Petzl to officially support thinner ropes, but has some downstream implications I get into below.

The belay learning curve for top-roping is very short. For the initial feed of rope through the device, the Grigri is ingrained with clear directional diagrams. Taking rope is identical to what you'd do with an ATC.

Feeding rope for lead climbs takes a bit more practice. Conventional belay technique has your brake hand on the rope at all times. You don't really modify that with the Grigri, but you may need to leave additional slack between the mechanism and your brake hand, and use a thumb from that hand to hold the locking cam down while you pull through. It is actually possible to feed rope very quickly without engaging the locking cam if both ends of the rope are vertical, but I found this method inconsistent. An advantage of manual-locking belay devices is that, when the lead climber falls, they allow the belayer to feed rope for a softer brake and a dynamic catch. This ability is negated by the Grigri's immediate cam engagement, though a lighter belayer may well lift off the ground, a dynamic catch in itself.

Descending and letting down climbers is a novel experience. All of the original Grigris I've used have been very forgiving with the thick and fuzzy indoor ropes I've encountered. The Grigri 2, not so much. The difference between your climber inching and plummeting is about 10% pressure on the handle. I eventually grew adept at quick and controlled descents after about a dozen belays, but only by fixing my hand in place and using my shoulder to adjust the pressure. Fingers alone inevitably led to a quick drop, followed by my climber lifting me off the ground when I let off and the cam suddenly closed. While Petzl's literature implies that the friction lip should control the speed instead of the handle, I've found that careful manipulation of both is necessary. Also of note: with the original Grigri, you could press on the cam to lower a hanging climber without using the handle. For better or worse, that's no longer possible.

On balance though, unless I need the additional versatility of a conventional ATC, I always reach for a Grigri. I don't recommend it at the outset to novices because it can promote sloppy belay technique, but after you've been at it for a little while, it's a wonderful accessory. A simpler, cheaper, and slightly less foolproof alternative is Mammut's Smart Belay Device.

ADDENDUM: The very first copies of the Grigri 2 were recalled for a defective release handle. Any new copy is likely to be post-recall. Beware used copies from early 2011. The affected serial numbers are on Petzl's website.

review_body:

The installation instructions seemed pretty straight forward and I even found a couple of youtube videos so I could watch someone else install them before going through the process on my own. This was my first ever grip installation so readers can consider this a review from someone fairly new to aftermarket firearm accessories.
My installation didn't go quite as smoothly as it should have. Unfortunately the hole in the Hogue plastic spring cup holder wasn't machined very well at the factory and there were some rough hard plastic edges inside that made re-installation of the grip pin impossible. I had to use a drill bit smaller than the diameter of the hole to remove the excess plastic material. This added 15 minutes to the installation process.
After finally re-installing the pin the rest of the process is pretty straight forward.
The new rubber grips slipped on fairly easily and fit pretty well. I wish they hugged the gun frame just a little better towards the top of the frame handle but overall the fitment is good. They feel good in the hand and make the grip a good bit thicker. I doubt most people with smaller hands would want to install these grips, but guys with larger hands will find them very comfortable. I haven't been to the range yet with this upgrade, but based on other pistols I own with factory installed Hogue grips I'm sure I will be happy with how they feel when shooting the pistol.

The 44 inch backboard will be too small, and it just may not be sturdy enough for some more serious basketball, but again, for $100, it's really pretty solid and I'm very happy with it. In 3-4 years I'll upgrade (although for my 3 year old this will still be good). All in all, I give it 5 stars and recommend for smaller kids and/or a small budget.

Box came in just 3-4 days, no damage, and everything accounted for. I'm fairly handy, but made sure I took my time so I didn't do anything wrong. I organized the parts, reviewed the direction and got started. I can see how someone could get this together in 90 minutes or so, but it took me longer. No issues, the directions are clear and it's really not very complicated. Once I had it together, I noticed the rim angle was tilting up, so I bought some extra washers (same size as those included), removed the backboard, put the washers behind the backboard on the upper two hole connections (2 high and 2 low), and it worked perfectly. The rim is 100% level now.

The sand is pain, but I got into a good routine with my kids helping. Bought 6 50 pound bags, and it could probably hold another bag. My method was to empty the sand bags into a wheel barrow first, and then fill a small bucket (used for car washing) with a few shovel fulls, and pour the bucket into the funnel while my kids held the funnel. Once empty, tilt the basket to get the sand to slide to the front, and repeat...fill the bucket, pour into funnel, tilt to slide the sand and so on. Probably took a few dozen or more to get all 6 sand bags in, but it moved quickly. Use the fill hole near the back of the base.

One last thing I noticed is that there is some play at the bottom of the pole either side to side or front to back. I stuffed a few nails in the gap between the pole and base to act as shims and it did reduce the play a bit.

product_title: Kershaw Ken Onion Chive 1600BBCKT
review_body: I've owned my black Kershaw Ken Onion Chive for about 10 years.  This is an all steel, automatic frame-lock lockblade knife (think legal, small switch-blade).  It can be opened and closed easily with one hand.  From a usefulness standpoint, that is a very nice feature since it leaves your other hand free to hold what you're working on.  Usefulness aside, it's also just plain cool!  The knife is a fraction under 3\\" long closed and has a 2\\" blade.  It came with the sharpest edge by far of any pocket knife I've ever bought - I'm talking razor utility knife blade sharp.  The steel is excellent and it has held its edge very very well over time (and I carried it every day for years).  Unless you use the thing constantly, you may never have to sharpen it.  This is probably a good thing because the curved scimitar blade shape and black coating make sharpening a bit trickier than for your common clip or drop-point shaped stainless blade.  It has a pocket clip mounted on one side.  I personally have never found it useful and think it degrades from the appearance.  But, I'm sure there are those who regularly clip their knives to their pocket or their money and think this is the greatest feature in the world.  The clip on mine has a bit of back and forth wiggle because the holes in it are a bit larger than the small bolts that mount it to the handle.  I consider this a bit of an annoyance defect.  However, the knife itself (body and blade) is machined absolutely perfectly.  Mine has been flicked open and closed thousands of times over the past 10 years and there is no wiggle at all.  Overall, the quality is fantastic.  The only real con in my eyes is that it's not particularly attractive (no matter which finish you choose), though it does have fairly nice / stylish lines and fits very comfortably and safely in your hand.  In sum, this is great, functional, use every day, little knife.  I paid almost $70 for mine from a mall cutlery shop before internet sales were the norm.  Nowthey're significantly cheaper, but I would buy it again in a heartbeat at the original price in this or one of the other finishes.  It's the coolest little knife I own - neat lines (if not pretty), sharp, one-handed operation, and very well made.

product_title: Econo Machete, 12 in.
review_body: This is just the machete you want for any sort of environment where some chopping & some batoning are required, but weight is also an issue.  I've used machetes for a year in South America where I had to clear trails, and while you *might* want a bigger blade for the initial blaze, for carrying on a daily basis and hacking new growth/vines, this sort of blade is perfect.  It's actually a harder steel than the machetes I used in the jungle, and will work better for some things, but will be more dangerous for running around with unsheathed (some guides in the mountains can use their soft stainless steel machetes to keep themselves upright on slopes.  I wouldn't do that with this machete because a) it's sharper and b) the blade might break).  For woody secondary growth, something like a kukri might be called for, but this machete will handle light stuff in forest understories much better since it can easily baton.  You might want to take some sandpaper to the rougher plastic edges of the handle so you don't wear your palm away, but I don't see a reason to buy something more expensive like a Kbar Cutlass - the technique you use will matter a lot more than the quality of the implement.

The watch typically works great, and on long runs it is nice to be distracted by flipping through the different screens, or by watching your speed. product_title: Horizon Fitness EX-79 Elliptical Trainer
review_body:
Ok, we all know what the challenge is, buy an elliptical that doesn't make noise, trouble-free operation and doesn't cost as much as a car.

Can it be done with the Ex-79? Yes and no.

The upside of this machine is that it's so quiet you don't have to raise the volume on your tv. Impressive.

The downside, it's not made in the US. Go to Horizon's website and they act like the equipment is built here. It isn't.

Shipping damage - The unit came to our house in a box that was damaged, so was some of the gear inside. The cup was smashed, several covers were cracked and the control console was defective. You can't use the built-in fan, it reeks of cheap plastic chemicals. Maybe someday the smell will go away, but it hasn't yet.

The good news is that we called the company and they were quick to respond with replacement parts.
It was also easy to build, with all the parts already organized in their own corresponding packets with instructions.

Would I buy again? Yes, it's a decent machine for the price. My wife loves it.

product_title: Zero Tolerance G10 Handle with Speed Safe
review_headline: One of the best knives under $100!
review_body:
I've had this knife for a few weeks now so I thought I'd do a sort-of first impressions review.

BLADE:
The ZT0350's blade is a nice thick slab of S30V steel, with a black DLC coating. It's 3 1/4 inches long and comes to a point that's somewhere between a regular drop-point and a sheep's foot. The tip is somewhat wide so it's not the best for puncturing, but it would be really hard to snap off. Out of the box it's sharp enough to shave with, and any time you want you can send it in to Zero Tolerance and they'll put a factory edge back on it for you free of charge.

DEPLOYMENT:
The easiest way to deploy it is to use the tang flipper. All it takes is a little bump and the assisted open takes over and whips the blade with a positive \\"shlack\\"! The right-handed thumb stud also works great, but the left-handed one is really hard to use normally and downright impossible when wearing gloves. The reason for this is that the handle is cut out more for the right-handed side, while the left-handed thumb stud is flush with the handle material.

LOCKUP:
This knife locks up super solid with it's beefy stainless steel liner lock, no wobble in any direction. The lock is also pretty easy to access for one handed closing, although it's a bit tricky since it is assisted open.

HANDLE:
As mentioned before this knife has thick stainless steel liners which are milled out near the bottom to save weight. Over them are textured G10 handle scales for a positive grip. The thumb ramp has gimping on both the liners and the handle scales, as well as the blade tang. There is similar gimping on the bottom of the handle for holding in reverse grip. This knife is extremely ergonomic, it just fits into your hand like a it was made for you. I've held it a lot and haven't noticed any hotspots yet. It also has a lanyard hole which is just barely big enough to fit 550 paracord.

POCKET CLIP:
The pocket clip is removable and can beput in any corner for right or left handed/tip up or tip down carry. It is attached via two T6 torx bolts. Like most high-end knives it's pretty stiff, but if you pull it out of your pocket fast enough it doesn't cause any problem. It rides fairly low for tip down carry however a good 3/4 of an inch sticks out for tip up carry.

SIZE/WEIGHT:
At 5 3/4 oz and a closed length of 4 5/8 inches this knife is pushing the limit of what most people \\"pocketable\\". I've been carrying it everyday since I got it and barely notice it though.

CONCLUSION:
The 0350 is a great knife for EDC, and I think it would excel as a camp/utility folder. If you're thinking about buying this knife I highly recommend you do it, it's an excellent blade. IMHO this is one of the best knives under $100 ($99.83 when I bought it).

product_title: Epee Blade - Vniti FIE Bare Electric
review_body: The Vniti's have held up at our club well for the upper level epeeists. The other blade that has had good longevity for us has been the LP stamped blade. The two blades have been very comparable in blade life though the LP stamped probably lasts a tad longer. The Vniti blades don't take odd sets like most of the forged blades we have used. They also do not hold a memory curve mid-blade like the LP stamped blades generally do. The Vniti blades are somewhat flexible but stiff enough they don't vibrate on percussive actions like the stamped blades can. Quality has been very consistent. Most of our fencers prefer the feel of the Vniti to the LP stamped for actions controlling the opponent's blade as it feels sturdier and has a better shape on the blade edges at the shoulder. Our \\"pick\\" style fencers, as well as our shorter epeeists, like it because it remains straight giving just a tad more reach and accuracy over the LP stamped once the LP acquires it's inevitable mid-blade curve. We cannot recommend most of the other forged blades we have tried as they have not had as long a life and/or they take dangerous sets near the foible.  Keep in mind that the Vniti is a bit heavier than the LP stamped as it is a forged blade. Setting the blade correctly at the shoulder (the tip angled slightly in and down) alleviates most of the issue. The blades can be a bit tough to set at the shoulder, and you can snap the blade at the tang if you force it, so we recommend a setting tool via one of the suppliers such as Absolute. The Vniti is much easier to wire than the LP as it does not have the 2 piece tang that is part of the LP manufacture process. We recommend wiping the blade with acetone (and letting it dry for a couple of minutes) before wiring as some of the black coating will release from the blade. The acetone also helps the wire adhere better to the blade as it will remove any oil from manufacturing and/or your hands.   NOTE: LP is now manufacturing a hybrid blade that is supposed to carry the best qualities of the stamped and forged blades combined into one product. However, that blade costs about twice what the Vniti does. We would still recommend the Vniti until more info is available on the new LP blade and/or the price drops.

product_title: Confidence Fitness 2-in-1 Elliptical Trainer with Seat
review_headline: Poor packaging, very noisy machine, uncomfortable seat
review_body: I'm disappointed with my purchase and would recommend spending a little more money to buy a better quality machine. I was excited to find a 2-in-1 machine for such a low price, but once I received it I realized why the price was so good. First off, the machine parts were packaged in a way obviously meant to maximize space and minimize shipping costs, and everything was crammed so tightly together that whenever we pulled something out we risked breaking something else. One plastic end-cap for a bottom leg of the frame was completely shattered with broken bits of plastic spread throughout the box. I now have to deal with requesting a replacement piece as it is a necessary part for the machine to balance without rocking. I imagine that most of the time the pieces arrive unbroken, but packaging could have been better.   My second problem with the machine, but one that I was prepared for based on other reviews, and one that won't be too hard to remedy, is that the seat is VERY uncomfortable. I need to find some kind of seat cover and until then I'm stuck using it as an elliptical only, it's that painful to sit on.   One of the structural flaws of this particular 2-in-1 is that, every time you switch between elliptical and bike mode, you have to move the arm pieces into different slots, otherwise they'll be in your way when you're trying to bike. Then using it in bike mode you have to lean far forward to be able to hold onto the handles (arm pieces); you can't bike upright with good posture.   My biggest beef with this equipment is that it's incredibly noisy! I watch tv on my computer while exercising, and even with having great external speakers AND a sub-woofer, I can't hear my computer with the sound cranked all the way up, over the noise of the machine!   I would not buy this again, I would spend more for a better machine.

product_title: Sentry Solutions Marine TUF-CLOTH Stop Rust
review_body:
I carry my pistol in a hiked-up belly band holster a couple inches below my armpit, since carry at work is verboten. I have a physical job, so every day when I take it off, it is soaked with sweat. Since it does not have a finish that is very resistant to extreme conditions like some manufacturers use, I had to clean and re-oil it every day or two to keep the rust at a minimum, but even with this effort, it would always have some somewhere that I would have to remove with very fine steel wool.

As soon as I got the Tuf Cloth, I did my usual cleaning and rust removal, and rubbed every part of the gun I could get to with this cloth. Whatever the chemical is, it works! There was ZERO rust on the weapon, even on the bare metal of the barrel, after weeks of daily wear in a sweaty, fat man's armpit. If you carry concealed anywhere that that your sweat may reach, and you like your gun, buy one of these. If any of your metal items are subjected to harsh conditions, buy one! There is plenty on the cloth to last for multiple applications on any number of items - guns, knives, whatever. Not that you'll need to reapply very often, though. Just to see how long a treatment would last, I wore the gun daily, and inspected it for rust, but did not clean it or repeat the treatment. After about a month, I noticed a little rust finally starting to form around the magazine release button. This area only got a cursory application since it is embedded in the plastic frame, so I suspect that proper application would stretch the time much longer.

review_body: Look guys, I know there are some of you out there that consider drinking a shake once a week and walking around the block for 5 minutes a week working out. The instructions that come with it clearly say \\"make sure the lid makes 2 clicks when you close it.\\" Also screw the lid on tight, then it probably won't leak.  For those that say the mixture is lumpy, you need to actually shake the thing.  If you're doing a real workout, you shouldn't have a problem shaking your container to get the lumps out.  Also keep in mind that every shake out there is different.  I've had some brands that stay lumpy even in a blender.  So try shaking it first, or try using a different brand of shake.  But, since I can actually shake a bottle, this one actually blends better than the \\"Shaker\\" brand ones with the whisk ball in the middle.  Ohh yeah, I also got two full scoops in my lid, 50g of protein in it.  You might have to pack it in, but it fit for me.  I go to school on the biggest campus in the nation and walk an average of 2 miles a day in between classes.  This bottle goes in my backpack and the powder stays separate from the liquid after bouncing around on my back, which allows me to have a fresh-mixed shake in the middle of the day.  So for those of you out there that actually take your workouts seriously, who have the arm strength to actually shake a bottle, and don't mind spending less than 30 seconds reading directions, buy this shaker.  I'm sure mom's out there know how to shake bottles after mixing formulas.  Don't be that guy that complains about lumps in his shake when there are women out there getting the lumps out of their shake.  This bottle is legit, and doesn't take much intelligence to operate.  Read the directions, and actually shake the bottle and you will have no problems with it.

once i get them all purchased, my plan is for my heavier dumbbells (40...35..30..& 25s) to occupy the notched area & the smaller ones (20..15..10..8..& 5s) to occupy the top & bottom cross bars along with my Perfect Push-up handles

product_title: Guide Gear Extreme Deluxe Hunting Climber Tree Stand
review_headline: You get what you pay for and you pay for very little. NOT a good buy
review_body: I started hunting on my father-in-law's land.  I found a great trail but no where to sit.  I wanted a cheap tree stand that I could move.  The price is what got me, you can't beat it.  But you get what you pay for.  First off, the thing is heavy, 30 lbs+.  I consider myself to be in above average physical condition and it was a pain to carry this thing the quarter mile or longer to my tree.  I had tried to assemble it in my living room and the directions suck. It doesn't tell you how to do anything.  I got on their website and found instructions for the same thing but with different parts, what the heck.  I finally got it together and put it around a tree in my yard.  It took me over 30 minutes and was really loud.  Once I got it up I didn't feel comfortable or safe in it.  I figured I bought it so I might as well use it.  I sit down by 6am normally so I was out there at 5:30 and it took me almost an hour to set it up, I had most of it already done, all I had to do was lash it around the tree and put the pins in.  After this I tried to get in it and it fell on my head.  I got on it and was about 6 feet in the air when both pieces fell.  I am glad I had my harness on.  After this I said screw it and let it sit until I was done for the day.  That afternoon I packed it up and sent it back.  Many pieces were plastic and broke when I put it together the first time.  I am an engineer and focus on quality control at my job and can tell you that this product is lacking the quality part.  Welds were small and weak, the sewing of the seat and padding ripped the first time I put them on, buckles are hard to work with especially when you have cold hands.  Spend the money and buy a name brand one.  The one good thing is that Amazon took care of me.  Shipping was great and so was customer service.

product_title: Hogue Rubber Grip Handall Jr. Small Size Grip Sleeve
review_body: The \\"Hogue Rubber Grip Handall Jr. Small Size Grip Sleeve\\" is a welcome addition to my Kel Tec P-11. Installation was as difficult as referred to in the instructions, but to follow them is get it on quicker and it will fit well. If you will heat enough water to submerge the grip - not to boiling, just very hot - that will loosen the rubber enough to start the installation process. There is an \\"up\\" arrow on the inside section of this grip to show \\"up\\", for obvious reasons. I pulled the back side on to about .25 inch and held it with my other thumb while stretching the grip as far as possible to get it on the front of the pistol grip (it definitely requires good hand strength). Do not use oil, Dawn or anything except water since you won't be able to get it off. Water will evaporate soon enough. After the grip is on the front and rear of the pistol grip, begin to work it up on each side, pull up once on the right, then once on the left, etc. Ensure you keep it straight during installation. This little piece of rubber gives me a positive grip - I know I have the butt of the pistol in my hand and my fingers \\"stick\\" to it a little - as soft rubber does - and out she comes solidly and ready for action. I have a Hogue forearm on a Stag Arms rifle I bought a couple years ago; that is where I first had any contact with that brand's merchandise. It is nicely \\"tacky\\" which gives me a confident grip on the front of the rifle. That is why I bought this Hogue pistol grip for my concealed carry weapon. It also gives me a very confident grip that I am touching it correctly and my hand will fold around it as it should. Try it, I'm sure you will find it a welcome addition to your piece.

product_title: Leupold Zero Point Boresighter 59012
review_headline: Works great but you must understand and follow instructions
review_body: Contrary to the other comments, this boresighter not only works as a boresighter to get you \\"on the paper\\", you can then use it to zero your rifle. After performing the boresighting correctly per the instructions, with your windage and elevation adjusted to match up with the center of the Zero Point grid, you then remove the boresighter and take a single shot at your target. Assuming you had your rifle rested properly and got a \\"good\\" shot at the center of the target, and your shot is \\"on the paper\\", you can then put your rifle back onto the rest and put the Zero Point back onto the end of your barrel in the same position and center its grid over the center of the target. (You can see through the Zero Point grid to your target). You can then adjust wind and elevation on your scope one more time to match up its reticle with the point of impact of your shot on the target, and you have then zeroed in your rifle with only one shot. Leupold calls this the \\"One Shot Zero\\".  If you are not sure that your shot was a \\"good\\" shot, you can shoot three shots and verify that you have a close grouping. You should let your barrel cool a few minutes between each shot. You then replace the Zero Point on the end of the barrel, place its grid centered on the bullseye of the target, and then make windage and elevation adjustments to your scope so that its reticle matches the center of your grouping.

product_title: BARSKA Digital Microscope with 3.5 Screen
review_headline: Buy the Celestron instead - this one compares very poorly.
review_body:
I ordered both this microscope and the competing Celestron [[ASIN:B0014YNGCK Celestron 44340 LCD Digital LDM Biological Microscope]] So that I could compare the two and be assured I was buying the best one. This Barska is already packaged up and ready for return to Amazon (Big thanks for Amazon's easy return policy which allows a person to compare products and keep the best one!) I would have just bought the Celestron because it had many good reviews whereas this one only had one review. However, the Celestron also had a few negative reviews complaining that there was a \\"dark spot\\" in the middle of the screen (These reviews about a dark spot were all a few years old...luckily I discovered this is no longer an issue as it would have been a shame to get stuck with the far inferior Barska)

Playing around with both it became immediately apparent that the Celestron is far superior to the Barska; yet at the time of this review the Barska was about $25 more expensive. Here is what I noted as different between the two:

*The case: Celestron comes with a nice, vertical, padded, fabric case. The Barska was in what seemed to me a cheapie, molded plastic case reminiscent of what you'd get with a cheap drill bought from the big box home improvement store. It is easier to use the vertical case, as you just slide the scope down in, put in the cord/wall plug close and zip it and you're ready to go. Additonally, this vertical case has a handle on top as well as a shoulder strap for easy carry. The Barska case was not so intuitive for putting the scope back in it took 3 tries to get it in correctly so that the lid would shut.

*The viewing experience:
---I hate to call it resolution, because they claim to be the same. However, the various items I viewed on each were always significantly more clear and easy to focus on the Celestron, using the 40x,10x, and 400x lenses. The digital zoom works nicely on the Celestron. I couldn't really tell if it was working with the Barska.

---Also, the menu on the screen for the Barska is not as intuitive - you go to \\"camera\\" to activate the viewing screen (huh?? - I'd of thought that was for taking pictures...) The Celestron defaults to the viewing screen, so you just have to turn it on.

*The slide holder and positioning: Forgive me for not using the appropriate names/terms to describe each part of the microscope - I'm not a lab tech. Anyways, The Celestron is FAR SUPERIOR in this area, as you can secure your slide in the clips, then there are two dials on the left side that allow you to move the entire slide platform left and right, front to back. This allows for much slower, more fine manipulation of the slide when viewing. With the Barska the platform is stationary, so you'd have to use your fingers and push the slide around to where you want it. If you are using the clips to hold it down you'd then need to use more pressure to get it to move than will allow for fine, minute, gentle moving of the slide. For me, this was huge. If I'm looking at a wet mount I need to be able to move it around to see what \\"critters\\" are in the sample so I know how the pt. may need to be treated (I'll be using this both personally and professionally...). If I have to use my finger to shove the slide around on the platform I won't have the delicate control & so it makes the job harder.

*Instruction manual: The Celestron manual is easy to follow and has multiple translations (English, German, Spanish, etc.) The Barska owners manual was seriously lacking and obviously not written by a native English speaker - someone not familiar with microscopes will be challenged figuring things out as the manual is no help. However, the Barska did have a CD in the case. It was completely unlabeled, so I have no idea if it was instructions, software to go with transferring images from the microscope or what, so perhaps it would have had some helpful information.

*Special & other features: I didn't test the picture taking features or using the optional SD card memory on either, so I can't comment there. However, the navigation on the Celestron was more intuitive. The Celestron comes with an adaptable plug that can pop in plugs for most nationalities (there's about 5 different ones in the case) The Barska had just a solid plug for standard Americas plugs. Both come with a small case of about 5 prepared slides to play around with. Both have the option of lighting from top, bottom or both. The Barska top light was on a bendable wire so that you could better focus it on the object being viewed, whereas the top light on the Celestron is not adjustable. However, the bendable feature didn't help the Barska at all, as no matter how I moved it the images on the Celsestron were brighter and more clear (as you'll see on the images I hope to upload...) I tried adding supplemental lighting to \\"brighten up\\" the image on the Barska, but it didn't help, so perhaps the darkness is related to something with the viewing screen instead(?) Hmmm - that one I just can't figure out.

Other than the details mentioned above, the two microscopes are quite similar. The Barska \\"looks\\" nicer because of the chrome detailing, however, that obviously doesn't make up for it's poor performance when compared to the Celestron.

Summary: Buy the Celestron not this Barska! It doesn't have any black spots on the screen - ignore those older reviews. It is very easy to use, comes with a handy carry/storage case, and offers features it's primary competitor doesn't have. product_title: Horizon Fitness T101-3 Treadmill
review_body: This is, without question, the worst product I have ever purchased.  Assembly was a nightmare.  The holes in the frame were not properly cut at the factory & the bolts would not thread.  Luckily, my husband has more tools than Home Depot & great skills, so he was able to (1) measure the threads on the bolts and (2) use his tap set to re-cut the holes.  If you don't know what a tap & die set is or don't know how to measure bolt threads, don't buy this treadmill.  When attaching the control console, only 3 of the 4 holes lined up properly - more poor workmanship.  Once assembled, the treadmill ran for approximately 10 seconds before shutting down.  After having to leave work early twice to place  phones call to tech support  (they are only open til 5pm), the problem was narrowed down to a non-functioning circuit board.  Days later, the new one arrived.  It was put in.  It still did not work.  An email was sent to the company outlining my problems; I still have not heard from them.  I attempted to call customer service; I only ever got a recording telling me that they were busy and could not take my call today (btw, don't believe the customer service hours that are posted on their website).  I finally gave up, and decided to send it back.  When disassembling it, I discovered that the next problem was that, at the factory, a large bag full of desiccant was jammed between the belt and the roller, preventing it from moving.  So as long as you don't mind re-cutting bolt holes, installing circuit boards, and cleaning up after sloppy assemblers, this is the product for you.  However, if you want a treadmill that you can actually walk/run on, you may want another product.  Throughout this whole miserable process, Amazon's customer service has been outstanding.

product_title: PowerBlock Elite Dumbbells
review_body:
I love these dumbells!

Previously, I had gotten the Weider Core Adjustable Dumbell set, which stuck quite a bit and required a lot of maneuvering to use. I returned them and promptly bought a set of Powerblocks. I got a fantastic deal, in which I got the two kits required to go from 5-90 lbs and the heavy duty stand for 619.00.

They came packaged in four boxes, two for each dumbbell, the first and second kit. Some weight kits (ahem weider core) come in one single box which will require your poor petite female delivery person to work hard for her money. Barely any assembly was required and they were ready to use.

Adjusting the dumbbells is easy. Ridiculously easy. You figure out what color corresponds to the weight you would like to select and you place the pin along that bar. It's difficult to place the pin unevenly, so you wont make that mistake unless you're trying.

The grips are ridiculously comfortable. There's no need for gloves at all, they feel so good. I still like wearing wrist wraps because my wrists are pitifully weak. You don't have to make huge adjustments for the size of them like you do with the selecttech (I don't own a set, but I have used them) because the dumbbell size is only as large as the weight you are lifting due to the set up being almost like nesting boxes. So a 5 lb dumbbell is about the size of a 5 lb dumbbell, just box shaped, unlike the selecttech where a 5 lb dumbbell is the same size (or at least length) as a 90 lb dumbbell.

I'm not using them at the higher weights (as I am a lady builder, and just recovering from a back injury) but I do know they would be a bit bulky at 90 lbs- it would require a bit of adjusting to get used to for certain movements.

If you want to use increment weights you have to take the handle out of the surrounding plates. Personally, it doesn't seem worth it to me, since I wont get that small of an adjustment in the gym unless I'm in the very low weights.

All in all, I love them for their value and how little space they take up in my small, pet filled home. I love that they're right there which means I don't have to go to the gym for a decent weight lifting session. They also would work spectacularly well for p90x or any other DVD routine that includes dumbbell based weight lifting.alue and how little space they take up in my small, pet filled home. I love that they're right there which means I don't have to go to the gym for a decent weight lifting session. product_title: Timex Full-Size Ironman Run Trainer GPS Watch
review_headline: Serious design flow for serious runners
review_body: It is with the great sadness I rate this watch with two stars. I really like the watch but...  If you don't care for your cadence then this is a really good watch and in that case I would definitely rate Timex Ironman Run Trainer at 5 stars. For the money it gives so much features that there is no question that it is superior to similarly priced Garmin watches. And if after a while it does not exhibit any issues with battery like my Garmin 405cx did then this will be even greater watch. I found myself constantly comparing Timex Ironman Run Trainer to the Garmin 405cx which is more expensive watch (I bought it for ~ $320 year and half ago) and most of the time the Trainer is on par with Garmin.  But I do care for cadence. And thus I have to use foot pod. Now look carefully. When you attach your foot pod the Timex Ironman Run Trainer AUTOMATICALLY OVERRIDES GPS distance and pace data with that coming from foot pod. I repeat - AUTOMATICALLY OVERRIDES. Which means that you don't really have a GPS watch anymore and the only way you can use GPS data from that point on is by looking at nice trace of your run on Google maps or whatever. But your distance and speed recordings are now no more accurate than would be those measured by any non-GPS watch with a foot pod. My small brain cannot grasp what the big idea is behind this design. Why on the earth someone would decide to override data from accurate equipment with inaccurate data from much less precise device is beyond my understanding. Don't Timex engineers understand that we buy GPS watch not just for looking at a map, but for getting accurate distance and speed measurements?  Now look, I understand that there are times when you would prefer to have foot pod data over that one from GPS. This is when there's no good GPS signal. For example in a gym. Or in the dense forest may be. But you don't have to be an engineer to figure out that the best way to design this would be to either let user to chose which data s/he wants to use or to automatically fall back on foot pod measurements when GPS signal does not produce accurate data. Better yet to use both. That what Garmin does and this really makes sense!  This was really huge disappointment for me since cadence is important for me. It is like tachometer in your car. If you don't drive stick then you don't care. But if you do then you cannot live without the tach.  I have a hope that Timex fixes this in a future firmware upgrade. After all if the equipment can use two channels of data and chose which one to record and to show then this choice most likely is controlled by software, not hardware. Garmin had similar problem some time ago and they fixed it with firmware upgrade. I would be very interested to see what Timex engineers are going to do about this huge design flaw.  If Timex fixes it in near future I would be more than happy to get back and give this watch a five stars rating. But until then I have to put 2 stars only.

product_title: Glock OEM Tac Light/Laser W/Dimmer
review_body: The Glock Tactical Light/Laser with Dimmer (GTL22) is a really nice product for your Glock. I have a Gen 4 Glock 19 and the light mounts really easy onto gun's rail and snaps positively and securely into place with little effort. Once in place the light/laser combination is very easy to use and the on/off/dimmer switch on the light can be accessed with no effort via the trigger finger whether you are shooting right or left handed. The mode switch (off/light/light+laser/laser) is on the bottom of the light and is also easy to reach but takes a bit more practice to use without having to flip the gun over to figure out which mode you are switching too.  Zeroing the laser in is quick and easy and once completed the laser holds zero flawlessly as far as I can tell. I zeroed the laser by just looking over the gun's iron sights and was was shooting tight groups at 25' in less than 15 rounds. Afterwards I was able to fire and reacquire quicker and more accurately with the laser than using the gun's build in sites.  A couple of small things I think that could be improved:  1. Using the dimming function is not all that easy without practice. Not a big deal to me but if the dimmer function is something that you want you should be aware of that.  2. The bulb is Xenon not LED. Glock does include a spare bulb with the light though which is a nice touch.  3. Size - the light isn't heavy but it would be nice if it could shrunk down a little more.  One issue with any laser/light combo is how to carry the weapon with the light attached. I don't currently have a holster I like that accommodates the light so it hasn't made it to an every day carry item unfortunately.
