review_body: I purchased this as a low-cost Christmas present for a co-worker who is a die-hard Seahawks fan.  It went great with his collection.

product_title: UTG Model 4 Flip-up Front Sight for Reg Height Gas Block
review_headline: Works well with gas block only!!
review_body: I purchased and mounted the UTG Flip up sight for my DPMS Oracle AR 15, it mounts to my existing front block very well!!  No wobble no play and just was finger tight.  Finish could be better, mine has some bare spots on the corners of the sight but what do you expect while only paying around $20.  I suggest this for a good back up system.  Good job UTG.

product_title: BARSKA Biometric Safe
review_body: Purchased this item because of the reviews.  Received item. Could not get the initialization (fingerprint step 1) to work.  Called tech support who went thru a series of checks.  Turns out it could not save fingerprints. Which means that any fingerprint would work.  Tech support said to return unit.    Plus, keys and other items were not packaged and therefore you could here the items rattling around in the safe?? Wonder if this was a previously returned item because the instructions show all accessories neatly packaged together.  I gave it two stars instead of one because support was quick to identify problem.

product_title: Nautilus R514 Recumbent Exercise Bike
review_body: As far as I'm concerned this is as good as any bike you would use at a health club.  It really is smooth and I can tell that it should last.  For the price it beat my expectations.  As far as assembly reviews, I would hope you are not trying to set this up out of the box so you can work out right away.  Set it up on an off day so it's ready to use at a later date.

product_title: Maxpedition Fatboy Versipack
review_body: This pack is extremely well made and sturdy.  Multiple pockets, the strap is long enough to adjust it to fit comfortably, it can just be slung over your shoulder or fastened more securely by also using the waist strap.  On the top flap is an area about 2x6 inches with the fuzzy side of velcro allowing for attaching other items.  Roomy enough to replace most day packs and excellent for travel.

product_title: 42 Head Laser Pointer Beam Keychain with Batteries
review_body: So I got my laser pointer today and it looked as if someone opened it:( Then I started to use it and the button got stuck inside so I tried to fix it only to find that the back threads that hold the cap on are weak and don't keep the batteries in. The laser is broken and the heads thing... yea I got three different types, what a joke. Would not recommend it to anyone, Don't waste your time or money.

product_title: GSI Super Quality All-In-One Waterproof Heart Rate Monitor Watch and Transmitter Slim Chest Belt - For Exercise, Sports, Running, Jogging Outdoor Activities - Measures Speed, Pulse, Distance, Fat And Calories - Alarm And Stopwatch Functions
review_body: I purchased this item as a Christmas gift...when it was open the metal piece that is on the front of the watch fell off...most luckily it can be glued back...however, It should of never fell off if it was constructed better...cheaply made watch.

product_title: A-ZOOM 38 Special Snap Cap 16118
review_body: Not much to say here: they're aluminum snap caps, they feed and cycle like live ammo, they're nearly indestructible. I like these over plastic snap caps very much. I couldn't tell you how many thousands of dry fires my snap caps have seen but they still work flawlessly.  The only negative comments I have are:  A) The red finish wears over time. Not a big deal, really. Just something to note.  2) Your weapon's steel extractor will (naturally) wear the aluminum case rim over time. Again, not a big deal, just dress the burrs with some 600 wet/dry sandpaper and carry on.  Buy lots to keep up your trigger press and weapon manipulation skills. They also work very well for mixing randomly in a magazine of live ammo to simulate a dead primer for tap/rack/bang drills. Highly useful!

product_title: Buck ErgoHunter Select Guthook Knife (Black/Silver, Large)
review_body: My wife got this knife for me as a birthday present and it came out of the box as sharp as a razor and it feels great in my hand.  The ridges on the spine of the blade and the rough edges on the side of the blade  really let you have a better grip and control over the knife when it really counts.  IT is heavy enough that you definitely know that it's in your hand. The grip is also a great feature of the knife and I haven't used it when it's wet out but from what I can tell it would be great.  The sheath is tough and will last a life time.  I would buy another one in a heart beat.

product_title: Cast Iron Kettlebells - Sold As Singles
review_body: The kettlebell was delivered right on time.  It was well packaged and it didn't roll around which was great since it's heavy.  20 lbs is no joke so be careful when you receive the package.  I tried lifting it up thinking it was just a box and then when I couldn't move it I realized that it was my kettlebell. Ha!

product_title: Galati Gear Single Magazine Pouch (Black)
review_body: Cheap made in china product that will do its job but will not likely last long under tough abuse due to relatively thin materials, and will carry most normal magazines excluding high capacity and the larger .45 ACP mags, which barely fit.

product_title: Monkey Light Bike Light
review_headline: Normally fun and safety don't go together ...
review_body: but the Monkeylectric lights are a total blast and give me the visiblity I need (keeping me safe) and want (it's a 2-wheel party and everyone shouts out \\"I love your lights!\\")  I have 2 sets now.  The first is almost 2 years old.  I've had to recharge the batteries only twice in all that time.  Mud, rain and 100 miles a week have not affected them.  This blows me away.  I lost a filling last year going into a pothole, but the lights still worked when I tried them the next night.  I just can't wait till they can make affordable the do-you-own design ones.  Highly recommended!  Favorite bike product of all time.

product_title: Gerber Steadfast Fine Knife 22-41120
review_body: Love the size and sharpness of this knife. The rubber grip gives it an awesome grip. The back of the handle can also be used for some hammering. I wish that Gerber should've given it some serration. Also I want to point out that the nylon sheath casing does not have any pocket or space to keep your fire starter etc. With that said it still is a very sharp knife right from the get go. My friend bought the Buck knife from Dicks Sporting Goods. Looks similar to this knife with the 6inc blade. It comes with a very neat looking leather sheath casing and is made in the good old U.S.A.

product_title: Fitness Quest Integrity 3000 Air Rower
review_body: Overall its been a sturdy machine had it for over 3 years,  have kids and the chain keeps coming off do to them messing with it, pain to get back on but not really a machine fault.  Its held up well biggest negative is its just not enough of a workout, cant really adjust it to a harder level, does a decent job very smooth, great range of motion very low impact, just dont expect to work up a major sweat, more like a brisk walk level, good for starter rower and it has held up well, just wish it had a few more difficulty levels, I'm am in no way a in shape person so not like I'm really pushing the machine, but if you love rowing and just enjoy the motion for the price  it is what it is and does do a light weight workout.  But again for someone overweight just starting out, not a bad option very low impact on all joints and easy enough to start out with

product_title: Reebok New Orleans Saints Drew Brees Replica Jersey
review_body: I bought my three sons a less expensive Saints shirt two years ago.  They were $30 less than the NFL authentic shirts out there.  While I think the authentic shirts are WAY overpriced at $65 (shame on you NFL), in the end they are worth it if you are a true NFL fan.  We just watched the Saints play and froze the screen on Drew Brees -- his shirt was exactly like theirs (except for the C for Captain patch).  Even the material looked the same but I can't be sure on that.  Now they wear them every game because they are proud of the shirt.  The old ones are long gone and never worn.  I learned my lesson on this one -- this is a psychological satisfaction product, not a pure economic one.  One more thing: do your homework on your hometown team's shirt.  The nearby outlet mall's Reebock store had an NFL-authenticated shirt on sale for $18.  But when I looked closely, it did not have the sleeve markings or the neck detail that the real shirt has -- again, important to the rabid fan.

product_title: Wilson Pro Overgrip (12 Pack)
review_body: I've been playing tennis for 20 years, and have tried many different products. These overgrips are the best. I've tried gamma and tournagrip, and these wilson grips are better than both. I would definitely recommend these over tournagrip. I would recommend these to anyone.

product_title: TMS QD Quick Detach Cam Lock Bipod Adapter
review_headline: Takes a lickin' and keeps on tickin'
review_body: I've now purchased two of these little gems.  The first was put to work on a FAL which was aptly nicknamed \\"The Beast\\". This rifle sported a 20 inch, hammer forged barrel with no suppression whatsoever.  Since the bipod leaped a considerable distance off the bench with every shot, this rifle was a perfect test bed for determining accessory durability.  If anything was going to test this product's quality and durability, it was the Beast.  (As proof of this, after 200 rounds, the Sun Optics scope mount I misguidedly purchased for the Beast had quite literally been shaken to pieces, making it absolutely useless.)  This TMS adapter (supporting a Harris bipod) survived well over 600 rounds without suffering any detectable wear or degradation in performance.  If you're in the market for a quick detach Harris bipod adapter, buy this one. I guaranty you will be happy you did.  As the ultimate testimonial, even after considerable use and abuse, I liked this product enough to purchase a second, which is going on the newest family member, a pre-ban HK 91 (nicknamed \\"Boomhilda\\").

product_title: Bongo Board
review_body: I was looking for balance boards that would give me a challenge and this one is pretty good.  I've bought several in the past that did nothing for me.  At first I was wary because it was so hard to get started and stay balanced.  However, after 2 days, I was able to at least roll back and forth on it without feeling like I'm going to bust my head.  I don't plan on doing any tricks on it thought and will most likely just stay on the carpet.  I'm glad there is a band holding the rollers to keep it from flying away.

product_title: Pachmayr Tactical Grip Glove for Springfield XD, XD(M) (Full size)
review_body: After recieving this grip I promptly placed it on my new Glock 17 gen.4. It just didn't feel right and the gun felt better without the grip. So, this may be because I have small hands or because it was a glock so I just dont use the grip. I recommend using thin skate-board like type of tape if you want enhanced gripping power.

product_title: Magpul Enhanced  70' Rubber Buttpad, Black
review_body: Awesome pad! Almost 3/4 of an inch. Vented on the sides, which gives it a cool look. As with all Magpul products I've purchased, this one is of quality and meets its goals as designed.

product_title: Athame: Roman (black handle) (RA152B) -
review_body: I love this athame!  The shipping was really fast.  The knife is a perfect size and lighter than it looks--which is good for when you need to hold it up a long time!  The sheath, which is included, is attractive too; much better than I was expecting.

product_title: Reebok Denver Broncos 2011 Sideline Coach Slouch Adjustable Hat Adjustable
review_body: Reebok Denver Broncos 2011 Sideline Coach Slouch Adjustable Hat Adjustable fits very well and has lasted a very long time so far its great

product_title: Plano Pro-Max Single Scope Contoured Rifle Case
review_body:
I was really happy when I got this case, it seemed great at first. The foam inside is good quality, but not glued in place (not a huge deal to me) the pillars will help prevent crushing. The handle is easily pulled apart making it easy to simply break the lock off (who cares? if they're stealing your gun they'll just take the case too and deal with the lock later)

product_title: Hawkeye Monster Archery Target Stand
review_body: The stand appeared to be a good product. But the design is very poor, as to the welded parts on the riser. Very weak and will need added support. Without adding support the weld will break when tipping the target back to move. Mine began to break before I ever had a target on it. I will fix it, but I do not recommend this product.

product_title: Benjamin Titan GP Nitro Piston Air Rifle
review_headline: GREAT AIR RIFLE, ESPECIALLY FOR THE PRICE!!!!!
review_body: Rifle is quiet, hard hitting, nicely styled, and accurate with the right pellets. I have owned this rifle for about a month now. I have been hunting with it twice and got two squirrels, one with a shoulder shot that passed high strait through,and the 2nd with a head shot that put him down, and the other with a head and chest shot. With the smaller pellets you must be extremely accurate with your shots or you may not humanely take down the animal. My buddy shot a squirrel with a shotgun while hunting in NC and the thing fell out the tree and was still trying to get away! (mostly abdominal shots) I have nothing but great things to say about this rifle, and if you can still get one, go for it!

product_title: The North Face TKA 100 Microvelour Glacier 1/4 Zip For Women Medium Black
review_body: I bought this for my daughter in law because she was looking for a North Face item. It's a nice pull over, thin but deceptivley warm but is the brand worth the price, no.

product_title: Princeton Tec Corona Bike LED Bike Light
review_headline: great light and rugged too, best of both worlds.
review_body: I picked up two of these lights a litte over a year ago for my wife and me.  These lights are not the brightest but bright enough that you wont out run the light.  They are great for urban and offroad use.  I have had cars flash their brights at me indicating they have obviously seen me comming, which is the point.  This light.is way more than a be seen light and really is functional. I use this as my primary light on my handle bar and the battery pack is secured in the same spot centered on the bar just infront of the stem.  The light looks great and I leave the light attatched to the bike.  The light has survived abuse and the hot summer sun pounding it day in and day out.  The battery pack is easy to change out batteries and is in a water resistant tube. I have used the light in down pours and it worked just fine.  I will buy this light again if needed for a handle bar light.  It is a bit big to attatch to the helmet with the battery pack.  I have used the.light.on the helmet then tossed the.battery pack in my camel back to power the light.  I would suggest the EOS for the helmet since it is a self contained unit without an external battery pack.  The run time is almost forever even on Kirkland brand batteries.  The estimmates on the web site are very conservitive.  I usually have to swap out batteries every Three month or so.  Princeton tech is awesome stuff and I believe it is still made in America.  You cant go wrong with this light.

product_title: Sportcraft CLX6250 LCD Dartboard with Cabinet
review_body: I ordered this board for a family game room. I figured the doors would be plastic but that was unimportant. The board came with 2 sets of very cheaply made plastic darts, which work fine with the board. We are not professional players but because there are 6 people in our family, less arguments if we have our own darts. Problem is that if you use a decent sets of darts the plastic in the board moves and errors out the board. I have never had a board that can't handle regular soft tip darts. Could not return because packaging was thrown out with Christmas trash. Went to a local store, paid half the price for a board that is 10 times better than this one.  Save your money because the board is way overpriced for the quality you are getting.

product_title: Pro Down Bulldog Youth Shoulder Pad
review_body: My son loved these and they are well worth the money.  Perfect for backyard football for a more realistic feel.

product_title: Competition Electronics ProChrono Digital Chronograph
review_body: Even with not-too-favorable reviews on Amazon and after a lot of research on the web, I decided to go with the ProChrono Digital chronograph and man am I happy with that equipment!  It worked immediately indoors with .177 air gun pellets then very well outdoors with .45ACP, .22LR and .308 Winchester. I had to work a little while indoorswith the ligthing (gave plenty of it with incandescent light) and noticed I had to set my sights roughly 2 inches above the chronograph to have good readings but outdoors, there was no tweaking at all required.  I am probably going to make a rough shield in front of the display (or buy the one they offer) to minimize powder residue when I use a rifle with a piece of lexan/plexiglass.  If I had one critic, it would be that when reviewing a string, one can only jump down the shot list numbers and not \\"go up\\" when pleased.  Interesting fact: a friend was at the range with his nearly $200 PACT chronograph and couldn't get it to work reliably. He came over to ask to use mine!

meaning, it doesn't really close up very well.

product_title: SKLZ Lightning Bolt Pitching Machine Pro
review_body: Had a few kids from our baseball team over to test this out (5th grade) and after a few minutes of being bored with the speed in which the balls were shot they ended up using it to shoot each other.  Now that lasted a good two hours.  Pros:  - No worries about your windows breaking or the paint chipping off your house.  These golf-ball-sized \\"baseballs\\" are made of a soft nerf-like foam.  This was a huge pro as using regular baseballs in the backyard just freaks me out.  As such they can't be hit as far either which makes gathering them up a breeze and you don't need a huge space to practice in.  - Really does help with accuracy.  These little guys are tougher to hit which, if you are looking at improving hand-eye coordination and accuracy of shots, the small balls will help get a more accurate swing.  It took quite awhile for the best batter of the bunch to zero in on the ball but once he did, he was able to get a good rhythm going.  - Fairly accurate.  We didn't have any wild unruly pitches.  It was pretty consistent in the speed, rhythm, and location of the pitches (until the last two balls... see \\"Cons\\")  - No fear of hurting the batter.  My kids, while not recommended, were using it to shoot each other.  No one was hurt and everyone was laughing.  I am not encouraging turning it into a cannon but if your little one does get hit in the leg while batting, it shouldn't turn into a trip to the emergency room.  - Not a bad price point for a cheap way to practice hitting in a small backyard.  Cons:  - Ridiculously short cord for the AC adapter.  I've had stock camera cords that are longer.  This is meant to be used outside and most homes don't have jacks every few feet like they do indoors.  Huge oversight.  - No instruction manual.  I figured out how to set it up but thought it was weird that there were no included instructions, warranty info, contact pamphlet.. nada.  - While the size of the ball is a challenge, the speed leaves something to be desired.  It would be nice if there was a variable pitching speed (even just a slow and fast option) or if it was just a wee bit faster.  At first I thought the speed would be good for younger players (no fear of getting hurt at that speed and it is close to the speed young children are pitched to) but the more I thought about it I realized that most younger players are not ready for the accuracy that it takes to hit a smaller ball... this is why they use larger balls with younger players.  - Needs to be placed on a few bricks/stool/bucket/etc. in order to work.  Even at the highest pitching height it still shot grounders.  We were using the included AC plug so it wasn't low output from batteries which caused the low pitches.  Once it was placed on a 6-ish inch bucket it shot to a good height for the boys.  - While the balls were shot out at nicely-spaced regular intervals, the last two balls always got \\"stuck\\" in the machine for awhile but did eventually come out (usually as we gave up and walked over to unstick the balls they would start firing).  - The tubes are just big enough to accommodate the balls that come with the machine which means they won't fit regular-sized baseballs so you will need to special order replacements.  Amazon sells them at this time which makes it easy.  Nothing worse than hunting down specialty items that are only sold by the manufacturer with exorbitant shipping.

product_title: Weems & Plath Nautilus Collection 1.5 High Sensitivity Barometer
review_headline: Heavy Duty, looks geat...Only one small complaint
review_body: I chose this barometer because of the dial face, it's easy to read and attractive. The case looks and feels tough. I shopped the web, looked at a lot of barometers, and this one just looks like the real thing! I was sold on it the first time I laid eyes on it. Weems and Plath make high quality instruments. I would give it 5 stars, but for one small thing. There are 3 slide pointers that rotate around the dial face, just on the outside of the glass. Two are red, one is white. I suppose the white pointer in the middle marks the daily reading, and the red pointer to the right is for recorded extreme high pressure, the one on the left for an extreme low. The pointer on the left slides so easy that when you move it to a position on the dial face (say the 9 or 10 o'clock position), it just slides back down to the bottom of the dial. Really worthless as it is. I'm just a little disappointed that this barometer that has so much going for it, only to have a cheap pointer added. What were they thinking? I'm going to email Weems & Plath and ask them about this. This isn't enough to make me send it back, I love the barometer...I just thought it's worth noting.

product_title: Marmot Driclime Windshirt - In Your Choice of Styles
review_body: This is one of my favorite pieces of outdoor clothing due to it's impressive versatility. In temps from 60 degrees to 30 degrees, it works great as a lightweight outer layer over a T-shirt or base layer. In colder temps, it can be used as a mid layer. It's impressively warm for it's featherlight weight, it packs down to the size of a grapefruit, and it does a great job of blocking wind & repelling light rain. If it's cool & windy outside, this is my go-to outer layer. It also breathes extremely well - makes it perfect for high-output activities in cool to cold conditions. Mesh vents under the arm pits allow you to jettison excess heat when you're working hard. It has only 1 pocket up on the chest, but pockets lower on the jacket would interfere with a backpack waist belt. IMO, this is a perfect piece of gear for hiking & backpacking - you'll never regret throwing it in your pack. The only thing I would change is the fairly boxy cut - I would like to see it slimmed down a bit for lanky, athletic builds like mine.

I don't know what people's expectations are when purchasing an ET, its an investment, but if you are time starved like myself and want to keep in shape and feel challenged this is the machine.  I like the fan, the fact that I can use my mp3.  The fan can be stronger and the speakers on the mp3 could be better, but the point is to get a good workout in!

product_title: LifeStraw Personal Water Filter
review_body: As an avid outdoorsman, and experienced traveller who has backpacked around many countries with questionable water quality, I am so excited to have the LifeStraw in my kit.   Before I bought the LifeStraw, I used Iodine to purify my water, but I never liked the taste, or the fact that I was using chemicals in my water. I also prefer ultralight hiking/travelling, and am on a budget, so I have never dropped $100 on a high quality pump filter.   When I heard about the LifeStraw, I was really surprised by how much it filters out for the cost! Only $20 and you get a 0.2 micron filter that removes everything but viruses and heavy metals.. usually filters that take out crypto and giardia are quite pricey.. and the LifeStraw uses no chemicals at all! The other thing that attracted me to it was the durability and weight. There are no moving parts, batteries or anythign that can break, and at 2 ounces it's like it's not even there. I carry it in my pocket when travelling and drink out of my water bottle with it. Even when I'm surfing in Mexico, I drink tap water through the LifeStraw instead of buying bottles of water (which you have no guarantee as to their quality). It's already paid itself off in that respect!  When I'm backpacking with my friends I often drink straight out of streams or little ponds just to get a laugh out of them, as the LifeStraw effectively removes turbidity and all the usual suspects from lake water. Nothing like drinking right from the source!   For the price, the weight, and the effectiveness, I can't recommend anything else!

product_title: MIR - 30LBS WOMEN ADJUSTABLE WEIGHTED VEST
review_headline: As good as it gets!...and instructions for those of you who want them.
review_body:
For my women in the service, this is for us!

I bought this despite the price because there really is no other option for women. I cannot wear men's vests because of my body type. I am about 5'6\\" but mostly torso and maybe 140 lbs athletic with a soft layer on top. I am generally fairly petite, maybe a 28\\" waist because I've put on weight, but I wear a 28F bra size so there is simply no way the one size fits all thing would work for me. For reference, I can tighten up a female level IIIa body armor about as tight as it gets. The only sports bras that are tight enough on my are the under armour ones in small. There is a reason why I have this as tight as it gets. So if you're my size, you can still wear this. On the other hand, you can back out all the straps a few inches in the shoulders and a ridiculous amount in the waist, so you can be a big strong awesome viking woman and still have this fit you like a glove. That is, if 30 lbs is enough for you.

This vest does a pretty good job of putting the weight between your breasts so it's not really pulling down on you, if you know what I mean. Nobody likes that feeling that their training equipment is going to put their breasts in their lap within the month. Sad face :( Make sure that it is nice and snug if you want to run with it. I fave mine adjusted so that when tight the belted area fits snuggly under the front of my ribcage so as not to bounce up on me when I run. I started with 18 lbs and will be slowly working my way up. Be kind to your knees, don't start with way more weight then you're used to. Give your body a chance to adjust.

I saw someone had a hard time figuring out how to put it on, so I will explain it...

The vest comes fully loaded with a belt strap on the side in a box with no instructions. There are five pockets on the front and five pockets on the back, each with a three pound weight that looks like a metal bar of soap. (Homey don't play that, hahaha...but I digress.) If you would like to take weights out, take the same amount from the front and back. If you take one from each side, take the middle ones. If you take two, take corresponding left and right ones so that the vest stays evenly weighted. The vest slips over your head with the side that has an X shape for your breast on the front. You can adjust the shoulder strap length by undoing the strap and pulling apart the front and back that are held together with velcro. I overlapped mine as far as they can go without interfering with the securing strap because I am small. Reattach the securing strap and your strap is now adjusted. Repeat on the other side. The belt is made of mostly velcro. There are two elastic sides that will allow you to breathe slightly. There is a velcro attachment with a double D ring (like a belt) that goes on the front. To make the belt smaller, undo the velcro on the back side and make it smaller. It is okay for the velcro to overlap. The belt will still work fine. Adjust it so that, when worn, the front side with the D ring is as tight as it gets for maximum security. Lastly, attach the back side of the velcro to the back side of the vest before you put it on. There is a big strip of velcro (hook side) that goes across the bottom row of pockets on the back. Put on the vest. Pull the belt around nice and tight attaching one side of the velcro to the front and then the other. Use the securing strap with the D rings to sinch it up and then use the velcro end to hold the strap down.

AFTER USING IT expect your neck and shoulder area (trapezius and levator scapulae) to be sore from having weight that you're not used to carrying there. This is great for training for a long backpacking trip or for wearing body armor for anyone in the service. For my martial artists, doing forms and stances in this vest will make your legs ready for anything. Just be aware that it will throw your trained balance off a bit. It's worth it.

Bottom line is that if you like training and you want some good resistance, but you are a small woman and/or find men's vests uncomfortable on your breasts, just buy it. It will be worth the money.resistance, but you are a small woman and/or find men's vests uncomfortable on your breasts, just buy it. It will be worth the money.

review_body: Prior to purchasing this bat I was using the Miken Ultra II in both red and black.  I broke three of them in a year and a half.  I take pride in taking care of my equipment (Not throwing bats against the fence or slaming it down on the ground).  I play twice a week with friends averaging about 20 - 30 hits on medium compression balls.  I purchased this bat in May 2011. I loved it from my first hit.  34/28 ounce end-loaded. review_body: Quick delivery, good price, well made.  Fits gun great, little jiggling needed, but that's normal. Used on my Taurus 9 shot target pistol, would recommend. Thanks.

product_title: Planet Bike Red Zeppelin C02 Inflator
review_body: Purchased this because of its size and ease of storage in my seat pack. On a recent trip I found out just how useful the Red Zepplin would be. The wife had a low tire and I tried to get it up to pressure with the samll hand pump but that is impossible and you know if you have tried it. So I took the inflator attached the co2 bottle and the tire was inflated in seconds. The control valve works great and allows for complete shut-off of the co2. When we got home from our ride I saw that the tire was still loosing air to I deflated the tire removed it and patched the slow leak in the inner tube. Using the Red Zepplin I was able to put in just enough to replace the tube in the tire before total inflation. If you are going to carry an inflator make sure you have several bottles with you as it will take 2 of the 16 gram co2 bottles to get your tire to the proper inflation or 1 of the 33 gram. This little jewel is a time and life saver while out on the road. I would recommend this to any one who rides the roads, unless you like to take a chance on walking back one day.

product_title: Crosman Pulse R76  Tactical AirSoft rifle. Full or semi-auto electric AEG rifle.
review_headline: good, reliable and gets the job done
review_body: So, first of all i want to state that this is a gun actually worth buying. At this point, I have put more than 20,000+ bbs into this gun and it hasnt jammed or stopped on me once. but aside all that, here are the bad parts. the gun does not shoot the advertised 375 fps ( using .2 bbs). I recently went to an airsoft scenario game where it was chronoed in at 260 fps using crossman .2 bbs. Though the fps is low, it does have its advantages. there is no required engagement distances in major games due to its low fps. Also, the hop-up in this gun makes up for its low fps. My friend has a classic army sportsline m4 and this gun was able to outperform it in both accuracy and range. Also the magazine is a bit wobbly but u can buy a ak mag from ASGI with will hold 600 round and will solve the wobbling problem. so, in conclusion its a good gun for a beginner to and intermediate airsoft player. Much like a real AK, if u need a cheap, reliable and good gun. THIS IS IT

product_title: MTech USA Tactical Folding Knife
review_body:
I received this knife fast with Prime. It came wrapped in plastic inside a small box labeled \\"M-Tech USA 440 Stainless Steel\\". This is a super cool knife for less than $10. Kind of a modern take on the classic stiletto style. The faux pearl handles are attractive and this knife has some nice weight to it. I really like this knife for the price but...

This is my first MTech knife and while it is incredibly cool it has its flaws as do most sub $10 knives. A little TLC from the buyer goes a long way. I know, I know..products should always leave the factory issue free but usually in this price point they don't. One of the handles was loose but after tightening all the torx screws (be careful not to over tighten)this knive was solid and rattle-free.

The blade edge on this knife out of the box was surprisingly sharp and it has a super pointy tip for stabbing as that is what the stiletto style is designed for. The one I received had zero blade play which again was surprising. The blade has a black coating that i don't see holding up with use but looks cool now. Some people have said the thumb stud is sharp and can tear up your finger and i concur. I had to file it down a little.

The thin liner-lock does not exactly inspire confidence but should hold up under light to medium usage and does seem to lock tightly.
The pocket clip is high riding similar to the SOG design and at this price point is unheard of. Combined with the smooth contours of the knife itself it is easy on the pocket. If the clip ever breaks it can easily be removed for a sleeker look and feel.

This knife did need some adjustments and lube but now i am very pleased with this knife.
EDC capability is up to the individual. Is it my EDC? No, I have far superior knives for that but if this is all you can afford I say go for it as this is WAY better than nothing in a pinch and it does look wicked cool.

To all the people who buy cheap knives, have the proper tools to make adjustments and your enjoyment of said knives will increase dramatically. Knives at this price usually fail under hard or heavy usage but for light duty they can deliver.
The knife has \\"MTech USA\\" on one side and \\"Made in China\\" on the other if you like Irony..
I would recommend this knife if you understand it for what it is...inexpensive cool factor!

product_title: INSANITY Base Kit - DVD Workout
review_headline: First time working out at home!
review_body: So I originally ordered the fast and furious workout as I was kind of stuck and not able to go to the gym. I am/was a bit of a gym rat you could say, I went about 4 to 5 times a week and I am a full time working single mom of a 4 year old. After trying that workout I was amazed that I could not even come close to keeping up with it, so I ordered the Insanity workout as I love to be challenged.  I did consider myself to be in decent shape, I'm 33 and don't really need to lose more than a pound or two, but after the fast and furious workout I have realized how much better shape I could be in!  I've only really completed two days so this is slightly premature, but I already love it. My daughter loves watching me jump up and down too (the comment about my bottom jiggling funny was not needed!) and I think it's good for her to see mommy workout. Usually she sits in the gym daycare so this is a better option. I'm even going with the meal plan as I recently quit smoking and drinking alcohol entirely about a week ago. Why not get even healthier?  I will update this as time passes-I'm excited to see the results and fully committed to the program, in fact I am off to the store right now to get some new food and a decent mat to jump on!  And yes, you definitely sweat a lot. It's winter in Colorado, snowy outside, I have the heat off, window open and I am still dripping sweat haha!

product_title: UTG PRO Made in USA AMD-65 AK Quad Rail Handguard
review_headline: Can't beat it for the price!
review_body:
The stock AMD65 forward hardware looks cool, but functions poorly. Even if you attach rails to the steel forend by removing the stock grip, it still gets really hot to use after 20 rounds or so.

This UTG rail system attached quickly, securely, and is reasonably comfortable and functional using the supplied rail covers. Those covers are the \\"fat\\" style however (in three segments per rail, which do not lock into the rail; just along the sides), which are a little too large for my preference, but still work just fine. I ended up replacing them with some slim rail covers that lock into the rail, which gave me a more precise \\"feel\\" and a more solid grip. A bonus of this rail system is that when stripped of covers, it weighs the same as the AMD65 factory hardware, so aside from additional rail covers or forward grips, it doesn't add any weight to the rifle when installed.

Each vertical side of the rail has three QD-push-button holes, which is very nice for getting a custom fit location for your 2-point sling, and you don't need to spend +$20 for a QD adapter! (The current Amazon product photo does not show these holes on the side rail, instead showing what appears to be a QD hole on the bottom rail. This photo is incorrect: no QD hole on the bottom rail, three on the each side rail. The sides of the bottom rail has five large milled ports for lots of ventilation). See my attached photo for this more updated version, or better yet, go to the Leapers site and check out all the details [..]

So, the upper rail has far more space then anyone would need for red dot optic mounting, and I was considering cutting back the front portion of the top rail to match the grip section, but I realized that this area provides a very nice protective cover for the front of the gas tube and it's interface to the gas block. Those are important areas that have been criticized for being a weakness (or at least the weakest point!)on the AK, so this extended rail provided much needed protection of this area... even if it looks a bit over-designed! I just put a slim rail cover over that forward area to cover the abrasive rails and provided even more impact absorbency. Considering the price difference for the next best options out there for the AMD65, this is a really good deal and a good choice for the average citizen.

I almost deducted one star from the overall rating due to the mounting system for the rail; it uses shims at the end of the receiver to create pressure against themselves and the factory forearm lock assembly to the front, which is locked closed prior to wedging the rail between these two friction points. While I was able to get the rail in tight and was able to align the rail using a deadblow hammer pretty quickly, I'm not happy with their failure to mill a proper connection interface in the front end of their assembly to properly allow for normal use of the forearm lock assembly, which would have provide a solid anti-rotation function which is not provided in UTG's design. I assume they did this to get a tighter fit for optics use, at the sacrifice of overall forearm integrity. That said, I think it would take at least a four foot fall onto a large rock to knock this rail loose, and you could probably bang it right back into position quickly with that same rock, so I think this rail is just fine for non-combat use.

Considering you get an optics rail, four rails total, enough rail cover sections to cover all the rails, enhanced protection of the gas tube/block, and six QD holes for sling mounting, All for a low price (and claimed to be Made in the USA for 922r(17) compliance), this is a must buy for the AMD65 owner! Only downside is that the top rail is too high for a co-witness of optics, but honestly, that's not a big deal.

Followup: After 2+ weeks of handling and a couple of range trips, I've just ordered two more of these UTG rails; one for my second AM65 build-up and one formy Romanian WASR 10/63. These can'te be beat for the price, and are solid enough for \\"para-military\\" use.for the price, and are solid enough for \\"para-military\\" use.

product_title: PowerLine PPR200X Power Rack with Lat Attachment
review_headline: PowerLine PPR200X Power Rack w/ Lat Attachment
review_body: Pros:  - Inexpensive  - Comes with Pull-Up bar   - Comes with a small paint kit to fix blemishes (about half ounce)  - Lat Attachment comes with a long Lat Pull-down bar and short Row bar  Cons:  - Not very sturdy  - Badges and stickers were already peeling off when I opened the boxes  - Entire assembly comes in 5 boxes  - Lat Attachment should be a cylinder beam instead of a square beam (causes unnecessary friction)  - Lat Attachment loading bar is STANDARD 1\\"  - Lat Pull-down and Row bar do no have a separate rotating collar (they usually move to protect your wrist)  Thoughts:  Bought from Fitness Factory. The entire assembly comes in 5 boxes. The boxes came in relatively good condition. This is the same product that Amazon ships.  If you're reading this, you are probably set in getting a home gym and I probably can't deter you. If not, keep in mind most people don't use a home gym enough to justify the space and cost. There is minimal maintenance but maintenance nonetheless. Squat racks are great but you also need an adjusting bench to maximize its utility. Another associated cost with these racks is buying a weight tree, as most do no come with a weight storage system.   The PPR200X is basically a cheaply manufacturer, mass produced home gym. Don't expect much. I regularly squat 300 with this rack (it's all the Olympic weights I own) and I don't think this rack will stand the test of time. I give it another 2 years... The lift offs and safety rods are quality, however, the eyelets are not. I see a lot of play when racking barbells and I rack very lightly. The lift offs should use 2 eyelets instead of 1 and it should be inclined, say 15 degrees or so. As it is currently designed, it is flat; under load, it is -5 degrees. I contacted the manufacturer's customer service line to buy an extra pair of lift offs and I never got a reply, email or phone; it has been a month. The rack wouldn't be so bad if the rear eyelets could somehow be reinforced. The pull up bar is asupport strut. It's thin so you'll need some athletic tape.  The Lat Attachment has too much friction due to the design. It should be cylindrical instead of square. There are no bearing, it is a friction system. It also is positioned too close to the rack (6\\" from the base) despite it poking out of the rear 19\\" from the base. Not a big deal when doing squats, but when using it to bench press or incline, this will be a problem. Read the description carefully, the loading bar is STANDARD 1\\" diameter and only 12\\" long. The rack, however, is fitted for Olympic barbells. The loading bar on the Lat Attachment can be fitted for Olympic plates if you go to your local hardware store and get PVC pipes and retrofit them.  This is a cheap beginner set. Don't get the lat attachment (It is also sold separately). I truly doubt the manufacturer will honor any warranty. Save up for better designed squat racks ($800+) or just get a gym membership.   Bottom line:  Not Recommended.

review_headline: Awesome knife at a great price but be CAREFUL!
review_body: I have a background in Filipino Martial Arts and knife fighting. As such I've collected a lot of knives over the years, most of them mid to high end. For the money this knife can't be beat. The blade is thick and huge, and given the recurve of the blade the cutting edge is even longer! The best part of the knife though is the handle. Your hand feels rock-solid and locked into this knife. I would feel very safe using full force stabs or chops with this handle. The Pommel also looks like it would break a nose or crack a skull with ease. Despite such a solid hand grip you can still transition easily between blade forward or ice pick grip. The blade opens easily with a downward wrist snap. Less easy is opening via the thumb stud or wave feature. The blade locks in with a concrete \\"snap\\" and this locking mechanism seems super solid with no blade play. Actually it was a little too solid when I first bought it. One of the common complaints I've read about this knife is that it's hard to close PERIOD, and very dangerous to one handed close. In my opinion given the size and sharpness and WEIGHT of this blade, your an idiot if you one hand close it. To me speed in opening is more important than being able to close it one handed. It was very hard to close even two handed until I started using the edge of a counter top and a towel (to protect the counter top)and depressed the liner lock a couple hundred times. This smoothed it out so now it closes nicely, but I still wouldn't one hand it. While big it fits in the pocket nicely with some adjustment. It can be an EDC if your pants allow it, and you'd definitively want to bring it with you if you have to travel through the bad part of town. The size and \\"snap\\" of it locking would scare the crap out of most criminals. Comes VERY sharp out of the box.

product_title: Confidence Slim Full Body Vibration Platform Fitness Machine
review_body: Received and assembled the Confidence Slim vibration machine today. As I had read from other reviews, the documentation is poor. However, assembly was a real pain because of the documentation but the way the machine was engineered. First the bolt holes that hold up the control panel were machined improperly so the bolts did not fit the holes. Had to purchase a reamer from the hardware store to make the holes large enough to fit the bolts. Had to go back to the hardware store and purchase a different size reamer because the nuts did not fit the eye bolts for the elastic exercise straps. The holds in the rubber mat for the eye bolts had to be re-drilled to line up with the eye bolt holes. After all that, the elastic straps that connect to the eye bolts had nothing to hook on to so when you finish with them, you just let them drop to the floor. I used plastic straps and hooks that are normally used to hang pictures to have a place to hang the straps when not needed. The machine is however very quiet as others have said. The machine seems to work very well and has a wide range of vibration settings. However, the mode settings will take some experience to understand what they are. I also think that after a few months of use, I will need to re tighten screws to keep parts from coming lose. I think this is the price you have to pay for a machine at this price. To save over a thousand dollars I think it was a good purchase but if you don't have someone to do a good assembly job, you might just have to pay more for a machine engineered to better specs.

product_title: UTG 126 Lumen Combat Xenon Light, Handheld and Ring Mount
review_body: The UTG Defender Series Tactical Xenon Flashlight that first arrived had a pressure pad that didn't work.  DO NOT ALLOW THE PRESSURE SWITCH WIRE TO TWIST AS YOU INSTALL IT.  YOU WILL DISCONNECT THE INTERNAL WIRE CONNECTION AND THE PRESSURE PAD WILL NOT WORK.  Needed to get a replacement.  That made me instantly decide that I might not be able to rely on the flashlight in a critical situation.  Points off there.  Shipping was super fast.  Installation on standard rails was simple and sturdy.  Good materials that are realtively well-crafted.  Put 1000 rounds through the weapon over the next week and saw no problems.  Bright light.  Good illumination in less than 20 meters.  If you're going to have the weapon out in the heat though, you shouldn't rely on the adhesiveness of the hook & loop for the pressure pad.  Being out in the sun for hours will cause the adhesive to loosen up.  Had I not anticipated that and put a hair tie around it, the pressure pad would have been flopping around.  As other reviewers have mentioned, there's no on/off switch.  The pressure pad (and the on/off button also provided) has to be pressed to keep the light functioning.  That's another reason not to rely on this type of light in a combat setting.  If you have to take your offhand off the weapon then you aren't going to have any light (which is consistent with certain tactical training, but still a downside that there isn't an option).  But if you're just looking for a good mounted flashlight for a good price, this product works just fine.

product_title: Hogue Stock Mossberg 500 Overrubber Shotgun Stock Kit with Forend, 12-Inch L.O.P
review_headline: Good stock.... no bolt to attach it.
review_body: Really Hogue? Really? No bolt or lock washer?? How hard would it be to throw a bolt in the box? Just fyi, you're going to need a 5/16, course thread bolt 5.5 inches long. Hex head or allen key head are probably best. Avoid flat head or Phillips as it will be hard to torque up the bolt and might round off the head. Use the provided washer, and go find yourself a bolt AND a lock washer. If you can't find a bolt, you can use a piece of all thread and red loc-tite on a nut to make yourself a bolt. When you assemble it, I'd recommend doing it once without the trigger group in and look inside the receiver to see if the screw pokes through. You want it as close to flush as possible. If it sticks out it's going to interfere with the trigger and it won't fire. At the same time, you want to engage as much of the threads as possible. Awesome stock, but about the hardware, Hogue... wtf guys. Come on.

product_title: Minn Kota Riptide ST Saltwater 80 RT80/ST/CP Bow-Mount Trolling Motor - 24v-80lb-54
review_body: I struggled with this very expensive trolling motor for 3 winters here in Florida, but it is on it's way to the dumpster this year.  The first year it worked for a couple of months before it started acting up.  The gyro would do strange things and almost knock you off the boat, then it quit running.  After an internal inspection, I noticed that all of the circuit board and electronic connections were not sealed in a water tight environment.  Worse than that, the plug in connections were not coated and very quickly became affected by saltwater.  This is why it quit running.  One of the power connections pulverized off of it's connection.  The service center did repair it under warranty, but it took a couple of weeks.  It did work for a while and then started acting up again.  Back to the service center to have one of the circuit boards replaced.  Another three weeks this time.  I had another trip to the service center last year, just as the warranty was expiring.  It then worked pretty good the rest of the winter.  I store my boat in the summer months inside, along with the trolling motor.  I launched the boat this week and put the Minn Kota on yesterday and had a lot of difficulty with the deployment mechanism.  It has always been prone to sticking.  This time it took over an hour to get it to work properly.  I was pleased that it started fine, but very unhappy to find that the directional controls were not working.  I then noticed that several pieces of wire had fallen out of the casing, that had corroded off of their connections.  I did not bother to take it apart to find out where they came from because it was obvious that it was shot and now truly a piece junk.  I am on my way to Outdoor World to get a new trolling motor.  It will not be a Minn Kota ST.  It will be a more traditional model.

product_title: Ka-Bar Adventure Potbelly Knife
review_body: When looking for a knife I was looking for a knife that was about 10-13\\" OAL and that would excel at shelter building and firewood processing because of extremely cold and wet conditions that we have in my area.  This knife is stout enough to hack through just about anything you put in it's way.  I considered the BK2 but thought that the Potbelly would fit my needs just a little better.  In particular I liked the extra length and the handle positioning.  I think the BK2 looks better but that was not one of my criteria.  I also liked the large pouch on the sheath.  In the pouch I'm able to keep a small flashlight, cord, stone, and a emergency kit in a sucrets tin.  I also have the \\"adventure cord tied to the back along with my ferro rod.  The \\"piggy back\\" is a nice addition and helps to fill the role of fine tasks.  I have to mention though that you can choke up on the choil and perform some surprisingly small tasks with the Potbelly.  This knife comes extremely sharp out of the box!  In the sheath this is a big knife and you know you have it on when you're wearing it.  The BK2 is a bit shorter but I can promise you that the extra 2 3/8 inches and forward handle positioning makes a big difference when hacking or splitting wood.  In closing if I was separated from my pack and all I had was my Potbelly, PiggyBack, and the contents I keep on the sheath I would have all the resources that I would need to protect me from the elements.  Steve Johnson did a great job matching form with function on this design.  If you are on the fence I would recommend that you check one of these out.

product_title: Sole Fitness F80 Folding Treadmill (Previous Years Model)
review_body: Here is my initial reaction to the Sole F 80. I bought mine from sears and picked it up and put it together.    1-This machine is clearly heavier than my old Nordic track that died after about 800 miles.  2-The machine was packed well and other than being heavy was easy to unpack.  3-The machine was put together in about an hour.  I don't get some of the reviews that say this machine was so difficult to put together.  Again something that makes me suspicious.  I thought the instructions were straight foward and there were no mysterious to figure out when putting during assembly.  4-after an initial run the machine is very stable.  Yes it does make noise when you heel strike, but other wise the motor and deck seem pretty quite.  I tend to be a heel striker so I make more noise.  It doesn't help that Im 6'4 260.  Again I am not sure what the complaint is from the 1 stars on noise.  This ain't a commercial tread mill people.  If you comparing it to a cybex, life star, or woodway that you find in your gym then you are a fool.  It wasn't supposed to be those and never will be.  YOU SPEND 1500 on this not 35-4500.  5-Speaking of height, the deck length is great.  Love it.  6-There were some complaints of beeps.  umm people get your tread mill serviced.  No beeps at all.  7-The display is straight forward and easy to read.  It is not real flashy.  8-The fans do seem pretty weak.  9-Haven't played with the Chest strap or I pod attachment, but after my initial thoughts on this treadmill I feel confident that I am going to find that the 1 stars way off on those also.  10-The deck folds up and drops very easily and nicely  As an initial review I recommend this tread mill.  As you do research on this tread mill you will not find one negative review from industry insiders.  I am suspect of the 1 stars.  I think they fall into two categories.  1-People that just got a lemon, something that can happen with even the most expensive treadmill.  That is what Warranties are for.  2- Fake reviews .  I will  up date this as I get more miles in, but so far I am very pleased.  Update:  Ok took a short break in run.    1-The chest strap works great.  again I don't know what some of the 1-2 star reviewers are beefing about.  The signal was strong and consistent.  My only negative on the chest strap is the battery case.  The person that decided to put the battery behind 4 ultra small screws should be hunted down and hung.  2-The I pod speakers sound fine.  They aren't a high end sound system by any means, but they certainly get the job done.  Again my findings make me real suspicious of the negative reviews.  3-I ran a short interval program.  I didn't find any problem with the time between speed changes.  Is it as fast as running out side or a cybex or wood way?  No.  But again....that is unrealistic.  The speeds change fast enough to do intervals as long as you want to.  Update:  The interval program is not really an interval in my mind.  It is more like a hill type program.  There are only 5 bumps and that does not increase with added time,  The bumps just get longer.  I wish the program was more of a standard Interval program.  Don't get me wrong.  It will make you sweat.  The program makes great use of not only speed, but incline to kick your butt.

product_title: Plano Tackle Box with Chill Bag System (Blue/Silver)
review_body: Although I was opposed to a hard case at first, I think this hard/soft tackle box was a great buy, especially at the price.  My favorite thing about this box is the versatility (although the cup holders on top are a nice touch).  The inside is divided into 3 equal sized sections capable of holding 2 Plano 3000 series boxes.  One thing that I really like is that I can choose how I set this up.  As shipped, one is empty, one has a cooler, and one has 2 tackle boxes.  If I want to bring more tackle, I can put 6 boxes in and ditch the cooler.  If I'm going to be dock/bridge/pier fishing, I'll use 4 boxes and a cooler.  If I have an extra reel or too much big stuff to fit in all of the outside pockets (or just want something to be protected), I can leave one or two sections open, and only bring 2 tackle boxes.  Also, all of my fishing buddies have soft cases for tackle, and after several years the zippers no longer work (which is to be expected, since we do almost all saltwater fishing).  Anyway, I don't mind pockets that stay open permanently, but I like to have at least one section that stays closed and protected for my tackle.  I haven't done a lot of fishing with this box yet, but so far it holds all my tackle and fit/finish seems to be nice.  I would definitely recommend this box to anyone -- whether you need storage space for lots of tackle while on the boat, or if you just want to bring a 6-pack out to the dock and keep one hand free to carry your rods.

product_title: Leupold 112180 RX-1000I TBR W/DNA
review_body: I purchased both units to compare the two, after which I took both the Leica CRF 1600 and the Leupold RX-1000i on a test run. Both units operated similarly. Press the POWER button once to turn it on, then press again to activate the rangefinder. I ranged the Leica out to at least 1300 yards, using a forest as a \\"target.\\" The numbers on the display of the CRF are thinner, while those on the Leupold are far larger. Other than thickness of the numbers on the display and the small reticular \\"square\\" that is to fit over the target on the CRF, and the larger reticle-type center-finder on the Leupold display, I found that either reticle would work equally effectively.   I found that the lens in the CRF was marginally more crisp than that of the Leupold. I had to really look into the rangefinders going from one to the other, but it was still difficult to decide which lens was the clearer. From a hunting standpoint, I frankly didn't see any meaningful differences in clarity. The power on the CRF is 7, while that of the Leupold is 6. I didn't find the power difference to be a problem. The field of view of the Leica is a bit larger than that of the Leupold, but again, only marginally.  Again, both rangefinders have excellent lenses and both would work well. Beyond 1,000 yards, the Leica wins out over the Leupold just because it has the longer range capabilities, leading me to believe that the Leica CRF would be the rangefinder of choice for hunters who plan to hunt animals at longer distances and need to know how far they need to climb or walk to get a shot at animals almost a mile away. Frankly, I don't know anyone who can accurately place an uphill or downhill shot at 1,000 yards or more, but I would guess that there are those  who can. If so, buy the Leica.  I also noticed that the Leupold offered a battery power status indicator in the display when the unit is turned on. I didn't notice this feature in the Leica during my cursory examination, although it may be a feature that can be programmed into the rangefinder.  The weights are about the same, although the CRF is about 1/2\\" longer---including the eyepiece---than the Leupold. The sizes are almost the same (the Leica is slightly larger), making them both pocket-friendly. The Leica touts that their unit can be used with eyeglasses if the rubber eyepiece is folded back. I found that this method reduced the field-of-view, and I ended up pushing my glasses over my forehead so that I could benefit from a full field-of-view. The Leica did, however, provide marks on their eyepiece to record diopter readings, while the Leupold didn't. It really is of little consequence. Once you get your eyepiece twisted to where your eye likes it, you don't need to change it. The diopter readings would be useful only if you lend your Leica to a friend who twists the eyepiece to his liking, then you have to twist it back to where it was originally---not a big deal.  I didn't get into the user-friendliness of the trajectory procedure because I have not had time, and I am not really interested at this point.  For ground squirrel/prairie dog/coyote shooters and those of us who hunt at distances far shorter than 1,000 yards, the Leupold would work just fine, and at a price that is about half that of the Leica CRF, the Leupold should be a serious consideration since I found that it picked up small plants, leaves and small objects on the ground with no problems. I am not a long-distance shooter; 300-400 yards is my maximum for ground squirrels. If I were lucky enough to hunt on huge open-ranges that offer long-distance shooting, I would definitely get into the 6mm-Creedmore-type rifles, but for now I must settle for shorter distances due to surrounding ranches, cattle, etc.This means that I must drag out my 22-250 for shots past 250 yards, so the Leupold would suit my needs just fine when used with the .222 and the .20 VarTarg.  Since I shoot where there are farm houses in sight, it would be helpful to be able to know how far away they are, just to find out if noise from the centerfire rifles might drive the ranchers or their wives nuts. For instance if a ranch were almost a mile away, I might be inclined to use the centerfires, rather than using the quieter rimfires. The Leica trumps the Leupold here, merely because of its longer-ranging capabilities.  One other point: the Leupold has the mode button on the side, making it a two-handed operation, rather than one-handed as with the Leica CRF. This probably doesn't make much of a difference once the figures are dialed in for bullet-trajectories, but I thought I would mention it. Also---getting nit-picky---the Leupold has a nubbed top cap which makes it less \\"slippery\\" when holding it. The Leica's surface is okay, but it would have been a plus if it were \\"stickier\\" when holding it. It probably makes little difference to those who hunt with gloves on, but I thought I would bring it up.  Both units have openings for lanyards and include lanyards in the shipping box.  So....IMHO, you can't go wrong with either rangefinder. It all depends on how much money you want to spend and the distances you need to know for your own particular hunting situation.  I like the 1600-yard feature of the Leica, but since I am a shorter-range shooter, I would have used it only to figure out how close the nearest rancher is.   There had been some negative comments on the Leupolds on some of the shooting websites, but frankly, I saw little clarity differences (if any) between the two rangefinder lenses. As I mentioned, Leica's readout font is not as \\"thick\\" as that of the Leupold, and the Leupold has the easy-to-read battery power status indicator that shows up immediately on the display when the power button is pushed during startup---a nice touch. The Leica might have this feature, but I don't remember seeing it. Some Leica owners have complained that the readout tends to be difficult to read sometimes in bright-sun conditions, but I didn't encounter such a problem.   I think Leupold has a winner with the RX-1000i. Don't get me wrong: the Leica is an excellent rangefinder, but I am going to keep the Leupold and will return the Leica, merely because for what I plan to use the instrument for, the much higher cost of the Leica doesn't appear to provide that much of a benefit over the Leupold. Keep in mind that my review was based on a fairly cursory side-by-side comparison of the display, range capability, size and a few other features that one brand might offer over those of the other. Owners of the Leica and Leupold might have different opinions, and if so, I invite them to chime in.    Cost-wise, from what I could find, the CRF 1600 prices are about the same ($799) across the board, with one exception: Cove Creek Outfitters offers them at $685. In addition, they offer the CRF 1000 for $529. Cove Creek didn't offer Leupold rangefinders, but they do carry Leupold scopes.

product_title: Moultrie Camera Security Box
review_headline: It's a universal box...so don't expect a custom fit.  Throw lock and cable away upon arrival.
review_body: The first thing I want on record is that this is a universal box...so if you're looking for a custom fit, you will be sorely disappointed.  I purchased this for a Moultrie I-40 trail camera and I experienced what many other did.  The camera didn't sit right in the box and the camera box doesn't come with parts to tailor the box to the camera being protected.  To get a custom fit, I went to a local auto parts store and found two auto trim panel retainers to stick into the box from the back and the hollow legs of the camera fit right into the retainers.  Then I went to a hardware store and purchased a brass bolt, some washers, and some spacers.  I removed the vertical adjustment knob, drilled a hole in the box to line up with the threads of where the vertical adjustment knob was, and with the brass bolt, spacers, and washers, secured the top of the camera to the box.  Then I ran the strap that came with the camera through the cut-outs in the back of the box and the camera fits in the box perfectly.  So...yes it stinks that you have to get all MacGyver on the box to get a custom fit, but it beats having to fabricate a box yourself.  The second thing is that yes...this box will not 100% keep thieves from stealing your camera.  If there is a determined d-bag that wants jack your camera, then this box will not stop the theft.  If this is out in the middle of the woods and not monitored daily, someone can cut the cable, pry the box open, cut the lock, or even chop down the tree it's attached to if they want your camera THAT bad, so you'll have to come to peace with that.  It's primary function is to keep your camera safer from the elements and DETER theft...but not prevent it.  That being said there are two items that come with this box that you should recycle as soon as you open the packaging: The lock and the cable.  The lock is cheap and the cable is even cheaper (a pair of side cutters would easily cut through the cable).  Moultrie should just reduce the retail price by $10 and simply sell the box.  If you want to truly DETER theft, then buy a shrouded padlock and a much thicker cable lock to replace the junk that came in the box.  The better lock and cable will keep honest people from messing with your camera and if a determined thief wants your camera, he'll at least have to put some effort into it!  In conclusion, plan on getting creative if you want your camera to fit perfectly in the box, plan on buying a better lock and cable, and realize that locks only stop honest people...not determined thieves.  Happy hunting!

product_title: CargoSmart Hard - shell Car - top Cargo Carrier
review_body:
First, I purchased this at a local brick and mortar \\"blue-mart\\" for less than it is listed here (by about 25%) It's cheap, it works, but may require a trip to the hardware store. Hands down it beats one of those scary rooftop bags people drive around with (at least until it rips). It's absolutely not a Thule or Yakima in quality but it doesn't cost anywhere near that much. This unit would be a beast to ship (due to packaging size) so you better check on return shipping policies or commit up front.

[Functionality]
It does what it advertises at a low cost - it will hold roughly two large suitcases with room for a bit more. Water resistance is there (it's plastic, after all) but it doesn't hurt to put some weather sealing in the front lip of the box.

The major downside for a low-cost cargo box is that the lid has no lift arms or hinges. Thus, you generally have to completely remove the lid (which is light) to remove or store cargo. Not a deal killer at this price range. A handy person will just go to the hardware store and grab some appropriate lift arms/hinges (and some weather seal or perhaps RV silicone, see above)

[Construction]
Construction is acceptable enough considering it's polypropylene (softer plastic) and not ABS (rigid plastic). Granted, rigid ABS plastic cargo boxes run over $300 pretty easily.

The latching mechanism works with a rear tug on the lid to latch and a forward push to release. A handle in the rear secures the lid when closing. Again, the lid is not attached by hinge or lift arm but it is very light. An eyelet is present for a lock on the rear handle.

[Installation]
The cargo box includes the necessary u-bolts, mounting plates, wing-nuts, and other parts. A cordless drill with screwdriver and drill bits is ideal (plus a wrench, ratchet, or pliers to steady a nut). This will probably take one *average* person 15-25 minutes. I took 30-40 minutes as I used manual tools and a corded drill at the end. Also, one of the screws was not machined/forged properly so the screw-head stripped a bit and took a while to secure.

The full box itself is incredibly light and an average person can lift it easily.

The cargo box has numerous alignment holes for the u-bolts. I only caution that you consider your cargo type, weight, and crossbar position for load balancing. As I mentioned earlier this is a softer plastic (not ABS). A heat-absorbing black, soft propy plastic box, 110+ degree plus heat, with say a load of bricks positioned between the crossbars is probably a bad idea. product_title: Ultega Pull-Up Bar
review_headline: Easy to assemble, difficult to mount
review_body:
The problem with this device (which I was really looking forward to using) is the door mounting element. Assembling the device took less than fifteen minutes. It seems sturdy enough and, while I can imagine repeated use tearing apart the foam rubber, this could be easily remedied down the road.
The problem is finding a doorway to mount it securely. As it turns out, none of the doorways in my apartment work. The one that might have a chance has a door frame that is too narrow. There is one small and flimsy metal piece that is supposed to help secure the plastic bar to the top of your door frame. Naturally, it is not strong enough and could easily be bent with your hands. Given a wide enough door frame ledge for the plastic crossbar to rest upon comfortably, there wouldn't be too much need to depend upon the flimsy guard, as the longer crossbar rests against the other side of the doorway and balances the stress. However, in my case, I don't have that. My door frames ledges are either not wide enough or I don't have enough space to accomodate the longer crossbar.
I have thought about some options and I could probably mount a 2 x 4 to an open doorway area and then get some stronger guards to prevent the crossbar from slipping off the 2 x 4. This should work and I'll give it a try (if the landlord doesn't mind...), but until then - consider this review a warning that the successful use of this device depends upon your doorways/doorframes and the available space around them.
I'll write more after I make the adaptations.

product_title: Snugpak Jungle Sleeping Bag, , LH Zipper
review_body:
Just got back from a 4 night trip. We were following a river and temps at night dropped to the mid 40's. I used this bag with a thermorest neoair. Every night I wore a mid weight fleece, a light weight fleece hat, and a pair of shorts. Two of the nights I needed to wear a pair of socks. I would classify myself as a hot sleeper and rarely stay in my other bags (rated to 0 degrees) all night.

My legs got cold every night. I would put the comfort temp of this bag (for a normal sleeper) in the mid to high 50's and not 45 degrees as advertised. My guess is that you would be extremely cold if you tried to use this bag much below 40 degrees without pants, a fleece, and a hat.

This bag packs small and doesn't weigh much. I like that I can make it a blanket due to the dual zipper design (one along the bottom and one along the length of the bag). Though this dual zipper design may be part of the problem with my legs getting cold.

I used a tent, so I cannot comment on the mosquito netting over the face. However, there does not appear to be anything to keep the netting off your skin, so I doubt it would be extremely useful.

Also, some of the stitching on the stuff sack has begun to tear.

All in all this will be my go to bag (due to size and weight) anywhere the low night temps are in the high 40's. If you are a cold sleeper or are going somewhere colder find a warmer bag.

product_title: Iron Gym Total Upper Body Workout Bar
review_headline: Fits great on my doorways.  Sturdy materials to support a large person.
review_body: There are so many reviews of the Iron Gym Total Upper Body Workout Bar that I don't know what else I can say, other than the reports of this product's great quality are not exaggerated.  After having read several reviews, good and bad, I knew that I needed to establish that my door frames were the right width for the workout bar so I measured the door frame width and the thickness of the molding on the upper part of the door.  The door frame was about 32\\" wide and the molding just under 1/2\\" thick - which seemed to be right for this product based on the reviews of others, so I ordered it.  The Iron Gym Total Upper Body Workout Bar arrived a day earlier than estimated in great condition.  There were no signs it had been tampered with or previously opened.  It came with the useless \\"Free Mail in Ab Strap\\" offer.  But since the shipping and handling is $8 and you can get ab straps at Wal-Mart for just as cheap, there was no incentive there.  Assembly was very easy.  The bolts fit into place with no problems.  Previous reviews that mentioned the little wrench that was included being of poor quality were correct.  Having read those reviews, I didn't expect much out of it.  I hand tightened the bolts in place then used the included wrench to tighten gently without over-stressing the tool.  But, still, by the time I was done, it was beginning to warp and wear out.  It's a one use only implement, I'm afraid.  I finished up tightening using a wrench of my own.  Once assembled, I placed it in the doorway to a back room in the house.  It held in place just fine and fit square on top of the door frame and flush against the wall on the door hinge side.  The pull up bar's padded ends fit square against the door frame with no overhang - just the right size.  I was nervous when actually putting my weight on it.  I weigh just over 220 lb.  I feared the crackling sound of wood moving and breaking and drywall disintegrating.  I slowly started putting my weight on the workout bar.  Nocrackles, snaps or pops. It held me and allowed me to do 3/4 of a pullup (I'm a work in progress), a complete chin up and several negative motions.  I also just hung from it several times.    There was a slight blemishing of the paint on the wall just above the frame - but I can only blame my weight and the materials used in my home's construction.  It's not the fault of the workout bar.  It's sturdy materials did their job - there was no bending of the bar that I could notice as I tested it out.  Time will tell what kind of padding I might need to supplement the placement of the bar.  All in all, this is a great piece of equipment.  People need to measure their door frame's width and thickness before purchasing the workout bar and assess the quality of their location's construction.    P.S.  I did not find the metal clip/door frame wedge included in the package to be necessary.

When I saw this TaylorMade Speed Sleeve tool at Golf Galaxy local store, I immediately picked it up without hesitation. Compared to the donut ring type of swing weight, this is a much better design. It is a simple concept which allows you to attach it to a regular golf club, given an Iron or a Wood.  The beauty of this swing weight is that you can hit the golf ball at driving range with the swing sleeve attached to the golf club. I brought it to the golf range and attached it to the 6 Iron. I made a few practice swing and then I went ahead to hit balls with it. Since it is heavily weighted, you will have to swing it with your back muscle (big muscle) and turn your hip prpperly to bring the club back in square at the impact zone.  After I hit 5 balls, I then switched to hit balls with 7 Iron. The immediate feedback is that now my swing is grooved with good tempo and smoother hip turn and shoulder turn. This tool will also help to reduce over-swing at the top. It is cheaper than other Swing Trainers ($70 range) and it works better than other Strength Trainers ($99 range) because it allows you to swing any club that you want.  Amazon has the same price as it is sold in a golf store. So you can pick it up here. However, as always, please be careful with this swing weight tool and don't practice too long with this tool attached to a golf clus, or else you might get muscle injury or fatigue.
