product_title: Clear Fly Fishing Bathroom Scale
review_body: I didn't buy it yet but its on my Santa list.  It reminds me of the barbed wire clear acrylic toilet seats they used to sell.  Scales are scary enough without vicious hooks threatening your bare feet.  Funny.  One thing, just because a scale is digital doesn't mean its more accurate.  The description should say what the accuracy is.  It could still be off five pounds, even if it shows one exact number.  on an old spring scale, you can wiggle your feet and see the needle move, so you know there's some error.  I have an old $10 Ikea scale that's fully 10lb light compared to the doctor's office, and I know that isn't just my shirt and pants.  Its also nice to know what batteries it takes, so you know how easy they will be to replace.  I avoid button batteries where I can because they are so hard to match and cost so much compared to AAA

product_title: iheater IH-1500W Quartz Infrared Portable Heater
review_headline: Not as great as I thought
review_body: It took me 2 years to decide to buy one of these infared heaters. I settled on the I heater. I work in the hvac field so i used some of the tools of the trade to test the performance of this heater. There is a difference between the small medium and large room settings. The small rm puts out 85 degree air. The large rm puts out 110 degree air. I have used the heater for 30 days. I use it in a very large room. The room is a open floor plan room with a cathedral ceiling 14 foot at highest point.(dinning rm kitchen and family rm). The heater is set at 75 and never shuts off for the 4 to 5 hours its on. The heater will raise the wall t-stat one to 4 degrees in the 5 hours it is on. I keep the wall t-stat set at 68. If I set the iheater at 72 it will shut off, but doesnt cycle like it should. The temp in the room drops quickly wants the heat source is off. It does keep the furnace from cycling on and off. I turn the iheater on at 4 and off at 10 and the furnace doesnot run during those hours. I did try the iheater in an other room. When i started the test it was 68 in the room with humidy reading of 37%. the iheater was set at 75. It took 2 hours to heat room to 75. The heater shut off. I took temp readings at ceiling it was 80. At the floor it was 70. The so called even heat from floor to ceiling is misleading. The humidy dropped to 32%. so the heater does remove humidy. But the iheater say it doesn't remove humidy. Now comes the electric bill.  The bill went up $23 from last year.$40 from last month. But I didn't use the furnace until the end of the month so that is not accurate gauge. The iheater is great for that all over warm feeling if you stand a few feet from it. Like other people have said if you stay in one room all the time then it is great. But the rest of your house gets cold. It can keep a room cozy. It cant heat 1000 sqft like the box states. It is better than the ceramic heaters but cost alot more too.   So my final word is this it saves on the gas bill but causes the electric bill to go up.

review_headline: still breaking it in - but i'm sticking with it (no pun intended)
review_body:
**UPDATED*** It's Feb. 2015 as I update, and still use this mat, and it's still wonderful. I love the longer length the best.

There are already 204 reviews of this item. I'm only adding my own in case someone looks *me* up and wants to see what items I endorse - but be sure to read the other excellent and detailed reviews of this item before buying.

I recently treated myself to the [[ASIN:B0000DZFXZ Manduka BlackMatPRO 71-Inch Yoga and Pilates Mat]], what one amazon.com reviewer called \\"the Cadillac of yoga mats.\\" The thing is a monster - larger than normal mats and very heavy (7 pounds, they say) but hey, I carry around books and a laptop all day when commuting to the City, so I figure so what if I carry one more thing. I do not sweat a lot, and I found it to slip some when I first used it, even though I did wash it down as instructed. But honestly, I don't care about that. I see others in class with gouges in their mats (toenails can do that much damage?) and this one comes with a lifetime guarantee. I'm getting up in age, and my joints don't need the extra stress of creaking on a floor that's less than ideally padded. I will update this review at some point when I've broken the mat in, but this is my mat for the rest of my lifetime.

In case you want to save a little, this beautiful [[ASIN:B004AIFFFS Embroidered Cotton Yoga Mat Bag]] fits the Manduka very well! It makes commuting with the Manduka manageable. The strap is adjustable, and there's enough room inside the rolled mat to stuff my yoga clothes. There are also zippered pockets, but I don't use them. It is as beautiful as the photographs indicate, and compared to the less-beautiful [[ASIN:B000VW4VWA Manduka MatSak]] that runs (at the time of this writing) $43 to $64, it's a beautiful bargain.

product_title: Maxpedition Malaga Gearslinger
review_body:
My 2nd Max pack. First was a Jumbo, but it wasn't jumbo enough. I use the packs for a different reason than most might: as a camera bag. I recently had surgery and need to get out and walk and found pretty early on I needed a bag to carry my camera, lenses and water. None of the 3000 camera bags (ok, so more like 9) that I have have a slot for water and none had the extra pockets for other little stuff. Plus, I don't have a sling camera bag. The Jumbo, then the Malanga seemed perfect for the task.
OK, a couple things: almost no padding. For a camera bag, not a good thing. I wrap mine in some velco-enhanced fleece padding and we're all good. Also they have plastic and metal pieces on the inside of the pockets which could scratch your camera. Something to think about if you're going to use it like me.
So why did I use for cameras? Most camera bags have tons of padding. Great for cameras and lenses - not great to haul around everywhere. Maybe if I was hiking on rocks, I'd take a Lowepro sling instead, but I'm walking flat trails in parks. A little care and user-installed padding and that's all I need. Also, since camera bags are for sensitive gear and contain so much padding, water is a strict no-go. I needed water for the walks. Between my dslr and water, I'd take water first. In the Malaga, water is provided for in the outside pouch closest to the wearer and separated from the gear by a waterproof layer. Fine for me.
I fit in this thing my Nikon D7000, 24-120/4 lens, Sigma 10-20 lens in a lens case, batteries and memory cards, SB800 flash, filter sachel, plus knives, power bars, first aid stuff and a multi-tool. Try that in your Lowepro sling!
The Jumbo actually was more comfortable on, but the Malaga can be switched from shoulder to shoulder, where the Jumbo is side-specific dependent on the model you select. The Jumbo also couldn't safely take camera and lens, plus extra lens. And it had no Camelbak pouch.
At a hundred bucks or so, it's also way cheaper than a camera bag. And when you leave the camera at home, perfect overnighter. But then, if I was going overnight, I'd take my camera.an a camera bag. And when you leave the camera at home, perfect overnighter. But then, if I was going overnight, I'd take my camera.

review_body:

The driver is absolutely awesome! I hit the balls farther and straighter than the guys I played with, who play more often than I do. It was crazy to see the ball fly so straight after they hit theirs to the right/left of the fairway. After that, I couldn't catch a break. Oh well, within time I'll get it.

I can't hit with a hybrid to save my life and I'm sure that will get some taking used to. I actually prefer the Irons for now. The PW is great, no problems with it. The putter is heavy and awkward but did the job nicely.

I'd prefer a SW as a PW isn't so great in the bunkers.

Some of the cons would be the broken leg on the stand on arrival. It was bent to the point of rendering it useless. The grips on the clubs are nice at first but they started to rub my right thumb raw. Definitely wanted another glove, lol. The clubs are tad bit heavy due to the steel shaft but it's not really that big of a deal.

Other than that, if you want a good set at a good price, these are it!

product_title: SOG Knives Twitch II Black TiNi - Knives & Accessories - Folding & Lock Back
review_body:
I bought this knife about 2 years ago from out local big box hardware store, at about the same price. There are a number of things I look for when purchasing a knife, one being made in America, the other is price. The Twitch II fit the bill on both of those criteria, now for the review of the knife itself.

Fit: I have fairly normal sized hands I feel, (lg. gloves) and the fit of this knife in my hand is very comfortable.

Opening: I must say, I've owned my share of pocket knives, made one too, and this is the easiest opening knife I've owned, barring the switch blade from my Marine Corps days. Truly, all you need to do is to run your forefinger along the spine where the blade protrudes out the handle and snap, it's open.

Closing: One handed, easy enough.

Sharpening: I own a Smith sharpening system, and this blade is easy to sharpen, and holds its edge extremely well.

Clip: The clip is very unobtrusive, and keeps the knife securely in my back pocket. It is very light and for the most part I do not even know it's there. Which can be a hassle if I've got to pass through a metal detector and have forgotten to take it out of my pocket.

I hope this helps to answer some your questions regarding this knife, I would definitely recommend buying.

product_title: Fox 40 Classic CMG Official Finger Grip Whistle
review_body: I can't say enough good things about this piece of fine Canadian engineering! Pealess whistles never jam or fail to shrill because there are no moving parts. The finger grip fits my hand very well, except when I wear gloves (which, fortunately, I rarely do), and doesn't accidentally shift or move. This means that my whistle is always right where I expect it to be, even when running. The documentation says that the finger grip is adjustable, but I have not managed to solve this riddle. The CMG (cushioned mouth grip) is intended to help referees who hold the whistle in their lips or teeth, which I do not, but it does allow my lips to make a tighter seal, so more of my force of air is pushed through the whistle. The lack of a reservoir (like pea-style whistles have) means that water and dirt are less likely to accumulate and interfere with proper operation. This whistle is capable of a 115 dB shrill, and the best part is that somehow it doesn't hurt the ears of the user. This whistle cannot be overblown (pea-style whistles tend to mess up when blown too hard or soft), though it quickly loses its effectiveness if underblown. I believe that this whistle (or another from Fox 40 if you prefer lanyards) is a must-have for any sports official.

product_title: United Cutlery Tomahawk Throwing Knife Set (3-Piece), Black
review_body: So I bought These knifes because they were not only cheep, but the amazon price was temporarily cut in half for about 4 bucks so I bought it without hesitation.   Unlike other throwing knives that are easy to throw and land on your target, this one is about 50 times more difficult. At first I thought they were crap because it took me approximately 85 throws before I could figure out the trick to throw them, and land my first hit.  It took 3 weeks of practice to be able to throw them one at a time and be able to land all 3 in a row, however my success at landing them is still below 9 out of 10.  I found out the trick is to keep the elbow of your dominant arm facing forward, and hold the back of the handle with only the top of edge of your thumb and index finger. Next your suposed to bend your arm back all the way, while still keeping the elbow pointing toward your target. At a moderate speed you must straighten your arm but keep your hand in a solid position and RIGHT as your arm straightens all the way you must let it slide while curving it as if your trying to make it spin in midair as it leaves your hands.  The Tips bend easily if you miss, or don't land properly, but are easily reflattenable when sharpened by a standard kitchen knife sharpening stone. (it's what you get for having stainless steel material) But who cares, you can't expect throwing knives to be made of better material, otherwise it's like buying golden bullets, their made of good material but useless after fired and unretreivable.  I would only recomend buying if Your  only a proffessional, do not buy if you were like me and just needed a quick set of blades to throw for amusement, because it could be very frustrating when your first 85 throws bounce off of the targeting board and almost hit you.   (Thats another factor, they bounce back when not thrown correctly so you REALLY have to know what your doing) But the bright side of these knives is THIS.  Once you master these knives, you'll be able tothrow and land OTHER knives that are much easier to use than this LIKE NOTHING. These are probably the BEST PRACTICE KNIVES out there, but NOT FOR FUN QUICK AND EASY INEXPERIENCED ENTERTAINMENT.

product_title: Bushnell 165 Lumen HD Square Beam Flashlight
review_headline: The square beam is a novelty, but this is a sturdy and intensely bright flashlight.
review_body:
While there may well be a practical (possibly tactical) application for the square beam for which I'm simply unfamiliar, I find it to be much more of a novelty. That said, it is certainly nice to know that there's intense light where you want it, no real fade or splash where you don't, with a very thin and nearly binary divide between the two. Perhaps that is, in of itself, the application.

Either way, let's talk about the flashlight itself. It has a heaviness that isn't off-putting, but lends a perception (buoyed by the feel of the metal) of sturdiness and solid construction. Indeed, we accidentally dropped this flashlight 9 feet from a ladder down to a concrete surface (looking around in the crawlspace above our garage) shortly after getting it, and aside from the slightest scratch where it hit, you can't tell that it was dropped -- certainly not in terms of its operability and performance.

If I have a complaint, and it's a small one that may simply speak to my lack of familiarity with this model and brand (as well as my history and familiarity with the Mag-Lite family of lights), it's the on-off process. There's a button on the base of the light (the end exactly opposite the lens). You press that to enable the on/off button located in the typical location on the upper shaft of the the light. This two-step process has already resulted in a situation where we turned off the flashlight on the shaft, but forgot to turn it off at the base, which meant that we had completely drained the (expensive) Lithium Ion batteries dead by the time we next went to use it. Lesson learned, we won't make that mistake again, but the value of a two step process remains lost on me (my best guess is no accidental turn-ons?). Still, it's a minor complaint.

Very happy with it, the above issue notwithstanding. Terrific and intensely bright flashlight.

product_title: Surly Polo Rear Hub Black 48h 135mm Fix/Fix
review_body: To be up front, I haven't used this product. I ride a Surly 1x1 with 32h Surly hubs, and I've been looking around for a higher-spoke 135mm flip-flop hub for a while, to no avail. I'm ecstatic that Surly is making hubs for the polo crowd, considering how many folks in my town play on 1x1s... however, I feel like they really missed the boat with this one, and here's why:  First, no one plays polo fixed. The few holdovers are using track bikes with 120mm dropouts anyway. The only people who buy this hub will do so with the intention of threading a freewheel onto one side, so a fixed/fixed hub is useless for polo.  What about the 48h free/free hub that Surly makes, you say? Still not ideal. Given that polo gears are very very low, to the point of being completely impractical for street use, a flip flop hub can be invaluable for players who have a long ride to the court (or who want to commute and play polo on their SS mtb). However, the cog sizes must be drastically different (5 teeth or more), and thus the rear rim brakes are unlikely to line up properly once the wheel is flipped.  There are a few ungainly solutions to this issue: use a chain tensioner (vulnerable to mallet whacks and crashes), adjust the brakes (ugh), carry a second chain (double ugh), or disconnect the rear brake, assuming you have a front one (I like redundancy when it comes to potentially life-saving components, thanks).   There is one extremely elegant solution: a fixed/free 135mm 48h hub. Disconnect that rear brake and flip your hub. Your polo bike is now your commuter. It's quick and easy and you've still got two brakes. I realize that you could just thread a freewheel onto one side of this hub anyway, but I'm pretty sad that Surly didn't just recognize that fixed/free is going to be a lot more convenient than fixed/fixed or free/free for many polo players. What's the deal, guys?

product_title: Manduka eKO 5mm Eco-Friendly Yoga Mat.
review_headline: Requires a break-in period, but great mat
review_body:
I got this mat about 9 months ago from the Manduka site. I followed their care directions exactly (e.g., leaving the mat open to air out because it is smelly, and I also rinsed it with the 50-50 water-vinegar several times a month). I practice 2-3 times a week, standard home yoga, not Hot Yoga. At first I was frustrated that the mat seemed slippery, especially in down dog and similar poses, but after about two months of use, it has finally become the mat I'd hoped for -- sticky, non-slippery, non-smelly, and non-toxic. It is also a heavier, bulkier mat, so perhaps not ideal for those who travel with their mats, but this is not an issue for me since I only do a home practice.

Thank you Manduka for making an excellent yoga mat. I highly recommend this mat. You just need to be patient and work with the mat's natural properties, and follow the manufacturer's recommendations. Namaste!

Update: after about 18 months, and after I started getting interested in Hot Yoga, I soon realized this mat won't hold up to the hot room. The mat started delaminating with threads coming loose. I emailed Manduka with a description and photos and they were great, gave me a credit towards a new mat and told me that the Eco Mat is not hot-room-tolerant. I did end up ordering one of their black mat pros for hot yoga (which I love), but I still have the Eco Mat for my kids to use when they do yoga with me. Manduka customer service is wonderful.

review_headline: Initially very tight, but loosens up and very good overall quality
review_body:
Underarmour Skull Cap Heatgear

This skull cap is very good at absorbing sweat and is made out of 95% polyester and 5% spandex. I use a Psycleskins beanie under my motorcycle helmet which is 84% polyester and 16% spandex, which in my opinion, is a better material. The Underarmour doesn't breathe as well as the Psycleskins because of the denser and thicker polyester.

In addition, the Underarmour has a very tight and thick elastic headband which makes it uncomfortable to wear over my ears. If I raise it a bit higher to clear my sunglasses/headphones, it can start riding up towards the top of my head. It actually fell off while jogging because it was so tight and kept moving upwards. If the elastic were looser, it would stay put. I wear a size 7.25-7.5 hat, and my motorcycle helmets are usually medium.

Aside from the thicker material and overly tight headband, it's not too bad overall. The price is certainly competitive.

Overall: 4/5 stars, too tight initially, but great at absorbing sweat.

UPDATE: After wearing it a few times, the headband has loosened slightly making it a perfect fit. It is still tighter than my Psycleskins beanie, but it is perfectly usable!

review_body: With all due respect to the above reviewer \\"James A. Holley\\", I couldn't disagree with him more. These rings are in fact very small, but that is by design. However, the rings are significantly larger in their Inside Diameter (ID) than the eye of almost any dry, wet, or nymph flies. It was VERY easy to use these rings on several 4x tippets and their matching leaders. I mainly use Orvis Mirage Fluorocarbon Leader and Tippets, as Nymphing in small streams and tail waters is my primary technique/location. (Approximately 80% of the time)    I have not tried these rings with Dry flies as of yet, but I do not expect to see any issues when I do as these rings do not cause ANY surface disturbance outside of what you would see with just a leader and tippet. With proper dry fly casting techniques, these rings should not be an issue.  One note: After fishing for a period, I did tend to forget about the ring and I occasionally would perform a poor cast resulting in a loose casting knot around the ring (entirely my fault). Very similar to what you would see with sloppy casting when using a strike indicator on the end of your leader. You do need to remember That these rings are there when casting and don't be a slacker like me.  :)

product_title: Uncle Mike's Neoprene Buttstock Shotgun Shell Holder (Black, 5 Loops)
review_body: I picked this up as a cheap way to carry extra shells on my tactical synthetic Remington 870 until I got around to buying and installing a SideSaddle-style shell carrier.  This gets the job done for a good price, but may not fit perfectly or stay put on some stocks.  It is what it is though; an inexpensive shell holder that is easy to install and performs just as advertised.  Pros:  The loops grip the shells tightly; even heavier magnum shells will only start to slide out after multiple hard, intentional jerks of the stock.  They won't come out accidentally in the field unless you're really swinging and jerking your gun around for an extended period of time, and even then, you should notice the slippage long before they have a chance to fall out.  After about a month of continuously holding shells, the elastic showed no indications of weakening.  The loops are also about the right length; long enough to have a good grip on the shell, while still leaving enough exposed to easily grab and extract a 2.75\\" shell.    The sleeve that slides over the stock is thin enough that it won't affect your cheek weld and sighting, though if you're holding your shells on the \\"inside\\" of the stock, you might have issues.  It's inexpensive  Cons:  When I bought mine (not from Amazon), it had an annoying tag sewn into the sleeve.  It was pretty tacky-looking, and was perfectly placed to flap into my sighting eye.  I used some small sharp scissors to remove it, which wasn't too difficult, but required some care and delicacy to completely cut away the tag without snipping any of the sleeve fabric.  On my 870, I had this holder slid down until the back-end was lined up with the joint between the butt of the stock and the recoil pad.  The sleeve was good and tight there, but didn't fit completely on the other end, where the cross-section of the stock was less than the relaxed circumference of the sleeve.  This detracted from the aesthetics of the stock somewhat, but more importantly, tendedto make the sleeve work its way forward.  I especially noticed this after extended shooting sessions in cold weather, while wearing a coat.  My coat sleeve kept pushing the holder forward, until it was up against the grip.  Again, your mileage may vary depending on your gun, but if your stock gets too narrow behind the grip, this holder may not want to stay put for you.  Other Notes:  The sleeve took a little more effort than anticipated to get on.  Afraid of tearing it, I didn't try to force it over the butt end of the stock.  Even with the recoil pad removed, it didn't want to stretch enough.  Depending on your gun, you may be able to slip the holder down from the muzzle end, but I ended up removing the stock to slide it on from the grip end.  I wouldn't really call this a con; worst-case, you'll spend a couple minutes with a screwdriver.  Just be aware that this may not be a simple slide-on-and-off accessory for all guns; install it at home, or at least check the fit before heading out into the field.

review_body: I had this scope for a few months now. I mounted it on an M4-AR15. I found the eye relief rather short (less than 3 inches at 9x). The point of impact changes significantly when changing magnification. I decided to keep it at 9x, and it worked fine for awhile, about 300 rounds. The range adjustment worked fine. A 400 yard shot on a 12x18 inch plate was easy. Then the POI started opening up. I resighted it and then I realized that the recticle was shaking at every shot. At this time I quit. I removed it from the AR and mounted it my heavy barreled 10/22. It's working fine for now with the virtually-recoilless 10/22 but I'm planning to get a better, not cheap, scope- both for the AR and the 10/22.  The red-dot is useless.  The quick-detach mount is practically functional.  Amazon service....EXCELLENT.

product_title: Maxpedition Larkspur Messenger Bag
review_headline: Great messenger bag for on campus use
review_body: I've been using the Larkspur bag while on campus for about a year now and love it. The bag fits me well and I'd say it's more of a medium sized messenger bag (Maxpedition lists it as a small on their website). I have plenty of room in the pockets to carry everything that I need as well as a little bit extra room in case I decide to throw some extra stuff in for the day. The interior hook and loop lining is really nice for mounting the accessory panels that Maxpedition has developed to custom tailor the bag to your uses (I'm using the Admin Insert panel).   There are only a few improvements that I would like on the bag and I'll probably modify my bag to get them. I would like an external Nalgene/water bottle pouch to stow my Nalgene while I'm walking on campus. I can put it on the inside of the bag, but the cold water will create condensation that will destroy my notes and texts. Maxpedition sells a hook and loop Nalgene insert that I'll probably buy and have stitched on the outside of the bag. I would also like to see it come with a padded strap since when you add some books to the bag, it really starts to cut into your shoulder. This isn't a design flaw of the bag, but just the way messenger bags are. I took the shoulder pad off my Maxpedition Versipack and it really improved the shoulder strap. It would also be nice to see some internal padding, but I plan on getting a new 10\\" netbook to put inside a padded sleeve to keep my computer safe. It would also be nice to see Maxpedition make a padded computer sleeve that mounts onto the inside of the bag via hook and loop to secure the case inside your bag.

product_title: Shakespeare Two-Piece Medium Heavy Action Ugly Stik Casting Rod
review_body: I got this rod to match up with my Abu Garcia Ambassadeur 5601 C4 reel.  I got the 2 piece instead of one piece because it is easier to haul it around in the trunk of the car without sticking into the rear passenger compartment.  On the very first trip,  I hooked a 24\\" Ling cod on the 2nd cast.  While trying to bring the Cod in, I hear a snap and look up and my rod had snapped right where the two pieces are connected together!  The graphite just fell apart into many tiny gray strands of fiber.  Luckily the fish was just a few feet away from the boat and we were able to get it onboard.  I tried to contact Shakespeare to get it replaced under their 7 year warranty.  What a joke that warranty is.  They require you to send it back to them at your expense, and then they also require you to send a $9.95 check to cover their shipping the replacement rod back to you.  Given it's a irregular size, it would have cost me $15 to ship it back to them. Add that to the $9.95 they wanted, that's $25 which is more than what I paid for the brand new rod from Amazon ($24).  Luckily I got this less than a month ago from Amazon, and Amazon agreed to send me a replacement free of charge and to also pay for shipping to return the defective unit back to them.  Top notch customer service from Amazon,  Poor warranty from Shakespeare!  I hope the replacement rod won't break as easily and that it was just a random one time occurrence.  People keep telling me ugly stiks are strong and durable.  This is my first ugly stick and so far it hasn't been a good one.  I may just have to go back to abu garcia rods and reels.

product_title: Cardio Club Step
review_body: My husband and I were looking for some aerobics equipment. We've got a small apartment and a young toddler, so we needed something compact without moving parts that could pinch small fingers. After looking at different steps, we chose this one.    As far as cons go, the biggest one is that the black foam isn't applied evenly. This isn't a huge deal by any means, but to the discerning eye, it is noticable. This also means that there's a few tiny little air pockets under there. I understand it's probably a bit difficult to evenly apply a large piece of thin foam, but when it's done wrong, it does make for a minor cosmetic issue.    Another con is the DVD. Watching it gives some good ideas for different steps to try, but following allong, especially at the beginner level, is difficult, just because they go fast without a ton of explanation. The music also reminds me of cheesy 80's workout videos. I'm not into routines and am more interested in just stepping, so I nixed the DVD, found some videos of different techniques on YouTube, and just step to some of my favorite songs instead. So if you could take or leave the DVD, I would say this is a minor con. If you are really interested in having a DVD, Cathe Friedrich does have some videos on YouTube that will allow you to check out her style before buying. It's great for some, but probably not everyone's style.    Another small con -- I use it on carpet, so though I do feel stable, it doesn't always feel 100% solid as if I were using it one a harder surface. No biggie, I still feel safe, and it doesn't wobble or anything like that. This might bug some people, though, so I thought I'd throw it out there.    Now for the pros -- it is very fun, as well as easy to put together. It is also a great size for my needs -- enough stepping surface to try a variety of steps, but it doesn't feel like it clutters my small living room. I also like the color. Though I don't have a ton of grey and black in my apartment, it doesn't clash with my decor quite like the teal and purple ones would. It's also rated fo higher weights than some of the others, so if that's a concern, this one is likely a good choice.    Also, when I'm not using it, my young daughter loves to use it to stack her blocks, line up her stuffed animals, roll toy cars across, crawl on, or do whetever. She thinks it's her special table. Though I know this is not a toy, it is nice knowing that it is safe to have with little ones around.

product_title: Well P-90 Laser Red Dot Airsoft Electric
review_headline: Good gun, but one bad thing.
review_body: I bought this gun and was very excited because it had good reviews and I needed a new gun. When it arrived i opened it up and was not disapointed! The gun is BIG AND SCARY! When I saw the photos I thought I was going to have to crunch up around the gun but it so big I don't have to! But even though it's really big, It's also very light. The accessories are really cool (except the silencer which just gets in the way) and the gun looks way cooler with them. you might want to take off the red dot sight: It's total junk. But the flashlight is really powerful so I actually use it at night. One of the things I really like is it comes with a paper target and mount that saves your BB's so you get a lot more out of each of your BB's.    Pros:  Scary  Comes with target  Good flashlight  shoots hard (OUCH!)  Shoots FAST   LOUD  Light    Cons:  Light   sight and silencer are junk  LOUD (soem people like that, some don't)  Jams    This gun is LOUD! So loud that I use some shotgunning earplugs. You do not want this gun on any stealth missions. Since the gun is gravity-fed, sometimes it jams because the BB's get in the way of each other. Just shake the gun and it should clear up. Just make sure to use .12 gram BB's to reduce jamming. All in All this is a really good gun. I would recommend this to anyone who wants a reliable gun that will last a long time.

review_headline: How to make your slendertone pads last forever
review_body: Before I bought this item, I kept seeing people complain that the pads wore out so quickly.  I saw some people that said that they drenched the pads in rubbing alcohol to make them last longer.  Others online recommended using window cleaner after each use.  And still others said to use water based lubricant.  I tried the rubbing alcohol and window cleaner and that didn't really work well because if you were using a towel to apply the stuff to the pads, the towel would stick and leave residue on the pads.  The water based lubricants would probably be too messy.  After thinking about it some more, I came up with the perfect solution.  I found something that combines all the things everyone else had recommended (or elements of each) in a nice, none messy solution...  so if you want to keep your slendertone pads working for a very, very long time, just use PURELL (OR ANY ALCOHOL BASED HAND SANITIZER) after each use.  Put a couple drops on there, rub it on the pad to cover the surface and then wipe off the excess or just let it dry.  No dripping mess, no towels sticking to the pads and no mess on you either.  Works like a charm and the pads become sticky and work like new each time.  I haven't had to replace any of my pads in months and months.

product_title: Horizon Fitness EX-59 Elliptical Trainer
review_body:
I'm sitting here with sore arms and legs, and a tired butt. I've had this wonderful, horrible thing for one day shy of two weeks, and it's been amazing. I've only missed two days of workouts. I find myself looking forward to getting home from work so I can use the damn thing. I've been burning over 600 calories per session, because I am awesome and amazing at everything. In less than two weeks, I have gone from unforgivable couch potato to a titan of exercise. I am like Zeus on this thing. A Lady Zeus. There is a long line of available and handsome bachelors outside my door at this moment. (That last part is untrue.)

So, like I said, I have used the EX-59 about a dozen times, compared to my husband who has used it zero times and prefers burritos. He is impossible to impress, and even he thinks it's a great machine - from what he has been able to observe. It's whisper quiet, has a decent stride for someone of my height (5'5\\") and feels pretty sturdy. The user interface is basic, but user friendly. It's clearly not a gym quality machine, but it's close.

UPDATE:
It's been a little over a month, and my love affair with the EX-59 continues. My husband was sure it was \\"a future expensive coat rack,\\" but I am victorious and shout \\"IN YO' *FACE*\\" whenever I use the elliptical, whether he is home or not. I have not had the police called on me yet. Since I refuse to weigh myself, I can only estimate that in the one month + four days I've been using this machine I have probably dropped between 7 and 12 pounds. The speaker, while a bit \\"meh\\" (it's a speaker attached to an entry level piece of cardio equipment, right?) is a huge bonus even if most audiophiles will be like, \\"AUGH MY EARS.\\" When you're a 33 year old woman sweating it out to Ke$ha, you really have no cred to stand on.

Here's what I don't get. Why is there a headphone jack on this thing? There's a male headphone plug so you can use the speakers with your ipod, but a separate female headphone plug so you can... listen with headphones? Why not just plug directly in to your ipod? That's like a gorilla wearing a gorilla suit. Maybe I just don't get it.an... listen with headphones? Why not just plug directly in to your ipod? That's like a gorilla wearing a gorilla suit. Maybe I just don't get it.

product_title: Bongo Board
review_headline: Muscle Builder and Lots of Fun
review_body: I'm in my 30s and started getting back into skateboarding at the local skate park  a few months ago after a 20 year hiatus.  I was doing decent enough, but I have problems going in both directions in the same stance confidently ('fakie' for the boarders).  I bought the Bongo Board hoping for more balance, and I was more than pleasantly surprised.  The hardware is very heavy-duty and sturdy.  I'm about 235lbs and my roommate is about 260lbs and it holds both of us fine.    It really does take about 3 days to get comfortable, but the included manual is great.  Since I was skating already, I picked it up faster, but my roommate, who's never skateboarded or done anything like that was grooving after 3 days.  We're still doing it on a carpet since the roll is slower.    After about 4 days of doing it inside on and off during the day, we were so sore in our legs and stomach.  You can immediately feel it in your butt, thighs and stomach if you follow the directions.  We just keep it in the living room and hop on it when the mood hits for a few minutes and it's fun and good exercise.    I cannot wait to see how my skateboarding improves.  I highly recommend this product if you want to build your core strength and are willing to realize that the board is a challenge no matter what your skill.  And it's FUN!!!

product_title: Bushnell Hybrid- GPS/Laser Rangefinder
review_body: Overall a good product.  The built in GPS feature had my regular golf course in it's library, which was a surprise.  A useful tool when I'm in spots where I can't see the flag. (Frequently.)  The laser range finder seems to correlate with the GPS yardages.  I range the flag and then use the GPS to see the yards to front and back of the green.  So far, very accurate.  It has added additional confidence to club selection and made the difference in those \\"in between\\" club yardages.  I read other reviews about the battery and have not had a similar problem.  I received the unit in the mail in the afternoon and let it charge overnight before using.  After one day and two rounds it was reading \\"100%\\".  After day 2 and one round the battery is now reading 90%.  As far as a golf cart charger feature, the mini USB is a common plug.  Pretty sure you could find a cheap cig adapter on line somewhere to solve that issue.  The only downside and it's less a downside and just a programming feature, is that when I use the \\"shot\\" function to measure how far my drive or approach shot went, you cannot menu out of that number without losing your place.  It would be nice to be able to go from your shot distance back and forth to distance to back/front of green etc.  Look out for sales or specials with free shipping that keep the price less than $400.00.

product_title: mini tactical m16 spring rifle, m203 spring grenade launcher, fps-200 fore grip, flashlight, airsoft gun(Airsoft Gun)
review_headline: Looks aren't Enough to save you.
review_body:
This Rifle Is Definitely 'Mini' If I Ever Felt It In My Hands, When I got it from my doorstep I Had my doubts about how it could be so small for a decent sized box.
well upon opening, it STILL Looked Kinda Big! Now, When I Held it is when the size really showed. it's The Lightest Airsoft gun I Ever Held, Weighing Less Than My Cell Phone, And Measuring Longer Than The Described 24 Inches. (Which Is A GOOD Thing)

Now, About The Performance And Quality.

The Magazine Works Like The Bigger Cousins, It opens in the bottom, so you can add ammo in there and then lower the spring to refill it.
Which WOULD Be Nice, If All The BB's Didn't Come Spilling Out of The Top Loading Notch.

The BARREL Of The Gun, Which is VITAL to aiming it, is BENT! That's Right.. BENT!! A Huge Killer for Airsoft guns.
Cocking The Gun Is Difficult And Cumbersome,I Feel As If I May Break it every time i try to do so.

The M203 Grenade Launcher Deserves Merits For Looking Interesting and Fearsome, As it is Full Size and looks and feels Odd and Over-sized On This Small Rifle And In case you are wondering, No, It Does Not Function AT ALL.

I conclude that It Looks Like a Scaled down model of a real m16 with a M203 attached. it may intimidate others in looks, but it's lethargic and handicapped performance Will leave you feeling a stinging regret.
I Do Not Recommend This To Anyone.

review_headline: Benjamin Trail NP XL Air Rifle air rifle 1100
review_body: Have had this gun for about six months now. The first one that was sent I had to return. The barrel was so crooked that the scope would not line up. Have seen this a lot in the reviews. Very nice gun very poor workmanship. Get a clue Crosman.

product_title: CYMA CM030 Airsoft Electric Pistol Metal Gearbox AEP
review_body:
*NOTE*: The information in this review is outdated as of 2012. Varying circumstances have affected the availability of this AEP, and thus the price.

First off, it must be stated that this is one of, if not THE best under $100 AEP's available, being cloned off the formidable (And expensive) Tokyo Marui g18. However, this gun was available for around $30 two years ago.

After rumors spread of its great (For a knockoff) performance, most retailers went out of stock... Until CYMA released more, at a higher price. $60-$90 is ridiculous for an off-brand clone, no matter its performance. At anything over $50, you'd be better off saving up to buy the real AEP these cheap clones are based off of. Even if this is the best cheap AEP around, you simply are not getting the value for your money as you would with the real Tokyo Marui g18, which is of superior quality in terms of materials and performance. (After a few hundred rounds, the materials in most cheap clones deteriorate, being made of cheap plastic.)

Wait for the price to drop or shop around for used/upgraded ones.

Note for new players:
-Spring pistols are almost universally garbage and definitely not for field play.
Anything over $20 for spring pistols is a ripoff.
-Almost all under $100 airsoft pistols and rifles available on Amazon are cheap clones of better brands that are designed to work for a few shots then fall apart in your hands. None are worth the price, even as just props for filming. (The low grade plastic is often glossy, there are easily visible \\"MADE IN CHINA\\" marks on most, and all will fall to pieces if not handled as if they are made of glass.)

This has been a Public Service Announcement.

product_title: Calypso Mako 6 SEC Telescopic Spin Rod
review_body: I recently purchased Mako 8' and 7' telescopic rods for my wife and me. We got them for surf fishing in Maui. We had read about the fishing there and wanted to give it a try. We were basically pleased with the rods. Their most pronounced strength is that they collapse for transport. They easily fit inside a large piece of luggage . . . and the plastic case provides adequate protection. These rods are pretty strong and adequate for fish up to 25-30 pounds. They're probably about as good as a telescoping rod can be. But any telescoping rod by nature is compromised and doesn't function like a good 2- or 3-piece surf rod. Because of the telescoping aspect, the reel seat is too close to the rod butt; this makes casting laborious and retrieving tiring. The guides are basically hybrid: larger than those of a bait-casting rod and much smaller than a normal spinning rod. When used with a medium-weight spinning reel, the small size of the guides reduces casting distance.  I give these rods a marginal recommendation. They function pretty well for what they are. If you're traveling to Hawaii and want to enjoy the surf fishing, consider packing your salt-water reel and purchasing a cheap rod one at of the island Walmarts. Then leave it at the hotel or condo when you leave. Better yet, there will be lots of local fishermen on the beaches around sunrise or sunset that would love to have it.  Don't even dream about landing the legendary ulua (giant trevally) with this rod; no chance!

review_body:
This is my second time to buy this product. The first time was last year and I used it all season. This is a really good product for the price.

Assembly was a snap (all of my holes lined up without any issue!). Don't forget to install your straps as you assemble the unit. You don't want to be trying to do that as you strap the ladder to the tree!

Installation is pretty easy as tree ladders go. Assembly it on the ground and just stand it up. Start strapping it off at the bottom and work your way up. Don't forget your full body harness! Never install or use any ladder stand without 100% tie-off!!! More hunters are hurt or killed falling from trees than any other way. Safety first, and maybe you'll get to hunt again!

One thing I really do like about this ladder is that the pin joints are flexible enough to allow for slight changes in direction. I have yet to find the perfect tree in the perfect hunting spot. That slight flexibility makes installing this ladder easier.

Thanks for a great product!

Bowkilla

review_body: These were cute.  The came just as they appear here.  They are pretty sturdy and look like they will last a while.  I am happy with this purchase.

product_title: Molten Digital Air Pressure Pump and Gauge
review_headline: Good Gauge and Built-in Manual Pump - Excellent for Volleyball
review_body: This is a good gauge that seems to be very accurate.    The built-in pump works very well for adding a bit of air when the ball is under-inflated.    It runs on a big watch-style battery.  I find that it needs to be replaced one time per year, but these batteries are only a couple dollars each.    To be sure, it is a manual pump.  I would not want to use this pump on a completely deflated ball, but it works great to add a little bit of air.  Given the small size and the small battery, it would be a little optimistic to think it has an automatic air pump.    For volleyball, it works great.  4.3-4.6 is the required psi for volleyball.  Those \\"analog\\" pumps with a range of up to 20-30 psi make me much more skeptical abouttime accuracy within the required VB range.

review_body: I love the versatility and ease of use of the ProForm Power 995. The only thing I see issue with....and it could be something I am not doing right, is the pulse taker. product_title: Crosman C31 air pistol
review_body: This is my 3 bb gun and first CO2 bb gun and I like it a lot. Im not in love with it because I don't like the hard trigger pull that lowers the accuracy in target practice. I don't hunt I shoot targets and it took me a while to start hitting bulls eye. This gun is powerful and should be used with caution and respect. I made my own target box made out of regular box, cut A4 size hole from one side to attach the sheet of paper with big and smaller circular targets and taped from all sides with masking tape and lined with 2 inch foam cushion on the back of the box to stop the bb's from getting out. The first shot I did was from 25 yards and I can barely see the target but the bb went through the paper target like a knife in butter but i didn't check the back of the box to see if the bb went out. Then I moved closer to 8 yards and start shooting. My target box was on a latter infront of a garage door made out of wood. When I finish the first magazine I checked the box and I saw that the bb's went through the box and half way into the garage wooden door. With my previous all metal blowback bb gun I never had even a single bb lodged in the cushion and this one ripped not only the target and the cushion but the 10 additional target sheets of paper I put in a pouch behind the box and the bb's made dings in the wooden door that was 3 feet away from the box. WOW.

review_body: I am very pleased with the seat.  The only down side was that the bottom box was a little shorter than the seat I was replacing. Made it a little shorter but other than that its a great seat. Wish they would of had the dimensions for the bottom box and option for a taller box.

review_body: Good- The shirt fits great and is very comfortable.  Also it was shipped very fast.  Bad- The New york emblem is about half the size of the one in the picture. Also it is more see-thru then I thought it would be.

product_title: Spyderco HoneyBee SS PlainEdge Knife
review_body: I have many pocket knives, including a good number made by Spyderco.  I was skeptical about what reviews said here about the quality of this knife but now I get it because I bought one and have been using it.  Very well made and machined.  Tight tolerances, very nicely honed edge, apparently pretty decent steel (I can tell by how it slides on crock sticks to edge it).  It's also a pretty decent sized knife.  It does NOT lock, like most Spydercos but that is partly the idea as I understand it from their website.  This is a knife that is more \\"legal\\" to carry with you (sort of a super sharp, very pointy pen knife) in places where there are issues about lockbacks (UK, New York, etc.)  I highly recommend this and I will be getting a number of them as gifts for friends.  I do not know how they can produce and sell this for 9 bucks.

product_title: Nanospeed 200
review_body: Great racquet for intermediate level players; good value for the price too. As another reviewer mentioned, it only comes with 3/4 length cover, which is a little cheap. review_body: Great little target although it's much bigger than I thought it would be. Great for plinking with a 22 or small caliber handgun. Haven't tried anything in a larger caliber yet.

product_title: The Biggest Loser 55cm Core Advantage Stability Ball (Orange)
review_body:
This is an excellent product! The ball is very well made and not slippery like many others on the market. I gave it 4 stars because the ball is advertised as being orange in color, but is actually very yellow. The hand pump that comes with the ball works well and better than any other I've seen for these balls (other than a power operated air pump.) Your arms will get a good workout while filling your ball! Finally, and most importantly, the ball actually keeps its air instead of leaking out slowly over time (like evey other one I've bought)!!

The kit also comes with a useful guide for the ball, a resistance band, and a jump rope. The jump rope that came with the kit is not the best. It is black rubbery and slippery. I ended up purchasing a better jump rope elsewhere. The resistance band is very stretchy and I do not use it often because I already own some better products.

Overall, this kit is worth purchasing for the ball and pump alone. It would be a very good starter kit for someone looking for some basic workout tools.

product_title: Elixir Arm Cooler Cooling Sleeves UV Protective Compression Arm Sleeves, 1 Pair, Various Color Available
review_headline: TOO SNUG for athletic/large arms, Nice material.
review_body: The Pros:   Nicely made, of 4-way stretchy nylon-type material [fabric weight falls inbetween a man's fine dress sock and a woman's stocking].      The \\"elbow\\" area of the sleeve is indeed knitted differently from the rest of the sleeve, though I don't know how much that contributes to the fit.      It is comfortable to wear, and it does seem to block sunrays [I also use sunblock on my arms].    The packaging is bi-lingual, though there are only a few words of English.    The Cons:  Too snug for athletic or big arms.  My arms measure about 8 1/2 inches at the wrist, about 13 1/2 ins. at the forearm just below the elbow, and about 15 1/2 inches near the bicep.  These sleeves are just too snug [too tightly fitting] to wear comfortably above the elbow.  I've been wearing them just on the forearm for cycling; the fit is still snug, but not uncomfortable [I let the excess material fold over at the wrist].    Overall: Nice, well-sewn affordable arm sleeves, but watch the FIT...this is \\"one size fits most/many\\" but NOT ALL.

product_title: Zumba Exhilarate Body Shaping System DVD Set
review_headline: AWESOME!! Got me off my bum again!
review_body: I spent 3 years eating anything I wanted and NO workout. Finally I thought SOMETHING has to be done- I do not want to end up with diabetes or something at a young age! So FIRST I did sign up for Weight Watchers and after getting a bit more used to my new eating habits decided OK time to workout. The treadmill did NOT look appealing and the stepper I bought so I could \\"exercise while I watched TV\\" just sat there too. SO one day I was bored and was flipping through channels when I saw the ZUMBA EXHILARATE infomercial. My mom had the very first Zumba DVDs which she seemed to enjoy but really were not for me. I saw this infomercial and for some reason just HAD to buy these. I was nervous cuz I have actually done that before- I bought winsor pilates and the beach body dvds off TV too and did each maybe twice and blah was bored. This came in the mail and after spending nearly $100 I said OK HAVE TO DO THIS. Well I was instantly HOOKED!!!!!! I stated with STEP BY STEP as the Beginner's Plan tells you to do and WOW I think Gina and Tanya are GREAT! The DVD has a feature where you can see the steps from the front and from the back so you can learn more easily. They are really good teachers and have such a fun and positive attitude while not being annoying or cheesy like some \\"aerobic teacher\\" from the 80s or something would be. 2 days later I did Activate and AGAIN love it!!! I LOVE that song MENEA MENEA! It is so infectious and fun!!! Makes u feel all cool when you do the steps lol the rest of the songs are awesome too- totally fun and great beats. At first I was disappointed because for some reason I thought the songs for Zumba would be those you hear from artists on the radio. They are not but in my opinion are actually much better!   In some workouts you keep watching the clock but with this by the time I remember to look there is only a few minutes left :-D I think that yeah sometimes the queuing catches you off guard but once you have done the DVDs more times you get familiar with the steps and routine and you feel like you are part of a dance team or something- all coordinated and stuff :) The MIX DVD is awesome too! SOOO cool how those guest dancers come on and do some amazing stuff that you can do too after you have gone through all the DVDs or hey even before! -Makes you feel great! I won't lie it DOES feel like a workout not just dancing but it really IS so much fun! I end up pouring sweat after each DVD and it just feels great!!! When I wasn't working out my highest loss at weigh in for Weight watchers was like 1.8 lbs with working out it was 3.4 lbs in one week! and I ate pizza and went to this place I love that has awesome Margaritas etc and everything. I know that would not have happened were it not for the workout- I probably would have lost very little or stayed the same for that week (based on previous experience!). I DO however recommend getting dance sneakers for this. I was working out on pergo floor with just running sneakers and my knee hurt! So I ordered the BLOCH dancing sneaker avail here on Amazon and NO MORE knee problems. Also it helps so that you can slide more easily into the steps without slipping entirely or sticking to the floor -makes the workout even more fun :-D  I do think having SOME background in dancing will help you though. But it doesn't have to be latin beats- if you line dance etc or have ever learned steps after watching someone patiently teach you, then you can totally do this :) Just play the Step By Step DVD until you get it (it's a workout too!)- you totally will get it they explain it very well! IN SHORT: LOVE THIS!!!!! TRY IT!!!

review_body: I've used the canoe loader several times and it works exactly as described.  I was so totally able to easily load the canoe onto the top of my sedan ALL by myself. product_title: Carson Optical MagniFlex Hands Free Tabletop Mounted Magnifier (CL-65)
review_body: The lens of this magnifier is made of cheep plastic and scratches easily. The clamp that attaches to a shelf has a post that's made of plastic or soft metal and that's  where the magnifier attaches itself to. After three months of use I was pulling the magnifier over to me and the post sheared off making the magnifier totally useless. product_title: spring heavy weight 1911 pistol airsoft gun yt385 fps-240(Airsoft Gun)
review_body: I bought this gun before a ww2 airborne display, and picked it up, smacked the magazine in, cocked it forward and said to myself \\"did i just order a real .45?\\" of course i didn't actually think that but the realism is just so amazing. i popped it in my m3 shoulder holster, fit like the holster was tailored for the gun. i read other reviews about it breaking when firing, and decided i wasn't gonna shoot it, mostly because i had no use to, it was just for me to display. i got asked so many times if it was real (i of course cocked it back and spray painted the barrel. all in all, a great display piece, but from what i have heard, not so good for shooting. Great for your kids to play army with or for reenactors looking for a cheap colt to set in your holster or take into the field for looks so you dont carry around your $6,000 actual 1911 .45 around.

product_title: Galco Tuck-N-Go Inside The Pant Holster for Springfield XD 9/40 3-Inch (Natural, Right-hand)
review_headline: Works without "super" comfort - but still works
review_body: Gun: Springfield Armory .40 Subcompact XD  Purpose: Conceal Carry in any clothing  Build: 6'3\\" Male    There's the background information you need I suppose, but this thing does exactly what it's intended to do. In trying to be super \\"discrete\\" they give you a very small and flimsy belt attachment, I don't suppose this thing will last years, but hey for the price I'm just looking to get enough out of it till my Crossbreed gets made!     Logistics: It's an in the waistband holster specifically designed to be used with a belt, and to be used in about a 2:15 position on your body. My personal preference is around 4-4:30, which it works for just not as well. Initially the gun is pretty stiff going in and out of the holster, going in much more so than coming out. I imagine within time as with all leathers, this too will loosen up, so no negative strikes there in the long run.     If you're looking for a temporary fix till you get your custom IWB holster made from one of the great creators of concealed comfort (Crossbreed, Theis, etc) this will do the job just fine! Use some pants that are around an inch too large, where a comfortable heavy duty belt, and use your shirt as needed to cover. Amazon Prime pretty much sold me on this the second I saw it for my needs. Solid 4 stars.

Pockets are perfect, they dont get in the way, and are easy enough to access...

eVent is an amazing material, I have been a GoreTex fan all my life, and I have to say that eVent has finally replaced the traditional GoreTex garments for me. If you need proof look at this information from the military:
[...]

product_title: Suunto Wrist-Top Computer Watch Replacement Strap Kit (Vector, Altimax. Mariner, Regatta, D3; Black Neoprene)
review_body: The wrist band came with all the accessories as promised and installed without a problem.  The shipping was timely.    My real issue is with the Velcro.  After the first week the looped side barley holds so now as I'm swimming or doing anything under water it continually unfastens and leaves the watch extremely loose on my wrist.      Its the looped side that is having issues and not the fuzzy side so I'm thinking of having a new section of looped side Velcro sewn on.  A much stronger and durable piece that will hopefully last much longer.    If you only need the parts then the kit is great but if your hoping to use the wrist band be prepared for a Velcro upgrade.    Aside from the Velcro issue the only other problem is that since its a cloth fabric it tends to smell funky after washing your hands several times a day without washing the band.  I end up taking the watch off after getting it wet until it dries and washing it 2-3 times a week.

product_title: Schwinn 240 Recumbent Exercise Bike
review_body: Best investment I've made in a while. I'm waiting for hip replacement surgery and I needed to do something to keep my leg muscles from crapping out on me.  We have an old Schwinn exercise bike in the basement but I have yet to find a regular bike seat that doesn't feel like it's going up my wazoo...it's torture, and I just have a hard time exiling myself to the basement to exercise.  This bike has the tractor seat and it's extremely comfortable.    I'm not even concerned about the warranty because Schwinn has been making a great quality product for many years.

product_title: Glacier Glove Synthetic Leather Palm Gray Sunglove

The bad:   - The grey color (the only color available) makes your hands look like zombie hands... and that's not cute....  :-P    I like the functionality of the gloves but I wish there were more colors, maybe some cute, fun colors...?

product_title: The Original McKenzie Lumbar Roll by OPTP - Low Back Support for Office Chairs and Car Seats
review_body: This back roll definitely does the trick for my lower back pain due to degenerative arthritis. I bought two, one for work and the other for my favorite recliner.  They strap on to the chairs and stay in place.  The material is soft to the touch and does well in the heat.

product_title: Hoppe's No. 9 Universal Field Cleaning Kit
review_body: I had to purchase the Hoppe's Boresnake seperately because i own a 40cal S&W chambered handgun... Sadly (and oddly) their kits that are very similar to this one don't come for the 40cal size. I would recommend this kit and buy the Boresnake seperately. It's got plenty of room for all the basics. I purchased the Boresnake and shoved it into the bottom pouch (the item picture has wipes sticking out of the pouch). Behind the oils there is another pouch, I moved the rods, handle, and pieces to that back pocket and placed a Hoppe's Nylon Utility Brush in the middle slot (where the rods are shown being stored in the product picture). I just put the wipes into a small ziplock bag and laid them flat on top of the oils, and then I even bought an oil wipe/cloth and placed that in it's bag on top of the wipes that came with it. It still folds up and stays closed with no problems (obviously fuller looking, and stuffed). But it holds it all, and that is basically all you need. It's small, and great for when you travel. If your going to shoot and not going home to clean it, your looking at the perfect thing. I camp and hunt on the weekends and sometimes go out of state, this is perfect. Just need to spend a few extra bucks on the other things and your set! I'd recommend this.

product_title: Smooth Fitness 5.65 Treadmill (2014 Model)
review_body: I purchased the 5.65 in Nov 2010. I selected the inhouse delivery due to the weight of the package.  It was delivered right to my bedroom and although it took me awhile to get it set up I was able to do it without any help.  I primarily wanted it for use during the winter months and during the real hot months of summer.  I have not experienced any problems with it in the last 8 months and I'm very pleased with it's operation. My wife and I only use it for walking so can't really comment on its performance during a jogging session. I have it set up in a small bedroom and really like the fold up feature that provides more space.  This is my first treadmill purchase and I am very satisified with it.

product_title: TYR Youth Flexframe Youth Goggle
review_body: I bought these goggles to see if they would work better for my son than his Speedo goggles which leaked constantly.  He's a very small 5 year old and these definitely fit better. Both my five and six year old say these are more comfortable than the Speedo goggles and they are certainly easier to find at the pool when they put them down since they are less common. My daughter has had Tyr goggles in the past and they do seem to tear more easily. I think the straps are softer, so I am careful when adjusting them.

product_title: Orvis Insulated Blackout Liner / Only 88"l, Each
review_headline: Great blackout liners for grommets- a little too long
review_body: These were the only blackout liners that I could find that would work easily with my new grommet drapes.  And they do!  They are easy to install and they do work at blocking out light and heat.  They don't come in extra wide width so I had to put two of these liners behind one of my extra wide curtain panels and to fix the gap in between, I just hot-glued them together!  I also hot glued the hem to make them the right length.  In the future, if I get longer drapes, I can just let out the hem and voila!

product_title: 50 X 25 Fish Net, fishing Nets for Golf, Backstop, Hockey, Netting, Baseball, Sports, La crosse
review_body: Works great for a Lacrosse backstop!  I used four large PVC poles (1\\"id x 10') and some para-cord to make a great backstop.  Design tip: Be sure to lay out the net on the ground before hanging it; otherwise it can easily get pulled into a non-symmetrical shape.  Trim down 1\\" wooden doweling to make a spikes for the base of the poles (Just to keep it from slipping.  It doesn't need to be very deep).  Trim down the dowel so that it is snug in the PVC, but not water tight (you'll want rain water, etc that gets into the pipe to drain down to the ground).  Run a line of para-cord all the way across the top of the net (This is important!), and then use zip ties to fasten the poles to the net with one pole at each short end and the two others evenly spaced in the middle.  With some help, set the poles in the ground and string adjustable guy wires (two on each end and then one each on the backside of the middle poles).  The net can be tensioned across the top using the wire that was laced into the net earlier (otherwise it will have large low spots between the poles).  The net should hang down to the ground (with ample overlap) and provide a resilient stop to even the most aggressive shooters.  Have fun!

Maybe they didn't appreciate caustic sweat from a few sticky hot days when every garment I wore looked like I'd marched through a garden sprinkler. Who knows?  I just know the wrists got floppy after a while.    The gloves finally died just about on their second birthday.  The stitching on the right thumb pulled out, and a day or two later I pushed my left thumb through the tip. I don't really hold their demise against them.  I was pretty hard on them. It's not their fault they were intended for a slightly more gentle life than the one I gave them.

product_title: Daiwa Minisystem Minicast Ultra-Compact Spincast Reel and Rod Combo in Hard Carry Case
review_headline: Satisfied with mine for nearly 30 years...
review_body: I first got my mini-cast spin-casting combo in the early 1980s and it's still going strong.    The key to satisfaction with any type of fishing rod and reel is to match its type to the job at hand.    For example, this \\"smaller than ultra-light\\" Daiwa Mini-Cast is NOT for inexperienced fishermen (who mainly know two things:  (1) Throw out a baited hook, and (2) Reel them in).    The lightweight rod is well matched to the 4 lb. test line that comes with the unit, but one should never \\"lift\\" out a fish using this ultralight type of rod, even with a little ol' 2 lb. bass.    The fish must be played until its fight is gone, then lifted out of the water by hand, or with a gaff or net.    I found the (supplied) 4 lb. test line well suited to this rod and reel, so I started with that.    With 4 lb. test, I have hauled plenty of 30-inch carp out of tidewater rivers, after fighting them for up to 30 minutes.    Why go for a lightweight rig?  Well, for starters, when fishing for trout or for smaller panfish, a lightweight rig can cast 1/16 oz. spinners and small jigs way farther out than stiffer eight-to-twelve pound line of the bigger rigs.    Secondly, the spin-casting method offers the unbeatable certitude of cast when night fishing, especially in woods-lined fishing waters where darkness and obstacles are maximal.    Third, in the dark, in cases of slack line (where most of your tangles occur in open-faced spinning reels), the enclosed bobbin spin-cast reel definitely shines for avoiding tangles.    Fourth, the simpler action of a push-button release is something that can be \\"muscle-memorized\\" even with your eyes closed, for a good cast without even seeing what you're doing--great for night-time work.    The best thing though, is the sensitivity of the ultra-light equipment when fishing for the pan, for such delectables as bream and other sunfish with their lady-like touch and pinky-finger sized mouth opening.  Setting the hook is far more sure--you can \\"feel\\" the slightest nibble right through the line to your rod hand.    Some things to remember are to set any drag pretty light with this reel, and \\"pump the rod\\" to play the fish, using the crank only to take up the slack when you've pumped 'em a few feet closer.    You'll easily feel when they run out of gas; at that time you can reel them close, but DON'T lift them from the water:  Either grab them with your hand, with a gaff hook or use a net.  The rod's not intended to take that kind of stress.    N.B.: Don't be sticking your fingers into a trout, pickeral or other toothy fish's mouth, but bass and other soft-mouthed fish can be grabbed by sticking your thumb into their mouth and grabbing their lower jaw.  Likewise, if you think you may toss back the fish you've caught, don't gaff them through the body or gill.  Hook them through the lower jaw; they'll thrive when released.    If you're going light, you won't carry a shovel for digging worms, so remember to stock a few small-sized flies on a felt, plus three small jigs (black-bluegill; yellow-crappie; red-bass), a popper or two, a gold-and-goldfeather Panther Martin spinner 1/16th oz. or smaller and maybe just one 1/8 to 1/4-oz. crankbait plug like the Rat-L-Trap shad or crawfish with \\"blood\\" marks).    Carry a few split shot sinkers and the smallest foam-type bobber you can find and now you have a total fishing rig for all \\"emergencies\\" at a reasonable price.  All this extra stuff can be carried in the compartments of the set.    Remember:  Point the rod toward the fighting fish when they jerk and run, to spare the line guides and rod, then pull them back gently to fight them closer.  THEN take up the slack with the reel as needed.    Doing things right with ultralights makes fishing a blast and extends equipment durability.

review_body: This is a decent reel from Abu Garcia... excellent build quality though the anti-backlash is less effective than I've seen in much cheaper reels. Rod is OK but much too stiff in the tip; normally you'd find a light action tip on a medium action rod, not so here. Recommend pairing this reel with a better rod; I simply mounted it on an older (and cheaper!) Shakespeare Ugly Stick with much better action.     The packaging though... this was the worst Amazon packaging job that I've seen yet and that's saying something! Rod was simply dumped into a long, soft cardboard box made from two golf club shipping boxes taped together. No protective materials of any kind, and two of the line guides on the rod were badly bent. Thought about returning it but since I discarded the rod anyway I let it go. How tough would it have been to simply use a hard cardboard tube for packaging?

product_title: MLB New York Yankees 3-by-5 foot Pinstripes Flag
review_headline: A great flag for the price - 2016 Update
review_body:
I fly this flag, along with my American flag, on a lighted pole next to my garage and driveway. And yes, it is mounted lower than the stars and stripes. I bought another one for our daughter as a present as she's a pure Yankee fan. My only negative comment is that I wish that it was double-sided with the same quality imprint. If you're going to fly it static, then pick the best side to face outward. It's not a huge drawback. Now that it's flown with dignity through Hurricane Irene (and without the slightest issue to material or print), I can't really tell the difference from one side to the other. Still looks great after the pole it rests on was bending in the wind!

Update - December 2016: Since this review I'm on my 3rd flag and I should have done this update a while ago. The overall integrity of the flag is fine except for the bottom stitching. I've replaced with like kind because I've not found another one of the same quality as my American flag that withstands just about anything. This will be the last replacement without taking the new flag to the local tailor and have a robust stitched bottom applied. The stitching fails rather soon and the flag has to be cut to get rid of all of the ragged pieces of flapping fabric. I should have learned my lesson two flags ago and fixed it from the start. Since it's not been a very big investment, I didn't take care of it from the start. That won't happen again because other than that, the flag is perfect and hold together quite well on the mast through all sorts of weather.

product_title: Swimovate Poolmate Pro Sports Watch, Black
review_headline: Better than Swimsense, but still not good enough
review_body:
I have both the Finis Swimsense and Pool Mate watches. Both are pretty lousy. Swimsense is the worse of the two, because it is very inaccurate at measuring strokes. Sometimes, when I made 20 strokes, that watch would only count 4 strokes. Where are the other 16 strokes???

Furthermore, it would incorrectly register my butterfly strokes as freestyle strokes. In fact, it has never once detected my butterfly strokes, after 7 uses, with more than 5 or 6 tries each times. Thus, out of 35 - 42 attempts, it has never once registered a butterfly stroke.

Poolmate does a good job of keeping the stroke counts correctly.

On the software matters, Swimsense provides a the better software than the Poolmate, which consistently crashed my Mac Book Pro.

Hence, out of the two watches, I discourage people buying either one.

Conclusion:
Swimsense - miss-counts strokes and distances, e.g. 4 for 16 strokes, 25 yards for 50 yards. Cannot detect Butterfly strokes from Freestyle. Requires frequent recharge.
Poolmate - It software crashes my Mac Book Pro. Makes no effort at detecting stroke types. But, it does a decent job of keeping strokes. And, it does not need to recharge.

If you take training seriously, go get a swimming coach. Right now, the technology is not there yet to replace the real thing - people.
