review_body: I was looking for a vertical foregrip for my AR-15.  I wanted something lightweight, short, and with enough diameter to give a good strong hold in my hand.  This Tapco intrafuse grip fits that bill perfectly.  I love this grip.  It is grippy enough to feel like it's not going to slip, but it's short enough to stay out of the way and not get snagged on stuff as some other \\"broom handle\\" type foregrips seem to.  My only gripe with this grip is the single screw attachment.  It feels firmly attached and I have had no trouble with it, but I feel like two screws to attach the grip to the picatinny rail would feel somehow more durable than the single one they have.  Like I said, no real problems encountered and the thing feels well-secured, but that would give me more confidence in the picatinny interface.  Otherwise, it's a great, simple piece of gear and the price here on Amazon is going to be tough to beat, I think.

product_title: Asics Men's Core Short Sleeve Top
review_body: I bought these shirts to use as an undershirt for my job, where I wear a lot of police related gear over it and need to stay as dry as possible in the heat. The material is very nice and the feel is excellent.  I normally wear a 2XL T-shirt so I had a difficult time deciding which size to order.  I went with XL which would have been perfect if I just wanted to wear this shirt to exercise in. This shirt failed me through no fault of its own on how the neck fits as its meant to be a runners shirt.  Once all of my gear was on, the collar bunched up and I got the \\"bacon\\" collar which made it look and feel strange. I have never had to make a return to Amazon, but it appears these will be heading back.  I ordered Large shirts which I am waiting for them to arrive to see if this fixes my collar issue.  I would recommend that if you order these shirts, to order a size smaller than what you normally wear unless you want a REALLY loose fit.  The price is excellent as well, where I paid half of what similar Under Armour or Nike Dri Fit shirts would cost ($12 a shirt).  Asics does not break tradition in the quality of their product as I only buy Asics running shoes as well.

product_title: Mir® - F.A.I. (Vest Only.) Weight Vest
review_body: I bought this vest on doctor's orders to wear a weighted vest and walk wearing it 2-3 times a week to try and reverse my osteopenia. I'm 70, 5'41/2\\" and weigh 120. I read the reviews on the vest, looked at the picture and thought it would work beautifully, since it was smaller than other vests and would hold more than enough weight for my needs (5-10 lbs.) As other reviewers wrote, it is sturdy and well made. What I didn't take into account was the size of the model and myself. It looked small on him, but it was BIG on me! It interfered with arm movement because it extended over my chest and beyond. It is sturdy because it is made with stiff, heavy material so it isn't pliable. Worse part was the recommendation that a buddy help with fitting it, because the velcro fastener winds around to the back. I live alone and needed something I could just put on at the gym and walk the track for 3 miles. I decided to return it since it wouldn't fit my needs. When I called the company, they gave me clear instructions on returning it and I received prompt refund minus my shipping costs both ways. For the serious weight trainer this would be a great product but not for women! I ended up buying a Gold's Gym vest with 20 1-lb weights to insert in its 20 pockets. It has the added benefit of a pocket for my iPod. Needless to say I only have 4 lbs in it at the moment but hope to increase it in the future. The vest is much larger but it is adjustable, zips up the front and is pliable so that it molds to my body and doesn't interfere with arm movement. However I did have another gym member wryly comment that I looked like a suicide bomber! I subtracted one star simply because I think it should carry a recommendation regarding size and perhaps best for use by men.

review_body: I'm a relatively new golfing enthusiast and I shopped around looking for a putting green that would help me develop a smoother stroke.  I bought this one based on the amount of 5-star ratings and I have not been disappointed.  It layed flat right out of the box with no creases or lumps.  The shallow holes on each side have helped me in developing that stroke i was looking for.  The slight incline even creates a small amount of break to take into account if you are putting at the outside holes from left to right or right to left.  Overall, I'm very satisfied with my purchase and would recommend this product to anyone looking for something to practice with at home.

product_title: Altus Athletic Altus Turbo Tower
review_body: The Turbo Tower took me all of about twelve minutes to assemble and, when finished, was about 3 feet X 3 feet at the base and roughly 5 feet in height.  Although my six-year-old son and 7.5-year-old daughter hung and climbed on the main exercise bar without issue, my first go at push-ups caused the bar to slip out of its \\"pinned\\" location.  (My second and third tries, however, were fine and the bar stayed locked, so I can't say if it was user error or not, but that first experience did give me a bit of a scare.)  I used the hanging handles to do some sort of pull-up exercise and everything went well.  While I don't have any weights, the tower comes with easily adjusted bar supports (you just pull them out and insert them at the desired height).  The main exercise bar itself is also easy to adjust, requiring only that you simultaneously lift two locking mechanisms, lower/raise the bar and then release the locks.  While the tower is a bit wobbly, it's not objectionable or cause for concern.  I've used professional stuff that does the same thing.  All in all, a pretty good piece of work out equipment.

product_title: Proform 585 CS Treadmill
review_body: After extensive research on budget-priced treadmill, I opted for the ProForm 585 CS for $499.99 with free shipping and a 10% off coupon (which off-set the cost of an extended warranty, recommended by nearly every source I consulted). I am pleased with my purchase.    I use this treadmill to run a few days per week. When I purchased this item, I gave up my gym membership and so far have no regrets.    It is sturdy, has speakers for a music player, and 1-button speed and incline control. Very easy to use, and comfortable to run on. The motor seems to be more than adequate, and has so far stood up to multiple runners of varying weights and sizes.     Only cons are that it came damaged (not enough to return) and that it was cumbersome to assemble, but well worth it in the end.     HIGHLY recommended for a treadmill under $500. I took a gamble on this, not being able to try it in person, but it far surpasses the performance of similarly-priced treadmills I found at the big box stores, including other Icon/Nordictrack/ProForm products.

product_title: CFF Heavy Knurled Vise Supper Gripper Hand Grip & Forearm Strengthener; Great for  Cross Training MMA Boxing
review_headline: Would not buy again due to quality
review_body: Problems I have with it are the build quality. It is obvious a poor cast of an Ivanko or Woody gripper that had the handles cut down unevenly prior to casting. After casting the knurled grips were put on. The knurled grips are overkill for this. They will cut up your fingers. If finger or hand slipping were a problem I would say wrap the handles with athletic tape or chalk your hands. The knurled hand grips are a bad attempt at trying to be like the CoC individual grippers which also cut your hands. The pin that holds the two pieces together is just that a pin. I expect it to break over time nor do I expect it to hold up to the full amount of tension you can put on this devise. The gripper is made of light weight metal I believe to be aluminum. It feels as though it could break if dropped on a concrete floor.     I would return it, but not for minus 25% restocking fee and the return shipping.    Other than the poor quality it does work. I hope that I do not have to do much to it to get it work the way I want. For those interested in a gripper like this I suggest the Ivanko or Woodys. Don't get fooled by \\"knurled grips\\" you won't need them unless you have a problem with very sweaty hands and towels. If you have callouses already on your fingers then this will be a good ex-foliating tool in addition to hand strength.    It also comes with no directions or information on how to use the gripper or adjust springs. You can find information on how to use this by searching for Ivanko or Woody hand gripper.

product_title: UTG Tactical OP Bipod, Rubber Feet, Center Height 8.3"-12.7"
review_body: Mounted to a rail placed on the bayonet lug of an AR-15.  Leg retraction is spring operated, where as in higher quality bipods the extension of the legs is spring assisted. Would recomend the version with the preset 5 position legs over this one.  Over-all works fine. Would recomend to a friend. review_body: Ahhh man...  I really like this tent in all respects except, as other reviewers have commented on, the floor.  It is totally unacceptable. Everything else is great. The floor is not.  Based on the reviews here on Amazon, I bought the Eureka! custom matched ground tarp to go with the tent, thinking I would be able to protect it.  Well just like the other reviewers, I set the thing up in the back yard to seal the seams and familiarize myself with the set-up procedure. When I took it down, there were small holes punched through the bottom.  This was set up on nice even grass with no obvious sticks or rocks.  I looked around the ground after, thinking I didn't make sure there were no rocks, etc.  I could not find a single rock or stick.  The floor material is just too flimsy.  I have purchased no-name, cheapo, brand tents that have had much better bath-tub type floors than this one.    Big disappointment on this.  I think that if Eureka! upgraded the floor to some decent material this would be the best tent ever, as it is, I cannot recommend it.      Update April 26, 2011.  Took the tent camping this last weekend.  At night, it rained pretty hard -- the tent stayed completely dry inside.  However when I took it down, I noticed more small perforations on the floor.  Also noticed that the supplied guy-lines, although smartly color matched to the tent fabric, are almost impossible to see at night. That was a real trip hazard. I will be replacing them with [[ASIN:B004MMEHTC Nite Ize RR-04-50 Reflective Cord, 50 Feet, Green]].  Otherwise the tent worked really well even with the small holes in the floor.

product_title: Tony Horton's POWER 90 DVD Workout
review_body:
I wanted to do more of my workouts at home AND be more active in the winter when it is harder to exercise outside. I made it about 21 to 28 days with these videos (late Nov to Christmas), without missing a workout. But after that... it got too boring to take any more. I tried switching to the next level \\"early\\". It was better, but boiled down to just more of the same. I just could not face the TV day after day knowing all the lame jokes and punch lines by heart.

I saw some great results in that month. Things were shaping up nicely and I felt very strong. I kept to my own strict eating plan, but did not use the Beachbody plan since my goals are different than the overall Power90 package. There is nothing special about the exercises included on this video. Just basic cardio and strength training. But the video is a nice way to pace yourself and balance your exercises. Tony is pretty calm in his approach to motivating on these videos.

I really like the general idea of the format for the videos. I like that you do not need lots of equipment. I like the pace. I like the length. I really liked the progress bar and timer. And I do go back to these videos on rainy days (now that it is spring) when I can not get outside to exercise.

But they are darn boring. (and I don't feel you get a lot for your money, but less than a gym membership???) Buyer beware.

review_body:
This is my first air rifle, but i have been a gun owner for years. I am a 22 fanatic especially. I was shooting with a friend a while back and he busted out a break barrel air rifle. We took a few shots and it reminded me of all the fun I used to have as a kid with a friend and his little daisy 10 pump bb gun. I decided to get one but didn't want to spend an bunch of money it. I spent a few months researching these low-end air rifles. The Phantom seemed to stand out a little bit above the rest so i went with it. I found it at Wal-mart for $80 without the scope. The scope that comes with this in the combo pack was not reviewed very well by many sources. I also don't like using scopes and would not use it anyway so why pay for it. Also, there have been complaints by some that this was advertised as a 1200fps rifle and when they got it found out it is actually 1000fps. I have only ever seen it advertised as 1000fps with the option of 1200fps with high velocity pellets. On the actual packaging it clearly states this, although if you are ordering online you may not be able to see the packaging. I have not actually tested the velocity myself but have seen chrony tests online and it seems to come in right around these figures. Now here are my personal findings after a few months of shooting.

I must say I like this air rifle a lot. I don't have a lot of experience with these but this one seems to live up to all of the things i have found on it through my research. It is a very solidly built rifle. The synthetic stock is made of a very high quality material that would be very difficult to mark up never mind break. It feels like it is a solid piece and there is no ringing or reverberation in it when firing that would indicate any hollow pockets in it. The barrel is very heavy and appears to have a nice rifling. The reciever (or what would be the reciever on a firearm, the part behind the barrel) also seems well constructed. The steel on the reciever and barrel seem to be real firearms grade steel. the barrel is comparable to the barrels on most of my 22 rifles and my 17HMR rifle. The blueing on all of the steel is also very nice, looks like a high quality finish. The rubber recoil pad is also a very nice material and sits comfortably in the shoulder. The cocking of the rifle is not overly difficult but you do need to tap the barrel at the top to get the initial break, you can't just grab it and pull it forward. I would assume that this is a good thing, and from my research this is true of all break barrels. I read one review that said the barrel does not lock in place and bounces open. I had this happen 2 times, however I had to really slam the barrel up to get it to do it, which i don't normally do. Over all the construction and materials are top notch. If you closed your eyes and I put this in your hands you would think I handed you a full sized 22 rifle. I find it hard to believe that they make much money selling this thing for $80. The only 2 things left on the rifle to go over are the trigger and the sights. As far as the sights go they are cheap but they work fine. I tried to find a rifle that didn't use these plastic sights but it seemed like everything under $300 used these plastic sights. The front sight is all plastic but feels pretty sturdy and durable. It is a green fiber-optic sight and it is also fixed. The rear sight which is adjustable for windage and elevation feels a little lacking. The rear sight on the Phantom adjusts easily with nice sharp clicks and is a set of red fiber-optics. It amazes me that they make a rifle of this quality and then throw on these cheap sights. I physically went to stores and checked out many different makes and models and they all used this stuff. The worst part is that if you buy any of the $30 to $50 pump air rifles you get a nice set of metal sights. It doesn't make much sense. Oh well. I had never used fiber-optic sights before, and I have got to say I am not a huge fan. They do work well, but I would much prefer a basic set of metal sights. The biggest complaint about this rifle is the trigger but I didn't have any problem with it. I am not into triggers the way a lot of people are. there is nothing wrong with customising triggers, I am just not into it. I have always prefered to just learn the personality (for lack of a better word) of the different triggers of my guns. As long as the trigger is acceptable to me I wouldn't mess with it. I have shot some guns that had terrible triggers on them and if they belonged to me I would get some work done on them but I have never owned a gun that I felt needed anything done to it. For me personally I think this makes me a more consistant shot with a large variety of weapons and it usually doesnt take me long to get the feel of a trigger unless it is very bad. I found this trigger to be fine for me. It is adjustable but I did not even mess with it. There is a good bit of creep and the release is not super crisp, but I had no trouble with it afer just 3 or 4 shots. I do agree that it is does not feel like a 2 stage trigger and if you are into triggers you will probably find this one lacking as I have not heard anywhere that adjusting it makes it any crisper, just lighter or heavier. I have put many rounds through it and it is getting less noisy. After getting the sights where I want them I have been shooting 5 shot groups at 25 yards with open sights that are just bigger than a golf ball (shooting bech rested). I have also been shooting gallon jugs at 50 yards unrested both sitting and standing without many misses. I have not done any actual target work out past 25 yards yet though. I have been using different pellets and have not noticed much difference but I have mainly been using cheap Crosman domed pellets from Wal-mart (250 for $2). I am very impressed with the way this rifle shoots and am very happy with my purchase. Well woth $80. review_body: An excellent beginner set.  I'm very pleased with the price and quality.  Note however, the max weight is 37 pounds (18. 5 lbs each dumbbell), not the 40 pounds advertised.  There are four 5 pound plates, four 2.5 pound plates, and a bar with two screw nuts.  The bar and nuts weighs 3.5 pounds each.  I weighed every piece in the set on a very precise scale and found that no two parts weighed the same.  The bar and nuts for example, varied from 3 pounds 8 oz (1587 grams) in the lightest configuration, to 3 pounds 9 oz (1628 grams) in the heaviest configuration.  So you should expect the bar and nuts to weigh about 3.5 pounds each.  Every other aspect of the set was as advertised and I was able to buy \\"standard\\" plates here on Amazon very inexpensively (about $1 per pound).  You can physically fit 4 plates on each side of each dumbbell for a total of 8 plates each.  So if you buy more plates, you can get a lot more weight on them if you like.  I'm sure 6 plates per dumbbell would be very safe, but 8 plates does push it to it's limits and you would have to be careful to tighten the nuts on very well.

product_title: Cold Steel Black Rock Hunter Grivory Handle

This knife will bite you.  Even though I underestimated it, I like the design of this knife pretty well. It stays closed, and it stays open. There is no way that the \\"lock\\" could fail unless the knife were to either come apart, or you let go of the handle. It just gives me the creeps when going from one to the other. This knife has earned my respect. If you are careful (as I will be from now on) it shouldn't be a problem to work it though. The blade has a deep hollow grind, so it cuts easily enough. It seems pretty durable too. I like that is efficient in its size. For its size, you get a lot of blade. Not too bad to put in a coat pocket or pack.

review_headline: Sad to say that this is a waste of money....

This system is definitely not made for anyone that wishes to get a consistently \\"high\\" heart rate, as the segments are very short with, what seems like neverending, breaks inbetween. The actual act of using the Wave is fairly simple, but I can see how it may be challenging for someone who is getting back into shape or has difficulties balancing. Truthfully, I get a better workout from the WAVE when I use it on my own as a stabilizer during weight training. product_title: Light and Motion SOLA 600 - Single
review_headline: Sola 600 an excellent choice of focus light
review_body: Just got back from Raja Ampat in Indonesia where I used the Sola 600 during an 11 day live aboard dive trip.   This light has 4 settings, 3 with normal white light and 1 with red light. The 3 level white light settings are useful and when on the full power setting there is probably enough light to use this with video, although I used it solely for shooting digital stills. The best part of this light is the red light setting which seems to make you almost invisible during a night dive. I could get very close to lots of the critters such as lobsters, shrimps and crabs without seeming to disturb them, this feature amazed the other divers as I was able to get much closer shots than they could with standard white lighting.  The light is also quite compact and light easily fitting into hand luggage if required. The battery life was excellent and because it uses an inductive charger it's very simple to top up the charge between dives with no bulky batteries to mess around with. Overall I am extremely happy with the Sola and would happily recommend it to others.

review_headline: Fair Price for Product/ Need Some Works
review_body: I was looking for a full tang small knife for all purpose usage. Could not find detail specs on the Product Description, such as blade thickness, blade length, full tang, etc.  After reading other people's reviews, I bought both \\"Fixed Blade Survival Knife Classic Black\\" drop point version ($16.75) and Tanto version ($13.75.) with Free Super Saver Shipping.    PROS:  1. Full tang.  2. Thick handle guard, which is soldered to the tang.  3. Sharpe enough right out of box.  4. Inexpensive price for such a knife.  5. Nice looking and felt balance in my hand.    CONS:  1. Arrived with pommel and handle were loose. Pin on pommel could be easily removed.  2. The velco strap is too short to have firm hold on the knife handle.  3. The handle is too small to have a firm hand grip.  4. Product Description on web page is wrong; there is no lanyard hole in the handle.    For such an inexpensive price that I did not expect to use it right out of box.  I removed the pin on the pommel and the handle; sanded down the coating on the tang and pommel. Then, used superglue to glue back the handle, pommel and pin to the tang. After the glue dry, it becomes a very solid piece of blade for my need.    After thought:  The knife would be perfect if it has (1) thicker blade and (2) bigger/thicker handle.  After all consideration, I could only give it a 3 stars rating.

review_body: I love the jumps.  I am now able to do the jumping around the house during my workout sessions that my knees would groan from before. review_body: I ordered these as a gift for my boyfriend. I did not order the stand that is suggested. They arrived 3 days after I placed my order without paying extra for expedited shipping. product_title: Steiner 8x42 Peregrine Binocular
review_body:
Last month I purchased a pair of these binoculars and I have been very impressed. They are spectacular! You get what you pay for. (If you look around, you can find these for less than half of their retail price.) While these cost a little more, several things make these worth the money. 1) They are crystal clear. These Steiner 8x42's easily outperform my bushnell 12x50's (as they should). You don't need the extra maginification and size when you have this level of clarity. I have a pair of 8x Nikon Travelites as well (also good binocular) but these Steiners are much clearer. 2) The color integrity is perfect. My wife is excited to use these for birding because they do not wash out the colors like a low to mid level binocular will. 3) They are exceptional in low light situations. I use these for hunting and they are able to grab alot of light at dawn, dusk, on cloudy days and in shadows (like looking from a sunny meadow into the shaded timber). 4) They are easy on the eyes. These do not hurt my eyes or give me headaches. Some lower quality binoculars will strain your eyes if you look through them for more than like 30 seconds. With these, your eyes don't have to work as hard so you can look through them for long periods of time without the eye strain.

In a sentance, these binoculars increase your viewing potential, they have allowed me to see what I could not see before.
I highly recommend them!

product_title: Armalaser - RSS Laser Sight - BRAND NEW - Style 'A' for TAURUS PT-145, KEL-TEC PF-9, H&K P30, KK45, HK45C, and All SIGS!
review_body: Cons:  On immediate observation I noticed the laser was not centered in the house, but rather positioned to the left half. Kind of a turn off as I would expect most weapons lasers to be situation directly below the barrel. Not a huge deal, but now you are trying to compensate for vertical and horizontal differences between the laser and the barrel of the gun.    The silver touch strip is very sensitive. It will activate with just the slightest touch, to the point where it almost feels like your not touching it all to activate it. Often I will carry my pocket pistol in my pocket with no holster, the thin pocket lining of a pair of pants is not enough of a barrier to keep the laser from activating.     The patterning on the laser is very sloppy, its not a nice precise beam/dot, it has a \\"speckled\\" glow around it. Most weapon lasers have this, not sure if the RSS is stronger and hence has a more pronounced glow, but its not something I would expect out of a 180$ laser. I have two very nice laser \\"pen\\" pointers I use for presentations that do not have the sloppy glow.    Perhaps the biggest compliant I have is that the laser does not function very well in cold weather conditions, if at all. The RSS takes on a mind of its own when its cold, if it does activate (which no joke about 90% of the time it wont) it will produce a very dim beam, to the point where it is almost too dim to see. Then it wont turn off with just a touch, Sometimes it takes a finger on each side and a squeeze to turn off, and sometimes even that doesnt work.    The stabilizer screws produce just enough of a gap between the two silver meeting points that they are basically useless.     Pros:  The RSS is light and small.    It holds zero well.    Armalaser customer service is great.    They have a very unique exchange program, BIG POINTS for that... Not because of my issues with the RSS but because I like the option that if something cooler comes out I can send in my old laser and have some nice upgradeoptions.    The Laser is very bright.    A few coats of nail polish on the silver touch strips solves some of the sensitivity issues.      All in all a decent choice. I was expecting the RSS to be super awesome for the price point it is offered at, but I am a bit disappointed. Had i paid 50 or even 75 bucks for this laser I wouldnt have too much regret, but dropping close to 200$ on the RSS I was expecting more. I also thought I would like the touch sensitive activation, but now I kinda wish i had a switch.     The stingray looks to be promising and I will probably inquire about upgrading to that model.

review_body: I used the marinade on our deep fried turkey for Thanksgiving and it received rave reviews from everyone.  Probably one of the biggest things people noticed was how moist and tender the meat was.  Also several mentioned that the taste and flavor were incredible.  I would highly recommend this product to anyone that would like to spice up their main course that would be sure to please even the worst food critic.

product_title: Bowflex Series 7 Treadmill
review_body: I wanted to wait and write this review after using this product for some time.  We purchased this back in September of 2010 and have used it approx. 4 days a week since arrival.  It wasn't too hard to set up but I did need help getting it out of the package.  It is very heavy! The deliverer was great and even set it in our garage where I wanted it to be placed.  I run ( 46 yrs old - female - 120 lbs. ) four days a week, four miles each run.  It is A LOT quieter than my old treadmill and so I don't need headphones to listen to my media set up.  (I have a screen with dvd or tv feeding into it.)  And that's good because this treadmill sits farther back from the wall therefore I can't use my headphones because the cord does not reach. Others have mentioned the fan.  I don't know of any treadmill where the fan really cools you off.  We purchased a large fan that we have set up for warm/hot days.  That is really the best way to cool off while running on a treadmill.    The controls took a little time to get used to but once I got into the habit they are very easy to use.  The cup holders are for bottles or something that has a lid.  Your drink will sit almost horizontal, but it works.  I have never had my bottle fall out. The tread area is comfortable to run on and well cushioned.  It comes with oil to lubricate your belt area and the guide says it will even alert you as to when it needs it.  I have not seen that as of yet. This treadmill also folds up and down very easily.  Much better than my old one!    My husband uses it off and on and he weighs about 180 lbs. and he doesn't have any problems with it either.  It's a solid machine and does the job.

product_title: Kel-Tec P3At/P32 Grip Ext Blk
review_body: If you own a pocket sized semi-auto, like so many with a CHL do, the Magazine extension is a must. This one made for the KelTec P3AT does not allow for more ammo but gives the ring finger a place to grip adding stability. These little 380 acp's create a jolt when fired. Mine installed on my KelTec P3AT's standard magazines in 2 or 3 minutes. Note - watch out or the mag. spring will fly away. It makes the handle a bit longer but doesn't interfere with how the gun fits in my pocket. I have one on all of my magazines and put them on my girlfriends' KelTec too.

product_title: 40" Anime Kenshin Sakabato Burgundy Reverse Blade Samurai Sword
review_body:
the sword is authentic to the rouroni kenshin/Samurai X series, the balde, as described is reversed, but the tip of the sword was not like most swords, which in the descriptions picture it is, it suddenly turns into a straight curve, rather than a gradual slope. the sword and sheath themself look amazing, but when i removed the sword from the sheath, it took extrenuos force, and i was afraid to break the sword or sheath. but, if left as is when recieved, it will look amazing in any persons collection if you want it for decoration its worth it, but if you want it to be functional, search for reverse blade swords and find the one that says it is made of carbon steel in the description,carbon steel is far more functional than stainless steel(which this one is made of),

a side note for those who are just starting a collection, 1060 carbon steel is the cheapest type of sword availible that is affordable(for most)
if you are willing to spend more, try out damascus,9260 spring, and T10 steels
most durable being damascus

Carbon Steel: the lower the # the more flexible the steel(bad below about 50) and high #s are more brittle(bad above 70), 1060 is a great compromise for both

product_title: MTech USA MT-113 Rescue Team Fixed Blade Survival Knife, Black Straight Edge Tanto Blade, Black Handle, 10-1/2-Inch Overall
review_body:
When I received this knife it came in its box wrapped in a paper envelope. I was not expecting the weight or size of the product I ordered. I could tell this knife was solid right from the moment I gripped it in my hands and made a few motions with it. The knife is not as sharp as I'd like it to be, but it is still very sharp(it does not shave hair). I tested the sharpness on paper, then cardboard, then wood. The knife will stick into wood very well, but the powder coating on the blade deteriorates on the top of the blade (the sides are fine). The knife is about 10 and a half inches long total and has a 6 inch blade. Tanto pointed, this knife is very solid and has a KA-BAR style handle. It is a bit different than the one shown, but the only difference is the label placement. The rubberized grip is a plus for me.

Overall, this gets a 4 star rating because it is solid and sharp, but the coating and grip were a bit cheap (but not too cheap)
I recommend this knife to anyone looking to get a solid blade for a very reasonable price. Or people who want a KA-BAR and jsut can't spend that kind of money.

review_headline: Great bar for the price, but be cautious

If you leave in a rented apartment as I do, then it would be better not to screw with the doors. In that case you can attach the chin-up bar by twisting it thoroughly. review_body: Pros: the bands work as advertised, and I'm quite happy with them.      : the package included the door hook--it too works very well.      : very fast delivery.    Cons: no box, delivered in a bubbled mailer envelope, which had 2 tears in it on arrival.      : shipping/handling charges too steep for this mailing.       : no DVD, though the description above indicates such in the features      : no 'instructional booklet', but a crumpled black & white Xeroxed copy of what appears as a   brochure with some exercises.      : no answer to my two emails asking about the DVD and questioning the Lifetime Warranty. I did receive the two automatic messages giving me a possible 'allow 3 days for response' type notice. We're past that.     Suggestion to company Astone:   please clarify the differences in prices/packages as to what's included. After contacting the company through Amazon and viewing the company reviews, there were others who complained of these same things. I like saving money, but the purchase leaves me feeling shaky about buying from other than Ripcords directly. Also, how does this affect the Lifetime Guarantee?                           ********************************************  UPDATE: Seller apologized for the late contact, and assured me he'd 'get to the bottom' of my first unanswered email. He then asked for verification of where I saw the DVD as included. I had relied on the Guarantee's phrasing, plus the pictures where the DVD is displayed on the \\"Intermediate Tension 4\\" box photograph. It was only then I bothered to read the writing below the DVD pix--it said 'optional' in font so small I must have dismissed it as a trademark notice instead. Seller offers DVD to make things right, I offer sincerest apology and promise to amend my review. As far as the steep shipping, he explained their 'fulfillment house' is very efficient and ships quickly, but they must also pay the high fee. Seller addressed the problems, refunded half my shipping, reassured meof the Lifetime Guarantee, and that's as good as it gets!

product_title: Affinity Ladies AVT Pink Golf Club Set w/Stand Bag &Free Putter Regular Length
review_body: I bought these clubs for my fiance for Christmas. She is just starting to learn the game, so they will be good for her, but they are clearly a starter set, but good clubs for the money.

product_title: Valeo Medicine Ball With Sturdy Rubber Construction And Textured Finish, Weight Ball Includes Exercise Wall Chart For Strength Training, Plyometric Training, Balance Training And Muscle Build
review_body: After a few months of indoor and outdoor (cement garage floor) use, this medicine ball has minimal signs of wear, is still round (ball slams) and is used almost daily. Very happy with the purchase.

product_title: Barnett Quad 400 Crossbow Camo Package
review_body: I bought this item for my boyfriend for Christmas but when he went to put it together it did not have the premium red dot scope as described it had the 4x32 cross hair scope!!  He was still happy with it and we decided to keep it and not send it back Amazon did give me a ten dollar credit for the mistake!!!

product_title: UTG Combat-Featured Operational Vest
review_body: Can't really say to much bad about it. I am starting to have a lot of success with UTG brand. Plenty of space and kind of straddles the chest rig/ crossdraw vest option, wish it came with a belt. I never did find a belt or drop leg system in this color for a good price. review_body: Worked well for about a year. Loved the roominess, but not the lack of dependability.  Lately it would not pop open as it should (even with fresh batteries).  Don't trust your life on this safe.  [UPDATE]  Even though it \\"stopped\\" working I did not throw it away and I'm glad I did not. product_title: Uncle Mike's Off-Duty and Concealment Nylon Original Zipper Close Gun Pak Belt Pouch Holster, Black
review_body: All in all not bad for the price, but a little small for my glock 33.  Plenty big for my kel-tec p3 though.  I'd like to see it have a stiffer back.  Convenient and preferable to me over a fanny pack.

product_title: Proguard Pro Hockey Goal, 4 x 6-Feet
review_body: I tried to find a review on this net before purchase, but not much out there. The box advertises that it is the \\"strongest netting on the market\\" however in my second session I put a slapper right through it.     I would like to think I am that tough but reality is I am a rec league hack and use a 100 flex because I am not strong enough to wield a 110 flex. So I would warn anyone with a strong shot to steer clear.     I found the engineering to be optimized for cheap shipment - not quality of product. It comes in about 14 pieces, which means a lot of joints and creates a little slop - not that that is really going to impact performance, but it does not make for a solid feel.      The net attaches easily with velcro flaps, problem is also in my second session it worked loose, just need to reattach velcro, but still not cool to be reattaching all the time. More concerning was that the netting was beginning to tear near the cross bar flap.    The velcro flaps wrap the posts, so you have cloth around all the facing tubes, which is kinda funky, but again not going to really be noticable for performance.     On the plus side the 2\\" posts provide some weight, and will probably stand up to some punishment. I think the way this is setup it kinda requires their proprietary net with velcro flaps, so we can't just swap out for another net as their is nothing to fasten too.    I am always worried about slamming reviews, because most people only right them when dissatisfied (guilty as charged). In fairness to the MFG if you can't effectively swing a 110 flex stick, you probably are not going to have a problem and I would say it is a good value for the price.    Its less than a week old so my local hockey shop allowed me to return it - so kudos to them.

review_body: I have an A5 with a low profile hopper. This offset basically turns your low profile hopper into a standard hopper, since it boosts the height a good 3.5\\". product_title: Smartwool - Phd Outdoor Heavy Crew
review_headline: In my opinion, the best of the best
review_body: I do a fair level of short-length hiking, from 5-7 mile conditioning hikes to 20-25 mile overnighters. My bottom line: I love the SmartWool PHD line better than any other sock I've tried. My beef with most brands of wool sock is that they don't snug up to the shape of your foot, so if there's a little looseness in your boot, the wool slides against your skin rather than the sock sliding against your boot. That results in unnecessary hot spots or blisters. The PHDs really shape themselves to your foot. The other problem I (and many) have with wool socks is that your feet sweat. It's too common to wear wool socks around, with or without shoes, and find that your feet aren't cold, but do feel wet or clammy. When I wear the SmartWool PHDs my feet stay warm and, more importantly, always feel dry. They wick the moisture away better than any other wool sock I've found. I wish I'd known about these back when I was active duty in the infantry!

product_title: Dye Precision I4 Thermal Paintball Goggle
review_body: I took it out to the field this past weekend and it held up great, easy ajustable fit, and easy to clean, came in a timely manner. Great buy from amazon overall.

product_title: Bag Balm Ointment, 8 Ounce
review_headline: Toxic to Humans.. AND it made my hands worse!
review_body:
So we haven't had a dishwasher for a while.. I have been hand-washing dishes and now my hands are chapped, sore, and the skin is flaky and starting to split. Hubby, ex-California cowboy, recommended this product. I open the can and it smells rather like a cross between iodine and Germolene. It looks rather like commercial engineering grease. The main ingredient, I noted, 8-hydroxyquinoline sulfate 0.3% (antiseptic) in a petroleum jelly USP and lanolin base. Now I was a little leary, being more interested in products containing Shea butter or Almond oil.. but I applied a small amount anyway. 10 minutes after applying it, it was still sitting on the skin surface.. that is a feature of Petroleum Jelly of course.. I couldn't touch anything, as this stuff was tacky and was picking up \\"stuff\\".. dust and dirt patricles off the interior of our SUV. Now it started to really smart! We got home 20 minutes later, and I had to really scrub my hands in hot water to remove every last trace of this stuff... twice! I can smell it that chemical smell an hour later. So I proceeded to check the main ingredient, 8-hydroxyquinoline sulfate out on cosmeticsdatabase, and checked out Bag Balm on Wiki, and discovered that it is NOT to be used for humans! It is only authorised for use as an animal product; In fact the ORIGINAL 1899 bag balm was even worse as it contained mercury, a dreadful neurotoxin. 8-hydroxyquinoline sulfate is associated with cancer and with systemic organ toxicity effects in animal studies.

Forget it.. there is much better stuff out there.. look for a cocoa butter or shea butter based product instead.

product_title: Guidecraft NHL Boston Bruins Toy Box
review_body: Bought this for my nephew, who is a HUGE Boston Bruins fan and he likes it very much. product_title: Valeo Burst Resistant Ball, 55cm VA3582PU

The price of this package is quite reasonable for the quality of the products provided.  I'm 5'3\\" and this ball fits me.  I'm retired (OK, read \\"old\\").  I am dealing with back injuries, and core strength issues.  The ball exercises prescribed by my therapist are easy and fun to do, feel more like play than work, and really do the job. review_body: This exerciser was purchased as a gift for my in-laws.  It's perfect for exercising when traditional exercises are not an option.  It's surprisingly sturdy and assembled quickly. product_title: Suunto Movestick Wireless PC Interface
review_body: Paid about $80 for this and waited for a long time until it arrived. It is so darn tiny and I wonder why it costs so much.    It almost never syncs up properly and all of this is done for . .  get this to upload your data online. I had to reinstall this several times as the connections don't work. It seems like a basic error on Suunto's part and we are taking the brunt for this.    When the excel functionality finally comes out, that would be worthwhile but otherwise I am not impressed and Suunto's support, when they can understand English, is minimal. review_body: I like the Schwinn 140 upright, I have one that I use myself. But this one was for a birthday gift and it arrived on time, but after assembly, we found that the pulse meter didn't work. So far it has been hard to identify who to call and so forth.

product_title: Affinity Revo 56 Degree Black Satin Finish Wedge (Men's Right-Handed)
review_body: Picked it up as a practice club for which it works well. Build quality is what you would expect for a club this cost. If you look around you can find 2-3 year old new wedges online (from the major brands) about the same price with better shaft choices, cavity backs, overall build quality, and nicer cut groves.

product_title: Crosman 88G Airsource Adapter for All Paintball Markers
review_headline: Works sometimes, gets stuck other times
review_body: This is a good adapter when it works, but I have had several problems with it.  It gets stuck on the paintball gun or the 88g tank easily, and sometimes the 88g tank will go on, sometimes not.  If you need to be able to use 88g tanks, it is not bad, but I would recommend using the regular-fitted tanks (the ones that attach directly to the paintball guns) if you can.

product_title: UTG Shooter's SWAT Bipod, Rubber Feet, Height 6.2"-6.7"
review_body: For the price this is a good buy. I haven't shot with it yet but it fits snug and looks nice.   -I wish the legs extended out a little more, its got so much style to its construction for only extending an extra inch or so. (cost it a 5th star)  -The release button for one of the folding mechanisms is a bit unpredictable but it appears to be a very minor flaw and by the looks of it may only be an isolated issue. (cost it a 4th star)

product_title: BOB Duallie Revolution Stroller
review_body: Bought this stroller for my 2,5 year old and 4 month old for our walks on beach when staying in Costa Rica. And I love it, it is so easy to push on sand  even with both kids in and loaded with towels, toys, diaper bag and more. The weight does not matter to us since we have different stroller for traveling and we did use it at the airport on the way to Costa Rica and it was very easy to fold and unfold without much practice. I do like the older model better since the extra padding might be nice for jogging and running, but I had stroller with nice padding before and my kids would get too hot. I do like the pop on car seat adapter or tray that the new version has but my 2,5 year old is fine with the pockets on the side and has no problem to put his snack , sippy cup or water bottle in. I did lot of online research and this stroller was the best option, and the price on Amazon is great, Get it before it is all sold out and there is only the new version!

product_title: Blackburn Voyager Click Head Light
review_body: I walked into my local bike shop and asked for a daytime conspicuity light that was small, inexpensive, and durable, and came out with this one.       Useful features include:    Easy to turn on/off with gloves on. I don't care for fussy switches. Just push the clear part to turn on / off. Has a blinking patten as well as steady on.    Small enough to carry in your pocket.    Inconspicuous on the bike. This thing is very small.    Unlikely to fall off. I've only put about 20 urban miles on this, but so far it hasn't moved.        As you would expect, this is not a \\"headlight\\" that will light up a dark road. It is a useful conspicuity light that will work in daytime or night time.      UPDATE:    Having owned this for a while, I'll add:    not easy to take off/on, especially with gloves or cold hands.     The batteries did not last long and need replacement. However, it takes two CR2032 batteries, which would be more than half the purchase price of a new unit. Not happening.      So not a good value in the long run. The Planet Bike headlights look like a better way to go, as they use AA batteries plus they can function as a headlight (which this unit does not).

product_title: Bowflex SelectTech 1090 Adjustable Dumbbell (Single)
review_body: Easy to use. Great for small workout spaces (i.e. dorm, bedroom, office). Really good for bust-em-out programs like P90X where quick weight changes are required. Only problem occurs when range of motion is limited due to the width of the dumbbell (about 18\\"). This problem rarely occurs (only two exercises in P90X are affected as far as I am concerned). I must follow up by saying that the benefits of having so many choices in one dumbbell far outweigh the costs. Also, you really need two of these to appreciate the effectiveness.

product_title: Magpul MOE MVG Grip, Black
review_body: This was a fake. I have to say that the seller did right by me and after 25 days I received a full refund for my shipping and the price of the item. This is the airsoft version of the Magpul item. If you look at where the top connects with the rifle it says PTS right there.

product_title: Timex T5J031 Unisex Digital Fitness Heart Rate Monitor Watch
review_body: This is my initial review and it is love at first sight. I am a male, 6 foot and about 150 lbs. Finally a HRM that is not like a Big Ben alarm clock strapped to my wrist. It is about the size of a normal size watch and seems to fit my personality and ego about as well as it fits on my wrist. If it could lay a little flatter it would be sublime but it is a good fit. The watch eas easy to set up and begin using. Nice basic function that are easy and straight forward. I loved the package as it did not require me to get out safety equipment to break into some ballistic plastic shell. I slid it out of the box, removed the plastic top and put my watch on. How refreshingly easy. I had a Sette that I thought was a bit more svelte but it melted in the sauna. Hopefully I wont forget this one off.   Now Timex. Here is personal request. If you could make a wrist HRM and blood oxygen monitor similar to this watch you would really have my heart and my blood to. It could be a simple plug in wrap around the forefinger gizmo that could be used with or without the watch. Of course something more innovative a sleek would be nice.

review_body: If you do yoga on a regular basis you owe it to yourself to get a quality mat.  I started off with a mat that I purchased at Target.  It was fine. product_title: Womens R-Gear High-Speed Compression Knee Short
review_body: It's harder to find women's compression shorts that are of a longer length so I usually end up buying boys or men's shorts. product_title: STIGA STIGA 54-Inch Mini Pong Table Tennis Table
review_body:
My wife and I love playing TT recreationally, but we live in an apartment with little room for a full size table. I previously tried the Spartan portable mini table tennis table, but that was a disaster. The table was super-heavy and the hinges broke even while we were unfolding it for the very first use. I then had to lug it to the store (Dick's) to return it. Given that experience, this Stiga table felt so much better. It does have its share of problems though.

Pros:
1. Relatively light weight (35 lbs)
2. Very easy to put together. Its basically 4 wing bolts, and then you snap on a few parts. No tools required. 5-10 minutes.
3. Decent playing surface for recreational use. Since the board itself does not fold in half, you can be sure that the surface is perfectly even.
4. Nice size for an apartment. The design of the legs means it takes up a very small floor footprint, while being reasonably sturdy.
5. 29\\" x 54\\" is a very playable surface. Sure, you don't move around at all compared to a full-sized table, but its still fun for 2 adults.

Cons:
1. From looking at the pictures, I assumed that this table folds up like an ironing board. It does not. You basically need to DISASSEMBLE it each time you want to put it away and RE-ASSEMBLE it before each play. Sure, the table is easy to take apart and put back together, but it still takes about 5-10 minutes. Also, assembly and disassembly require you to turn the table upside down, risking damage to the playing surface and requiring some strength. If you're looking to stow the table away after each use, you might be disappointed. I sure am.
2. The included rackets are plastic toy-like child rackets. It can seriously hurt an adult's wrists using them. Be sure to get a full-size pair.
3. The reason the spartan table was so much heavier is that the playing surface had wood and metal reinforcement on all sides. The MDF surface of the Stiga table is largely unprotected. You need to be careful not to place anything on top of it, even in storage. Even if you need to move it (while assembled), two people would probably need to lift it by the legs, rather than holding it by the playing surface. With careful use though, it looks like it should last a while. Only time will tell.
4. Compared to portable tables where the playing surface folds in half, the size of this table can make it unwieldy to store.
5. The net is only 3 inches wide. The height can be adjusted to make it up to 4.75 inches tall, but leaving a gap at the bottom.
6. Pricey. The components are nothing fancy. This ought to be much cheaper.

product_title: Injinji 2012 Performance Original Weight Crew Toe Socks
review_headline: Exactly what I was hoping they would be
review_body: I'm a professional product photographer who recently took a studio job requiring me to stand and walk a minimum of eight and usually ten hours a day.  I've always had wide feet and have experienced issues with corns and blisters around my toes from time to time in the past.  With the new work, I found the problems to be back full force.  I ordered one pair of Injini crew socks to try them out.  I just got home from work, my feet feel great, and I ordered thirteen more pairs.  That is how much I like these.    A few notes for people to understand them:    -They take a bit longer to put on than normal socks.  You're supposed to put them over your forefoot first, work the fabric around your toes, then pull them the rest of the way onto your feet  -They fit fairly snugly.  Make sure you don't have rough calluses or toe nails, or you stand a good chance of snagging them.  -They breathe VERY well, as would be expected of a high-grade synthetic wicking material  -Friction between your toes is tremendously alleviated.  In my opinion, this is due to a combination of the slippery material of the socks and that the wicking material keeps your feet drier.    and, here's a big one:    -Everyone's toes and feet are shaped differently.  You can't expect these to fit like a second skin, spray-painted onto your foot.  I have very long toes.  The the first three toes on each foot are close, but not quite long enough.  The remaining two are just about right.  It is unreasonable to expect these to perfectly on every person.  Also, after you've worn them for a while, they settle well into place.    Again, I couldn't be happier.  Buy one pair, try them for a day (not just for ten minutes), and you'll probably love them.

product_title: INSANITY Base Kit - DVD Workout
review_headline: Rrrrrripppp....yes, that was the sound of my abs flexing
review_body:
This is a nuts set of workout DVD's. I am overweight and just shy of 40, but I have dreams of getting back into my pre-marriage body. I decided to seize the day and go for it, and I am not sorry. My muscles are currently screaming, every bit of me hurts. Every day, I both love and dread pushing play on this dvd, because I know what will happen when I do. I will spend 45 minutes gasping, lurching around, heart pounding, sweat running off me like a monsoon, desparately trying to keep up with a workout designed by fitness demigods. Afterwards, when I can catch my breath and pull myself up of the ground, I feel so good it is not even funny. Yesterday when I finished my workout and was talking to my wife, I said \\"You know what I feel like? I feel like I'm on vacation!\\". You know, that feeling you get on day 1 of vacation when you have the whole thing stretching before you, when there is a cool drink in your hands and not a care in the world? That's how I feel when my blood is pumping, when my body is sore and I am so proud of myself.

I can't even begin to keep up with this video, but that is ok. I keep my heart rate up, I have a great time, and I try to get a little better every day. I'm not done with the program yet, I hope I have the stamina to keep it up, but for now, this is fantastic.

The DVD's themselves are good, the music is fine, the instructor is incredible and never demeaning. I feel like he is speaking directly to me and he is very encouraging. I am also encouraged when the folks exercising with him can't keep up, because I know that if these very in shape people can't do it, then I am in good company. The rest of the package is fine. I'm on weight watchers, so I'm not using their eating plan. I'm not changing diets midstream. Anyway, the workout calendar is nice, I keep it up to date and it is a good motivational tool for me. The DVD case is compact and sturdy. It's a little pricey, but I think that it is worth it so far. It is giving me back my self respect.

----**UPDATE**
I've done the program now for 21 days. I have gone down 2 pant sizes, lost 11 pounds, am losing my love handles, have had to take my belt in 2 notches (almost 3!) and am getting my neck back! The workouts are very active. They are very intense, and the more I do them, the more intense they can get. When I first started, I could not do the exercises with anything approaching good form. 3 weeks on, my form has improved, but now the workouts are tougher because I'm pushing myself harder to complete them. Shaun T. is inspirational,and I have a love hate relationship with him on the DVDs! I yell at the screen as I exercise. Get yourself a good pair of shoes, it made a huge difference to me, and make sure you do all the warm ups. If you are chunky like me when you start, don't be discouraged, just keep at it, do your best, and so far the results have made me a believer. It has been a very hard 3 weeks, but I love the way I feel, I'm happy to be in clothes I thought I would never wear again, and my wife and co-workers all notice the difference. This set has made a big difference in my attitude towards exercise, and I think I'm going to do P90x when Insanity is done!

--**Update**
Day 31 of insanity here, down 14.1 pounds, ran 5k yesterday, pushing harder. The workouts don't get easier, but there is a huge sense of accomplishment every day as I fill in the workout calendar. Someone told me today that I look thinner, and I was very excited. I'm still thick, don't get me wrong, but I'm getting there. Insanity has made me excited to get physical.

--**Update**
5 weeks of insanity done, 17 pounds down, preparing for a 4.5 mile run this weekend, really nervous about starting week 6--it supposedly gets even insaner (?). My wife has joined me for some of the workouts and my kids are now doing it with me (as much as they are able, and they have a great time!)--the whole family has gotten into it. Can't say enough about how good I feel--it is a crime to feel this good, I swear.

--**Update**
I must admit that I look forward to these little updates, as I use them for encouragement. Anyway, day 45 of insanity is today. From a discipline standpoint, this is a daily decision--these workouts are hard. I feel great, but every day, I look in the mirror and think a)this is great and b)long way to go. On the up side, my belt is too big, have to use it on its tightest setting. I'm down 18.5 pounds since I began. I can see my neck--and it is not just a solid column of blubber. I have abs popping out (!) (although they are still buried under some belly fat--let's face it, I started this waaaay overweight). My wife has now joined the culture of fitness in our family, and is working out regularly. The second month of insanity, which starts 6 weeks in, is significantly more insane than the first month (which I didn't think was humanly possible). Shaun T goes completely nuts, and the workouts are tougher, more intense, longer, and still lots of fun. I could never have dreamed 45 days ago of keeping up this level of activity. Back on day 1, the first warm up blew me away and I wanted to lay down and cry. Now, the warm up still kicks my rear end, but I know it is because I am trying HARDER working STRONGER doing Better. My flexibility is so much increased! I walk around and I feel stronger in everything that I do. Listen folks, this is a great program. If you have the determination, it will change you, mentally, physically, cardiovascularly. It is so hard, but soooooo good.

--**Update**
Today is day 59 of Insanity. Wow. I can't believe I have almost made it through the first round. I weighed myself today, and I am down 21.8 pounds. My old pants are falling off me--literally. I put them on yesterday just to walk around the house because they were in the top of the \\"clean\\" pile, and they fell right off. I had to change clothes! I'm using a smaller belt I never thought I would use again. My size 36 jeans are now my jeans of choice (down from busting out of size 40's to the point that I wouldn't even wear jeans because they were not comfortable). I'm planning on doing Insanity: The Asylum when this round is done, which will turn the Insanity journey into a 90 day (actually, 93) day trip. Then, on to p90x!

--**Update**
This will likely be my final update. I finished Insanity 2 days ago. Wow. Wow. It was a bear. The last week was so intense, I struggled just to keep up (two Max Plyo workouts? Two Max Interval workouts? And Cardio Abs twice??). I'm 22+ pounds down, happy as a clam, sore as can be, and chomping at the bit to keep going. I did my final fit test, and more than doubled many of my exercises--I would NEVER have believed it possible. I was still sucking wind by the end of the fit test, because I was pushing as hard as I could to better my last scores. I started the sequel to this video set (Insanity: The Asylum) yesterday, and it is equally intense, but different. I'll probably review it as well when I have done more of the workouts. Anyway, I could never have survived even 5 minutes of the Asylum if I hadn't done Insanity first.

In the end, this set worked for me because I needed someone to push me. Or I thought I did--I really ended up pushing myself, but the videos gave me the structure and the tools to get it done. I promised myself I would do it every day, even if I had to workout at midnight. It was just me, a pair of shoes, and my DVD player, kicking some butt. Some reservations here--it is not easy on your joints. I'm 40, and overweight. Some exercises were just too hard on my knees, and I modified them. I kept my heart rate up. Shaun always says \\"exercise at your own level\\", but what I told myself was \\"exercise just a little past your level\\". So I did, and it worked for me. Take their warnings seriously--don't do this if you aren't willing to push, and if you have health concerns, then for heaven's sake, choose something else. But if you are willing to get your goose cooked on a daily basis and come back and ask for seconds (!), then this is a great choice. Cheers to everyone in the Insane Posse of Fitness Gazelles, and I hope that these updates have helped. Be smart, work hard, and whatever method you are using to lose weight, Insanity or something else, keep it up. I'll be doing the same!

--**Update**
I know that I said that the last update would be my last update. But I wanted to give a status report 1 year on--I'm now just shy of 50 lbs down since I began one year ago. I did the following things--I did Insanity x 1 round, Insanity Asylum x 1 round, P90x+Insanity hybrid x 1 round (P90x + insanity cardio), P90x straight up x 1 round, and I'm now in the midst of a p90x2 + Insanity hybrid with 3 weeks to go before completion. I also run 1-2x per week for 45min to 60 min on the elliptical because I enjoy it. I do insanity with a 20 lb weight vest on now sometimes, and I run on the elliptical with a weight vest. I have gone from being able to do 1 (count it, 1!) pull up to 10 sets of 8 pullups. They aren't the prettiest pull ups around, but I get up, all on my own. I can do push ups until the cows come home. I'm still about 20 lbs overweight from what I'd like to be, but I'm not complaining. At 50 lbs in a year, you can see that weight has been slow but steadily coming off. No loose skin, lots and lots of muscle coming on. I'm still a big dude--but I now RUN up and down the stairs at work. And I'm out of breath--but I love it. I'm not yet back in my wedding suit, but I've pulled out clothes I haven't worn in YEARS. Yesterday, I had to take off a sweater because it swallowed me whole. Then I put on another sweater--and it was too big also.

All of this is to say that I haven't done anything that crazy, not really. About an hour a day, sometimes more because I really enjoy it now, sometimes less when I'm tired. product_title: Under Armour Mens HeatGear Athletic Shorts
review_headline: Superbely constructed; Best for those with big quadriceps
review_body: I ordered the Coach's Short in size medium. This size is likely best for a waist (not nominal pants size) measuring 35-38 inches - distinctly larger than the stated size range. The legs are HUGE, with a diameter of 15.5 inches at the base. This means the base opening has a circumference of over 48 inches. Compare that measurement to the circumference of your quads. For most middleweight or thin males, these shorts would be much too baggy. I returned mine for this reason.  The appealing pluses:  - Deep and sturdy side pockets. Very nice.  - Rear pocket. This pocket uses a button for closure. This is great for casual use, but is not practical if you exercise on your back (during Pilates, for example).  - Mid-weight fabric is not flimsy and appears durable.  Bottom line: This is a generously cut, superbly constructed garment. The button on the rear pocket defines it as a casual short that is unsuitable for some activities. If you have really big legs, the Coach's short should be great. This short is not designed for those of lean build. I really liked its features and construction, and wish it had fit me. I hope my experience helps you make your purchasing decision.

review_body: I love this device.  I prefer this over the gri gri, because it is safer for beginners to use. review_body:

As far as the manufacturer, this replacement head doesn't come close to the original pump head.

review_body: I like the fit and feel and look of these pants. review_body: Overall the LED light is decent. I own about 12 different lights, 3 different brands and by far Surefire is the highest quality. For as inexpensive this light is it is good, bought several as presents and have heard no complaints.

review_body: I took these hunting this year and was very pleased with their clarity, ease of use, and durability. I compared to my son's Leupold and I could not tell the difference.

product_title: Knee Warmers
review_body: Got these for my mother who has arthritis in her knees. She loves them. They're superwarm (she had been wearing tights and warmers now it's just the warmers) and unlike other knee warmers and wraps, they don't add extra bulk under jeans. She highly recommends them.

review_body: So good I went back and bought one more and gifted one as well. UA is always a bit scratchy to me but I will live with it. It allows me to dress lighter with less layers.

product_title: NCAA Florida State Seminoles 100% Cotton Long Sleeve T-Shirt
review_body: I bought this shirt for my husband as a Christmas gift - he loved it!  The sizing was true and in good quality.  The item arrived very quickly and we are stationed overseas.  I would buy from this seller in the future.

review_body: I have used many different types of cuffs for a very long time and say that there are two big differences that I have to say I dont like. review_body:

review_body: The only dvd I watched was the beginner/20 minute work out. It skipped and stopped so many times that I am just returning it to amazon. I did not bother watching the other dvd's. I will just attend the free zumba class offered at my work.

product_title: MaxxDry Shoe Dryer XL
review_headline: worth every penny - perfect for cold weather surfers
review_body: after reading a lot of the reviews on MaxxDry, i decided to order one to dry out my surfing boots and gloves - even though they were new, after just the first session they stunk like roadkill as I tried drying them out of a steam heat radiator in my small NYC apartment. I ordered this model instead of the wide body because the price was so much better and it came with the boot towers. after a couple of hours, my boots/gloves are dry and odor free. I'd also say the motor is much quieter than expected - i thought it was going to sound like a hair-dryer running, but it's more comparable to the hum of a small room fan you might use during the summer to create a breeze. This was a great bonus bc I work from home, in a small apartment and couldn't afford to be using the phone while trying to hear/shout over a loud fan/motor running in the background. I don't even notice the noise which is great. I hope it holds up but even if it only makes it a year or so, I'd def just get another one for $49 = $0.13 a day for a year of dry, non-smelling gloves and boots. looking forward to using it on snowboarding boots, running shoes and cycling shoes, too. great product and much easier than trying to make my own contraption from PVC and all that. one click order, showed up the next day, done and done. also seems smaller, lighter and more compact than expected which I like bc it's easy to get \\"over geared\\" doing a few sports. this easily fits in an out of the way corner and does its job better than expected.

product_title: Bushnell Tactical Elite 1x32 Red/Green T-Dot Riflescope
review_body: I've used mine and it does the job to the extent that it was designed to...nothing more. Those who rate this scope poorly because it doesn't deliver ACOG performance are just not living in the real world. If you want or expect more, buy a high-end scope. If you aren't looking for (or don't need)the best, this one will do...if your life doesn't depend day-in & day-out on your equipment.  This sucker is heavy at approximately one pound. If you aren't a strong individual and/or you plan on carrying your weapon for extended periods of time, you'll want a lighter scope if you are mounting this on anything heavier than an M4. With a modified HK93 (tri-rail handguard, tactical flashlight & laser), this scope puts the whole rig over 11 pounds with a partially loaded 40 round magazine. This isn't necessarily a negative, just an observation.  In regards to the negatives, there's no excuse for having a reticle that's ghosted or gives off a double image such as mine does. Also, the overall finish on the product was okay at best. At the relatively low price point, it simply isn't worth the time and energy to send back for a replacement or repair, and I think Bushnell is counting on that. Bushnell's quality control leaves much to be desired, in my opinion.   Overall, I would recommend this scope to someone who is looking for a low-cost alternative to \\"the real thing\\" and doesn't plan on carrying their weapon into combat. This will suffice for wowing them at the range or for fast acquisition of a home invading bad guy. However, if you need a tough tactical reflex sight/scope for military applications...save up and buy the real thing.  UPDATE: I ended up selling this sight for $80. I decided that the combination of a ghosted image with the heavy weight was a deal breaker. I ended up buying a Walther PS 22 red dot AND a Trijicon Reflex sight, but would still give this sight a 3 out of 5.

product_title: RAD Cycle Products Indoor Exercise Bike Trainer with Six Levels of Resistance Work Out
review_body: I bought the  trainer because the price; it is unbelievable $60.    The noise it create is notable but my bike seem to be more noise. I have a old road bike with 700c wheels (with slip tire surface), the sound is not mainly comes from the tire, but from the freewheel and chain. So be sure you have smooth rotating system in your bike,which can reduce the noise and, more importantly, the vibration create from your bike.    The trainer is quite sturdy and easy to lock your bike on. However, the assembly of the trainer is poor. After I ride it for 10 min, I heard scratch sound from the roller. That is because there is a hex loosen due to centrifuge force; I screwed it back and solve the problem. Moreover, I found out the the alignment of the trainer is not right, which makes my bike skewed. I padded it with some corrugated paper to solve it, that is about 1 cm.    People who want to buy the product have to concern about vibration problem, especially for whom live in apartment. I bought an exercise mat and try to reduce the vibration; it works, but this is still a problem. Hope the people downstairs won't complain me...    The product claims they have 7 resistances, however, they all feel the same. Look into the resistant system, it has two fixed magnet face to each other, and a rolling metal disk in between. The metal is made of non-magnetic substance, maybe aluminum. I can't understand how will it create resistance. I just leave the shifter unused. The original resistance serves me well.    By the way, if you don't have quick release skewer, you will have difficult to put your bike on. Although they provide you one, it is hard for you to change into it. You might need some special tools or just go to the bicycle store for help.      Overall, when outside is covered by snow and ice, it is a good and cheap choice for you and your bike.

I assume from this I am not alone in my accessment of this. I can use the lighter, it hurts my thumb, but my girlfriend can't press the ignition switch forward. product_title: P90X DVD Workout - Base Kit
review_headline: The real thing!  But someone tell Wesley. . . .
review_body: All in all, this is a very good set of workout videos: balanced, entertaining and encouraging. I particularly like the thoroughness of the upper-body exercises, thanks to the use of the chin bar and dumbbells -- not just relying on push-ups, as some trainers seem to.      The criticisms of P90X from detractors are generally nonsense. My favorite is that this is a rip-off offering nothing different because anyone will get a lot fitter working out for an hour every day.  Well, no freakin' duh. Everyone knows you have to eat better and exercise more, but clearly everyone doesn't do it, so when someone comes along who can get you to actually do it -- as Tony Horton is clearly doing -- I say heap on the praise.      One thing that cracks me up: On the Kenpo disc (one of the best), Tony goes on about what a bad-ass Wesley is, how he developed the Kenpo program, etc. Meanwhile, all through the workout Wesley is phoning it in! Everyone else is throwing solid punches, and he's slogging his arm back and forth like Aunt Bea on downers.      I agree with others who say the product-pushing is annoying, but it's minimal. So just stick with P90X's excellent workout program, and make your own recovery drink.

product_title: TSD Tactical WE 1911 Gas Blowback Airsoft Pistol with Caspian Trademark (Port 5.1 Slide)
review_body:
This pistol works pretty well after breaking in/polishing components. There is flashing from the die casting process that needed to be removed from the slide lock before the slide would lock back on an empty mag. I need to tear down the grip of the gun to make the grip safety work. Accuracy is just ok due to loose fitting parts in the slide (outer barrel to slide, inner barrel to outer barrel). The accuracy is still good enough to hit a man sized target at 50ft. Gas consumption is about 3 out of 5, 5 being very gas efficient; you can go through 2-2.5 mags full of bb's before you run out of gas. Trigger pull is great just like a real 1911, it has a crisp clean break with no creep. Fit and finish is pretty good. The only obvious thing wrong that I can see when the gun is assembled is the polishing on the hammer; there is light pitting on the sides that was never polished off at the factory. The pistol that was shipped to me has a different grip on it. They shipped my pistol with the upgraded Shooters Design brand plastic grip with gold WE logos.
I have a couple of upgrades planned for the pistol to accurize it. A tight bore barrel and custom barrel bushing should help a lot with accuracy, and a mag-well would top things off nicely. I also put some blaze orange sight paint on the front post, this makes a really good sight picture.

product_title: Smith & Wesson Extreme Ops CK5TBS Liner Lock Folding Knife Partially Serrated Drop Point Tanto Blade Albumin
review_headline: Great knife. Caution though, slightly changed from original I purchased.
review_body: For the price, it's difficult to beat this knife. I've become a fan of the Smith and Wesson knives found here on amazon.com. I own one of the search and rescue knives, 3 of the boot knives, and 3 of these folding knives. This knife is of high quality, especially for the price, and easily beats comparably priced Gerber knives.    My first one of these I ordered back in April of 2010. I was EXTREMELY pleased with this knife. For under $11, it simply couldn't be beat. It opened easily with a one-handed flick of the wrist, and held up to much abuse over the nearly 1 year I had it. I've used it for food purposes, opening packages, digging holes, throwing, whittling, prying, and pretty much anything you can think of. My only real complaint with it was in regards to the pocket clip, as it had a tendency to loosen over time (I only tightened it once however). The blade was always able to swing out with a simple wrist flick, and was faster than most automatic and spring assisted knives.    My wife wanted one of these, so we ordered her one, within the last 90 days (1st quarter of 2011). When it arrived, I noticed several differences between mine and hers. The first was that the knife didn't swing open with a simple wrist flick. The second being that it was overall \\"thicker\\". It appears that they are being manufactured differently at this point. The increased thickness was a little disappointing to me, as I was so familiar with my knife (like an old friend), that I knew its feel very well. The third thing that I noticed was a slightly different finish on the blade as opposed to the one I carried at the time.    Fast forwarding a bit, I seem to have misplaced or lost my beloved knife, and ordered a replacement. Unfortunately, it is the same, changed, model that my wife received. I'm sure that I'll get used to it, and will of course loosen it up to swing open easily, but if I would have given the \\"original\\" model 5 stars, I must subtract a star for various flaws the current model has. The most annoying of which (and I need to test this on my wife's to see if it's a problem on her knife) is that when flicking the blade open, the blade stop gets jammed, and won't allow you to close the blade without tearing up your fingers. Honestly, if I'd known that this knife would have changed, even so minorly, I would have purchased 10 of them back last year.    With all of that said, it's still a top-notch knife, which I do highly recommend, at a great price point, and you won't be disappointed.    EDIT: 03/20/11 - I have my found my original knife! I can definitely confirm manufacturing changes at this point, most specifically relating to plastic washers/spacers in the body of the knife separating the blade from the frame. These have increased in thickness, and are causing the lockup issue on the newer knives. I'm looking into a solution.

review_headline: Guess you get what you paid for...
