product_title: Buck Knives 0503RWS PRINCE Folding Pocket Knife with Wood Handle
review_headline: The perfect knife for everyday use, but not like the "made in USA" original
review_body:
My father bought this knife for me before I joined the Boy Scouts in 1978. I still carry it in the original open-top sheath on my belt EVERY DAY! This is my favorite knife of all time and has been with me through hundreds of hikes, camp-outs, fishing trips, hunting trips. It is used almost every day for my cutting needs and has never let me down!

I bought one for each of my older sons when they joined the Boy Scouts (sort of a family tradition now), and I must say that I have seen the quality of the knife get worse over the past 30 years. The one I bought 10-years ago for my oldest son (now 20) was a good blade, but lacked the \\"refinement\\" on the case and wood that my original has, and the sheath lasted only 3-4 years before the belt strap broke. The one I purchased recently for my younger son (now 11) is a much cheaper blade (made in China, not USA), lacks high-polish and shine on the blade, and the wood, bolsters, and rivets look to be \\"thrown-together\\". The craftsmanship has truly been lost in the name of cheap mass-production overseas.... I guess when my youngest (1-yr old) is old enough for Boy Scouts I'll still buy him one to keep with tradition and provide him a perfect-size, every-day knife, but I'll probably be buying a different Buck for him to actually use in the field, unless the quality improves in the next decade!

review_headline: Sloppy -- appears they are shipping something different from picture
review_body:

product_title: Kinetic Home Trainer Folding Bicycle Tire
review_body: It is too bad Kenda did not partner well to provide Kurt Kinetic a complimentary level of quality product.  The install of this tire was very difficult. When I took it out to the range for the first time after putting it on, I was immediately satisfied with my purchase. The recoil reduction system is amazing. There is still slight recoil but nothing close to what it was. There was no break in period, just install and it was good to go. To anybody considering purchasing a new stock for recoil reduction, purchase this one. I would recommend this to anybody with a compatible shotgun without hesitation.     Pros  Adjustable buttstock for comfort to fit anybody.   Pistol grip for a more natural feel, or anybody used to rifles or pistols.   Easy installation. product_title: LifeSpan SP1000 Stretch Partner Stretching Machine
review_body: I have some chronic lower back issues so I'm often on the lookout for \\"solutions\\". I use the Precor 240i stretch machine at the YMCA but the price point is just too high for a collection of aluminum pipes, a seat and handle bars. The LifeSpan SP1000 arrived at my door. Box was a bit beat up...so it was handled a bit roughly by someone along the way. Some smaller parts were scattered throughout the box so I was concerned something might be missing. Assembly was made more difficult by poor instructions but if you have even average mechanical skills its nothing to put together. You may need a helper to hold things for you. All parts, tools were included. The build quality on hardware is as good as Precor, although the seat and knee platforms aren't as well made. However they are more than adequate for home use. With the addition of a torquing joint at the base of the handlebar post you actually can do a few stretches that can't effectively done with the Precor. I can do a circuit of stretching in less than 10 minutes if I'm in a hurray so I'm happy. The design and workmanship are good. I'm 5'11\\" and have no problem with the size so I'm unsure what the commentary about it being for smaller person is referring to. I had an issue with the cross bar that attaches to the base of the handlebar post...it was welded off-center. I contacted LifeSpan and they sent me a new one after an email, phone call, and photograph I attached to email showing flaw. So, customer service would get a top rating from me based on that action. This is a solid investment in your health. Get one.

product_title: Rivers Edge 13' Pack-N-Stack Ladder Stand
review_body: I have always used a climber stand (Lone Wolf S&C) but this year I was selected for a managed hunt very near my home and thought that a ladder stand might make it easier for me to hunt more consistently. I purchased the River's Edge portable ladder and was extremely impressed. Easy to assemble both for the first time and in the field,it lived up to the portable claim. I liked the dark brown paint on the stand. It blended perfectly into the tree I used. I found the seat very comfortable for numerous 8-10 hour sits. My only gripe is that the stand is a little short for bow-hunting.  While I took a nice eight-point from it, many deer noticed me and watched me carefully as they munched the acorns around the stand. One more 2-3 ft section would be helpful and wouldn't add that much more weight. Maybe it should be an option to purchase. All in all a great product.

product_title: Pressureless Tennis Balls - 4 Pack by Unique Sports
review_body: This is the first time i've used pressureless tennis balls. I bought the four-pack since I didnt want to invest a lot of money up-front for the trial run.     I've also never used this brand before (\\"unique\\"), though wilson and penn also make pressureless tennis balls, these were reviewed fairly positively elsewhere so I thought i'd try them out.     My first impressions: they're good. i'd buy them again for sure, and unless i'm playing in a serious match with someone, i'd use basically these all the time.    They play like a \\"slightly wet\\" tennis ball, if you've ever played on a wet court then you know what I mean. I dont mean soaked, but wet. They're a touch heavier when you hit them, in the same way.    But they're bouncy as heck, unlike wet tennis balls; and so they're much better than regular worn-out tennis balls that most people use for practice.     In the bounce test they bounce less high than new-balls-out-of-the-can, but a lot higher than dead-balls-we-used-to-practice-with.     So in terms of bounce they're great and supposedly that bounce never fades. This makes then great for practice or even hitting around with someone if you dont want to waste a new can.     The main difference then comes down to 'feel', that slightly-heavier \\"like-a-wet-ball\\" feel they have when you hit them. Not soaked, just damp or wet ball.     I didnt mind that; i've played my share of games in the rain or right after a rain, and i'm not a tennis-ball-nazi. But it will depend on your tastes of course. My partner across the tennis court did not like that slight change in feel and insisted on putting them away. I guess he's a ball-nazi.     But I dont doubt I can find other tennis players who wont mind it and with them I'd just use these exclusively because they last forever, dont go flat, and are cheap.

product_title: Foam Roller - Full Round 12" x 6"
review_headline: Excellent product - perfect density, not overly hard
review_body:
This is a simple piece of equipment, and it serves its function very well. Among the many foam rollers I have tried, I like this one the best. I use it regularly on my own legs and back to treat trigger points, loosen soft tissue, and increase circulation, and I recommend it to all of my yoga students and massage clients, as well.

Some customers who review rollers insist that only the super-hard, high-density rollers will do, but that's a mistake based on a \\"more pain equals more gain\\" mentality. Muscle tissue, nerves, and blood vessels can be irritated and even damaged by rollers that are too hard. To heal muscles, it is indeed important to massage them deeply and strongly, but it is also important to maintain a hint of softness in the work.

It is much better to ease muscles back to health with patient, consistent and intelligent work than it is to try to force them open in a punishing way. The problems we get into with our bodies are primarily caused by a combination of misunderstanding and willful ignorance about the ways that our bodies respond to stresses. Don't cause more damage when your body is asking for thoughtful attention.

Do yourself a favor and use a well-made roller with a touch of softness to it. Use this roller.

I already had pretty strong hands from these two hobbies, and did wonder how much a difference it could make. I had actually started climbing to build up arm strength for submission wrestling, and people I trained with already remarked how strong my grip was.

I ordered it and started to use it directly, I had ordered the red one (50lbs force) because the reviews on Amazon said the easier ones became too easy too fast (to order the red one solo on amazon isn't currently possible, hence reviewing it here). The red one still challenges me (around 3 months after buying it).

I tried to use it at least three or four times a day, and used it by just closing it solidly 20 times in each hand. Then it grew to thirty, fourty and then fifty times in each hand. My forearms would sometimes almost cramp up after working with it. One day I had to sit through a load of boring lectures and did 500 squeezes with each hand in groups of 100. My arms were swollen up like popeye for a day after that, my watch was almost popping off.

I'm not sure yet how this will affect my BJJ game, I ripped tendons in my knee in a match and haven't trained since I bought this thing. However I kept climbing and it REALLY shows a difference there. Grips that used to just be theoretical to me before are now actual, I feel way more confident hauling myself up and also find that I don't get tired out so easily. I should be back at BJJ soon and am really eager to see how much this will change my game.

To return to the actual details of the product, it's solid (just a thick rubber ring) and will obviously last a long time. It does smell of rubber, although it doesn't transfer to the hands as much as some reviews here make out.

The bottom line is this, it's cheap as hell, durable, does exactly what it says and incidentally relieves some stress I guess. I would absolutely buy it again if I lost it or whatever.it or whatever.

product_title: IronMan LXT850 Locking Inversion Therapy Table
review_body: [[VIDEOID:mo12MK8YRJXT652]]I have had this inversion table for about two weeks now. So far I'm very satisfied. It does provide immediate yet temporary relief of back pain. I say temporary because it's too early to tell if I would get a long lasting relief from back pain. I will update you in few months.  Here are my observations:  - Package was a bit roughed up from its journey. It came with one of the plastic \\"cups\\" that go on the hinge of the stand broken. But I could do without that part since it's just an esthetic part of the equipment.  - Assembly was not too difficult. It took me a little over 4 hours to assemble it because I was watching TV too while assembling it. :) But, I believe it could be put together in about 2 hours.  - Manual is confusing on certain steps. The nuts and bolts were not labeled so, I had to rely on trial and error on certain steps.  - It does come with all the tools you need to assemble it. I.e..light weight screw driver etc.  - The headrest is not adjustable. It looked from the picture that you could adjust the headrest. But I ended up not needing to adjust it anyway, so no biggie.  - Like others mentioned, it's a bit painful on the feet if you are fully inverted for more than few minutes. Wearing sneakers or very think socks helps a bit. I come back up after few minutes to give my feet a break and invert again.  - The blood rushing into your head problem gets better as you get used to being inverted. Mine's almost gone by now. I no longer feel the blood rushing as much. Just a bit.  - The locking mechanism needs a bit getting used to. It may feel stuck or broken at first until you get used to it and know how it works.  - The equipment is very sturdy and feels \\"safe\\" while on it.  Overall, I'm satisfied. If you suffer from lower back pain related ailments this definitely will help you. I think I may have a mild case of sciatica and am hoping this tool will help relieve some of that so I could get back to what I love doing... running marathons!!  Good luck!!!  Update: 12/04/2011  It has been over a year and half since I bought this equipment and I thought I would give an update of my experience.  I must say this is one equipment that is worth every penny. I can't describe enough how satisfied I'm with it so far. Every time my back aches, I get on it for few minutes and when I'm done the first thing that comes out of my mouth is \\"Wow\\". The pain just magically disappears and the feeling is almost euphoric. No pain medication can work that fast!  I have not had any issues with it so far. Nothing is loose or broken. It is still as sturdy and works as great as it did on day one. I highly recommend it!

product_title: Polar CS600X Heart Rate Monitor
review_body:
I spent an hour hooking it up to my bike, and setting the speed sensor to magnet distance using flashing red light, as per instructions. I took it outside to ride test it, and within 30 seconds it beeped at me and said to check the speed sensor. No matter what I did standing alongisde the road, I couldn't make it work.

I took it inside and went through the whole \\"seek sensor\\" steps as per instructions, for another hour, but nothing. Nothing I did could make the red light flash again, so the speed sensor either has a dead non-replaceable battery, or is defective. I have asked the seller whether they will take care of it, or if I have to hassle with Polar. It's annoying having a > $300 bike accessory I can't use for at least the next week while I find out what I'm supposed to do.

1) Seller sends me a working speed sensor - 4 days minimum
2) Polar sends me a RMA, I send them a speed sensor, they analyze it, send me another one, possibly with or without a charge - 2 weeks minimum
3) I order a new speed sensor, am out $55 I hadn't planned on, and still risk it working or not - 4 day minimum

Alas, I'll see about posting more when I find out.

UPDATE: Amazon allowed me to return the item for refund. I did not re-order. Instead I got a $30 wired sensor cycle computer.

product_title: Keiser M3 Indoor Cycle Stationary Trainer Exercise Bike
review_headline: Once I tried it, I *had* to buy it...
review_body: I've been doing quite a bit of research for which bike to buy for home use. I was initially interested in just getting what I have at the gym the Schwinn Evolution. In a store, I was almost sold on the Schwinn A.C. classic or sport, but the seat was very uncomfortable, and I while I loved the magnetic resistance, I wasn't quite convinced by the ride.    Then I found all of these fantastic reviews on the M3. I called around, but it turned out none of the stores that sell them in the area, had them on the floor as demo. Finally, one sales person admitted to me that even though he (and everyone else agreed) thinks it's a fantastic bike, they don't keep it on the floor because their margin of profit on them is much smaller than it is on other bikes.     I didn't want to invest without trying them out, so I called Keiser and found out who our local rep is. Sure enough, he had one we could try in his garage. This is the most amazing piece of engineering I've ever seen on a bike!!! This guy had been with Keiser for 18 years, and knew every detail of what's going on. Basically, they started developing this bike after years of taking losses because they conformed to the price standard in the market, and at that price, could only manufacture bikes that like every other bike, would break and need maintenance. The maintenance cost them too much money, and they got tired of it. Being a small independent company, they decided to do something about it, and the M3 was born. They are ruthless about their price policy of it, even if you buy 250 of those, the discounts are fairly minimal. On the other hand, these bikes require NO maintenance!!!    If you look at their 3 year warranty carefully, you'll see that labor is not included. I called to ask about that, and they claimed on the phone that labor is not NEEDED, because everything you might ever need to do, is so simple you could do it yourself. Well, my spouse has a strong engineering background (experimental physics), and we inspected every aspect of this bike. They're right. It is TRIVIALLY simple to put together, and there's basically nothing that could break!! If you can handle a screwdriver, you can handle this bike! The engineering is GORGEOUS, someone really put a LOT of thought into the design. And the ride, oh the ride... Smoothest ride EVER! And SO comfortable! Everything from the saddle to the positioning, just perfect!!! The balance feels just right, it's super quite, and most importantly, there are really no parts there that could break, except perhaps the computer. As far as maintenance is concerned, according to this guy, it's limited to cleaning up your sweat from the bike, after a workout...    I should mention, when I was looking at the Schwinns, they offered me the floor model at a ~15% discount. The flywheel looked pretty scratched, basically it looked used. The demo we saw, is the same demo the guy has been using for 5 years, to show gyms, take to shows, show private clients, etc. If he had told me he only unpacked them yesterday, I would have believed him. They looked brand new, 5 years later!    Finally, Schwinn spin bikes division has been sold and resold and keeps moving hands. You really don't know who you're buying from (the Schwinn A.C. are on the Nautilus website - their latest buyer, rather than on the Schwinn site). Keiser is solid, made in the USA, and you know who \\"their daddy\\" is... And keep in mind if a sales person tries to sell you a schwinn over the keiser - their margins of profit are MUCH smaller for the keisers, and they usually work on commission.     Anyhow, to make a LONG story short, we bought the bike. It was a no brainer. I'll update my review after I've used them for a couple of months at home, but I fully expect the 5 starts to remain. If you can't find this bike anywhere to try them out before buying, I recommend you call Keiser, and they'll help you out.    *** ADDED A FEW MONTHS LATER *** (Jan 2011)    Now that I've tried these in my pregnant and non-pregnant state, I can stay 100%  - I absolutely adore this bike!! I've been using it almost daily. It's SO smooth, quiet, and comfortable - in seated AND standing positions! I don't get the people who talk about wrong fit. I am 5'6\\", my spouse is 6', and it adjusts to each of us perfectly. Maybe if you're extremely tall or extremely short it might be an issue, but then I bet a lot of other bikes would be too. This is just a very natural ride, the computer is fantastic, and overall, I can say only good things about this bike (and I've tried many other bikes at gyms, including the popular Schwinn Evolution. I *far* prefer this one to any of them!)

product_title: Polar F6 Women's Heart Rate Monitor Watch (Pink Coral)
review_body: The Polar F6 Heart Rate Monitor is a fun little gadget to help you get motivated to work out.  You can track how many calories are burned, and check that you're in your fat burning heart rate zone while you work out.     WIth regards to fit, my wrist is 5 3/4 inches in circumference and this watch fits perfectly.  The watch can be adjusted as small as 4 1/4 inches to as big as 7 1/2 inches.  The spacing between the adjustment holes is about 1/4 inches apart and there are 19 holes, so there is a wide range of adjustment options.  The face is about 2 inches tall and 1 1/2 inches wide.    The stock transmitter is just fine, it came in medium.  It slips right under the band of my work out bra and stays there during cycling, running, and Tae Bo.  I haven't had a problem with it slipping while I work out, and I work out pretty hard (average 450 calories per workout) and have been working out with it for about 7 weeks now.    The only downside is that the program Polar uses to download your workout information to your computer is not Mac compatible for the F6.  So if you have a Mac, make sure to check that the Polar you are purchasing is Mac compatible, as Polar has made some of its newer Heart Rate Monitors Mac compatible.    I would order from this seller again.  I ordered my product around midnight on a Saturday and got my F6 the following Monday!  Quick!

product_title: G.I. Style 2 Quart Bladder Cover (Olive Drab - Green)
review_body: This is the same type of canteen that I used when I deployed to Iraq in the two year's, and it held up to the most brutal use. When I conducted house to house searches, this canteen kept me hydrated when I ran around in 100+ degree heat. I've also slung this canteen as a rifle support for my M-4 and cushion in addition to my MOLLE body armor. I've also remember stepping on this canteen a lot when I was riding as a gunner on an uparmor humvee and dismount on the Bradley tank. I choose this over the camelback because 1) the camelback was uncomfortable for mounting and dismounting on the tank, it hunched my back when I sat down in tight compartment, 2) No matter what, I was always out of water because it can only carry 100 oz of water, 3) a camel back made it hard to maneuver with straps hanging around both of my shoulders, 4) the straw keeps getting in my way or it dangles when I run around, and 5) it was a hassle to get the straps on my shoulders when moving around in a hurry.       The canteen is angled so it's easy to drink out of. The cap comes in two different styles, one with a gas mask adapter and a regular cap, and I've also seen mouth tube adapters, but never actually needed one (mainly because it tangles with my other equipment). The mouth is a 1\\" standard opening small enough to pour water in and drink out of, which can be hard to clean and fit ice cubes into the canteen. One method I found useful to keep the water cool in hot weather is to wet the cover and let it hang in the wind. The construction is almost like a rubber-type plastic, it's very thin, but holds up well to being stepped on without bursting. The bladder is not meant to hold hot water, but warm water is ok. The buckle release is extremely reliable, it can endure multiple impacts and scratches without jamming or breaking. The cover is made of polyester, and the inside is lined with fur to insulate the bladder. I found the cover to be useful for carrying maps, and a note pad. The strap is all metal construction with adjustments for a long or short sling, it's long enough to fit around my body armor and wide shoulders. On the back of the cover are 2 Alice clips that can be mounted to the molle system or a ruck sack.

product_title: OnPar Golf Touchscreen GPS
review_body: Pros:  When I bought OnPar over a year ago, I did so because it was the only model I found that kept detailed scoring (putts, GIR, FIR).  Like other users have said, you have to read the entire manual to fully understand how to use the device.  It is not complicated, just take the time to read the manual and you will get the hang of it quickly.  I know at least on my home course, the yardages are accurate to within at least 5 yards.  I am not Tiger Woods nor Arnold Palmer, so that is close enough for me.  I love that the device allows you to zoom in, as well as move your target around.  If you are on the tee box and want to be 100 yards out on your second shot, the touchscreen allows you to set your target distance in order to set up the 100 yard second shot.  Another great feature is the ability to measure each shot and apply a club to each shot.  This will give you an average/min/max distance for each club as well as make suggestions based on your averages.  You also have the ability to mark the clubs you carry in your bag.  The only con to this is that it still shows EVERY club when applying a club to a measured shot.  The list should be narrowed to the clubs you have selected as being in your \\"golfbag\\".  So far the battery life has been as advertised.  I can go an entire round and not even use up half of the battery life.  You do have to download courses, and if there is a course they don't have, you can request that course be added.  I did this once and it took only about 2 weeks for them to add.  Sounds like some users have had a much longer wait, but my experience with getting courses mapped has been positive.  There is one negative to this and I have listed it below.  At least there are no extra fees for downloading courses.       Cons:  The device firmware does have some freezing issues.  This usually happens to me around the 14th hole.  It still works but will not automatically update your position/distances to the green.  I wasn't sure if it was a bad device or the software.  I emailed customer service about this and they said they are working on an update for the freezing issue with the software.  The only other main issue I have is that I have a Macbook Pro and the device is not compatible with Mac yet.  I even have Windows on my Mac, but CS said you have to have a PC.  The OnPar website states \\"(Mac version coming soon)\\" and has said this since I first bought my device over a year ago.  When I first emailed CS about a release date for the Mac software, they told me by the end of 2010.  I emailed them again on this issue and they now tell me that it will be the first half of 2011 before the Mac version of Synchro is released.  I do not have regular access to a PC so this makes it difficult to update the device firmware, add/delete courses, and check my stats.  I guess I do not understand how it can take so long to create the Mac version.  I guess they have a few other issues to work out first.  OnPar also maps their courses via satellite images.  They do not \\"walk\\" the courses as Skycaddie claims.  I live in TX and at my home course, there are a few holes where rivers/creeks/ponds were obviously dried up when they did the mapping because they do not show up when using the device there.  I know where they are so it's not huge issue for me, but a golfer who has never played that course, may have no idea the hazards exist and that there may be water in them.  You can also send a request to UPDATE a mapped course (which I need to do), but you are still relying on a possibly inaccurate interpretation of the hole.  I question whether Skycaddie has really walked all the courses they have available for download, so I do not know how much more accurate it may be than OnPar.    I paid $400 for this thing and would not recommend paying that much for it.  Knowing what I know now, I would probably pay about $200 for the device as it is right now.  I know it's cheaper now, but with the Skycaddie SGX (I have read very mixed reviews on this as well) now available with many of the same features, do your research before buying either one.  As I have yet to see a retailer who buys/sells used GPS units, so once you buy it you're stuck with it (short of selling it on ebay/craigslist).  I love my OnPar when it does not freeze up.  I rate this as 3 stars now, and will update to 5 stars if/when they fix the freezing issue and the Mac compatibility issue.  With the kinks worked out, this could be one of if not the best, golf GPS units available.  Well, that's my take on the OnPar GPS device, I hope it helps you one way or the other.

review_body: OK first of all, if you dont know how to sharpen a blade properly, or need a pre sharpened blade out of the box dont buy this machete.    Now if you can sharpen a blade and want a custom sharpen on it this is an awsome blade. This is #7 for me in the machete blade world. I have multiple sog, cold steel and a few other name brands this is one that is a keeper. The second i got it out of the box i noticed it was not sharpened(not a problem for me for i know how to sharpen and i like to customize it my self.) The construction seems primative but thats the way it should be it was made to chop through brush and small braches not a show piece at all.(also good for the silent zombie dismemberment lol) the blade is properly weighted to the front for a hard swing increased the PSI once the strike has landed. The hilt is light and very strong but for those who have soft hands or a weak wrist you might like to wrap the handle with 550 cord or something of that nature to increase comfort.    The blade is not weak by any nature but it does have a small flims in it which for me is great because the blade will not break under a strike but will move enough to stay intact. I have put it through a strenious stress test under a shop press to see how may PSI it would take to warp/break the blade so far it has taken 450PSI from the side without warping the blade and the handle took every bit of it. i went into the wood and cleared a path 4 feet wide and 40 feet long with my custom sharpen on it(about 40 minutes of work) and the path is clear as a day. the blade stayed in tact very light dulling and the handle didnt even flinch. My hand was slightly sore and my wrist also.    Over all if you need to clear some brush for a path or need it for survival i highly recomend this blade. it stood up to a magnitude of test and kept on going.

product_title: Schwinn 140 Upright Exercise Bike
review_body:
This is the third exercise bike I have owned, and by far the best. I researched many options before settling on this one, including the lower priced Active 10, 120, and 130 (no longer available) models. I also went to stores to try them out. This is the most expensive of the models above, but seemed to have the best features in this price range. To put this review in perspective, I am a 37-year-old 5' 6\\", 130 pound female, and work out 4x/week on average for 30-40 minutes.

Pros:
1. 16 resistance levels - makes a huge difference over bikes with 8 resistance levels. Switching between levels is very smooth. I owned one with 8 levels, and only used two of them. Everything else was too hard or too easy, and the jump between levels seemed too big. This feels more like something from the gym.
2. Really smooth and quiet - the quietest bike I have ever ridden.
3. Telemetry heart rate monitor - in addition to the contact hand grips (which I have never found very effective on any bike), this bike has built in telemetry, so if you own a Polar heart rate monitor, it will display your heart rate on screen.
4. Display readout - includes additional items, like RPM and Interval Time, which help you monitor how hard you're working out.
5. Heavy and solid - this could be a negative to some people, but the bike is a hefty 88 pounds, and feels very solid.
6. Very adjustable - In addition to the usual adjustment of seat height, there is a fore/aft seat adjustment, as well as adjustability of the handlebars.

Cons:
1. Water bottle holder - this is pretty minor, but I have the hardest time getting a water bottle into the holder. It is just too close to the handlebars. Maybe a different bottle would work better, but I have to sort of bend my bottle to get it in there.

That's about it. So far, just a great bike! If you are looking for a comparison of features between Schwinn models, their website has a great side-by-side comparison.

Update 7/29/12

I still use this bike regularly. It has held up well, although the water bottle holder is still problematic. One other comment - I definitely wouldn't recommend this bike for guys over 6'. My knees get pretty close to the handlebars, and my husband can't use it at all.

product_title: Kershaw Unisex Skyline Knife - 1760
review_headline: Great Knife At An Affordable Price
review_body:
=== Specifications - \\"The Facts\\" ===
-- Blade Steel: Sandvik 14C28N Stainless Steel with Stone-Washed Finish
- A stonewashing looks similar to bead/sand blasted frosting. The blade is refined by tumbling with an abrasive media, or \\"stones.\\" The finish tends to mask any scratches that occur with use.
-- Blade Shape -
-- Handle: Textured Black G-10 Polymer
-- Blade Length: 3.125 inches (7.9 cm)
-- Closed Length: 4.25 inches (10.8 cm)
-- Overall Open Length:
-- Weight: 2.3 oz.
-- Lock Type: Liner Lock
- The \\"liner\\" is a metal part that forms part of the handle. When the blade is fully deployed, part of the liner, called the liner lock, wedges underneath the blade, locking the blade in an open position.
-- Opening Mechanism: Ambidextrous Thumb Stud or Flipper
- A thumb stud is a cylindrical shaped stud that is attached at the base of the blade near the handle, allowing deployment with one hand. The blade opens when moderate pressure with a rotation sweeping motion is applied on the thumb stud with one's thumb.
- A flipper is an extended part of the base of the blade that protrudes on the back side when the blade is closed. The blade flips open when some moderate pressure is applied by one's index finger on the flipper.
-- Pocket Clip: Reversible, Right-side Pocket Clip
-- Lanyard Hole: Yes
-- Function: Everyday Carry, Utility

=== Overview - \\"First Impressions\\" ===
The Kershaw Skyline is a handsome everyday carry (EDC) folding knife. It features a stonewashed stainless steel blade with black, aggressively textured G-10 polymer handle scales. The blade's 3.125 inch length and drop-point blade shape makes it ideal for everyday utility use. The very light 2.3 ounce weight and medium size makes it easy to pocket and a very light burden.

=== Performance/Lasting Impressions - \\"Things to put on the backburner.\\" ===
-- Lock - The Kershaw Skyline locks up very well. Once locked, the blade does not wiggle side-to-side or forward-backward. Liner locks, by nature, are thin; however, for the Skyline, it is more than sufficient. In addition, when the knife is in the closed position, it will not inadvertently open. It takes deliberate and moderate pressure on the thumb stud or flipper for it to open. By pushing the liner lock to the left unlocks the blade to close. Gimping on the liner lock makes closing the blade easy work.
-- Maintenance - The knife is completely user maintainable. All of the screws accept Torx bits. At the knife's pivot point, the use a phosphor bronze washers that allow the blade to open and close smoothly unlike some other knives that uses plastic or Teflon spacers that becomes brittle overtime.
-- Opening - The knifes opens very quickly and smoothly with the use of the flipper. The use of the thumb stud, however, is very difficult. The thumb stud is located too close to the handle, making it hard for the thumb to have any purchase on the stud. The thumb stud is also too close to the knife's pivot point, giving very little leverage to open the knife. Lastly, the shape of the thumb stud resembles a volcano, with the smaller part on top and a large base, reducing the grip on the thumb stud. This makes this knife almost exclusively a flipper opening folding knife.
-- Customization - The pocket clip is reversible for either tip-up or tip-down carry. However, the handles are drilled and tapped for clipping on the right pocket. There are no options for left pocket carry. In either tip-up or tip-down configuration, the knife protrudes about a half-inch out of the pocket. It would be nicer if it would carry deeper, but this is minor.
-- Blade Steel/Sharpness - The Sandvik 14C28N stainless steel, according to the included literature, is \\"shaving sharp.\\" Out of the box, the knife is indeed shaving sharp. This knife should hold up after some use in everyday carry. (I may add to this review later when it comes time to sharpen the knife.)
--Handle Texture/Shape - The black G-10 handle scales has a high traction texture looks like \\"checkering\\" and has the traction of skateboard tape. Even though the aggressive texture is great for maintain control over the knife when cutting and handling, the texturing under the pocket clip makes it a bit hard to clip your pocket and may shred the pocket. The handle's shape is ergonomic and feels solid in hand. A half-moon shape is cutout beneath the blade on the handle giving a perfect place for the index finger adding to grip and control.

=== Recommendation - \\"What I think...\\" ===
This is a wonderful and good looking everyday carry folding knife. If you want a light, compact, sharp, and affordable knife to carry around for whatever task arises, then this is the blade to get. As a right-handed person, the right pocket only setup is not an issue for me; however, for left-handed knife carriers, this may be a major detractor. The aggressive handle texture beneath the pocket clip may be annoying; however, is not a show-stopper for me. I live in an area that has a 4-inch blade restriction, and this knife, with its 3+ inch blade, fits the bill. I understand that this knife is not perfect, but the Kershaw Skyline meets my expectations for a less-than-forty-dollars knife (as of 2010); therefore, I recommend the Kershaw Skyline folding pocket knife for anyone looking for a good budget knife.later when it comes time to sharpen the knife.) --Handle Texture/Shape - The black G-10 handle scales has a high traction texture looks like \\"checkering\\" and has the traction of skateboard tape. product_title: The Complete Knife Throwing Guide by Gil Hibben 64 Pages
review_headline: Good Starting Point For Knife Throwers - Recommended!
review_body:
We bought this Gil Hibben \\"Knife Throwing Guide\\" to help get us started in knife throwing. My son and I have started throwing as a hobby and it has proven a fun pass time with a healthy bit of competition as we both improve. We have started with [[ASIN:B003H4BVS6 3 Pieces Black Spider Throwing Knife Set 6\\" Overall Length]] (which work well), and recently ordered (and like) [[ASIN:B001BG7APA United Cutlery Gil Hibben Small Competition Triple Thrower Set w/Leather Sheath]] as well.

As other reviewers have noted, the book is very thin but it is packed full of important practical information that would be hard to piece together from other sources. The section on knife selection is very well written but certainly does read a little bit like an advertisement for his line knives (but then again he IS the \\"leader\\" in this field).

The throwing instruction sections are very good, including easy to follow instructions with pictures and illustrations are very helpful, especially showing the proper grip for the \\"standard\\" overhand release. Additional pictures on other release methods would have been welcome. There is also an interesting section on axe throwing, but I'm not ready to tackle that area yet.

The section on choosing and building a targets was very worthwhile to me since we have a dedicated practice area for our throwing. Expert advice on what \\"works\\" is why I invest in these types of books since it tends to save in the long run.

As noted above, this is a good starting point and certainly worth the investment if you are planning on taking up this fun hobby.

Recommended!

CFH

product_title: Princeton Tec Yukon HL LED Headlamp
review_body:
I was fly fishing before dawn one morning, wading across a river that is popular with rafting trips. In the pre-dawn gloom, I noticed a faint light coming from underwater, which seemed REALLY odd. I was in waist deep water, and waded over to where I saw the light shining. Looking down into the water, I could see it was a headlamp that someone had dropped. I picked it up with my wading stick, and soaked my arm up to the shoulder to retrieve it from the current. It was a [[ASIN:B000BJ1LIK Princeton Tec Yukon HL 3 LED Hybrid Headlamp (Blue)]] and was just faintly still shining. It had probably been dropped the night before upstream and had swept down to this current eddy.

Well, I turned it off and threw it into my chest pack and went back to fishing for about three or four hours. When I got back to camp, I pulled it out and inspected it, seeing that it had gotten water inside the lens because the lens hadn't been screwed on tightly (it is sealed by an o-ring like a dive light). Also, water had intruded into the battery compartment. I pulled out the batteries and disassembled the lamp and blew out the water, then set it aside to dry for the rest of the day. That night, I put in a fresh set of batteries, and it worked just fine. Sweet! I had a new headlamp!

Fast forward THREE years: Finally, the wiring developed a short inside the battery compartment in a place that was not really fixable. I sent an email to PrincetonTec explaining that I was NOT the original owner and had actually found the light underwater in a river, but wanted to know if I could PAY to have it repaired, I liked it so much. I got an email asking for my address.

Five days later a BRAND NEW Yukon HL lamp arrived in the mail from PrincetonTec. I was blown away.

Two years later, I drop the headlamp (actually flung it across the room on accident) and the battery compartment clip breaks. Again, I email asking to purchase a new clip. Not only does the customer service rep answer my email WITHIN AN HOUR, she asks for my address so she can ship me a new clip at no charge.

Awesome lamp, even better customer service! I will never buy another brand of headlamp besides PrincetonTec, that is for sure!answer my email WITHIN AN HOUR, she asks for my address so she can ship me a new clip at no charge. Awesome lamp, even better customer service! I will never buy another brand of headlamp besides PrincetonTec, that is for sure!

B) Both hooks are plastic, so attaching to the Ski eye, after a couple gentle waves hit, broke the first hook, I then tied the rope to the \\"screw' part, and used the other plastic hook to the ski eye, and less than 30 min later, it broke also. review_body: just as i had expected these weights feel comfortable in the hand and do an excellent job of ripping your muscle, they also make good sand bags for sighting in

review_body: I'm not small man, at 6' and 260lbs, I have a lot to move around. No, I don't work for the company

product_title: Century 13318P-100-012 Womens Boxing Gloves (White/Blue, 12 oz)
review_body: I bought these gloves for Thai Kickboxing, that cover material is a little thin and tore open after my 4th class. So these gloves would be great for low impact boxing. Fit was great, wrist suppost is ok. Again I say, not for high impact punching, but would be suitable cardio training.

product_title: Women's Schwinn Ranger Mountain Bike - 26"
review_body: This is a late review after having used the bike  for over two 2 years. I use it recreationaly to ride with family and friends, on paved sidewalks, dirt trails in the local park or just around the neighborhood roads. I cannot comment on its suitability for Mountain biking purposes, although I would think it will do just as well! I am of a smaller build  (5'3\\") and was looking for a bike that will not be too heavy, and easier to handle. I really wanted an Aluminum frame for that purpose, but could not find any within my budget. So after reading the good reviews, I purchased it(pre assembled) and use it when ever the weather is pleassant.  The best part for me is that althoug this bike is a steel frame, it is lighter than most other comparable models. The gears shift smoothly, makes climbing uphill easy! The brakes work fine, I have never had any issues with them. The seat that came with it is certainly replaceable, and I did. The bottle holder and seat pouch serve thier intended funtions and I love not having to spend  any more on accesories!  I have even riden it several times with a Kangaroo Wee ride child seat attached in the front, and I must say I had no problems with leg space or balancing.  In a nut shell, I LOVE this bike!

product_title: Everlast Mixed Martial Arts Advanced Target Mitt
review_headline: Impossible to fix on hand firmly.
review_body: My previous mitts are much cheaper than these Everlast MMA Punch Mitts but my previous were more comfortable due to adjustable hand velcro.  These just keep moving, so I have to adjust again after a couple of punches.    Just a cheap fixing strap could make this a good product.

product_title: Stealth Cam Jim Shockey "Sniper Pro" 8.0 Mega Pixel Digital Camera
review_body: Don't waste your money!  I own 4 different trail cameras and this is the worst one.  All the other cameras i own were less expensive than this one as well.  I tried using the video setting and camera setting and all my nighttime footage was black.  In a few of the nighttime videos you could barely make out a deer.  I was out bow hunting, took a deer which walked 10 ft away from the camera right in front of it and nothing.  I took the deer and after getting down from the bow stand the camera took a photo of me and i walked the same path as the deer.  No telling how many animals have walked by and nothing.  Most of the pics are blank as well.  The day pics of deer it did get looked good, but overall the camera is garbage.   I tried to call stealthcam several times and waited on hold for over an hour each time before getting disconnected.  I emailed them and they want me to pay to ship it back so they can fix it.  Worst customer service ever.  They said it will take 4-6 weeks to fix and send back.  The season will be over by then.  What a waste of money.  Don,t make the same mistake, buy something else.

product_title: Osprey 10-40x50 IMR 30mm Tube Tactical Riflescope TA104050IMD
review_body: This scope has amazing value. I would guess something like this would be in the $600-$1,000++ range. But for under $200 you just can't pass this up. It's built extremely well. I would compare the quality and lens clarity to my Nikon Bushmaster scope. Wind, elev, and parallax knobs are sturdy when fastened properly, zoom is very smooth, and the red/green infinite variable illuminated mil-dot is phenomenal.  The pop up lens covers are see through for speedy shooting.    One thing I was skeptical of before purchasing was the beginning magnification of 10x and it's minimum range ability. I've found with the parallax adjustment, which acts as a focus, you can shoot a minimum of about 20-25 yards. I hope this helps someone.     I foresee demand increasing, which means price will increase. So when they are back in stock I'd get one ASAP!     The first (currently) user pic is mine. I picked up the 8\\" two step sunshades at [...]. I'm also selling a new in box version of that savage 17hmr rifle email socotx@live.com for info.    Happy shooting!

product_title: Stamina InTONE Jogger with Handlebar Plus Jogger Workout DVD
review_body: I have had my jogger several weeks now but just started using it this week and I really like it. I bought a Leslie Sansome walking dvd and walk, bounce, kick, etc on the jogger for a low impact workout. I like outside walking but that is not always possible for me so this is perfect. I recommend this jogger to anyone & everyone!

product_title: Hunter Safety System Reversible Safety Harnesses
review_headline: So Easy You'll Actually Wear It
review_body: I purchased a safety harness years ago, the older, strictly nylon webbing and buckle kind that gets tangled up and takes 10 minutes of sorting out before you can actually figure out how to put it on. product_title: Confidence Fitness Space Saving X Bike
review_body: I like this bike. I fits between the bunk and the passenger seat fairly well. I use a bungee cord to hold it in place, although I have never had it move from its location. The bad part is the digital counter isnt calibrated very well, and after two or three days it quit registering the bike, so no minutes, miles or cal count. Im betting its a lose wire, but i use a timer on my phone and just pedal til I think I might die, or after 20 minutes, whichever comes first.     Its a good buy for a trucker who doesnt want to get out and walk in the weather or bad areas we sometimes deliver to. I turn on a movie and just start pedalling. Its well worth the 129 bucks I spent, and with it right in front of you anytime your in the sleeper, your bound to use it just to get your money's worth!

product_title: NiteRider MiNewt 200 Headlight
review_body: I ride in the dark a lot because I commute to work in the early moring. My life is dependent on my lighting and after daylight savings, I always ride with two independent systems because they are so prone to failure. NiteRider taught me this lesson, but I've since determined that NiteRider is the riskiest one I've used. They have failed on me so many times. They have always been great about repairing them after the fact, but that's no help if you're stuck in the dark.  Plus Features   Plenty of light   Fairly easy to mount   Strobe is better than others  Problems   Very suseptable to rain damage. I ride in the rain and often have my bike on the car in the rain. The one time I got any feedback from Niterider about why my light failed they said it was water.   Connectors are a real problem. The wire has to be aligned with a flat spot on the battery and this is almost impossible to do with heavy gloves on in the dark.   If you own multiple NightRider systems you're in big trouble because the chargers and batteries are identical in every way but if you use the wrong battery, charger, or light they say it will destroy the unit and I suspect that may be why I had so many problems even though i learned to put a sticker on each unit when I got it saying what it went to. I wrote NiteRider about this but they never responded.    Rubber bands deterioate after a year.  These lights might be good for the occasional night rider, but not for the serious user in my opinion.

product_title: Water Blocker Sock
review_body: I ordered this sock with the special cuff but all I got was the regular waterproof sock from Big Edge, which I already have.  I can always use another pair of the regular waterproof sock, but it certainly doesn't give you the water seal promised by the product that I had ordered. I noticed that Big Edge was gracious enough to mis-label their the packaging, going right over the original label, although the top of the package clearly says \\"all season socks\\". The cuff seal is not there, so if you ordered the sock with a cuff seal and then were sent the wrong thing, you might have a water leakage problem. So, buyer beware. I'll keep the socks, as I said I can always use them, but it was disappointing to get the wrong one. Do NOT use Big Edge. product_title: Attwood 9065-1 Battery Box Standard
review_headline: Nice battery box, but with one fatal flaw...
review_body: I thought this would be a great battery box when I ordered it.  It's a good price, with a good marine name (Attwood).  However I had to return it as it had one fatal flaw.  This is a \\"vented\\" battery box... which is good, but they decided to put the air vent holes on the top of the battery box directly over the terminals!  What good is a battery box on a boat if you have water/rain splashing and having that water being directed to drain directly on top of your live electric metal battery terminals/wires and then ultimately filling up with battery box with water so your battery is \\"swimming in a bath of water!  I guess I could have put a couple of pieces for tape over the holes as there is already plenty of venting in the box where the cable openings are, but why not just buy a marine ready box?    I understand from Attwood's web site that they make a \\"non-vented\\" version.  It's harder to find, but boaters should get that box instead.

review_body: This is the best Kill Bill Demon Sword you can buy...it is made from 1045 or 1060 High Carbon Steel if I remember correctly and is not the cheaper ones that are made of either stainless steel that is sharper like a knife, but breaks if used for a sword.  Stainless steel is only good for less than 12 inch blades.  Then there is the cheapest 440 High Carbon Steel that this one is not...What you want to look for is Real Ray Skin, Full Tang, Double Peg, Leather or Nylon wrap (Ito), Hamon (hand made would be best), and good metals for the tsuba etc.  Katanas come in various sharpness depending on the usage.  If you want a good heavy weight cutter, you want a blade that is heavier and not as sharp (sharp blades break quickly unless you pay the Yakuza price of $1500 for a cheap handmade)  Anything under $1500 should not be razor sharp unless you want it to break.  Best blades to get would be 1045 or 1060 High Carbon Steel.  Make sure you wipe the blade after cutting acidic things like fruits etc.  Also, make sure you oil the blade with Choji Oil (you can make your own if you mix mineral oil with clove oil).  Regardless, this is the best blade you can get for this price range.  Leather handles, real ray skin, and over 1045 High Carbon steel is excellent!

product_title: MTech USA Tactical Folding Knife
review_headline: Look Closely- Be Sure You're Getting What You Pay For
review_body: Before you buy this knife, look closely at the picture given. The M-Tech knife is a plain manual folding knife. I purchased the M-Tech knife last year, however I lost it, so much did I like it that I bought it again. On arrival(which may I say, was very prompt) I discovered that this was a knock-off by a different company.         If you want the M-Tech knife look very carefully at the picture. Some things to look out for are:  1. The M-Tech knife is a manual knife- the knock-off is spring assisted(I know you can't tell this by looking at the picture, I just forgot to mention it earlier)  2. The M-Tech will have \\"M-Tech USA\\" stamped on the top right hand side of the blade - The knock-off has \\"Stiletto\\" written there instead.  3. The thumb-Stud on the M-Tech is located on the top side of the blade- The thumb-stud on the knock-off is on the top flared cross hilt.         These are the main things, other minor details such as shorter handle scales made out of lesser quality Mother of Pearl, are not easily seen in a picture. If I was buying the knife that I received I would be very pleased with it. However I would just like the knife described, pictured, and named on the page.           M-Tech Knife: Five Stars.         Knock-Off: Not original, but still Five Stars.

product_title: Gamo MTS 1000 Moving Target System
review_headline: How to make this system work almost flawlessly
review_body: This target system will be a big disappointment to you unless you do something about its instability. The track is made of six one-foot sections, held together by a few plastic gizmos at each junction. Every little movement of this set up will throw the track alignment out of whack, and cause the track car (which carries the deer) to hang up. But it's fixable. Here's what I did....    I got a 7 foot length of 2x6 and layed the track out on it. A straight edge should be used to *precisely* align the track pieces. Then drill a hole through the bottom of each track section and screw it into the 2x6. The result is a rigid, nearly flawless, track. The car runs without pause, and resets the deer briskly at each end. Very neat, very fun.    The only drawback is that the system is not easily broken down. So don't. I attached a handle to one end of the 2x6 and just drag (it's kind of heavy) the system into the garage when I'm done for the day.

product_title: Oceanic Vortex V-6 Full Foot Split Fins
review_body: On my first cruise I decided to give snorkeling a try and I must say I hated it very much. They dropped me off in very deep water with a large snorkeling vest that dug into my armpits, and very large heavy rubber fins that were like anchors. It was a hard workout keeping my legs horizontal, It was a struggle keeping me a float. The snorkel they supplied me with was always letting water in my mouth. I thought I was going to drown. I am serious! I struggled to keep a float and was last to get back to the boat because I was tired a worn out.    The party with me brought their own snorkeling equipment with them and had a great time (They went on several cruises). Of course they did not mention anything to me before the trip that it was best to bring my own gear. The next year I brought my own gear.    I read lots of reviews on the net and decided to buy these fins along with a Oceanic Reefsport Snorkeling Vest (The perfect snorkeling vest). I also bought a Ultra Dry Snorkel ( A dry snorkel is a must have) and a right fit mask. I had a great time! These fins are light and moved me with a little amount of effort. I was able to hover like a frog with a light flick of my feet. These fins are not like non split fins at all. All it takes is a  flicker of the feet to get me going. Very easy to use. If you do get these fins get the Oceanic Reefsport Snorkeling Vest also. The Oceanic Reefsport Snorkeling Vest is soft and small. It does not dig into you and it held me up perfectly (225 lb with a little amount of air) when I wanted to relax for a few seconds in the water and drift.  I really had a great time. These fins are great.        Things you need when you are going on a snorkeling excursion.    1. A good set of fins.  2. A good Snorkeling Vest.  3. A mask that fits your face.  4. A dry snorkel.  5. A large mesh bag to carry your gear and towels.  6. A waterproof case\bag for cellphone, money, and ID cards to get back on the ship.  7. Water shoes (To walk on the beach when not snorkeling)

review_body: I haven't bow hunted since 05' and was getting a little \\"bow fever\\" so I went out looking for a new bow to shoot. I was shooting the infamous whitetail II. product_title: Shorty Sheild Half Helmet Shield 3 Snap Solution
review_headline: Great for knocking down the wind, if you use it right
review_body: This works well, but you need to be sure that you've got the half-helmet sitting exactly right on your head.  I tended to wear my half-helmet too far back on my head, and that puts the shield up too high, funnels wind toward your face, and gives you a sore neck from trying to tip your head down.  A guy at the local cycle shop, where I got my helmet, helped me to figure out the solution: make sure that the front of the helmet is right over your eyebrows.  Then, you'll find that this shield sits exactly right, with your eyes looking right through the middle of it.  I should also note that the seller is awesome, they shipped it out right away and the item looks great.  Yeah, there's a minor blemish on the front lower edge, and they explain that on their ebay page, it's part of the manufacturing process.  It's a trivial thing, and the shield itself is great.  Much better than just a pair of cheap sunglasses!

product_title: Mountain House Lasagna With Meat Sauce
review_body: The good: Edible both from-the-package and fully-cooked (though I admit to having to take a moment to summon up the courage to try this one uncooked: the noodle and tomato-sauce-powder combo had a pleasant salsa-chip vibe going on, but the crunchy beef chunks made me squirm), convenient, light weight. I can't call this a two-person serving - I could probably have finished the package off solo under normal conditions.    The bad:  Prepared as directed, it was rather soupy.  I'd cut out about 1/4 the water if I were eating it again.  It was considerably more acidic tasting than I expected.  I personally didn't really enjoy it, but I admit that it's not much worse than the frozen stuff you can pick up in a grocery store, aside from the texture (which still wasn't horrible.) I also sampled this one while sitting around on a lazy Saturday evening, rather than after building up an appetite all day out in the elements like usual.

product_title: Timex Ironman Men's Race Trainer Heart Rate Monitor with Data Xchanger Watch, Black/Grey, Full Size
review_body: I love this Timex HRM. Great product, easy to use, comfortable, stylish very user-friendly.     The HRM Strap  The adjustable strap is a good design. You'll definitely forget you're wearing it after a minute or two. After 20+ sweaty workouts, no grime/ salt build-up...be sure to rinse it daily. There is no pinching on my skin and it doesn't 'bulge out' in the middle like Polar.     The Watch  The watch is well-constructed and very breathable. Timex is a well regarded timekeeper and the user-interface is very intuitive. Other than basic time/ date functions, it has 3 alarms, two time zones and a really neat Interval timer.....great for working on sprints etc. The Heart Rate Monitoring is pretty straightforward...you can set target zones etc....it will beep if you're above your zone (you'll have to program that). The Time Device Agent...isn't much to write home about....it is very easy to sync your watch. If you have Windows 7, the troubleshooting page will guide you through set-up. You can edit the type of workout and view graphs of your target zone, recovery period etc. Provides a ton of information. The only thing is I wished it would sync with Google Health or Cardio Labs (for your phone)...but you can manually add your rates.   I deducted one star...because yes, they bands cannot be replaced yourself if they break...you'll have to ship it to Timex if that happens. I haven't had any break...but it's something to keep in mind. I got a 2-year extended warranty from square trade which should offer me some protection.     Data Xchanger  Simple thumb-drive USB plug which wirelessly syncs the watch data with the Timex Program. If your watch doesn't have this you can buy it separately, but this version ships with it....worth the extra price.   Overall, a great product that is functional yet attractive.

product_title: Garmin Oregon 450T GPS
review_body:
I purchased this unit for light hiking, based on years of positive experiences with Garmin products. I returned it after one use.

The problem is simple: The screen, even at its brightest, is too dim for easy use in normal daylight. It's not unreadable, but it's very difficult to read. Instead of a quick glance, you have to stop walking, press the screen to wake it up, and then manipulate it to the proper angle so you can see it correctly. Even at its highest brightness, it's not bright enough.

The unit seems rugged, well-designed, and easy to use. I wanted to like it. With a bright enough screen, I would definitely have kept it. For a casual hiker like me, though, a $2.99 app on my iPhone works far better. I suppose if I end up needing something more rugged and task-specific I'll have to find something different, because this unit was a big disappointment.

product_title: UTG Premium 1 Rings, High, Weaver Mount, See-Thru
review_body:
I'm going to keep this review short and sweet. I have used this model of rings on my Remington 700 in .308 with 26\\" hbar and a couple of different scopes. I use a machined aluminum pic-rail that only ran me about 40 bucks. In each set up the rifle, and myself, are keeping under 1/2moa out to 200 yards. I have not had the opportunity to shoot beyond that distance as of yet but I can't imagine it being any different out to 400 or 600 yards. My question is, why do I need to spend between 90 and 140 bucks on a set of rings when these do the intended job with results to back them up? Am I going to shoot tighter groups than 1/2moa by dropping another hundred dollars on rings? I doubt it.
These mount up tight, stay tight. I never have a ring related loss of zero or had any of them break for any reason. They are my rings of choice, I don't care what I'm shooting.

review_body: 20 minutes after receiving this product, my five year old son had torn the cover by simply running his finger along the edge as he looked at the cards he had just put in. product_title: TYR Lycra Swim Cap
review_body:
I've had Speedo & Keifer lycra caps - learned years ago that by far the easiest way to deal with my long hair (below shoulder blades & very thick) is to first shove it under a lycra cap, then slide a silicone cap over it to keep most of the chlorinated water off of it. the TYR caps are definitely larger, I think you get at least another inch of height on the cap - which if you've any amount of hair at all I think makes the fit vastly better. I have a somewhat small head - just a lot of hair. The Speedo's would barely cover my hair, and if my hand slipped pulling on the silicone cap the Speedo lycra would just pop right off, whereas the TYR stays in place.

I also learned the trick of wetting my hair before a swim and putting a light leave-in conditioner in, before stuffing it underneath the swim caps, in order to have the least amount of chlorine water absorbed. I tried using a silicone cap alone - they provide good protection, but with all my hair it was just a complete pain to get it all underneath the silicone cap. The addition of the lycra cap makes the whole hair preservation process a lot simpler.

product_title: Contigo Kids bpa Free Mug 4 Pack - Two 9 oz Lavender Mugs & Two 9 oz Pink Mugs
review_headline: no way to clean inner rubber seal
review_body: We have had these mugs for almost a year and they have seen daily use.  I LOVED them until recently.  No valves to clean, no leaks, no problem!  But then a month or so ago I happened to look closely at the inner rubber seal as I was washing them.  I usually press the button and let warm soapy water go through the lid, as recommended, to clean them.  This time I happened to notice the part of the seal that goes underneath the plastic edge when it is sealed.  You can only see it when pressing the release button and looking down into the sippy hole from the top.  There was black mildew all along the lip of that rubber seal.  On closer inspection, I turned the lid over and looked inside and could see more underneath.  I tried removing it with toothpicks, soaking it in baking soda and warm water as the Contigo site recommends, and even a brief soak in a bleach solution (not recommended, but this was my last resort).  Nothing worked.  The next time I filled it, I could see black particles floating in the water.  Disgusting.  The gasket can be removed and cleaned, which I had previously done, but there is no way that I have found to clean the inner seal.  The automatic seal is great - except for the fact that it never thoroughly dries even when properly cleaned, since it is always closed unless the button is pressed.  Now I'm wondering how long my child was ingesting mildew, and need to find some replacement cups.  The company website says it will only replace or refund purchases made directly from their company and I don't want to pay return shipping for a partial refund through Amazon.  Unless someone has a solution for this problem, I would no longer recommend these cups.

He uses them every day and they have lasted great so far.  I would recommend these for anyone who needs to do exercises  on the arms or shoulders!

product_title: CARBINE GUN CASE
review_headline: Doesn't fit the full length M1
review_body:
Unless there is some fake M1 reproduction that's smaller than a genuine M1 garand (which we all know would be highly stupid), well, this case does not fit my grandfather's M1 (the one he used in WWII, which is why I bought it). This was intended as a gift for my father. We specifically picked this case, NOT THE CARBINE case. But the carbine case is the case he received, and incidentally, it doesn't fit the M1. So, he's easy-going, thankfully, and the case fits a shotgun and he's pretty happy about that.

In the future I will probably not buy from Sportsman's Guide. My father told me that he stopped buying products from them for this very reason--the products they ordered were not the products they received, far too many times. I'm sure the actual M1 garand case that's NOT the carbine case is awesome. I'll just never know because they sent the carbine case. For Christmas, I intend to find the proper case for the M1 and I'll most likely get it from Cheaper than Dirt. I've never had a problem ordering from them--the products I specify are ALWAYS the products I receive. I hate to give a bad review, but it's quite frustrating to send a present to someone who lives far away from you and end up having to explain why they didn't get the thing you meant for them to get. I'm just really glad Sportsman's Guide didn't send him camouflage lingerie or something. Ha ha. But seriously, how difficult can it be to run your business right?

product_title: 50-lb. Pistol Crossbow
review_body: I bought this same crossbow for my own little X-mas present and I wanted to kick myself for even thinking that it would be worth it. First off the string has to be put on yourself! If you know how it will take about 15 minutes If you don't then don't bother you will end up trying to find something to help get it on easier (like a screwdriver) and your line will snap.Yes, I did this because after a half hour of trying to put it together I was desperate. Needless to say you actually have to twist the string just right to get it to go on (even on my 2nd string I still used something to pry it on). It's really impossible to do it without using something for leverage. Ok, once you finally get the string on you will think that you are ready to go...not so. The string, once cocked back and safety on, is in a very dangerous place...I had it go off repeatedly even in safety! Stupid crazy!! You would think this was enough, but(lol) when I did get it working properly after several repeated attempts when I would press the trigger, the string would actually go right over the arrows and just hit air. This now happens on every attempt. Bottom line I say just get the arrows and throw them yourself... you will get more enjoyment!

Even after long use after the crack it hasnt gotten worse or anything and its not really that noticeable. I'm not into airsoft wars but I bought some extra bbs and a gel target that catches the bbs and have had much fun with it. Overall, I think it's a great gun and i've had fun with it thus far, no, it's not perfect but it is only $12 and the shipping is free so you can't beat that in my opinion.

product_title: Captains of Crush Hand Gripper
review_body:
For all those \\"used-to-be\\" gym rats (like myself) who never trained on grippers before, this is a great addition to that renewed workout schedule. Doubtless you're like many others who've used the grippers of yesteryear, with the colored plastic handles. They serve a purpose and can set the stage for these Captains of Crush Hand Grippers.

After reading the reviews and attempting to judge which set to purchase, I decided on the No. 1 grippers. For those eager to gain that powerful handshake, these grippers are an excellent choice. There are guys out there who live to crush the hands of others in a hand shake. One buddy of mine does it all the time..his hands are rough like boiled leather due to working outside all the time. His grip is amazing for a smaller guy, and he has no trouble reaching into a pot of boiling water to take something out. I'd say his grip is a match for mine or perhaps a bit better.

Aside from that, there's only been a time or two when someone's handshake felt like a true heavy-duty vise grip. It's those that I'll never forget, since they were so overwhelming. That's the grip I want.

**Note: the shipping time on these was AMAZING! Ordered Tuesday night after 8pm and was told to expect shipping time of 3 to 5 business days. To my surprise, they arrived in the mail that Friday. I was blown away, because I didn't expect them till the following Wednesday. Kudos to Amazon and IronMind!**

When the box arrived, it contained the gripper set, a short instruction manual, the order/receipt and a cool IronMind catalog [like 50pgs]. I'm sure glad I didn't order the No. 1.5 or 2.0. These grippers are NOT EASY! Since I don't have a set of warm-up grippers [as recommended in the above-mentioned literature], I was slightly concerned. They were not lying when they said most guys at the gym cannot close these. I'd bet it's quite true.

**Recommend adding the Starter or Trainer as a warm up gripper**

Not knowing what to expect, I gave it the old college try. My first set was less than stellar. I failed to fully close the grippers with either hand. The diamond grips on the handles are excellent and by the 2nd set my hands had that strength \\"memory\\" back [to some degree]. I was able to close the grips completely 3x with the right hand and 2x with the left..and did a total of 6 reps for each hand.

Due to my inexperience, I waited about 20mins between sets, not wanting to accidentally injure myself..especially so soon after trying. By the third set, I was ready again and was able to close the grips 2x with the right hand and nearly 2x for the left [about 1/4in open]. Remaining reps were judged as \\"less than manly\\", with accompanying facial contortions, spastic arm raises and guttural noises.

**Note: I am mixing the conventional and upside-down grip methods**

Since this is my first week with the grips, I'm taking IronMind's advice and only doing sets 3x per week. If all goes well, I should be ready to increase sets and reps after 2-3 weeks. At that rate, I should be very comfortable with these -- and ready to move up to No. 1.5 in two months. My first main goal is to conquer the No. 2 gripper.

In my estimation, these gripper levels are much like hurricanes or earthquakes..as you graduate to the next level, your grip strength rises geometrically. For example, a Category 2 hurricane requires 10x the strength as a Cat1..so by the time you reach Cat5 [155mph+], it requires 10,000x the power required to create a wind speed 2x faster than at Cat1[70mph+]. product_title: NEMO Nano Two Person Ultralight Tent 2009
review_body: Bought this tent as a closeout from a major outdoor retailer's outlet site along with the fitted footprint. It's been set up twice indoors (to check it out) so far and we are planning on using it outdoors for the first time this weekend. The tent itself packs down very small into it's drybag-style compression sack and the poles have their own separate bag for storage. The tent comes with 5 aluminum Groundhog-style tent stakes, which is a sufficient number to stake out all four corners and the vestibule. You will need 4 more stakes if you need to guy it out for wind. The Nano seems well thought-out overall, with a good ratio of size to weight. It seems to fit our Kelty Light Year down bags fine side-by-side, but I'm 6'3\\" and use a long sleeping bag and JUST fit this tent with no room to spare. The internal pole system makes for a very tight, ridged tent. I don't see this thing getting knocked down or collapsing under the weight of weather. You would be breaking poles or tearing fabric before this happened; about the only thing I can see happening is it blowing away if not staked properly.  We also own a Eureka! Spitfire 2 which is one of the few lightweight 2 person backpacking tents that will accommodate tall folks. It is also a fine tent and has been with us on numerous backwoods adventures. It has some problems though, the first being that it is very long and it is sometimes difficult to find a suitable space to pitch it. It is also noisy and loosens up in wind, and as it is not free-standing, is prone to collapse. I am hoping that the Nano will resolve these two issues, and that the Nano's vestibule will provide a dry place for boots and such.  UPDATE: Used the Nano overnight 3/19/2009 and the one of the vestibule zippers separated during setup. We went ahead and used it anyway and did o.k. because it was a clear night with lows in the upper 40's. Tent was comfy enough even with the vestibule not completely closed. Returned the damaged tent to the place of purchase and they just happened to have another one, so we're going to give it another shot. Hopefully, the new tent will not have this problem - if it does, we'll probable just continue using the Spitfire 2 or possibly get the Black Diamond Skylight 3. Happy camping!

product_title: Speedo Women's Race Learn to Swim Super Pro Swimsuit
review_headline: A fitting guide for those unsure (at the bottom)
review_body:
Alright, I went out on a limb when I bought this because, let's be realistic: one cannot hope to find a bathing suit at the end of the October for a good price. Enter: Amazon. I just got this bathing suit last week, and I have to say it is great. I am a 'more-than-average swimmer', I go swimming 3-4 times a week, even during the winter months (I swim in an indoor pool...).

Pros --
1. Very happy with the slimming of this new bathing suit as compared to my worn and stretched-out version (and also 'see-thru' spots where the chlorine got to it). It slims down the body very well and makes the legs look lengthy (something I need since I have short legs)

2. Since I swim in an indoor pool, it is, of course, a public pool with a high chlorine content. I chose to go with Blue instead of Black (because black, it seems to me, is more easily able to see the chlorine effects after a period of time), and so far the fabric seems to be holding up just fine against the outrageous chlorine content of the public pool.

3. I didn't buy this suit for style: I bought it because I needed something that I could wear 4 times a week at the gym. If you are looking for something stylish (and possibly low-cut), look elsewhere. But I needed a bathing suit that wouldn't 'ride down' when I was swimming, and this one is high-cut, which is just what I need to keep the ladies in place while I swim.

Cons --
1. Amazon is usually very fast with their shipping. I don't know if it is the time of year and I'm buying a stupid bathing suit or what, but the shipping this time was about 7-8 days, where usually it is about 3-4 days. If you need one quickly and it is during the 'not normal time' to buy a bathing suit in your corner of the universe, then I would go with the 1-2 day shipping or get it somewhere else.

2. Sizing. Oh boy. Let me just say this: if you are \\"pear-shaped\\", go with one size up from your cup size. I bought a 36 but I'm having a hard time getting my ass into it, next time I think I will go with the 38 and see how that turns out.

SIZING TIPS
------------------
Of course, anything can help at this point, right? When you click on the \\"Sizing Chart\\", it gives you a sizing chart for Amazon.com, and NOT for Speedo. Don't even bother going to the Speedo website (unless you live outside the US, I mean), because it gives the whole sizing chart in centimeters, ugh. Speedo sizing chart can be found here:

Amazon doesn't let me post the website but it is Dick's Sporting Goods store, go to google and type in this (leave out the quotes):
\\"dicks womens bathing suit sizing chart\\"

Start with your bra size as a baseline, and adjust up or down depending on your waistline (or butt-line, in my case).
